author: bharvey88
body:
## What changed

WizMote buttons 1 to 4 can now pick a page under **Showing**, not only what the panel follows.

- New button choices: `scoreboard`, `clock`, `smartboard`, and `fx:Effect,Palette,speed,intensity` (Effects with an effect of its own). Only the effect is required; the palette defaults to Default and speed and intensity to 128. Names are checked against the effects and palettes the build has, in any case, and come back in the panel's spelling.
- An Effects button keeps its setup in the button's existing saved bytes (effect name in the 16-byte name, palette as its WLED palette id, speed and intensity in the other fields), so the saved settings don't change size. The effects package hands the component the effect and palette names at boot (`set_request.h` `FxNames`).
- A press goes to the YAML through a new `remote_page` action (`pages/wizmote.yaml`): an Effects button sets its effect, palette, speed and intensity first and then switches Showing, so the old effect never flashes up. A page that is already showing stays.
- A button that follows something (a team, a playlist, a sport row, All favorites, Live games, or its own favorite) now also switches Showing back to the Scoreboard when the Clock, Smart board or Effects is up. It also ends After the game's clock or Smart board: a `held` flag in the wake state keeps it down until a game of the owner's goes live again, so it comes back after that game's final. `held` is kept in RTC memory; the mark changed, and the old layout is still read (with `held` off), so the update doesn't wake a panel After the game turned off. A **Nothing** button and an empty favorite's button still do nothing.
- Device page: each Remote picker has a **Showing** group. Picking **Effects** saves what Effects is set to now and shows it as "Effects: Rain, Ocean"; **Change** under it opens that button's own Effect, Palette, Speed and Intensity, which change the button only.
- Docs: `using/remote.md` (the new choices, the scoreboard coming back, a button's own effect) and the After the game section of `using/brightness-and-clock.md`; the app picker note is one Coming in the next app update note. Changelog lines under Unreleased.

## API

No new keys. `remote1` to `remote4` in `/gameday/set`, the state's `remote[n].v` and the settings backup take the four new values. `tests/fixtures/api/set_forms.json` lists them.

## Testing

- `make -C tests`: all suites 0 failures (test_parse 12371 checks; new checks for the page values, fx parsing and refusals, resolve, the settings import, and the After the game hold across a game).
- `python3 tests/web/mock_device.py --selftest`: 230 set cases, 0 failures (three new cases).
- Device page tests: a new test for the page choices and an Effects button's Change controls; the full suite passes locally.
- `esphome compile firmware/gameday.yaml`: compiles.
- Panel bench on a scoreboard75 test panel, with a bench build whose four extra buttons run the same press script a real WizMote press does: 15 of 15 checks passed. The four values saved and read back; the Effects button put Showing on Effects with Rain, Ocean, speed 40, intensity 200 (the log's first effect line was "Effects on: Rain", so the effect from before never started); pressing it again stayed on Effects; Clock and Smart board buttons switched Showing; a team button brought the Scoreboard back from the Smart board, Effects and the Clock; a Nothing button left the Clock up; with After the game on Show the clock, a team button ended the clock ("no clock until the next game's final"), and it stayed down 90 s later, after a restart, and after switching After the game to Show the Smart board. The panel was put back on its release build, and its settings matched the copy saved before the bench.

author: mrkhachaturov
body:
## What this changes

CI now gates pull requests the way orca-server does, versions like orca-server, and publishes only on purpose.

- `build.yaml`: changes filter, PR title through the hk `commit-msg` hook, lint, `test:series`, `test:unit`, the image, and `Gate` as the one required check.
- Versioning as in orca-server: Dekart 0.27.0 releases as `27.0.N`, the last slot ours, so one upstream version can carry several releases of the series.
- Publishing: dispatch `Build` with `patch` = N. It pushes `27.0.N`, `27.0`, `27` and `rolling` to `ghcr.io/astrateam-net/geoart`, attests it, and refuses a tag that is already published. Pull requests and `main` build and run `tests.yaml` without publishing.
- `image.yaml` is a reusable workflow whose jobs inherit the caller's permissions: read-only for builds, write for a release.
- The build cache is geoart's own `geoart-build-cache` package. The first release pushed the image by digest only (`sha256:20e043c4…`, no tags) and then failed writing the cache into the containers repo's `build_cache` package, which I had copied by name.
- `test:unit`: `go vet`, `go test` and vitest on what the series and overlay touch.
- `CODEOWNERS`, dependabot for actions, PR template, `renovate.json5` that leaves the submodule and upstream's go and node alone.

After merge: a ruleset on `main` like orca-server's, then the first release with `patch` = 0.

## Owner

- [x] Neither — docs, CI or tooling.

## Checks

- [x] `mise run lint` and `mise run test:unit` pass locally.

author: cg-pm
body:
## The bug

`docs/PRODUCTION.md` §5b2 step 3 has the operator run `logins.sql` as RDS's master user. On RDS that fails:

```
ERROR: must be able to SET ROLE "aintercept_worker"
```

RDS's master user isn't a superuser. Since Postgres 16, a `CREATEROLE` role that creates a role gets `ADMIN` on it but not `SET`, and `ALTER DATABASE … OWNER TO aintercept_worker` / `ALTER SCHEMA public OWNER TO aintercept_worker` need `SET`. The existing `TestLogins` runs as a superuser, so it never saw this. The in-cluster Postgres and Compose run `initdb.sh` as the superuser, so they're unaffected.

## The fix

`logins.sql` grants the caller membership in `aintercept_worker` before handing it ownership: `GRANT aintercept_worker TO CURRENT_USER`. For a superuser it's harmless, and a re-run only emits a `NOTICE`. The chart's copy is updated too (the chart test holds them equal).

**`TestLoginsAsManagedAdmin`** reproduces the RDS case. A `CREATEDB CREATEROLE` login (not a superuser) creates the database with the built-in locale, as §5b2 says, runs `CreateLogins` twice, and checks that the worker owns the database and can apply the schema. **Without the grant it fails with the error above**; with it, it passes. Verified against a real RDS for PostgreSQL 17 as well.

## Docs

- §5b2 step 3 says why the grant is there.
- §7: the observer's role is scoped to `<prefix>/raw/*` and `schema-samples/*` (it said "the telemetry prefix").
- New **upgrade notes** for releases before the workers. These are the things that bit an upgrade from v0.4:
  - The observer writes `<prefix>/raw/` now. A role scoped to the old `dt=*` layout gets 403 on every write and records nothing, with traffic unaffected, so it fails silently. Widen it before upgrading.
  - The `process` role goes, the worker needs one, and the API reads `raw/` only.
  - Nothing is migrated: the UI starts empty at the upgrade, and old-layout data recorded meanwhile isn't shown. Keep `shaped/` readable for a rollback.
  - Order: the AWS side (database, logins, Secret) has to come first, and the old UI freezes on what it last loaded until the release replaces it.

## Checks

`make check` passes (Go 1.26, as CI pins): the Go packages, the API's 257 tests (95% coverage), and the UI's 1,018.

author: webcast-com
body:
Adds a way to answer "is the database wired?" at any time, without changing anything.

- `scripts/database-status.ts` (`npm run db:status`): reads the live site's `/api/health`, then connects read-only to the previous database and to the Supabase database, and reports whether each answers, how many accounts and posts each holds, whether the Supabase Data API is closed, and what is left to do. A missing or mistyped `SUPABASE_DATABASE_URL` is named (placeholder password, direct host instead of pooler, wrong user form, `sslmode`).
- `.github/workflows/database-status.yml`: runs it from Actions → "database-status" → "Run workflow"; the report is on the run's summary page. It also runs on a pull request that changes the check itself, which is how this pull request produces a first report.
- `scripts/copy-database.ts`: a string that is not a `postgres://` URL is no longer described by host and path, because its "path" could be the password.

Every query is a SELECT in a read-only transaction. No password is printed.

Tested against local databases: no secret set; tables missing; tables present but empty; tables open to `anon`; fully copied; five malformed or unreachable strings (none echoed a password).

author: cdeust
body:
Refs #118

Follow-up of review 1 of #346 (notes 1 to 3, "no action before merge"), in `consistent_control_names`.

## Root cause and change

1. **Sentence-start misses (note 1).** A definition's text joins its blocks (nested item, heading's next paragraph) with a line end, which `requirementDefinitions` makes indistinguishable from a hard wrap inside a paragraph; and `:` opens the statement after `AC-001:`. So a criterion wrapped before the name and one whose statement opens on the name are not reported. Telling them apart needs a change of the shared block reader used by three other rules, so this slice writes the two misses in the code comment and the CHANGELOG and pins them by a test, as the review asked.
2. **French RFC 2119 keywords (note 2).** `NOT_A_NAME` held only the English keywords; `Le bouton DOIT copier le code.` read a control named `DOIT`. The French forms (`DOIT`, `DOIVENT`, `DEVRAIT`, `DEVRAIENT`, `PEUT`, `PEUVENT`, `NE`, `OBLIGATOIRE`, `RECOMMANDÉ(E)`, `OPTIONNEL(LE)`, `FACULTATIF/VE`) are added. A test now covers a number word on its own (`The toolbar shows "Two" buttons.`).
3. **Wording (note 3).** The `withoutCodeSpans` comment and the #346 CHANGELOG entry no longer say the pairing is CommonMark's: it is within one paragraph, but a span can close across a paragraph or table-cell boundary, and a backslash before a backtick is not an escape.

## Tests (clean worktree of `49b052c`)

- `unit` (`pnpm build && pnpm test:coverage`): 156 files, 2289 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `regression`: 6 unittest groups, 124 tests OK; `pnpm test:perf` 3 files, 24 passed.
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0.
- The French-keyword test fails with the code of `main` (1 failed, 14 passed); the two pin tests pass on `main` by design.

## Not verified

The hosted Pipeline and the review. `npm install -g pnpm@10` of the ci.json commands was skipped (pnpm 10 already installed).

author: ma-do-ka
body:
## Build 72 (v1.1.17) — delivery diagnostics telemetry

Telemetry only: no delivery decision, gate order, guard condition, pacing value, or threshold changes. Behavioural identity verified by cross-review.

Motivation: two distinct delivery failures on Build 71 (2026-11-18) could not be fully adjudicated from existing logs:
- A follow-up take blocked by `prior_input_unverified` — the log could not separate which guard condition fired, and the reconcile attachment event was not recorded.
- A 342-char take rejected with `current_target_not_text_input` — the rejected element's role was not recorded, so a false negative could not be distinguished from a correct rejection.

### Changes
- Gate-rejection records now carry `role_bucket` (allowlisted at retention: the 15 denylist roles + 5 text-input roles, else `other`/`none`), raw AX read states for subrole / selected range / selected marker (`value`/`noValue`/`unsupported`/`timeout`/`error`/`skipped`), raw `editable_state` (the gate still consumes the folded value), and `denylist_hit`.
- `prior_input_unverified` records `start_blocked` and `fresh_matches_prior` as separate booleans plus `unverified_predecessor_count`.
- New `reconcile_attachment` record (short take ids, source events posted / receipt presence, candidate state, monotonic uptimes), registered as a buffer milestone so it survives eviction and appears in `input_summary v=2`.
- `captured_during` renders `unknown` when no receipt exists (diagnostics-only field; delivery logic uses a separate value).

### Verification
- Mac SelfTest: 301 cases / 52,152 assertions / 0 failures.
- Targeted XCTest suites (isolated copy): 54 tests pass; full suite runs in CI.
- Cross-review (different vendor): APPROVE, behavioural identity confirmed identical; two telemetry nits from review fixed and re-reviewed APPROVE.

The `swift test` full suite cannot run on the local Mac (CommandLineTools lacks the Testing module); CI is the full-suite gate, as with previous builds.

body:
**[디자이너 Luna]**

작성자: **[디자이너 Luna]**
Refs #311 (이슈는 #323이 닫아요. 이 PR은 #323 리뷰에서 나온 규격 보충이에요)

## 왜
#323에서 Theo가 짚은 문제예요. CSS 배율은 장치 픽셀 정수 배율 ÷ dpr이라서, 667×375 @2(iPhone SE급)에서는 **1.0**이 나와요. 이 배율에서 얼굴 이름표 셋이 5px씩 겹쳐서 `のばすドスンプピッ`가 띠 하나로 보여요. 같은 배율에서 게이지 이름표도 막대 첫 칸을 5.3 내부 px 덮어요. 6-4-2 표와 6-3-2에 실제로 나오지 않는 배율(2.667)이 적혀 있었고, 이 기기는 "지원 기준 아래"로 잘못 넘겨져 있었어요.

## 바뀐 것 (`docs/design/ui-interaction.md`)
- 6-4-2: 배율 표를 실제 기기 값(2 / 1.524 / 1.333 / 1.0)으로 고쳤어요. **CSS 배율 < 1.2이면 HUD 이름표 전부(얼굴 3개 + 게이지)에 `font-feature-settings: "palt"`와 `padding: 0`** 규칙을 넣었어요. 글자는 11px 그대로예요. #323 A안(10px)과 B안(숨김)은 실측 표와 함께 쓰지 않는 이유를 적었어요
- 위아래 padding도 0인 이유: 1.0배에서 `1px`면 이름표가 y 36–49가 되어 `HUD_AREA` 아래끝 48을 넘어요
- 6-3-2: 게이지 이름표 문단을 고쳤어요(1.0배는 지금 끝 x 89.3인데, 규칙을 적용하면 79.2)

## 실측 (667×375 @2, headless Chrome + Noto Sans CJK, #323 빌드에 CSS를 넣어서 측정)
| 안 | 틈 のばす–ドスン / ドスン–プピッ | 게이지 이름표 끝 (막대 84) |
|---|---|---|
| 지금 | −5 / −5 | 89.3 |
| 10px + palt (A) | 0.7 / 1.9 | 해당 없음 |
| **11px + palt + padding 0** | **2 / 3.3** | **79.2** |

## 구현 (Theo 후속 PR, L0 규모)
`placeHudTags`에서 `scale < 1.2`일 때 클래스(또는 inline style)를 붙이고 CSS 한두 줄을 넣어요. `HUD_AREA`는 바꾸지 않아요.

## 리스크
- iPhone Safari는 Hiragino 글꼴이라 `palt` 폭이 Noto와 달라요. 구현 뒤 Safari에서 틈을 한 번 더 봐야 해요
- 1.0배에서 글자가 바탕 끝에 붙어 조금 빡빡해 보여요. 1.2배 이상은 지금 그대로라 영향이 없어요

body:
## Scope

- Add an opt-in hand-aware known-development opponent suite to isolated Iron training: tight value, balanced range, loose station, bluff pressure, and the existing passive calling station.
- Freeze a 5,000-hand, 50-cell checkpoint31 safety plan with a reduced learning rate and distinct recorded seeds.
- Let the real-controller evaluator use the same suite for a separately seeded development comparison. Existing known and unknown evaluation suites retain their behavior.

Related: #400. Stacked on Draft #399; merge order matters.

## Evidence and outcome

- Focused Python tests 40/40 and action/range/training tests 29/29 pass. Known game bug regression 49/49; RL safety 66/66.
- Frozen source `4257425b` passed provenance and local seed collision checks. One isolated 5,000-hand run completed with 50/50 cells at 100 hands each, 5,000/5,000 zero-sum hands, and 82,300 legal decisions. This is safety and cause evidence only.
- Normal float32 ONNX export exceeded the existing score tolerance (2.2888e-5 > 2e-5) and was preserved as failed. A separate float64-core export passed 10,000 score samples and 630,000 legal-mask checks with zero action differences.
- Fresh, frozen known-development comparison: each arm 500 independent 20-hand sessions / 10,000 hands across 50 cells; both full trace audits passed. Candidate minus checkpoint31: all +6.678 [descriptive 95% +0.024,+13.565], cash +0.055 [-8.610,+8.796], MTT +13.300 [+2.785,+23.635] fixed-limit big bets/100 hands. Nineteen of 50 cells are negative, including 6/6 cash vs bluff_pressure at -54.250. **Checkpoint32 is not selected for continuation.**
- Same-observation six-seat diagnosis found effective <=2-card raises increasing from 41 to 97 among 227 legal call/raise decisions, while both models called all five initial-street 9-low-or-better completed hands with legal raises. Separate known-development same-hand replay of 90 selected 9-low-or-better opportunities favored aggressive action by +0.700 big bets/selected decision, but actual six-active coverage was only one state. This is local cause evidence, not independent policy EV.

[Full immutable evidence and limits](/Users/koki/Documents/Codex/MGX-RL-Artifacts/d03-iron-hand-aware-training-20261118/report.md)

## Boundaries

PR CI is still empty. No candidate enters the public model directory, registry, deployment, or Iron promotion. The range posterior in Draft #398 remains disconnected from live action EV. Rejected unknown-v1 holdout remains excluded. Company OS human adoption gate remains separate.

author: patrickdappollonio
body:
Agents often write a test to prove a removal took effect: it asserts a deleted function, flag, or file is gone. Removed code never changes, so that test can never fail again and guards nothing. The same goes for tests of the browser or standard library, tests of what the type system already guarantees, and tests that mock the code under test and then check the mock. This PR teaches the skills to spot these tests, building on a test-pruning skill a teammate wrote.

- **`code-simplification`** now treats these as a third kind of test that proves nothing, next to tests that work out their own answer and tests that check how instead of what. It also flags tests that copy another test. It reports each one with its fix, and when you ask it to clean up the tests, it deletes them along with any production code that only existed for them.
- **`adversarial-review`** (full, quick, and fast) now looks for these tests in its test review.
- **`implement-plan`** now tells its coding agents never to write a test that a removal worked. The proof of a removal is the remaining tests passing.

The copies of these rules inside `implement-plan` and `effective-go` are updated to match, and each changed plugin has its version bumped.

author: mcereal
body:
The "now" items of [decisions/signed-firmware-updates.md](https://github.com/ternmesh/spec/blob/main/decisions/signed-firmware-updates.md) and [decisions/keys-at-rest.md](https://github.com/ternmesh/spec/blob/main/decisions/keys-at-rest.md) (#58), in the specification. Companion protocol → **version 13**.

Firmware: ternmesh/firmware#117

> **Version clash:** #60 (blinded announces) also takes companion version 13. Whichever merges second becomes 14; the renumbering is mechanical (the version sentence, `VERSION` in the generator, the `older` connection and `unknown_to_older` entry), and I can do it on request.

## The problem

A node runs any image anyone who can drive it gives it, and a node without a screen pairs with `123456`, which everyone knows. So anyone in Bluetooth range could pair with such a node and install their own firmware: every key, every group, every message (memo, threat 1(a)). An nRF52840 node also takes any image while its bootloader waits (1(b), 1(c)). The specification said nothing about who made an image, and "Signed firmware" sat under *Not yet specified*.

## What changes

**Signed images** (companion.md, new section).
* A **release key** is the publisher's Ed25519 public key. An image's **signature** is Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure) over the 48 bytes `"TERN-FIRMWARE-V1" || SHA-256(image)`, the image exactly as published. It verifies only if it is 64 bytes, `S` < L, and one of the verifier's keys accepts it.
* Publishers SHOULD put it beside the image as `<name>.sig` (the 64 bytes alone).
* `UPDATE_BEGIN` gains `signature` (`bytes` up to 64; empty = none). A node updated over this protocol refuses an `UPDATE_BEGIN` whose signature does not verify over `digest` with `ERROR` 11, after the size checks, on every `UPDATE_BEGIN` (resumed ones too), leaving any update under way as it was. A node MAY be set to take unsigned images for development, but nothing over Bluetooth or this protocol may set it. A node holds a short list of keys so a key can be rotated.
* Clients SHOULD hold the same keys and check before sending either way, and MUST NOT send an image that does not verify unless the user asks after a warning.
* A client of version 12 sends no signature, so a checking node refuses every image from it: older apps must be updated to update newer ESP32 nodes.

**The bootloader window, said plainly.** "While the bootloader waits, anyone in range can install an image": it holds no bonds and checks no signature. The SHOULD that a bootloader wait over Bluetooth after a break is dropped (memo option I); a bootloader that falls back to the old firmware is named as the one that closes the window sooner, and clients SHOULD check the package, send it at once, and warn the user. Nothing here replaces a bootloader.

**Being at the node** (Bluetooth LE). A passkey that is not shown (the default `123456`, or one set with `SET` 4) is taken only in the **pairing window**: `PAIR_WINDOW` (180 s) after a start by hand (power on, reset, woken from off by the button) or a press of the button. A set passkey is held to the window only once the node has a bond. A passkey shown on the screen needs no window. Restarts the node makes itself (a setting, an update, `WIPE`, a fault) open nothing, so nothing done over the air or by a client opens it.

**`WIPE`** (`0x37`). The node answers `OK` (or `ERROR` 8), then erases its identity, sessions, contacts, groups, messages, cards, positions, settings and Bluetooth bonds, and restarts with a new address. It may keep its airtime, which is no secret. It SHOULD erase the storage, not just mark records unused. Clients must ask the user first, and on `OK` forget the bond.

**What holding a node gives** (What the node holds). Nothing here protects a node's keys from whoever holds it; a lost node has given up its address, sessions and groups. first-contact.md's *Not yet specified* gains **revoking an identity**.

## Why this shape

* **Over the digest, checked at `UPDATE_BEGIN`.** The digest is already in `UPDATE_BEGIN`, so a node refuses in a second rather than after four minutes, and needs no second pass. `UPDATE_END` still checks the bytes against the digest, so nothing is lost. The prefix separates this from anything else the key might sign and names the format.
* **`bytes`, not a fixed 64.** "No signature" is then explicit, which a developer's node reads.
* **A list of keys.** One compiled-in key could never be replaced without the old key.
* **Not the bootloader.** The image never passes through the nRF52 application (memo option C, rejected). Saying so is better than implying otherwise.
* **Window, not per-device passkeys.** Tern does not make boards and cannot print labels; a power cycle or a button press is something every board has.
* **No confirm field in `WIPE`.** Frames are typed and CRC'd; clients are held to asking the user. Anyone who can send it could already read everything it erases.

Alternatives considered are the memo's (D, E, H: bootloader replacement, Secure Boot, bonded-only bootloader), all deferred or rejected there.

## Vectors (`vectors/companion.json`)

* `release_key`, `release_seed`: a **published test key** (seed = SHA-256 of a label), never for use.
* `signatures`: message and verdict for the image's own signature, another image's, the right signature given with another digest, another key's, `S` past the group order, one byte short, and none.
* `update` now signs its `UPDATE_BEGIN`; `refusals` adds unsigned, wrong-key, short, non-canonical and wrong-digest `UPDATE_BEGIN`s (all `ERROR` 11), and shows a refused one leaving an update under way intact.
* `older` adds a version-12 client: its unsigned `UPDATE_BEGIN` gets `ERROR` 11, and `WIPE` gets `ERROR` 1. `unknown_to_older` adds `WIPE` at 12.
* `wipe`: `WIPE` answered `OK`.
* `vectors/tools/companion.py` now needs `cryptography` (CI already installs it) and checks Ed25519 against RFC 8032 TEST 1 and the library's refusal of `S` ≥ L before computing anything. Every generator's `check` passes.

## What clients must change (version 13)

1. Say `HELLO` 13.
2. Hold the release keys; verify `.sig` before sending an image either way; refuse unsigned ones unless the user insists.
3. `UPDATE_BEGIN` to a node of 13+: `size`, `digest`, then a length byte (64) and the signature.
4. Read `ERROR` 11 at `UPDATE_BEGIN` as "not signed by a key this node holds".
5. Before `UPDATE_BOOTLOADER`: check the `.zip`'s signature, send at once, warn that anyone in range can install an image until it finishes.
6. Offer `WIPE` behind a warning; on `OK` forget the bond and everything held for the node.
7. When pairing fails: tell the user to press the button, or power-cycle / reset, and pair within three minutes.

The release files and `latest.json`'s `signature` field are defined in the firmware's `docs/signing.md` (publication is the publisher's business, as this section says).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01VUf1Kmet2nagtETDEfzKfk

author: pown3d
body:
## What and why

On an iPad held in landscape the bottom bar of the iPhone is replaced by the permanent sidebar of the `iPad · paysage` mockup (approach C, `docs/ios.md` §3 and §3.1).

- **Which navigation** is decided by the window, not the device (`NavigationLayout.choose`, in `LuciumKit`): sidebar only when the window is regular in width and in height, wider than tall, at least 700 pt wide and not set in the accessibility text sizes. Everything else keeps the bottom bar: iPad upright, Split View, Slide Over, a small Stage Manager window, an iPhone sideways (even a Max, whose width is regular but which is short).
- **The sidebar** (320 pt, on the colours of the space): back / forward / reload, favourites, the space and its profile (a menu), pinned tabs with folders that open in place (`SidebarOutline`), Today with "Archive all", the archive, downloads, a menu for privacy / lock / licenses, and the space buttons. The page sits on a card beside it, under a toolbar with the address and the page actions (share, save as PDF, downloads). It can be hidden.
- **The lock**: everything the sidebar lists is read through the model's lock-aware readers (`SidebarContent`), so a locked space has no row in it (no favourite, pinned tab, folder, Today tab or archived page); it says why and offers to unlock.
- Tab gestures, favourite tiles, the tab title and the address label are extracted from the tabs sheet and the bottom bar so both navigations share them. New icons `icon-sidebar` and `icon-download`, six FR/EN texts.
- A picture of the result is in `docs/images/ios-ipad-paysage-fr.png` (iPad Air 11-inch, 1180 × 820 pt).

## How it was checked

- `swift test` in `ios/LuciumKit`: 244 tests pass (12 new: the layout rule and the outline).
- XCTest on an iPad Air 11-inch simulator (iOS 26.5) and on iPhone 17 Pro (the CI's default): `SidebarTests` (7) and `ScreenshotTests` (5) pass. The tests read the colour of a strip of the screen to know which navigation was drawn and `SidebarContent` for what it lists (the accessibility tree is not published in a process nobody listens to; tried, empty).
- `pnpm lint`; `ios-contract`, `ios-privacy-manifest`, `ios-file-names-contract`, `public-tree` tests pass.
- **Mutations, each applied then removed, the named test fails** (table in `docs/ios.md` §11):
  - layout rule: regular width, regular height, `>` vs `>=`, 700 pt, large text, loop guard and depth guard of the outline (`NavigationLayoutTests`, `SidebarOutlineTests`);
  - the sidebar reading `state` instead of the model: `testALockedSpaceListsNothingOfItselfInTheSidebar` fails (the three lists come out full);
  - large text ignored on screen, `if sidebarShown` replaced by `if true`, the bottom bar always chosen: `testTheScreenHasTheSidebarOnAnIPadInLandscapeAndTheBarEverywhereElse`, `testHidingTheSidebarGivesThePageTheWholeWidth`, `testTheSidebarInTheDarkSchemeAndWithLargeText`.
- Not run: the full `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:engine` (opens windows), a real iPad. Not proved by the tests: real rotation (does the web view survive the switch between the two navigations without a reload?), real Split View / Stage Manager windows, hardware keyboard, drag and drop, VoiceOver order. Taps, swipes and long presses are not played (the sidebar's rows are the same gestures as the sheet's, `tabActions`).

## Checklist

- [x] Typecheck / lint / the tests touched pass locally; the iOS job runs the rest.
- [x] Every new guard has a test, and I saw it fail without the guard (see above).
- [x] Pure logic is in `LuciumKit`; no Electron code touched.
- [x] UI change: it follows the mockup `iPad · paysage`; the additions and the differences (no "Retouches" / "Vue scindée" / "Historique", the actions menu in place of a share button, a "Pinned" header with a new-folder button, a close button on Today tabs, no "+" in the footer) are listed in `docs/ios.md` §3.1.
- [x] Every new text is in both catalogues (`Localizable.xcstrings`); no colour written in the Swift sources; icons are the project's (no SF Symbols).
- [x] No code, image, font, icon, sound or data file from another browser or product.
- [x] No AI assistant, account, sync, telemetry or new connection.
- [x] No new dependency.
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/ios.md`, `ios/README.md`).
- [x] Every commit carries a `Signed-off-by` line.

## Notes for the reviewer

- Merged on top of #58 (downloads, share, PDF): the sidebar reuses its `PageActionsMenu` and `DownloadStrip` and adds an icon-only downloads button in the footer.
- The `+` button of the mockup's footer is left out (no room for it at 44 pt next to archive, downloads, "More" and three spaces); "Spaces and profiles" is in the space menu at the top.

body:
## Summary

This is T4 of the test-slimming plan, covering the `compositor.rs` and `shm.rs` tests. Production code is unchanged.

| File | Lines |
| --- | --- |
| `handler/compositor.rs` | −469 |
| `handler/shm.rs` | −332 |
| `test_support.rs` | +71 (shared buffer fixtures) |
| `proxy/harness.rs` | +45 (`Session::shm_pool`, `Session::shm_buffer`, `pub(crate)`) |
| `state/render.rs` | +11 |
| **Net** | **−639** (after review) |

Test counts: compositor 100 → 92, shm 48 → 42.

- **SHM and native buffer twins merged.** Seven SHM/native test pairs are now one test each, looping over `BufferKind`. Each merged test asserts everything both halves checked.
- **Typed comparisons.** Byte and opcode parsing is replaced by typed requests and events compared whole. The `set_app_id` tests pin the full namespaced ID literally, and the damage tests assert exact rectangles.
- **SHM table tests.** The validation, copy and lifecycle tests are tables. The lifecycle tables cover each buffer kind both with and without a surface showing the buffer.
- **Protocol errors through `Session`.** The SHM protocol-error tests now run end to end and also assert the error's object.
- **`render.rs` property test fixed.** It now checks that every copied pixel lies within 2 pixels of a damaged one. Before, making `to_buffer` copy the whole buffer under a viewport source passed the entire suite.

## Commits

1. ♻️ Merge the SHM and native buffer lifecycle twins.
2. ♻️ Decode the compositor tests' queued messages.
3. ♻️ Move the test buffer fixtures to `test_support`.
4. ♻️ Table the SHM validation, copy and lifecycle tests.
5. ✅ Drive the SHM protocol-error tests through `Session`.
6. ✅ Make the `render.rs` property test check copied pixels against the damage.

## Review

A Claude reviewer and deepseek both found no coverage loss. Both confirmed that each merged twin asserts the union of its halves, and that the stale SHM fixture hides no precondition. The review also fixed two tests that could not fail:
- **The render property bound** now allows a copied pixel at most one pixel past one that touches the damage, with closed edges. Growing an edge by two used to pass all 20,000 cases.
- **`native_buffer_damage_uses_recorded_dimensions`** now sets a buffer transform, so the recorded size reaches the result. Before, reporting native buffers as 1x1 passed it.

Negative queue checks became whole-queue comparisons. Fixture helpers name their sender in failure messages, and the ARC app ID is asserted literally.

## Coverage map

### Fixture notes

- `test_support::register_test_buffer(ctx, kind, guest, host)` pairs a 1x1
  buffer and registers it as SHM (a mapped host copy, `StalePixels::all()`)
  or native. Old SHM lifecycle tests mostly registered their buffer
  `in_sync_on(TEST_SURFACE)`; `delayed_shm_release_…` used `all()`. The
  fixture uses `all()`, as a new buffer has. That changes only whether a
  commit of the buffer copies pixels. The copy succeeds (a zero pool into a
  private mapping), so no lifecycle outcome depends on it. Only
  `a_delayed_release_…`, `a_detached_use_…` and `destroyed_pending_shm_attach_…`
  commit such a buffer, and the first two now also commit it with a copy.
- The compositor's `setup_ctx` now also enters its host `zaura_shell` in
  the object table, as a real bind does, so typed decoding can name its
  interface.
- `host_requests(ctx)` decodes the queued host requests by their senders'
  interfaces and compares them whole. A request from an object whose
  dispatch metadata is gone (a released Aura surface) is compared by
  `queued_headers`.

### Removed or merged tests

Every mutation was applied to production code at the base, where the old
test(s) failed, and to this branch, where the full `cargo test -p
sommelier` failed in the listed new tests (only the covering ones are
named; most mutations also fail other tests).

| Removed test | Covered by | Proving mutation | Old suite | New suite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `damage_only_commit_preserves_released_local_use` | `damage_only_commit_preserves_a_released_use`, Shm row | M4 | fails | fails |
| `damage_only_commit_does_not_resubmit_released_current_buffer` | same, Shm row (`Released` excludes `AwaitingRelease`) | M4 | fails | fails |
| `damage_only_commit_preserves_released_native_use` | same, Native row | M4 | fails | fails |
| `attaching_idle_shm_buffer_without_commit_keeps_release_edge` | `attaching_an_idle_buffer_without_commit_keeps_its_release_edge`, Shm | M2, M3 | fails | fails |
| `attaching_idle_native_buffer_without_commit_keeps_release_edge` | same, Native | M2, M3 | fails | fails |
| `delayed_shm_release_before_pending_commit_keeps_host_buffer_alive` | `a_delayed_release_before_a_pending_commit_keeps_the_host_buffer_alive`, Shm (now also checks `buffer_is_released` after the first release, as the native twin did) | M1 | fails | fails |
| `delayed_native_release_before_pending_commit_keeps_host_buffer_alive` | same, Native | M1 | fails | fails |
| `replacing_pending_destroyed_native_buffer_does_not_wait_for_release` | `replacing_a_pending_destroyed_buffer_does_not_wait_for_release`, Native | M3 | fails | fails |
| `replacing_pending_destroyed_shm_buffer_does_not_wait_for_release` | same, Shm | M3 | fails | fails |

| `pool_resize_accepts_the_same_size_and_rejects_shrinking_as_invalid_fd` | same, rows 4096→4096 and 4096→2048 | M8, M8b | fails | fails |
| `rejects_buffer_size_overflow` | `validates_buffer_layout_against_pool_bounds` | M11 | fails | fails |
| `validates_nv12_two_plane_pool_layout` | `validates_buffer_layout_against_pool_bounds` | M10, M10b | fails | fails |
| `gbm_stride_must_cover_the_guest_row` | `validates_shm_format_stride` (gains the RGB565 stride-19 row) | M12 | fails | fails |
| `destroyed_attached_shm_buffer_stays_mapped_until_host_release` | `destroying_a_submitted_buffer_defers_its_host_destroy_until_release`, row (Shm, shown) | M13, M15 | fails | fails |
| `destroying_submitted_non_shm_buffer_defers_until_release` | same, row (Native, not shown) | M13 | fails | fails |

| `native_release_before_guest_destroy_is_recorded` | same, row (Native, shown) | M14 | fails | fails |

The two shm lifecycle tables run every kind with and without a surface
showing the buffer, so they cover both old preconditions and two new ones.

### Mutations

| ID | Where | Change |

author: benmerckx
body:
Reach made every function with a C symbol a root, including every `@:hxmc.callback` (its `hxmc_cb_<name>` symbol, on the function or on its `__callback` wrapper). So a module's callbacks kept it alive, along with everything they call, even when nothing else of it ran. In a helder iOS app, `AppleWebView.startTask` was a root while `AppleWebView.new` was not live: a web view's callbacks, a loopback `WebServer` and socket code got linked into an app that makes no web view.

## What changed
- `FuncInfo.callback` (Ir.hx) marks a callback's entry. Lower sets it on all four kinds: the struct wrapper, the plain wrapper, the span-kernel wrapper, and the function itself for `@:hxmc.unsafe`/no-GC callbacks and on wasm.
- Reach no longer roots these. It marks one live where live code has `ECallHost("hxmc_unsafe_Mem_sym", [EStr(sym)])` of its symbol. Both ways of taking a callback's address lower to exactly that: `Callback.addr` (FnLower ~3687) and a typed binding's callback parameter (`callbackAddr`, ~4497). So does an explicit `Mem.sym("hxmc_cb_…")`. A wrapper's call of the function keeps the function live as before.
- `@:hxmc.export` and the other fixed-symbol entries (Objective-C register functions, method entries and dealloc, COM vtable descriptors and thunks, JNI natives, block invokes) stay roots: the runtime or data tables reach some of them by name.
- `-D hxmc.stats` now prints `n of m callbacks` on Reach's line.
- Docs: hxmc.md "Reachability", interop.md "Callbacks".

Checked for other references: no C, JS or script source in the repo names an `hxmc_cb_` symbol (`git grep hxmc_cb_` finds only `Lower.callbackSym`). Every std callback (Gc, Threads, Faults, Ssl, Jni/ObjC/ComKind, Pgo, ThreadApi, Foreign, Start) is reached through `Callback.addr` in Haxe code. A dead callback is never emitted, and no emitted code references it. The corpus links on every lane that ran, with no undefined `hxmc_cb_` symbol.

## Test
`CallbackLive` (new corpus case). `Viewer`, a subclass that is never made (only `Std.isOfType` names it), takes its callbacks' addresses in an override. `// not-live: Viewer.open Viewer.started Viewer.idle Server.new Server.serve` covers a wrapper callback, an `@:hxmc.unsafe` callback, and the class only they use. With main's tool the case fails (`Viewer.started <- (a root)`, and Server through it). Live callbacks (`twice`, allocating, through its wrapper; `add`, unsafe) are called back through `@:hxmc.indirect` C function pointers. Passes natively and on wasm32-wasi.

## Measurements (macos-arm64)
| | main | this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bin/hxmc/hxmc` | 25,545,232 B | 25,545,232 B (`__text` +1,664 B: the new code) |
| CallbackLive | 512 functions, `__text` 152,164 | 507 functions, `__text` 151,620 |
| ForeignKinds | 714 functions | 713 functions |
| Hello, ThreadNatives | 509 / 677 functions | unchanged |

No callback became dead in the tool itself, because the tool is a Mir host (it has macros): `Driver.run` skips Reach there and keeps every function. The std's callbacks are mostly in modules that load only when used, and there their addresses are taken, so ordinary programs barely change. The gain is in programs like helder's, where a class Haxe keeps (but never makes) holds callbacks. I couldn't measure Everbloom from this branch: helder's sources don't build against main's std (kernel errors in `hxmc.simd.Ref`, with main's tool too).

## Tests run (this Mac)
- `make quick`: x64 440/440, x64 RT_VERIFY verify-tags 440/440, wasm node 358/358, wasm compacting RT_VERIFY 358/358. `units` fails ("module cache store, frontend seam"), as it does on main on this machine.
- `make check`: stopped at 2 h before the later lanes. Passed: native macho (MachOCheck all passed) and Mac Catalyst 441/441. Failing with main's tool as well: x64 16K 439/440 (`ObjCWeak`'s retainCount line, a GC-timing count). Failing because of this machine: iOS simulator 432/434 (`Ffi`, `CVars`: dyld loaded the macOS dylibs the x64 lane left in `bin/hxmc-t`). Can't run here: arm64 (no qemu), windows (no wine), x64 glibc, readelf, shared, jni (no glibc toolchain). Not reached: ThreadNatives x30, the compact lanes, debug info, UIKitCheck. A separate `make native-check NATIVE=uikit` hung on the simulator past 40 min and was stopped.
- `make fixpoint`: byte-identical (module cache cold, warm, off).
- `make crosshost`: 2476/2476 identical.

body:
## Why this exists

PR #200 merged at `9c22027` and includes builder commit `617e211` (sandbox jail and owner-only rules in the repo). It does **not** include `627c79b`, which was pushed after that merge.

`627c79b` is not an ancestor of `origin/main` (`334575f`). Current main still loads the plain textarea builder and `terminal-builder.css?v=20261117-builder-2`.

This branch is `origin/main` plus one cherry-pick, now `55051b6`. It does not rewrite history and it does not touch `backend/rules/firestore.rules`, `assets/js/terminal/app.js`, or `assets/js/terminal/pages.js`.

## What was missing

- Dark builder surfaces that beat `funded-system.css` `!important` input styles, scoped to `#fx-page-body .fxb` so the command bar, desks, and other inputs stay as they are.
- CodeMirror 5.65.16 vendored in `assets/vendor/codemirror` (MIT). No runtime CDN. Textarea fallback if the editor script is absent.
- Line numbers, JavaScript highlighting, indent, find/replace, undo/redo, and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, S, F, and H.
- Run shows syntax errors, runtime errors, and a missing-snapshot message. It does not invent prices.
- If the account refuses a save, the project stays in this browser under `fx-term-builder-v1:` plus the signed-in user id. The page says that copy will not follow to another device. It does not call that an account save.
- Add to my terminal says it was added on this browser only when the account write fails.
- Layout: projects on the left, editor and console in the center, preview on the right, assistant along the bottom, with a resize handle.

The sandbox jail from `617e211` is unchanged.

## Tests on this branch

- `scripts/test-terminal-builder.cjs`: passed
- `scripts/test-terminal-builder-sandbox.cjs`: passed in Chromium
- `scripts/test-terminal-builder-ui.cjs`: passed in Chromium, including light-theme field colors, run/stop, missing prices, browser-only save, reload, install wording, a second account, and an accepted mock account save
- Firestore rules file is byte-for-byte the same as `origin/main`. Emulator coverage from the merged rules was not re-run because this commit does not change them.
- Safari and Firefox were not run. No WebKit or Firefox browser is installed in this environment.

## Live Firestore rules

author: kblok
body:
Closes #1740

## What
Adds the JUnit XML report (`JunitReport.RenderJunitReport`, `JunitReportOptions`) and the `JunitReporter` that writes `junit.xml` beside `report.json`. A carriage return in a failure message or body is kept as ``, so a CI parser reads it back (upstream tester-army/e2e `aadf955`, #1860).

## Value
CI systems (GitLab, GitHub test summaries) get a JUnit file from the run itself, with failure screenshots linked as `[[ATTACHMENT|path]]`, and no longer need a separate logger package.

## Upstream parity
Verdict: **complete, with justified exceptions** (below).

| Upstream | Port |
|---|---|
| `report/junit.ts` `renderJunitReport`, `JunitReportOptions` | `Report/JunitReport.cs` `JunitReport.RenderJunitReport`, `JunitReportOptions` |
| `junitReporter`, `attachmentBase`, `fileReporter` | `JunitReporter`, `JunitReporter.AttachmentBase` |
| `failureScreenshot` (`failure-text.ts`) | `FailureText.FailureScreenshot` |
| `sanitizeRecordedText` in errors | already ported (#1717) |
| docs `reporters.mdx` | `COMPATIBILITY.md`, `running.md`, gitlab and vercel-previews guides, API reference regenerated |

Port-only: `JunitReporter` is a class deriving from `Reporter` (the port has no `fileReporter` factory); `JunitKit` test helpers; `CaseOutcome` (an enum where upstream's `RenderedCase.outcome` is a string union); `PosixJoin` (Node's `path.posix.join` has no .NET equivalent); `JunitReport.XmlForbidden` is upstream's `XML_FORBIDDEN` as a static `Regex`.

## Upstream tests and local match
`tests/E2E.Tests/ReportJunit/`: `RenderJunitReportTests` (describe `renderJunitReport`, includes the one named in the issue: `Keeps_a_carriage_return_in_the_failure_message_and_body_as_a_character_reference`) and `JunitReporterTests` (describe `junitReporter`). All pass (40).

## Not ported (issue #1762)
Five `it` that need serial groups or the `test.fail` expected-failure record, which the port's report lacks: the two `times/reads a serial member…`, `links … failed serial member`, `keeps the expected note between…`, `links … test.fail pass…`. Also `expectedNote` and the serial read in `renderResult`. The other #1860 tests are #1742 (cli-step) and already-ported `sanitizeRecordedText` ones.

## Checks
`dotnet csharpier check .` clean. `ASecretInAnEngineOptionTests` fails here only because Chromium cannot be installed in this sandbox. This change does not touch the agent, so the real-model tests were not run.

author: mazzucci
body:
The menu's first page gets og.png's battle under it: a band across the foot of the screen, the Castle and its Watchtower on the left, four Archers at the front with their bows drawn and raised at three large Drones hovering over the clash, Knights and a Guard behind them, Androids in the first rank, the Buggies and the Launcher a step into the field, the Veteran (the Bruiser) at the blast, and the Data center and its Wind turbine standing clean on the right. No gold crystals (the mines replaced them). The band's top fades into the page's own floor, so the premise line and the buttons sit on the plain floor as before; the image is a thing of the shore (under the page, `z-index:-1`), so it can push nothing.

**One scene for both pictures.** `tools/scene.mjs` holds the battle (`[frame, x, y, seat, scale]` in fractions of a 4:1 band, plus a 21:9, a short-landscape and an upright variant); `tools/og.mjs` and the new `tools/menu-art.mjs` both read it, so the card and the page cannot drift apart. og.png is regenerated from it in this PR (1200x630, 204 KB, under the 300 KB budget, text unchanged).

**The images** (`public/menu/`, committed like og.png; Chromium's own WebP encoder, no new dependency): one is loaded per device, picked by the `<picture>`'s sources (upright, then `max-height: 420px`, then `min-aspect-ratio: 2/1`, else the desktop's), `fetchpriority="low"`, `decoding="async"`; the shore's gradient floor is the fallback while it loads and if it never does.

| class | image | shown at | bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| desktop | 1920x480 | 1440x900, 1280x720, 1920x1080 | 93.7 KB |
| wide (21:9 and wider) | 2560x480 | 2560x1080 | 99.5 KB |
| landscape phone (height ≤ 420) | 1688x268 | 844x390 at 2x (3x upsamples 1.5x) | 55.0 KB |
| upright phone | 780x398 | 390x844 at 2x | 28.8 KB |

**How it is drawn.** `tools/menu-art.mjs` renders the ~50 sprites the scenes use from the game's 3D models through `tools/render3d` at twice the atlas's scale (a new `zoom` option in `render3d`'s `window.render`, three lines; `generate.mjs` passes none), lays the atlas's ground tiles and effects, tints each unit's team mask with its seat's tint as the client does, bakes the night veil, the top fade and a clearing at the top middle (the footer line's room on short screens), and writes WebP from the canvas. Output committed; `MENU_ART_SPRITES=dir` keeps the renders between runs.

**The page.** `index.html`: a `<picture class="scene">` as the first child of `#menuHome .shore`. `src/style.css`: the band is the bottom 40% of the screen (36% under `max-height: 420px`, 26% upright), `object-fit: cover` anchored at the bottom, drifting with the tide's `ebb` keyframes at 37 s (one composited transform; none under `prefers-reduced-motion`). Over it only the lowest tide line stays, moved to the band's foot (`bottom:-26px`; `-60px` on 21:9 where its SVG is scaled wider; the short phone's and the upright one's are already at the foot); the two upper lines and the bank's stones go. **Under 360 px of height there is no band** (568x320: it would sit under the buttons): the shore is as it was.

**Legibility** (WCAG contrast of the text's color against what sits behind it in a screenshot with the text hidden: the mean / the brightest 5% of pixels in the text's box, i.e. the worst letter). The buttons are opaque and unchanged. PLAY (SINGLE PLAYER) is at the same pixel as before on every size and nothing scrolls.

| size | PLAY's bottom | premise | How to play · About | build stamp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1440x900 | 481 / 900 (as before) | 5.4 / 5.4 | 5.5 / 5.5 | 5.5 / 5.4 |
| 1280x720 | 391 / 720 (as before) | 5.4 / 5.3 | 5.3 / 5.2 | 5.0 / 4.9 |
| 2560x1080 | 571 / 1080 | 5.4 / 5.4 | 5.5 / 5.4 | 5.4 / 5.4 |
| 844x390 @3x | 216 / 390 (as before) | 5.4 / 5.3 | 5.3 / 4.9 | 5.3 / 5.1 |
| 667x375 @2x | 208 / 375 | 5.4 / 5.3 | 5.2 / 4.7 | 5.3 / 5.0 |
| 390x844 @3x | 418 / 844 (as before) | 5.4 / 5.3 | 5.6 / 5.5 | 5.6 / 5.6 |
| 568x320 @2x (no band) | 178 / 320 | 5.4 / 5.3 | 5.7 / 5.6 | 5.7 / 5.6 |

Before this PR the same texts read 5.4–5.6 on the plain floor. Every mean and every worst point is at or above 4.7; the 1280x720 stamp's worst point is 4.87 (the desktop band's fade is 66% of its height, with the clearing).

**e2e** (`test/e2e/field.e2e.mjs`, 7 scenarios): the right image per size class (1440x900, 1280x720, 2560x1080, 844x390, 390x844), the band under the premise line, only the lowest tide line left, PLAY at the same rectangle with the band removed and with the image blocked (the shore's floor shows), the drift stopped under reduced motion, no band and the shore as it was at 568x320. The first page's existing test (gameplay.e2e.mjs) now expects two things drifting when the band shows (the band and the lowest line), the three lines only under 360 px of height.

**Crops** (the four menu sizes, 2560x1080, 667x375, 568x320, og.png and og before/after) are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-mazzucci-projects-ebbfall/404927fd-039e-5d7a-93a0-98eec60b5b04/landing-design/final/crops/` on the build machine.

**Every sprite in the scene is today's.** The sprites are rendered from the models on this branch (origin/main, 02055cc), not taken from og.png's era. Since og.png was last drawn (7c43712, #259), these commits changed models the scene draws: #319 and #306 the Bruiser (team color trimmed, dark leather, the hammer tipped back); #304 the Rider's bolder spear, strike-pose effects on the Knight, Guard, Rider, Bruiser (expedition-units.js, kingdom-units.js, kingdom.js, models.js); #294 melee strike poses (the same files; new frames, not the walk frames used here); #291 and #288 the Wind turbine (three solid blades) and the Substation; #280 the Drone's body and the Bot; #279 the Uplink's one dish (not in the scene); #277 the art polish over every model (distinct silhouettes, lighter values, trim-only team color: Castle, Watchtower, Knight, Guard, Archer, Rider, Balloon, Data center, Buggy, Android, Drone, Launcher, Veteran, the countryside's marks); #267 the Rover as the long rocket Launcher; #317 the Expedition's sites (not in the scene). The atlas in `public/art` is already regenerated from these (it is what the game draws), and og.png now draws from it too.

body:
## R168｜真正定位黑板擦魔法首发卡顿：原R147 Chrome CPU Profiler 证明WebGL驱动同步（**QA研究 / NO-GO**）

### 基线为**完全未修改的R147原Web游戏**
Z890 RTX5070Ti Chrome157 Vulkan、CPU×2限速、真实16/16人物和60卡，下载75,569,762字节原始GLB/VRM，全程没有低精替身/减贴图/删魔法。
- 真实 E06 黑板擦**首发最大longtask 346ms、帧p99 233.3ms**；二次施放longtask 0、p99约33.4ms。
- 首发Chrome CPU Profiler归因 `getProgramInfoLog`≈500.9ms**累计采样时间**（不是一次函数实际耗时）、`shaderSource`、`getShaderInfoLog`等；再次施放这些峰值消失。与 R166 动态光源引发Shader排列变化相吻合。
- Three.js首次Shader使用期的驱动诊断与链接状态同步是关键贡献因素，但单次Profiler样本并不能提供所有GPU侧因果。

### 三条捷径实际反例（从未默认应用）
| 做法 | 额外准备 | 首发最大longtask | 首发p99 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 原R147 | 0 | 346ms | 233ms |
| QA跳过Three.js开发期Shader日志检查 | 0 | 308ms | 217ms |
| QA提前`renderer.compile`真实E06+2点光源 | 62.8ms | 323ms | 233ms |
| QA真正4×4离屏画一次原始E06 | **792.7ms** | **388ms** | 217ms |

- **日志关闭不是性能解决方案**：阻塞转移至`getProgramParameter`（≈497.8ms累计采样），首发仍卡。事后主动检查170个已编译Shader的`LINK_STATUS`均成功。
- `compile`只预热部分变体，前置62.8ms仍卡；原始离屏渲染增加近0.8秒等待但仍卡，强制拒绝。
- 改造版分别手动验证170/184/208个程序链接成功；不以失效Shader、降低画质换帧率。
- CPU Profiler自带测量扰动，各变体单次受控样本；不能宣传几十毫秒的数值差异为显著提升。

### 全部源码及实证
- [中文技术报告](https://github.com/star8592/AfterSchoolDuelClub-Playtest/blob/research/duel-web-r168-first-spell-cpu-trace-20261118/r45-duel/docs/R168_FIRST_MAGIC_DRIVER_SYNC_CPU_PROFILE.md)
- [4组8次机读验证](https://github.com/star8592/AfterSchoolDuelClub-Playtest/blob/research/duel-web-r168-first-spell-cpu-trace-20261118/r45-duel/qa/evidence/r168-cpu-profile/r168-final-summary.json)
- [原始R147首发DevTools CPU Profile](https://github.com/star8592/AfterSchoolDuelClub-Playtest/blob/research/duel-web-r168-first-spell-cpu-trace-20261118/r45-duel/qa/evidence/r168-cpu-profile/original-unmodified-first.cpuprofile)
- [关闭诊断首发DevTools CPU Profile](https://github.com/star8592/AfterSchoolDuelClub-Playtest/blob/research/duel-web-r168-first-spell-cpu-trace-20261118/r45-duel/qa/evidence/r168-cpu-profile/skip-shader-log-first.cpuprofile)
- [真实离屏预热首发 CPU Profile](https://github.com/star8592/AfterSchoolDuelClub-Playtest/blob/research/duel-web-r168-first-spell-cpu-trace-20261118/r45-duel/qa/evidence/r168-cpu-profile/render-hidden-spell-first.cpuprofile)
- 可重跑QA脚本`browser-r168-first-spell-cpu-profile.mjs`和只在QA中支持的三种测试开关。

### 发布
**Draft / NO-GO / 不合并、不部署**。正式R147仍默认检查Shader错误。与R164大屏、R165魔法多样化、R167常驻灯光槽位的未验收性能改动完全隔离。下一步应对WebGLProgram的真实材质Shader键和动态光源组合做减少变体的最小化设计、真实手机A/B，不删除任何特效或角色动作。

Documentation only: no code, no changeset.

## Parts 4c and 4d of RFC 0003 are not scheduled

The README listed the plain view of one graph (4c) under 0.13 and groups in the layout (4d) under 0.14. Both were written for Semlia's ontology map. Semlia has drawn that map itself since its ADR 0012 (G6, its own colours by business domain, its own grouping); only its change view is kgdiff's. The second host, kgstrata, draws in 3D with its own renderer and asked for partitions in the model instead. No host needs either part, and designing them without one would be guessing.

body:
QUEUE п. 8а TAX-APP. Сервер — be#200 (TAX-2, на проде): `tax`, `tax_off`, `can_change_tax`, `tax_choices`, предупреждение `tax_turned_off`, `PUT /my/visits/:id/bill { tax_id | tax_off }`. Вид — `design-mockups/payments/`: app-fee-draft-off, app-tax-pick, app-tax-off, app-tax-readonly.

**Что меняется на экране счёта (только черновик, только когда цены видны технику):**
- Раздел **Tax** между скидками и итогами.
  - С правом (`can_change_tax`): переключатель **Taxable** и строка ставки «Tax NY (8.875%) · On $161.00 · company default · tap to change» с суммой и стрелкой. Строка открывает лист **Tax rate**: ставки из `tax_choices` в порядке сервера, у каждой — сумма налога на этом счёте, у ставки компании — «Company default»; Done шлёт `{ tax_id }`.
  - Taxable выключен: строки ставки нет, плашка «The office sees «Tax turned off» on this bill. Turn it on again any time before you issue.»
  - Без права: одна строка ставки под замком «set by the office» (или «Tax · turned off», если выключил офис).
- **Итоги:** строка налога — имя ставки и база («Tax NY (8.875%)» / «On $161.00»), при выключенном — «Tax · turned off $0.00». Внизу — «No tax · balance due».
- **Предпросмотр** — как печатает PDF (billPdf.js): «Sales tax · Tax NY (8.875%)», при выключенном «Sales tax · not charged $0.00».
- **Edit line:** при выключенном налоге — «Tax is turned off on this bill».

**Отличия от картинки (на решение Дизайнера):**
1. Заголовок раздела **Tax**, а не «Tax and card fee»: переключателя платы за карту пока нет (решения владельца нет, сервера нет).
2. Если в счёте выбрана своя ставка, первой в листе стоит **«Company default»** (`tax_id: null`): сервер называет ставку компании только когда счёт на ней, а вернуться к ней нужно.
3. Ставка, которую офис скрыл после выбора, остаётся в листе выбранной с пометкой «Hidden by the office · stays on this bill» (сервер её не сбрасывает).
4. Нет ставки у компании, но есть из чего выбрать: «No tax rate yet · The company has no default · tap to choose».
5. Под «All companies» в листе нет: `tax_choices` не несёт `company_id`. Нужно — маленький PR сервера.

**Деньги:** приложение налог не считает; сумма у ставок в листе — только показ, тем же округлением, что `taxCents` сервера (на стенде совпала с ответом сервера после выбора). Отказы: 403 `no_tax_permission` → «The office sets the tax of your bills. Ask the office to change it.» и перечитать счёт; 400 `tax_not_allowed` → «This rate is no longer in the list. Choose another one.».

**Проверки:**
- `npm test` 343/343 (было 335; новый `src/bill/tax.test.mjs`).
- Порча 10/10 (округление, «Company default» только у своей ставки, повтор той же ставки не шлётся, право только при `true`, цены скрыты, метка ставки компании, выключенный налог, слова 403, итоги и низ при выключенном).
- Против сервера main `6e7216f` на стенде (своя база, убрана): 39/39 — выбор ставки, возврат к ставке компании, выключение и включение, ставка NJ на счёте NY (400), скрытая после выбора ставка, право выключено (403 и замок), выпуск с выключенным налогом, журнал `bill_tax_changed`.

author: echoofdawn
body:
Closes CMT-1650 (Echo closes the commitment after merge).

## ELI16

On the Conversations page the agent suggests groups of chats, and the owner can Reject a suggestion (it should never come back) or Accept it (a group is made and the chats move in). Until now each of the agent's computers remembered those choices only for itself. If you rejected a suggestion on one computer, another computer could offer it again, and an Accept continued on a different computer (or a second browser) could make a second, empty group.

This change sends the owner's choices to every computer of the agent as small records on the journal the computers already share. A Reject anywhere hides the suggestion everywhere. A started Accept shows Continue everywhere, and carries the group's name and which chats are in it, so even a computer that never built that suggestion can finish the same Accept. The request number for each Accept is now worked out from the suggestion itself, so every browser and every computer asks for the same group. Each computer's own memory file keeps only its own choices; the others' choices are combined in when it reads, so turning the feature off or rolling back needs no repair.

## UX Impact

- Owner on a multi-machine agent: a rejected suggestion no longer reappears on another machine's dashboard; an Accept started on one machine shows "Continue" on the others (reason line "Started on another of your machines." when that machine never built it) and finishes into the same group.
- Single machine: no visible change, except that a second browser tab continuing an Accept can no longer create a second group.
- No new screens, buttons or routes.

## What changed

- New replicated kind `conversation-graph-suggestion-record` (store `conversationGraphSuggestions`): `src/core/ConversationGraphSuggestionDecisions.ts` (row schema with snapshot integrity and derived-request-id checks, order-independent fold, outbox store, drain with backoff/cap/rotation, boot wiring).
- `ConversationGraphSuggestionService`: overlay in `load()`, `save()` never persists the overlay, decisions recorded on reject/start/accepted, boot + first-read backfill, derived create request id (`suggestionCreateRequestId`), running-Accept test for builds.
- Wiring: kind registration, forced-on store flag with kill switch `multiMachine.stateSync.conversationGraphSuggestions.enabled: false`, peer-commit observer, AgentServer option through both graph surfaces; journal tables, evidence label, reconciler allowlist, ladder entry (finished), awareness entry.
- Spec: `docs/specs/conversation-graph-suggestions-replicated-decisions.md` (+ ELI16), converged in 6 rounds (report in `docs/specs/reports/`); parent spec §5 replaced.

## Coordination

The parallel conversation-groups-phone change (branch `echo/mobile-conversation-groups`, not yet a PR) moves Accept into `ConversationGraphSuggestionAccept.ts`. This PR does not touch that orchestration. Expected small conflict in `ConversationGraphSuggestionService.ts` (`beginAccept`, `accepted`, `load()`, header). Whichever merges second: add a rejected `recordDecision` to `closeAccept`, pass `result` through `accepted`. `suggestionCreateRequestId(id)` equals its `acceptRequestId(id, 'create')` (pinned by a unit test).

## Tests

- Unit: `conversation-graph-suggestion-decisions.test.ts` (23), `conversation-graph-suggestions.test.ts` (31), `CoherenceJournal.test.ts` (42), plus maturation-ladder (81) and awareness-registry (45) checks — all passing.
- Integration: `conversation-graph-suggestions-replicated.test.ts` (4) — two machines through the real router: reject on A honored on B, Continue on B with A's request id, concurrent starts converge, legacy decisions migrate once, idempotent re-delivery — passing.
- E2E: `conversation-graph-suggestion-decisions-alive.test.ts` — real journal/emitter/reader + wiring checks (queued behind the shared suite lane at push time; Local Verify runs it).

Second-pass reviewer (multi-machine state, high risk): concurred.

Constitution counterpart: none — no constitution file or CODEOWNERS path touched; serves "An Instar Agent Is Always a Multi-Machine Entity". Approval: Justin's standing rule that only constitution changes need his approval, plus his go on 2026-11-17 15:37 PST (topic 134088).

### mirror: plan each platform from its own closure record

The mirror build was Darwin arm64 only: VellumMirror.cmake stopped unless
APPLE, and every closure had to be the export receipt's Darwin one. A
platform other than macOS now plans from its own record under
provenance/framework/platforms/<platform>/: one closure manifest per unit
from Pulp's own configure for that platform, carrying the build graph and
no file content. The record pins each manifest digest, the Pulp commit and
exporter blob that wrote them, the configure identity and options digest,
the runner image and the renderer asset.

mirror_package.py takes the platform from --platform or the target's
system and processor, refuses a platform no record lists before any other
work, refuses a record whose pins do not hold, a closure source framework/
lacks (port it through the ledger first), and a ledger source whose scope
leaves out the platform whose closure compiles it. The provenance lane
proves each record's commit is on Pulp main and its exporter blob is Pulp's
at that commit. The CMake evaluator of per-source options knows each target
system's platform variables; off Darwin the compiler is unrecorded, so a

No record lands here, so no platform is enabled, and the macOS plan is

## Summary

Until now the mirror build was Darwin arm64 only: `VellumMirror.cmake` stopped unless `APPLE`, and every closure had to be the export receipt's Darwin one. With this PR, a platform other than macOS plans only from its own closure record under `provenance/framework/platforms/<platform>/`. The record holds one closure manifest per unit, written by Pulp's exporter from Pulp's own configure for that platform. The manifests carry the build graph and no file content.

The record pins:
- each manifest's digest;
- the Pulp commit and exporter blob that wrote the manifests;
- the configure identity and options digest;
- the runner image;
- the renderer asset;
- the Pulp workflow run that exported them, and the digest of the artifact it uploaded.

No record lands here, so no platform is enabled. The macOS plan is byte-identical, proven by snapshot, including with another platform's record present.

The team lead ruled that a closure-only record is outside Decision 0010's "no export", since it adds no framework content. The owner approved the per-platform guard rewrite, which still takes two reviews. Both are in DECISIONS 2026-11-16 08:50Z. The design is in pulp-planning `vellum-move/plans/mirror-multiplatform-20261116.md`.

## What changes

- **`mirror_package.py`:**
  - Takes the platform from `--platform`, or from the target's system and processor.
  - Refuses a platform no record lists, before any other work.
  - Refuses a record whose pins do not hold.
  - Refuses a closure source that `framework/` lacks ("port it through the ledger first").
  - Refuses a ledger source whose scope leaves out the platform whose closure compiles it.
  - Plans a source the closure and its ledger row both name only once.
- **`VellumMirror.cmake`:** keeps macOS on the receipt's closures. Other systems pass their system and processor through, and stop without a locked Skia/Dawn archive. Objective-C++ is enabled only on Apple platforms.
- **The provenance lane:** proves each record's commit is on Pulp main and its exporter blob is Pulp's at that commit. It fails closed without a Pulp checkout.
- **The per-source options evaluator:**
  - Knows each target system's platform variables.
  - A compiler condition is decided from the compiler facts Pulp's exporter records (pulp#12456: `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID`, `CMAKE_CXX_SIMULATE_ID`, `MSVC` "1"/"0").
  - Without them, the condition fails closed off Darwin.
  - Shared decision vectors in `tools/mirror/fixtures/source-option-vectors.json` pin 13 cases.

## Per-source options gated on a compiler condition

These counts come from running the evaluator over the transferred CMake under the receipt's Release configure, with only the system and processor changed. Every `set_source_files_properties` in Pulp main `core/` was also read by hand (12 calls).

| Configure | Result | Sources with options | Compiler-gated and affecting the build |
|---|---|---|---|
| Darwin arm64 (control) | decided | 2 | 0 |
| Linux x86_64 | decided | 1 (`css_weight_font_manager.cpp`) | 0 |
| Windows AMD64, no compiler recorded | refused | | 1: `if(NOT MSVC)` around `-fno-rtti` on `css_weight_font_manager.cpp` |

The other compiler-gated calls are ANDed with Debug or UBSan conditions, which a Release closure decides as false. The `plugin_view_host_stub.cpp` calls are on a Pulp-kept file no unit closure carries.

Linux is not blocked. Windows is decided once its closure records the compiler (pulp#12456), and a test pins all four compiler forms.

- **Tests:**

  - `test_verify_extraction`: OK.

- **Gates:** `scripts/gates.sh` fast, 8 passed and 0 failed. It ran with a scratch Python 3.14 venv carrying PyYAML 6.0.3, because the host Python 3.15 has none.

author: ryantxu
body:
Follow-up to #138019, addressing its review comments, plus a fix for the slow shutdown that made the routed integration tests take about 10s each.

### Changes

- **First star as a non-admin.** The stars update route created the object with a collection-level `Create`, which the owner authorizer rejects when the caller isn't an org admin. It now does a named `Update`, which the owner-scoped store turns into a create. The SDK client reads the object first unless it gets a resource version, so the route passes `"0"` (unconditional) when nothing is stored, and the store clears that `"0"` before creating.
- **`metadata.name=` on owner-scoped lists.** The owner-scoped store ignored the field selector and returned every owned object, so an admin opening org or team preferences got their personal ones instead. It now returns only the named object when the caller owns it or the owner authorizer allows a `get` of that name (including the explicit team lookup). Any other field selector returns a 400.
- **Installer logging.** `coreAppsFromInstallers` and `directInstallers` take a `ctx` and log with `logging.FromContext(ctx)`, as `pkg/router/AGENTS.md` requires.
- **Slow shutdown with the routed core apps.** The HTTP server stops before the API server. In routed mode the apps' operators hold watches open against the HTTP server, and those only end when the API server stops, so shutdown waited out the whole 10s grace period. Watch requests (`watch=true|1`) now end when shutdown begins. The `apis/preferences` integration package went from about 36s to about 7s.

### Tests

- Unit: stars route (first star is an unconditional update), owner-scoped store (name selector), watch ending on shutdown.
- Integration: `TestIntegrationStarsUpsert` (first star as a viewer, deleting the last star and starring again, plain PUT without a resource version, PUT to another user's name is forbidden, collection-level create is forbidden) and a name-selector list test for preferences, both in the legacy and routed modes.

The shutdown change is in `pkg/api` and is independent of the router changes, so it can be split out if preferred.

body:
## Summary

The extern-c port respell rule, inert without its table. `tools/mirror/port_respell.py` recognises one kind, `extern-c`: a `pulp_*` function or object a `framework/` file defines with C linkage. That is the one Pulp name that clashes with Pulp's own copy at link time. The rule respells it in every `framework/` file. `PULP_*` macro names clash with nothing and stay as counted name debt. A table entry of any other kind (closure-macro, file-macro, link-export, opt-in-switch) is refused. The scope follows the 2026-11-18 14:30Z entry in pulp-planning `vellum-move/DECISIONS.md`.

Per the rule-data split, `provenance/framework/respell.json` and the respelled files are not here. They follow in a data pull request once this lands, so the merged rule judges them.

## What the verifier proves when a table exists

- The table is exactly the C-linkage definitions the origin bytes imply. A transferred file's origin is its transfer-record blob, and a ported file's origin is Pulp's bytes after the rename.
- No `framework/` file keeps a respelled name's old spelling, and none pastes a `PULP_`/`pulp_` fragment with `##`.
- A transferred or ported file spells a Pulp name the Vellum way only where the table's respell of its origin does, so a hand respell fails.
- An appended Pulp-origin row's blob is Pulp's bytes after the rename and the current table's respell.
- A landed row's blob is the same bytes respelled by some subset of the base table. A later entry respells a landed or transferred file by an edit that must be exactly that respell. An entry is new unless its name, kind and evidence all landed.
- Without a Pulp checkout the result is `deferred`, never `proved`.
- Deleting the table is refused only while some file still carries one of its Vellum spellings. A missing record blob is an error.

## Inert without a table

With no table, the verifier proves no respell and reports no respell check (`test_without_a_respell_table_the_rule_is_inert`). The mirror plan no longer reads the table at all. `framework/` and `provenance/framework-name-debt.json` are byte-identical to `origin/main`.

## Checks

- `tools/ci/rule_data_split_check.py --base origin/main --head HEAD`: passes.
- `verify_extraction.py` with `--pulp-root` (the gates-cache mirror-receipt checkout) and without it: pass.
- `test_verify_extraction` (123), `test_mirror_package` (181), `test_framework_ports` (45) and `test_port_respell` (22): pass. Every touched script parses on Python 3.9.
- Against the local data commit (table of the four names, `VELLUM_GIT_BASE` at this head): pass both ways, `framework_respell_proved` is `True` with Pulp. Controls fail as expected: a stale caller, a dropped entry, and an extra edit beside the respell.

author: xinthefreefallxai
body:
Big Wins #21, #22, #23 (wait_spin part) and #26, from the 2026-11-17 review of Fortune's Eden, EmblemWeave and Eden. Each change has its own switch. Technique only, credited.

## Render thread: cheaper held-result checks (#21)
- `[nvn] out_memo_dirty`: a draw checks only the buffer slots a bind changed since the last check, while the held-result generation is unchanged and no slot was left over a held result. Otherwise it does the full pass as before. Technique from EmblemWeave's perf branch (Stephen Jayakar, 0c04e18).
- `[nvn] out_prog_dirty` + `out_memo_held`: a program bind marks only the bound slots of a graphics stage that becomes active, and slots over a held result are listed instead of forcing a full pass. Technique from moistman7 (ed40ace); upstream measured replay going from 9.9 to 9.55 ms a frame at ~3,000 draws.
- Built on our `lean_draws` bound-slot masks, which already do upstream's `out_masks`.
- Measuring: `[nvn] out_prog_ab = 1` with `replay_stats = N` switches the set every window. A second `nvn.rstats` line gives short/full passes a frame by cause. `[nvn] rt_check = 1` verifies every skipped slot.

## `[kernel] wait_spin` (#23)
- `auto`: with 8 or more physical cores, `spin_us = 30` (main, Basic_Worker) and `lock_spin_us = 30` (main) become the defaults. Keys set by hand still win. From metrist38 (e5fc38d).
- `feedback_fast` isn't ported: `lean_draws` already does a single image lookup in `is_color_feedback`.

## `[nvn] reserved_sampler` (#26)
- Texel-fetch handles (sampler id 0) sampled with filtering get a linear, clamped sampler instead of the nearest dummy. This fixes the blocky sky clouds. From moistman7 (ba21f5b).

## `[gfx] astc_gpu_load_ms` / `astc_gpu_load_s` (#22)
- After a load (a present interval over 100 ms), a present's ASTC transcode budget is at least 8 ms for 3 s, while textures are queued.
- At 120 fps the existing long-frame boost fades within a few frames, and stand-ins stayed ~1.5 s on screen after loads. The frames after a load get slower while the queue drains, so textures arrive sooner.
- The `nvn.astc_gpu` summary counts load windows. `astc_gpu_load_ms = 0` restores the old behaviour.

## `[nvn] bound_upload_defer` now off by default
- With it on, textures a model on screen needed were held back during a load-in burst, and the model sampled the black dummy for a split second after every load.
- Off on the user's PC: no black. The load-in frame took 436 ms instead of 193 + 283 ms over two frames, under the game's fade.

## Checks
- `nvn_replay.cpp`, `nvn_gpu_texture.cpp` and `nvn_astc_gpu.cpp` pass a clang C++20 syntax check on Linux.
- `kernel_sync.cpp` uses Windows APIs. It matches upstream's code, which builds there, but isn't checked here.
- User's PC: `rt_check` 0 mismatches over ~170 M checks; the short path took 99.5–99.8 % of draws; the held-result check went from 0.56–0.60 to 0.45–0.51 µs a draw (~0.2 ms a frame at ~2,400 draws); stand-ins after loads averaged 0.5–0.9 s, down from 1.56 s; the clouds look right.

The prior descriptions confused the public browser examples on ListPull.com with the larger applications and services that the portfolio is meant to document.

I reviewed the [Engineering](https://listpull.com/engineering.html) and [Solutions](https://listpull.com/solutions.html) pages, the original portfolio descriptions, and Jay's resume.

## Changes

- Reframed the ListPull projects around the problems being solved and the underlying engineering work.
- **Creative Editing Applications**: image/vector editing, object state, transformations, layer management, and creative production work.
- **Video Editing & Production**: editing timelines, media handling, timing, previews, and connected production workflows.
- **AI Research & Development Workflows**: Ollama, PostgreSQL, third-party API retrieval, and natural-language research over structured data.
- **Market Analytics & Data Platforms**: integration of multiple live data feeds, React/Angular views, PHP services, authentication, APIs, and charts. **CSV is not portrayed as the underlying platform's data source.**
- **Forecasting Services**: Node.js, ARIMA, per-symbol caching, provider integrations, intraday and daily projections. The public chart example is not portrayed as the entire forecasting service.
- Updated the other project summaries to describe actual engineering responsibilities rather than advertise tools.
- Renamed the relevant links to **Related browser example** to identify their intended role without turning every project story into an explanation about demos.

- All project periods present.
- Checked HTML element counts, same-page links, and browser-example destinations.

## Scope limits

The résumé and original portfolio support the listed data, API, AI, forecasting, and enterprise architecture details. ## Summary

#3982 第一批：`RAW_UNDER_OUT` 裡「只在建目錄時用了裸 `mkdir`」的那幾筆。合入後 #3982 還有其他工具族要遷，**不關票**。

- 有五支工具原本用 `output_write` 包住裸 `mkdir`／`os.makedirs` 來建輸出目錄，現在改走目錄入口 `_lib_io.ensure_dir`。例外類別與訊息都和原本一樣（`cannot create directory <path>: … — check the value given to <flag>`），差別只在寫入稽核記錄的是哪個入口。這五支是：
  - `generate_tenant_fixture`（共 3 處）
  - `assemble_config_dir`
  - `baseline_discovery`
  - `da_assembler`
  - `state_reconcile`
- 三個目錄旗標宣告 `output_dir_type()`：`baseline -o`、`generate_tenant_fixture -o`、`assemble_config_dir --output`。
- `ensure_dir` 對空路徑恢復 `os.makedirs("")` 的語意（ENOENT）。這是獨立審查找到的回歸：`Path("")` 等於 `.`，於是 `baseline -o ""` 從 rc 2 變成把 CSV 寫進目前目錄。
- 測試清單跟著實量縮減：
  - 閘門 `RAW_UNDER_OUT` 從 18 筆減為 13 筆。
  - #3215 的 `test_output_write_sites_stay_guarded`：`GUARDED_FILES` 拿掉 `generate_tenant_fixture` 與 `da_assembler`（上限 22 → 20），三個 `_KNOWN_SITES` 改成實量值。
  - `test_output_dir_flag` 比對旗標名稱時，接受 argparse 依宣告順序印出的寫法（`--output/-o`）。
- `migrate-credentials --manifests-out` 也在清單上，但它的拒收訊息要不要改用共用句，還在等 owner 裁決，所以不在這一批。

## 變化表

以 main（`65c3e3902`）與本分支逐格比對。

| 情境 | 前 | 後 |
|---|---|---|
| 三個目錄旗標給 `-` | rc 0，建出名叫 `-` 的目錄並寫入 | rc 2，解析時就拒收，argparse 點名旗標 |
| `baseline -o - --dry-run`、`assemble_config_dir --check --output -` | rc 0，沒有寫任何東西 | rc 2，解析時就拒收 |
| 目前所在目錄已被刪除時，`generate_tenant_fixture -o out` 與 `baseline -o out` | rc 2，印 traceback 後接 `unexpected internal error` | rc 2，只印一行 `cannot create directory out: …` |

以下情況在兩邊實跑結果相同（獨立審查）：
- 父目錄是一般檔、目標是既有檔、symlink 指向目錄、懸空 symlink、結尾斜線、`./-`。
- 空值 `""`（含 baseline，修正之後）。
- 非 root 時父目錄不可寫、目錄本身不可寫。

整合樹（本分支疊上當時的 main）全量測試，跑在 `b5e906807`：

- 1 個 failure 是 `test_bench_workload_effect_reference`，它比對 main tip 的 git 狀態；單獨重跑和下面的重跑都通過。
- 30 個 error 全在 `tests/federation-e2e`，需要叢集，是本機既有的基線。

在 `c4e781f46` 上重跑 `tests/shared`、`tests/ops`、`tests/dx`（`ensure_dir` 是共用入口）：

```
$ env -u PYTHONUNBUFFERED python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 3 tests/shared tests/ops tests/dx
35516 passed, 825 skipped, 5 xfailed, 9 warnings in 1478.51s (0:24:38)
```

併入 main `a683d9743`（#4045）後，重建 binary，再跑一次動到的範圍（`ea4cea12d`）：

```
$ env -u PYTHONUNBUFFERED timeout 2400 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 3 tests/shared/test_output_path_write_failure.py tests/shared/test_output_dir_flag.py tests/shared/test_write_failure_class.py tests/shared/test_output_write_sites_stay_guarded.py tests/dx/test_generate_tenant_fixture.py tests/ops/test_assemble_config_dir.py tests/ops/test_baseline_discovery.py tests/ops/test_da_assembler.py tests/ops/test_state_reconcile.py tests/ops/test_migrate_rule_outputs.py tests/lint
```

_Requested by **ysuga** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0154kytMaftRmHqeTm2uh5L5?thread=cmsg_0154kytMaftRmHqeTm2uh5L5RypK15HrehnSjxs1hGtrZd)_

#555・#556 への指摘の対応です。

## 1. 線の端を容器の箱・処理の楕円に付ける(CSS)
- 出力の丸を取っ手(`.react-flow__handle`)そのものを 14px にして描いていた。React Flow は右の取っ手なら取っ手の右端から線を出すので、線の端が図形から 7px ほど浮いていた
  - 取っ手は 2px のまま図形の縁に置き、丸は `::after` で描く。擬似要素への押下は取っ手の押下になるので、掴める範囲は変わらない
- 楕円は縁から 2px 内側に描いているので、処理・容器処理の左右の取っ手も 2px 内へ寄せる
- セレクタが `.connectablestart`(React Flow の既定で接続できない取っ手にも付く)だったため、容器などにも丸が出ていた。`.connectable.connectablestart` にして処理・容器処理だけにする

## 2. 接続メニューの「一番下のボタンが無い」
- 引数の無い処理(readonly の counter_get など)へ落とすと、引数のボタンが 0 個の空のメニューが出ていた。引数の無い処理は線の受け先にせず(`isValidConnection`)、離してもメニューを出さずに「引数が無いので、つなげません」と知らせる

- 要素は自前で選択を持つ(`elementsSelectable={false}`)ため React Flow の枠消しが効かず、押した後に Chrome の青い枠が出ていた。`:focus` の枠を消し、`:focus-visible` のときだけ破線の枠を出す

- `tsc -b`、`eslint src`、`npm run check:fonts` 通過
