author: garrytan
body:
A full test run whose failed jobs were re-run now still records every test file it ran, and names the files that passed only on the re-run, instead of recording none. This keeps the run usable as evidence for its tree without ever counting a re-run pass as a clean pass. Nothing to do as a reader.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `scripts/ci-manifest.ts` takes each job's receipts at that job's newest attempt (`buildSide(..., 'job')`), instead of flagging every receipt from an earlier attempt as stale. Files whose newest receipt came from a later attempt are marked `rerun: true`, and the manifest gains `attempts`. A receipt from an attempt after the manifest's own is a problem. `passedFiles` no longer counts re-run files as passed, and the new `rerunProblem` says why.
- `scripts/lib/ci-run.ts` (nightly-watch) reports a run with re-run files as incomplete evidence, so it never clears a failure or closes an incident.
- `scripts/ci-full-suite-tree.sh` refuses outright when the manifest still lists a failing test, and writes `rerun_files` and `attempts` into `tree.json` when any file was re-run. `files` and `tests` cover the whole suite across attempts.
- Docs: `docs/ci-red-runbook.md#ci-failure-manifest` and `docs/ci-event-parity.md` no longer say a partial re-run leaves an incomplete manifest.
</details>

<details><summary>Who reads this evidence, and the proof for each</summary>

Real run: Test run 44208223866 (head 77799a40, tree 0fbb06af), attempt 2 after `test (7, 8)` failed in attempt 1. Its published attempt-2 manifest is `complete: false` with 1356 problems ("comes from attempt 1 … re-run all jobs"), and its `tree.json` has no `files`.

Rebuilt from that run's 70 downloaded receipt artifacts with this branch: manifest complete, 6504 file/lane/arm entries, 0 failures, `attempts: [1, 2]`, 292 entries marked rerun (all from `test (7, 8)`). `tree.json`: 5699 files, 72052 tests, `rerun_files` = that shard's files. A clean single-attempt run (44207021193, one commit earlier) recorded 5698 files and 72049 tests; the one extra file is new in this tree.

- **Master-push reuse** (`scripts/ci-reuse.ts` `decide`): reads only the record's run, attempt, sha, event, workflow and tree, never `files`. Dry run against the real run, with the rebuilt `tree.json` substituted: `reuse: true, identical_tree_full_run`, source run 44208223866 attempt 2. Same result as with today's artifact. A failed run still refuses: `test/scripts/ci-reuse.test.ts` (`run_failed`, newer failed run on the tree).
- **Reuse gate** (`decideGate`, used by `scripts/pregate-remote-gate.sh`): same dry run gives `state: reuse`, 72052 tests, 0 failed. A failed full run refuses: `test/scripts/ci-reuse.test.ts` and `test/scripts/pregate-remote-gate.test.ts`.
- **gstack's run-evidence check** (`gstack-pregate clear --run`, `lib/ci-carry.ts` `findCarry`, gstack 1.100.0.0): today's `tree.json` refuses with `no_tests` ("lists no test files (a rerun of only the failed jobs records none)"); the rebuilt one is accepted with 72052 tests and 5699 files.
- **nightly-watch** (`scripts/lib/ci-run.ts`): new test in `test/scripts/nightly-issue.test.ts` (a reused run whose source passed files only on a re-run keeps the incident open); it fails without the `ci-run.ts` change.

New `test/scripts/ci-rerun-evidence.test.ts` builds the attempt-2 receipt shape. Before the fix it failed 3 of 3 with today's "tree.json records no executed test files … comes from attempt 1" warning. It now checks: every file is covered across attempts and the re-run files are named; a single-attempt run records no rerun; a failing job that was not re-run green, or whose re-run left failing receipts behind, writes no `files`.
</details>

<details><summary>Open question for gstack</summary>

gstack's evidence check ignores fields it does not know, so it accepts a `tree.json` with `rerun_files` the same as a clean one. Whether it should treat re-run files differently is gstack's call; this PR only records them.
</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

- /ship (gstack 1.100.0.0, unattended) ran at c25ba0e3 and finished at 20a1e92d. Review plan: `REVIEW_PLAN: class=code pass=1 next=full dispatches=2` (batched specialist covering testing, security, state-machines and red-team, plus a native adversarial read). One round, no fix round needed: 0 blocking.
- Findings, all skipped as below the blocking bar (no failing test, production break or data loss): the later-attempt receipt guard in `scripts/ci-manifest.ts` has no committed test (behaviour checked by a QA probe instead); e2e.yml's `executed-receipts` does not need `postgres15-compat`, so a re-run of only that job keeps the old manifest and refuses evidence (fails closed, and touching `.github/` is out of scope); the `ci-full-suite-tree.sh` attempt-mismatch hint still says to re-run the whole workflow; a file is marked re-run relative to the earliest attempt among artifacts, so a re-run of every receipt job looks like a whole-workflow re-run; the manifest's `rerun` flag shares a word with the receipt kind `rerun`.
- Exploratory QA: 2 of 2 smoke probes pass on synthetic receipts (a re-run keeps every file and names the re-run file; a receipt from a later attempt than the manifest's leaves `tree.json` with no files).
- Documentation audit: updated `docs/ci-red-runbook.md` (completeness list names a later-attempt receipt instead of an older attempt) and `docs/architecture/key-files/ci-health-and-test-guards.md` (the `ci-manifest.ts` entry). Changelog fragment reworded to pass the prose check.
- Ship receipt not written yet, because the remote_gate obligation needs the full run at this head (full-ci label, then `scripts/pregate-remote-gate.sh`).
- Strict PR: touches `scripts/ci-manifest.ts` and `scripts/ci-full-suite-tree.sh`, so it never reuses its own runs.
- Second sighting of the flaky `test/serve-stdio-lifecycle.test.ts:714` (a 20 ms progress note against a 60 ms deadline) in run 44208223866 attempt 1; not fixed here.
- Checks run before push: targeted suites (ci-rerun-evidence, nightly-issue, full-ci-workflow, ci-reuse, pregate-remote-gate, ci-executed-counts, ci-manifest-diff: 208 pass), `bun run typecheck`, `GBRAIN_VERIFY_SKIP_TYPECHECK=1 bun run verify` (103 green), `bun run regen:all` (structural-suites.tsv updated).
- gstack: ok 1.100.0.0 for=ship. Records under GST-2926.
</details>

author: dtumad
body:
A deterministic oracle chooses one path through a polynomial program. `PFunctor.FreeM.toQueryProgram` sends each operation to its existing polynomial object with the identity continuation. `countQueries_toQueryProgram` proves that CSLib counts exactly the length of the chosen path. `queryUpperBound_of_isTotalRollBound` turns a monotone structural budget for an input family into a CSLib query upper bound. The translation permits independent position, answer, and result universes. The count and upper-bound statements use CSLib’s answer and result universe.

The repeated-query regression exercises the converse. It asks the same Boolean question twice and asks a third time if the answers differ. Every fixed oracle makes two calls, while a branch of the tree makes three. The structural budget therefore remains useful for stateful handlers. [CSLib’s query framework](https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/401)

The full `./scripts/validate.sh --lint --test --axioms` suite passed at `76b46150`, including consumer builds and the zero-debt axiom sweep. A separate VCVio consumer typechecked the specialization to `OracleComp.IsTotalQueryBound` through ordinary imports on Lean 4.36. This follows the interaction-cost work in #387 and the release in #477.

author: kaoston
body:
## O problema

Em 17/11 o relatório mostrou 4 toques em "Entrar no grupo" vindos do anúncio v3, e a Meta só contou 2 leads para ele.

Um dos 4 não era gente. Às 15h23, 44 segundos depois de o conjunto do v3 ser ligado e antes de qualquer exibição, um acesso abriu `/entrar?c=v3` e tocou no botão. O endereço era da rede da própria Meta (AS32934): é a revisão automática do anúncio. O User-Agent era de celular comum, então o filtro de robô, que olha só o User-Agent, não pegou. O acesso contou como toque do anúncio e virou um Lead enviado para a Meta.

## A correção

`encurtador/servidor.mjs`: quem vem da rede da Meta é tratado como robô no `/grupo` e nos links curtos. Continua sendo redirecionado como todo mundo, mas não conta clique e não dispara a conversão.

- `ehRedeDaMeta(ip)`: IPv4 e IPv6, com a lista de blocos do RIPEstat (announced-prefixes de AS32934) em 17/11/2026.
- `pedidoDeRobo(headers)`: robô pelo User-Agent ou pela rede.

Quem navega de verdade pelo Instagram ou pelo Facebook sai pela rede do próprio celular, não por essa, então gente de verdade não é afetada.

## Testes

- `testes/bateria/encurtador.mjs`: 13 endereços da rede da Meta reconhecidos, 22 de fora (operadora brasileira, vizinho de bloco, endereço malformado) recusados; `/grupo` e link curto pela rede da Meta redirecionam sem contar; gente pelo mesmo anúncio conta um toque.
- `testes/bateria/conversao.mjs`: revisão da Meta vai ao convite e não vira conversão; gente de operadora comum vira.
- `node testes/bateria/todas.mjs`: todas passam.

## O que não muda

- O relatório de 17/11 já gravou os 4 toques do v3; o número certo de gente é 3.
- Entra no ar quando o encurtador for republicado no Railway com este código.

body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ puma (5.6.5 → 8.1.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/puma/puma) · [Changelog](https://github.com/puma/puma/blob/main/History.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Parser Allows Remote Memory Exhaustion

Impact

PROXY protocol support for Puma was added in version 5.5.0.

When PROXY protocol v1 support is enabled, Puma reads incoming bytes into an internal buffer. It waits for "\r\n" to determine whether a PROXY v1 line is present. If an attacker opens a TCP connection and continuously sends bytes without CRLF, Puma keeps appending to this pre-parse buffer.

This can cause unbounded in-process memory growth and additional CPU cost from repeatedly scanning the growing buffer for CRLF. A single, unauthenticated TCP connection can drive significant memory growth and may cause process/container OOM or degraded availability.

Only Puma servers using the following non-default config are affected:

   set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

author: rustyeddy
body:
Closes #14 (re-scoped to JSON files; see the issue)

SQLite is deferred until the schema settles; the `journal.Journal` interface and record semantics are meant to carry over.

## Summary
- **`internal/journal`**: narrow `Journal` interface (`Append`, `Get`, `Latest`, `List`) and `Files`, one immutable JSON file per record revision under `records/<kind>/<id>/<revision>.json`.
  - Written to a synced temp file and hard-linked into place, so an existing revision is never overwritten; also linked at `revisions/<revision_id>.json`, making revision IDs globally unique.
  - Identity: logical `id`, `revision` from 1, immutable `revision_id`, validated `supersedes_revision_id` chain. Redelivery of an identical record is a no-op (even after a crash between the two links); conflicting content or a reused revision ID is `ErrConflict`.
  - `journal.json` format version; an unsupported version is refused. IDs are path-escaped and cannot escape the directory. Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339 with nanoseconds. Records read back are checked against their path.
- **Engine**: new `firm.Observer` (`RunStarted`/`StepFinished`/`RunFinished`) via `Engine.WithObserver`. Records success, stop, failure and cancellation. Fails closed: a journal write error fails the run and no further agent runs. `firm` does not import `journal`.
- **Records**: `run` (rev 1 "running" at start, rev 2 with the outcome, so an interrupted run stays visible), `step` (per agent, with SHA-256 digests of the skill instructions used), `model_call` (per provider attempt, including failures: provider, model, tokens, cost, error). A model-call journal failure fails the call.
- **CLI**: `run --journal DIR` (off by default). `/journal/` gitignored.
- **Docs**: `docs/research-journal.md` persistence section, README, architecture.

## Verification
`make check` (gofmt, vet, `go test -race ./...`) passes. Tests cover: restart, retained superseded revisions, failed / stopped / canceled / interrupted runs, exact nanosecond UTC timestamps, redelivery and conflicts, revision-chain validation, path traversal, crash recovery between the index and record links, format version, write failure (read-only dirs), corruption detection, fail-closed engine behavior (journal error at start and after a step), model-call records for failed and successful attempts, and a CLI end-to-end run. Also ran the CLI and inspected the files.

## Notes
- Hard links need a filesystem that supports them (any Linux/macOS local FS; not some network or FAT filesystems).
- Journal data is research evidence: back it up deliberately; retention and backup policy are still unspecified, as the contract says.
- Not covered: order/fill/reservation records (paper-trading issue), concurrent writers from multiple processes (single process assumed), JSON export command.

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ puma (5.1.1 → 8.1.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/puma/puma) · [Changelog](https://github.com/puma/puma/blob/main/History.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Parser Allows Remote Memory Exhaustion

Impact

PROXY protocol support for Puma was added in version 5.5.0.

When PROXY protocol v1 support is enabled, Puma reads incoming bytes into an internal buffer. It waits for "\r\n" to determine whether a PROXY v1 line is present. If an attacker opens a TCP connection and continuously sends bytes without CRLF, Puma keeps appending to this pre-parse buffer.

This can cause unbounded in-process memory growth and additional CPU cost from repeatedly scanning the growing buffer for CRLF. A single, unauthenticated TCP connection can drive significant memory growth and may cause process/container OOM or degraded availability.

Only Puma servers using the following non-default config are affected:

   set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

author: gecube
body:
## What

The contract of #1287 (PCI DSS v4.0.1 6.3.2, 6.5.4; SOC 2 CC6.8). The maintainer decided ([comment on #1287](https://github.com/lajstrom/lajstrom/issues/1287)) on **A**: a repo policy `requireAttachments: [{predicateType, signedBy}]`, decided by #101's Decider at its enforcement points.

- **`policy.requireAttachments`** of a hosted repo is a list of requirements. A version's manifest meets one when it has an attachment labelled `verified`, of a predicate type the requirement matches, signed by one of the requirement's names: a key of `attachments.trust` or an identity of `attachments.keyless.identities`.
- **Second in the decision**, right after a `deny` verdict. A version that misses a requirement is `deny`: it is left out of every rendered index, its download is `403`, and under `enforcePull` its `/v2` manifest is refused to a consumer's token. No `allow` rule lets it through.
- **An upload is never refused for it.** The version shows up once the rows of its attachment commit, which invalidates the repo's documents.
- **`GET …/versions?unmet=<predicateType>&signedBy=<name>`** lists what a requirement leaves out, before it is set and after.

[ADR 0033](https://github.com/lajstrom/lajstrom/blob/docs/1287-require-attachments-contract/docs/adr/0033-required-attachments-of-a-version.md) records the options, the decision and the defaults below. Docs only.

## Why

compliance.md lists 6.3.2, 6.5.4 and CC6.8 as gaps on #1287. "A label never blocks a push" (guides/sbom-and-scans.md), and #101's policy refuses what a rule or a verdict denies, not a version that lacks an attachment. So nothing keeps a version from being served before, or without, its SBOM, its provenance or its signature.

## Contract

- **policy.md §11** (new), "Required attachments":
  - what meets a requirement, per variant; the predicate type and its match; the names and the trust;
  - who sets it, and how; the validation, and the repos that cannot have one;
  - every version, whenever it was pushed; a version before its attachments, and the invalidation;
  - where it is decided; rules, verdicts and quarantine; the reads.
- **policy.md §3**: the requirement is step 2 of the decision, with its reason; an `allow` rule is no exception to it.
- **policy.md §6**:
  - §6.1: the render reads the verified attachments once, and their rows invalidate it;
  - §6.3: an upload leaves the requirements out;
  - §6.5: under `enforcePull`, a consumer's token is refused and a producer's (`push` or `attach`) reads; `detail.requirement`;
  - §6.6: the message, and `requirement` in `policy.refuse`.
- **policy.md §8, §9**: not in the deny list; `requireAttachments` among the repo settings. The header gets the status and ADR 0033.
- **manifest-profile.md §6.3**: a label refuses no push; a repo that requires attachments reads it. Header.
- **index-schema.md**, Attachments: `ListAttested`; the invalidation in the transaction of the rows; `VersionFilter.Unmet`; no migration.
- **layout.md**:
  - the Reader gets `ListAttested`, and `ListVersionPage` takes a `VersionFilter`;
  - the models get `VersionFilter`, `Requirement` and `Attested`;
  - `policy` gets `Subject.NoRequirements`, `Verdict.Requirement`, `Options.Trust`, `RequireAttachments` and `CheckRequirements`; `attest.Trust` gets `PredicateTypes`.
- **http-routing.md**: the `/v2` manifest row (§2); a frontend's refusal (§3); `?unmet=&signedBy=` on the versions (§4).
- **rbac.md §5**: `policy.refuse` traces a required attachment; a change of one is `repo.update`.
- **guarantees.md INV-38**: a version that misses a required attachment is kept out too.
- **Not contract, here too:**
  - ADR 0033 and its index row;
  - `docs/compliance.md`: 6.3.2, 6.5.4 and CC6.8 ("decided, being built"), the Gaps row.
- **Left to the implementation:**
  - api.md (the policy key, `?unmet=`), `openapi.yaml`;
  - docs/policy.md and guides/sbom-and-scans.md: a requirement step by step, a CI that attaches before consumers pull;
  - the threat model.

## Defaults proposed for what the decision left open ("+" or change one)

1. **No `allow` rule lets a version without its attachments through.** The requirement comes second, right after a `deny` verdict, before the `allow` rules, the `deny` rules and quarantine. *Not taken:* after the `allow` rules, as the `deny` rules are: an allow list (`allow @acme/*` beside `deny *`) would then exempt every version it names.
2. **Old versions count too.** Turning a requirement on hides at once every version without the attachments, whenever it was pushed. *Not taken:* exempting the versions pushed before the requirement, which would read `org.opencontainers.image.created`, a time the pusher writes.
3. **Only an attachment labelled `verified` counts**, signed by a key or a keyless identity the requirement names. *Not taken:* counting `untrusted` or `unsigned` attachments, or any attachment of the kind.
4. **A name dropped from the configuration stops counting at the next start**, without waiting for a reindex. *Not taken:* the stored label alone, under which a key removed from the trust keeps letting versions through until each repo is reindexed.
5. **`signedBy` is required.** *Not taken:* no `signedBy` meaning any key trusted for that predicate type.
6. **A name the trust does not have is refused when the policy is written** (`400`), and so is a name trusted for no type the requirement matches; `lajstrom`, the policy key's, is not a name. *Not taken:* accepting it, after which a typo hides every version of the repo.
7. **Changing it needs `manage` on the repo**, as every key of a repo's policy; the change is a `repo.update` row. *Not taken:* the admin role only.
8. **Under `enforcePull`, `/v2` refuses only a consumer's token.** A token that grants the repository `push` or `attach` still reads the manifest, because `cosign sign`, `cosign attest` and `oras attach` read it before they attach. *Not taken:* refusing every token, under which nothing could be signed on such a repo; answering `HEAD` only, since cosign v3.1.4 reads a tag, and signs, with a `GET`.
9. **`signedBy` is a list, and any one name suffices.** *Not taken:* a single name (the issue's spelling), under which a producer's new key means changing every repo's policy at the same moment.
10. **A predicate type also matches its longer versions after a `/`**: `https://cyclonedx.org/bom` matches `https://cyclonedx.org/bom/v1.6`, as the kinds of manifest-profile.md §6.1 do; a signature counts as `https://sigstore.dev/cosign/sign/v1`. *Not taken:* exact match only, which breaks when a tool moves to the next CycloneDX version; kind names (`sbom`).
11. **Each variant needs its own attachments**: a wheel is not served on another wheel's SBOM. *Not taken:* one variant's attachments counting for the whole version.
12. **Hosted repos only, and not `oci` or encrypted ones.** `400` on a proxy (it would never fetch a version that has no attachment yet), on an `oci` repo (it indexes no attachments) and on an `at-rest` repo (its attachments are encrypted and never verify). A group's members' requirements hold through the group. *Not taken:* accepting the setting there, where it would refuse every version.
13. **The reason names the first requirement not met**, `requires an attachment https://spdx.dev/Document signed by release`, and the `policy.refuse` row carries it. *Not taken:* listing every requirement not met.
14. **Not in the deny list.** *Not taken:* listing those versions, which would change the signed list at every push and every attachment.
15. **A listing of what a requirement hides**, `GET …/versions?unmet=<type>&signedBy=<name>`, usable before the requirement is set. *Not taken:* no listing; the decision on every variant in the answers of the list.
16. **At most 16 requirements per repo, and 16 names per requirement.** *Not taken:* no bound.

**During a rolling update:** a replica of the release before ignores `requireAttachments` when it reads a repo, and serves its versions as if i

author: rservant
body:
Tests the promotion alert's 60,000-character hard guard, which had no test (#2937).

**The guard works.** The new test passed on its first run. To prove it can fail, I made the guard return `body` unconditionally. The test then failed with `expected 310219 to be less than or equal to 60000`. I restored the guard and nothing in `promotionAlert.ts` changes in this PR.

**What the new test does.** Reasons are capped at 40, so the old test never reached the guard. The affected-district list and the length of each reason are not capped. The test feeds 20,000 district ids, which makes the body about 310,000 characters, and checks that the result:

- is at most 60,000 characters;
- contains "Body truncated to fit GitHub's 64KB issue limit";
- still starts with the heading and the start of the affected-districts list;
- ends with the clear-path line and the auto-close footer.

**Rename.** The older test matched `/truncated/i` on the reasons-cap line, not on the guard. It is now named for what it checks (the 40-reason cap). Its assertions are unchanged.

**Characters or bytes.** The guard counts UTF-16 characters (`body.length`), not UTF-8 bytes. I did not change it. GitHub's rejection message for a long issue body reads "maximum is 65536 characters", so a character count is the right unit. I could not confirm this against the live API without filing an issue, which is outside this task. If GitHub were counting bytes, 60,000 two-byte characters would be 120,000 bytes and the guard would fail. The alert text is mostly ASCII, so this is a low risk either way. Ron or the COO can ask for a byte-based guard in a follow-up.

**Verification.** `npx vitest --run scripts/lib/__tests__/promotionAlert.test.ts`: 30 passed. The pre-commit hook ran typecheck and lint on both commits.

body:
## Summary

The built-in **Static File Server** widget served `os.homedir()` with `dotfiles: allow` and no `Host` / `Origin` checks. That is the same DNS-rebinding class fixed for the MCP widget in GHSA-45rj-2wq9-r9mr, but the sibling widget was left out of that fix. A rebound page could read files such as `~/.ssh/id_rsa` as same-origin.

Reported by @manus-use via private vulnerability reporting.

## Changes

- Reject requests with an unexpected `Origin` header, and validate `Host` against the loopback bind (including `localhost` / `::1` aliases) before `express.static` runs. Wildcard binds skip the `Host` check (there is no meaningful allowlist) but still reject `Origin`.
- Change defaults: `directory` → `~/electerm-share` (created on start), `dotfiles` → `deny`. A plain home-directory share is no longer the default.
- Report the real bound port in `serverInfo.url` so port `0` works for tests.
- Add `src/test/unit-ci/widget-local-file-server.spec.js` covering valid/alias/rebound `Host`, any `Origin`, and dotfiles defaults; update the two e2e assertions for the new `dotfiles` default.

Existing saved widget configs are unaffected. Users who intentionally relied on the old defaults can still set `directory: ~` and `dotfiles: allow` explicitly.

## Verification

- `npm run test-unit-ci` — 1612 passed, 0 failed
- `npm run lint` — clean

author: shixiangwang
body:
## What this does

Resolves the RB-15 cloud-dispatch residual from #1171 — with evidence, not by assumption.

**Probe result: no leak exists on the cloud path (case b).** A rule whose command prints `$SENTINEL_AMBIENT` / `$ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `$OXO_FLOW_MASTER_KEY`, generated with those sentinels exported in the submit process, produces bodies that contain:

- Kubernetes: `command`/`args` only — no `env` block is generated without sensitive refs;
- AWS Batch: `containerOverrides.command` + `resourceRequirements` — no `environment` key;
- GCP Batch: runnable `script.text` or `container.commands` — no `taskSpec.environment`.

None of the sentinel values appears anywhere in the bodies, and the generators read no ambient state (`std::env` is read only by the HPC `env_isolation_prefix`). The submit-side CLI (`kubectl`/`aws`/`gcloud`) inherits the operator's process environment to authenticate, but that environment is never written into the manifest/spec, so it cannot reach the job. A cloud job's environment is therefore the image `ENV` + the declared `envvars` embedded in the command as `export K='V'` + the `OXO_FLOW_SENSITIVE_<n>` secret references. Routing these bodies through `RULE_ENV_ALLOWLIST` would add no isolation — there is nothing ambient to clear.

## Tests (one per backend)

Each test re-executes the test binary in a child process with sentinel ambient credentials (`std::env::set_var` is unavailable under `forbid(unsafe_code)`) and fails if a sentinel value or any `env`/`environment` channel appears in the generated single or array body; it also asserts declared `envvars` still reach the body through the documented command channel. A handshake marker prevents a silent empty-filter pass.

- `backend::k8s::tests::kubernetes_job_body_carries_no_submit_host_environment`
- `backend::aws_batch::tests::aws_batch_job_body_carries_no_submit_host_environment`
- `backend::gcp_batch::tests::gcp_batch_job_body_carries_no_submit_host_environment`

Negative controls run manually: inlining `SENTINEL_AMBIENT` into `containerOverrides.environment` (AWS) and adding a name-only `env` `secretKeyRef` (Kubernetes) both fail the tests.

## Docs / ledger

- `docs/guide/src/reference/workflow-format.md` — new "Cloud job environment" paragraph under Environment specification; the stale "do not yet route … clean only by omission" bullet is corrected.
- `docs/guide/src/how-to/run-on-cluster.md` — note stating exactly what a cloud job sees and that `OXO_FLOW_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` does not apply to cloud jobs.
- RB-15 ledger: the cloud bullet now records the established boundary and the three test names. RB-15 maturity stays **Prototype** (not marked resolved).

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — pass

author: joelanders
body:
## Problem

The alpha.15 macOS arm64 release build failed the core-capacity check with "MD capacity capture produced no finite audible output".

Each capture got an empty data folder. The Machinedrum then runs its first-launch factory setup and reboots in process, followed by a normal boot of about 11 s. In a 20 s capture that reboot can fall on the only note that would sound (notes are at 10.0, 13.1 and 16.3 s; boot hides the first two anyway). With the block link (509ee86de) the reboot lands just before the 16.3 s note; without it, just after.

It is not a product regression. In paced (real-time) 40–45 s captures with the release PGO build, the block link on and off give the same per-second output for:
- a normal launch with the factory cache present
- a project restore at 20 s
- a first launch: sound returns after the reboot either way

## Change

- `check_mdmm_core_capacity.py --md-factory-cache PATH` copies the cache into every MD capture's `nvram/`, so the measurement is of a set-up machine, as on a user's every launch after the first.
- `build_mdmm.sh` passes `GEARMULATOR_MD_FACTORY_CACHE` through when set.
- Without a cache, MD captures run 40 s, long enough to sound after the reboot.
- The receipt records `md_seconds` and `md_factory_cache`.

No product code changes.

## Tests

- `test_check_mdmm_core_capacity.py`: 6 tests pass.
- With the cache, against the alpha.15 arm64 PGO build, every MD and MM capture is audible. The CPU gates still need a quiet Mac: this run was under a load average of about 20 from other jobs.

author: holgerleichsenring
body:
Application deployment templates, series 2026-11-18-3863. Specs a–d are built. e–h are planned.

## What a deployment template is
A deployment template is the existing template binding with `kind: deployment` and `environments`. It is a context of another agent-smith project, pinned at a revision. Its `.agentsmith/contexts/<ctx>/deployment.yaml` declares:
- `delivery` (only `gitops_pr` is built)
- `files` an application of that kind needs
- `parameters`
- `secrets`, by name only
- `environments`, each with `manifest`, `version_key` and an optional `promotes_from`

The binding sets these per environment: a `repo` from the repos catalog (default: the context's own repo; never checked out by coding runs), `approval` (default **on**) and `parameters`. All of it is editable in the Config studio's templates rows.

## Specs
- **3863a, binding:** kind and environments in config, studio, schema and docs. Rules are shared by the loader and the studio. The binding is addressed `template:deploy:<ctx>`, so it never collides with a code template for the same context.
- **3863b, make-deployable:** runs open the deployment template read-only. The coding master is told the declaration path, each bound environment's repo, approval and parameter values, and three rules: copy or adapt the declared files; ask (with a recommendation) for a parameter nobody gave; reference secrets by name only. A deployment template gives no code advice.
- **3863c, deploy run:** the `deploy` preset, started by `DeployLauncher` through `POST /api/projects/{p}/deployments` (`runs.control`). It reads deployment.yaml at the bound revision and picks the version: the one you typed for an entry environment, or the source environment's manifest value for a promoted one. It rewrites only the scalar at `version_key`, on a fresh `agent-smith/deploy/...` branch, and opens a PR. With approval off it merges in the project's merge mode, and Armed or Refused merges are reported. It then reads the PR's CI once through the CI loop's `IPullRequestCiReader` (#860). The run is listed on its ticket via `ShownOnTicketOnly` and doesn't touch that ticket.
- **3863d, dashboard:** ··· → Deploy… on the ticket page.

## Planned
- e: deploy by triggering the provider's pipeline
- f: follow a deploy PR until it is merged and its CI has settled
- g: suggest make-deployable when a series adds a new service
- h: auto-promote into environments without approval, and let the series run call deploy

Secrets are never created or stored.

Every spec commit passed the spec gate (`.claude/spec-gate.log`). An adversarial review ran before the build (BUILD WITH CUTS, all cuts applied).

author: filipnowakowicz
body:
When another PR merges while a homeserver deploy is building (~15–20 min), the run used to fail red with `Refusing a stale main commit`, even though the newer push deploys the same changes. Three runs on 2026-11-18 failed this way.

**Superseded commits skip instead of failing**
- `scripts/check-deploy-merge-gate.cjs`: when main has moved on, emit a notice, set output `current=false` and return. Missing merge-gate evidence, direct pushes and timeouts still throw.
- Each later job/step runs only while `current == 'true'`; a re-check after the build skips the deploy job (and its environment) entirely.

**A newer push cancels an older build, never an activation**
- The merge-gate check is its own `gate` job, so a commit that will never deploy can't join the build group and cancel a real build.
- Concurrency moves to job level: `deploy-homeserver-gcp-build` (`cancel-in-progress: true`, cancelled runs show grey) and `deploy-homeserver-gcp-activate` (`cancel-in-progress: false`). Stale bundles on the builder already expire after a day.

**Real failures notify main**
- A `notify` job (`if: failure()`) posts to the private ntfy topic that main already shows as desktop notifications, linking to the run. It needs a repository secret `NTFY_TOPIC_URL`; without it the job stays quiet.

**Other**
- Tests cover the skip outputs and assert the gating and concurrency wiring.
- `docs/operations.md` drops the outdated "disabled in GitHub" wording.
- Archives learning candidate `2026-11-18-deploy-stale-main-reads-as-failure` as promoted.

Validation: `bash scripts/test-deploy-homeserver.sh`, `actionlint`, `prettier --check`, `validate-candidates.sh`.

Stacked on #702 (the geo wrap): both change the catalogs. When #702 merges, this pull request moves to `main`.

## The change

`@procedures/dag` gets a procedure for each function of `@mark1russell7/collections/dag` with JSON inputs and a JSON output, next to the hand-written `dag.traverse`. `node scripts/wraps.ts generate` writes `src/manifest.ts` from the types, so no generated procedure can drift from its function.

- 8 of 11 functions have a procedure: `dag.buildLeveledDAG`, `dag.buildNodeMap`, `dag.createNode`, `dag.filterDAGFromRoot`, `dag.getAncestors`, `dag.getDescendants`, `dag.getTopologicalOrder` and `dag.visualizeDAG`. Each one has no effects.
- A `Map` of nodes is a list of `[id, node]` pairs, in the input and in the output (the codecs of #703). A `Set` of ids is a list of ids. Thus the output of `dag.buildLeveledDAG` is the input `dag` of `dag.getTopologicalOrder` and `dag.visualizeDAG`.
- The 3 functions with a function parameter are exemptions with the reason `function-parameter`: `createProcessor`, `executeDAG` and `executeDAGSequential`.
- The wrap is not pure: the package root and `./module` have `dag.traverse`, which reads the workspace and calls git. So the gate of kind 1 does not apply.
- The package uses `@mark1russell7/collections` `^0.11.3` (before: `^0.10.0`). 0.11.0 changed only the range of `rigor-statistics`, so the entry `./dag` and the re-exports are the same.
- `dagManifest` and `dagHomeProcedures` are new exports (the API report has them). The README tells the generated procedures, the exemptions and the update of the manifest.

## Version

The changeset gives `@procedures/dag` a `patch`: new procedures and new exports, and before 1.0.0 a feature raises PATCH (D13: an additive change).

## Checks on this machine

- `vitest run` in `packages/client-dag`: 25 of 25 tests pass, with the 4 new tests of `src/module.test.ts`. They compare each procedure with the function of the home, and chain `dag.buildLeveledDAG` into `dag.getTopologicalOrder` and `dag.visualizeDAG`.
- `typecheck` of the package passes. `node scripts/wraps.ts check --package client-dag` passes.
- `dag` is not a namespace of the MCP tools, so `tools.snapshot.txt` does not change.
- The catalogs `PROCEDURES.md` and `PACKAGES.md` need the build of all packages. The first CI run writes them, and the next commit takes them from its artifact.

body:
## Summary

This is the first increment of P4.3: the part of `neuron-client::render::ff` that models DX8RENDERER's device state, as record 0004 (O25) sets out. Everything here is platform-free and tests on every host. Resources, the device facade, the recording backend, the trace reader, the shaders and the Direct3D 12 backend come in later increments.

## Changes

All of these are in `crates/neuron-client/src/render/ff/` and are new.

- **`state`** covers the 76 render states and 27 stage states of DX8RENDERER's tables, plus the 14 pipeline properties.
  - Each state is a typed value with its Direct3D 8 number. The raw bits are kept, and a value outside a type's range becomes `Other`.
  - `RenderStateId`, `StageStateId` and the typed `RenderState` and `StageState` enums are generated from one table per kind.
- **`defaults`** reads the built-in tables, overridden by the engine INI section the way `ReadProfileNumber` reads numbers: `true`/`yes`/`false`/`no`, hex when the value holds an `x`, otherwise `atoi`. Hardware-quirk pipeline keys are ignored (T22, D202).
- **`model`** holds the render, stage and pipeline caches with the C++ set and get rules:
  - 256 render-state slots and 8 × 29 stage slots;
  - pipeline slots that only an enabled property can change;
  - `reset_render_states` as in `ResetRenderStatesToDefaults`.
- **`fvf`** gives layouts in Direct3D 8 element order. The stride is DX8RENDERER's own `VertexStrideFromFvf`, which differs from Direct3D's rule for `PSIZE`, `XYZB2`, `XYZB3` and `XYZB5`.
- **`geometry`** has `PrimCountFromVerts` with its signed division, and the fan-to-list conversion, which keeps the winding.
- **`transforms`** keeps the `D3DMATRIX` stores (affine and transposed) and does the Z flip through neuron-core's `MulTransform`.
  - It follows the `VIEWSPACE_LIGHTS` rules of `SetModelview`, `GetModelview` and `ApplyIdentityTransforms`.
  - `SetOrtho` and `SetPerspective` compute in the reference's f64-then-f32 order. The C++ takes the tangent of the whole field-of-view angle it is given, not half of it.
  - It also holds the texture-stage and palette transforms.
- **`lights`** is the light manager:
  - records keyed by the caller, with indices that only grow;
  - the once-per-generation dirty queue, and the flush that every draw runs;
  - after a reset, the C++ restarts the generation counter, so a light last queued in generation 0 is not re-queued. The model keeps this.
  - `SetLight` data is sent at once;
  - a draw uses at most sixteen lights (owner answer 3);
  - the material.
- **`draw`** builds what a draw needs from the model:
  - `PipelineKey` holds only what Direct3D 12 bakes into a pipeline state. Fields of a disabled feature are normalised, so states that draw alike share a key.
  - `DrawConstants` holds what the shaders branch on.
  - `unemulated_states` and `unemulated_stages` report what a draw relies on that the shaders do not emulate.
- **`arena`**: generational handles for resources.

**Design documents**
- The P4.3 row in `design/README.md`, and ledger row 18 (DX8RENDERER) set to in progress.
- Record 0004 said 74 render states. DX8RENDERER's table has 76, so the record is corrected.

## Decisions

None.

## Divergences

- **D202:** the hardware-quirk pipeline keys in the engine INI are ignored (T22). The shipped INI sets none of them.
- **D203:** the C++ indexes its state caches unchecked. Here an out-of-range render or stage number is an error, and an out-of-range pipeline id is ignored (undefined behaviour in the reference).
- **D204:** texture-coordinate sets past 7 add nothing to the stride or the layout (undefined behaviour in the reference).
- **D205:** `add_light` and `update_light` take a copy of the light data. The C++ reads the caller's struct at the next flush instead. Trace format v1 records the data at the draw that uses it.

These four wait for owner review.

## Testing

Linux host, plus clippy for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy with `-D warnings` on both targets, and `cargo xtask check-policy` pass.
- `cargo test -p neuron-client`: 45 tests pass, 40 of them unit tests in the library. They cover the state tables and their round trips, `ReadProfileNumber` parsing, the cache rules, strides and layouts including the quirks, primitive counts, the transform round trips and the Z-flip rules, perspective and ortho, the light queue, the flush, the reset quirk and the 16-light cap, key normalisation, the constants, and the report of unemulated states.
- `render_defaults` reads the shipped `outdir/NeuronComponents.ini` `[RenderPipeline]` section, which gives alpha test `GREATER`, `ZFUNC` `LESSEQUAL`, `ALPHAREF` 0 and `LOCALVIEWER` off.
- Not compared with the C++ yet. Model replay of renderer traces, which compares every value the C++ handed back, comes with the trace reader (record 0004, point 12).

## Open items

- Resources: buffers, textures, the per-FVF dynamic vertex rings and the scratch index buffer.
- The device facade over these parts, the recording backend, and the trace format v1 reader with model replay.
- The HLSL shaders with compiled blobs and `cargo xtask shaders`.
- The Direct3D 12 backend (P4.2).
- The RenderTrace proxy changes for v1 (header defaults, frame images, `LightData` lines), and the `Oracle.exe render-replay` mode.

---

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets` pass (add `--target host-tuple` off Windows). Run for `neuron-client`, the only crate changed.
- [x] `cargo xtask check-policy` passes; `cargo deny check` is not affected (no new dependencies)
- [x] Committed vectors were not rewritten to make a failing comparison pass; no dumps or vectors made from `outdir/` are committed
- [x] Ledger rows and `design/README.md` progress are updated

Closes #45

## What changed and why

Seven places in shipped text restated something another place owns and had drifted from it (findings 15, 20, 21, 28 and 29 of `production-readiness-audit-2026-11-17`, and the two parts of finding 23 that #32 did not take). Each now says what its source says. Each was read on `main` at `59025e1` first: none had been corrected by an earlier merge.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Module closes | Modules 1 and 2 listed Module Completion's steps without Step 0; Module 5 put the summary before the recap and named no progress update; Modules 3 and 3b numbered steps 1 to 4 and left Step 0 out | Modules 1, 2 and 5 list its Step 0 checks, progress, recap, summary, as Modules 4, 6 and 7 do. Module 5 keeps its citations, in that order. Modules 3 and 3b say "Run Module Completion's Step 0 checks first, then:" before item 1 |
| 2 | Module 4's secondary offer | "Free raw data" and "Synthesized test data" as equal options | One offer, both entry names kept, no question: free raw data is recommended, synthesized test data is the fallback when nothing in the collection fits |
| 3 | Two citations in `ground-rules.md` | The sentence above the stage table cited INV-140 for both of its subjects; the retired list named INV-141, which is in force | The sentence cites INV-140 and INV-141; INV-141 is out of the retired list |
| 4 | The generated-scenario marker's readers (`graduation/SKILL.md`) | Three readers by step number, with Module 6 Phase C step 13 left out | Module 4, Module 6 Phase C and Module 6 Phase D. The marker test's docstring repeats the same list |
| 5 | `source/hooks/fallbacks/checkpoint-tick.md` | "as `module-completion.md` describes" | "as the "In-progress recap checkpoint" rule in `ground-rules.md` describes" |
| 6 | Comment in `source/scripts/package_bootcamp.py` | Named `tests/test_package_bootcamp.py` for the pin | Names `tests/test_quoted_sizes_say_what_they_missed.py`, which holds it |

Two things a bootcamper can see change: the wording of Module 4's secondary offer, and Module 5 no longer creating `docs/mapping/mapping_[name].md`, which nothing reads. A file of that name left by an earlier run is left alone. No script behavior, configuration key or registered invariant changes. Every changed passage sits outside every host marker and names no assistant, so all five packages get the same text.

## Approach

Implemented directly; no competing approaches were raced. Assumptions taken are recorded in the Clarifications comment on the issue.

## Tests

  - Item 1 reads the order of the steps from the opening of `module-completion.md`, finds every close under `source/skills/` by scan, and fails on a close that omits Step 0 or lists a step out of order. Changing the order in `module-completion.md` makes every close fail.

  - Item 4 fails when a file under `source/skills/` contains the marker, is neither Module 1's writer nor `graduation/SKILL.md`, and its module and phase are not in the list.
  - Items 5 and 6 fail when the pointer or the comment names a place that does not hold what it points at.
  - Item 7 fails when a file under `source/` names a `docs/mapping/mapping_…` document, and when the `_mapper.md` structure has no `## How to run` section.
- `tests/test_gate_options_have_handling_steps.py` gains `Module4StatesOneDataHierarchy` (5 tests) for item 2: the offer's order, "recommended" and "fallback", no 👉, "last resort" in the handling entry, and the three steps under **Agent behavior** in order. Its existing tests pass unchanged.
- Negative controls run on every pass. Run once in a throwaway clone of `59025e1` holding only the two test files: 21 of the 35 new tests fail (`FAILED (failures=21, errors=2)`) and 3 of the 5 Module 4 tests fail (`FAILED (failures=3)`).

## Local CI mirror

#426 made `BIBLE.md` the one style bible but kept the JSON loader, marked deprecated, "until a later release". Its last user was Raccoon World, which moved to `BIBLE.md` in clockgrove/raccoon-world#163. A search of the org's code finds no other JSON style bible, so the loader is removed now.

## What changes

- **`loadStyleBible`** reads only `BIBLE.md` and returns its style view. A JSON file given as `--bible` is refused with exit 2 `invalid_input`, and the message names `BIBLE.md`. Removed with it:
  - the JSON schema, `validateStyleBible`, `JSON_BIBLE_NOTICE` and `isMarkdownBible`;
  - `styleBibleLicenses`, which nothing called;
  - the loader's `log` option and its `markdown` flag. `--lock-bible` now defaults to `--bible`.
- **The perspective anchor in the style view.** An anchor that is the perspective sample and also names a subject now stays in that subject's references, as the JSON bible allowed. Only a perspective sample that names no subject is left out. Raccoon World's perspective anchor names no subject, so its references don't change.
- **`bibleStyleText`** (style outliers) reads only the front matter, with no JSON branch.
- **`StyleBible`** is documented as the in-memory view and never a file. The type keeps its name because the extension API exports it.
- **Pack test kit:** `@clockgrove/assetgrove/testing` gains `bibleMarkdown(view?)`, which writes a style view as a `BIBLE.md`. Packs used to write `sampleBible()` to disk as JSON; the search package's hosted tests now write it with `bibleMarkdown`. `docs/extensions.md` lists the new function.
- **Tests:** every fixture now writes a `BIBLE.md` through `writeStyleBible` (`test/fixtures/synthetic.ts`, built on `bibleMarkdown`) instead of a JSON bible. The CLI tests cover the JSON refusal and `BIBLE.md`'s refusals for a missing version, a bad palette swatch, an anchor with no path, a subject with no references and a missing perspective sample. A new test in `bible-view.test.ts` covers a perspective sample that names a subject.
- **Docs:** `target-profile.md` drops its deprecated-JSON section. `decisions.md`, `generation-knobs.md` and the search package README now name `BIBLE.md` as the only format.
- **AGENTS.md:** a new rule. When a file format, flag, command or code path is replaced, the old one is removed in the change that moves its last user, not left deprecated for a later release.

## Verified

- `pnpm check`: Prettier, ESLint and `tsc` are clean, at the root and in `packages/assetgrove-search`.
- `pnpm test` at the root: 1462 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm test` in `packages/assetgrove-search`: 149 passed, 0 failed. The first push missed these tests, and the `pack` job caught it.

author: guilleojeda
body:
## Changes

- Keep an owner’s pending exit choice independent from a write and its follow-up read. Put the recovery action in the active surface and restore usable focus when it changes.
- Require the confirmed claim’s ID and revision before completing the history update. Treat lost photo finalization results as uncertain when the write cannot be confirmed.
- Use the same administrative outcome handling for classification, moderation, and claims. A result that needs verification pauses the affected controls and preserves independent corrections until refresh.
- Serve the session check and account logout during creator initialization outages. Bound the logout wait and allow a safe provider-only continuation after local cookie deletion. Apply the private cache and noindex policy across private responses.

## Verification

Browser tests exercise writes with interrupted receipt delivery, navigation and focus during recovery, and logout with interrupted responses. HTTP tests cover photo transactions, strong account lookup, session binding, and the actual packaged response policy.

author: emerconn
body:
Bug: connect, sleep the board (greys out), tap connect → "connect failed: 2; is cardguard awake?". Wake the board: Bluefy shows it reconnected, but the page stays greyed out with the error.

Cause: the connect tap stopped the background retries and its failure didn't restart them. iOS kept its connection request open and reconnected when the board woke, but the page gets no event for that and nothing was retrying to notice.

Fix:
- A failed connect tap restarts the retries ("cardguard not reachable; is it awake? retrying…"); each try also adopts a link iOS reconnected by itself.
- Retry loops are numbered, so a tap or a new drop retires the running loop: never two at once.
- Bluefy's bare error codes go to the debug log instead of the status line.

Tests: your sequence (fails before the fix), plus "only one retry loop runs, however often connect is tapped". 10/10 pass. Web app only.

author: phungtruong1997
body:
## What and why
P-4, slice 2 of 4 for R-4 (referral program), designed in UX-2. **Stacked on #197 (P-3)**: this PR targets P-3's branch, so its diff shows only P-4. Retarget it to `dev` once #197 merges.

A referred friend now gets "Referral discount" applied automatically at checkout, classic and block, on a first order that meets the minimum. When that order completes, the referral goes On hold. A daily job pays the advocate the snapshot's points when the hold ends (Rewarded). These cases pay nothing:
- a first order under the minimum, with another coupon (when excluded), or with the advocate's own email → Rejected
- a refund, cancel or trash during the hold → Rejected ("refunded during the hold")
- a coupon window that closes with no order → Expired

A full clawback after payout → Reversed. Lite gets only four generic seams and earns exactly as before.

## Changes
- **Lite seams:**
  - `EarningService::award_flat()`
  - `ContextFactory::from_user( …, $order_id )`
  - actions `yayloyalty_order_awarded` (from `OrderListener::route()`) and `yayloyalty_order_reversed`
  - `ExpiryRunner::register_daily( …, $accepted_args )`
- **Keeping the referral row out of the friend's order:** the advocate's row carries the friend's order id so refunds claw it back. `LedgerEntry::get_own_order_id()` and `source <> 'referral'` keep it out of:
  - the orders list points column, Missing points and the grant check
  - the advocate's history and earned email
  - the daily earning total
- **Pro `ReferralCoupon` / `ReferralCartSync`:** the virtual `yl-referral-{id}` coupon in base currency. It's auto-applied before the points discount, taken off silently when it no longer applies, never added next to an individual-use coupon, and labelled in block checkout.
- **Pro `ReferralLifecycle` / `ReferralQualifier`:** the first order's completion leads to on hold or rejected. A refund during the hold rejects, and a full clawback reverses.
- **Pro `ReferralPayout`:** claims `on_hold → rewarded` and writes the ledger row in one transaction.
- **Pro `ReferralRunner`:** the daily `yayloyalty_referral_run` releases holds and expires lapsed referrals, in batches with a cursor.
- **Knowledge docs:** architecture, helpers, integrations, decisions and e2e.

## Worth a closer look
- `includes/Pro/Referrals/ReferralPayout.php` `pay()`: claims the referral before paying, inside one `Transaction::run`. A referral that a refund, Reject or another payout already moved is never paid, and a gate skip rolls the claim back (`ReferralPayoutAborted`).
- `includes/Models/LedgerEntry.php` `get_own_order_id()` and `includes/Repositories/LedgerRepository.php` (`points_by_orders`, `no_earn_row_sql`, `points_earned_on_site_day`): Lite reads that now leave referral rows out. See `decisions.md` "A referral payout carries the friend's order".
- `includes/Pro/Referrals/ReferralLifecycle.php` `qualify()` / `has_earlier_order()`: the earliest live order is "the first order", and the minimum is read the way the cart showed it, rounded to base decimals.
- `includes/Pro/Referrals/ReferralCartSync.php`: priority `PHP_INT_MAX - 1`, plus `woocommerce_check_cart_items` at 0 so WooCommerce never removes a stale code with an error.
- `includes/Engine/Earning/Listeners/OrderListener.php` `route()`: `yayloyalty_order_awarded` fires here, not in `on_awardable()`, so a guest order claimed later never qualifies (BL-9's default).

## Verified
- [x] `yayh verify P-4 --run`:
  - unit and integration for P-4 pass; the full integration suite has 45 tests
  - `@P-4` and `@flow-earn-on-completed-order` e2e pass
  - phpcs exits 0
  - `release lite 1.0.0` passes, and `unzip -l … | grep -i referral` exits 1
- [x] The hook and schedule checks on this worktree's e2e site: `has_action( yayloyalty_order_awarded )` → hooked, and `yayloyalty_referral_run` pending → 1. The plan's commands were corrected to `yayh e2e cli wp`, since plain `wp` hits the dev site.
- [x] Unit: 150 tests. E2E: `@P-4`, `@P-3`, redeem classic and block, earn on a completed order, and `@smoke` all pass.
- [x] `./scripts/run.sh build pro` passes. `yayh code unused` and `yayh debug markers` are both empty.
- [x] The manual walk-through items are covered by tests: hold, release, reversal and refund during the hold are integration tests, and the $60 / $40 checkout case is the e2e spec.

## Not verified
- With YayCurrency active and a non-base currency: the coupon now stays in base currency so YayCurrency converts it once, but this wasn't run against YayCurrency.
- Lite on a fresh site (purchase earning unchanged, no referral line). The zip validates, but the Lite zip has a known activation fatal on `dev` (P-3 Risks).
- `composer lint` across the whole repo, which has a known baseline failure on `dev`. phpcs on the changed files is clean.

## How to test
1. On a Pro site, Referral → Settings: fixed $10, $50 minimum, 1,000 points, 14-day hold, and Program live on.
2. Give a customer a code (`UPDATE wp_yayloyalty_customers SET referral_code='TESTREF' WHERE user_id=<id>`). In a private window, open `/?yl_ref=TESTREF` and register a new account.
3. Add $60 to the cart. The classic cart and block checkout show "Referral discount −$10.00". Lower the cart to $40 and the line disappears with no error.
4. Place the $60 order and complete it. `SELECT status, first_order_id, hold_until FROM wp_yayloyalty_referrals` → `on_hold`, 14 days out.
5. `UPDATE wp_yayloyalty_referrals SET hold_until=UTC_TIMESTAMP() WHERE status='on_hold'`, then `wp action-scheduler run --hooks=yayloyalty_referral_run`. The status is `rewarded` and the advocate has 1,000 more points. The friend's order points column doesn't include them.
6. Edge case: refund the order fully. The advocate loses the 1,000 points and the status is `reversed`. With a second friend, refund during the hold instead: the status is `rejected` with `refunded_during_hold`, and no `referral` ledger row is written.

## Decided
- The advocate's row carries the friend's order id and is excluded from that order's own points (see Changes, and `decisions.md`).
- A first order that completes while the referral program is off, or that was placed after the coupon window, leaves the referral pending, and the job expires it. A later order that completes first changes nothing.
- The payout waits (on hold) while the loyalty program is paused, while the advocate's account is deleted, or while the first order isn't completed.
- The coupon is checked against a subtotal rebuilt from the cart items (`RewardCoupons::displayed_subtotal()`). Any processing or on-hold order blocks a second use.
- Block checkout's "Referral discount" label is a small inline `registerCheckoutFilters` call added to `wc-blocks-checkout` (Pro only).
- `ReferralQualifier::check()` takes plain facts, not a `WC_Order`, so it stays pure. `ReferralRepository::due()` serves both job phases.
- Every Decided entry with its reason is in the plan, `docs/plans/referral-friend-discount-hold-and-advocate-payout.md`, under Risks.

## Open decisions and later work
- BL-12 (deferred): should the activity log show a referral payout to the advocate?
- BL-13 (decision, default: a referral's status only moves forward): should deleting a refund bring back a rejected or reversed referral?
- BL-14 (decision, default: it stays off for that session): should a referral discount the friend removed come back?
- BL-8 (open, default: no cap): cap per advocate.
- BL-9 (open, default built: a claimed guest order never qualifies).

## Review
- **Per-task risk-3 reviews (yay:bug-reviewer), all fixed:**
  - T1: the hook fired for claimed guest orders; referral rows counted toward the daily limit and showed in the friend's order points, Missing points, the grant check, and the advocate's history and email.
  - T2: the discount could be reused while the first order was processing; a stale code was removed with an error; it could join an individual-use coupon; one-cent rounding.
  - T3: the minimum used how prices were

body:
## Summary

- **Pick the language an AI summary is written in.** The assistant panel has a new "Summary language" picker with the translation languages (Tiếng Việt, English, 日本語, 中文, 한국어). Summaries follow the app's language until another is picked. The pick is kept while the app runs, for every chat. Changing it writes a summary that's already on screen again in the new language.
- **Stickers for punctuation and emoticons.** A draft that is only `?`, `!!`, `?!`, `...`, `:)`, `=))`, `:(`, `T_T`, `<3`, `^^`, `-_-`, `+1`… now gets stickers (🤔 for a question, 😂 for `=))`), and sending one replaces the draft. A `?` ending a short sentence adds a thinking sticker after what the words pick. When someone sends only such a symbol, the reply stickers answer it in kind.
- **A number sent alone gets stickers**, the way Vietnamese chat uses them: `1` (yes, seen, got it) → 👌 👍 👀, `0` (no) → 🙅, `100` / `10/10` → 💯 🤩. Sending a sticker replaces the number. A lone number from someone else is answered too: a 1 with a thumbs up, a 0 with a pleading look. A number inside a sentence ("còn 1 bug") stays a number.
- **✨ runs at once when it has only one choice.** With an empty draft, the composer's AI menu held a single item (Suggest replies), so a tap now runs it directly. With a draft, the menu still offers replies and the rewrites.

## Test plan
- [x] `dart analyze lib test`: no issues
- [x] New tests: the summary language picker (follows the app language, then keeps the pick), symbol, emoticon and lone-number matching in both suggestion modes, ✨ with and without a draft

author: muxagent[bot]
body:
## Summary
On macOS the `[ui-stall]` line printed "free RAM unknown MB (as of the last heartbeat)": it read the heartbeat's cached figure, whose only writer is the Windows memory call, so it was never set there.

- On macOS the stall now asks the system at the stall: it runs `/usr/bin/vm_stat` (part of macOS) and takes free + inactive + speculative pages times the page size on its first line, as MB. The text is parsed by `parse_vm_stat`, which every platform compiles and tests, like the Linux readers. If the tool cannot be run or its text is not what is expected the line says "unknown".
- The label "(as of the last heartbeat)" is gone: the figure is read now.

The heartbeat's own pressure tracking has the same gap on macOS (and Linux): its physical-RAM figures are written only in the Windows branch, so the RAM pressure tracker there never sees a total and stays idle. That is left as it is here; it needs its own change and a look at what level to call pressure on a Mac.

## Tests
`cargo test -p agentmux-cef ui_stall` (8 passed), including a new test for `parse_vm_stat` on Apple-silicon and Intel page sizes, a missing speculative line, empty or foreign text, and a key that only starts like a real one. `check-function-sizes` and `check-file-sizes` pass. The macOS-only call (`fresh_phys_free_mb`) is not compiled on the Windows build used here; a macOS build check is asked of the starpower testers.

## Objetivo

Las pruebas unitarias (#41) y las del proxy (#30) usaban dos copias casi idénticas de los hooks de módulos de Node para ejecutar los `.ts` de `src/` sin Next. La única diferencia eran los sustitutos de `next/headers` y `server-only`. El comentario de `tests/unit/hooks.mjs` ya indicaba que se unificarían al integrarse el #30. Este PR deja una sola copia.

## Cambios realizados

- **Carpeta compartida:** `tests/support/` contiene `hooks.mjs`, `register.mjs`, `next-headers-stub.mjs` y `server-only-stub.mjs`.
- **Hooks:** se conserva la versión del proxy, porque es la más completa: resuelve el alias `@/` y los imports relativos sin extensión, sustituye `next/headers` y `server-only`, y transpila TypeScript con la versión del proyecto. Solo cambia el comentario inicial.
- **Archivos eliminados:** las copias `tests/unit/hooks.mjs`, `tests/unit/register.mjs` y `tests/proxy/register.mjs`.
- **Rutas actualizadas:** `test:unit` en `package.json` y el lanzador `tests/proxy/run.mjs` ahora cargan `./tests/support/register.mjs`.
- **Pruebas:** ninguna cambia. En total son 9 archivos, con 10 líneas agregadas y 54 eliminadas. Los archivos movidos conservan su historial porque se movieron con `git mv`.

## Decisiones a revisar

- **Sustitutos en las pruebas unitarias:** ahora también se cargan ahí. Ninguna prueba unitaria actual importa `next/headers` ni `server-only`, así que no cambia nada. Si una prueba futura los importa, recibe el sustituto en vez de fallar fuera de Next.

## Archivos de otras áreas

No toca código de `src/`, ni archivos de backend, ML, configuración o workflows. Simulé la fusión con `git merge-tree`:

- **`main` (`6b596b7`):** sin conflictos.
- **PR abiertos del HU04 (`funcionalidad/cambiar-estado-ticket`) y del HU10 (`funcionalidad/metricas-conteos`):** sin conflictos. Combinando los tres cambios, `test:unit` da 60/60 y `tsc` pasa.

1. `cd frontend && npm ci && npm run test:unit` (44/44).
2. `npm run test:proxy` (82/82; requiere `openssl` en el PATH).
3. `npx tsc --noEmit && npm run lint && npx prettier --check tests package.json`.
4. `git grep -n "tests/unit/hooks\|tests/proxy/hooks\|tests/unit/register\|tests/proxy/register"` no devuelve resultados.

author: ilovecrayons
body:
## What was wrong

A wake restored a saved session VM with `--restore source_url=file://<dir>` alone, so Cloud Hypervisor used its default `copy` mode: it read the whole memory file (0.6 to 1.3 GB on moss, growing with use) into guest RAM before the guest ran a single instruction.

## What changes

- Restores pass `memory_restore_mode=ondemand` (Cloud Hypervisor v54.1, `docs/snapshot_restore.md`): the guest resumes at once, each page loads from the file on its first touch through userfaultfd, and a background thread loads the rest. The mode is strict, so a restore that cannot use it fails and the existing cold-start fallback applies.
- Only the unit a restore starts may open `/dev/userfaultfd` (`DeviceAllow=/dev/userfaultfd rw`, added when the launch carries `--restore`); a booted VM's unit, including every terminal, dictation and update VM, gets no access. Cloud Hypervisor tries it before the `userfaultfd(2)` syscall, which needs `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` with `vm.unprivileged_userfaultfd=0`. The monitor runs as root, so the device's `0600 root` mode admits it. Hosts need Linux 6.1+ with `CONFIG_USERFAULTFD` (Debian 12 and Ubuntu 24.04 have it); `vm install` now opens the device next to `/dev/kvm` and stops with the error, and `docs/install.md` and `docs/security.md` say so.
- The snapshot directory is still dropped before resume: `vmm/src/memory_manager.rs` (v54.1) opens the memory file once at restore and keeps the fd until every page is loaded, then the handler thread exits and closes it.
- Cloud Hypervisor refuses `vm.snapshot` with 409 while an on-demand restore is still loading (`VM on-demand memory restore is still in progress`). A save right after a wake now retries the snapshot every 200 ms for up to 60 s, logging once that it waits, while the VM stays paused (loading goes on while paused). Each snapshot call keeps the caller's context and the API client's 2-minute bound.
- A short memory file now fails the restored guest instead of the restore (copy mode read it all first), so `save` fsyncs the snapshot directory and its files before it records the VM as saved.
- vhost-user devices do not work with on-demand restore. A saved VM never has one: `save` refuses VMs with a virtio-fs share (that refusal predates save/restore), so no copy-mode branch is needed.

## How it was verified

- `TestKVMSaveRestoreKeepsProcesses` now keeps over 1.5 GiB in a 2 GiB guest's `/dev/shm`, syncs and drops the host page cache before each restore (as on a host where the VM slept for minutes), and saves again right after the first wake, while the memory still loads (the engine logs `wait for the VM to load the memory it was restored with`). Same processes and boot ID after two rounds. It logs each restore, then the first exec and the time until the guest has read all its memory back.
- That test on a hosted KVM runner, two rounds each:

| | copy (main) | on demand (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `restore` returns | 4.37 s, 4.39 s | 0.57 s, 0.41 s |
| first exec in the guest | 4.45 s, 4.50 s | 1.04 s, 0.77 s |
| guest has read all 1.5 GiB | 7.24 s, 7.28 s | 5.94 s, 5.85 s |

  Runs 44237926389 (copy) and 44237933374 (on demand). The second save after a wake took 9.0 s against 11.0 s in copy mode, so waiting out the load costs nothing extra there.
- Full KVM suite on this head (16318bb9): run 44257187364, green.
- Unit: `TestSaveRefusesSharesAndRestoresAVMWithout` checks a restore launches with `memory_restore_mode=ondemand` in a unit that may open `/dev/userfaultfd`, and covers a save whose first two snapshots are refused while loading; `TestVMUnitsWriteOnlyTheirOwnPathsAndKeepFewCapabilities` checks a booted VM's unit may not open it.

This PR was made with the help of Claude Code.

author: radatta
body:
## What

The review's stop-and-ask (`docs/ops/REVIEW.md` → _Round 2 and later_) gets a third trigger, the **twin**: from round 2 on, a serious `cause=fix` or `cause=sibling` finding in the mechanism an earlier round's fix already patched. That pattern means the design is wrong, not the code. So the lane stops patching and asks, and its pick is to re-plan that piece: move the judgment to where it is made once, or narrow the scope.

Every stop now works the same way: the round's findings stay unpatched, and the ask offers patch-and-recheck, re-plan, or ship. A new **The pick** bullet says what to recommend:
- At a twin, re-plan. The re-plan gets a fresh round 1 with its lenses, never skipped.
- At the cap with no twin, on a diff with no risk class: fix the open list, then run one final broad review (every lens the branch's paths trigger, over the whole branch diff), fix its S1/S2 with no further round, then ship. Not another narrow recheck.

A twin also counts in a dev-fix chain, from its round 1 (not in a rebase chain).

## Why

A recent lane's review had falling serious counts each round, so the "no fewer" trigger never fired. But rounds 2, 3 and 4 each found a serious bug in the same mechanism, and each fix opened a twin. The structural fix came only at the four-round cap. The lesson lived only in the hub's memory; lanes read REVIEW.md, so it belongs there.

## Changes

- `docs/ops/REVIEW.md` — the twin trigger and _The pick_. "Serious again" defers to the stop. _The round record_ says "stop-and-ask" for "round cap". "Twin call site" became "another call site" in the intro and the `sibling` Coverage row, so a plain sibling doesn't read as the stop.
- `docs/ops/FEATURE-WORKFLOW.md` — phase 6's restated stop triggers became a pointer to REVIEW.md (one home per fact). "Round cap" became "stop-and-ask" in both mode lists and phase 7, so the autonomous exception list covers a round-2 twin.
- `docs/index.md` — REVIEW.md's line names the stop-and-ask instead of "the four-round stop".

## Decisions (autonomous)

- At any stop the round's findings stay unpatched, so nothing ships unrechecked behind the ask.
- "Not complex" means no risk class, the doc's existing line between simple and risky.
- A twin outranks the cap: at a twin the pick is re-plan, even at the cap.
- Round 2 counts, but only within the patched mechanism. A serious regression in a caller or another module still goes through "Serious again".
- What the final review can't fix goes back as `[ask-maintainer]`; an S1/S2 never ships unasked.
- A twin counts in dev-fix chains only. A rebase's bad conflict resolution says nothing about the design.

## Testing

Docs only: no dev deploy, no dev check, no dev-test matrix. `pnpm gate:fast` is green (typecheck, lint, the scripts tests the diff reached).

## Review

Three rounds.
- Round 1, `code-reviewer`: 1 S2, 6 S3.
- Round 2, `review-fixes` plus `review-shell` (added late: the workflow-docs row): 4 S2, 11 S3. The serious ones sat in the text round 1's fixes had patched, so the stop/pick text was simplified rather than patched.
- Round 3, `review-fixes`: 1 S2, 3 S3, all in the round-2 wording (a re-plan's lens set below the _Picking lenses_ floor, the ship option's open list, rebase chains, re-plan ids). At the stop-and-ask the maintainer chose to apply the four one-clause fixes as spelled out, gate once, and ship with no further round, so they are fixed without a recheck.

**Open findings shipped:** none (the round-3 fixes shipped without a recheck, by the maintainer's call).

## Follow-ups

- `.claude/agents/review-fixes.md` uses "twin" for any sibling and doesn't name the mechanism per finding. Aligning it with this rule is a `.claude/` edit.
- `CLAUDE.md` → _Feature workflow_ phase 6 still says "4 rounds at most" only, and `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ops/HUB.md` call the approval "the review's round-cap decision". Both are still true but incomplete (logged as F267).
