author: trent-s
body:
### Description

What:
- Kustomize token: clone-pr-and-build now passes the GitHub token to make bundle, so the kustomize install script calls the GitHub API with a login.
- Safer diagnostics step: capture-diagnostics checks that oc exists and the cluster answers. If not, it prints the reason and exits cleanly, with the last lines of oc's error if there are any.
- New failure diagnostics: a new action, capture-crc-failure-diagnostics, runs only when a step failed. It collects:
  - crc status and the tail of ~/.crc/crc.log
  - when the cluster answers, nodes, cluster operators, machine config pools, pods that aren't ready, the Events of pods that can't start, and recent warning events

  The result goes to logs/crc-failure-diagnostics.log and is uploaded with the existing logs.

Why:
Recently e2e job failures have been erratic and the logs are not conclusive regarding causes such as:
- Rate limit: the kustomize download is unauthenticated, and GitHub rate-limiting tends to cause failures before CRC even started.
- Misleading oc not found: the diagnostics step ran oc even when CRC never started. The "oc: command not found" or "Missing or incomplete configuration info" error hid the real failure.
- No cause recorded: when CRC failed, nothing said why. e.g.,  in one observed run the CRC cluster's catalog pods were stuck in ImagePullBackOff, but the log had no error text.

The token removes one source of random failures. The diagnostics make the next CRC failure explain itself, and the job still shows the original error.

**Read-only project (EPERM under the Aiterm fork write-ban)**
- `tryAcquireWriterLock` treats EPERM/EACCES/EROFS from the lock write as "cannot be the writer": it answers `taken` with `unwritable: <errno>` (no throw). The direct engine, the fallback engine and `activate` already serve read-only on `taken`; none retries.

- Second layer found while testing: a read-only connection to a WAL database with no `-wal`/`-shm` cannot create them in a folder it cannot write (`attempt to write a readonly database`), so reads failed even after the first fix. author: trop3n
body:
Follow-up to #3. Stacked on `bar-mosaic`; it will retarget to `main` once #3 merges.

## Key
- **Key Low / Key High / Key Softness / Key Invert** pick which bars get the effect, by the average brightness of the clip under each bar. A bar is kept or replaced as a whole, so it is never cut in half at the key edge.
- **Outside** picks what replaces the other bars: Original (the clip), Dashes (caps only) or Gap Colour.

## Blocks
- **Block Scale** N merges N bars along the row and N rows into one block, in the same warped coordinate (u / N). It needs no extra passes, and blocks line up with the bars around them.
- A spot uses its block when the block's average brightness is inside **Block Low..High**. This gives the mix of fine rows and big blocks in reference clip Video-68826.

## Testing
- With the new controls at their defaults, output is identical to #3 (pixel diff 0 on a Crater Lake frame).
- `cargo test`, `fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` pass. fx-host GL checks pass. About 2.2 ms per frame at 1080p with blocks on, about 1.7 ms off.
- Checked on the waterfall and Crater Lake clips from the Resolume comp: key boundaries follow whole bars, and blocks meet bars cleanly.

author: jbuffin
body:
## What and why

Closes #765

A module plugin can now put short notices at the top of its page and tell Admiral its first page is still loading. Until now a module's page was only groups of rows, so a plugin had no way to say "your token expires in 3 days" or "still fetching".

**What a plugin can send.** Two new optional fields on a page answer:

- `notices`: up to 20 items, each `{id, text, tone, link?}`. `tone` is `info`, `warn` or `error`; anything else reads `info`. `text` is cut to one line of at most 300 characters. `link` is `{label, url}` with an http(s) url; a bad link drops only the link. A notice's `action` is ignored. More than 20, a missing, repeated or unusable `id`, or a malformed `notices` or `loading` refuses the whole answer, and the last good page stays.
- `loading: true`: before any good page, the module shows its notices above a skeleton instead of an empty page. After a good page, a loading answer changes nothing the engineer sees (groups, notices and waiting count all stay).

**What the engineer sees.** Notices draw between the title and the groups, in the plugin's order, with a tone color from Admiral's tokens (`warn` uses the needs tokens, `info` the accent, `error` the error color). A link opens in a new tab. Notices stay above the sign-in card and above an error note. They never add to the waiting count or the nav badge. A page with no notices looks as it did.

`docs/plugins.md` and `docs/api.md` describe the fields, the limits and the refusal rules.

**Calls the Agent Brief didn't settle** (reversible defaults):

- A `loading: true` answer after a good page changes nothing (groups, notices and waiting all kept), but still clears a page error. This is the literal reading of the brief.
- A `loading: true` answer before any good page serves its notices only (groups `[]`, waiting 0), and those notices survive `auth_required` and `error`.

**One departure from the tests as first written.** The tests expected a notice whose text is `"\nlater line"` to be dropped. The existing one-line rule (used for row titles) takes the first non-empty line, so the notice reads "later line". Notices reuse that rule rather than adding a second one; the test now pins "later line" (the review agreed).

## What was checked

- **Tests**: 17 Go tests (parsing, limits, runner state, last good page, loading, auth/error, waiting count) and 11 component tests (order, tone, link, notices above skeleton, sign-in card and error). No new E2E test; nothing in this change needs a layer above these.
- **Review**: found two blocking items, both fixed: acceptance-criterion tag comments in the tests, and a miscounted sentence in `docs/plugins.md`. Four LOW items were also fixed (stale doc comment, a shared `parseLink` for the notice and detail-view link rule, the refusal for malformed `loading`/`notices` now documented, and the `"\nlater line"` case).
- **Security review**: no high or medium findings. Notice text and labels render as text, urls are checked on the server and again in the client, the link has `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and limits apply to a loading answer too.
- **Fix check**: all six fixes confirmed, nothing introduced by them. Targeted Go and component tests pass.
- **WebKit check**: 44 of 44 checks pass in WebKit at desktop (1280x800), iPad (834 wide, touch) and phone (393 wide, touch): loading, notices in order and tone, link opens a new tab, loading after a good page, auth and error states, long text wraps with no sideways scroll, dark theme contrast, and no element when there are no notices.

**Not checked:** real iPad or iPhone hardware (the check ran in Playwright WebKit, not Safari on a device), and landscape iPad. A notice with an unknown tone or a bad link url was not looked at in the browser; the Go and component tests cover them.

**Open for a human:** the notice link's tap target is 89x24 px on iPad and phone, under 44 px, and a notice with a link is 42 px tall against 34 px without. One `min-height` change covers both. Details are in the PR comment.

**Rebased onto main** (`9f1f1fca`) to clear a conflict with the module action changes (#781, #782) in `internal/sources/page.go` and `web/src/app/shell.css`. Both sides are kept. `forgetStepsLocked()` runs only when an answer's page is actually taken, because a loading answer leaves the last good page, and so its step actions, as they were. The reviewer and the security reviewer checked the resolution only and found nothing blocking.

## E2E evidence

Commit `cb3a8f93`, which is this PR's head. From `make e2e` on that commit, the Go e2e failed on one test:

```
--- FAIL: TestAScoutLaunchedThroughTheAPIIsGuardedAndSailsAtItsStop (15.71s)
    guard_scout_launch_test.go:61: ADMIRAL_SCOUT = "/private/tmp/adm2333308600/h/worktrees/inlet-iguana", want the resolved checkout "/private/tmp/adm2333308600/w/scoutrepo"
FAIL	github.com/jbuffin/admiral/e2e	178.300s
```

It fails the same way on a clean build of `main` at `9f1f1fca`, without this PR, so it comes from main (a no-skill ship now runs in a worktree, #773, and the scout test expects the checkout, #779). Nothing in this PR touches scouts. Because `make e2e` stops at the Go failure, Playwright ran on its own on the same commit:

```
  62 passed (1.8m)
```

No `skipped` or `flaky` lines were printed.

author: joshborseth
body:
## Summary

The simulation ticks at 120 Hz but the client renders faster. Until now a click was acted on by the next tick, using that tick's view angles and remote-player view tick, up to about 8 ms after the click. During a flick the crosshair had already moved on, so the shot did not go where the player clicked. This change fires the shot from the view at the click, the way CS2's sub-tick input works, on both the predicting client and the server.

## Design

- **Capture.** `FpsPlayer::input` records yaw, pitch, and the current render view tick when the fire press event arrives. Every mouse motion event before the press has already been applied by then. The first press since the last tick wins.
- **Input.** The next tick's `PlayerInput` carries `fire_aim: Option<FireAim>`, which is the press angles minus the tick's angles. That input's `view_tick` is the one captured at the press.
- **Sim** (`rust/sim`). `PlayerInput::shot_view()` returns the press angles when a `FireAim` is present and the tick's angles otherwise. `player::step` passes them through `CombatInput` into `CombatEvent::Fired { yaw, pitch, .. }`. The client's local hitscan and the server's `Shot` both read the angles from the event, so recoil, spread, the hitscan direction, and the server's check all use the same values. Movement and the view still end the tick at the tick's yaw and pitch.
- **Held automatic fire** keeps the tick's angles. Those shots are timed by the weapon's cooldown on the tick cadence, not by a button event, so the tick's view is the view at that moment. Interpolating between the two ticks' angles would invent a mouse path we never saw.
- **Validation** (`net::subtick::check`, a pure function). Each axis of the press aim must lie between the previous input's angle and this input's. Yaw is compared the short way around the circle. The slack is 2 wire steps (about 0.01°), enough for rounding. An axis outside that range is clamped to the nearest end, so a forged snap lands no further than the view actually turned. A flick away and back within one tick is clamped as well, by design. The server checks against the avatar's previous applied angles. The client runs the same check against its previous input before predicting, and the check returns a value the wire carries exactly. A checked press aim therefore passes the server's check unchanged, and the two sides agree bit for bit. The view tick still goes through `rewind_target_for` clamping as before.
- **Exact local hit test.** If a render frame passes between the click and the tick, `NetClient` keeps remote players' hitboxes posed at the click's view tick until the tick fires. Bodies keep moving. The local hit marker then tests the same pose the server rewinds to.
- **Wire** (protocol 19). One flag bit per input. On the press input only, the flag is followed by two zigzag varints of 1/65536-turn steps, capped at a quarter turn. Redundant resends cost one bit each. The decoder rejects offsets past the cap.
- Bots and offline play send no press aim, or a client-checked one offline, and behave as before.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` all pass. That includes new tests for:
  - `net::subtick`: between, clamped, slack, yaw wrap-around, idempotent re-check, and no press aim without firing.
  - The protocol: round trip with redundancy, quantization, and rejecting offsets past the cap.
  - The sim: the press shot uses the press aim, held fire uses the tick's angles, and the state is unchanged.
- `rust/sim/tests/determinism.rs`: press aims are now in the scripted stream, checked like the server checks them. The state hash still matches main's `REFERENCE_HASH`, so the press aim changes no state. A new `SHOT_REFERENCE_HASH` covers every shot's angles. It matches in debug and release.
- `cargo build -p shooter-game` passes. Godot tests, run with `.github/scripts/godot-tests.sh`:
  - New `subtick_test`, at a fixed frame rate: a click on a board followed by a flick away hits the board. Held fire with the view turned away misses. A click on a view neither tick passed through is clamped and misses.
  - `net_test` has a new online check: click on the strafing bot, flick half a radian away before the tick, and the server confirms a hit. It passed in all 7 local runs, needing 1 to 5 clicks.
  - `smoke_test` and `bots_test` pass.
- `gdlint` and `gdformat --check` report no problems.
- Flaky locally under heavy load, in parts of `net_test` this PR doesn't touch: one run failed the existing bot-shooting checks (the same check failed main's CI run 44232117289), one hit an "unknown baseline" snapshot decode, and one client crashed with signal 11 after the new check had passed.

author: kunal2016
body:
Name: Kunal Sinha
Team: 01-data-a

Data A, task 3.4: H3 (the same content in another language) for dedup v1.1, in `teams/01-data-a/dedup/`. The translation finder (`h3.py`) and the step that applies its matches in `dedup.py` (`h3_join.py`). **Report-only: it removes nothing until TSAI rules on keeping or removing translations.**

## What's in it

**Finding translations (Aneesha Das; reviewed in patilvijay23/era-v5-lab#44):**
- `h3_design_v1.md`: the method (H3-a to H3-d), validation (E5) and open decisions.
- `h3.py`, `h3_signals.py`, `h3_align.py`: the measurement job. Candidates by retrieval (LaBSE vectors, batched on 1 GPU) and same-URL pairs, then sentence alignment; a pair qualifies by sentence coverage, with a threshold per language pair (default 0.7). Writes `h3_matches.csv`, keyed by `(pack_id, split, part, row_in_part, doc_id)` of the cleaned parts.
- `README_h3.md`, `requirements_h3.txt` (pinned), `h3_local.json`, and the local run of 17 Nov (`jobs/logs/2026-11-17-h3-local.txt`): 305.0 s for 6,000 documents.

**Applying them in dedup (Kunal Sinha):**
- `h3_join.py` and an optional `h3` key in `dedup.py`: `{"matches": "<h3_matches.csv>", "remove": false, "parallel_packs": []}`.
- **Exception handling, so valid translations stay:** H3 never chooses a survivor. With `remove: false` (the default) it only reports, in `h3_pairs.csv`. With `remove: true`, the only removal is a train translation of a held-out document (rule 0). No H3 match counts inside a pack that is parallel by design (`parallel_packs`, e.g. Pralekha, BPCC).
- H3 removals, if ever enabled, go into the same `remove_list.csv` and `dedup_log.jsonl` (`rule` H3, `stage` cross_language), so the pipeline still gets one list.

## Evidence

- **No change without H3.** On the overlap rerun's returned files (#469), `dedup.py` with no `h3` key gives byte-identical `remove_list.csv`, `dedup_log.jsonl`, `heldout_duplicates.csv`, `empty_documents.csv` and `dedup_groups.csv` to 6cfc24a (the code TSAI ran for #547), and the same summary counts; `h3_pairs.csv` is not written.
- **Tests: 207.** 158 pass on Linux (the dedup suite, the 10 `h3_join` tests and the H3 signal tests); `test_h3.py` and `test_h3_align.py` (49) need `torch` and pass on Windows (Python 3.14), where all 71 H3 tests pass.
- **The two halves fit:** `h3.py` writes exactly the 13-column header `h3_join.py` reads; `dedup.py` with an empty `h3_matches.csv` runs and leaves the remove list unchanged.

## Still open

- **E5c, the measurement job** on the cleaned parts of #244 (as the overlap rerun): job request to follow in this PR.
- **TSAI's ruling** on keeping or removing translations (H3-f), and which language pairs are in scope.
- **The Sanskrit threshold:** LaBSE at 0.7 finds only 19–29% of FLORES Sanskrit translations; it waits for E5a′ (another encoder) and E5d (bilingual readers).
- `parallel_packs` is empty until the first sources' manifest names the packs that are parallel by design.

author: dotcoocoo
body:
Adds Apple VideoToolbox H.264 and HEVC (built in). They run the VideoToolbox hardware encoders in StudioCraft's own process on macOS, for MKV recordings without `ffmpeg`.

- `craft-hwenc-native` gets `vt::Encoder` and `vt::available`, with the same `Config`, `encode`, `flush` and `codec_private` as the NVENC and Media Foundation encoders. The calls go through the `objc2-video-toolbox`, `objc2-core-media`, `objc2-core-video` and `objc2-core-foundation` bindings, added for macOS only. Off macOS, opening one returns `Error::NoDevice`.
- The session is created with `RequireHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder`, and a session that VideoToolbox reports as software (`UsingHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder` false) is not used. `kVTVideoEncoderNotAvailableNowErr` at creation or preparation returns `Error::Busy`, which the hardware test tries again later.
- Profiles are H.264 High and HEVC Main at automatic level. Frame reordering and open GOPs are off, real-time is on, and colors are BT.709 limited range. Quality level q maps to a session quality of `(100 - 2q) / 100`. An encoder without a quality setting gets an average bitrate of a tenth of a bit per pixel per frame. Bitrate mode uses `ConstantBitRate` where macOS has it (macOS 13 and later, looked up at run time). Otherwise it uses an average bitrate with a one-second `DataRateLimits` ceiling, and an encoder that refuses the ceiling does not open.
- The `avcC` or `hvcC` record comes from the parameter sets of one gray frame encoded in a separate session. A sample whose format description or in-band parameter sets differ from the record stops the recording. Parameter sets and access unit delimiters are left out of the packets, and so are HEVC end-of-sequence and end-of-bitstream units.
- Each frame goes in at a whole-frame time in the session's timescale (the frame rate's numerator). A sample later than the oldest pending frame drops the frames in between, and an earlier one is an error.
- `studiocraft-encode` adds `VideoToolbox`, registered as `vt_native_h264` and `vt_native_hevc` after the Media Foundation encoders. `hardware::for_candidate` maps `vt_h264` and `vt_hevc` to it, so the studio's Hardware encoder tests them in the process for an MKV recording and records with the built-in twin. The two names have rows in every locale catalog.
- FFI stays in the private `vt_ffi` module with SAFETY comments. NOTICE names the FilmCraft source of the session code.

Tests: the bookkeeping runs on every platform. body:
A thread now brainstorms instead of editing by default. What Claude proposes, options and edits alike, shows as cards you pick from, and on the map.

**Options**
- Claude offers alternatives through a new MCP tool, `anur_offer_options`: each a title and the section's whole new text. It does so by judgment, also for asks like "make this sharper".
- Cards in Think and dashed blue boxes off the section on the map; hover a box for its text.
- **Use this** replaces the section's own text through the page (one ⌘Z undoes it); **Add as subsection** puts it under the section.
- **Explore this** works an option through before picking; options found while exploring nest under it ("Within …" in Think, children on the map).

**Edits are one more option**
- Each edit Claude makes is a card beside the options ("Edit to Pricing": Use this, Show on page, Set aside) and a dashed amber box on the map. The page's Apply is now Use this. Using or setting one aside clears the card and the box (the preview update now tells Think and the map).

**Also**
- Agent, mode and model sit on the send button's line as compact text, each as wide as its value.
- The map refits when new boxes appear, until you pan or zoom.

body:
## Summary

Go side of `count_records` (feature `reporting-mcp`, T2): a read-only MCP tool that counts the records of a module, optionally grouped by a closed-list field and bounded by dates.

- `ontology`: `Service.Countable` + `Store.Countable` read only `id`, `marking` and the `group_by` field's JSON value (cap 20000, fetches 20001 to set `truncated`), ordered by id. No `GROUP BY` in SQL. The dated variant reuses the timeline rule: `left(payload->>field, 10)` must match `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` and lie in the `DayBound` bounds.
- `integration`: `count_records` input after `get_timeline`; `readCall.count` checks module → dates → date field → `group_by` policy (`clear` only) before reading any row, then passes every row through `session.Records` as a raw record (`title: ""`, `date: null`, `fields: {[group_by]: value}` or `{}`), drops withheld ones and counts the rest. `privacy.Release` writes the single access-log row.
- Groups: count desc, then value asc as text (`String(value)`), `null` last; a number sorts before an equal-text string so the order never depends on map iteration.
- `analyst/domain/progress.go`: label «Contando registros…».
- Existing tools unchanged; the pinned tool counts in `mcp_args_test.go` move to 7/9.

## Specs covered

S3 (contract), S4 (privacy: switch off, `clear` only, restricted not counted, access log), S5 (Go half; parity cases are T3).

## Checks

- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./...` (apps/api-go, `SIPGES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` = throwaway loopback PostgreSQL from `scripts/agents/test-pg.sh`): all packages ok. `TestMCPCountRecords` and `TestMCPReadToolsAnswerNoDataWithTheSwitchOff` confirmed running (not skipped) with `-v`.
- RED first: `TestCountRecordsHasItsFixedSpanishLabel` and the four MCP integration tests failed with `Herramienta desconocida: count_records` before the implementation.
- `go vet ./...`: ok.
- `golangci-lint run ./...`: 0 issues.
- `prettier --check` on the changed JSON/mjs: ok after `--write` on `mcp.mjs`.
- `node apps/api-go/internal/integration/testdata/mcp.mjs --check`: exit 1, both files "drifted" — **expected**: the TypeScript `count_records` is not on this branch yet. It must pass once T1 lands; that is the seam check for T3.

Rules → tests (`apps/api-go/internal/app/mcp_integration_test.go`): (1) switch off / no data key via `mcpReads`; (2) total without `group_by`; (3) grouped, null last; (4) dates bound the count, undated and non-ISO records excluded, empty range; (5) dates on `actores`; (6) `2026-13`, `ayer`; (7) name (`Nombre_Actor/Organizacion`, `Actor_Principal`), text (`Descripcion_Hecho`), non-allowlisted (`Observaciones`); (8) a `restringido` record is not counted; (9) one access-log row per count, none for refusals.

## Descriptor generation

The TypeScript tool is not in this worktree, so a scratch harness outside the repo (`mktemp -d`, removed) imported the real `mcp-tools.ts`, built the exact S3 zod schema with the same `zod` instance that `apps/api` resolves, spliced the tool into `MCP_TOOLS` right after `get_timeline`, and then imported the real `mcp.mjs`, which rewrote `domain/mcp_tools.json` and `testdata/mcp.json`. `mcp.mjs` gets the `count_records` `FIELDS` entry (`module: "eventos"`, `group_by: "Tipo_Evento"`, `from: "2026"`, `to: "2026-12"`). Two runs produced byte-identical output. `mcp.json` diff is large because the seeded generator shifts every later tool's cases.

## Open points for T1/T3

- Check order of refusals in Go: unknown module → invalid dates → no date field → `group_by`. T1 should match, or parity will show it.
- Unknown module answers «Módulo no válido» (the existing wording in `create_record`).
- Group values keep the stored JSON type (a number stays a number), as the guard sanitises it.
- The 20000 cap / `truncated: true` has no test (it would need 20001 rows); a small unit test on the service with a fake store could be added in T3.

## Log entry proposal

`L<n>` — T2 done (Herdr tab `report-go`, PR #<this>): Go `count_records` in `integration/application/mcp_count.go`, `ontology` `Countable` (id, marking, field value; no SQL aggregate), descriptors regenerated through a scratch harness splicing the S3 schema into `MCP_TOOLS`; `go test ./...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` green against a throwaway PostgreSQL; `mcp.mjs --check` expected to pass only after T1 lands (seam check in T3). Risk: item 2 (egress guard), verified in T5.

## Why

The `eslint` CI job has failed on every recent pull request with the same 26 errors, so a red check meant nothing. This clears them: `npm run lint` now exits 0 (158 warnings remain, none blocking).

- `use-mobile.ts`: `useSyncExternalStore` instead of an effect that sets state. Still false on the server and for the first client render.
- `login/page.tsx`: the recovery email falls back to the account email as a derived value.
- `student/tutor/page.tsx`: removed a redundant message reset; every place that clears the active session already clears the messages.
- `teacher/submission/grade/page.tsx`, `teacher/network-students.tsx`: the "nothing to load" case no longer sets `loading` in an effect; the spinner condition accounts for it.
- `teacher/students/page.tsx`, `math-builder-modal.tsx`, `demo-carousel.tsx`, `navigation-chatbot.tsx`, `teacher/network/page.tsx` (limit drafts), `teacher/vault/page.tsx`: state that follows a prop or another value is adjusted during render (React's documented pattern) instead of in an effect.
- `motion/animated-sidebar.tsx` (2 errors): the trigger writes the ref it destructured rather than mutating the hook's return value.
- `__tests__/curriculum-tag.test.ts`: the `require` sits on the line its disable comment covers.

## Explained exceptions (12)

Each has an `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/set-state-in-effect -- reason` on the one line.

# Plan 579: Split success card shows month, date, package, tax and VER

Up from 20,500/0 — the suite total at the PR's base (Plan 578 merge #1506).

## What changed

The split success card (`renderSplitReceiptCardHtml`, the on-screen receipt
for the biggest counter payments) showed the total received, the customer,
the area, the remaining balance and the leg rows — but no billing month, no
payment date, no package, no tax and no VER reference, although the combined
object already carries all of them. A customer photographed the card could
not tell which month it settled. The single-payment card beside it already
showed all four.

- **Month row (D2(a)):** the month NAME via `monthName` (`'October'`) — the
  single card's form, so the two cards beside each other read alike. New
  import edge (`monthly-complaint-report.js`, heavy but cycle-free: it
  imports only complaint-register.js / downtime-analytics.js, neither of
  which leads back here). Half-width, directly after Area, conditional on
  `monthName` returning non-`''`.
- **Date row (D3(a)):** the payment date RAW (`'2026-10-29'`) — the
  sheet/draft form; `formatQcReceiptDate` cannot be imported (cycle:
  nav-quick-collect.js imports this module). Half-width, after Month,
  conditional on `combined.date`.
- **Package row (D4(a)):** `splitPackageDisplay(combined)` (`'3Mbps /
  100GB'`), half-width after Date, conditional on a non-empty package.
- **Tax row (D5(a)):** full-width before the legs, in the single-card
  form — `🧾 ${SALES_TAX_RECEIPT_LABEL}`, `PKR
  ${formatReceiptMoneyFigure(cents / 100)}`, no `+` prefix. The figure is
  the distinct-bill tax via `splitSalesTaxCents(combined)` — NEVER a
  per-leg sum (a naive sum prints double, PKR 390 for a PKR 195 bill tax).
  Conditional on `> 0`; an untaxed split shows no tax row.
- **VER (D1(b)):** per-leg stamps appended to each leg row value via
  `splitLegVerificationStamp` (the Plan 560 pattern, same module, no new
  import) — each stamp verifies via `verifyReceiptCode` for its own leg's
  facts. There is deliberately no combined receipt number to bind a
  combined code to, so no combined VER row. A leg without a receipt number
  shows no stamp.
- **D7(b) — the raw `Number(remaining)` formula is FIXED (566's R11
  hand-off, this PR owns it):** the still-owed figure is read through a
  finite-cents guard (a non-finite cents field falls through to the next
  finite field, defaulting to 0) and rendered via
  `formatReceiptMoneyFigure(remaining)` — the 566 single-card pattern
  (`firstFiniteRemainingPayable`) in cents. Whole-rupee figures print
  byte-identically; only the non-finite path changes (Infinity → hidden
  row, never "PKR ∞").
- **D8(a):** `'Still owed'` stays as-is.

No builder change, no sheet/draft change, no single-card change, no
caller change, no CSS/HTML/app.js change, no new i18n keys (hardcoded
labels, matching the sibling card — parity stays 4,675/4,675), no new hex,
no computation/figure change (the tax row only READS
`splitSalesTaxCents`). All new rows are conditional, so hand-built combined
objects without the fields render exactly as before.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| §2 line numbers re-verified on THIS base (508b433f) | All confirmed (card :981, builder :521, helpers :711/:723/:737, Number(remaining) :1042, monthName :179, caller :6405) |
| Repro BEFORE (real copy) | 17 pass / 5 fail (B1–B5 — the prep's exact prediction) |
| Neighbour baseline BEFORE (21 files) | 289/289, 0 fail |
| New test file `tests/plan579-split-card-month-date-package-tax-ver.test.js` (21 tests: G1 7, G2 3, G3 3, G4 6, G5 2) | 21/21, exit 0 |
| Focused + neighbours (24 files incl. new file + build-output + build-scanner-safety) | 323/323, exit 0 |
| Repro AFTER (real copy) | 22/22 PASS (B1–B5 flipped; A/C/D/E hold) |
| Full unit gate | 20,521/0 via the 4-chunk fallback (5,909 + 5,905 + 4,397 + 4,310; each chunk EXIT 0, 0 fail) — the single run was SIGTERM'd with a 0-byte log |
| Build gate | EXIT 0, dist 23 |
| D9 print-preview (headless Chromium, 360px) | Eyeballed — all four rows legible, tax PKR 195 once (absent when untaxed), per-leg VER legible, leg 2 wraps cleanly at the separator, no horizontal overflow on any card; measured heights recorded (see below) |
| CI test job 134577191948 | completed SUCCESS; log independently re-fetched (302-capture, signed URL, no auth): `UNIT 20521 pass / 0 fail / 20521 tests (1121 files)`, `Built static app in dist/ (23 bundled files)` |

## Fit record (D9, recorded not blessed)

Measured at 360px in headless Chromium (card height, before/after on the
same fixtures): taxed card 509px → **618px (+109px)**; untaxed card 509px
→ **573px (+64px)**. 552 arithmetic predicted +86px taxed / +43px untaxed
(Month+Date row +43, Package pairs with Next-due-date +0, Tax row +43);
the extra ~21–23px is the one wrapped leg line (leg 2's value wraps once
at the "·" separator when the VER stamp + TID are both present — legible,
no overflow). No row was shrunk to compensate.

## Disclosures

- **Terms block renders as an empty box in headless (pre-existing, NOT
  579):** the terms box below the leg rows renders empty in the headless
  screenshot on ALL FOUR cards including the base renders. The text IS in
  the HTML — the box uses `.qc-urdu-gradient` (background-clip: text with
  transparent colour inside @supports), which this headless Chromium build
  does not paint. Identical on base, so a pre-existing headless artifact;
  579 does not touch the terms block. On the phone the gradient text
  renders (polish17 precedent). The Urdu in the tax label renders visibly
  in the same screenshot (fallback font, no Noto Nastaliq in headless —
  the same pre-existing condition as 574/577/578 D8).
- **One test fix during the run:** the G2 cross-verification test first
  failed because it passed `paymentDate` to `verifyReceiptCode` — the
  verifier destructures `date`, not `paymentDate`. Fixed to `date: leg.date`
  (the key `receiptCodeForReceipt` itself maps to); re-ran green. No
  production code changed for it.
- **Full gate via the 4-chunk fallback:** the single `test-gate.mjs unit`
  run was SIGTERM'd mid-way with a 0-byte log (the established pattern);
  the four alphabetical chunks sum to exactly 20,521 = 20,500 + 21, with

- **Two re-pins, both by design with why-comments naming Plan 579:**
  `tests/qc-success-card-month-name.test.js:145` (asserts the `monthName`

author: tonypine
body:
## References

- Ticket: [TP-1544](https://linear.app/tonypine/issue/TP-1544/three-elixir-tests-that-fail-at-random-in-ci-pass-every-time)

## This PR

Nothing changes on screen. Three Elixir tests that failed at random in CI on unrelated changes now wait on the state they check instead of racing a timer. The races were in the tests, not in the code they test.

- The webhook setup cache's reload test and the setup checks' reload test used a debounce of zero or near zero and then read the server's state a fixed number of times, so a busy machine could fire the timer before or after the reads. Both now use a long debounce, confirm that the two events started a single timer, and fire that timer themselves.
- The agent processes ledger test slept 200 ms and hoped the grace timer had removed the stopped agent. It now waits until the server's state no longer holds the agent, then reads the ledger.

Each test passed 51 runs in a row with `--repeat-until-failure 50`, run alone: the run rules forbid generating load on the shared host, so each race was made deterministic instead of being reproduced under load.

author: dcsshiva
body:
Some phones showed a white screen. Before this change, `#root` stayed empty until a single 1.66 MB script had downloaded and started, so anything that stopped or slowed that script left a blank page.

## What changed
1. **Loading screen right away.**
   - `index.html` shows the logo and "Loading… · ஏற்றுகிறது…" while the app downloads.
   - The stylesheet no longer blocks the first paint. A small Vite plugin (`nonBlockingCssPlugin`) loads it with `media="print"` and switches it to `all` once loaded; `main.tsx` waits for `link#hr-css` before drawing, so nothing shows unstyled.
   - After 12 s, a "slow internet — wait or Reload" note appears.
2. **Start-up failures show a message instead of white.** A plain-ES5 safety net in `index.html` runs before the app:
   - script can't be downloaded → "Could not download the app";
   - error before the app starts → "The app could not start".
   - Both cards are bilingual and have Reload plus tips (internet, open in Chrome/Safari not WhatsApp, iPhone "Block All Cookies", update Chrome / Android System WebView).
   - A lazy chunk missing after an update triggers one reload (`vite:preloadError`).
3. **Blocked storage no longer stops the app.**
   - Affects iPhone "Block All Cookies" and some private / in-app browsers, where `localStorage` throws. Before, `forceVersionRefresh` threw before React mounted.
   - Now the app runs on in-memory storage and shows a dismissible note that sign-in won't be remembered, with the fix.
   - `forceVersionRefresh` is also guarded on its own.
4. **Smaller first download.**
   - `/classic`, `/classic/login`, `/help-guide` and `/unsubscribe` are `lazy()`.
   - jsPDF + autotable now load inside `payslipPDF` (port section 68).
   - Main bundle: **1.66 MB → 0.95 MB** (430 → 289 KB gzipped).
5. **Browsers too old for the app** (below Chrome 87 / iOS 14, or no ES modules) get "Please update your browser" with Android and iPhone steps.

## Tested (real build, Playwright, Pixel 5 emulation)
| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | app in 1 s | app in 1 s |
| Storage blocked | **blank** | app + storage note |
| Slow 3G (400 kbps) | **white for 36 s** | loading screen at 1 s, slow note at 13 s, app at 24 s |
| Script can't be parsed (old browser) | blank | "Please update your browser" |
| Script fails to download | blank | "Could not download the app" + Reload |
| Script throws at start | blank | "The app could not start" + Reload |

- Payslip PDF still downloads (lazy jsPDF).
- tsc is clean, 98 node tests pass and the vite build is clean.

author: speech115
body:
## Why

Goal: stop drawing FloodWaits. On 2026-11-17 `archive backfill --private` on `main` drew a `FLOOD_WAIT` of 85165 s (about 23.6 h), and `recklessou` one of about 23 h.

The private walk already holds each dialog's entity, but passed only an `@username` ref to `backfill_one`, which resolved it again. Telethon's `get_entity("@name")` always sends `contacts.ResolveUsername`, and Telegram caps that at about 200 a day. 465 of the 544 dialogs backfilled that day had an `@` ref. No `FLOOD_WAIT:` row landed in `sync_state`, so the flood hit in the resolve step, before history was read.

## What changes

`enumerate_private_dialogs` also returns the entities it walked, and `backfill_private` passes them through `backfill_dialogs` into `backfill_one`, which resolves only when no entity was given. The explicit-CHAT path is unchanged. The JSON keeps `chat` as `@username`, so CONTRACT.md is untouched.

## Proof

`scripts/repro.py`:
```
FAILS ON BASE	tests.test_cli_archive_phase3::test_backfill_private_reuses_walked_dialog_entities
FAILS ON BASE	tests.test_cli_archive_phase3::test_private_backfill_does_not_skip_delta_only_state
2 of 48 changed tests fail on origin/main
```
(The second fails on base only because the internal function now returns four values.)

`scripts/mutate.py`:
```
killed	src/tgcli/archive/backfill.py:47	entities is not None -> (entities is None)
killed	src/tgcli/archive/backfill.py:103	entity is None -> (entity is not None)
0 of 2 survived
```

Live, on `main` while its `ResolveUsername` flood was still running (it ends around 2026-11-18 12:40 UTC):
`tg --account main --json archive backfill --private --max-dialogs 3 --limit 1` exited 0 with `stored: 3`; 2 of the 3 dialogs had an `@username` ref. On 2026-11-17 the same command on `main` exited 5 within about 30 s on each of 17 runs.

Gate: `gate: all checks passed` (run with `UV_NO_CONFIG=1`; the global uv `exclude-newer` breaks `uv lock --check` on this Mac regardless of this change).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Telegram API usage on the private backfill hot path; behavior for explicit CHAT args is unchanged, but incorrect entity pairing could mis-target peers.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Private `archive backfill --private` no longer re-resolves `@username` refs** after the dialog walk already has each peer’s Telethon entity. That second step used `contacts.ResolveUsername`, which Telegram caps (~200/day) and which recently triggered multi-hour `FLOOD_WAIT`s before history fetch even started.
> 
> `enumerate_private_dialogs` now returns the **entities collected during `iter_dialogs`**, and `backfill_private` threads them through optional `entities` on `backfill_dialogs` into `backfill_one`, which calls `resolve_entity` only when no entity was supplied. **Explicit CHAT backfill is unchanged** (still resolves refs). JSON output still uses `chat` as `@username`.
> 
> A regression test asserts private backfill succeeds when `get_entity` would fail, proving walked entities are reused.

A runner uses the state backend that a job names.

Ran: `go test ./internal/runner/ ./internal/dispatch/`, `make lint-core`. `scripts/verify/fresh-run.sh` on this commit: thirteen work items, twelve in `Done` and `WI-0005` in `RolledBack`, the chain verified at 316 events, no error line, no `agent.failed` event.

The first full run on this commit failed: Docker refused to start the container of the local cluster (`docker run` ended with status 125) in the apply of `20-cluster`. The second run on the same commit passed. The cause is not known.

author: tomassasovsky
body:
Closes #1843. The console's Wi-Fi, network settings and connectivity now follow Raspberry Pi OS: NetworkManager drives the radio through wpa_supplicant, with Pi OS's files, and the image differs only where the A/B appliance needs it. The full table, with sources, is in `docs/NETWORK_PARITY.md`; it is repeated below.

**Not built in CI.** The main workflow does not build the image, so the recipe changes (two new bbappends for wpa-supplicant and avahi, a changed networkmanager bbappend, the bundle recipe) have only static checks. The image needs an appliance-release run, and then `deploy/rpi/verify-network-on-device.sh` on the console.

## What changed

- **Backend.** The networkmanager bbappend no longer enables `PACKAGECONFIG iwd`, so NetworkManager uses its default backend, wpa_supplicant, and `networkmanager-wifi` depends on wpa-supplicant. `PACKAGE_EXCLUDE += "iwd"` fails the build if anything brings iwd back.
- **Removed, iwd only:** `iwd-main.conf`, `segno-iwd-tame` and its unit, `wifi.backend=iwd` and `wifi.iwd.autoconnect=no` (with the rest of `99-segno-wifi.conf`), the wpa_supplicant mask.
- **Removed, replaced by Pi OS's mechanism:** `segno-wifi-regdom`, its unit and `/etc/segno/wifi-country`; the country is now `cfg80211.ieee80211_regdom=AR` on the kernel command line, as raspi-config writes it.
- **Removed, obsolete:** `segno-wifi-ctl`'s repair of consoles from before #468 (killing a stale fallback supplicant, `managed yes`), its `iw ... power_save off` call, and the per-profile `powersave=2` on new profiles (the global setting covers them).
- **Added from Pi OS, word for word:** Debian's `NetworkManager.conf`; Debian's `wpa_supplicant.service` (`-u -s -O "DIR=/run/wpa_supplicant GROUP=netdev"`, enabled), D-Bus activation file and D-Bus policy, with a `netdev` group; Debian's `no-mac-addr-change.conf`; raspberrypi-net-mods' `rpi-no-scan-rand-mac-address.conf`; raspberrypi-sys-mods' `rfkill_default.conf`; raspi-config's `default-wifi-powersave-off.conf`; pi-gen's Avahi `publish-workstation=yes`. wpa_supplicant is built with every option Debian adds to upstream's defconfig, except three (below). `dnsmasq.service` is no longer enabled (dnsmasq bbappend): Pi OS ships only the program.
- **NetworkManager's state on /data.** `var-lib-NetworkManager.mount` binds `/data/NetworkManager/state` at `/var/lib/NetworkManager`, so the Wi-Fi switch, each profile's last-connected time and the IPv6 secret survive an update, as they do on Pi OS. `segno-nm-persist` is now a unit that creates both `/data` directories and keeps keyfiles 0600.
- **Why a join failed.** `segno-wifi-ctl connect` reads wpa_supplicant's journal lines for the attempt (`-t wpa_supplicant -t NetworkManager`, from the attempt's cursor). `wrong-password` only after `WPA: 4-Way Handshake failed - pre-shared key may be incorrect` (wpa_supplicant 2.11 `events.c`) whose disconnect came from the access point with reason 15 (4-way handshake timeout), 14 (MIC failure) or 23; wpa_supplicant writes the same line for any drop during the handshake, its own timeout and a router restarting mid-join included, and those are `no-connection`. `not-found` from nmcli's error or NetworkManager's `reason 'ssid-not-found'`, `no-address` from `ip-config-unavailable`, both only from NetworkManager's lines about this join's activation on wlan0, and `no-connection` for the rest, including `CTRL-EVENT-ASSOC-REJECT ... status_code=16` (#1816) and `Authentication with ... timed out.` (#470). NetworkManager's `no-secrets` is still not evidence. The app's four messages are unchanged.
- **segno-wifi-retry** stays, with its rationale rewritten for wpa_supplicant (below).
- **Tests.** `run_wifi_join_error_tests.sh` uses wpa_supplicant 2.11 and NetworkManager 1.50 line shapes. New `run_network_config_tests.sh` checks every Pi OS file word for word, that nothing of iwd is left, that the bundle recipe's SRC_URI and `files/` match, and the saved-network path; in CI it also loads a keyfile shaped like the console's with `nmcli --offline` (network-manager is installed there with a `policy-rc.d` so it does not start). The cmdline test checks the regulatory domain. `run_wifi_regdom_tests.sh` is gone with its script.
- **Docs.** `docs/NETWORK_PARITY.md` (new), `docs/RUNNING_ON_RPI.md`, `deploy/yocto/README.md` (it said no Avahi ships; Avahi runs and the console answers as `segno.local`), `docs/PROGRESS.md`.

## Raspberry Pi OS against the image

Sources:

| Short name | Source |
|---|---|
| RPI | `archive.raspberrypi.com/debian`, trixie and bookworm `main/binary-arm64/Packages` (Release of 2026-11-17) |
| IMG | `2026-10-06-raspios-trixie-arm64-lite.info`, the package list of the current image (pi-gen `b2cd98a9`) |
| NM-D | Debian network-manager packaging, salsa.debian.org/utopia-team/network-manager, tag `debian/1.52.1-1` (`e0a3970c`) |
| WPA-D | Debian wpa packaging, salsa.debian.org/debian/wpa, tag `debian/2%2.10-24` (`2414487d`) |
| SM | github.com/RPi-Distro/raspberrypi-sys-mods, `pios/trixie` (`15fa4481`, 1:20260914) |
| NETM | github.com/RPi-Distro/raspberrypi-net-mods, `pios/trixie` (`9f03eb4a`, 1.4.4) |
| RC | github.com/RPi-Distro/raspi-config, `trixie` (`22cea75e`, 20261026+2) |
| PG | github.com/RPi-Distro/pi-gen, `arm64` (`c0d2c9f2`) |
| FW | github.com/RPi-Distro/firmware-nonfree (`2788cb5`, `rpi-brcmfmac.conf`) |
| NM | NetworkManager 1.50.0 source (`src/core/nm-manager.c`, `nm-policy.c`, `devices/wifi/nm-device-wifi.c`), the version the image runs |
| WPA | wpa_supplicant 2.11 source (`wpa_supplicant/events.c`, `wpa_supplicant.c`), the version the image runs |


### Packages

| Item | Raspberry Pi OS trixie | Image | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| NetworkManager | network-manager 1.52.1-1+rpt4 (RPI, IMG) | NetworkManager 1.50.0 (meta-networking walnascar) | deviates: the version comes with the pinned Yocto release. Same upstream project. The `+rpt4` delta adds netplan, which Pi OS uses for Imager's cloud-init first boot; the console has no such first boot. |
| wpa_supplicant | wpasupplicant 2:2.10-24+rpt3 (RPI, IMG) | wpa_supplicant 2.11 (poky walnascar) | deviates: the version comes with the pinned Yocto release. Same upstream project, one release newer. |
| iwd | not installed, not in the archive (IMG, RPI) | not installed; `PACKAGE_EXCLUDE += "iwd"` fails the build if anything pulls it in | changed to match (the image ran NetworkManager on iwd since #470) |
| iw, wireless-regdb | iw 6.9, wireless-regdb 2026.05.30 (IMG) | iw 6.9, wireless-regdb-static 2025.02.20 | deviates: wireless-regdb's version comes with the Yocto release. Same signed `regulatory.db`. |
| firmware-brcm80211 | 1:20260519-1~bpo13+1+rpt2 (RPI) | linux-firmware-rpidistro 20230625-2+rpt3 | matches: the 43455 firmware, clm_blob and nvram are byte-identical (#1818) |

### NetworkManager

| Item | Raspberry Pi OS trixie | Image | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wi-Fi backend | wpa_supplicant: NetworkManager's default; Debian's `rules` does not set `config_wifi_backend_default`, and no file sets `wifi.backend` (NM-D) | the same: the recipe's `wifi` option without `iwd`, no `wifi.backend` anywhere | changed to match (was `wifi.backend=iwd`, `wifi.iwd.autoconnect=no`) |
| Build options | Debian's meson flags, iwd support compiled but unused, internal DHCP client (NM-D `debian/rules`) | the recipe's PACKAGECONFIG: wifi, nmcli, ifupdown, dnsmasq, nss, systemd; internal DHCP client | deviates: iwd support is not compiled (it is unused on Pi OS too); no ModemManager, Bluetooth or PPP plugins, since the console has no modem and no Bluetooth (#1199) |
| `/etc/NetworkManager/NetworkManager.conf` | `plugins=ifupdown,keyfile`, `[ifupdown] managed=false` (NM-D) | the same file, word for word (networkmanager bbappend) | changed to match (the image had none) |
| `/etc/network/interfaces` | absent: pi-gen excludes ifupdown (PG `scripts/common`) | absent | matches |
| Scan MAC randomisation | `/usr/lib/NetworkManager/conf.d/rpi-no-scan-rand-mac-address.conf`: `wifi.sca

## 무엇을

시연의 날짜 이동을 서버가 아니라 **프론트 목업**에서 하기로 한 결정(D-12, 2026-11-18)을 문서·배포·API에 반영합니다.

**왜:** 앱 시계는 하나(D-08)라, 발표자가 `PUT /demo/clock`으로 날짜를 옮기면 그 순간 심사위원이 새로 만든 계정의 날짜도 같이 옮겨집니다. "처음부터 출시 그대로 체험"과 "며칠 걸리는 장면 보여 주기"를 한 서버에서 함께 할 수 없습니다. 목업에는 시연 시드·시계·대기부터 모드·초대 코드가 이미 있습니다.

| 장면 | 어디서 |
| --- | --- |
| 처음 열기 → 닉네임 → 동의 → 기분 → 미션 → 다 했어요 → 그룹·도움받기 | **실서버**(`SITE_ADDRESS`), 새 계정으로 라이브. 심사위원도 직접 |

author: davidaventimiglia-professional
body:
Closes #1451.

## The defect

When retention stops reaching a still-attached retirement and the `pgpm_detach` job does not appear to hold its detach, `_retain_recall` cleared the mark at once. Two readings of "does not hold" were wrong. In both, the job then ran the detach after the mark was gone, and the rows left the parent with nothing recording it:

1. **pg_cron's cache.** pg_cron starts a run with the command it has cached. An idle (a `pgpm.schedule()` re-run) reaches that cache only after it commits. In the same transaction as `set_retain` and `retain()`, the recall read the idle, and a run carrying the detach landed once the transaction committed.
2. **Row security.** pg_cron keeps a `pgpm_detach` job for each role that ran `pgpm.schedule()` and shows a role only its own. A tick run as the table's owner, with the jobs scheduled by an administrator, read no job (or could not read `cron.job` at all) as an idle job.

## The fix (the design agreed on the issue)

The not-armed branch now treats a retirement pgpm dispatched (`detach_dispatched_oid` set) differently. An undispatched mark is still cleared at once, as before.

- **Who can read the job.** With pg_cron installed, "no job holds it" is a reading only for a superuser (who sees every job) or for the one non-superuser role whose job holds the detach. A non-superuser's dispatch arms its own job, a superuser's every one. The new column `pgpm.part.retiring_by` records that role:
  - written by the tick that makes a new mark (a retry on an older mark leaves it null);
  - kept by the first dispatch of this release's mark and by that role's re-dispatches;
  - nulled by another role's re-dispatch, since two jobs may then hold the detach.

  A tick as any other role keeps the mark and logs `fail_retain_recall`, counted in `status().retain_drop_failures`, naming its role and the role to run as (or a superuser, when no one role is recorded). So does a non-superuser's tick on a mark older than this release, which an older pgpm may have dispatched (an upgrade run by a role that could not read the job leaves no record). A mark this release made whose dispatch was refused (`retiring_by` set, nothing dispatched) is held by no job and is cleared at once by any tick, as before. Without pg_cron nothing can run a detach, and the reading stands for anyone.
- **Job read idle: wait, then clear.** The first tick that reads the job idle records its transaction in `pgpm.part.recall_idle_xact`. A tick for which that transaction is no longer in progress (so the idle it read has committed) starts the clock in `recall_idle_at`. A tick a minute after that clears the mark, provided the #652 signals still show no run of the detach. A run that lands during the wait finds the mark kept, and #1438's recall releases the table, logged and counted.

Why the transaction and not just a later tick: the first reading can happen in the idle's own transaction (V-02's shape), and so can a second `retain()`. A clock started inside that transaction would count from before the idle committed, so a transaction that ran longer than the minute would let the very next tick clear the mark while pg_cron's cache still held the detach. Parts K and N test that.

The idle state is cleared everywhere the mark is cleared (`_disown_retirement`, `_disown_foreign_mark`, the recall's own clear) and by every dispatch (`retire()`'s record of it). So a clock never carries over from one dispatch to the next (part M).

## Sites

| Site | Role | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_retain_recall`, not armed and attached, dispatched | cleared the mark | changed: kept and counted unless the tick is a superuser or the one role whose job holds it; otherwise transaction, clock, and clear a minute on |
| `_retain_recall`, not armed and attached, undispatched | clears the mark | unchanged for a mark this release made (dispatch refused). Changed for a mark older than this release, with pg_cron: a non-superuser's tick keeps it, counted; a superuser's waits out the idle (transaction, clock, a minute) as for a dispatched mark (round 3, V-01) |
| `retire()`, the mark write | marks the retirement | also records `retiring_by` on a new mark only |
| `_retain_recall`, armed / landed / pending / identity branches | #1438's design | unchanged. A role that cannot see the job reads it as not armed and takes the branch above |
| `_retain_recall`, landed, release's `_idle_detach_job` | idles the job, releases the table | changed (round 2, V-01): only a tick that reads the job holding the detach (the same rule) releases it, since only it can return that job to idle. Any other keeps the mark, the table out of the parent, counted. The release's check now says to run it as a superuser |
| `retire()`, record of the dispatch | sets `detach_dispatched_oid` | also keeps or nulls `retiring_by` (above) and clears the idle state |
| `_disown_retirement`, `_disown_foreign_mark` | clear the mark | also clear `retiring_by` and the idle state |
| `_detach_job_holds` (install pass) | seeds an older install's record when the job holds the detach | unchanged. Unreadable reads as "does not hold", which leaves no record; the recall now keeps such a mark for a non-superuser (round 1, V-02) instead of clearing it. Records it seeds carry no role, so only a superuser's tick reads them. A mark it leaves unrecorded waits out the idle under a superuser's tick too (round 3, V-01), since an older pgpm may have dispatched it |
| `forget()`, read of the job | idles a forgotten table's detach | unchanged here. Run by a non-superuser it can leave another role's job armed, which detaches a re-created table's same-named partition (round 2, V-02): filed as #1461 by the maintainer's choice |
| `_retain_recall`, landed, no record of the dispatch (#705's disown) | disowns the mark, idles the job it sees | changed (round 4, V-01): asks the same reading first, so with pg_cron a non-superuser keeps a mark older than this release (`fail_retain_recall`, counted) rather than release a table another role's job may take out again |
| `retire()`, pending or detached under a mark with no record (#705) | disowns the mark, idles the job it sees | changed (round 4, V-01's sibling): with pg_cron, a non-superuser keeps a mark older than this release, logs `fail_retain_drop`, counted, and drops nothing (`_unrecorded_mark_unread`) |
| `_detach_reap`, pending under a mark with no record (#705) | disowns the mark before the FINALIZE | changed (round 4): the same mark is kept for `retire()`, which refuses it; the FINALIZE still runs |
| `_disown_unvouched_retirements` (install pass), pending or detached with no record | disowns the mark | changed (round 4): skips the same mark, leaving it to a superuser's tick |
| `_dispatch_detach` | counts the `alter_job` rows the caller sees | unchanged. Unseen reads as no job, which logs `fail_retain_detach`, counted |
| `status()` | counts the failures | adds `fail_retain_recall` (exact value) |

Size: core +5,487, archive 0, hypertable 0 (minified, against `main` `340b8988`, whose core is `51d6e30`'s). Round 1's fixes added 1,318 of it, round 2's 889, round 3's 25, round 4's 1,713.

Why this size: past the 4,700 line, by the four rounds of verification. Each refusal this PR adds has to say who may settle it and how, at its own site: the recall's two `fail_retain_recall` messages, `retire()`'s `fail_retain_drop` for an older mark, and the dispatch-role bookkeeping (`retiring_by`, the idle columns and their clears at five sites). The one rule they share, "with pg_cron only a superuser reads an older mark's job", lives in one helper (`_unrecorded_mark_unread`) and in the recall's `v_read`, rather than being restated per site. About a third of the growth (1,699 of 5,487 characters, measured on the minified diff's string literals) is message text the operator reads; the rest is the reading rule, the wait, and the bookkeeping and clears of the three new columns.

body:
C20 PR 2: skill traits on the server, built to docs/tech/skill-traits.md. Each active skill that takes points gets a default and an extra; the extra opens at the skill's last evolution. A player chooses a trait out of combat. The world uses every skill with the player's trait.

## What it does

- **Data:** the 29 traits from §3 go under each skill's last stage in `skills.yaml`, and `actions.yaml` gains `combat: 5s`.
  - The loader resolves the extra on top of the last stage with the stages' own merge and checks. It refuses everything §2 lists.
  - `Skill.TraitOpen(points)`, `Skill.Trait(id)` and `Skill.Spec(points, trait)` sit beside `StageAt`.
- **Choosing:** `ChooseTrait{skill, trait}` gets a Response and shares the skill points' rate limit. The world refuses, in this order:
  1. `CHARACTER_DEAD`;
  2. `SKILL_NOT_LEARNED`;
  3. `TRAIT_UNKNOWN` (330036);
  4. `TRAIT_LOCKED` (330038);
  5. `IN_COMBAT` (330037).

  Otherwise it sets the trait, sends a `StatsChanged` and saves at once. The trait already chosen answers OK and changes nothing.
- **In combat:** a player stays in combat for 5 s of ticks after each `Damage` naming them, dealt or taken. The world stamps both sides as the tick's events go out. A join or a map change starts out of combat, and a town has no `Damage`, so a town needs no check of its own.
- **Uses:** every use resolves with `Spec`: shape, targets, power, status, move, dodge, cooldown, energy, buff and the tick check.
  - A use waiting for its turn keeps the trait it was pressed with.
  - A buff keeps its trait beside its points, on the caster and on each party member it reaches. The trait goes through the handoff, the checkpoint (`character_skill_timers.trait`) and a fresh join's sheet, and `on_hit` reads it.
  - A trait saved but not open yet, or one the skill no longer has, is used as the default.
  - `SkillUsed.trait` says which extra was used.
- **Stored:** migration 00010 adds `trait text not null default ''` to `character_skills` and `character_skill_timers`. A trait the data no longer has is kept and saved back as it was, as a skill the data no longer has always was; play uses the default in its place. Refusing it made the whole checkpoint fail after a data change that renames or removes a trait.
- **The wire:**
  - `ChooseTrait` is ClientMessage field 31.
  - `SkillPoints.traits`, `SkillTimer.trait` and `SkillUsed.trait` are new.
  - The three new codes go through the error chain, `codes.json` and `errors.ts`.
- **The generator** writes each skill's traits, the extra with its resolved stage, and `actions.combat_ms`. `server/testdata/traits/extras.json` holds the loader's extras in the generator's form. A Go test writes and checks it, and `gamedata.test.ts` checks the generator against the same file.
- **The harness** logs each fight's damage a second, and each boss's minutes, on every extra beside the defaults.
- **Docs:** an "As built: PR 2" note in skill-traits.md §10.

## Tests

- **Loader:**
  - every refusal;
  - the extra on top of the last stage, in the fixture and the shipped data: Concussion, Puncture, Blur, Iron Wall, Fury, Ice Arrow, Dive, Ice Prison;
  - `TraitOpen` and `Spec` one point short of the last stage, at it, and from the first point of a skill with one stage;
  - the 29 skills with traits.
- **World:**
  - the refusals in order, in and out of combat, and dead;
  - set and saved, and the trait already chosen;
  - the combat clock from a hit taken only (one player) and from a hit dealt only (another). It lets a choice through exactly 100 ticks after the last of them.
  - the town right after a fight;
  - Concussion stunning and its 7 s cooldown, against the default;
  - a waiting use keeping its trait;
  - a buff keeping Expose through a change, its on-hit armour break, the checkpoint and a fresh join;
  - a stored trait not open, or unknown, used as the default;
  - a join's sheet with Fury's running buff;
  - the tick check over an extra.
- **Character:** the round trip in the service, the adapter and Postgres, where a changed trait rewrites the row. Traits the data lacks, on a skill and on a buff's timer, save as they were.
- **Gateway:** `ChooseTrait` routed as the sender, and `IN_COMBAT` answered.
- **End to end:** `TestATraitOpensAtTheLastStageAndWaitsOutAFight`.
  - A Beginner is refused Concussion at 24 points, chooses it at 25, and Crushing Blow stuns a slime.
  - A change mid-fight is refused with `IN_COMBAT`.
  - The player walks back out of sight along the chase's own trail, and the change goes through 101–111 ticks after the last fight event, over 11 local runs. It is judged by the world's ticks: the choice that went through was at least 100 ticks after the last `Damage` naming the player, and no try sent after a frame that late was refused.
- **Mutation checks:** 40 rules broken one at a time, and each was caught by its test. That covers the refusal order, both sides of the stamp, the clock's boundary, every place a use reads the stage, the buff's trait at each hop, the loader's checks, the service, the SQL `WHERE`, and each wire conversion. Breaking the generator's merge fails `gamedata.test.ts`. Three wire conversions were only caught after I added their trait to the outbox and Welcome tests. One defensive clone in `chooseTrait` survived its mutation: the sheet and the checkpoint already copy the map, and nothing else holds it, so I removed the clone.

author: yueranyuan
body:
## What broke

On the MacBook (volter-org install, 2026-11-18), a kit owner and its stack died of SIGBUS while the stack's native gateway kept running. The gateway (`hermes-gateway … orchestrator.mjs --root <home>`, pid 19514) was orphaned (parent 1) and kept the home's gateway lock. Every later stack's gateway logged `<home> is served by pid 19514` and waited for the claim. The kit owner's readiness check (`install-owner.ts`, 8 s) failed with `prepared kit stack did not answer its owned readiness door` and restarted the stack. This looped for about an hour, so the kit owner stayed `transitioning` and every release was refused. It ended only when `supercode orchestrator stop --root <home>` was run by hand.

## Cause

The keeper's design is that its children end with it ("When any of them ends, all of them end"). It does this with signal and exit handlers, which cannot run when the keeper is killed abruptly (SIGKILL, SIGBUS). Supercode's runtime records the other half: a second daemon on a home waits for the claim and serves once the first is gone. So nothing ever ended a gateway whose stack had died.

## Fix

A prepared stack is the one stack its kit owner runs, and that owner holds the home alone (`kit-owner.sqlite`). So an orchestrator already serving the home when a prepared stack starts is one an earlier stack left behind. Before starting its own gateway, the stack reads `supercode orchestrator status --root <home> --json`. If the state is `up`, it ends that orchestrator through its own stop door (`supercode orchestrator stop --root <home> --json`) and says so. If the door fails, the stack says why and starts its gateway anyway, and the home's gateway lock still decides who serves the home, as before. Hermes stacks and stacks that are not prepared are unchanged: they have no exclusive kit owner, so this argument does not hold for them.

The keeper's header line about children ending with the stack is edited in place to describe the abrupt case.

## Verification

I read both sides: `keeper/start.ts` and `keeper/install-owner.ts` here, and supercode's `sdk/orchestrator/bin/runtime.mjs`, `daemon-control.mjs` and `packaging/npm/lib/orchestrator-lifecycle.mjs`. A stop receipt of `stopped` is sent only after the daemon has cleared its lease and released the gateway lock. `bun build --no-bundle` transpiles the file cleanly. Following the repository rule, no tests were run.

## Summary

`__add_access_ids()` left an access method without `access_id` when the generated identifier duplicated one of an earlier access method of the same object. It now draws again until the identifier is unique within the object, at most 10 times per access method (`retries=9`, like the object identifiers); when the attempts run out, it logs an error and raises `InternalServerError` (500), before anything is written to the database.

Docs: none changed. The README already says that access methods get random identifiers; uniqueness within an object was the intended behaviour, and the 500 only occurs with id settings that leave fewer possible identifiers than access methods per object (e.g. `id_charset: "a"`, `id_length: 1`). The scope was kept to `register_objects.py` and its tests, as other PRs edit the docs in parallel.

Goal: remove the drift and MCP N+1 reads seen in production traces, and add a standing per-request query budget with labelled DB spans, so the next N+1 shows without an audit.

## What changed

- **`/v1/tasks/drift`:** the merged-without-deploy class reads a page's deploy records in one statement, not one scan per PR (114 per request in production). The statement is the per-PR predicate of `deployRecordForPRTx` once per PR, with the same membership test (`deployedPRs`), so the judgement is unchanged.
- **MCP `task_search` and the duplicate-candidate path:** hits are read in one batch (`TasksWithSpawns`: the summary fields and the spawn record), not one `GetTask` per hit (about six statements each).
- **Query budget:** telemetry counts the statements a request runs and logs `db.query_budget_exceeded route=… count=… budget=…` over `QueryBudget` (50). The count is per request context.
- **Span labels:** every DB span carries a label: the explicit one (`telemetry.Label`), else the verb and first table (`select tasks`). Sentry keeps the label as the span description and no longer receives the statement text; its scrubber already dropped everything except `db.system` and `db.rows_affected`.
- **OTLP:** the default route group is now `reads`: task routes, `/v1/search`, the console (`/ui/`) and `/mcp`. `HANDOFFKEEP_OTLP_ROUTES=tasks` restores the old set.
- **Tests:** `testdb.AssertQueryBudget` runs read routes under the budget: drift, task get, console attention and work-status, MCP task_get, operator_attention, decisions_pending, task_search.

## Acceptance (closed contract)

1. `go test ./internal/telemetry/ ./internal/testdb/` passes locally (no database needed). Covers: the budget line (`TestQueryBudgetLogsRouteOverBudget`), the per-request count (`TestQueryCountCountsEveryStatement`), and the span label (`TestQuerySpanCarriesLabel`).
2. `go test ./internal/store/ ./internal/mcp/` passes locally. Its PostgreSQL tests skip without `HANDOFFKEEP_TEST_DB_URL`. Those, run in CI: `TestDriftMergedWithoutDeployReadsAPageInOneStatement` (at most 2 statements for 40 PRs), `TestReadRoutesWithinQueryBudget`, `TestTaskSearchReadsHitsInOneBatch` (statement count equal for 1 and 40 hits), `TestMCPReadToolsWithinQueryBudget`.
3. `TestDeployRecordsForPRsBindEveryPlaceholder` passes locally: each batched statement binds exactly its arguments, for PostgreSQL and MySQL.

author: silver2dream
body:
The first part of the workbench: `awkit ui` opens a page on this computer that shows where the work is, without the terminal. This part only shows; planning, approving and starting work come in the next parts.

## What a person gets

- **Overview**: the line from the brief to the merge (需求 → 議會 → 工單 → 寫程式 → 審查 → 合併). Each ticket is a token on it; a stuck one sits on a yellow siding. Below: what needs the person, what just happened, tickets merged, the run, the milestones.
- **需要你處理**: stuck tickets, plans waiting for approval, what `awkit status` warns of.
- **工作看板**, **活動紀錄** (all, by who, or only warnings and errors), and a ticket's sheet: its history, what it waits for, its issue and pull request on GitHub (told apart: 工單 #306, PR #313).
- **健康檢查**: `awkit doctor`, both halves, asked in the project's own folder.
- **你的專案**: add, open, take out (the folder is not touched).
- **Teaching**: a welcome with three ways out — a 6-step spotlight tour (Esc pauses it at its step), skip all teaching (undo in the toast), or only the checklist. The checklist ticks itself as the person does things. Help brings any of it back, with a glossary. Progress is kept in the person's own settings file (`%AppData%\awkit\workbench.json`), not in the project or the browser.
- Ctrl K finds a page or a ticket; `?` opens help. Light and dark. Works from 390 px wide up.

Yellow is kept for one meaning, "this needs you"; a warning is orange. Where GitHub cannot be asked, the page says it does not know, not that nothing is stuck.

## Changes

- `web/`: the page (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, Vite 8), built into `internal/workbench/dist` and embedded. Only `dist/.keep` is committed; an awkit built without the page still builds and says so.
- `internal/kickoff`, `internal/doctor`: the pre-flight checker can be put `In` a project folder (git and gh are asked there); the "what a run needs" half of the doctor moves from `cmd/awkit` to `internal/doctor` so the workbench and `awkit doctor` run the same checks. Nothing changes for `awkit run` or `awkit doctor`.
- `internal/workbench`: health returns both halves; a file of an earlier build is a 404 rather than the page; tickets carry their GitHub address (`internal/status`).
- CI: a `workbench_page` job (npm ci, typecheck, vitest, build, then checks awkit serves that page and every file it names). Release: the page is built once and embedded into each platform's awkit; a build without it fails.
- Docs: `docs/user/workbench.md`, README (both), architecture, contributing.

## Verification

All outside this repository; the repository itself was not used for any run.

- `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` (Windows): pass. New tests: the checker asks the folder it was put in (`TestPreflightChecker_In`), the health endpoint asks the project's folder and returns both halves (`TestHealth`), the built page and every file it names are served (`TestAssets_TheBuiltPage`).
- `web`: 27 vitest tests (routing, event wording, times, every onboarding transition incl. undo, the app's entry states). Breaking the code 10 ways one at a time: all 10 caught.
- Click-through in Chrome (Playwright) against a stand-in server with every ticket stage, in the session's scratch folder — 17 scenarios, all pass: the welcome (Esc and outside clicks do not close it), every tour step at 1440×1000, 1366×768 and 390×844 (spotlight on its target, the card inside the window and off the target, focus kept in the card, arrows, Esc pause and resume, skip and undo, finish), the checklist ticking itself, help, glossary, palette, theme, every page, project switching, add and remove, routing, a locked page, the live stream, the mobile menu, dark mode, and no page scrolling sideways at any size.
- Every visible button and link on all six pages clicked one by one: each does something (dead-control scan).
- The real `awkit ui` on a copy of a test project in the scratch folder: the key leaves the address and becomes an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie; a browser without it, or with a wrong key, is refused; an event a run writes shows without reloading; the health page lists the same 12 checks `awkit doctor` prints in that folder.

Found and fixed while verifying: a ticket opened from the palette could not be closed with Esc for ~0.2 s (the closing palette took it) — menu actions now run once the menu is gone; the board's last column was cut at 1366 px; warnings used the "needs you" yellow; the mobile menu stayed open over the tour; the health page showed only half of `awkit doctor`; where GitHub could not be asked, the page said nothing was stuck.

Found by code scanning on the server of the first commit, and fixed (with tests): `events?session=../../x` read another file of the project — a session is now looked up among the files runs left; the address with the key redirected to the path it came with, so `//elsewhere?token=…` went to another site — it goes to `/` now; a project added from the page could be a relative path, taken from wherever awkit ran — it must be a full path now. One warning is left on purpose: the cookie has no `Secure` flag. The workbench speaks plain http on 127.0.0.1 only, and some browsers refuse a `Secure` cookie there, which would lock the person out.

## Notes

- `npm audit` reports picomatch (ReDoS, every version, no fix yet) through vite and vitest. It runs only while building, on the repository's own globs; nothing of it is in the page. The shadcn CLI, which pulled in most of the other advisories, is no longer a dependency: its stylesheet is kept in `web/src/styles/shadcn.css`.
- Check messages of `awkit doctor` and server errors are shown in English, as the commands print them.
- Next parts: planning with the council in the page; starting and stopping runs (a run started from the page goes on when the page is closed, and stops only when done or when someone stops it); settings and new projects.

author: huntrw6
body:
## What changes for the operator
Song cards used to say `Ab (was C)` whenever the key differed from the original recording. Now a card shows just the key (`Ab`), and `Ab (was G)` **only** when the key was changed in Playback in the last 24 hours (G = the key before that change). The hover says it in words: "Key changed in Playback from G to Ab in the last day". The words go away by themselves when the day is over (no reload).

## How
- **Backend** (`crates/stagepilot-playback/src/key_watch.rs` is the table, `crates/stagepilot-server/src/playback_key_watch.rs` the file, `playback_library.rs` the hook): the helper does not say when a key changed, so after a setlist's songs are read (same place they are parsed and cached, no extra helper request) each song's `key` is compared with the key last seen for the same `setlist_song_id`. First sight: remembered, no change. Same key: nothing. Another key: `key_was` = old key, `key_changed_at` = now (UTC), new key remembered. A change back is a new change.
- `LibrarySong` has `key_was` / `key_changed_at` (RFC 3339 UTC), sent while the change is remembered, however old. `generated/ts/LibrarySong.ts` regenerated by the repo's own `export_bindings` test; `frontend/src/types.ts` matches.
- **File** `playback-keys.json` beside `settings.json` (same directory function and write pattern as `service-pin.json`: temp file, fsync, rename; `STAGEPILOT_PLAYBACK_KEYS_PATH` overrides). Written only when a song is seen for the first time or a key changed, never on an ordinary read. Only `setlist_song_id`, key names and times (no titles). At most 500 songs (oldest read first out), songs not read for 7 days dropped when it is next written, missing/damaged file ignored (one warning), a failed write is a log line and a retry at the next change, never a failed request. Memory-only in tests/demo (`memory_tokens`). Forgetting the Library Link or saving another Playback computer empties it (other computer = other song numbers).
- **Frontend**: `keyWas(song, now)`, `songFaceFacts/songFacts/chipLibrary(…, now)` take the clock as a parameter (pure; `key_original` is no longer compared, the field stays in the data). `useKeyChangeClock` re-renders the cards once a minute only while some card shows "(was)" (no timer otherwise); used by the Playback songs chips and the Lighting panel's song chips.
- CHANGELOG (Unreleased) and `docs/playback-api.md` updated.

## Checks (clean clone, Node 22.23.5, rustc 1.98.1)
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p stagepilot-playback -p stagepilot-server --tests -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p stagepilot-playback`: 121 lib tests + all its integration tests pass (replay and real_replay unchanged: 1 + 1 passed)
- `cargo test -p stagepilot-server --no-fail-fast`: lib 52 passed (6 new: file store), `tests/playback_library.rs` 78 passed (4 new). 672 tests passed across both crates, 1 failed: `tests/pco_lengths.rs` ("Playback never confirmed the saved scan", a different test of the 8 each run). **That file flakes on an untouched `origin/main` too**: 4 runs of `cargo test -p stagepilot-server --test pco_lengths` on a clean worktree of `origin/main` failed 1, 2, 1 and 2 of 8; on this branch it passed 8/8 when run alone. Unrelated to this change (Playback scan status timing), not touched.
- Frontend: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors (12 warnings, none in touched files); `npx vitest run` 135 files, 2021 tests passed; `npm run build` ok.
- New tests: change table (first sight, same, change, change back, damaged/foreign file, 500 cap, no write when unchanged, 7-day drop, file round-trip, restart keeps it, unwritable file); `LibrarySong` JSON; fake-helper integration (fresh pairing plain, changed key shows `Ab` / was `G`, change back, restart keeps it, forgotten library records nothing and empties the file); fact function at 0 h / 23 h 59 m / 24 h 1 m / exactly 24 h, `key_was === key`, missing/unreadable time, missing old key; hover text; card text with a fake clock including "goes back to Ab after the day with no reload" and "no timer when nothing shows".

## Notes
- The task text mentions `songKeyLength`; there is no such function on `main` or in #355–#357 (checked their diffs), so only `songFaceFacts`/`songFacts`/`chipLibrary` changed. #357 adds a second caller of `songFaceFacts(library)` (in `PlaybackLibrarySongs.tsx`): after the two PRs meet it needs the `now` argument (`useKeyChangeClock`, as here).
- Opened from `origin/main`, so it may need a small merge with #357 in `PlaybackLibrarySongs.tsx`.
- No rig, no real Playback or Planning Center contact; all against fakes.

## What's new
- **Boss abilities (638)**: which creature casts which spell comes from AzerothCore. That includes SmartAI, `creature_template_spell`, and the `SPELL_*` enums of C++ scripts that register exactly one creature. What each spell does comes from the Classic Era client's spell tables (cast time, interrupt flag, dispel type, mechanic, effects). `classifySpell` sorts each spell into interrupt / crowd-control / healer-danger / dispel / tank-danger / positioning / special-mechanic using fixed rules, which are documented.
