author: erik117-debug
body:
## The bug

The crewmen's poses were made against nothing. In a10's cryo bay the assistant rested his right hand 0.013 units (about 4 cm) inside the console, and both crewmen typed with their fingertips up to 0.003 into the keys in the keyboard close-up. On the bridge the two pilots held both hands 0.016 to 0.021 inside their chairs' consoles for the whole scene. The crewman has no finger nodes, so the hands can't be posed finger by finger.

## The fix

`crewman_hands.c` reads the crewman's forearm and hand vertices as the tags load. Each tick, for a crewman playing a scripted animation or seated, it casts a line from the shoulder to each of those vertices against the level, vehicles, scenery and machines. The deepest vertex inside a surface is lifted 1.5 mm clear by bending the elbow: the forearm and hand turn about the elbow, measured again up to three times, by no more than 30 degrees. A vertex more than 0.03 behind the surface is past something thin and is left alone. Idle and walking crewmen aren't measured, and the animations and model are unchanged.

## Checked

Checked by tracing every arm vertex against what is in front of it, tick by tick. After the fix the assistant and both pilots never have a vertex inside, and the technician keeps one tick at 0.007, at the start of a move made 0.028 deep, in a shot that doesn't show his hands. Frames of the booth shots show the assistant's whole hand resting on the console where it was cut off before, and the bridge shots show no odd poses. The fix costs about 0.36 ms a tick on the bridge (0.85 ms at most). The new harness test covers lifting, leaving alone, the cap and which crewmen are measured, and each of its six controls fails it.

## Follow-up commit: Lift only the seated crewmen's hands, at the elbow or the shoulder

### Why

The hands to fix were the seated crewmen's at the bridge desks, not the cryo bay pair's, so the lift now applies only to a crewman in a seat; the technician and assistant are posed as the animations have them again.

### The change

Measured with the player on a10's bridge as the level plays: the two crewmen at the middle desks held their forearms 0.026 to 0.046 units and their hands up to 0.075 inside the keyboard tray, the screenshot's view. Bending the elbow freed the hands but left the forearm beside the elbow up to 0.017 inside, which the elbow can't lift. So a forearm's vertex is now lifted by raising the arm at the shoulder (the upper arm, forearm and hand turned about the upper arm's node), and a hand's by the elbow as before, each joint capped at 30 degrees, up to four passes. The turn uses the game's sine and cosine.

### Checked

Every seated crewman's forearm and hand vertices are now at most 0.002 inside anything, never more than 2 mm for a tick; a camera behind one of the middle crewmen shows his hands on the keys where they were inside the tray. The fix costs 0.71 ms a tick on the bridge's nine seated crewmen (1.5 ms at most). The harness test adds a shoulder case and two controls (standing crewmen bent, forearm lifted by the elbow); its seven controls fail it. The bridge and cryo scenes run without halts.

## Checked on this branch

Rebased on `testing`: `ninja windows` builds, and the changed C files compile with implicit declarations as errors. The harness tests of the files it changes pass (120 tests): `test_coop_pickups.py`, `test_coop_vehicles.py`, `test_crewman_hands.py`, `test_elevator_carry.py`, `test_listener_motion.py`, `test_picture_function_inputs.py`, `test_script_stale_objects.py`.

author: skylerberg
body:
Rename `Instance.key` to `Lowered.Item.t` and remove the `instance` library.

A key names one function or datum that the backend emits: a definition
at a ground instantiation, generic or not, or a compiler-generated item
such as drop glue, a vtable, or an entry. "Instance" suggested a
type-class instance or a generic's instantiation, and most variants are
neither. The lowered IR refers to these items by key, and every
dependent of the `instance` library already depends on `lowered`, so
the key moves into `lowered` and the `instance` library is removed.

Renamed identifiers:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `Instance.key` | `Lowered.Item.t` |
| `Lowered.function_ref`'s `Instance` | `Item` |
| `C_instance`, `Emit_c.Builder.instance` | `Item_code`, `Emit_c.Builder.item_code` |
| `C_types.context.instances` | `referenced_items` |
| `Lowering.finish_instance` | `Lowering.finish_item` |
| `Targets.lower_instance_call` | `Targets.lower_item_call` |
| `Instance_table` | `Item_table` |
| `instance_values`, `create_instance`, `list_instance_parts`, `list_instance_edges`, `collect_ready_instances` in the database | `item_values`, `create_item`, `list_item_parts`, `list_item_edges`, `collect_ready_items` |
| `Part.locate_instance_package`, `Part.find_instance_definition` | `locate_item_package`, `find_item_definition` |
| `Codegen_support.instance`, `make_constant_instance` | `item`, `make_constant_item` |
| The prover's `Logic.Symbol` field `instance`, `show_instance`, and `~instance` arguments | `type_arguments`, `show_type_arguments`, `~type_arguments` |

The prover used "instance" for a callee's type arguments, which
codegen already calls `type_arguments`.

Other changes:

- Move name mangling into `Emit_c.Mangling`. Only C emission names C
  identifiers. `Emit_c.make_symbol` gives the backend and the tests an
  item's symbol.
- Rename `make_type_symbol` to `Mangling.make_type_name`: a C type name
  is not a linker symbol.
- Remove `Emit_c.Builder.instance_key`. The backend and the build tests
  read an item's key from its fragment.
- Remove the duplicate `type t = key`.
- Change the fragment hash context to "item fragment hash" and the
  fragment placeholder prefix to `@item_`. Every test key changes once,
  so cached test results run again once. The emitted C is unchanged.
- Fix a bug message that called the impl of a call through `any` an
  instance.

## Local checks

- `dune build` and `dune build @fmt`
- The `For_testing`, comments, and qualified-names checks
- Every suite under `stage0/test/codegen`, `database_tests.exe`, and `prover_tests.exe`: all pass

author: ventsislav-georgiev
body:
## X-ray search

- **A cap on a turn boundary keeps every whole turn (#475, NIT-UF1).** When the 500-hit cap falls exactly at the start of a turn, all 500 hits are kept: 40 turns of 25 hits give 20 whole turns (1.97.0 gave 19). The oldest kept turn is left out only when the hit past the cap belongs to it. The same holds for a shell's ring.

## X-ray terms

- **Filenames by their extension (#476, NIT-UF2).** A backticked name of letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-` is a filename, not a term, when its last extension is a common file type (`docker-compose.yml`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `README.md`). A lowercase dotfile (`.env`, `.gitignore`) is a filename too. Member access, domains and dotted names stay terms: `os.path`, `Math.max`, `github.com`, `socket.io`, `ASP.NET`, `v1.2`. `node.js` counts as a filename, because `.js` is a file extension.

## X-ray refs

- **Long tool names cut on a character (#477, NIT-UF3).** A tool name longer than 127 bytes is cut on a UTF-8 character boundary, so a mention's `tool` never ends in U+FFFD.

## Tests

- New rows: 40 x 25 search hits (transcript and shell), the filename/term grammar, and a long non-ASCII MCP tool name. Each fails on 1.97.0.

## Gate

- Suite full: 247/0 (try 1, load 44). Suite lite: 169/0 (try 1, load 41). strict + clang analyzer full and lite: 0 nonzero.
- ASan full (410c35c, box load 7-214): xray_view 94/0, xray_remote_view 91/0, xray_deny, xray_resolve, xray_golden 453/0, xray_claude 342/0, xray_view_turns 139/0, serve_test 280/0, xray_unit: 0 failed, 0 sanitizer reports.

author: gomesalexandre
body:
hyperswap-v3 priced LP `apyBase`/`apyBase7d` from the subgraph's `poolDayData.feesUSD`, which is gross: for the top pools `feesUSD / volumeUSD` equals the fee tier exactly (3000 -> 0.3%, 500 -> 0.05%). HyperSwap's pools have the Uniswap V3 fee switch on, so part of that never reaches LPs. Same fix as uniswap-v3 in #3218: read each pool's `slot0().feeProtocol` and scale both APYs by the LP share.

**On-chain (HyperEVM, 2026-11-18):**
- every one of the top 8 pools by TVL reads `feeProtocol = 102` = `0x66`, so 1/6 of each swap fee goes to the protocol and LPs keep 5/6
- the fees really accrue: WHYPE-UBTC (`0x3a36b04bcc1d5e2e303981ef643d2668e00b43e7`, $2.1M) holds `protocolFees()` = 2.16 WHYPE + 173,622 UBTC units
- some smaller pools read `feeProtocol = 0` and are left unchanged

**Live run, master vs this branch in the same minute** (58 pools, $8.64M):
- 92 of the non-zero APY values move by exactly 5/6; the 8 values from `feeProtocol = 0` pools stay the same; two small differences come from the subgraph updating between the two runs
- WHYPE-UBTC ($2.1M): `apyBase` 5.61% -> 4.68%, `apyBase7d` 61.58% -> 51.31%
- WHYPE-USDC ($1.1M): `apyBase` 10.33% -> 8.61%, `apyBase7d` 63.30% -> 52.75%

A pool whose `slot0` read fails is dropped for that run (per-pool `permitFailure`), so a broken read can neither fail the whole adapter nor publish that pool at the gross fee. Merkl rewards are unchanged.

author: mapringg
body:
## Summary

Boundary defaults that let a large app reach zero module findings without one barrel for everything it shares. Stacked on #51.

- Every `src/components/*` folder is its own module, imported through its group, such as `@/components/chart`. `src/lib` and `src/components/ui` stay open.
- A module now has three entries: `index`, `index.server` and `routes`. `index.server` is the server-only surface. The Next route-layering default still stops route files from importing a feature's `*.server.*` files, but it now lets them import its `index.server`.
- `standard/server-entry`: code that ships to the browser imports no `index.server` entry. That means a `"use client"` or `.browser` file, or anything one reaches through the browser graph `standard/zod` already uses.
- `standard/index-exports`: a plain `index` imports and re-exports no `*.server.*` file and no `src/lib/api` module. Those belong in `index.server`.
- README, `schema.json` (the two new `allow` ids), the oxlint config, the defaults snapshot and `standard explain` all cover the new rules.

## Evidence

**Before:** `src/components` was one module, a feature had only `index` and `routes`, and 18 plugin rules.

**After:** 20 plugin rules. `pnpm test` passes 697 of 697. Strict `tsc --checkJs` passes. `oxlint` reports no errors and the three existing warnings. 69 non-test lines changed (size S).

Failing-first: `581a29b` fails 3 tests before `9db53b8`.

Boundaries under the derived defaults, read-only, before and after this PR:

| | repo-a develop | repo-a adoption stack | repo-b | repo-c |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Findings before | 1326 | 933 | 200 | 46 |
| Findings after | 1229 | 836 | 200 | 46 |
| Resolved by group entries | 115 | 115 | 0 | 0 |
| New cross-group imports | 18 | 18 | 0 | 0 |

Of repo-a's 933 on its adoption stack, 115 disappear because they already import a group's `index`. 722 become mechanical through a plain group or feature `index`, since the target is neither a `*.server.*` file nor imports one or `lib/api`. Another 95 become mechanical through `index.server`, since a server file imports a server target. One needs a move: a client file imports a server target. Of repo-b's 200, 163 are mechanical through `index`, 33 through `index.server`, and 4 need a move. `server-entry` and `index-exports` find 0 on all three adopters today, because none has an `index.server` yet.

## Migration

For each finding, export the target from its group's or feature's `index`, or from `index.server` when the target is server-only, and import that entry. Keep `"use client"` files on `index`. When a client file needs a server-only target, move the shared part down into `components` or `lib`.

## Known limits

The mechanical counts read only each target's direct imports. A plain-index target that reaches server code further down still needs review, and `standard/zod` and `server-entry` catch it once the index ships to the browser. `index-exports` matches specifiers by name, `*.server` and `lib/api`, not by resolution. No adopter files were changed. No merge or release.

## Review round 2

Rebased onto #51. Failing tests `4ddccae`, fix `e05f398`.

- **P2 server-entry:** it now resolves each import, re-export, `require()` and static template `import()` with the same resolver as the browser graph (relative, tsconfig paths, package.json `imports`). It reports any resolved `*.server.*` file reached from client-reachable code, not only `index.server`. A `#report` alias, `` import(`./load.server`) ``, `require("./load.server")`, a direct `./load.server` import and the chain `index` → `export * from "./data"` → `export * from "./load.server"` all fail. The chain fails at `data.ts`, which ships to the browser. The browser graph no longer marks `*.server.*` files as browser code.
- **P2 index-exports:** it stays the early per-file guard for a plain `index`. Imports are resolved, and API modules come from a legacy `api-modules` list during adoption and from the derived `**/src/lib/api/**` (`API_MODULES` in defaults) otherwise, so there is no hard-coded `lib/api` path.
- **P3 browser.mjs:** the graph stores a hash of every source file's path, size and mtime (plus manifests and tsconfigs). It checks that hash at most once a second and rebuilds when it changes, which also clears the shared resolver cache. The README says an editor result can lag by up to a second, unsaved edits count after saving, and the CLI and CI are authoritative. Template `import()` without expressions is followed.
- **P3 boundaries fix message:** it lists only the entries that apply. `routes` is listed only for modules under `features/`, and `index.server` only when the importer doesn't mark itself as browser code (`"use client"` or `.browser.`).

Re-measured (plugin and CLI at `e05f398`): server-entry 0 and index-exports 0 on repo-a develop, repo-a #778, repo-b and repo-c. Boundaries totals are unchanged at repo-a #778 836, repo-b 200 and repo-c 46. None of the 836 offers `routes` for a components group.

Gates at `e05f398`: `pnpm test` 711/711, `pnpm typecheck` 0, oxlint 0 errors.

**Follow-up:** rebased onto #51's ai-render scope fix. The round-2 commits are now test `cadfe78` and fix `9a06330`. Gates at `9a06330`: `pnpm test` 712/712, `pnpm typecheck` 0, oxlint 0 errors. The throwaway migrate run at this head is described in #50.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** defaults

author: 284km
body:
Repeatedly stepping and dropping generators in mere-ruby rebuilds and sorts the entire live-block snapshot after each small local allocation change. Keep a bounded thread-local log of up to 64 additions/removals and apply short bursts by binary insertion/removal. Overflow, shared-list generation changes and inconsistent deltas retain the complete locked rebuild.

Capture bounds before free/reallocation and initialize block capacity before registry publication. Recording activates after the first scan; programs without the coroutine scanner leave the hook unset. This changes the generated C executable/library runtime; pin decisions, reachability limits and region retirement retain their existing semantics.

On the same mere-ruby source and O2 build, three alternating fresh-process samples at 4,000 generators improve the median from **19.731s to 9.839s**, with median peak RSS **410.61 / 411.09 MiB** (arm64 macOS). Results at 1,000/2,000 generators, full ranges and the reproducible workload are recorded in `benchmarks/coro_scan/README.md`. Growth remains faster than linear; this is not an end-to-end CI timing claim.

Validation:

- `dune runtest`: 3,305 passed, 0 failed.
- `python3 scripts/coro_scan_index_check.py`: independent registry oracle, O2 and ASan/UBSan in executable and library modes. Five deliberately broken variants each produce their required assertion witness. Covers local churn, freed/reused blocks, growth, overflow, cross-thread shared changes and TLS isolation; short updates must avoid a full sort. Added as a separate CI coroutine step.
- `python3 scripts/coro_scan_stability_check.py`: 12 positive and 8 negative controls passed.
- `sh scripts/coro_check.sh --poison`: interpreter, C and LLVM cases passed; RISC-V cases skipped locally because MEMU was not configured.
- Downstream O2 interpreter: all 703 corpus programs match Ruby 4.0.9 with the hash index on/off. The pinned CRuby enum/enumerator/lazy-enumerator suites preserve the control's exact named-case results (224 tests, 1,460 assertions, 0 failures/errors, 1 existing skip).
- `actionlint` and `git diff --check` passed.
- `ruby scripts/ci_gate_check.rb --self-test`: 200 checks assigned exactly once, 155 negative controls caught and all setup/distribution/bootstrap/release checks passed. The new gate is required in the coroutine group and protected against removal, renaming, bypass, optional status and wrong routing.

Wasm/RISC-V backends are unchanged and were not separately benchmarked. Hosted CI remains required for the broader platform matrix.

author: taehyeooo
body:
## 한 것

홈·내 여행·영상 기록이 호출하는 `GET /api/trip-drafts/auto`는 초안과 분석을 엔티티로 읽어 사용자 조회가 두 번 추가됐습니다. 카드에 필요한 값만 조회하도록 바꿔 예열 JWT HTTP 요청의 SQL을 5→3회로 줄이고 엔티티 로딩을 없앴습니다.

### 분석·선택 이유

요청은 DB 조회와 영상 URL 정규화·초안 JSON 파싱만 수행하며 외부 호출은 없습니다. (a) 조회 최적화, (b) 사용자별 짧은 캐시, (c) 둘 다를 비교해 **(a)**를 선택했습니다. ADR 0034·0036의 scalar projection을 적용해 불필요한 사용자·상세 요약 로딩을 줄이고, 144MiB 힙에서 캐시 상주 비용과 커밋 후 무효화 경합을 추가하지 않습니다.

| 초안/분석 수 | SQL 전→후 | 엔티티 전→후 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5→3 | 4→0 |
| 8 | 5→3 | 18→0 |
| 20(응답 10) | 5→3 | 42→0 |
| 빈 목록 | 1→1 | 0→0 |

캐시는 전후 모두 없음이며 적중·만료·무효화는 해당 없음입니다. 요청 중 동일 영상 키를 재사용하고 표시하는 최대 10개 카드만 JSON을 파싱합니다. 사용자 존재를 처음 확인하는 JWT 요청에는 기존 정책에 따라 SQL 1회가 추가됩니다.

### 쓰기·무효화 경로

응답 캐시가 없어 다음 요청에서 DB를 읽습니다. 자동/대체 초안 생성·처리 상태/내용 변경·답변·닫기·승인, 사용자/관리자 여행 생성·삭제와 여행 장소 연결 변경, 저장 장소 추가·삭제/분석 결과 교체, 최신 분석 완료·제목/상태 변경, 위치 바로잡기, 오래 멈춘 초안 실패 처리, 계정 삭제를 확인했습니다. 각 경로와 영향은 [P3 기록](https://github.com/Trovapp/trova-backend/blob/0de4a60e6486df404b3499d8c062bbc6381ac6b8/docs/monitoring/2026-11-18-perf-phase1/README.md#p3-자동-초안-목록-조회-466)에 적었습니다.

위치 바로잡기의 `placesChangedAt`과 상세 `placesChanged/currentJobIds`는 그대로입니다. #151 관련 자동/대체 초안 표시 테스트, 최신 DONE 분석/URL 별칭, 이미 여행이 된 영상을 제외한 뒤 10개 제한, 없는 작업/잘못된 JSON의 응답을 보존합니다.

## 확인한 것

- 테스트 먼저: 변경 전 SQL 목표 테스트 실패(5→목표 3), 변경 후 SQL 3·엔티티 0 확인.
- 전체 DTO·순서 동등성, 초안/분석 수 1·8·20, 빈 목록과 생성·완료·닫기 직후 반영, 여행·저장 장소 삭제 직후 반영, 대체 초안·타 사용자·최신 실패 분석·없는 영상·placeCount 회귀 테스트 4개 추가.
- 기존 자동 초안과 위치 바로잡기 테스트 포함 전체 `test build`: 1,235개 중 1,229개 통과·기존 조건부 건너뜀 6개·실패/오류 0개(JUnit XML 합산), 새 테스트 4개 모두 통과; `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 4m 5s`, `8 actionable tasks: 6 executed, 2 up-to-date`
- P1·P2와 같은 WSL JDK 21.0.13+9, Gradle Wrapper main, H2, offline. 산출물 위치만 임시 init script로 변경했으며 테스트 제외·의존성/전역 설정 변경 없음.
- 첫 전체 실행에서 JSON 숫자 노드의 Long/Integer 비교 오류 3건과 기존 H2 컨텍스트 수명 충돌 2건 발견. JSON 양쪽을 동일하게 직렬화/파싱하고 새 테스트는 P2의 격리 컨텍스트를 공유하도록 수정했습니다.
- `git diff --check` 통과.

| 요청 항목 | 코드/기록 | 검증 |
|---|---|---|
| 호출·쓰기 경로 분석과 대안 비교 | README P3 절 | 코드 읽기·SQL 전후 실측 |
| SQL/불필요 로딩 감소 | `AutoDraftQueryService.java:38`, `TripDraftRepository.java:51`, `ProcessingJobRepository.java:26` | `AutoDraftReadPerformanceTest.java:115` |
| 응답·쓰기 직후 반영 보존 | `AutoDraftQueryService.java:46` | 같은 테스트 `:142`, `:163`, `:199` |
| 위치 바로잡기 안내 보존 | 기존 `PlaceRelocateService.java:43`, 상세 DTO | 기존 PlaceRelocateService 단위/통합 테스트 |
| 캡처 | 화면 조작 도구 미제공 | 요청의 예외에 따라 생략 |

## 확인하지 않은 것

Grafana 캡처는 화면 조작 도구가 없어 생략했습니다(캡처 경로 없음). 요청에 주어진 p95 약 351ms는 재측정하지 않았고 H2 SQL 감소를 운영 응답 시간 개선으로 환산하지 않습니다. 후보 초안/분석 전체 행 수·JSON 크기는 사용자 이력에 비례하며 여러 SELECT 사이 동시 쓰기 일관성은 기존과 같습니다. 운영 PostgreSQL 실행 계획·힙 바이트·앱 안내 띠 실화면은 미확인입니다.

루트 .env 복사, 운영 DB/서버, 개발 DB 계정, 로컬 8080, Gemini 접근과 머지는 하지 않았습니다.

Closes #466

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/121909
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122160
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/132561


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

Fixed a query like `WHERE g AND intDiv(1, x) > 0 AND toBool(b)` failing with `ILLEGAL_DIVISION` although the column `g` rejects the row that would throw. When the `WHERE` AND chain was split into several filters (`query_plan_merge_filters`, enabled by default), a conjunct written after a bare column was evaluated before that column was applied.

### Description

On 26.10.3.7, at default settings and with no table, `SELECT count() FROM values('g UInt8, x Int32, b String', (0, 0, 'true'), (1, 1, 'true')) WHERE g AND intDiv(1, x) > 0 AND toBool(b)` is rejected with `Code: 153 ILLEGAL_DIVISION` instead of returning `1`.

With `query_plan_merge_filters` a `WHERE` AND chain is split into a sequence of filters, left to right, so that a conjunct runs only on the rows the ones before it accept. The splitter (`trySplitSingleAndFilter`) only considered function conjuncts, because a conjunct it has split stays in the remaining chain as an input column and must not be split again. That rule also skipped a column the user wrote, so `intDiv(1, x) > 0` was split first and ran on every row. The splitter now records the names of the conjuncts it split and splits any other column like a conjunct. Reordering of cheap conjuncts and the rule that the last function conjunct is not split are unchanged. PREWHERE already applies a bare column as its own step.

Plans change only when a bare column is written before the conjunct the splitter would split first: one more `AND column:` line in `EXPLAIN actions = 1` and one more `FilterTransform`.

The new test covers `UInt8`, `Nullable(Bool)`, `LowCardinality(UInt8)`, `Int32`, `Float64` and a sparse column, a guard merged from a subquery, and the split order. It fails on master at its first query and passes 50 randomized runs. Same class as #121909, fixed for `JOIN` push-down by #122160; found while working on #132561 (mine).

body:
Part of #9402. With the new `separate_constant_pool` setting on (it's off by default), Cranelift returns each function's constants as a separate blob with relocations. Wasmtime puts them in a `.wasmtime.constants` section between the page-aligned text and `.eh_frame`, as alexcrichton suggested. It's enabled with `-C cranelift-separate_constant_pool=true`.

On AArch64 a constant load becomes an `adrp` into a fresh vreg and a load from it, as cfallin outlined, with a relocation for each.

riscv64, s390x and Pulley return an error with the setting on, as do cranelift-jit and cranelift-object for a function with constants. Winch ignores it.

With the setting forced on locally, the wast suite and tests/all pass on x86-64, and the wast suite passes on AArch64 under qemu. I haven't run it on AArch64 hardware, macOS or Windows. With it off, `.text` matches main for the 28 Sightglass modules below. Most of the size change is page padding of the text.

| Total `.cwasm` bytes, 28 Sightglass modules | setting off | setting on | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| x86_64 Linux | 14,229,528 | 14,219,568 | -0.070% |
| AArch64 Linux | 18,525,504 | 18,461,288 | -0.347% |

body:
Step 0 of `docs/ipad-live-default-plan.md` (PR #320). It stacks on the plan branch like Steps 1 to 5 (#333, #337, #331, #336, #332).

## What

- **Appearance > Writing > Open notes in** (Live, Markdown, Preview, Split). It's kept on this iPad (`@AppStorage`), not in `settings.json`, so a restored desktop backup leaves it alone (I3). It defaults to **Preview** until Step 8 (I4).
- **Every note opens in it**, and a tab you choose lasts until another note opens (I3). The note that was open when the app was ended comes back in its own tab. A new note opens in the setting's view, or in Markdown when the setting is Preview (I5).
- **One layout for all four tabs.** `SplitLayout` takes `showing` and lays out the same two views with `AnyLayout`, so the text view keeps its identity: **undo survives a look at the Preview, at Split and at Markdown** (D7). Under the Preview the text view is hidden. A PDF quote or citation made while the Preview shows still goes to the end of the note (`EditorHandle.isShowing`).
- **An edit from outside the text view clears its undo** (D7).

## Found on the way

Giving up the keyboard inside `updateUIView` (directly, or by hiding the view or turning its touches off) made the keyboard's tracking ask SwiftUI to render inside the same update. That's an AttributeGraph cycle, and it held the main thread; I found it by sampling the app while a UI test stalled. The hide now happens on the next turn of the run loop.

## Checked (Simulator, on a Mac shared with five other Simulator sessions, load 300 to 800)

- **`OpenNotesInUITests`, 5 new tests, all pass:**
  - every note opens in the setting's view, and a tab chosen lasts until another note opens;
  - the setting chosen in the sheet is kept across launches;
  - ⌘Z undoes typing after a look at the Preview, and after Split and Markdown;
  - an edit from outside the text view leaves it nothing to undo.
- **Existing suites that pass:** `LayoutUITests`, `PdfMarksUITests`, `PolishUITests`, `AccessibilityUITests` and the picker-order test of `LiveUITests`. Two Forest audits failed once because a tap on the restore alert was lost under load; both pass on a rerun and on the base commit.
- **One existing test fails:** `LiveUITests.testSwitchingTabsKeepsTheCaretAndTheTextAndTheLiveLookComesBack`. It **fails the same way on the base commit** under this load: its Markdown tap isn't retried.
- **Not done:** the rest of the UI suite was not rerun.

## Left for you (Gate LD0)

Manual-test items 340 to 343: the setting, a new note, and undo after the Preview by finger, gesture and Magic Keyboard. Item 342 also asks whether **VoiceOver skips the hidden editor under the Preview**: XCUITest still lists a representable's hidden view, so the Simulator can't answer it.

## After merging the plan branch (Steps 1 to 3)

I merged the plan branch, now carrying Steps 1 to 3, into this one. The three conflicts in `NoteDetailView`, `NoteEditorView` and the manual-test page were both sides adding; I kept both.

- **Pass on the merged build:** all 5 `OpenNotesInUITests`, `LayoutUITests`, 6 of 7 `LiveLinksUITests`, and 2 of 6 `LiveCodeUITests`.
- **Fail the same way on the plan branch without this PR, so they're not Step 0's:**
  - `LiveLinksUITests.testTheArrowAppearsWhileTheCaretIsInALinkAndOpensTheOtherNote`: the ↗ sits 80 pt off the caret's line, with identical numbers on both builds.
  - `LiveCodeUITests.testTheLightSchemePaintsTheCodeFill`.
- **Fail here and weren't rerun on the base:** the Dark, Cream and Forest code-fill pixel tests. They need a rerun on a quiet Mac.

author: colneech-dev
body:
A series that moves the unspent-output set out of the transaction index and onto the path a validating node needs for pruning. Each step is its own commit(s) and the tests of each came with it.

1. **`gettxoutsetinfo`** (also its own pull request; the same commits): the unspent set of the chain, read from the index or from the blocks, and its hash. It is the reference that every later step is checked against.
2. **A write-back cache over the transaction index.** The `CTxIndex` changes of one block are held in a cache and reach `blkindex.dat` once, in `Flush()`, where the block code wrote them one by one. Reads see the cache first.
3. **The unspent-output set and the per-block undo data in LevelDB**, beside the index. First as a shadow (both paths run and are cross-checked input by input at every block connect), then `-coinsvalidate`, which connects a block's inputs from the unspent set, and which is on by default (`-nocoinsvalidate` keeps the index path). `gettxoutsetinfo` reports how many blocks were checked against the set.
4. **Script checks of a block run together on several threads** (`-par`), and are skipped under an assumed-valid block (`-assumevalid`).
5. **Pruning** (`-prune=<MiB>`): old block files are deleted, and validation comes from the unspent set. A rescan over pruned blocks is refused; the start-up verification stops at the pruned part.

**Build requirement: LevelDB.** It is now needed to build. `contrib/build-leveldb.sh` builds the pinned release (1.23, static, no snappy), and the build and release workflows build it first and pass it to cmake on every platform (the Windows cross build with the MinGW toolchain, the MSYS2 job with the MSYS Makefiles generator). A distribution's `libleveldb-dev` works for a local build. The workflow changes could only be exercised by this pull request's own CI.

## Tested
Upstream master plus this series alone (Linux, with LevelDB from the distribution): the unit tests pass and the whole functional suite passes (38 of 38, none skipped, with v4.9.0.0 as the second build for `feature_cross_binary`). `feature_prune.py`, `feature_script_checks.py` and `rpc_gettxoutsetinfo.py` are the new tests.

author: mintleaf84
body:
## 做了什么

让 agent 在真写之前能**预演**，跑飞时被**挡住**而不是压垮库。对应 `ai-native` 计划 P0 的两条硬门槛（也是接 dsh/MCP 的前置）。

### 1. 5 个写接口支持 `?dryRun=true`

覆盖：
`POST /practice/answers`、`POST /recall/reviews`、`POST /recall/decks`、`POST /recall/cards`、`DELETE /recall/decks/{deckKey}/cards/{cardKey}`

实现方式：**真实事务 + 哨兵回滚**（`services/dry-run.ts`）。服务端跑完真实写入路径后抛 `DryRunRollback` 强制回滚，只把结果带出。因此：

- 预演与真执行**共用同一段代码**，"预演说 3 条、真写 5 条"在结构上不可能出现；
- 预演同样暴露 `400`（题目不存在，带 `invalidQuestionIds`）/ `404`（卡片不在卡组里）/ `403`（作用域不足）——预演通过 = 真请求不会因参数被拒；
- 删卡预演只统计不删除，返回将连带删掉的 `reviewLogs` / `cardStates`，响应 `deleted=false`，避免把预演当成功。

### 2. `/api/external/*` 限流

- **按 API Key 计**（不按 IP：agent 常共用出口 IP，按 IP 会把"一个跑飞"放大成"所有人 429"）；
- 读 600/min、写 120/min；
- 超限 `429` + `Retry-After`，body 里同时给 `retryAfter` 秒数（agent 不解析响应头也能退避）；
- 复用 `lib/auth/rate-limit` 的滑动窗口（新增 `checkRateLimitWith`），没有自造第二套限流。

### 契约与文档

- 18 条外部操作全部声明 `429`；5 条写操作声明 `dryRun` 参数；
- 重新生成 `docs/openapi.json`，`contract:check` 通过；
- `docs/api.md` 新增 §9 dry-run 说明，§8 把"无限流"改成实际额度。

## 验证（本机实测）

| 闸门 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 error |
| `vitest run --maxWorkers=6` | **212 文件 / 1729 用例全绿**（基线 210/1716，新增 2 文件 13 用例） |
| `npm run lint:ci` | 126（基线已收紧到 126） |
| `contract:check` | 与快照一致 |
| `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` | 通过（仅存量 low/moderate） |
| `next build` | 本机 GLIBC 不支持，交由 CI |

新增用例的核心断言：
- `external-dryrun.test.ts`：逐接口对比"预演计数 == 真执行计数"，并断言 dry-run 前后 **7 张表行数完全相等**；
- `external-ratelimit.test.ts`：429/Retry-After、读桶与写桶隔离、按 key 分离。

## 已知影响

- `DELETE` 响应新增 `reviewLogs` / `cardStates`，`POST /recall/cards` 响应新增 `created`：字段级新增，向后兼容（既有 `toEqual` 断言已同步更新）。
- 限流是**单实例内存窗口**，与 `lib/auth/rate-limit` 同一局限；多实例需外置（已在可扩展性清单里）。

## Sourcery 摘要

支持安全的外部写入预览，并保护外部 API 免受过量请求流量的影响。

新功能：
- 为五个外部写入端点添加 dry-run 支持：返回预测结果，同时保持数据库不变。
- 为外部端点添加基于 API 密钥的速率限制，分别设置读取和写入配额，并提供重试指引。

错误修复：
- 确保 dry-run 请求使用实际写入路径，并保留正常的验证和授权错误，同时不持久化任何更改。
- 在卡片删除响应中，加入受影响的关联审核日志和卡片状态数量。

改进：
- 复用共享的滑动窗口速率限制实现，以支持可配置的外部 API 限流桶。
- 在外部 API 契约和文档中统一说明 dry-run 和速率限制行为。

文档：
- 在外部 API 指南中说明 dry-run 语义、受影响的端点、速率限制、重试行为和删除影响。

测试：
- 添加测试覆盖 dry-run 行为一致性、回滚行为、验证错误、幂等性，以及按密钥隔离读写速率限制。

author: mzabielski
body:
Part of #1448 (UX audit 2026-11-17, DS-15).

## What changes

`@endora-commerce/admin-kit/ui` publishes **`EmptyState`**, extracted from `FormsListPage.tsx`: a decorative icon, a title, at most one line and at most one action, drawn with the existing `.b2b-empty` classes (Picture Superiority: never a bare grey sentence).

```tsx
// "nothing here yet": the screen gives the icon, the title, the line and the one action
<EmptyState icon={<ClipboardList size={20} />} title={t('list.empty.title')}
  description={canWrite ? t('list.empty.body') : t('list.empty.bodyReadOnly')}
  action={canWrite ? createButton : null} />

// "your filters match nothing": kit copy and an outline Clear filters button
<EmptyState variant="no-results" title={t('list.emptyFiltered')} onClearFilters={clearFilters} />
```

- Variants are a discriminated union: `no-data` (default) needs `icon` + `title`. `no-results` needs only `onClearFilters`, and `icon` (default `SearchX`), `title` and `description` can override it.
- New `core` keys `common.emptyState.clearFilters`, `common.emptyState.noResults.title` and `common.emptyState.noResults.body`, in EN and PL.
- Clear filters is `outline` with a 44 px touch height (`min-h-11 sm:min-h-9`), so it is never the view's primary (Von Restorff, Fitts).
- It is not a live region, because it mounts with its text already in place (WCAG 4.1.3). The list's result count is what gets announced.
- `data-empty-state="no-data" | "no-results"` lets a test tell the variants apart.
- There is a kit README section and a `minor` changeset.

## Screens migrated

- **Forms list** (the source): it has a title and a line of its own now. A reader is told who can create a form. While the empty state carries *New form*, the header hides its copy so two primaries never compete. The no-results state uses the kit variant.
- **Form entries**: gets a title and a line, plus the no-results variant.
- **CRM opportunities**, **Tasks**, **My tasks**, **Projects**: both variants. Copy unchanged.
- **Task settings lists** (`SettingsEmptyState` now delegates to the kit), **Project templates**, **Custom fields**, **Price books** (both variants).
- **Product feeds**: the list, the runs tab, delivery (two states), the run's "no issues" state, *My templates* (now with an icon) and the template builder's "no fields yet" (now with an icon).

## Not migrated

These are still hand-made `.b2b-empty` blocks or still need more than a swap:

- `inventory/.../InventoryPage.tsx`, `catalog/.../ProductsList.tsx`: #1615 (ListToolbar) rewrites the code around them. `ProductsList` also has an inline button inside its sentence and two actions, so it needs a design change (CAT-02), not a swap.
- `inventory/.../AvailabilityNotificationsPage.tsx`, `LowStockPage.tsx`, `WarehousesList.tsx`, `price_lists/.../DisplayModeOverridesPage.tsx`: #1613 (PageHeader) adds a `ui` import and rewrites their headers. They are a one-line swap once #1613 merges. Warehouses and Availability also say "match the current filters" even when there is no data, so they need the no-data / no-results split.
- `product_feeds/.../TemplateFieldList.tsx`, the "no field matches your search" line: the list cannot clear the search (the parent owns it), so `no-results` needs a callback prop first.
- Dependents that also need other DS changes, left alone on purpose: **CONTENT-13**, **SALES-24**, **SHELL-12**, **SHELL-13**, **SHELL-20**.
- PR #1616 (ListPage) files are untouched. Its `emptyState` slot can take an `<EmptyState>` once both merge.

## Checks

- New `admin/test/kit/kit-empty-state.test.tsx` covers both variants, EN + PL copy, the callback, omitted parts and axe.
- `FormsListPage` and `EntriesListPage` have new empty-state tests.
- The forms, CRM, tasks, projects, custom fields, price books and product feeds suites pass (78 files, 723 tests).
- typecheck passes for admin, admin-kit and the 7 touched modules. Lint shows 0 errors.
- `check:class-vocabulary`, `check:admin-surface`, `i18n:hardcoded` (0 regressions, 0 drained, so no ledger change), `check:naming`, `check:language` and `check:release-intent` are clean.

author: xxpbsxx
body:
### What
Makes `kern.proc.pid`, `kern.proc.pid_td` and `kern.proc.proc` report the process record, `kinfo_proc`, with the 1,096 bytes that a PS5 on firmware 11.60 reported to a payload process, where AnyPS5 reported FreeBSD 11 amd64's 1,088 bytes. Four probes on that PS5 only read `sysctl`; the first comment has the raw output of the two that read `kern.proc.pid` (first and second probe below), the second comment that of the two that read `kern.proc.proc` and `kern.proc.pid_td` (third and fourth probe):

- `kern.proc.pid`, own pid. The size query with a null buffer returned 0 with a length of 1096 (first probe, line 18; second probe, line 10). A 1096-byte and a 0x448-byte buffer returned 0 with a length of 1096 and `ki_structsize` 1096 (second probe, lines 4, 5 and 7); `ki_pid` equalled `getpid()` and `ki_ppid` equalled `getppid()` (second probe, line 5). A 1088-byte (0x440) buffer returned -1 with errno 12 (`ENOMEM`), the length after the call was 1088 and 1088 bytes were changed, so the console copies what fits and then reports `ENOMEM` (first probe, lines 12 and 15; second probe, line 8); the same holds for 512 bytes (first probe line 16, second probe line 9) and 1 byte (first probe line 17). The pids -1 and 0x7fffffff returned -1 with errno 3 (`ESRCH`) (first probe, lines 21 and 22; second probe, lines 13 and 14), as the Debt entry says for AnyPS5. The console also answered for the parent pid and pid 1 (second probe, lines 11 and 12; third probe, lines 29 and 30); AnyPS5 answers only for its own pid, which the entry already states, and this change does not touch that.
- The offsets of `ki_pid` (72), `ki_ppid` (76) and `ki_comm` (447) of FreeBSD 11 amd64's `kinfo_proc` held, so the 8 extra bytes are at the end of the record. The probes do not say what they contain, and this change fills them with 0 like the rest of the unfilled record.
- `kern.proc.proc`. A PS5 payload process listed dozens of processes, each a record of 1,096 bytes: the size query returned 104120 in the third probe (line 4) and 105216 in the fourth (line 4), and the read in the fourth returned a length of 99736 with 91 records, all 91 with `ki_structsize` 1096 (line 5; 91 times 1096 is 99736). The number of records differs between the runs, so no count is taken from them, and no pid or name is printed in either probe. AnyPS5 lists one record.
- `kern.proc.pid_td` (`KERN_PROC_PID` with `KERN_PROC_INC_THREAD`). The console returned -1 with errno 2 (`ENOENT`) for the size query, the read, a read with three helper threads running, and the pids of the parent, 1, 0x7fffffff and -1 (third probe, lines 18 to 24). AnyPS5 returns one record per live guest thread. That difference is not changed here; the entry now says that the console answers `ENOENT`.

In `core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/SystemConfiguration.cpp` (line numbers at `main` `194964cd3ce`, the base of this branch) `GuestKinfoProc` (`:199-218`) ended in `reserved6[484]` with a `static_assert` on `sizeof == 1088`. `GuestProcessRecord` (`:221-228`) sets `structSize = sizeof(process)`, and the three sysctls build their records from it: `kern.proc.proc` (`:514`, its size query `(EstimatedExtraProcesses + 1) * sizeof(GuestKinfoProc)` at `:512`), `kern.proc.pid` (`:530`) and `kern.proc.pid_td`, with `GuestProcessRecord()` per thread (`:240`) and a length of `records.size() * sizeof(GuestKinfoProc)` (`:547`). `CopyOut` (`:39-54`) already copies `min(capacity, size)` bytes and returns -1 with errno 12 when that is less than the size, which is what the console does, so it is unchanged. The fix is `reserved6[484]` to `reserved6[492]` and the `static_assert` to 1096 (2 lines in `SystemConfiguration.cpp`); the size query, `ki_structsize` and the process and thread lists follow from it. The six-record size query of `kern.proc.proc` (from #22014) becomes six times 1096.

Only `kern.proc.pid` was measured with a buffer of its own size. For `kern.proc.proc` the record size is measured, the number of records is not copied, and for `kern.proc.pid_td` the console does not answer, so its 1,096-byte records are not measured. A caller that asks for its own record with a 0x440-byte buffer, as Source Port (PPSA20040) does for the debugger check, now gets `ENOMEM` with the first 1,088 bytes copied, as on the console; no title was run for this PR.

The test, `core/libs/tests/GuestSystemConfiguration.cpp`, changes 21 occurrences of 1088 to 1096 (including the six-record size query of #22014) and adds one case: a 1088-byte buffer returns -1 with errno 12, a length of 1088, 1088 bytes copied, the byte after them untouched, `ki_structsize` 1096 and the right `ki_pid`. The values pinned are the console's from the probes above; the values of `ki_flag` and of the other unfilled bytes are not pinned.

Debt: there is no new fragment file. A second fragment on the same entry would be a fold error, which `tools/check_conventions.py` reports as an error, so the text is edited in the two merged fragments that are not folded yet: `docs/dev/debt/changes/fix-libkernel-sysctl-proc-list-size-estimate.md` (#22014, `kern.proc.proc`, 916 to 899 characters) and `docs/dev/debt/changes/fix-libkernel-sysctl-proc-pid-thread-id.md` (#21986, `kern.proc.pid` 869 to 997 and `kern.proc.pid_td` 953 to 995 characters, counted without the leading "- "). They are other authors' files, and the change to them is deliberate. `kern.proc.proc` now says the record is 1,096 bytes and that a PS5 payload process lists dozens of processes of that size, titles not measured; `kern.proc.pid` says the record is 1,096 bytes as a firmware 11.60 payload reports it and that here a 1,088-byte buffer gets `ENOMEM` after a 1,088-byte copy (the console's own result for that buffer is in the raw output, lines 12 and 15 of the first probe, and is not stated in the entry); `kern.proc.pid_td` says the console answers `ENOENT`. All three entries are at most 1000 characters. `tools/debt_fold.py --check` reports nothing for `kern.proc`.

### Tested
Measured on a PS5 with firmware 11.60 (`kernel_get_fw_version` 0x11600005), from a homebrew payload process (ps5-payload-sdk v0.45, elfldr). First probe 2026-11-17 at 23:35 UTC, second 2026-11-18 at 00:05 UTC, third 2026-11-18 at 04:36 UTC, fourth 2026-11-18 at 05:05 UTC (the console clock printed 01:17:39, 01:47:32, 06:18:05 and 06:47:41 and runs 1 h 42 min ahead of UTC). A title process may differ. In the first comment, the lines that print `ki_flag` and byte counts of the record (line 14 of the first probe and line 6 of the second) and the value of the first characters of `ki_comm` are removed and replaced by a note; the other lines keep their numbers. The second comment has the two other probes as printed.

| Call | PS5, payload process, firmware 11.60 | AnyPS5 `main` before | here now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kern.proc.pid` size query, own pid | 0, length 1096 (first probe line 18) | 0, length 1088 (code, `:199-228`) | 0, length 1096 (test) |
| `kern.proc.pid`, 1096-byte and 0x448-byte buffers | 0, length 1096, `ki_structsize` 1096 (second probe lines 4, 5, 7) | 0, length 1088 | 0, length 1096 (test) |
| `kern.proc.pid`, 1088-byte buffer | -1, errno 12, 1088 bytes changed (first probe lines 12, 15) | 0, 1088 bytes, no error | -1, errno 12, 1088 bytes (new test case) |
| `kern.proc.pid`, 512-byte and 1-byte buffers | -1, errno 12, 512 and 1 byte changed (first probe lines 16, 17) | -1, errno 12, same copy (`CopyOut` `:39-54`) | unchanged |
| `kern.proc.pid`, pid -1 and 0x7fffffff | -1, errno 3 (first probe lines 21, 22) | -1, errno 3 | unchanged |
| `kern.proc.pid`, parent pid and pid 1 | 0 (second probe lines 11, 12) | errno 3 (entry states it) | unchanged |
| `kern.proc.proc`, record size | 1096 in all 91 records read (fourth probe line 5) | 1088, one record | 1096, one record (test) |
| `kern.proc.pid_td`, own pid | -1, errno 2 (third probe lines 18 to 20) | one record per live thread | unchanged, entry states the console result |

author: byran-carlock
body:
Follow-ups to PR #189 from its final review. Work rigger keeps is reaped and never deleted from under a person, and a refusal from git never costs a tree its files. The session host's version is checked against the minimum the hooks need. The conflict-marker and stop checks now hold in the cases they missed, and a speculation lane git refused keeps its work through every way its group can end.

## Conflict-marker text in a new file

Before, the checkpoint's conflict-marker scan read tracked files only, so marker text an agent wrote into a new file was committed: the checkpoint's `git add -A` stages it. Now the scan of the tree also reads untracked files that are not ignored (`git grep --untracked`), the set the checkpoint's add stages. In a file git does not track, only a complete set counts: a start, a separator and an end line, in that order. Git writes a conflict hunk only into a path its index holds, so a start or end line alone in an untracked file (a quoted email, a fixture showing half a conflict) is the file's content. A staged new file is in the index and keeps the tracked rule. Otherwise the marker rule is the one the stack uses: a marker set counts only when HEAD does not already carry it at that path, so a complete set in an untracked file always counts, since HEAD carries nothing at its path.

The refusal says that conflict-marker text is present in file content the commit would carry, and gives both ways out: resolve it, or, where the lines are meant to be there, commit the file yourself so its committed text holds them. The stop hook asks the same question through the same function, so it holds a session over such a file too, and the text it holds the session with states the same rule.

Each path the scan hands git is read literally, through `literal_pathspec`, the one helper `own_commits_refusals` now uses for its pathspecs too. Before, git read a path starting with `:` as pathspec magic: a new file named like `:notes.md` was never scanned, and one named like `:(x).md` made git exit 128, which held the run as a fault.

Tests: one `worktree.rs` table, each row asking the stop hook's check and the checkpoint itself:

- a complete set in a new file, in a new file inside a new directory, in a new file `status.showUntrackedFiles=no` hides from status, and, on Unix, in new files named like short and long pathspec magic each refuse both, with nothing committed or staged; the hook's line names both ways out, and the kept tree carries the file as it stands;
- a complete set in an ignored file, which no commit takes, refuses neither, and so does a start line alone in a new file, an end line alone in a new file inside a new directory, and a start line alone in a new file status does not list;
- an end line alone in a staged new file refuses both.

## A conflict hunk around a carried marker set is refused

Before, markers were counted per complete set, so a conflict hunk wrapping a marker set HEAD already carried matched the carried set, and the checkpoint commit and the merge finalize let it through. Now each counted line is keyed by its path, whether it sits in a complete set or alone, and its text. In a file git tracks, a start or end line in no complete set counts on its own, against HEAD for a commit and against HEAD and MERGE_HEAD for a finalize, through the one function both use, so the hunk's own start and end lines count as introduced. A lone `=======` is still never counted.

Departure: two rows pinned as allowed at b98b87d7, "a start marker with no end" and "the markers out of order", are now refused in a tracked file. Letting a stray start or end line through is what let the wrapping hunk through. In an untracked file they are still allowed (above).

## A carried marker set on a CRLF checkout is not introduced

Before, the count keyed on the raw line with its trailing carriage return, so on a checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` a carried set counted as introduced and every checkpoint was refused. Now each line is keyed without its line ending.

## A plan in a nested output under an untracked parent holds the stop

Before, with the output at `docs/specs/` inside a `docs/` git tracks nothing in, status named only `docs/`, which lies outside the output. `own_commits_refusals` found nothing, so the stop was allowed with the plan uncommitted. The conductor then:

1. read the same function once the session ended (conductor.rs, the plan commit), found nothing, and took the outcome as no plan;
2. recorded the producer unit as integrated with no artifact;
3. at the stage's end, found no work in the unit's tree, so it removed the tree and deleted its branches.

The plan was lost without a word.

Now the output and the rest of the tree are each read by their own scoped status read. An entry outside the output that is a parent of it (`docs/`) is read again file by file with the output left out, and each file is named by its first directory beside the output. So a refusal names `docs/scratch.md` or `docs/notes/`, never `docs/`, which holds the plan. The Stop hook and the conductor call the same function, so the fix covers both. The outcome is now "uncommitted", which fails the attempt and keeps the tree.

Departure: a parent entry is not simply counted as inside the output. Under that rule, a `docs/` holding only scratch files would hold the session for work that never lands. A row pins that it raises no refusal.

## Status records come from standard output alone

Before, the whole-tree status read returned git's standard output and standard error together. A warning git gives on standard error, such as `could not open directory 'sealed/': Permission denied`, was parsed as a changed path by every reader of a tree's changed paths: the checkpoint's marker scope, a review round's residue guard, and the gate verb's changed-path line. The scoped read the nested-output fix adds took standard output alone, which would have left two status readers with different stream rules. Now one status read serves every caller (`status_read`). It parses records from standard output and keeps any warning beside them. `path_is_dirty` still reads a tree git warned on as dirty, now on purpose, since git could not vouch for the whole tree, and its doc says so. Every caller that decides whether a tree may be removed asks `path_is_dirty`.

Tests: a clean tree beside a directory git cannot open reads dirty and names no path; a new file beside it reads dirty and names that file alone.

## Held refs by their full names

Before, `held_refs` read `%(refname:short)`, which git shortens ambiguously beside a tag or remote ref of the same name, so a held ref could be listed or deleted under the other ref's name. Now it reads full refnames, strips the held namespace itself, and every delete names the full ref.

Tests: a held ref beside a same-named tag and a same-named remote ref is listed and reaped by its own name, and the tag and the remote ref stay.

## Every keep has a reaper, and a person's commit on a kept ref stays

Before, integration deleted only the unit's current kept ref. A unit that escalated twice had its first keep set aside under `rigger/orphaned/<unit>-<sha>`, as did a keep made while the kept ref was checked out, and nothing reaped either: `reap_held_refs` deletes only refs whose tip HEAD's history holds, which a keep commit never is. And `delete_kept` deleted whatever the kept ref pointed at, a commit a person made on it included.

Now each kept tree is recorded, by ref and commit (`Kept`), on the `UnitFailed` of the attempt that kept it (`kept`). The fold accumulates them on the unit, never overwriting an earlier one. A run reads them at its start. Where a unit's work lands (the single lane, the speculation winner, and the branch GC), `reap_keeps` reaps every recorded keep:

- each kept ref of the unit's (its own, and each one a recorded keep names) is deleted when its tip is a recorded keep, and set aside under `rigger/orphaned/` when it is not, so a commit a p

author: wrkode
body:
## Summary

Per-host agent enrolment now refuses to run while the manager can read the host-agent subordinate CA's key Secret, or holds common RBAC paths to it. Development builds only (`-tags virtrigaud_dev`). Release builds gain no flag and no behaviour change. No CRD or protobuf change.

**Why.** The chart's default `rbac.secrets.scope: cluster` lets the manager read every Secret. A compromised manager could read the sub-CA key and mint CA-valid host-agent certificates with no approval. The opt-in namespaced grant already existed, but enrolment was not tied to it.

**What changes.**
- **Chart.** With `experimental.hostEnrolment.enabled`, rendering fails unless:
  - `rbac.secrets.scope` is `namespaced`;
  - the enrolment and key namespaces are not listed as provider or workload namespaces;
  - `rbac.additionalRules` does not cover Secrets;
  - `caKeySecret` is set when a cert-manager signer is used.
- **Development manager, at startup.** It refuses enrolment when any of these is allowed, cluster-wide or in the declared key namespace:
  - read or write access to Secrets;
  - impersonation, ServiceAccount token creation, binding changes, `bind` or `escalate`;
  - pod entry paths (`pods/exec`, `pods/attach`, `pods/ephemeralcontainers`, changing a running pod) and `nodes/proxy`.

  A `SelfSubjectRulesReview` also catches name-limited grants. Any review error or incomplete rule list refuses.
- **New flag.** `--dev-host-enrolment-ca-key-secret=<namespace>/<name>`, required with a cert-manager issuer. It exists only in development builds.
- **Periodic re-check.** The same checks run in the admission gate every three minutes. No CertificateRequest is decided while they fail.
- **Warning only.** The manager logs a warning when it can create or change workloads in the key namespace, because access reviews cannot see admission policies.

## Limits (also in the guide)
- The checks are defence in depth against misconfigured RBAC. They do not prove the manager cannot reach the key.
- Grants in a third namespace are not reviewed.
- With the default `rbac.scope: cluster`, the manager can still reach the key through a workload unless an admission policy blocks it. The guide describes the policy.
- With an external PKI alone, the operator must declare the key Secret if the signer keeps its key in the cluster.

## Webhook authorizers
**Enrolment refuses on any cluster with a webhook authorizer in its chain, and there is no override.** Those clusters always report incomplete rules, and this commonly includes managed Kubernetes. The maintainer chose to keep this refusal for development builds. Tested with fake-client cases only, not on a managed cluster.

## Upgrade impact
Development setups that use enrolment must move to `rbac.secrets.scope: namespaced` and declare the key Secret. The Kustomize `config/rbac/role.yaml` grants Secrets cluster-wide, so a manager authorised by it now refuses enrolment until that grant is narrowed.

## Testing
- `make fmt`, `make lint`, `make test`, `make build`, `helm lint` and the `hack/verify-*` scripts: pass.
- Dev-tag lint of the changed packages: 0 issues.
- `go test -race ./cmd/manager` in both builds, and the controller dev suite with `-race`: pass.
- New tests:
  - fake-client cases for each review;
  - envtest with the chart's real RBAC under `rbac.scope=cluster` and `namespace`, and with name-limited grants;
  - a subprocess test that a real development manager exits;
  - chart render failures.
- The last commit changes two sentences of the guide; only the lab-name scan was re-run after it.
- Dev-tagged tests do not run in CI, because there is no dev-tag job. They were run locally.
- Automated security review ran four rounds. Rounds two and three found Major gaps, which are fixed. The final round found no Critical or Major defects, and its two doc findings are fixed here.

Not human-reviewed yet. Automated review is not human approval.

body:
## Summary

Merges upstream Triton `570e5b4dd1e2..93035c4472eb` (302 commits, `__version__` 3.9.0) into the TileIR backend. CUDA Tile IR stays at 13.4; the CUDA 13.5 upgrade is a separate pull request on top of this one.

### Merge

- `compiler.py`: keeps the target-bound driver and the TileIR load path; upstream's launcher shared-memory reservation and metadata `warp_size` apply to the non-TileIR path.
- `semantic.py`: takes upstream `make_tensor`; keeps the TileIR `gpu.barrier` bridge.
- Gluon tutorial 08: takes upstream (Gluon is not a TileIR frontend).
- CI files this repository had removed stay removed; the two customized workflows are kept.
- `README.md` is kept; upstream README edits are carried in `README.original.md`.

### Adaptations required by the new upstream and LLVM pin

- Honor `TRITON_FORCE_DISABLE_FP_FUSION` in the TileIR backend. Upstream now disables implicit FP fusion by default; the TileIR backend keeps its existing default (fusion on).
- Keep the CUDA Tile `SymbolName` trait when LLVM provides it, keep CUDA Tile textual formats non-strict on newer MLIR, and spell empty CUDA Tile shapes explicitly.
- Keep TileIR launcher float scalars parsed as double (upstream changed `ty_to_cpp`).
- Lower the CUDA NVVM intrinsic helpers that upstream now uses (exp2 FTZ, TF32 rounding, xorsign/abs min/max, E2M1x2 packing) and the packed FP4 maximum-code sequence to native TileIR operations.
- Lower `tt.approx_divf`, `tt.annotate` and the `div.full.f32` inline assembly used by the new upstream division tests.
- Accept `max_occupancy` as the TileIR occupancy tuning key. On TileIR it is a compile-time hint (capped at 32), not a launch-time cap; the previous `occupancy` key remains as an alias. README and tuning notes are updated.

### Fixes for existing TileIR issues found during the sync

- `rint` / `nearbyint` returned `+0.0` instead of `-0.0` for inputs in `(-1, 0)`.
- NaN-ignoring float `min` / `max` reductions returned `∓inf` instead of `NaN` for an all-NaN lane (the reduce identity is now a quiet NaN).
- The TileIR launcher allocated one attribute-name string per launch.

### Test classification

New upstream tests that hit existing TileIR limits are classified in the conftest tables without editing the upstream tests: checks that read a specific compilation stage (PTX, TTGIR, LLVM IR), compiler instrumentation (ConSan, IISan), the Gluon frontend, scaled dot products mixing two operand formats, AOT, and the launch-time `max_occupancy` tests.

## Testing

x86_64, NVIDIA B200 (sm_100), CUDA Tile IR 13.4, at `424d833bf`:

- TileIR FileCheck tests: 22 / 22.
- 64 test pipelines: 60 pass, 0 fail, 4 not applicable (`unit-language-test_clc`, `unit-language-test_reproducer` and `unit-instrumentation` contain only expected-failure cases; `unit-plugins` needs a plugin-enabled build).
- Pipelines with JUnit output: 18944 passed, 0 failed, 1512 skipped, 4982 xfailed. The two batched matmul pipelines: 0 failed.

Not run: the multi-GPU `distributed` pipeline, performance comparison, aarch64.

## Merge note

Please merge with a merge commit rather than a squash, so the upstream history stays connected.

author: emelin2004
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"emelin2004"} -->

## What broke
Telemetry for 0.1.35.18: 12 of 14 consoles crashed, and 58 of 59 crash reports are `RSX: Failed to compile fragment shader` (VKProgramPipeline.cpp:125). It happens in every game, including the XMB and `gs_gcm_basic_triangle.elf`. The shader logs from 8 consoles all show the same error:

```
ERROR: 'rop_control' : undeclared identifier
ERROR: '' : missing #endif
```

## Cause
#94 added an INVERT block to `RSXROPEpilogue.glsl` that tests `UWP_LOGIC_INVERT_BIT` in `rop_control`. On UWP, `GLSLCommon.cpp` always defines that bit, so every fragment shader contains this block. But `VKFragmentProgram.cpp` only declares `const uint rop_control` when the shader also uses alpha test, depth compare or range, ROP remap or programmable blending. Every other shader fails to compile.

## Fix
On UWP, `insertMainEnd` now always declares `rop_control`. The INVERT emulation still works the same way. Upstream (non-UWP) builds produce the same code as before. GL and the shader interpreter already declare `rop_control` everywhere, so they are not affected.

Scope: port-wide, one file.

## Checked
- I took a failing shader from a .18 crash log and ran it through `glslangValidator`. Before the fix it fails with the same `rop_control` error. With the declaration added it compiles to SPIR-V.
- Not built and not tested on a console yet.

Discharge a named native-dispatch obligation only when the actual selected lowering has no generic-tower edge and its operands satisfy an audited proof. Both censuses remain complete, but COMPLETE+EMPTY is not reached and whole-hub omission remains disabled.

## Changes

- Share native-member publication, namespace-pair admission/selection, and console call-shape admission between facts and lowering. A debug assertion checks certificate publication against the selected intrinsic.
- Require every generated copy, span, arity, operand shape and named/HIR twin to agree. Include computed class members and decorator arguments in that agreement.
- Certify selected Math.abs/round/min/max with Number operands, Number.isInteger/isSafeInteger with one primitive operand, and selected console.log with no arguments or one String plus thread-family never.
- Retain all unproved guards/protocols. Default console publication refuses its mixed Other/Console callee set; tests preserve that refusal and exercise console's positive route with namespace pairs off. Two nested Math.abs calls retain unequal fast/generic operands after inlining; JSON, strings, collections, now and cross-module bodies also remain open.

The user-visible surface is diagnostic proof metadata in `crates/perry-wpfacts/src/derive/dispatch/` and publication in `crates/perry/src/commands/compile/program_facts.rs`; `docs/src/internals/program-facts.md` documents the boundary. **Problema encontrado no código:** dois motores de geração de jogadores de seleção ainda usavam listas fixas brasileiras, independentemente da nacionalidade: (1) os 25 convocados IA da Copa e (2) os 11 companheiros persistentes na jornada do jogador.

author: bouweandela
body:
The `gh-pages` branch has grown to about 1.2 GB of (compressed) history, which makes every full clone of the repository large. This PR stops new simulation output from being committed to it, and adds a cleanup job to the Documenter workflow that removes old PR previews and simulation output and squashes the branch history.

## Where the size comes from

- **Tutorial simulation output.** `docs/make.jl` writes a `.gitignore` into the build so that `.jld2` output isn't deployed, but its pattern `examples/**/*.jld2` doesn't match `tutorial/*.jld2`. As a result `tutorial_floes.jld2` (60–100 MB each) and the other tutorial output files have been committed about 50 times. The current `gh-pages` files still contain 63 `.jld2` files totalling 1.4 GB, out of 2.5 GB for the whole site. No page links to them.
- **PR previews are never removed.** `push_preview = true` deploys every PR to `previews/PR<n>/`, and nothing deletes them. There are 24 previews now, 17 of them for PRs that are already merged.

## Changes

1. `docs/make.jl`: ignore `*.jld2` at any level in the docs build.
2. New `cleanup` job in `.github/workflows/Documenter.yml`, based on [Documenter's recommended cleanup workflow](https://documenter.juliadocs.org/stable/man/hosting/#Cleaning-up-gh-pages). It runs **before** the docs build, on pushes to `main` and on manual runs (`workflow_dispatch` on `main`):
   - deletes `previews/PR<n>` for every PR that GitHub reports as `MERGED` or `CLOSED`. Folders that aren't PR previews, and previews whose PR can't be looked up, are kept with a warning.
   - deletes all `.jld2` files
   - squashes the history into a single commit and force-pushes with `--force-with-lease`. On pushes to `main` this only happens when something was deleted; manual runs always squash.

   The build job runs after the cleanup, and also when the cleanup is skipped (pull requests, tags) or fails. As a result the docs deployment always pushes on top of the cleaned-up branch, which also starts the GitHub Pages rebuild. The workflow's existing `pages` concurrency group ensures no other deployment (PR previews, `main` or tags) pushes to `gh-pages` while the cleanup runs. Running on `main` also means it always has write access, including for PRs from forks. A PR closed without merging is cleaned up on the next push to `main`.

## Safety

- Apart from the deleted previews and `.jld2` files, the current files of `gh-pages` are kept exactly, so `dev/`, `v0.1.1/`, `stable`, `v0.1`, `versions.js` and the previews of open PRs stay online. Only earlier states of the branch are dropped. The git tags point at commits on `main` and are not affected.
- A backup of the current branch is available as `gh-pages-backup` (same commit as `gh-pages`, `0b34d88`). Once the cleanup has run and the site has been checked, delete the backup, because the space is only freed after that.

## After merging

The merge itself triggers the first cleanup, followed by the `dev` docs deployment.

1. Check that https://subzero-sea-ice.github.io/Subzero.jl/stable/ and `/dev/` still load.
2. Delete `gh-pages-backup`.

Existing clones keep the old history until each contributor runs `git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now` (or waits for automatic cleanup). A plain `git fetch` handles the force-push without errors. Contributors who don't want `gh-pages` locally at all can exclude it:

```bash
git config --add remote.<name>.fetch '^refs/heads/gh-pages'
```

## Testing

- Validated the YAML and ran `shellcheck` on the cleanup script.
- Ran the cleanup script with `bash -e` against a local repository with the same file layout as the current `gh-pages` (empty files), the real PR states from GitHub, and two extra folders `previews/foo` and `previews/PR99999`:
  - **push to `main`:** deleted the 17 previews of merged PRs and all 63 `.jld2` files, and kept `dev/`, `v0.1.1/`, the `stable` and `v0.1` links, `versions.js` and the 7 previews of open PRs, in a single commit. The two extra folders were kept with a warning.
  - **second push with nothing to delete:** no push, and the branch was unchanged.
  - **manual run:** squashed again, without deleting anything else.
- The job itself can only run on GitHub once it is on `main`.

author: kiko0301
body:
## Problem

`RAGMiddleware` kept the static-mode reply scratchpad in a single slot on
the instance:

```python
self._cached_inputs: list[TextBlock | DataBlock] | None = None
```

`on_reply` filled it with the reply's own inputs and read it back in
`on_reasoning`; `on_reply`'s `finally` set it to `None` unconditionally.
That is per-instance state, but a middleware instance may legitimately be
shared across agents — `ReplyBudgetControlMiddleware` says so explicitly
and keeps all of its runtime state in `agent.state.middle_context` for
exactly this reason:

> The middleware is stateless on the instance itself — all runtime state
> lives in `agent.state.middle_context`. This means the same middleware
> instance can safely be shared across multiple agents.

`RAGMiddleware` documented no such restriction, but two concurrent replies
through one instance broke each other:

```text
A's reply queried KB with: ['bob: what is the refund policy?']
A's actual user message   : ['alice: how do I reset my password?']
B searches after A finished: 0
```

Agent A's first reasoning step retrieved against **Bob's** message and
injected those chunks into Alice's reply; then Alice's reply finished
first and its `finally` wiped the slot, so Bob's reply performed no
retrieval at all — silently losing the RAG context it was configured for.

## Fix

Key the scratchpad by the agent it belongs to, and drop only that agent's
entry when its reply ends:

```python
self._cached_inputs: dict[int, list[TextBlock | DataBlock]] = {}
# on_reply:      self._cached_inputs[id(agent)] = blocks
# on_reply/finally: self._cached_inputs.pop(id(agent), None)
# on_reasoning:  cached_inputs = self._cached_inputs.get(id(agent))
```

Each reply now searches with its own inputs and cleans up after itself,
whether the instance serves one agent or many.

## Test

- `tests/middleware_rag_test.py`:
  `test_concurrent_agents_keep_their_own_inputs` drives two overlapping
  replies through one `RAGMiddleware` instance and asserts that each
  agent's first reasoning step embeds its own message, and that the
  second agent still searches after the first reply has ended. It fails
  on `main` with
  `- ['bob: Are cats mammals?'] / + ['alice: Where is Paris?']`.
- Existing suites pass: `tests/middleware_rag_test.py`,
  `tests/middleware_test.py`, `tests/rag_knowledge_metadata_test.py`,
  `tests/rag_vdb_qdrant_test.py`,
  `tests/service_chat_middleware_factory_test.py` (94 passed).
- black / flake8 / pylint / mypy clean on the touched files.

author: zranitm
body:
## What

The design for PvP, from the user's request on 2026-11-18: "lets build pvp feature - match making - for now we only have bot", then "we'll have 1v1 and 3v3 then 15 v 15 in a bigger map for guild war, we dont add guild now and all of them can be experienced with bots".

- **Product:** a new group, I. PvP:
  - [I1. PvP matches](docs/product/features/pvp/i1-pvp-matches.md): the queue, offers, bots, equal stats and the arena build, combat between players, and leaving.
  - [I2. Arena: 1v1 and 3v3](docs/product/features/pvp/i2-arena.md): best of three rounds.
  - [I3. Battlefield: 15v15](docs/product/features/pvp/i3-battlefield.md): capture points.
  - [I4. PvP rating and ranks](docs/product/features/pvp/i4-pvp-rating.md).
- **Tech:** [docs/tech/pvp.md](docs/tech/pvp.md):
  - the pvp module (queue, matcher, offers, ratings);
  - match instances opened on demand, with a return point;
  - one hit path for mobs' and players' hits;
  - server-side bots that press keys through the players' checks;
  - round and capture rules, the protocol, failures in area 55, the client, balance targets, testing, and a six-PR build.
- **Pointers:** pages that said "no player-versus-player" now point at matches, and the Arena window takes V in the default key bindings.

## The user's choices

- **1v1 and 3v3:** best of three. 1v1 rounds last 60 s and 3v3 rounds 90 s, with the larger HP share winning on time.
- **15v15:** in this feature, as an open queue won by capture points. Guild war comes later.
- **Stats:** equal for everyone; the player's own traits and bar are their build.
- **Matching:** players first, then bots after 15 s.
- **Rewards:** rating and rank only, one rating each for 1v1 and 3v3.

## Libraries considered

Every library below was cloned and read, never built or run.

- **go-openskill** (MIT):
  - The source is clean: pure math over gonum, with no exec, network, cgo or init code.
  - But pkg.go.dev lists no importers and it has no tag.
  - Instead, Weng-Lin's Bradley-Terry is written in-house, about 80 lines, and pinned to openskill.py vectors.
- **go-behaviortree** (Apache-2.0):
  - The source is clean and it's maintained.
  - But it has 5 importing modules, and the bots would use 2 of its node types.
  - Instead, the bots use a priority list.
- **Glicko-2 libraries** rate one-on-one only, **TrueSkill** is patented, and **Open Match** needs Kubernetes.

author: siebe-studio
body:
## What changes for CLI users

- **A fourth question, "Add a GitHub Actions workflow that deploys it?"**, with no as its default, and `--github-actions` / `--no-github-actions` to answer it up front. With yes, the project also gets `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which checks every change, deploys `main` to `prod` and gives each pull request a `pr-<n>` preview stage with a comment linking to it. `stacks/github.ts` mints the scoped Cloudflare token the workflow needs and stores it as repository secrets. The project's README gains a "CI/CD" section with the setup steps.
- **`create-effect add github-actions`**: lays the same files over a project created earlier. A file its owner changed is left alone and reported with a link to what it would have become.
- **`create-effect.json`**: every project records its features and the CLI version that last changed it. `add` reads it and stops when the feature is already there. A project without the file is treated as having no features.
- **Foldkit DevTools for agents**: every new project has an `.mcp.json` for `@foldkit/devtools-mcp`.
- **Generated `AGENTS.md`**: points agents at the docs the dependencies ship (`node_modules/effect/AGENTS.md`, the Alchemy and Foldkit `llms.txt`) and says where tests go.
- **Generated README**: credits Siebix next to the create-effect link.
- **API telemetry** (first commit): the template's API Worker provides `Cloudflare.Telemetry()`.

## Website

The home page says "Four questions" with the new one in the sample session, lists the deploy workflow, logs and traces, and agent tooling under "What you get", and drops CI/CD from the roadmap.

## How it is built

The workflow's files live in `apps/cli/overlays/github-actions` and are laid over the template by `layer` in `src/template.ts`: `package.json` is merged, Markdown is appended, and any other file replaces the project's only while that one is still what the template wrote. The overlay carries its own `alchemy.run.ts`, so a change to the template's has to be made in both; the root `AGENTS.md` says so, along with new sections on changing what the CLI creates and on what each test file is for.

## Verified

- `bun run check`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run test` pass. The e2e test creates a project with and without the workflow and runs each one's lint, typecheck and tests.
- A test asserts that `add` ends in exactly the files the flag creates.
- In a real terminal: answering y writes the workflow, Enter leaves it out, and the flags ask nothing. `add` works on a fresh project, says "already has" on a repeat run, keeps an edited `alchemy.run.ts`, and refuses a folder that is not a project.
- A generated project with the workflow added ran under `bun run dev`: the website greeted by name through the API with no console errors.
- The DevTools MCP server, started as the project's `.mcp.json` starts it, found the open browser tab and returned the live Model and Message history.
- `alchemy provider check-env`, as the workflow runs it, passes in a generated project with the three variables set.

## Not verified

- The generated workflow has not run on GitHub, and `stacks/github.ts` has not been deployed. Its token permissions are this repository's list minus Access and zone rights.

## Worth a look

- Previews are served on public `workers.dev` addresses, unlike this repository's, which sit behind Access.
- The generated workflow does not pin a Bun version.
- `create-effect add` is now the subcommand, so a project called `add` is created as `./add`.
- Projects from 0.1.1 have no `stacks` entry in `tsconfig.json`; after `add`, `stacks/github.ts` passes lint there but is not typechecked.
- For a kept file, `add` links to the overlay on `main`, which exists only once this is merged.
