author: grzegorz914
body: On a webOS 11 TV whose key handler Glasshouse knows, the remote's **Guide** button can now open Glasshouse Home's guide. It is offered as **Glasshouse Home's guide** on the Remote tab and as **The remote's Guide button** in Internet TV on the Home tab, as on TVs before webOS 11. It opens the guide from any app and from Home itself, and closes Home's player first when a channel is playing. On Live TV and the HDMI inputs LG's own guide stays, as before. On the same TVs the **Input** key can open an app, an HDMI input, Live TV or the Glasshouse input bar, set on the Remote tab, and the bar is offered on the Inputs tab as before webOS 11. It cannot do nothing, and no media key or action can be set on it, as LG's key handler only launches an app there. Setting either key restarts the TV's screen once, and setting it back does too. It takes about 35 s until Glasshouse Home has LG's Home's place again, and the dashboard says so. A TV whose build is not listed is not offered the choice, and nothing on it is changed. ## Technical details **Why it was not possible.** webOS 11's key filters are native. `libappLaunch.so` reads the configd value `com.webos.keyaction.tvGuide` for `id` and `fgAppIdsForByPass` only, launches the app with a fixed `{}` as parameters, and ends the key without launching when that app is already in front (`isForegroundApp`). Glasshouse Home opens its guide from the launch parameter `{ glasshouse: "guide" }`, which never arrived, and with Home in front the key did nothing. **The Input key** has no value to read. `libappLaunch.so` opens LG's input picker from a text kept in `.rodata`, `{"id": "com.webos.app.quickinputpicker"}`, which two places in `handleHotkeys` use. The findings are in `TV-RESEARCH.md`. **`lib/guidepatch.js`.** Reads `/usr/lib/libappLaunch.so.1` and finds its build by SHA-256 with the places it changes put back, so a change anywhere else refuses it. For a build it lists, it makes a copy in `/var/lib/tvweb`, bind mounts it over LG's file and restarts `surface-manager-daemon.service` once to load it. There are two changes, each made only while its key is set. For Guide, three edits: the launch parameters point at `{"glasshouse":"guide"}` kept in padding at the end of `.rodata`, and the branch after `isForegroundApp` becomes a `nop`. For Input, the picker's text names the app or input chosen, an id of up to 30 characters as the text is 41 bytes long, which takes all but two of the 30 apps and inputs a C5 offers. Setting a key back mounts a copy without its change over the last. A copy that is mounted cannot be written over, so each has a name of its own, and the ones left are deleted at the next change after a restart of the TV. Nothing of LG's is in the repository, LG's file on the rootfs is not touched, and a restart of the TV puts LG's library back. One build is listed, an OLED48C31LA on webOS 11.2.0, firmware 44.00.92, and another is added with its SHA-256 and edits once it has been tried. **`lib/remotekeys.js`.** On the native path, `action:homeGuide` is a choice of the Guide key alone, offered when Glasshouse Home has a playlist and the build is listed. Set, `com.webos.keyaction.tvGuide` becomes a launch of `com.webos.app.home` with LG's `fgAppIdsForByPass` kept, after the change above is in place. With no Glasshouse Home guide to open, or a build that refuses the change, the key is left to LG as on the earlier TVs, and a set key is applied again at each server start, which also makes the change after a restart of the TV. **As LG has it** writes LG's value back as for the other keys. The Input key is offered on the same builds. It takes an app, an input or the input bar, whose app is put on the TV and kept loaded as for the JavaScript filter, an id the text can hold, and neither nothing nor an action. `lib/inputbar.js` offers the bar on webOS 11 where the handler can be changed. After the compositor restarts, the view of Glasshouse Home under it is gone and sam still counts it as running, so `lib/home.js` closes it and opens it again once the compositor is up, as it does after a wake. Without that, the watchdog gave LG's Home the place and Glasshouse Home came back only at the next press of Home. **Dashboard.** The Remote tab and the Home tab offer the Guide choice, the Remote tab and the Inputs tab the Input key's, and each carries a note on the restart (2 new strings, translated into every language file). The key's tile shows the choice by name, and the Input key's list leaves out what its launch cannot do. **Docs.** `docs/TV-CHANGES.md`, `docs/dashboard/remote.md`, `docs/dashboard/home.md`, `docs/dashboard/inputs.md`, `docs/tested-tvs.md` and `docs/development/TV-RESEARCH.md`. **Tests.** `test-remotekeys-webos11.js` registers a small stand-in library as a listed build. It checks that only the Guide key is offered its choice, that setting it writes the configd value with LG's bypass list and mounts and restarts once, that **As LG has it** puts LG's value and library back, and that without a Glasshouse Home guide the key is LG's. For the Input key it checks that an input, an app and the bar each change the text and nothing else, that nothing, LG's picker and an id that is not one are refused, that the bar's app is put on the TV first and taken off with the last key, that the Guide key's change and the Input key's stay as the other is set and cleared, that no mounted copy is mounted or written again, and that Glasshouse Home is told at each restart of the compositor. A library not listed is left alone and refused. ## Testing - OLED48C31LA, webOS 11.2.0, firmware 44.00.92. With the changed library mounted by hand while trying the edits, **Guide** opened Glasshouse Home's guide from another app, from Glasshouse Home itself and while an Internet TV channel was playing, where it did nothing before. **As LG has it** gave LG's guide again, and setting and clearing it from the dashboard moved `com.webos.keyaction.tvGuide` between LG's `com.webos.app.livemenu` and `com.webos.app.home`. - After a restart of the TV, with LG's library back and the key still set, Glasshouse built the changed library, mounted it and restarted the compositor itself, and **Guide** opened Glasshouse Home's guide again without anything done by hand. - Input key on the same TV: set to HBO Max, **Input** opened it. Set to the input bar, **Input** opened the bar, and **LG's list** gave LG's list again after the copy of the library was written under a name of its own, which a first version without that did not (the write failed, as the earlier copy was mounted). After each restart of the compositor Glasshouse Home came back by itself, which before the change it did only at the next press of Home. - `scripts/check-all.sh` passes, except the dashboard browser tests, which were skipped locally because Playwright is not installed.

author: mattxlau
body:
## What this does

Option B, bridge only. Worked out on a Fire TV Cube (Fire OS 7.7, Android 9), where Keep watching only ever showed Plex. Three commits:

**1. Fire OS package names** (`fix(bridge)`). A Fire TV ships YouTube, Prime Video and HBO Max as Amazon's own builds, under other package names than the Google TV ones in `bridge/apps.py` (`com.amazon.firetv.youtube`, `com.amazon.firebat`, `com.hbo.hbonow`; Fire OS's own Settings is `com.amazon.tv.settings.v2`). The bridge took them for apps it had no name for: the watch loop never logged what played in them, `/api/apps` said they were not installed, and every launch and deep link went to a package the TV does not have. Each app can now list its other builds (`"packages"`), `BY_PACKAGE` knows them, and a new `pkg_of(app)` picks the build this TV has at every launch, intent, `wait_for_app`, installed check, Keep watching card, `finish_play` and move site (audited one by one, listed in the commit). `public()` adds `packages` to `/api/apps` where there are several. A Google TV with the usual packages behaves exactly as before: `pkg_of` returns the canonical package whenever the TV has it or the installed list is not read yet.

**2. YouTube videos as a list of their own** (`feat(bridge)`). YouTube stays out of Keep watching (it buries everything else, and a video's name matched to a film put that film in the household's taste, issue #23). Now a video that has played the one minute is written to `history.jsonl` as a line with `"type": "video"`, by the title the media session gave, with no finder call, no poster and no year. `store.history()` leaves those lines out, so Keep watching, the picks, the taste, the Ask context and `/api/history` never see one; `store.videos()` / `keep_videos()` list them alone. `GET /api/continue` keeps `items` and gains `videos`: one card per title, newest first, at most 10, within 30 days, per person and TV, `kind: "video"`, honouring the same remove by hand. Opening one (`POST /api/continue/open` with its id) searches YouTube's installed build for the title through the `https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=` link, never the show finder; where the link does not take, the app opens by itself. Spotify, Twitch and Moonlight are still never logged.

**3. Review fixes** (third commit), found by a review pass before opening this:
- `launch_app`, `search_in_app` and `h_continue` read the installed list first (`settle_builds()`, the cached 1800 s read `play()` already does), so the first launch or card after a bridge start goes to Amazon's build instead of a 504.
- Kids mode: `kids_list` hands the TV the build it has for each allowed app and show, so the kids dock on a Fire TV keeps its YouTube, Prime Video and HBO Max tiles (docs say what option A gets instead).
- A video is hidden under its own key (`video:<title>`), so removing a Bluey video never removes the show "Bluey" from Keep watching, or the other way round.

**4. Amazon's YouTube opens its search from the link Alexa sends it** (fourth commit, found on the Cube). The web results link brought Amazon's YouTube to its home and nothing else, so a video card only opened the app. The link Alexa's own voice search sends that build, `youtube://search?query=<title>`, opens its results page, cold or already open, with or without the BROWSABLE category and the `isVoice` flag (the page takes about ten seconds to draw). `SEARCH_LINKS_BY_PACKAGE` holds the build's own link and `search_link()` picks it for a video card and for `search_in_app`; a Google TV keeps the web link it was tested with.

**5. A video card opens the exact video** (fifth and sixth commits). The TV's media session gives a video's title, its channel as the subtitle and its length, never its id, so a video line now keeps `channel` and `duration_ms`, and the bridge finds the id the way the move feature already does: `move.youtube_video_id` reads YouTube's public results page (no key, no sign in) and answers only on a sure match of the title and the channel or the length, else "unsure", because a wrong video is worse than none. The lookup is warmed in a task of its own as soon as the line is written, so the watch loop never waits on the network, and the task is held until done; an OK press waits on that same task for up to 15 s, an unsure answer is remembered ten minutes so a press does not pay the lookup again, and a line with neither channel nor length (one written before this, or a session that gave neither) goes straight to the search. A sure id goes to the installed build as its watch link (`"method": "deeplink"`, `video_id` in the answer) and YouTube resumes it from the account's own history; else the search link, else the app. YouTube's title and channel also no longer go through the show finder in `media_read` (a channel named like a show and a video like one of its episodes came back renamed).

**6. A video card shows YouTube's own thumbnail, and a found id is kept on disk** (seventh and eighth commits). A found id goes to `bridge/data/video-ids.json` (keyed by normalised title and channel, at most 500 entries, the oldest dropped; a hand edited or non-object file reads as empty and heals on the next write), so a bridge restart or the lookup's six hour memory never costs a press the network again. A card whose id is known carries `video_id` and `backdrop` = `https://i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/mqdefault.jpg` (16:9, no bars, served for every video), which the TV home fetches straight from YouTube's image host the way it already fetches JustWatch posters, with no page change; a card not yet found starts the lookup in the background from `GET /api/continue` (one task per video, the unsure mark honoured), so the next fetch of the row has the picture. Note for review: `store.py` now imports `move` for the id pattern and the title key, so the store's import chain pulls in aiohttp and the ADB library; it runs in the same venv, but it is a heavier import than before and easy to lift into a tiny module if you would rather.

Docs in `bridge/API.md`, `docs/CONFIG.md` (Keep watching, kids `apps`), `docs/TV-COMPATIBILITY.md`, `docs/UPDATES.md`.

## Limits, written down

The exact video depends on YouTube's public results page, which has no contract: the lookup already retries the page's other layout, and when the page stops being readable the card falls back to the search. A title many channels reuse is told apart by channel and length; a live stream has no length, so its channel decides.


The Fire OS packages were read from one Cube with `pm list packages`; Netflix, Disney+ and the rest were not installed there, so only the three apps (and Settings) have alternates. Naming an alias package explicitly in `/api/launch` opens whichever build the TV has, not that literal string. A video keeps only its title: the media session gives no video id, so opening it is a search, not the video itself.

## Tested

- `tests/test_fire_os_packages.py` (11) and `tests/test_youtube_videos.py` (11), no network, plus the existing kids mode and Keep watching suites; the whole Python suite (963 tests) passes but for `test_lg_power`'s `test_off_again_right_after_off_turns_on`, which errors the same way on main under `discover` (order dependent, passes alone).
- On a real bridge (Debian container) with the Fire TV Cube: `/api/apps` now reports YouTube, Prime Video and HBO Max installed with their `packages`, and `/api/continue` returns `videos` next to the Plex `items`. Then with someone at the TV: two YouTube videos (a live stream and a music video) played past the minute were logged as video lines under `com.amazon.firetv.youtube` and came back as two `videos`, and a Friends episode in HBO Max was logged as a show under `com.hbo.hbonow` and became the first Keep watching card, with its poster. Opening a video card from the TV home then sent the web results link and Amazon's YouTube showed its home (the same finding as killy10o10/couch-tv#4 on a Fire OS 8 stick); with the fourth commit the bri

author: kikoncuo
body:
## Why

The production host ran out of disk twice in November. About 8 of the ~18 GB/week of growth was the same tooling installed over and over. Every `qm-sbx-*` container starts from an image with an empty `/opt/agent-venv` and no office tools, so agents `pip install` and `apt-get install` into that container's own writable layer, and Playwright, pip and Hugging Face write their downloads into each scope's home volume.

## What agents actually install (read-only survey of production, 2026-11-18)

I read every sandbox container's writable layer and every `qm-home-*` volume from the host. Nothing was started or changed.

**46 sandbox writable layers, 27.5 GB in total**

| Path | Total | Containers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/opt/agent-venv` | 11.3 GB | 37 |
| `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` (ffmpeg, LibreOffice and Tesseract libs) | 5.5 GB | 25 |
| `/usr/lib/libreoffice` | 3.6 GB | 16 |
| `/usr/share` (pocketsphinx, fonts, tessdata) | 2.1 GB | 25 |
| `/tmp` (agent scratch, not tooling) | 3.9 GB | 46 |

**Home volumes: per-scope download caches**

| Cache | Total | Homes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.cache/pip` | 5.1 GB | 58 |
| `.cache/ms-playwright` | 4.0 GB | 6 |
| `.cache/huggingface` (faster-whisper small/tiny/base) | 2.5 GB | 6 |

**Install frequency across the 46 sandboxes**
- pip packages:
  - 17–20 sandboxes: python-docx, beautifulsoup4, requests, numpy, openpyxl, pypdf, PyMuPDF, pyyaml
  - 10–12: xlsxwriter, tabulate, python-pptx, psutil, playwright
  - 4–9: pymupdf4llm 9, faster-whisper 6, reportlab 5, httpx 5, pdfplumber 4
- apt packages: tesseract-ocr 19 (spa 11), LibreOffice ~16, ffmpeg ~15, poppler-utils 7.
- Most of the venv bytes are PyMuPDF (1.5 GB across containers), Playwright (1.5), numpy (1.3), onnxruntime (1.0, pulled in by pymupdf4llm and faster-whisper) and ctranslate2 + av (1.4, faster-whisper).
- Left out because few sandboxes install them: matplotlib (3), pandas (0), opencv (3), edge-tts (3), rembg (1), azure-cli (1).

## Change

- **`local/Dockerfile`.** This is the local-sandbox-only layer on top of the shared `fly/Dockerfile` base. It now bakes:
  - apt: LibreOffice writer/calc/impress, Carlito/Caladea/DejaVu fonts, Tesseract with Spanish, poppler-utils and ffmpeg.
  - Python: every package at or above the install threshold above. The versions, transitive ones included, come from the new `local/agent-constraints.txt`, followed by `pip check`.
  - Playwright's chromium in `/opt/ms-playwright` (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`).
  - faster-whisper's `small` model in `/opt/hf-cache` (`HF_HUB_CACHE`).
  - `PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1`.
- **Build-time checks that fail the build.**
  - `soffice --version` runs.
  - Tesseract lists `spa`.
  - `pdftotext` and `ffmpeg` run.
  - Playwright launches its chromium.
  - Whisper `small` loads with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- **`local/agent-constraints.txt` is an exact-pin lock.** It is the `pip freeze` of a clean venv resolved with `--uploaded-prior-to 2026-11-11`, so every version is at least 7 days old, the same cool-down `.npmrc` uses.
  - The build fails unless `pip freeze` equals the lock exactly, so a new transitive dependency cannot slip in unpinned.
  - The lock resolves identically on arm64, which `qualify-local-provider.sh` uses.
  - The staleness fingerprint includes the lock.
- **Caches are baked, not shared.** A writable cache volume mounted into every scope would let one scope plant wheels, browsers or model files that another scope then runs.
- **Nothing baked goes under `/root`.** Docker copies an image's `/root` into each new home volume. The build ends with `rm -rf /root/.cache`, and the image's `/root` is 68 KB, the same as the base. `HF_HOME`, and with it the HF token, stays in the home volume.
- **Agents are told what is installed.** The local backend's environment profile, rendered into the system prompt as "Runtimes" and "Installed CLIs", now says the standard local image has the baked Python packages and `soffice`, `tesseract`, `pdftotext` and `ffmpeg`, and asks agents to check before installing. Without this they would keep running `apt-get install libreoffice`. It is worded as "the standard local image" because images built by the `qm` CLI's docker backend do not carry these tools.
- **Core resolves the sandbox image on every provision (`src/sandbox/local-sandbox.ts`).**
  - Before, core memoized the image ID once per process. A rebuild then needed a core restart, and a container created from the moved tag before that restart was recreated on every turn.
  - Now `preflight()` keeps only the daemon check memoized. It resolves `LOCAL_SANDBOX_IMAGE` to an ID each time and repeats the fingerprint check only when the ID changes.
  - Containers still run by tag. A rebuilt image reaches each scope with no restart: a turn that finds its container **stopped** on the old ID recreates it on the new image.
  - A **running** container is always reused as is. Teardown parks with `docker stop` only when nothing is live, so a turn in progress, or a container kept warm for a background job or browser session, is never removed under it, whichever core process asks. Neither is a container this core still holds a handle on, even if it was stopped from outside.
  - A failed `docker image inspect` only says "image not found, rebuild" for "No such image". Any other failure reports Docker's own error.
  - Running by the memoized ID was tried and dropped. With the containerd image store, a rebuilt tag makes the old ID unresolvable at once, and on overlay2 the nightly prune removes it.
  - Regression tests:
    - `a rebuilt tag moves a parked sandbox onto the new image without a core restart, never a running one`, which covers a live handle and keep-warm from a second sandbox instance;
    - `a Docker failure after startup is reported as itself, not as a missing image`.
    - The fake Docker refuses to run a stale `sha256:` reference.
- **`test/local-sandbox-image.test.ts`** checks:
  - baked caches sit outside `/root` and are set before the steps that fill them;
  - `HF_HOME` is not moved;
  - pip keeps no cache;
  - there is exactly one pip install, bound to the lock, with only bare package names (no extras or version specifiers), every one pinned there;
  - each of those `ENV`s is set exactly once;
  - the build checks that `pip freeze` equals the lock;
  - the build clears `/root/.cache`;
  - the environment profile names every baked package and binary, matched as whole words.
- **`deploy/dokploy/README.md`:**
  - builds from `Omniloy/qm`, because the baked layer exists only in this fork;
  - drops the redundant manual base build;
  - explains the lock and that runtime model and browser downloads now live in the container layer;
  - documents how a rebuilt image rolls out.

## Image size trade-off

Measured unpacked on disk with `du`, `linux/amd64`, on the current base:

| | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Whole image | 2,399 MB | 5,045 MB | **+2,646 MB, once** |
| `/opt/agent-venv` | 23 MB | 865 MB | +842 |
| `/opt/ms-playwright` | — | 701 MB | +701 |
| `/opt/hf-cache` | — | 464 MB | +464 |
| `/usr/lib/libreoffice` | — | 271 MB | +271 |
| `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` | 334 MB | 584 MB | +250 |
| `/usr/share` | 197 MB | 296 MB | +99 |

Compressed, the image goes from 0.88 GB to 2.22 GB.

That is 2.6 GB once on the host. Today the same tooling costs about 20 GB spread over 46 writable layers, plus 11.6 GB of pip, Playwright and Hugging Face caches in home volumes. It pays for itself after about three sandboxes that would otherwise have done a full install.

## Verification

- Inside the built image:
  - python-docx writes a DOCX, `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf` turns it into a PDF, and `pdftotext` reads the text back.
  - `tesseract` lists eng, osd and spa.
  - Playwright launches its baked chromium with no download.
  - `WhisperModel('small')` loads offline.
  - Re-running `pip install` for baked packages reports "already satisfied".
  - All 17 baked modules import.
- Rollout path, driven

body:
This PR covers the Form S changes made on V2. W, WH and P forms are intentionally left unchanged for now.

Changes

Structured applicant address

Text fields use title-case typing.
Includes a migration for the new columns. The migration has not been run, so run it only after review.
Date of Birth rules

Earliest year is 1935 and minimum age is 18, with new error messages.
Applied on the register page (client and server) and on Form S apply, edit, renew, alteration and digitisation views.
Input format is DD-MM-YYYY, with a flatpickr date picker.
§7b Board meeting gate

The applicant types the Date of Meeting and meeting number.
The server checks them against cc_board_details through the new form-s.board-meeting.verify route (throttled to 60 requests per minute).
A match enables the organisation, member, address, designation and document fields. A mismatch disables and clears them, and shows "Date of Meeting and Meeting details do not match the Board records."
The server re-checks on submit. The board table is no longer embedded in the page.
Unchanged, locked rows are exempt.
Chronology checks (Form S only)

Year of passing must be at least DOB year + 15 and not in the future.
Experience From must be at least DOB + 18 and not in the future.
Experience To must not be in the future unless "Till date" is selected.
Enforced in the browser and on the server at store, update, draft_update, draft_submit, draft_renewal_submit, submit-returned and alteration store.
Also enforced at PayU initiate() on the saved data, because paid N/R applications are saved as drafts.
Renewal, alteration and digitisation applications, and returned applications, may carry unchanged legacy rows over from finalised applications. New applications are strict.
New FormSSubmissionGuard service holds the rules. New payu-error.blade.php is shown in the payment popup when the check fails, and no transaction is created.
Declaration text

The single-sentence declaration from apply-form-s is now used on the Form S edit, renewal, alteration and digitisation views.
Other

PayUPaymentController::initiate now checks that the application belongs to the logged-in user.
config/database.php uses a PHP-version-safe constant for the MySQL SSL CA (fixes the PHP 8.5 deprecation).
Impact on existing data (read-only check on the dev DB)
Saved Form S applications that would be blocked at payment: A 1/15, D 8/31, N 18/56, R 0/13. Examples are DOB 1997 with year of passing 2010, and board meeting mismatches. Applications already processed are not re-checked.

Not included, to be done separately

updatePayment hardening. It does not yet require PayU success, and its routes are outside the auth group. initiate() also takes amount from the browser.
The simulated "UPI" payment path.
DOB, format and declaration changes for the W, WH and P forms.
Wiring the new address columns into the model and save paths.
Known issues

A renewal draft save can be blocked by the client check while the server accepts it.
The PayU popup status polling continues after a failed start.
Nothing has been tested in a browser yet. Verification was php -l plus read-only DB scripts.

author: raghav19
body:
## Summary

The agent builds with `buildctl`. `buildkitd` runs in a second gVisor container. No listener, `crane` or context registry is needed.

```text
sandbox.service                       (agent, gVisor, no network)
  Requires/After
sandbox-builder.service               (NEW, buildkitd rootless, gVisor, no network)
  tmpfs state  -> destroyed at each stop
  buildkitd.sock in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sandbox/buildkit
       ^ mounted read-only in the sandbox at /run/sandbox/buildkit
agent: buildctl build ... --output type=oci,dest=image.tar   (BUILDKIT_HOST is set)
```

```diff
 .sandbox/
 ├── sandbox.container            # Requires the builder, mounts the socket folder
-├── runsc.conf                   # runsc only
+├── runsc.conf                   # runsc and runsc-builder (network=none, host-uds=create)
 ├── justfile                     # setup links the builder unit
+├── builder/
+│   └── sandbox-builder.container   # the Quadlet unit and its limits
 └── image/tools/infra.toml       # + buildctl
+├── docs/diagrams/architecture.{drawio,svg,png}   # shows the builder
+├── docs/internals.md            # the builder in the cast, phases, lifetimes and design reasons
+├── README.md                    # flows of setup, run, image build and build in the sandbox (mermaid)
-├── build/                       # the Valkey queue (compose, ACL, tests)
+docs/research/remote-buildkit-for-agent-sandbox.md   # the research and the spike results
```

A stop or a restart of `sandbox.service` stops the builder. The cache and all build files go with it.

![Architecture of the sandbox and the builder](https://github.com/raghav19/engineersdaybook/blob/df90a83cf6989614562da9f62829d5550e809a96/.sandbox/docs/diagrams/architecture.svg?raw=true)

## Evidence

- **Before:** `podman build` cannot use a remote BuildKit. The plan needed an unwritten Go listener (`build.sock`), `crane` and a context registry.
  **After:** these checks ran on the host (Podman 6.1.4, `runsc` release-20261102.0), with the unit files of this branch.

```text
systemctl --user start sandbox-builder   -> active, container "(healthy)"
HealthCmd=false (never healthy)          -> `systemctl start sandbox` fails in 3 s: "A dependency job for sandbox.service failed"
buildkitd frozen (SIGSTOP) after start   -> health fails, builder killed (exit 137), systemd restarts it, new builder "(healthy)"
client in a 2nd runsc container (host-uds=open, socket folder read-only):
  buildctl debug workers                 -> lists 1 worker
  buildctl build (COPY)                  -> OCI tar arrives in the client
  buildctl build (RUN echo ... > /marker) -> passes, OCI tar arrives in the client
  (base image from --oci-layout, because the builder has no network)
write marker in builder tmpfs; restart builder -> marker gone
systemctl --user start sandbox           -> builder starts first
systemctl --user restart sandbox         -> new builder container id
systemctl --user stop sandbox            -> builder container removed
no-new-privileges=true                   -> rootlesskit hangs, no socket (so it stays off)
limits tested: MemoryMax=2G, CPUQuota=200%, TasksMax=512, tmpfs 1 GB (TasksMax is 1024 in the unit; not retested)
  idle: 75 threads, 230 MB.  small build: 95 threads, 300 MB
  RUN dd ... count=1500 (1.5 GB) -> "No space left on device", builder stays healthy, 0 restarts
```

Detection of a frozen builder takes about 100 s, because the health start period is 60 s.

Not tested: `just sandbox setup` (needs `sudo` and the Bitwarden token), `buildctl` in the real sandbox image (the image is not rebuilt), a `FROM` pull through iron-proxy, and a push to a registry. I removed the test links from `~/.config/containers/` after the tests.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Revert the commit and run `just sandbox setup`.

**Blast Radius:** sandbox start.

- `sandbox.service` now requires the builder. If the builder does not start, the sandbox does not start.
- After the merge, run `just sandbox setup`, which links `runsc.conf` and the builder unit. Without the new `runsc-builder` entry, the builder fails to start.
- The first start of the builder pulls `moby/buildkit` (pinned by digest). This needs the network of the host.
- Run `just sandbox build` to put `buildctl` in the image. Until then, `buildctl` is not in the sandbox.
- The builder gives code execution in the builder to any holder of the socket. BuildKit has no authorization. The builder holds no secret and has no network.
- This PR removes the Valkey queue (PR 314): `build/`, the `queue`, `queue-check` and `queue-down` recipes, and the `podman-compose` and `yq` requirements of the justfile. A host that ran the queue keeps its `sandbox-queue` container and `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sandbox-queue/`. Remove them by hand. The Bitwarden secret `QUEUE_WORKER_PASSWORD` is not used any more.
- The untracked Go listener (`code/agent-sandbox/builder/`) is not part of this PR.
- Open item: `network=none` for the sandbox container (TODO in `runsc.conf`).

author: mcroomp
body:
Lets phones record video for experiments. Each recording is saved in the experiment's directory, next to `experiment.txt` and `mavlog.json`.

## How it works
- `serve --https-port` also serves LinkHub over HTTPS. Phone browsers only allow camera access over HTTPS. The self-signed certificate is kept in `<data-dir>/tls/` and is only regenerated when the LAN address changes, so each phone accepts the certificate warning once.
- `run_linkhub_ui.cmd` now listens on `0.0.0.0` with HTTPS on port 9443.
- **Phones register independently of experiments.** **📷 Cameras** in the header shows how many phones are connected and opens a QR code for `https://<lan-ip>:9443/camera`. On the phone, tap **Enable camera** once and leave the page open. After that, a reload reconnects without a tap.
- The phone page checks in with `POST /v1/camera/{device}/heartbeat` every 1.5 s, and the reply says whether an experiment is running. The phone starts recording when an experiment starts and finishes the file when it stops. It then waits for the next experiment.
- **Disconnect** on the phone finishes and uploads any recording, releases the camera, and removes the phone's registration with `DELETE /v1/camera/{device}`. It then closes the page, or shows a Disconnected screen with **Reconnect** if the browser won't close it.
- Recordings upload as ordered 2 s chunks to `POST /v1/experiment/{id}/video/{stream}?seq=N`. Each recording gets its own file, `video-<device>-<rand>.webm` or `.mp4`, which grows as chunks arrive. Repeated chunks are acknowledged without being written again, so phones can retry; a gap in the sequence returns 409. The final chunk is accepted for up to 120 s after stop.

## Testing
- `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. Tests cover phone registration and heartbeat, the camera status endpoint, ordered chunk appends and TLS host detection.
- `npm run build` passes.
- Live server check: a browser tab acting as a phone, with a synthetic canvas video standing in for the camera, enabled once. It then automatically recorded two experiments in a row; each directory got its own finished `video-*.webm`. The header showed "📷 1 camera".
- Disconnect during a running experiment: the recording was saved and marked finished, the registration was removed, and the tab closed.
- Not yet tested with a real phone.

body:
## Summary

**1. Dedicated Reservation group.** The "Reservation" nav link and the pages behind it were gated on `Recevio_Reception` OR `Recevio_Helpdesk` — anyone in either group automatically got access, with no way to grant or withhold it per person. Added a dedicated `Recevio_Reservation` group, seeded via migration, assignable from the Users page.

### ⚠️ Rollout — action needed right after this merges

This is a **hard cutover, not additive**. Nobody currently has `Recevio_Reservation` — the "Reservation" link disappears from **everyone's** nav the moment this deploys. An admin needs to assign the group to whoever should keep using it right after this merges.

**2. Blank personal info on the profile page.** Showed stale `AdminProfile.first_name`/`last_name`/`email` (only ever filled by the disabled LDAP backend) instead of the real, populated `auth.User` fields. Fixed.

**3. AttributeError generating the BHP PDF.** Stamped `visitor.end_time` (only set at checkout) instead of `start_time` (always set) — crashed for anyone still on-site. Fixed.

**4. New kiosk "Confirm guest" host-signature flow.** A visitor's host can now sign on the kiosk to confirm they've received their (approved, still on-site) guest — new `Visitor.host_signature`/`host_signed_at` fields, new kiosk screens, shown on the GuestBook detail page and used as the BHP PDF's "Brüggen employee signature" (preferred over the old admin-profile signature). Per your explicit choice, this replaces the kiosk start screen's settings gear button entirely — printer settings are no longer reachable from the kiosk UI. Also removed the unused Send/Print columns from Pending Approvals, and fixed the notification bell clearing itself the instant it's opened instead of when staff actually visit Pending Approvals.

**5. DataError importing hosts from Excel (`/hosts/import/`).** `Host.phone` is `max_length=9`; Excel stores phone numbers as plain integers with the `48` country-code prefix (e.g. `48668376832`), which Python reads back as an 11-digit string — 2 over the column limit, crashing the whole import with `value too long for type character varying(9)`. Added a normalizer that strips the country-code prefix (and any `+`/spaces/dashes), defensively keeping just the last 9 digits of whatever's left so an unexpected format truncates instead of crashing.

## Test plan
- [x] `python manage.py check` — clean
- [x] `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` — no pending `GuestBook` changes (only the pre-existing, unrelated `background_task` drift)
- [x] 102 tests passing in total; 5 new this round cover the phone normalization (country-code prefix, separators, already-short, overflow-truncation) and an end-to-end import of the exact kind of row that crashed in production

author: davidlinnnn
body:
Prototype for #240. **A side track:** the December pilot ships on PostgreSQL as built, with the outbox queue and ADR-0009's feed ([#78 C39](https://github.com/davidlinnnn/data-ingestion/issues/78#issuecomment-6949497546)). This PR changes no pilot code. Its verdict feeds #239, the post-pilot port to MongoDB, which gates PROD.

## Summary

The question: can a change stream copied into a feed collection replace the Change Feed, with nothing missed, repeated or out of commit order per Document, through tailer takeover, a woken stale tailer, reader restart and oplog loss? On MongoDB 8.2 (the company's major), it can, under four conditions.

```text
tailer (lease holder, epoch E)
  watch revisions (inserts only)
  per batch, one transaction:
    insert feed entries at '%06d%012d' % (E, seq)   # duplicate position => fenced
    update lease where epoch == E: token, seq       # last write; 0 matched => fenced
  on ChangeStreamHistoryLost (286):
    t_rec = fenced majority write
    snapshot-scan revisions at t_rec, insert what the feed lacks, reopen at t_rec
```

```diff
 docs/prototypes/mongodb-admission-prototype/
+├── VERDICT-240.md         # the answer, the ADR-0009 inputs for #239, the list for #137
+├── exp5_feed_tailer.py    # writers, two tailers, reader, faults, checks
+├── exp5_run.sh            # every full run, in order
+├── evidence/8/exp5-*/summary.json
 ├── rs.sh                  # + major 8 (8.2.12, ports 37081-37083)
 ├── summarize.py           # + experiment 5 table
 ├── evidence/RESULTS.md    # regenerated, + experiment 5
 └── README.md              # + exp5, three harness faults
```

## Evidence

Every number is in `evidence/RESULTS.md`, Experiment 5.

| Run | Committed | Missed / repeated / out of order | Takeover (s) |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Sequence, lease update first, 7 faults | 125,732 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 4.0–4.8 |
| Derived, lease update first, 7 faults | 125,732 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 4.2–5.0, one **80.2** |
| Sequence behind the epoch, lease update last, 7 faults + 2 freezes | 125,732 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 4.0–5.1 |
| 3 in-transaction freezes, lease update first | 37,273 | 0 / 0 / 0 | **61–81** |
| 3 in-transaction freezes, lease update last, plain sequence | 37,273 | 0 / 0 / 0 | **68–88** |
| 3 in-transaction freezes, lease update last, epoch in front | 37,273 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 4.2–4.9 |

- **Before:** the positive controls break the checks. With no fence, sequence positions gave 16 repeated and 16 out of order. With no recovery, 5,618 and 2,318 changes were missed.
  **After:** with the fence and recovery, every run shows 0 / 0 / 0, and all 17 woken holders were fenced.

- At 12 changes/s, the delay from commit to the projection's read was p50 76 ms, p99 160 ms.
- The derived control without the fence did not fail. Its positions deduplicate themselves; the verdict says why that is no guarantee.

**Door:** two-way

Adds docs and throwaway prototype scripts only. The raw records (170 files, 210 MB) stay out of git and are hashed in `EXCLUDED.sha256`.

author: lisachenko
body:
## Summary

This is a plan only, with no implementation yet. `docs/prometheus-metrics-plan.md` sets out how to expose Prometheus/OpenMetrics metrics from every worker of a fork family through the arena:

- **Core design:** each worker claims a shard, and each series has one cell per shard. The hot path is a plain store through a view that is bound once per process. It takes no lock, and no update is lost because each word has a single writer. A scrape adds up the shards.
- **Repository split:**
  - Generic primitives go here. These are an `Arena` float view and process recovery, `Ipc\ShardTable`, `Ipc\CellPlane` and `Ipc\FixedIndex`.
  - Everything that knows about Prometheus goes in a new repository that depends on this one.
- **Types covered:** Counter, Gauge (seven aggregation modes), classic Histogram, GaugeHistogram, Summary (windowed mergeable quantiles), native histograms, Info, StateSet, Unknown, exemplars and `_created`.
- **Exposition and endpoints:**
  - Text 0.0.4, OpenMetrics 1.0 and protobuf, selected by content negotiation.
  - An in-band handler, PSR-15 middleware or a forked exporter process.
  - A deployment matrix covering FPM with preload, pcntl/Swoole, RoadRunner and FrankenPHP.
- **Delivery:** a memory budget formula, phases with gates, and open questions for the maintainer.

## Evidence

`spikes/s18-sharded-metric-cells.php` measures the paths the design chooses between. It was run on PHP 8.5 NTS on a 4 vCPU VM:

| Path | ns / increment |
|---|---:|
| `AtomicInt::add()`, uncontended | ~500 |
| `AtomicInt::add()`, 4 workers on one cell | 6 000–7 000 |
| `Arena::readWord()` + `writeWord()` | ~110 (also loses 46–77 % of updates when shared) |
| bound view, one cell per worker | ~17 uncontended, ~45–60 with 4 workers |
| bound view, cells 8 B apart (false sharing) | ~125–140 |

With one writer per cell, the totals were exact on every run.

## Notable findings recorded in the plan

- `PersistentStore::bootShared()` needs a live `Arena` object, so an FPM worker cannot reach an arena that was created in `opcache.preload`. Supporting FPM will need an arena recovery entry point.
- RoadRunner starts its workers with `exec` rather than `fork`, so they are not a fork family. The README's "blessed setups" should be checked against this.
- A view cast out of a temporary holder `CData` keeps pointing into that holder. Once the holder is freed, writes silently go nowhere.

## Test plan

- [x] The spike runs to exit 0 against this package's `Arena` (twice)
- [ ] Spike S18 has not yet been re-run on PHP 8.4. That re-run is part of Phase 0 of the plan.

author: cluelessuk
body:
## What

Require Intel’s `UpToDate` status by default when `c8s verify` or `c8s cds verify` checks a TDX quote. This combines Aamir Rasheed’s work in #1804 and #1805 for #1802.

## Why

A genuine TDX quote can come from a platform Intel rates `OutOfDate`. Operators can now pin the VM’s measurements and require an acceptable Intel status in the same command.

## Why is this the best solution?

The pinned attestation library already authenticates the quote, collateral and component statuses. The CLI selects the accepted statuses once. The local verifier selects the online TDX path in one place and shares the quote and measurement checks with its other callers.

## Review focus

- Online verification rejects a disallowed status with exit 2 and returns exit 3 when required collateral cannot be obtained within the deadline.
- The verdict reports the least favourable component status and the earliest signed next update across TCB information, QE identity and both revocation lists.
- A saved signed quote checked against live Intel PCS produced exit 2 by default, exit 0 with `OutOfDate` explicitly accepted and exit 3 with an expired deadline. On a live TDX deployment, run `c8s cds verify "$CDS_URL" --image-policy-file "$CDS_PIN" -o json` with the CDS address and its expected pin.

body:
Closes #190

## Plugin tools run inside keel (#190)
keel's harness builds a plugin's MCP server (keel-git, keel-db, keel-ci, keel-cluster, keel-library, keel-links) once per engine and runs each tool call in a thread with the agent call's key. Before, every agent call / KeelBot turn started each plugin server's Python just to list its tools (the kept list never matched: the key is in the env), and every tool call started it again.

Measured (KeelBot turn, instant stand-in model, Git plugin on): first turn 2.35 s → 1.23 s, next turns 1.6–1.75 s → 0.26 s. One git tool call ~0.6 s → in-process.

## Agents use their tools (#191)
- A part's `mcp` can name `base` tools (never deferred). Git: git_status, git_diff, git_log, pr_status.
- `prefer`: Bash command patterns a tool covers (git status/diff/log/show/blame/branch, gh pr view/checks, gh run, kubectl logs/describe/get, psql/mysql/sqlite3…). A matching Bash call ends with a one-line hint naming the tool, once per tool per call.
- The system prompt gets a short "keel's tools for this project" part: each server's prompt, the tools in the list and the ones to load, and to use them over Bash when one fits.

## Review comment box streams KeelBot's answer (#192)
- Web: the answer shows as KeelBot writes it (helper.delta); helper.finished fetches the stored answer at once (polls 0.4 s, then 1.5 s as fallback).
- JetBrains 0.5.4: live text as it arrives, and helper.finished wakes the poll.

keel 0.37.0 · Git plugin 1.1.0 · Database 1.0.1 · CI 1.0.1 · Cluster 0.3.1 · Review 1.2.1 · JetBrains 0.5.4

author: subhangr
body:
Lane C of the Slack bridge: `integrations/slack-bridge`, the Slack connector runtime. It speaks bridge runtime protocol v4 as provider `slack`.

**Stacked on #1504** (the frozen v4 contract). Until #1504 merges, this diff also shows its commits. I'll rebase onto `origin/main` once it lands.

## What's in it
- A new standalone npm package outside the bun workspace, with its own lockfile, like `whatsapp-bridge`. Its only runtime dependency is `ws`.
- `src/runtime/protocol.ts`: a byte-identical mirror of the canonical protocol. The glob added to the contract test in #1504 checks it.
- `socket-mode.ts`: a minimal Socket Mode client.
  - `apps.connections.open` is called with the xapp token as the Bearer.
  - `hello` marks the socket live.
  - Every envelope is acked with `{envelope_id}` before any work is done.
  - On `disconnect` (`refresh_requested`/`warning`) it opens a fresh socket at once. `link_disabled` and other reasons back off.
  - Backoff on drops; ping liveness; honours Retry-After on `apps.connections.open`.
- `connection.ts`, one Slack app install:
  - `auth.test` (scopes from the `x-oauth-scopes` header) produces `state linked` + `account`. On a Grid org install, `teamId` falls back to `enterprise_id`.
  - Tokens are sealed under `stateKey` (AES-256-GCM, 0700/0600, atomic rename).
  - Bad tokens produce `logged_out` with Slack's code (`app_token: <code>` for the xapp token). A held token Slack later refuses is wiped.
  - With no credential stored: `no_credential`. `disconnect{logout}` deletes the sealed bytes.
- The allowlist guard (D28): an event from a channel that isn't connected is acked, counted and dropped, and only its channel id is read. Outbound to such a channel is refused, and DM ids are never accepted.
- Inbound:
  - text: mentions are shown as names and the ids kept in `mentions`; links and escapes are rendered;
  - threads: `thread` and `replyTo` name the root;
  - files: `MediaRef`, handle = file id;
  - reactions, converted to unicode;
  - edits: `message_changed` with `edited` only, so unfurls and reply-count updates are filtered out;
  - deletes;
  - bots: the runtime's own messages are skipped, others are marked `bot`;
  - `users.info` is cached for an hour;
  - `/tm8` slash commands: `body` `/<cmd> <args>`, `slashCommand {'/tm8', text}`, id `cmd:<trigger_id>`. Commands from a channel that isn't connected get an ephemeral note in the ack;
  - `message` and `app_mention` events for the same message are merged, and so are envelope replays;
  - channel rename/archive/left/joined become `conversation-state`.
- Outbound:
  - `send`:
    - tm8 markdown is converted to mrkdwn and split at about 3,500 chars, keeping code fences balanced; later parts are retried on 429;
    - `thread_ts` is only used when the value looks like a ts, so a `cmd:` id posts to the channel;
    - `send.voice` becomes `username`/`icon_url`.
  - Files: streamed from `outbound-media` with its length, then `getUploadURLExternal` → upload (no token on the URL) → `completeUploadExternal`. With a voice, the caption goes as a separate voiced message.
  - `react`: replaces the reaction the runtime put on that message earlier (📨 → 👀 → ✅). `cmd:` targets give `not_reactable`.
  - `media.fetch`: `files.info`, checked against the channel, then `url_private` with the bot token, limited to `maxBytes`. The token is only sent to Slack hosts.
  - `conversation.list`: `users.conversations`, paginated.
  - A 429 settles as `{reason:'ratelimited', retryable:true, retryAfterSec}`. Other Slack codes are mapped to retryable or permanent.
  - `typing`/`read` are ignored. `group.*` frames are answered with an error.
- Heartbeat with drop counters. Several connections run in one process.
- `README.md` covers the dev run, env vars and tests. Lane E owns the Dockerfile, manifest and SETUP guide.

## Tests
`cd integrations/slack-bridge && npm ci && npm test && npm run typecheck`. That is 90 node:test cases (the same runner as whatsapp-bridge) and takes about 6 s.

The suites run the real `HttpWsLink` + `Runtime` + Socket Mode client between two fakes:
- **`test/fake-slack.ts`**, a reusable fake Slack:
  - the Web API;
  - a Socket Mode WS server that records acks;
  - upload and `url_private` endpoints;
  - 429 and error injection;
  - the Grid org-install `auth.test` shape.
- **`test/fake-tm8.ts`**: the `/v2/bridge-runtime/*` POSTs plus the push WS.

The suites are connect, inbound, outbound and units. The contract mirror test passes with the new copy.

Not tested: a real Slack workspace (no tokens here); the runtime against the real tm8-server (that is the later end-to-end test, which can import `fake-slack.ts`); Enterprise Grid org-wide installs where methods need `team_id`.

## CI
CI does not run integrations suites, and the lane push token has no `workflow` scope. The job is therefore committed as `integrations/slack-bridge/ci/slack-bridge.workflow.yml`: path-gated on this package and the canonical protocol, node 22, `npm ci`, mirror `cmp`, typecheck, test. It needs someone with workflow scope to `git mv` it to `.github/workflows/slack-bridge.yml`.

author: staticfloat
body:
General's AutoMerge rejects a breaking release (a major bump, a minor bump of a 0.x package, or any bump of a 0.0.x package) unless its release notes mention "breaking" or "changelog". `contrib/release.sh` only wrote the commit list. That is why BinaryBuilderToolchains 0.4.0 (JuliaRegistries/General#176727) was rejected until registration was re-triggered with hand-written notes.

## Changes

- **Breaking check:** `release.sh` compares the new version with the previous release using Julia's `[compat]` semver rule. The previous release is the tag the notes are collected from, or else the `Project.toml` version before the bump. If there is no previous release, the release counts as non-breaking.
- **New option:** `-b/--breaking "<text>"`, repeatable, one list item per use. A breaking release with no `--breaking` is refused before anything changes, also with `--dry-run` and `--edit`. The error shows how to supply the text.
- **Notes format:** with breaking text the notes read:
  ```
  Release notes:

  ## Breaking changes

  - <text>

  ## Changes

   - [sha] subject
  ```
  Non-breaking releases keep the old format. `--registrator-comment` still prints the whole section.
- **Cleanup fix:** `git commit --edit` and `git tag -F` strip lines starting with `#`, which dropped the `##` headings. The commit now uses `--cleanup=scissors` when editing, and the tag uses `--cleanup=whitespace`.

## Testing

All runs were in a scratch clone at the commit before the 0.4.0 release, with the `BinaryBuilderToolchains-v0.4.0` tag removed.

Dry runs:
- BinaryBuilderToolchains 0.3.7 → 0.4.0 is refused without text, with or without `--since BinaryBuilderToolchains-v0.3.7`. With text it produces the format above.
- A patch bump to 0.3.8 keeps the old format.
- LazyJLLWrappers 1.2.5 → 2.0.0 is refused, and 1.2.5 → 1.3.0 is allowed.
- The fallbacks for no tags and for `--since <sha>` work.

Real runs:
- With and without `--edit`, the commit and tag messages are identical and keep the headings.
- `-r` reprints the full notes section.

author: a-jay85
body:
After a `go()` tap opens a new screen, the next tap's `ui.plan` couldn't reuse the look before (it showed the old screen), so it slept about 0.4 s and looked again to be sure the button stood still. That was most of the ~1 s between the menu showing and the TAG tap.

Now `ui.plan` remembers where each button stood when two looks agreed it was still (`RESTED`, keyed by target, screen and window bounds). Later in the run, one fresh look that finds the button within 0.01 of that spot counts as still. That's still two spots that agree, one of them from earlier in the run. A different layout (or a screen still sliding) won't match, so it falls back to the usual two looks.

Only `go()` taps use it (`tap(rested=True)`), because `go()` taps again if a tap is lost. Never for tiles: a list still loading shows old tiles in the same spots.

Menu to a known tag row, ready to tap (`speedtest.py tags --n 5`, rounds 2-5):
- iPhone (Fallen): 3.5-3.6 s -> 2.6-3.0 s.
- Pixel (CPD): main 5.9, 4.1, 5.9, 4.6 s; this branch 4.5, 5.7, 4.2, 3.4 and 3.8, 3.6, 5.1, 4.0 s. The Pixel's looks vary a lot, but it's no slower.
- No "didn't land" in any of the three runs (15 menu and 15 TAG taps with the change).

Tests: readers and lints the same. `tests/layout.py --record`: ui.py gained `RESTED`.

Siblings: `ui.plan` callers are `base.tap` and `ui.cmd_tap`/`cmd_press` (command line, `rested` off). `base.tap` callers other than `go()` keep `rested` off (tick boxes and taps with no retry).
Speed elsewhere: every script's `go()` taps go through this one `ui.plan`, so all of them get it (MENU, TAG, DONE, CLOSE, TAGS and the rest, on both phones). Nothing else to copy.

The same-name `tap`s in gift.py, trade/phone.py and trade/trade.py tap fixed spots through `base.click` and never call `ui.plan`. The same-name `plan`s in ivc, pvpc, roster and trade plan runs, not taps.

author: susannschmelzer29-lab
body:
## What changed

Steps 2–5 of `14_career_pipeline/PLAN.md`, built and tested:

- **Step 2, job research** behind one source interface: the Arbeitsagentur Jobsuche API, the state career portal of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern (read directly, robots.txt allows it) and three job boards via Apify actors. Each ad gets a work model (four classes, with a reason) and a match score from the skills vocabulary, with met and missing skills named. Unclear ads are set aside in their own list, split by two tested rules.
- **Step 3, bottlenecks:** profile and market bottleneck, pooled over runs, each with its sample size, plus their overlap. One history row per run date.
- **Step 4, recommendation:** certificate or project side by side, only after the same gap led three runs. A learning goal in the private config pauses new recommendations. Effort and cost come from a catalog (`vocabulary/learning.yaml`) and read "bitte prüfen" when empty, never an invented figure.
- **Step 5, learning loop:** a ratings file in the private folder; from 20 ratings the rule is compared with a logistic regression and a decision tree under cross-validation. A model ranks only if it wins and the owner opts in, and a regression check falls back to the rule. Search terms and source switch-off are only proposed. Changes of these settings are logged with the previous value.

## Why

The pipeline should research the job market weekly and recommend next steps, without ever deciding on its own and without leaking the owner's private search criteria into this public repository.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Privacy:** the owner's wishes (work model, hours) are read from the private config only. A hard-coded ordering that encoded them was found during this work and made config-driven. Test fixtures use neutral, fictional values. The changed files were scanned for contact data, company names from the private folder and tokens: none found.
- **Scraping:** the plan excluded scraping. The owner chose to allow the Apify job boards on 2026-11-18; the exception and its limits are written down in PLAN.md. One public-sector portal was checked and deliberately left out.
- **Counting in code:** no language model decides a score, a gap or a recommendation.
- **Data needs time:** steps 3–5 are built and tested, but the market bottleneck, the recommendation and the learning loop only say something after several weekly runs and 20 ratings. The report states this instead of guessing.
- **Open:** the `schedule` key in the private config is not read yet; the scheduled task is fixed weekly. Must-have and nice-to-have requirements are not told apart yet.
- **New dependency:** `scikit-learn` (learning loop).
- **Tests:** 133, offline, fictional data (`python -m pytest` in `14_career_pipeline`).

author: stevechurch
body:
Phase 4a–4d of #8: GitHub pull requests at parity with GitLab merge requests. Stacked on #14.

## What now works on a pull request

- **Findings** on a line (`POST pulls/{n}/comments` on the current head, re-anchored to the diff as GitLab's are) or on the whole PR or a line the diff no longer has (`POST issues/{n}/comments`, starting with its `path:line`).
- **Reply** (`addPullRequestReviewThreadReply`; to a plain comment it is a new conversation comment), **resolve** and reopen (`resolveReviewThread`/`unresolveReviewThread`), **comment**.
- **Approve** (a review with `APPROVE`), **withdraw** (dismissing your latest approval).
- **Hold** is a `REQUEST_CHANGES` review carrying the hold note; lifting it dismisses that review with the release note. It blocks a merge where branch rules require reviews.
- **Your own PRs**: merge (`PUT pulls/{n}/merge` on the head you saw, the way GitHub's button would), merge when green (`enablePullRequestAutoMerge`) and cancel, mark ready, choose reviewers and ask again, **Update branch** (`update-branch`), retry a job and retry failed Actions runs.
- **Agents**: review and fix agents run on GitHub PRs, and queued findings carry `provider: 'github'`. A PR from a fork cannot be fixed here, as its branch is not on `origin`.
- **Full auto** reviews GitHub PRs, with your login on each MR's own forge, and runs with GitHub on and no GitLab token. With GitLab and GitHub both off it says there is nothing to review.

Caps now true: `post`, `hold`, `withdrawApproval`, `rebase`, `autoMerge`, `ownMr`, `agents`, and `retry: 'actions'`. `todos` and `generalThreads` stay false: GitHub has no to-dos, and a comment on the whole PR cannot be resolved.

The involved search gains `reviewed-by:@me`, as any review you send takes GitHub's request away.

## Not done

- `brief`, `approvers`, `myMrs` and `myEvents` (standup, game and board) still read GitLab only.
- Post all sends one review comment per finding rather than one batched review.
- A fine-grained token now needs write access to pull requests and Actions; the manual says so, Setup still lists the read scopes.

## Testing

- New `engine/src/github.writes.test.ts`, `github.own.test.ts`, `auto/github.test.ts` and cases in `lib/github.test.mjs`, against the fake GitHub. Each new behaviour checked failing without its change.
- The GitHub golden baseline is unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Final validation (`mise-pnpm/verify.sh`) ran `mise install --locked --dry-run` for every tool in the lockfile, ignoring the lock-group verification modes recorded by `prepare.sh`. Under mise >= 2026.11 with `MISE_SAFE=1` this always fails for Conda tools, even when their group is verified by regeneration (observed in maya0513/vfox-moonbit#91).

## Change

- `verify.sh` reads `$RUNNER_TEMP/lock-groups.json` written by `prepare.sh` and runs the locked dry-run only for tools in groups with `"verify": "locked"`, per lockfile.
- Groups with `"verify": "regenerate"` are skipped; they were already re-locked and compared during preparation.
- When the file is absent or the array is empty, the previous blanket behavior is kept, so consumers without lock groups are unaffected.

## Tests

New regression tests in `tests/mise-lock-groups.test.ts` (all fail against the old script, pass with this change):

- final validation dry-runs only the tools of locked groups
- final validation skips the locked dry-run when every group regenerates (with a dry-run failure injected)
- a failing locked dry-run still fails final validation

Full `mise-lock-groups` suite: 25/25 pass. `shellcheck` clean.

Closes #56

author: tamircohen28
body:
## Why

Dependabot alerts #39 and #49 (high): GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5. zod < 4.6.6 can exhaust memory validating oversized collections, and the 3.x line gets no fix.

## What

- Root `package.json`: `"overrides": { "zod": "^4.6.6" }`. The published `@production-master/mcp-tool-contract@0.1.0` declares `zod ^3`, and publishing a new contract version is a separate step. The override puts the contract, the MCP SDK (`^3.25 || ^4.0`) and mcp-server on one patched copy.
- `packages/mcp-server`: `zod ^3.24.2` → `^4.6.6`.
- Lockfile: the zod entries were dropped and re-resolved, because npm keeps an existing lock entry over a new override. Result: a single `node_modules/zod@4.6.7`.
- New `zod-version.test.ts`: fails if the contract or the SDK resolves zod < 4.6.6, and pins the one behaviour change below.

## Behaviour change (reviewed)

I diffed `tools/list` from a real stdio server on main (zod 3) and on this branch:
- **`add_evidence`, generic `{ type, payload }` variant: `payload` is now required.** Before, `z.unknown()` keys were optional; zod 4 makes them required. `{type:"note"}` with no payload used to pass and is now `invalid_arguments`, and the advertised schema now lists `payload` as required.
- Advertised object schemas drop `additionalProperties: false`. At runtime, unknown keys are still stripped on both versions: I checked with `get_summary` plus an extra key.
- Integer fields gain `maximum: 9007199254740991`.

The same validation ran on both versions for invalid args, immutable-field corrections, extra keys and big integers. The only difference was the payload case.

## Verified

- `npm run build`, `lint`, `typecheck`: pass. `npm test`: 6 files, **45 passed**.
- The new test fails 3/3 when copied onto main's zod 3 tree.
- `npm audit --omit=dev`: **0 vulnerabilities**.
- Live stdio server: `initialize` OK, `tools/list` returns 20 tools with input schemas, and a bad `create_snapshot` call returns a clear validation error.

## Scope

This fixes the repo lockfile, CI and the Docker image. npm only honours `overrides` in the installing project's root, so users of the **published** `@production-master/mcp` package still get zod 3 under the contract until contract 0.1.1 ships: ProductionMasterAI/production-master-service#1801.

## Follow-up (not here)

Make `payload` explicitly `.optional()` in the contract source, widen its zod range to `^3.25 || ^4`, cap the unbounded `scopes` array in `mcpSessionMintRequestSchema`, and publish 0.1.1. Then this override can go.

author: afaq-ahmad
body:
## Problem

PK-001. PR #87 preserved area references during outages. Its text list could not filter events, and the published collection did not project the recorded corridor association.

## Approach

Published the coverage audit and acceptance plan before code in [checkpoint 2c232c2](https://github.com/afaq-ahmad/pakistan-flood-monitor/commit/2c232c2885923e3ed6b9135cda39366751598e17). My Area now selects configured corridor IDs and filters one published snapshot. Unknown associations remain in All published events. The map is optional and uses the available container width.

## Changed components

- Public Dashboard, its API-backed data adapter, and the canonical `GET /public/events` projection.
- Public route and Streamlit integration regressions.
- [Master task plan](docs/engineering/MASTER_TASK_PLAN.md), [journeys](docs/product/FARMER_LIVESTOCK_USER_JOURNEYS.md), [QA matrix](docs/product/FARMER_LIVESTOCK_QA_MATRIX.md), roadmap, API guide and handoff.

## Migrations and configuration

None. Existing canonical pilot corridor IDs supply the selector. The API adds a nullable `corridor_id` under the existing publication gate. No new provider request.

## Tests run and results

- Four new API/UI cases failed before the edit. The focused dashboard, publication and official sources group passed 34 tests after it.
- `APP_MODE=test .venv/bin/python -m pytest --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket tests/ -q --tb=short` passed 278 tests with 475 warnings.
- SQLite upgrade, downgrade, and re-upgrade reached `b4d9d93f2a10`. Compile, tracked-data isolation, documentation links and whitespace checks passed.
- GitHub Actions reported failure with zero jobs on [main](https://github.com/afaq-ahmad/pakistan-flood-monitor/actions/runs/44274735400) and the [selector checkpoint](https://github.com/afaq-ahmad/pakistan-flood-monitor/actions/runs/44276177058).

## Scientific assumptions and data limitations

Selection uses exact canonical configuration IDs and recorded event associations. Reference map lines are illustrative. District, tehsil, village and farm coverage are unverified. Publication and detection times stay separate from feed freshness. Unavailable measurements remain unavailable. No new public observations or site-specific risk is derived.

## Screenshots

Chromium startup failed while creating a local socket. AppTest verified text and selection in the no-feed states and responsive map configuration. Browser, 360 px and keyboard checks remain open.

## Backward compatibility and rollback

The public schema change is additive. The dashboard accepts the historical `aoi` alias when `corridor_id` is absent and retains published events without an association. Demo district filtering remains available. Revert the workstream commits to roll back.

## Out of scope and follow-up

PK-001 remains partial pending browser acceptance and verified administrative data. The next product slice uses PK-010 to validate and attribute English preparedness sources, followed by human Urdu review. PK-006 intake retains privacy and persistence prerequisites. PK-007 property exposure remains blocked pending the documented data and scientific validation.

## Self-review checklist

- [x] Documentation was published before implementation.
- [x] The selector uses configured IDs and the existing publication gate.
- [x] Matched, unassigned, empty, unavailable and demo use cases are covered.
- [x] Offline and migration checks passed.
- [ ] Browser/mobile and hosted CI verification pending.

body:
## Why

Owner, on #123: "Paper trading is a misleading name… Also Strategy builder and Optimiser link to paper trade only". Placing real orders from a page called Paper Trading, behind a mode switch, invites mistakes.

## What

- **Paper Trading (`/paper-trading`) is paper only again.** The Live switch is gone. In our build it shows a "Live Trading" link.
- **Live Trading (`/trade`)** has its own page, first in the sidebar's Trade group, and exists only in our build.
  - Same order ticket and basket as Paper Trading, sending real Zerodha orders through the dashboard (the #123 confirmation, rules and halt).
  - No paper account on the page; today's Kite orders sit beside the basket.
  - Outside our build, `/trade` redirects to Paper Trading.
- **"Trade live" beside every "Paper trade"**, staging the legs at `/trade?legs=`. Nothing is sent until you confirm there. It appears in:
  - Strategy Builder
  - Optimizer (cards and table)
  - option-chain basket drawer (new `"live"` send target)
  - contract page
- The Orders page and Live Trading share `KiteOrderBook` (status, halt, book, cancel, modify).

## Found while verifying

- `vite.config.ts` imports `routes.ts` in Node, where `import.meta.env` does not exist. A bare `import.meta.env.VITE_DASHBOARD_KITE` crashed the dev server's config load, and would have broken the build. It is now read guarded, like `lib/desk.ts`.
- The "VITE_SITE_URL is not set" warning had unescaped quotes (`"…fall back to "/"."` evaluated to `NaN`), which failed any build without `VITE_SITE_URL`. This was a #116 slip; production sets the variable, so it never fired there. Fixed.

## Verification

- **Production-like `vite build`** (`VITE_DASHBOARD_KITE=1` plus the production URLs) succeeds and emits the LiveTrading chunk.
- **Live-mode tests:**
  - no `/trade` route, no link, and paper buttons outside our build
  - Paper Trading stays paper in our build, links to `/trade`, and the route sits in the Trade group
  - `/trade` ticket → confirmation; nothing sent until Live Trading is on and the box is ticked; fill reported
  - `/trade?legs=` basket goes buys first, one leg at a time
- **Affected suites:** 165 tests pass.
- **Full terminal suite:** 3105 pass. The one failure is his existing Participants date test, which also fails on his untouched code.
- **Browser**, against the local fake-Kite stack:
  - Live Trading page: heading, banner, ticket and Kite book
  - sidebar Trade group: Live Trading, 1Cliq Trade, Orders

- tsc and eslint are clean.

author: ferni-agent[bot]
body:
## What

Behind a new flag, `CALL_CONSENT_NATURAL` (off by default; with it off, the reply path matches main), an owner's natural yes to a call or text read-back places it. Refs #4093. Refs #3876.

Prod, 11-11 to 11-18 (counts only): 5 read-backs, 1 placed call. 3 of the 5 were cancelled 4–16 s after the read-back was *stored*, by the owner's own words while still asking. The judge called most natural answers unclear.

With the flag on:

1. **Spoken, not stored.** Only owner finals that *begin* after Ferni's latest asking turn (the read-back) started playing can answer it. This uses the existing LiveKit `agent_state_changed` / `user_state_changed` events: each event is stamped with how many times Ferni had started speaking. LiveKit stamps `user_state_changed` when the VAD fires, not when the words began, so the VAD's start lag (its minimum speech, set explicitly at Silero's default, plus a model window, Silero's slow-inference threshold and a 220 ms slow-CPU margin, about 500 ms in all: `config/vad-timing.ts`) is taken off the owner's stamp. A yes whose VAD fires within that lag of the read-back starting may have begun before it, so it isn't heard and Ferni asks again (fail closed). Earlier words, including a yes said during a filler before the read-back, are neither a yes nor a no. A session that never reports Ferni's speaking state reads every final, as main does.
2. **The judge decides natural answers, inside a word gate.** The lexical clear-yes is still the fast path. A reply the allow-list can't read is placed on the consent judge's `yes` only if every word is in a small yes set (yes, sure, perfect, do it, go ahead, please, now, the action's own verb and the person's pronoun), it isn't over Ferni, and it isn't a question. No name counts, not the person's, the owner's or Ferni's ("Okay, call Riley.", "Yeah, do that, Ferni."), nor a bare "right" ("Yeah, right."). A reply that trails off in hesitation ("Okay, so, um, well.") isn't a yes at all, even to the fast path. Because names don't count, "Perfect, call Dad." asks again while "Yes, call Dad." places on the allow-list: asking again is the safe side, and intended. A reply with a digit is never placed on the judge's yes, even one repeating the read-back's own digits (a new number already ends the window on main). Anything else gets the one "Just to be sure" ask, whatever the judge says. A judge `unclear` or an error stays unclear. A bare "Wait." or "Hold on." cancels. The judge is also told that a joke not meant as a request is off topic.
3. **A yes with a message is read back first.** "Yes, call him and tell him I'm running late" gets one ask with the message read back: `Should I call Dad now and tell them "I'm running late"? Just say yes or no.` Only a yes to that adds the message to the call's purpose, as data. The same holds with `OUTREACH_SERVER_CONFIRM` on: the stored read-back is asked again with the message, and the server's send carries what was confirmed. A message with digits, quotes or brackets isn't carried; that reply gets the plain ask, and the call goes with its purpose unchanged. Only the message's length is logged. After the send, the model is told to say it will pass the message on; that note holds none of its words.
4. **The args are fixed at the yes.** What a yes sends is computed before the attestation write (`MESSAGING_PIPELINE`) is awaited, so nothing said during that await reaches the call. Crisis risk landing during the await holds the send (item 5).
5. **Crisis risk on the call holds every outbound action for the rest of it.** The hold starts at the first crisis read on the call, with or without a window open: a crisis line this gate hears (over Ferni or split across finals), or risk the safety kernel already noted on the call (`crisisRiskNoted` in `crisis-call-risk.ts`, the call state the crisis gate and turn pipeline write; read by the live call's session id, the same id they note under). It is checked when a tool is called, and once more inside each send function, right before the send (`heldBeforeSend` in `sendOnYes` and the server-confirm `sendTaken`), so no path can skip it: not the server path that awaits `prepare` before sending, nor its early send that skips the settle timer. At the send, a crisis read still in flight on the call (the yes turn's own or an earlier turn's) is waited on, up to 1.5 s (`CRISIS_READ_WAIT_MS`): if it finds risk, the call is held; if it is still pending at the bound, only this attempt is held ("Nothing was sent yet; ask me again in a moment.") and a fresh read-back can place it once the read settles clean. A gated action with no call id to read the call's state by is held too (outcome `no_session`, counts only), never skipped. Then any read-back waiting or just cancelled is dropped, and every gated outbound tool (a call, a text, a message to someone else) returns "Nothing was sent" until the call ends: no fresh read-back is stored and no later yes sends anything. The emergency-contact flows aren't gated by this tool wrapper and keep their own crisis handling.
6. **Only allow-listed read-only runs keep the window.** Any tool run between the read-back and the yes voids it, including owner-only senders like `sendMessageNow` and `callUser`, an unknown tool, or one with no name. Only `callStatus` and `getContactInfo` are skipped.
7. **Over-talk at the tail: not built.** The playout signal can't tell when the number was spoken (there are no word timings), so this item is skipped as the spec allows.

**In both flag states**, a count line `CONSENT_NATURAL_DECISION {natural, lexical: yes|no|neither, judge: yes|no|unclear|error|skipped, outcome}` logs at each decision: when the model calls the tool again, and when an owner's no cancels the window. It carries enums only, no words, so the flag can be measured in prod before it flips.

Unchanged: `OUTBOUND_CONFIRM` always on in prod, the crisis-turn rules, the read-back naming who and which number, and a second unclear cancelling.

## Overlapping issues

This resolves none of #2942, #2943 or #3104; it only touches the same files.
- #2942 (a retry that renames the person re-previews an approved call) is about `continues()` / `sameAction`, which this doesn't change.
- #2943 (yes given, model never calls the tool) is the server-side send, which this doesn't change.
- #3104 ("I'll call him myself" not sticky; accented names) is the REDIRECT list and `namesSomeoneElse`, which this doesn't change.

For #3876, this covers only the consent side: a joking yes to a read-back isn't confirmed. It doesn't stop the unasked tool call or offer that the issue is mostly about.

## Lane

**Consent/privacy lane.** It's also in the **crisis lane by files**: `src/services/safety/index.ts` gains one export (`crisisRiskNoted`, read-only, so the gate goes through the safety index as the architecture gate requires); `consent-window.ts` imports the safety kernel and is listed in CODEOWNERS and `autonomy-policy.json`. The new `consent-send.ts` (the send on a yes and the crisis hold, split out to keep both files under 500 lines) acts on crisis lines, so it is added to both lists.
