author: jianc99
body:
The twenty-sixth block of the round after Splash 1.7.0, on the checkpoint block (#93). Two commits, in the engine's real-model oracle test; no product code.

## Why

Two checks of the oracle compared paths of the same model against fixed bounds set from the Qwen models:

- The greedy chain allowed a token half a logit below the one-row path's best. Flint's paths round further apart: its routed experts' column and staged tiles sum a row in different orders, and its attention carries that on. On a 64 GB M5 Pro its UD-Q4_K_XL failed the check in some runs at 0.53 and 0.80, as 1.7.0 does, with every operator computing correct values.
- The branched-paths check bounded a lane's cosine to its chain by 0.999, or 0.99 for bf16 states or MoE without alike partitions. Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M misses that by rounding alone on a 16-core M5 Pro (0.998385, under 1.7.0 too).

A fixed bound is either too loose for the models that round little or wrong for those that round more.

## What changes

Each check now measures the model's own rounding in the same run and bounds itself by it.

- **Near ties.** The chain's tokens are forced again in branch-free steps of 16 rows, which run no tree, no acceptance walk and no commit along a chosen path, against one row a cycle. A token's gap must stay within twice the 90th percentile of the largest difference among the 16 highest logits, at least 0.05 and at most 2.0.
- **Branched paths.** A branch-free twin of the same rows in the same widths gives the bound: five times its least cosine's distance from 1. A twin further than 0.95 from its chain fails as a control off. The check prints the ratio.
- A lane that does not retain its path, and one short of the boundary or of its capture, now fail apart.
- A forced path's last row selects none of its children's tokens, so that a path ends where it was forced: on the 35B a row whose first child is a stop token selected its later child's, and the lane retained a row more than its path.

## Measured

On the branch with this block, one run of each:

| model (Mac) | near-tie gap / bound | branched least / twin least / bound | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit MLX (M5 Max) | 0.0015 / 0.354 | 0.999100 / 0.999097 / 0.995486 | pass |
| Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M (M5 Max) | 0.040 / 0.384 | 0.999328 / 0.999573 / 0.997867 | pass |
| Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M (48 GB M5 Pro) | 0.135 / 0.292 | 0.998248 / 0.999369 / 0.996845 | pass |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M (M5 Max) | 0.013 / 1.549 | 0.998633 / 0.997494 / 0.987472 | pass |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 4-bit MLX (M5 Max) | 0.185 / 2.0 | 0.996989 / 0.989213 / 0.946067 | pass |
| Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B PQ2_0 (M5 Max) | 0.006 / 0.347 | 0.999960 / 0.999916 / 0.999579 | pass |
| Flint UD-Q4_K_XL (64 GB M5 Pro) | 0.343 / 2.0 | 0.999427 / 0.997418 / 0.987088 | pass |
| Flint mixed-3-4bit MLX (64 GB M5 Pro) | 0.587 / 1.825 | 0.999943 / 0.999905 / 0.999527 | pass |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 (M5 Max) | 0.057 / 1.160 | 0.997058 / 0.995924 / 0.979619 | pass |

The branched values repeat bit for bit between runs, as the forced steps do. The near-tie gap and bound follow the steps a run takes, which follow the step costs it measures at warm-up: across two runs the gap moved from 0.53 to 0.34 on Flint UD-Q4_K_XL and from 0.23 to 0.59 on its MLX checkpoint. The smallest margin under a bound is 0.157 (Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M on the 16-core M5 Pro).

The near-tie bound is tighter than the fixed half logit on the models that round little (0.29 to 0.39 on Qwen3.8-27B) and reaches its ceiling of 2.0 on Flint UD-Q4_K_XL, whose own rounding goes past it. Errors of the kind the check exists for lie 10.8 and 11.0 below the best logit.

## What the checks still cannot see

On a dense model a skipped path commit moves the next logits less than rounding does, so the branched-paths check does not catch it there (a mutant passes on Qwen3.8-27B and fails on Flint). The mixed-step and rows-of-no-lane checks are unchanged and bitwise.

## Testing

- A mutant that commits a step along a branch other than the accepted one fails the branched-paths check on Flint at 2.4 times the bound's distance, and passes it on Qwen3.8-27B, as above.
- The build, `make check-python`, `make check-source` and the CPU engine suites pass on the branch (M5 Max).

author: mrcastilla8
body:
## Objetivo

Aplicar el ciclo Draft → Ready → posmerge sin ejecutar CI completa durante desarrollo en Draft y sin alterar los despliegues productivos.

## Disparadores

| Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|
| PR a `master` en todos sus estados | `opened`, `reopened`, `synchronize`, `ready_for_review`, `converted_to_draft`, `edited`; los jobs de Draft se omiten |
| Push a `master` | Se conserva para CI posmerge |
| `workflow_dispatch` de validación/benchmark | Se conserva; benchmarks solo manuales y protegidos de cancelación |

## Cambios y checks

- Se conserva el contexto obligatorio exacto **validate**.
- Las cuatro particiones E2E y el clasificador documental permanecen; E2E general solo puede omitirse con clasificación documental exitosa.
- `validate` incorpora `npm run test:unit:taxonomy`, `npm run test:release:policy` y `npm run test:e2e:pricing` con `src/features/pricing/testing/playwright.config.ts`.
- Se conservan `test:release:boundary` y `test:production:auth` en la compilación API.
- Auditoría `npm audit --audit-level=high`, lockfile, evidencia JSON y SHA del código auditado; un hallazgo High/Critical bloquea `validate`.
- El verificador de `validate` exige cada resultado requerido y solo admite omitir la suite E2E general cuando la clasificación real es documental.
- `sync-master-developers.yml` y el workflow Vercel `repository_dispatch` permanecen sin cambios.

## Pruebas y evidencia

- Focalizadas: `node --test scripts/ci/verificar-resultados.test.mjs scripts/ci/draft-ready-policy.test.mjs` — 71/71 PASS.
- Cobertura incluye todos los jobs obligatorios ante éxito, fallo, `skipped`, cancelación y ausencia; comprueba la excepción E2E documental y los cuatro checks nuevos.
- YAML parseado con PyYAML y `git diff --check` — PASS.
- Las pruebas validan la configuración declarativa; el evento real de GitHub se observará en Draft y Ready posteriormente, sin cambiar este PR a Ready.
- Suites completas de frontend no ejecutadas localmente; quedan diferidas a Actions en Ready.

## Riesgos y limitaciones

- La auditoría podría encontrar vulnerabilidades preexistentes High/Critical y bloquear el check; el artefacto por SHA permitirá revisar el impacto.
- La suite Pricing requiere su configuración Playwright propia y se ejecutará en GitHub con Chromium.
- El PR está en Draft y todavía no se han observado sus ejecuciones de Actions.
- No se cambió ni activó despliegue de Vercel ni se modificaron variables.

## Criterios de aceptación

- No iniciar suites completas en Draft; Ready y cada nuevo commit Ready vuelven a validar.
- Volver a Draft difiere suites pesadas y regresar a Ready revalida el código actual.
- `validate` falla ante resultados obligatorios fallidos, omitidos indebidamente o ausentes.
- Posmerge `master` conserva la CI y los workflows de publicación/despliegue no se disparan por PR Ready.
- Las cuatro particiones E2E y el criterio documental estricto se conservan.

## Reversión

Revertir el commit de este PR restaura el workflow y los agregadores anteriores. No cambia la protección de `master` ni requiere acciones en Vercel.

## Correcciones de revisión incorporadas

El agregador `validate` hace checkout y prepara Node 22 sin `npm ci`. Las cuatro suites nuevas se omiten durante benchmark manual exclusivo. La evidencia de auditoría separa SHA evaluado, HEAD/base del PR e ID de ejecución.

`actionlint` y Go no están instalados en el entorno local; el YAML pasa PyYAML y las regresiones focalizadas.

## What changed

A respected worker earns a small bonus on civilian jobs (#2703, chapter #1018, docs/architecture/reputation.md section 8).

- `LF_ReputationPay.c` (new): `LF_ReputationPayDef` (faction, percent per tier, lowest tier first, clamped to 15) and `LF_ReputationPay.Bonus/Percent/TakeLastBonus`.
- `LF_CivilianJob.CompleteRun` adds the town tier's percent of the run's BASE pay; `Dropoff` books it as its own ledger line, reason `standing-bonus` (summed with a contract's bonus part, which already used that reason). A contract's multiplier does not compound it. Police and medic duty pay never calls it.
- Config: shipped TOWN row `0 0 0 5 10 15` for tiers -2..3 in `Configs/Reputation/LF_Reputation.conf`.
- Hook outside the owns-list (about 5 lines, said here as asked): `m_aPays` field on `LF_ReputationConfig` and the conf row above.
- Docs: `docs/features/reputation.md`, `Reputation/Feature.md`.

## Tests

`LF_Test_ReputationPayBonus` (LOGIC): percent by tier 0 0 0 5 10 15; tier-3 parcel run pays 40 + 6; tier 0 and a police tier-3 character pay the plain base; contract at tier 3 pays 60 + 6 (not 69); a config of 90 clamps to 15.

- Red: `RED PROOF OK`, first `a contract pays base times the multiplier, plus the tier bonus on the base only (expected 66, got 60)`.
- Green: `--only LF_Test_ReputationPayBonus,LF_Test_ReputationContract` passed=2 failed=0; `--tier all` passed=1005 failed=0.
- `tools\cli validate`: ok (validate-scripts.ps1 and website-content skipped by the incremental cache).

No screenshots: no player-visible change beyond more cash in the same notification.

## Manual testing

1. Host DebugWorld, sign up for the parcel job, give yourself town standing 1000 (tier 3) and finish one run at the drop site: the cash is the base plus 15 % (40 + 6) and the ledger shows two lines, `job-pay` 40 and `standing-bonus` 6.
2. At town tier 0 the same run pays exactly 40 and no `standing-bonus` line.
3. Take a contract at tier 3 and finish it: base 40 x contract multiplier plus 15 % of 40, not 15 % of the multiplied pay.

REVIEW-NEEDED: money. Draft, no auto-merge; the lead runs the independent review (interrogate) before merge.

## Review findings

# Review slice-2703 (money: self-check by the builder; independent reviewer still needed)

- [x] fixed: bonus counted against the contract multiplier would compound; it is a percent of the base only, asserted with 66 not 69.
- [x] fixed: the bonus would have been paid inside the `job-pay` ledger line; `Dropoff` now sums the contract and tier parts into the `standing-bonus` line.
- [x] fixed: a stale pending bonus from an earlier run could be paid on a later one; `Bonus` clears the entry first and `ForgetCareer` calls `Forget`.
- [x] dismissed: a client could read or request the bonus; the code is server-only (`CompleteRun`, `Dropoff`), no RPC and no replicated state added.
- [x] dismissed: persistence; the bonus is derived from the saved tier at pay time and the pending map is session state cleared on use, so no save section is added.
- [x] dismissed: integer overflow; base pay is a small int and the percent is clamped to 0..15.

author: riiy
body:
## Why
The long-term objective is a **7×24 unattended AI Quant Research Agent**: humans set goals/safety, the system discovers, tests/falsifies, archives and iterates. P0 is deployed by the user and safely returns `IDLE_NO_APPROVED_TASKS`, but cannot autonomously discover new evidence or execute a new hypothesis. Stop expanding P0 infrastructure; move to a **single real end-to-end research loop**.

## Implemented (separate opt-in P1, P0 service untouched)
- `quant-research-loop --home runtime cycle --policy runtime/research-loop.policy.json`: at most **one Crossref metadata request per UTC day**, min 24h spacing, hardcoded HTTPS origin and query, 20 works max, 1 MB response cap, 15s timeout. **Zero LLM calls/cost** and no arbitrary commands.
- Save complete Crossref response bytes to immutable `runtime/agent/evidence/crossref-poll-*.json`, SHA256, paper DOI/title/pub year/first-seen date, deduplicate by DOI in separate SQLite. A title is a hypothesis cue **not verified empirical results**.
- Only the **first** new-to-local-registry calendar/weekday crypto return DOI can start the already frozen `BTC_WEEKDAY_INFORMATION_v1` retrospective information test. Others are archived, no automatic additional tests of same mechanism. `BLOCKED_MISSING_SPOT` waits on input without another API call. Invalid data or interrupted study => `FAILED_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, no parameter rescue or silent rerun.
- Frozen single Monday indicator (not a seven-weekday search) versus fixed price/vol/volume-only ridge baseline. Evaluation **2022–2023**; fit/standardize 2020–2021 only; controls through t−2; **2024/2025 never parsed**, using existing 2020–2023 spot canonical SHA256. Four AND gates: >=2% relative OOS MSE gain, 14-day paired-block bootstrap 95% lower bound >0, positive in BOTH evaluation years, beats zero-return forecast. STOP / ARCHIVE or retrospective mechanism-only PASS / HUMAN REVIEW. **Never alpha or trading approval**.
- New P1 policy and **disabled** P1 systemd service/timer example; P0 existing hourly timer/database untouched. P1 shares only `runtime/PAUSED`.
- `docs/AUTONOMOUS_RESEARCH_LOOP_V1.md`, README, and STATE.md restore the full long-term objective while distinguishing code/CI from live research.

## Technical verification
**19 offline unit tests passed in authoring environment**: source-metadata parsing, DOI dedup, bounded polling, policy drift and unsafe path/flag guard, source outage, persistence, waiting-for-data resume without redundant HTTP, single template idempotence, immutable report, study failure and interrupted-claim review, CLI status schema, frozen sample calendar, positive-signal synthetic control and 2024 data-access break. GitHub CI to verify integration in Python 3.11 / 3.12.

**No real Crossref call or real BTC Kill Test occurred during this PR creation**; no claim of a genuine autonomous research report until operator runs this against its pinned local data.

## Important methodological limits
- **Narrow preapproved mechanism template**, not a general autonomous literature reasoning model. No paper body/causal claim validation.
- Results from 2022–2023 are retrospective; a paper registered in 2024/2025 may itself examine 2022–2023. The source is not historical point-in-time investable information.
- A missing title cue is discovery-only progress, not completed falsification. If the current small query yields no eligible article, do not widen/retune queries to manufacture a result.
- All archived funding, attention, trend and volatility studies remain closed; 2024/2025 sealed holdouts and trading remain disallowed.

## Manual operator smoke after review (no service enable)
```bash
git fetch origin && git switch --track origin/feat/autonomous-research-loop-v1
pip install -e .
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
cp deploy/quant-research-loop.policy.example.json runtime/research-loop.policy.json
quant-research-loop --home runtime status
# Explicitly makes one external Crossref metadata request and may run ONE research-only frozen test:
quant-research-loop --home runtime cycle --policy runtime/research-loop.policy.json
quant-research-loop --home runtime status
```
The existing `runtime/agent/orchestrator.sqlite3` is preserved. New `runtime/agent/autonomous_loop.sqlite3` is a separate store.

**PR only.** Owner reviews/merges and explicitly authorizes P1 service activation separately; no direct `main` changes or host timer operations.

body:
Hybrid route PR-4 (plan/specs/hybrid.md section 4): the `hybrid` and `full` stages of `exopipe3 hybrid`.

## What it does
- `lib/hybrid/master.py`: production `notaper_largescale.py` (exopipe main 4c7098c) `hybrid_unit` / `hybrid_full` and their helpers, line for line. Constants are bound from the config (`bind()`, 43 globals): the hybrid scales 30 / 60 wavelengths, the striation selection and restored-base paths and scopes, and the tolerances (identity 1e-5, large scales 1e-3, own-beam 1e-4, striation identity 1e-6). A refusal is `ReconRefusal`. Every file read is recorded (`READS`), and FITS are read with `memmap=False` (package-wide).
- `stack_refused` reads the stack unit's v2 record. A Taper residual stack refused by HG5 (the rebuild test) is the reason the CLEAN-residual product is skipped. A stack record that did not end done, or an HG1 refusal, refuses the unit.
- The Full cell's `PBdiffuse_deep_Full.fits` is written by the Robust 0 unit only (`hybrid_full.PBDIFFUSE_WEIGHTING`).
- `steps/hybrid.hybrid_master_unit`:
  - No reconstruction record means no input. A recon or wideband record that did not end done refuses the unit.
  - A wideband or Full member without a passed hybrid refuses the unit.
  - A refusal removes everything the unit wrote.
  - A CLEAN residual that cannot be made because its Taper residual stack was refused is recorded as a refused item, gate `taper-residual-stack`, and the unit still ends done.
  - The unit's inputs are the files it read, excluding its own outputs. Its admitted nights are the hybrid's span.
- Content tests:
  - `hybrid_master_product`: name grammar, with the scope, Taper, robust value, lsrecon + lsfill and the kind's token; grid equal to the Taper master; finite and nonzero; caveat cards at the caveat scopes.
  - `hybrid_pbdiffuse`: grid; a finite positive peak of at most 1; not a product name.
  - `hybrid_record`:
    - the unit;
    - test_hybrid: identity, NaN mask, large scales, small scales outside the caveat scopes, verdict consistency, and compact sources with the 18 MHz / Red tolerance;
    - the recorded product tests: beam-corrected identity, and the CLEAN-residual read-back or a recorded reason for its absence;
    - each product's md5 against its file.

## Testing
- `tests/test_hybrid_master.py` (CI, 5/5):
  - the bound constants equal production's;
  - each record rule broken alone fails only its own test;
  - the product tests, including a wrong kind token, a wrong robust value, a shifted grid and missing caveat cards;
  - `stack_refused` reading a v2 record;
  - the unit's no-input, refusal-cleanup, refused-item and input-recording paths, a wideband member without a hybrid, and Full with no members.
- `tests/test_hybrid_config.py` 10/10: the CLI test now expects the hybrid units to be ported; they refuse on HG0 there, because the test points `hybrid_stack.COADD_SB` at a missing directory.
- Parity on lwacalim07, run on byte-checked copies of production's inputs and compared with production's lsrecon runs (data md5 of every FITS, header cards, record values):
  - **18h 46 MHz Robust -0.75**, against Run_20261028_234240: the hybrid, pbcorr and cleanres data are bit-identical. The hybrid's data md5 dec69e70… equals the archived product in Run_NOTAPER_HYBRID_QUARANTINE_20261111. Header difference: v2 carries the 7 cards of the 11-11 Release 1 header repair (ASTREF, CALBP, FLUXREF, MDWSTAT, P1RUN, P2RUN, SCALE_A) and 2 HISTORY lines, because it reads today's installed Taper master, which has them; production read it before the repair. The record differs only in paths and md5s, plus the 7 fields 4c7098c adds.
  - **04h Blue Robust -0.75** (striation-restored base), against Run_20261031_172532: the hybrid, pbcorr and cleanres data are bit-identical. The hybrid's data md5 fc7a20a8… equals the archived product. Headers are equal, except for the HISTORY timestamp. The record differs only in paths and md5s.
  - **18h Full Robust 0**, against Run_FULL_20261108: the hybrid, pbcorr and PBdiffuse data are bit-identical. The hybrid's data md5 12c18ff5… equals the archived N016 product. The header differs by the 3 repair cards (ASTREF, FLUXREF, MDWSTAT) that today's installed Full Taper master carries. The record differs only in paths and md5s. The unit read 114 inputs and admitted 16 nights. A first run refused, because the PBdiffuse test required a minimum of 0 or more; production's map is the same file (md5 7148564b…) with -0.0019 near the horizon, as installed PB maps have. The test now checks for a finite peak in (0, 1].
  - **18h Full Robust -0.75** (after the review fixes), against Run_FULL_20261108: the hybrid and pbcorr data are bit-identical. The hybrid's data md5 8b16b7fd… equals the archived N016 product. This unit no longer writes PBdiffuse; the map written by R0 is unchanged. Production refused the 18h 82 MHz Taper residual stack on its rebuild test, and the parity staging writes that refusal as the v2 stack record (HG5). The unit read 129 inputs and admitted 16 nights.
  - **Determinism**: 18h 46 MHz run twice gives the same data md5 for all three products.
  - **Production's 912 hybrid records** (all 24 LSTs × 19 scopes × 2 weightings): the v2 record tests that read only the record give the recorded verdict for every one (888 pass, 24 caveat; 0 disagreements). Every record's product name is present in HQ11. The md5 test was not run on these records; it would read about 2700 Lustre products.

## Risk
High (archive products). One `/code-review high`.

## How to revert
Revert the merge commit. The hybrid and full units then refuse as "not yet ported" (PR-1 behavior); nothing else reads these modules.

author: satyajit1106
body:
## Scope
Second step of the SCORM fix. #232 unpacks each package into `training-content/<uploadId>/`. This PR serves those files over HTTPS at `/scorm/<uploadId>/<path>`, so a course can load on the app's own origin. It needs that origin to reach the app's SCORM API through `window.parent`, which is B3. It also removes the browser-side CORS failure.

The player is unchanged until B3. This PR adds the infrastructure, the API field and the dev forward.

### What changes
- **`infra/terraform/scorm_cdn.tf`** (new):
  - A CloudFront distribution in front of the private assets bucket, using an **origin access control**. Price class 200, which includes India.
  - It uses the AWS-managed `CachingOptimized` and `SecurityHeadersPolicy` policies.
  - A **bucket policy** with a single statement: only this distribution may `s3:GetObject`, and only under `training-content/*`. Everything else in the bucket stays reachable only through IAM roles and presigned links.
  - A **CloudFront Function** (`functions/scorm_path.js`) maps `/scorm/<32 hex>/<path>` to `/training-content/<32 hex>/<path>`. Every other path, and any path containing `..`, gets a 404.
  - Output: `scorm_content_domain`.
- **reference-api:** READY packages now carry `LaunchURL` = `/scorm/<uploadId>/<LaunchPath>`, a relative, same-origin, URL-encoded path. Other packages are unchanged.
- **`vite.config.js`:** the dev server forwards `/scorm` to CloudFront when `VITE_SCORM_PROXY_TARGET` is set. Without it, nothing changes.
- **`github_actions_terraform.tf`:** the workflow role may create, read and update these CloudFront resources and put the bucket policy. It still cannot delete a distribution.

## Risk
- The bucket had **no bucket policy** before; this adds one. Run the check in step 1 below before applying, because Terraform would replace any policy that was added by hand.
- Access control on `/scorm/*` comes from the unguessable 32-hex upload id; there is no per-user check yet. Training content is not sensitive. Signed cookies can be added if Vodafone requires them.
- Course HTML will run on the app's origin, so it is trusted like app code. Packages are uploaded only by the Admin and Creator roles.
- Cost: CloudFront's always-free tier covers 1 TB transfer, 10M requests and 2M function runs a month.

## Deploy
The workflow role changes in this PR, so per AGENTS.md §6 this apply runs **from a terminal** with the `vshield` SSO profile, not from the Actions button:
1. `aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket security-awareness-poc-satyajit-2026` should print `NoSuchBucketPolicy`. If a policy prints instead, stop.
2. In `infra/terraform`, run `terraform plan`. Expect **4 to add** (origin access control, function, distribution, bucket policy), **2 to change** (the reference-api Lambda and the workflow role's policy), and **0 to destroy**.
3. Run `terraform apply`, then `terraform output scorm_content_domain`. The distribution takes about 5 minutes to deploy.

## Tests
- `ruff check` is clean, and the full backend `pytest` suite passes, including the new `launch_url` test.
- I ran the CloudFront Function under Node against eight paths: a valid launch file, an encoded space, `..` and `%2E%2E`, a bare `/scorm/<id>/`, a short id, `/training-content/…` and `/`. Only the two valid paths were rewritten; the other six returned 404.
- `vite.config.js` loads both with and without `VITE_SCORM_PROXY_TARGET`.
- `terraform fmt` is clean. `terraform validate` could not run in the cloud sandbox (no provider download), so the plan in step 2 is the first full check.

## Revert
Revert this PR and apply from a terminal. The distribution, function, origin access control and bucket policy are destroyed (an intended destroy; the bucket and its objects are untouched). reference-api stops returning `LaunchURL`.

author: atretyak1985
body:
## Goal

Перебудувати вкладку «Запуски» фази за D-27 … D-31 без зміни даних і API: одне речення-вердикт, блок «останній результат», один картковий список сесій по спробах, одна дія «Перевідкрити…».

## Completion Report

**Covers:** D-27, D-28, D-29, D-30, D-31.

**Shipped** (`tools/swarmery/web`):

- `src/pages/plans/runsModel.ts` + `runsModel.test.ts` (new, 17 unit tests) — pure verdict (`runsVerdict`), card role/title (`runRole`/`runRoleLabel`/`runCardTitle`, never `s.title`), attempt groups (`phaseAttemptGroups`) and whole-plan phase groups (`planPhaseGroups`).
- `PlanSessions.tsx` rewritten as the Runs tab's one card list: `SessionCard`/`LinkedCard`/`GroupBlock`, grouped by attempt under an open phase, by phase (+ the plan-run controller's own group) over the whole plan. The existing `scopePlanSessions` toggle, its numbers and its aria-label/data-tip wiring are untouched.
- `PhaseDetailPanel.tsx` Runs tab rebuilt: the old `<ol>` of `RunRow`s, the badge row (`RunStateChip`/`RunModelChip`/`DocModelChip`/`VerifyVerdictChip`/`SurpriseChip`/dep chips/the inline run button) and `RunsReviewBlock` are gone, replaced by the verdict sentence and a "Last result" block of 5 `Row`s (Executor, Guard check, Verifier, Review → Review tab, Plan compliance → Report tab). `RunModelChip`/`DocModelChip` kept, moved beside the model/effort pickers (still exercised by `Plans.phaseRunModel.test.tsx` / `Plans.phaseDocModel.test.tsx`). The executor row reuses `RunCompletedChip`/`RunOutcomeChip` for its clickable diagnosis affordance, so "ran · N/M" still opens the run-diagnosis modal (`Plans.reverify.test.tsx`).
- `ReviewStateLedger.tsx`: exported `Row`, `DOT`, `RowTone` and extracted `guardRowView` (same guard-findings text the State block's Guard row always used) so the Runs tab's Guard-check row reads it identically. `Row`'s `status` now accepts a `ReactNode` and its `link` accepts an in-app `onClick` action, not only an external href — both additive, no existing caller changed shape.
- `PhaseReopens.tsx` + `.test.tsx`: dropped the "Reopened" history list (each reopen's reason now reads as its attempt group's caption in `PlanSessions`/`runsModel.phaseAttemptGroups`); kept the one "Reopen…" button and its form unchanged, added the explanatory sentence for both the offered and withheld states. Rendering moved to `EpicDetail.tsx`, after the card list, so it sits at the bottom of the tab as D-31 asks — `PhaseDetailPanel` no longer owns it.
- `EpicDetail.tsx`: mounts `PhaseReopens` after `PlanSessions`, computing `canReopen` itself (`phaseStatus(...) === 'done' && runState !== 'running'`), the same condition `PhaseDetailPanel` used before.
- Deleted `RunsReviewBlock.tsx` + its test (now fully unused — its job is the Review tab's own block, already shipped in phase 5).
- `Plans.sessionScope.test.tsx` rewritten for card-based assertions (role/attempt-group text instead of literal session titles) — same SC-1…SC-7 claims, same toggle/number wiring, now also asserting no card ever shows the service-prompt text.
- i18n: `npm run i18n:extract` + filled all 30 new `uk` strings in `src/locales/uk/plans.po`, reusing the existing "In progress" → "У роботі" wording from `insights-system.po` where the same English string is shared; `npm run i18n:compile` after.

**Verify** (from `tools/swarmery/web`):
- `npm run lint` — green (only pre-existing biome schema-version notices, unrelated).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — green.
- `npm test` (vitest) — **1929/1929 green**, 173/173 files. (One flaky, unrelated focus-timing test in `Sessions.test.tsx` failed once under full-suite parallel load and passed cleanly alone and on every other full run — not touched by this phase.)
- `npm run build` — green.
- `npm run screenshots` — **green**, full run, exit 0, all shots and shell-scroll assertions. It needs a live dev server in mock mode (`VITE_MOCK=1 npx vite --port 5173`, per the script's own usage comment) — my first attempt started a plain `npx vite` without `VITE_MOCK=1`, which hung on `/sessions/1?tab=timeline`'s `[role="tabpanel"]` because the unmocked page has no real daemon at :7777 to answer it; that was my own setup mistake, not a product defect. Re-ran with `VITE_MOCK=1` and it completed cleanly end to end, including every Plans/Runs-adjacent shot. Generated PNGs were a local run artifact and are not committed.

**Where reality diverged from the plan's risks:**
- Risk 1 (attempt marker may need inference from run order) **happened as expected**: the data carries no explicit attempt number, so `phaseAttemptGroups` reads one attempt per session in a phase's run list, oldest first. A phase whose executor also spawned a subagent tagged to the same `phaseId` will over-count its attempts by exactly that subagent — documented in `runsModel.ts`'s header comment and in `Plans.sessionScope.test.tsx`'s fixture comment, not guessed at silently.
- "Plan compliance" (D-30) has no single existing field named that; I mapped it to the phase's own completion chip (`phaseChip`/`PHASE_CHIP` — done/unverified/unreported/started/blocked/pending) with `completionBlockers` as the row's detail, linking to the Report tab per the doc's own instruction. This reuses data already computed in `PhaseDetailPanel`, rather than inventing a new concept.
- "Verifier" and "Review" last-result rows read `phase.verifyVerdict`/`phase.verifyDetail` and `phase.reviews?.[0]` respectively — both already shipped fields, not new ones.
- No `## Forecast` section exists in this phase doc, so no `kind: posterior` block was added (there is nothing to mirror a `kind: prior` block against).

No decision was skipped: D-27…D-31 are all implemented as described above.

### How to verify

- [x] На вкладці «Запуски» кожна сесія фази показана рівно один раз, карткою
- [x] Жодна картка і жодна підказка не показує службовий промпт як назву; назва це роль і, якщо є, короткий підсумок
- [x] У режимі «ця фаза» картки згруповані по спробах із сумою вартості кожної; фаза з однією спробою має одну групу
- [x] Перемикач «ця фаза N / весь план M» показує ті самі числа, що й старий «#1 (N) / усі (M)», і в режимі плану групує по фазах
- [x] Над сесіями є речення-вердикт і блок «останній результат» з одним рядком на роль; рядка бейджів на вкладці немає
- [x] Блоку рев'ю з markdown і знахідками на «Запусках» немає, рядок «Рев'ю» веде на вкладку «Рев'ю»
- [x] «Перевідкрити…» є на вкладці один раз, з поясненням, і надсилає той самий запит, що й до зміни
- [x] Картка відкриває сесію кліком і в новій вкладці, фокус клавіатури видно
- [x] Фаза без запусків показує порожній стан без порожніх блоків
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run screenshots` зелені; старі тести оновлено, не видалено

## Remaining

_None — every id this phase claims is cited in its report._

- D-27

author: ykzts
body:
## 変更内容

`packages/video-backfill/src/queue.ts` を役割ごとのファイルに分け、依存の向きと、積み直すときの「変わっていなければ、書き込む」の確認を直しました。コミットは3つです。

### 1. ファイルを分ける（`refactor(video-backfill): split the queue into files by role`）

| ファイル | 中身 |
| --- | --- |
| `types.ts` | ジョブと結果の型（`BackfillQueueOptions` を含む） |
| `keys.ts` | キーの作り方（ジョブ、ロック、実行の結果）と、有効期限の定数 |
| `jobs.ts` | 状態の遷移（`BACKFILL_JOB_TRANSITIONS`）と判定（`getJobActivity`）、ジョブの組み立て |
| `scripts.ts` | Lua のスクリプトと、それを呼び出す関数 |
| `queue.ts` | `BackfillQueue` クラスだけ（199行） |
| `runs.ts` | 一括チェック |

- Issue の表にない `jobs.ts` を足しました。状態の遷移（#7083 で入ったもの）と、ジョブの項目の組み立て（積む、1ページ進める、失敗を数える）を置いています。`queue.ts` を 200 行以内にするためでもあります
- `src/index.ts` は、名前を明示して公開します。公開する名前は、`getBackfillRunResultKeys` が増えたほかは変わりません（型チェッカーで、変更の前後の一覧を比べました）。`scripts.ts` の呼び出す関数や `jobKey` などは公開しません

このコミットでは、Issue のとおり `onFinish?(job)` で終えたジョブを知らせる形にしましたが、3つめのコミットで置き換えています。

### 2. 番号で比べる（`refactor(video-backfill): compare job versions when queueing a job again`）

- ジョブに `version` を持たせ、書き込むたび（積む、取り出す、保存、終える、戻す）に 1 増やします。`ENQUEUE_SCRIPT` は、JSON の文字列ではなく、読んだときの番号と Redis のジョブの番号を比べます
- 番号のない、保存済みのジョブは 0 として扱います（`version?: number`。使う側のテストのジョブを書き換えずに済むよう、省略できる型にしています）
- 文字列の比較のためだけにあった、`CLAIM_SCRIPT` の `\/` を戻す処理を削除しました
- `src/testing/scripts.ts` の模倣と、`@shinju-date/msw-handlers` のテストも、同じように直しました

### 3. 結果をジョブと一緒に書き込む（`fix(video-backfill): save the outcome of a job of a check with the job`）

Codex のレビューの指摘への対応です。`onFinish` では、ジョブを終える保存と、一括チェックの結果の書き込みが、2回の呼び出しに分かれます。2回目が行われないと（ワーカーが止まる、Redis が失敗する）、結果が失われ、その例外で batch の履歴の記録もとばされていました。

- `onFinish` をやめ、`BackfillQueueOptions.finishedJobKeys`（終えたジョブを、ジョブと一緒に書き込むキー）にしました。`FINISH_SCRIPT` が、ジョブと同じスクリプトの中で、渡されたキーにも書き込みます
- キーは、`runs.ts` の `getBackfillRunResultKeys` が作り、batch（`apps/batch/app/videos/backfill/route.ts`）が渡します。`queue.ts` は、渡されたキーに書き込むだけで、一括チェックを知りません
- この点は、Issue の「`onFinish?(job)` に知らせるだけにする」とは違う形です。依存の向きは Issue のとおり直したうえで、この PR より前と同じく、1回の書き込みで保存します

## 関連Issue

Closes #7084

- `packages/*` のビルドのあとに `pnpm run check:package-exports` が通る（ビルドは `packages/*` だけで、アプリは確かめていません）
- `packages/video-backfill` のテストを、本物の Redis（`redis-server` と、Upstash の REST API と互換の中継）に対しても実行し、127件すべて通った。わざと誤りを入れると失敗することも確かめた
  - `ENQUEUE_SCRIPT` の番号の比較を外す → 同時の積み直しのテスト2件が失敗する
  - `FINISH_SCRIPT` の、追加のキーへの書き込みのループを壊す → 結果の書き込みのテスト4件が失敗する

追加したテスト:

- 同じジョブを、2つの依頼が同時に積み直しても、片方だけが成功する（読み取りと書き込みの間に、もう片方を割り込ませるものと、`Promise.all` のもの）
- 書き込むたびに `version` が 1 増える／番号のない保存済みのジョブを積み直せる／項目の並びが違っても、番号が同じなら積み直せる
- 完了と中止のジョブを、渡されたキーにも、1回の呼び出しで書き込む／進めた、戻した、ロックを失ったジョブは書き込まない
- 一括チェックの子ジョブの結果を残す（`runs.test.ts`、batch の `route.test.ts`）

## スクリーンショット

UI の変更はありません。

## 補足情報

- 受け入れ条件の「使う側の import を、書き換えずに済む」について: 今ある import は、そのまま動きます。ただし、依存の向きを直したため、実行の結果を残すには、ジョブを処理する側がキーを渡す必要があり、`apps/batch` のルートに `getBackfillRunResultKeys` の import を1つ足しました。`apps/admin` は変えていません

# Règles de contribution
> [!CAUTION]
> Afin de garantir une application stable et pérenne dans le temps, nous t'invitons à vérifier que tu as bien respecté les règles de contribution. Sans cela, ta Pull Request ne pourra pas être examinée.

- [x] Cette Pull Request porte sur une seule fonctionnalité ou un seul correctif.
- [x] Cette Pull Request n'est pas faite essentiellement avec de l'IA.
- [x] Pour tout changement majeur, j’ai créé une issue afin d’échanger avec les mainteneurs de Papillon sur la meilleure façon de l’intégrer.
- [x] Ma Pull Request respecte les conventions Conventional Commits et Conventional Branch ainsi que les conventions de codage de l'application.
- [x] J’ai testé mes modifications sur iOS et Android, et l’application fonctionne correctement.
- [x] J’emploie un langage informel, clair et concis dans mes messages.
- [x] J’ai documenté mes changements de manière appropriée, soit dans la description de la Pull Request, soit dans le GitBook.
- [x] J’ai ajouté les traductions nécessaires dans au moins un fichier de langue.

# Résumé des changements

> [!NOTE]
> Cette Pull Request corrige plusieurs bugs de l'emploi du temps liés aux fuseaux horaires, à l'affichage des samedis/dimanches et aux statuts PRONOTE.

- **Fuseaux horaires locaux (`#599`)** : Remplacement des formatages et regroupements UTC (`toISOString().split("T")[0]` et `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")`) par `format(d, "yyyy-MM-dd")` et `startOfDay` / `endOfDay` de `date-fns` dans les services PRONOTE, ÉcoleDirecte, AppScho, Multi et Skolengo, ainsi que dans `database/useTimetable.ts` (`Q.between(startOfDay(day.date).getTime(), endOfDay(day.date).getTime())`).
- **Cours sans matière, personnels et statuts PRONOTE (`#690`, `#667`)** : Sécurisation du libellé avec `c.subject?.name || c.status || c.notes || "Cours"`, ajout de `c.personalNames` dans `teacher`, refonte de `mapCourseStatus` pour s'appuyer sur `course.canceled`, `course.test` et `course.status` (afin de ne pas marquer à tort une sortie pédagogique maintenue comme annulée), et classification des pauses chevauchant `12h–14h` (`hStart < 14 && hEnd > 12`) en `"lunch"` (Pause méridienne) dans `ui/components/Course.tsx`.
- **Semaines ISO, samedis et changement de compte (`#629`)** : Passage de `date` dans `getWeeklyTimetable` pour calculer les bornes ISO de la semaine via `startOfISOWeek` / `endOfISOWeek`, sécurisation de `lesson.subject?.label || "Cours"` dans Skolengo, alignement de `useCalendarState.ts` sur `getISOWeek(date)` sans double incrément le dimanche, et réinitialisation de `useWeekendVisibility.ts` lors du changement de compte actif (`lastUsedAccount`) tout en incluant le samedi lorsque `date.getDay() === 6`.

author: jpkha
body:
# Context

A user can unregister their own platform, but a platform admin who is not a member of the organization has to edit the database. This PR gives platform admins (BYPASS) a page listing every platform registration, whatever its organization, and a way to unregister one.

What changes:
- **New admin page** under Settings › Management, "Registered platforms" (`/app/admin/registered-platforms`), visible to platform admins only.
- **Table**: platform title and URL, product and version, organization, tenant, contract and commercial model, status, last connectivity check, registerer, credential, and the service instance / platform / tenant ids.
- **Filters**: product, status, organization, and a free text search on title, URL, ids, tenant, organization name and registerer email.
- **Unregister**: on an active registration, behind a confirmation dialog naming the platform and its organization. It does what the user's own unregister does: the registration becomes inactive, the organization admins get the usual email, and telemetry records it. Unregistering an already inactive registration does nothing.
- The credential column says whether a platform token is stored. The token value is never read nor returned.
- For non-admin users the unregister flow is the same, except that an unregistered platform can no longer use its token (see below).

No screenshot yet: the page was not run in a browser, only covered by component tests.

## How to test

1. Log in as a platform admin (BYPASS) and open Settings › Management › Registered platforms.
2. Check that registrations of organizations you are not a member of are listed, with their organization and registerer.
3. Combine the product, status and organization filters and the search box; the list and the count follow.
4. Click **Unregister** on an active registration, confirm: a success toast appears, the row turns inactive, and Mailpit shows the "platform unregistered" email for the organization admins. The button is gone on that row.
5. Log in as a non-admin user: the menu entry is absent and the page says you are not authorized. The `adminRegisteredPlatforms` query and `adminUnregisterPlatform` mutation answer `FORBIDDEN_ACCESS` (Bruno requests added in `bruno/registration/`).

## Related issues

- Closes [feat(admin): H9 admin view of registered platforms with unregister xtm-hub-private#92](https://github.com/XTM-Hub/xtm-hub-private/issues/92)

# Checklist

## Quality

- [ ] I consider this work complete and ready for review
- [x] I tested all features and edge cases
- [x] I refactored code where necessary to improve quality
- [x] I made sure my code meets development guidelines
- [x] I performed a self-review of my code
- [ ] I added the `skip-feature-env` label if a feature environment is not needed for this PR

## Testing

- [x] I wrote test cases for the relevant use cases (unit, integration or e2e tests)
- [ ] (Bug fixes only) I added tests that reproduce and verify the fix

### What tests have been made

- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [ ] E2E tests
- [ ] Local manual tests

# Additional information

**API (additive, no breaking change)**
- `adminRegisteredPlatforms(first, after, orderBy, orderMode, searchTerm, filter)`: an offset-paginated connection, page size capped at 100, default order is the most recent connectivity check first.
- `adminUnregisterPlatform(serviceInstanceId)` returns the registration after the action.
- Both are guarded with `@Guarded(bypassOnlyGuard())`, the decorator `access-control.md` asks for on new operations, rather than the `@auth(portalCapa: BYPASS)` directive. Who can call them is the same. Access matrix tests cover anonymous, user and admin.

**Credential shape, ready for the key pair migration (H1, xtm-hub-private#85)**
- `credential { kind has_token }`, where `kind` is `token` or `none` today. H1 can add a `key` kind and the `public_key_id` / `key_enrolled_at` fields without breaking clients. The page already shows an unknown kind as its raw value.
- The query selects `token IS NOT NULL`, never the column itself.
- There is no credential filter yet: every registration has a token until the key pair credential lands, so it would select nothing useful. It can come with H1.

**Unregister flow**
- The user and admin unregister now share one helper. Setting the status to inactive is a conditional update (`WHERE status = 'active'`), so of two concurrent unregisters only one sends the emails and the telemetry event.
- The admin path skips the organization capability check and logs the admin id, service instance, platform, tenant and organization with `logApp`. Telemetry records the admin as the user who unregistered.
- The admin path acts on behalf of the organization the list and the dialog show, the one of the newest subscription, so the email goes to the admins of the organization the admin confirmed.
- Unregistering now cuts the platform off, for the user's own unregister too. The token stays stored, but an inactive registration no longer authenticates:
  - the `@platform_token` directive accepts an active registration only (`consumeProvisionedNewsFeedItems`, `autoRegisterPlatform`); the news feed also refuses an inactive registration itself and keeps its items provisioned;
  - a connectivity refresh of an inactive registration answers `inactive` and only records the check: the URL, version, contract and tenant name it sends no longer change the row;
  - a Hub-deployed trial still authenticates through its deployment request, so its first auto-registration works as before. An unregistered trial calling `autoRegisterPlatform` again still passes, without reactivating its registration.
  - Contact sales and the document download already required an active registration.
- The list pages by offset itself rather than through `paginate()`, which would select the token column and count an `id` column `PlatformConfiguration` lacks.

**Out of scope**
- The "reset credential" action is still under discussion in the issue.
- No migration, no new environment variable, no new dependency.

author: ryceg
body:
## Why

xDrip+'s Nightscout REST uploader gzips its body and sends it chunked. The web's `/api` proxy copied every incoming header, so `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` reached Node's fetch, which refused the request (500 "fetch failed") before the API saw it. Behind that, the API did not inflate gzip request bodies, which Nightscout's body-parser does.

## What

- `buildProxyHeaders` strips the hop-by-hop headers (RFC 9110 7.6.1, plus any named in `Connection`), and `Content-Length` and `Expect`, since the body is buffered. undici rejects a mismatched `Content-Length` and any `Expect` the same way.
- `buildProxyResponseHeaders` strips hop-by-hop headers, `Content-Encoding` and `Content-Length` from the upstream response, whose body fetch has already decoded.
- The API uses ASP.NET Core request decompression (gzip, deflate), placed after `UseRouting` so an endpoint's `[RequestSizeLimit]` bounds the inflated body (Kestrel's 100 MB otherwise).

## Tests

- `api-proxy-headers.test.ts`: every hop-by-hop header, a `Connection`-named one, `Content-Length`, `Expect`, `Content-Encoding` kept on the request, the response helper (9 of these fail on main).
- `EntriesGoldenTests.PostEntries_CompressedBody_IsInflatedAndStored`: gzip and deflate bodies to `/api/v1/entries` are stored (400 on main).
- `RequestDecompressionSizeLimitTests`: a gzip body that is small on the wire but inflates past the custom sound upload's 512 KB limit is refused (passes only with the middleware after routing).

## Gates

- Solution and every integration project build; API unit tests 14068 passed; Infrastructure.Data unit tests 1920 passed.
- Web: svelte-check 0 errors; vitest node suite 2760 passed; `lint:ci` clean; `lint:copy` 0 errors.

## Review

Hostile review (Opus): two findings fixed (decompression moved after routing with a size-limit test; `Expect` dropped), one doc nit fixed.

Closes #3465

author: lrivals
body:
## Résumé

### Pagination intelligente
Les recherches sont triées des plus récentes aux plus anciennes. Après chaque page, le scraper compare les dates des annonces au dernier passage de la recherche (`data/.search_state.json`, clé `site|profil`) :
- toutes antérieures (marge 1 jour, dates au jour près / fuseaux) → les pages suivantes ont déjà été lues, arrêt ;
- page sans dates exploitables → arrêt seulement si toutes ses annonces sont déjà en base.

Dates utilisées : LBC `index_date` (date de remontée, celle qui ordonne le tri « Plus récentes », exposée en `listed_at`), sinon `published_at` (SeLoger, Bien'ici).

Garde-fous :
- parcours complet au premier passage, puis tous les `SMART_FULL_SCAN_DAYS` (7) jours pour revoir les prix des annonces anciennes ; `scrape --full-scan` pour le forcer ; `SMART_PAGINATION=0` pour désactiver ;
- l'état n'est enregistré qu'en fin normale (`stale` / `end` / `max`) : un passage bloqué ou en erreur ne fait sauter aucune page au suivant ;
- PAP (défilement infini, pas de dates) inchangé.

### Top 50 quotidien
- `NOTIFY_TOP_N` (défaut 10) : taille du Top, découpé en plusieurs messages sous la limite Telegram de 4096 caractères (Top 50 ≈ 2 messages sur la base actuelle).
- `NOTIFY_TOP_HOUR` (optionnel) : en mode `daily`, pas d'envoi avant cette heure.
- Le Top n'est envoyé que si le run a récupéré au moins une annonce.

## Vérifications
- `pytest` : 724 passed, 1 skipped (nouveau `tests/test_smart_pagination.py`, tests Top N et pipeline).
- Run réel Bien'ici (état temporaire, sans écriture en base ni notification) : 1er passage 10 pages, 2e passage arrêté après la page 2.
- LBC / SeLoger non testés en réel (risque DataDome) : à surveiller dans `journalctl --user -u scraper.service | grep -i pagination` après les prochains runs du timer.

## À noter pour la relecture
- `_scrape_current_page` retourne désormais les annonces ajoutées ; `scan_status` est posé par `_paginate*` / `fetch_annonces`.
- Le `.env` local (non versionné) a été complété avec `NOTIFY_TOP10=daily` et `NOTIFY_TOP_N=50`.

author: emchristiansen
body:
## Problem

Muninn serves the Observatory site from a `dx build --release --platform web --features voice --package observatory_site` dist. That build runs Cargo inside the dev shell, outside Buck2 and NativeLink.

The generator can compile a package for wasm32 only as a **library cdylib** (`[wasm] packages` with `[package.metadata.buck2.wasm]`). A Dioxus web app is built from its **binary** target: `observatory_site`'s `src/main.rs` calls `observatory_site::main()`, which runs `dioxus::launch`. Its library has no `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]`, so its cdylib would not boot. Adding a start function to the library would make the app launch twice under `dx`.

## Change

`[package.metadata.buck2.wasm] bin = "<name>"` makes the module that binary target compiled for wasm32. Generation then emits:

- `rust_binary(name = "<name>-wasm-<key>")`:
  - the binary's crate root, with the module's features;
  - the module graph's dependencies, as their `-wasm-<key>` variants;
  - the package's own library, as the graph's variant (`<lib>-wasm-<key>`);
  - the profile's flags **plus its link-time flags**, such as `-Clto=fat`. The library variant then takes no link-time flags, because it links into the binary.

  It is wasm32-only, like every module rule.
- `configured_alias(name = "bin-wasm-wasm32[.<variant>]")` for `[wasm] platform`, whose default output is the module. Generation owns it, as it owns `lib-wasm-wasm32` and `wasm-test-module-wasm32`.
- No `lib-wasm-wasm32` alias for such a package.

Refusals:

- a `bin` that names no binary target of the package;
- a `[package.metadata.buck2.test-env]` entry naming a binary module, which has no `[cdylib]`. It is refused as a module `[wasm] packages` does not build.

`CACHE_VERSION` goes from 17 to 18, so a cached run regenerates once.

## Tests

`test_a_binary_wasm_module_is_its_binary_for_wasm32` covers:

- the binary rule's crate root, features, dependencies and `-Clto=fat`;
- the library variant without `-Clto`;
- the dependency's feature from `voice`;
- the alias, and that no `lib-wasm-wasm32` is emitted;
- byte-identical output on a `--no-cache` rerun, which caught the alias-ownership bug during development;
- the refusal for an unknown `bin`.

The three cache tests now expect version 18.

## Checks

Local Cargo in Muninn's dev shell (cargo 1.100.0). Local Cargo is a disclosed departure, as in earlier fork work.

| Check | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --check` | 0 |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | 0 |

body:
The second compiler gate, and the tool that runs it.

**Correction to `33a30826`'s merged message:** the 1.0.0 compiler was MSVC **14.50.35728** (family 14.50.35717), which Epic lists as **preferred, not banned**. The file `docs/release-manager.md` carries the same correction. UnrealBuildTool checks the banned and minimum ranges against the compiler version and the preferred ranges against the MSVC family (`MicrosoftPlatformSDK.cs`), so both numbers matter.

## Tools

**`Tools/check-toolchain.py`** (release gate, offline) reads the version and family a build names and classifies it against the pinned `Engine/Config/Windows/Windows_SDK.json`:
- banned and minimum ranges → compiler version
- preferred ranges → MSVC family
A banned version fails; a version outside the preferred families warns. Not wired into `validate.py`: today's evidence would be judged against a moving rule set, so this runs on release evidence.

**`Tools/compile-with-msvc.py`** (engine tier, supervised) replays the response files UBT already wrote for the module with a chosen MSVC. It retargets the pinned `/external:I` include directory to the chosen compiler, restores the `/std:` flag that lives in the per-file response, rebuilds the shared PCH, and redirects every object, PCH and log into scratch. It drops UBT's `/experimental:log` and `/sourceDependencies` so nothing is written into an engine or repository Intermediate folder.

**`docs/release-manager.md`** records the gate as manual, with the reason: `release-check.py` reads evidence schema 1 and cannot verify a compiler family offline.

## Results

| Run | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fixtures | `python Tools/test-check-toolchain.py` | pass: 14.50.35728 preferred, 14.44.35230 preferred, 14.44.35209 banned, 14.43.34808 banned, 14.50.35720 banned, 14.38.33130 allowed |
| today's real build evidence | `python Tools/check-toolchain.py --log .local/executions/9493c1e7…/01.log` | `PASS: MSVC 14.50.35728 (family 14.50.35717) is preferred` |
| new main, 14.43.34808 | `python Tools/compile-with-msvc.py --msvc 14.43.34808` | **247 units, 0 errors, 0 C4702** |
| v1.0.0 sources, 14.43.34808 | `python Tools/compile-with-msvc.py --msvc 14.43.34808 --sources <ef1d1e1f worktree>/Plugins/TurboMCP/Source/TurboMCP` | **246 units, 253 errors, all C4702, failing file `TurboMCPWidgetPersistenceTest.cpp` only** |

14.43.34808 is banned, so it is used only as the available stand-in to reproduce the C4702 shape.

## Evidence

`python Tools/validate.py` on clean head `0ef637a4`: **36 passed, 0 failed**, exit 0. Report `C:\Dev\_x3\.local\validation\4a71630fdbb1452fae66865da48cdff2\report.json`, `commit: 0ef637a49b6e052246468d285a232872be628807`, `dirty: False`.

## Why

`ghcr.io/ublue-os/kinoite-main:44` moved to `44.20261118.3` with kernel **7.3.4-200.fc44**. The unchanged admission correctly refused the 7.3.3 module with "kernel/core package does not match reviewed ABI" (PR image gate `44262380167`). Every desktop x86 build now stops at that step.

- Stock 7.3.4 still lacks the SMOCF05 match: the vendor transport only has the aliases `SMOCF00` and `SMO8B30`.

- The review script and packager now derive every SRPM, tarball, NVR and requires name from the single reviewed kernel constant.
- The native toolbox old/fixed compile changes the aliases only by `acpi*:SMOCF05:*`. The 7.3.4 vermagic matches, and the review signature is verified.
- The module is signed with the unchanged dedicated module key (certificate `b8c98812…`) and packaged as `kmod-moos-smocf05-7.3.4-200.1.moos1.fc44` (20,779 bytes). `admit.py check-package` passes. The vendor vmlinuz, core and transport digests come from the signed RPMs.
- The sensor signature, package, backport, readiness and hwdb tests pass.

Kernel trust (MOK/keyring), physical rotation acceptance, and the full image composition are separate. The full image composition runs in this PR's image gate and in a local `just build`.

author: shugo
body:
A `date` column can now be read as a `Date`, Quarz's new calendar date (quarz-lang/quarz#884), and a `Date` can be sent as a parameter.

```quarz
row = conn.query("SELECT day FROM stats WHERE day >= $1", [Date.new(2026, 11, 1)]).rows[0]
row.date(0)     # Date
```

Closes #38.

**What it adds:**
- **`row.date(i)` and `row.date?(i)`.** They parse the text the server sends: PostgreSQL's ISO form `YYYY-MM-DD`, which pg asks for. `date` raises `PG::NullError` for NULL; text that is not a date raises `ArgumentError`, as the other readers do.
- **`row.dates(i)` and `dates?`** for a `date[]`, as `times` does.
- **What a `Date` cannot hold** raises `ArgumentError` naming the value and saying to read the column as a string:
  - `infinity` and `-infinity`;
  - a year beyond 9999 (`10000-01-01`);
  - a BC date (`0044-03-15 BC`).

  The README says so.
- **`row.time` on a `date` column** is unchanged: midnight UTC, pinned.
- **A `Date` parameter** is sent as its ISO text, which a `date` column or `$1::date` takes. An `Array` of `Date`s is a `date[]` and is sent typed: OID 1182, as arrays of Ints, Bools and Bytes are. `date[]` has one meaning, so a bare `unnest($1)` resolves without a cast. The parameter `ArgumentError` lists `Date`.

**Tests**, in `test/query_test.qz` (`test_dates`, against a server):
- reading: a date, NULL with `date?` and `date`, `0001-01-01`, `9999-12-31` and 2024-02-29;
- `time` on a `date` column;
- the four values a `Date` cannot hold, through `date` and through `dates`, each with its message;
- text that is not a date;
- parameters: `$1::date + 1`, a `date` column with `=` and `<`, a year-44 date written and read back, `= ANY($1)` with a `date[]` holding a nil, a `date[]` round trip, `pg_typeof($1)` giving `date[]`, and `unnest($1)` without a cast.

**Verified:** `quarz test test/query_test.qz` passed (58 tests) and `doc --check` exited 0, with quarz main c6ca7ec4. The five checks follow in a comment.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact Unsubscribe links used a token that identified only the user while the email type came from an editable query string, and GET /api/email/unsubscribe immediately mutated preferences. A scanner or tampered URL could silently disable all optional emails and even password-reset/account emails, causing account lockout or missed security/lifecycle notifications. ## Root cause The unsubscribe token did not bind the preference type, GET performed the mutation, and required account/security email types were included in opt-out catalogs and preference updates. ## Fix - Bind unsubscribe JWTs to the exact preference type and reject legacy/tampered tokens. - Make GET confirmation-only; POST performs the unsubscribe. - Treat password reset and account/lifecycle emails as required: no unsubscribe footers, hidden from the preferences catalog, ignored by direct preference updates, and always sent despite opt-outs. - Add a DB-free critical regression script covering this behavior. ## Validation - npm run test:critical-bugs

author: raphael
body:
When a user starts agents from the terminal instead of the Chorus dialog, Surla prints the commands to run. In a usability study the user had to guess a model name and set `yolo:true` for every agent without knowing what it bypassed, because nothing listed the models or explained `yolo`.

Chorus v0.13.0 answers both: `chorus team inspect --space <id> --choices choices.json` lists, for each chosen program, its models and reasoning efforts, marks a chosen model the program does not list, and states the exact permission flag `yolo` adds and what it bypasses. Surla now requires Chorus v0.13.0 and points to that command:

- The printed terminal step names `chorus team inspect --space <id>`, `chorus team launch --help`, `chorus team inspect --space <id> --choices choices.json` for models and permission effects, and `chorus team launch --space <id> --choices choices.json`, with the project's actual space ID. The step and its recovery text are shortened so that the whole step stays within the project step's 512-character limit for long and quoted space IDs.
- `surla` refuses to start the team with an older Chorus, before it changes anything, naming the required version, as it did for the previous minimum.
- The README, How it works, Reference and Architecture playbook describe the inspection and the new minimum.

Upgrade: install Chorus v0.13.0 or later (`chorus update -yes`) before using this version of Surla.

body:
## Summary

Add one BF16 SYCL operator for `RMSNorm(x) * (1 + scale[indices]) + shift[indices]`, including H3's strided AdaLN tables. It includes a Python guard, tests, and a benchmark.

[#497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/497) uses LayerNorm and a gated residual without indexed tables. [#545](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/545) adds indexed scale/shift but runs RMSNorm separately.

## Operator performance

author: thomtrp
body:
Stacked on #30744, which stops the runtime reading these columns. This PR drops `core."workflowVersion"."workspaceWorkflowVersionId"` (and its unique index) and `core."workflow"."lastPublishedVersionId"`. `core."workflow"."workspaceWorkflowId"` stays, because webhook URLs use it.

## Why 2.62
The 2.61 backfill (#30693) reads both columns. It is a workspace command, and a version runs its instance commands before its workspace commands, so a 2.61 drop would run before the backfill. The drop therefore ships as a deferred 2.62 command, following "Shipping a command for a future version" in `UPGRADE_COMMANDS.md`:
- it is registered but dormant now;
- it runs once 2.62 is the current version.

This PR and #30744 must merge while 2.61 is current, so that 2.61 servers already stop reading and writing the columns. The drop then runs one release later, the same gap `jobConfig` had (unused in 2.60, dropped in 2.61).

## Changes
- **Upgrade:** `DropLegacyWorkflowVersionIdColumnsFastInstanceCommand` in the 2-62 folder drops the index and both columns. `down` restores them. It is registered in `INSTANCE_COMMANDS`.
- **Entities:** both properties keep their `@Column` and are typed `WasRemovedInUpgrade<string | null>`, as `jobConfig` was. Servers on 2.61 still select them during an upgrade, and the pending-migration check stays empty.
- **Flat entities and writers:**
  - the two properties leave the flat-entity property configuration;
  - the workflow manifest converter, the core workflow creation and draft version creation stop writing them;
  - the compared-properties snapshot drops `lastPublishedVersionId`.
- **Trigger map cache:** the upgrade-window guard keyed on `workspaceWorkflowVersionId` being hidden now keys on `isSystemSideEffect` (added in 2.45, after the `coreWorkflowId` backfill). Once the dropped column is marked removed, the old guard would have emptied the trigger maps for good. Without any guard, a cross-version upgrade from an old version computes trigger maps before active core versions have a `coreWorkflowId`, and the upgrade aborts.
- **Tests:** unit and integration tests stop selecting or asserting the two columns.

## To do at the 2.62 bump
- Add `@WasRemovedInUpgrade({ upgradeCommandName: DROP_LEGACY_WORKFLOW_VERSION_ID_COLUMNS_UPGRADE_COMMAND_NAME })` on `WorkflowVersionEntity.workspaceWorkflowVersionId` and `WorkflowEntity.lastPublishedVersionId`. Adding it now would fail boot, because the decorator names a dormant command. `2-62/__tests__/drop-legacy-workflow-version-id-columns-entity-wiring.spec.ts` enforces this: it passes while 2.62 is a next version and fails after the bump until both entities name the command.
- Remove the `IDX_WORKFLOW_VERSION_WORKSPACE_VERSION_ID` declaration from the entity. It stays for now so that the pending-migration check generates nothing while the drop is dormant.
- The two entity properties go once 2.62 leaves the cross-upgrade window.

## Validation
- Targeted specs pass: 12 suites, 139 tests, including the upgrade decorator validation, the flat-entity property snapshots, the manifest converters and the new wiring spec.
- Lint and format are clean on the touched files.
- I did not run the integration suites or a local upgrade; CI covers them.

author: mrkkrp
body:
Close #510.

Where a conditional chooses the operator of a bind's pattern written
infix and a do block hangs after the `<-`, the `do` came out under the
`#endif` at the column of the statement, where it ends the statement
before its body and does not parse.

The merge ends each branch with a separator that the code shared after
the conditional puts alone on its line (PR 388, PR 472), and ends that
line before a body hanging after it (PR 505). The `=` of an equation
and the `->` of a case alternative are printed with their body, but the
`<-` of a bind and its body are two things the configurations share, so
the line of the `<-` ended with it, and the body that followed, a group
that opens with a space, began the line under the `#endif`.

Where all a shared thing prints goes into each branch, the next shared
thing, if nothing comes between them and it puts nothing on the line it
continues, is now cut where that line ends as well (`afterChoice` in
`woven`): a hanging body is attached under the `#endif` as the next pass
attaches it, after a break and one step in.

The issue's input

```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE CPP #-}

module A where

next queue = do
  item
#ifdef WITH_SEQUENCE
    :<
#else
    :|
#endif
    rest <- do
      pop queue
```

now comes out, in one pass and with `--check-ast --check-idempotence`
passing, as

```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE CPP #-}

module A where

next queue = do
  item
#ifdef WITH_SEQUENCE
    :< rest <-
#else
    :| rest <-
#endif
    do
      pop queue
```

as it does with `rest` written in each branch. A hanging `case` and
`forM queue $ \x -> do` after the `<-` declined the same way on master
and now come out one step in as well; a body that does not hang came out
right already and comes out as before.

Results:

- `cabal test`: 21135 examples, 0 failures, 42 pending.
- `TILIA_ORTHOGONALITY=1` over our own corpus: 852 examples, 0 failures.
- Hackage records: no change. Over the whole corpus, the new rule changes
  a document only in the new vendored example.
- Benchmarks: against master, 48.850 G instructions before and 48.852 G
  after over 91 benchmarks (+0.00%); format 27.4035 G before and after
  (+0.00%), synthetic/conditionals +0.00%. `cabal bench` fails on recall
  megaparsec-9.8.1 (+0.6% instructions against the record) on master as
  well on this machine, so the record is left alone.

Description saved then a refused name: "Saved the description, but not the name: ...", typed name and saved text kept; the retry saved only the name (no second description call). Pasted U+2028/U+0085 turn into spaces; the API refuses U+2028 with "Description cannot contain line breaks". Earlier at e3a7aa23: box only on non-Base skins, short text refused with typed text kept, save/reload/clear. Plugin routes and the in-game side (RPCharacters #159 on Dev) tested earlier.

## What players get
Every wardrobe skin except Base can have its own description: what other players read in game while the character wears that skin, instead of the character description. The box isn't shown on Base or for characters still waiting for acceptance.

Purpose (usability): a reader sees what mcl-whiteboard talks to, which containers it runs as, and what it is made of, today and in the storming board the plan builds, without reading the code. The gate fails CI by name when a diagram goes missing or drifts from its generator.

Refs #1, #12. Design: #1 (issuecomment-6976595393), as amended by the reviewer (issuecomment-6976646368); PASS issuecomment-6976693480.

### What it changes
- **The gate pin** in `.github/workflows/c4-model.yml` moves to `399162a9d3dcac07b904ed12f203f42165c577e8`, which asks for a Container diagram. Commit 1 moves only the pin. Its c4-model run, [44291508293](https://github.com/macula-services/mcl-whiteboard/actions/runs/44291508293), fails by name: `c4_model: no assets/*container*.svg: a service is planned from its Context and Container model`.

- **The Context** names the board's people: the facilitator, the participants, the builder, and the planned expert agent.

## Ajustes
- Un «Guardar» por grupo, con «Cambios sin guardar», «Descartar» y «Corrige el campo en rojo para guardar».
- Confirman antes del PUT: el check-in, el primer precio de la pausa (no se puede quitar), un cambio de precio y las pausas por año a 0.
- Vaciar un precio ya puesto se explica en el campo y no se guarda (antes se guardaba sin efecto).
- «¿Salir sin guardar?» con `useBlocker` al navegar, y `beforeunload` al recargar o cerrar.

author: lbajsarowicz
body:
This pull request adds one GitHub Actions workflow that checks every pull request, every push to `master` and the merge queue if you use one: Composer validation, PHP lint, the Magento coding standard, `setup:di:compile`, static content deployment, the existing unit tests and PHPStan. It runs on the latest patch of each supported Magento Open Source release line, on the lowest and highest PHP version that release supports, and reports one `Result` check that you can require before merging. ### Your existing CI The repository already runs `extdn-static-tests.yml`, `magento-integration-tests.yml`, `phpstan.yml`, `release-actions.yml`. Magento Check runs next to these workflows and changes none of them. It adds: - `setup:di:compile` and static content deployment on a real Magento install - Magento 2.4.7, 2.4.8 and 2.4.9 (the current matrix stops at 2.4.8), refreshed automatically when a release comes out - PHP lint on each supported PHP version ### Why - Compilation errors, code a newer PHP rejects and failing unit tests show up in the pull request instead of in a shop after a release. - The list of releases refreshes on every run, so a new Magento or PHP release is tested as soon as it is supported, without a change to the workflow. - PHPCS and PHPStan findings are shown inline in "Files changed". PHPCS checks the PHP and PHTML files a pull request changes (the whole file, including code that was already there), not the whole module. PHPStan analyses the whole module at level 1. - No account, no Magento credentials and no repository secrets. Compute on GitHub-hosted runners is free for public repositories; runs use Actions concurrency and keep their reports as artifacts for 7 days. ### How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR T["Pull request / push"] --> M["Version matrix"] M --> J1["Magento 2.4.7 @ PHP 8.2"] M --> J2["..."] M --> J3["Magento 2.4.9 @ PHP 8.5"] J1 & J2 & J3 --> R["Result"] ``` Each Magento and PHP combination is one job: ```mermaid flowchart LR S["composer validate
PHP lint"] --> I["Install Magento
+ this module"] I --> P["PHPCS"] I --> C["di:compile
static content"] C --> U["Unit tests"] C --> PS["PHPStan"] ``` Each job runs in the [Warden](https://warden.dev) image `wardenenv/php-fpm:-magento2`, which carries PHP with every extension Magento needs, Composer and Node.js. Magento is installed from the public Mage-OS mirror with the module from the pull request's checkout, and the job checks that the installed module is that checkout. Unit tests and PHPStan run only after compilation and static content deployment succeed. The `Result` job collects every combination into one table in the run summary and fails when any check failed. Files added or changed: - `.github/workflows/magento-check.yml`: the workflow. - `phpcs.xml.dist`: the Magento 2 coding standard. - `phpstan.neon`: level 1 with `bitexpert/phpstan-magento`, which knows Magento's generated factories and proxies. - `composer.json`: `require-dev` with `magento/magento-coding-standard`, `phpstan/phpstan`, `bitexpert/phpstan-magento` and `phpstan/extension-installer`, and `allow-plugins` for the two Composer plugins that register the coding standard and the PHPStan extension. Both are root-only settings: a shop that requires this package installs none of it. ### Security and trust - I get no access to this repository: no collaborator invitation, no GitHub App, no secrets. - The workflow runs on `pull_request`, never `pull_request_target`, so a pull request from a public fork runs with a read-only token and without secrets. - The check jobs get a temporary token with `contents: read` (checkout) and `pull-requests: read` (list changed files). The matrix and result jobs get no permissions. The token cannot push, comment, create releases or publish anything. - `actions/checkout` does not store the token in the checkout (`persist-credentials: false`). The checks are two actions I maintain, [github-action-magento-extension](https://github.com/lbajsarowicz/github-action-magento-extension) and [github-action-magento-matrix](https://github.com/lbajsarowicz/github-action-magento-matrix) (MIT). They execute code in your CI: Composer installs Magento and the tools (including the two plugins above), then compilation, unit tests and PHPStan run PHP. Both are referenced by their major tag `@v1`, so fixes reach you without another pull request, and also run without your review. If you want to review every update, pin both actions to a commit SHA (`@ # v1.0.0`) and update them yourself or with Dependabot. Network traffic from the runner: the matrix action asks magento.watch for the list of supported releases and sends this repository's public name in its User-Agent (set `send-repository: false` on that step to leave it out; if the request fails, a bundled list is used). The runner pulls the Warden PHP image from Docker Hub; Composer downloads Magento from the Mage-OS mirror and the tools from Packagist. Logs and reports stay in GitHub Actions. This is a compatibility check, not a dependency audit: Composer's advisory blocking is switched off inside the temporary Magento project so older release lines still install. ### After merging (optional) Merging the workflow does not make the check required. To block merges on it, in Settings: 1. Let the workflow run once on `master` in this repository; GitHub only offers checks it has seen. 2. **Rules › Rulesets** (or **Branches** for classic branch protection) for `master`: enable "Require status checks to pass" and add `Result` only. The per-version job names change with each Magento release; `Result` fails whenever one of them fails. 3. **Actions › General**, if the repository allows only selected actions: allow actions created by GitHub (`actions/checkout`, `actions/cache`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `actions/download-artifact`) and add `lbajsarowicz/github-action-magento-extension@*` and `lbajsarowicz/github-action-magento-matrix@*`. 4. **Actions › General › Approval for running fork pull request workflows from contributors**: keep GitHub's default or anything stricter. ### Test plan The workflow ran on this branch in my fork on 5 combinations (2.4.7-p10 @ PHP 8.2, 2.4.7-p10 @ PHP 8.3, 2.4.8-p5 @ PHP 8.3, 2.4.8-p5 @ PHP 8.4, 2.4.9 @ PHP 8.5); every check passed or had nothing to run; each combination took at most 3 minutes: [run](https://github.com/lbajsarowicz/contribution-multisafepay-magento2-core/actions/runs/44291529423). > [!NOTE] > I contribute to open source to help keep Magento and Adobe Commerce fast and secure. > More of that work, and how to reach me: [lbajsarowicz.me/open-source](https://lbajsarowicz.me/open-source/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=pull_request&utm_campaign=oss_footer&utm_content=MultiSafepay__magento2-core)

author: catborise
body:
## Summary
- **Restore over, again:** the copies' names came from the VM, the disk and the backup's minute only. A second restore of the same backup over the VM (or of another backup taken in the same minute) picked the name of the disk the VM already ran from and was refused. Names are now chosen at submission, numbered from 2 when taken, and kept in the job intent (`names`) apart from the VM state rechecked before and after the copies.
- **Schedule run reasons:** a failed run stored the formatted English error and the page could not translate it. `BackupRun.note` now keeps messages (text and values) like job errors, shown with a new `words` template filter; migration 0006 replaces the column (prod has no stored notes).

## Tests
- `test_the_same_backup_restored_over_again_takes_the_next_free_name`, `test_a_name_taken_after_the_job_was_queued_is_refused_and_nothing_removed`
- `test_a_vm_that_cannot_be_backed_up_fails_once_with_the_reason` now checks the Turkish rendering with its value in place.
- Full suite: 2759 tests OK; ruff clean.

author: richman68899-hash
body:
## Problem

The revision-sprint content filter accepted any value that Python could convert with `float()`. That includes `NaN`, infinity, and booleans. The shared numeric grader rejects these definitions, so the sprint could select a question that it cannot score reliably.

Invalid or negative tolerances also passed the sprint's eligibility filter.

## Changes

- Reject boolean answer keys and boolean tolerances.
- Require finite numeric answer keys and tolerances.
- Reject negative tolerances.
- Preserve valid numeric and numeric-string answer definitions.

## Tests

Adds a course-bank integration regression covering valid numbers, NaN, infinity, Boolean answer keys, NaN tolerance, and negative tolerance.

## Scope

This is a question-eligibility guard for revision sprints. It does not change the shared grader, question content, or tolerance policy for existing lesson screens.

Psalm drops the taint of an object when a dynamic property is read from it (a `stdClass` row, a decoded JSON document).

```php
<?php
$document = json_decode((string) $_GET["document"]);
if ($document instanceof stdClass) {

}
```

**After**
```php
    echo (string) $document->title; // TaintedHtml
```

## Sprint 2.2 — Durable Sync (rebased on latest main)

This PR is based on the latest Lovable-synced `main` commit and preserves its guide-intent, chat de-duplication, and glass UI changes.

- Add a persistent IndexedDB queue for validated project/source descriptors only.
- Coalesce updates per project and fingerprint manifests to avoid redundant syncs.
- Retry transient failures with persisted capped exponential backoff.
- Persist the project revision after a source-stage partial failure and retry from that committed revision.
- Block auth/revision/tombstone/account-owner conflicts rather than silently rebasing or resurrecting sources.
- Wake the worker on startup, authentication, online/focus/visibility, and newly queued manifests.
- Queue local project/source writes and reconcile existing local projects during workspace bootstrap.
- Make chat drawer auth bootstrap fail closed to a clear login state instead of leaving an infinite loading spinner when Supabase/anonymous auth is unavailable.
- Extend PGlite tests for two-device stale project/source revision compare-and-swap.
- Update E2E smoke to verify the SQL-guide prompt survives the login gate when CI has no Supabase auth configuration.

## Data boundary
Raw files, dataset rows, query results, DuckDB state, and credentials remain local. The queue stores only validated project/source descriptors and safe metadata.

## Verification
No database migration or production data mutation is included. CI will validate TypeScript, Vitest, PGlite RLS/CAS tests, and build.

The Claude plugin directory refused the plugin: it accepts scripts only from Verified organizations, and the three skills ship Python scripts. This splits the repository into two plugins so the MCP server can be submitted on its own.

# Règles de contribution

- [x] J’ai testé mes modifications sur iOS et Android, et l’application fonctionne correctement.

- [x] J’ai documenté mes changements de manière appropriée, soit dans la description de la Pull Request, soit dans le GitBook.
- [x] J’ai ajouté les traductions nécessaires dans au moins un fichier de langue.

# Résumé des changements

> [!NOTE]
> Cette Pull Request déroule correctement les événements iCal récurrents (`RRULE`), prend en compte les `VTIMEZONE`, `EXDATE` et `RECURRENCE-ID`, et ajoute un cache mémoire par URL avec déduplication des requêtes en vol.

- **Déroulement des récurrences (`services/local/parsers/ical-event-parser.ts`)** :
  - Enregistrement des composants `vtimezone` dans `ICAL.TimezoneService.register(vtz)`.
  - Séparation des `vevent` maîtres et des exceptions (`event.isRecurrenceException()`), puis liaison par `uid` via `masterEvent.relateException(exceptionEvent)` sans fuite entre UID distincts.
  - Ajout des paramètres optionnels `(rangeStart?: Date, rangeEnd?: Date)` à `parseICalEvents` et `parseICalString` pour dérouler les occurrences récurrentes via `event.iterator()` (plafonné à `MAX_ITERATIONS = 2000`, arrêt dès `next.toJSDate() > rangeEnd`), résoudre les détails via `event.getOccurrenceDetails(next)` et produire des identifiants déterministes `${baseUid}::${startDate.getTime()}`.
- **Cache et résolution par ID (`services/local/ical.ts`)** :
  - Mise en cache mémoire du texte brut `.ics` par URL (TTL 5 min) avec déduplication des requêtes réseau simultanées.
  - Passage de `(weekStart, weekEnd)` depuis `getICalEventsForWeek` et support des IDs d'occurrences contenant `"::"` dans `getICalCourseById` en ciblant la fenêtre `[occMs - 1000, occMs + 1000]`.
- **Tests unitaires (`services/local/parsers/ical-event-parser.test.ts`)** : Couverture de `RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY`, `EXDATE`, `RECURRENCE-ID` modifié avec `VTIMEZONE` et appel sans bornes.
