author: max-clauseo-agent
body:
Owner thread: host follow-ups (iris)

host: on Windows, Claude's shell deny rules are a short fixed list that does not grow

## What changed

On Windows, Claude's launch settings no longer carry the walked shell deny list
(`agent/data_fence/shell_deny.rs`). That list multiplied every target by each spelling of the
data folder, each separator, each shell and each folder the launch walked into. On a test laptop
it came to 9,472 rules and 656 KB. At 12,116 rules and 843 KB, Claude Code's classifier stopped
giving a verdict, so every command that needed it was refused.

A Windows launch now sends a fixed list from a new module, `agent/data_fence/fixed_shell_deny.rs`.
It covers 11 secret places under `<data>`:

- `agents/codex-acp`: Codex's home, with its login and transcripts
- `agents/signin`: the sign-in state
- `agents/claude-acp/login-source`
- `agents/claude-acp/home/.credentials.json`
- `agents/claude-acp/home/.claude.json`: account state, with an API key when one is set
- `run/*/relay-token`: the case-law relay token
- `run/*/proxy-secret`: the egress proxy password
- `launch-settings`
- `settings.json`
- `state.sqlite`: the host's store
- `search.sqlite`: the search index

Each place is denied as the target and everything under it. Each rule goes out once for every
combination of:

- **Spelling of `<data>`, at most 2.** The default folder is written as `ai.clauseo.desktop`
  alone, which every spelling of it ends in, so it always counts as one.
- **Separator:** `\` and `/`.
- **Shell:** `PowerShell(…)` and `Bash(…)`.

The rules use the same rendering as before (`render`). The list does not grow with matters,
conversations, run folders or walked folders. Only the bytes of each rule grow with the path's
length.

Unchanged:

- the `Read`/`Edit` denies
- the own folders' shell allow rules and their glob denies
- the host's auto-deny (`asks.rs`/`outside.rs`)
- Codex
- macOS and Linux
- no history rules on Windows (as in 629bb732a)

The shed path (`SHED_AT`, `shell_rules_within`) is gone. The walked generator is now built in
tests only (`#[cfg(test)]`), beside the rule matcher those tests share.

## Before and after

The long default path is `C:\Users\Rohan Shiralkar\AppData\Roaming\ai.clauseo.desktop`, with
30 matters, 50 conversations and 5 run folders. The settings file is measured as JSON.

| | Shell deny rules | Settings size |
|---|---|---|
| Before (walked list with its variable forms) | 3,126 (2,934 of them from the walked list) | 243,910 B |
| After | 236 (44 fixed, 192 own-folder glob denies, 1 `Bash`) | 98,754 B |
| After, with an 8.3 second spelling | 428 | 190,366 B |

The 8.3 case doubles the `Read`/`Edit` rules and the glob denies. The rule generator never makes
an 8.3 spelling, so real launches have one spelling.

The after count is the same for:

- 1 or 30 matters
- 1 or 50 conversations
- 0 or 5 run folders
- a short or a long path

## No longer covered by a shell rule

These are left to Claude Code's classifier, under the `Read`/`Edit` denies and the host's
auto-deny:

- other matters' notes
- other conversations' work folders
- other projects' tool results and transcripts
- logs, counts, updates, the skill packs
- the rest of Claude's config folder
- the data folder named alone, a `..` after it, and the shared and read-only places

Also not caught:

- a configured data folder written through a variable or a share path
- an 8.3 short name
- a `cd` first
- a path built at run time

## Tests

New, in `data_fence/fixed_shell_deny_tests.rs`:

- `the_shell_deny_count_is_fixed`: the fixed list is 44 rules, at most 200, and identical across
  1/30 matters, 1/50 conversations, 0/5 runs, a short or long path, and with or without an 8.3
  spelling. All shell denies are identical for a given number of spellings: 236 with one, 428
  with two. A configured folder spelled two ways gets 88 fixed rules, the same at 30/50/5.
- `the_settings_for_the_long_path_stay_small`: under 150 KB with one spelling (98,754 B). With
  two spellings it is reported and kept under 300 KB (190,366 B).
- `each_target_is_denied_in_every_form`: each target is denied for every lead and separator, in
  both shells, quoted or not. This covers the default folder through `%APPDATA%` and its bare
  name, and a configured folder with its 8.3 spelling.
- `what_is_not_a_secret_is_left_to_the_classifier`: no shell rule covers the own run, work and
  notes folders, another matter's notes, the plans folder, tool results or `tools`.
- `a_windows_launch_has_no_history_rules`

Changed:

- `shell_deny_real_tests::a_launch_past_its_budget_sheds_the_variable_forms`: **removed**,
  because shedding is gone. Its `logged`/`Log` helpers went with it.
- `shell_deny_real_tests::the_worst_realistic_launch_fits_the_settings_file`: now measures the
  fixed list against Claude Code's 2 MiB cap instead of `SHED_AT`. The worst launch is now
  219,215 B.
- `shell_deny_real_tests` parse test: the fixed rules are added to the rules it checks.
- `shell_deny_launch_tests::the_canary_launch_with_its_history_fits_its_budget`: fixed rules,
  with the budget set to 256 KB instead of `SHED_AT`. It measures about 213 KB, for two spellings
  of a long Devanagari path.

author: meszmate
body:
roll code's landing check and `roll secrets scan` only matched values roll secrets already stores (by fingerprint). A newly pushed AWS or Stripe key landed silently. This PR catches them by their shape, as GitHub's push protection and GitGuardian do, using roll-auth's shared detectors (`credentials::find_all`).

**On a change** (`secret_leaks.rs`, the same pass as `secret_leak`):
- **What it reads.** Only the change's own added lines since its merge base, so it stays O(change). It keeps the existing limits: no binary files, no files over 1 MiB, no lines over 4 KiB. Each run of added lines is read as one text, so a private key's block counts as one match.
- **Already stored.** Matches go to `SecretEnv::leaks` with the other candidates. One roll secrets holds stays a `secret_leak`.
- **Placeholders.** They are dropped by `credentials::placeholder`. With the known prefix set aside, a match is a placeholder if a part (split at `_`/`-`) starts or ends with example, fake, dummy, test, sample, placeholder, redacted or changeme, or if it repeats one character 8 times in a row. Private keys are never treated as placeholders.
- **Allow-list.** `.roll/secrets-allow` comes from the default branch's head and is read with `roll.toml`. It holds path globs (matched with `code_review::glob`, the shared table) and `sha256:` fingerprints. It is applied when findings are shown, so editing it on main takes effect without the change moving.
- **What it reports.** A `secret_unstored` notice by default. With `[secrets] unstored_credentials = "block"` in the default branch's `roll.toml`, it is a blocker. Each one names the kind, `path:line`, the suggested key, the env read for the file's language and `roll secrets scan --store KEY=path:line`. It carries `path`, `line` and `fingerprint` and never the value. At most 200 are kept per change and 20 shown, plus one line counting the rest.
- **Without roll secrets.** It still runs; nothing counts as stored.
- **Bypass.** An admin bypass lands over `secret_unstored` as over `secret_leak`, audited as `secret_unstored_bypass`.

**CLI.** `roll secrets scan` lists unstored matches (`--json`: `{file, line, unstored, kind, fingerprint, suggested_key}`). `.roll/secrets-allow` is read from the working tree's top.
- `--staged` refuses on one unless `--allow-unstored`.
- `--store [KEY=]FILE:LINE` reads the value from the file and sets it as a new key in the folder of `-e`. It refuses a key that already exists and prints the replacement.

**Not built:** a "Store in roll" button on the change page (roll reading the value from the change's blob into the project the repo is trusted for). The notice names the CLI command instead.

Contract: `docs/code/http-api.md` and `apps/dashboard/src/lib/code-api.ts` (`Blocker.path/line/fingerprint`). Docs: docs/secrets.md ("Credentials roll doesn't hold", scan) and docs/code/architecture.md (blockers, `[secrets]`).

**Tests**
- `queue.rs::a_credential_roll_secrets_doesnt_hold_is_a_notice_or_by_roll_toml_a_blocker`: notice, value never shown, placeholder ignored, allow-list by glob and by fingerprint, block mode.
- roll-auth unit tests: the placeholder rule, the allow-list format, suggested names.
- `roll-cli/tests/secrets.rs`: `--staged` refuses; `--store` stores the value and prints the replacement.

Test keys are built from pieces at runtime.

**Gate** (one run, `ROLL_TEST_JOBS=6`): `pnpm test:code` all green (872 Rust tests, typecheck, dashboard and desktop vitest), `cargo test -p roll-secrets`, `cargo test -p roll-cli --test secrets`, clippy `-D warnings`. Two earlier runs at load 70–128 failed on unrelated lease and timing tests (webhooks outbox, roll-cluster suite); the webhooks one passed 3 of 3 alone.


## From the thirty-first security review
- **Medium: `block` mode failed open.** When roll secrets' `leaks()` lookup or reading the diff failed, `prepare_leaks` only logged and stored no facts, so `unstored_findings` found nothing and the change landed. Now:
  - When the stored-value lookup errors, the credentials are still found, and all of them count as unstored, as without roll secrets. The facts are marked for retry, so the next look asks roll secrets again.
  - When the diff (or the merge base) can't be read, the head is marked unread. Under `block`, that's a `secret_unstored` blocker, "couldn't check this change for credentials: try again, or an admin can land it over this". An admin bypass still lands it, audited as before. Under `warn`, nothing is shown.
  - `secret_leak` keeps its behaviour: on a failed lookup it has nothing to report, and it's retried at the next look. The same change doesn't fix it, because a leak needs roll secrets' answer to name the key.
- **Gate** (`ROLL_TEST_JOBS=6`): `pnpm test:code` all green (872 Rust tests, typecheck, dashboard and desktop vitest), clippy `-D warnings` on code-control.
- **Test:** `queue.rs::a_credential_roll_secrets_doesnt_hold_is_a_notice_or_by_roll_toml_a_blocker`. Its block-mode repo now uses a roll secrets whose lookups all fail (`DownSecrets`), and the change still can't be queued. Before the fix, this was the fail-open path. The diff-unreadable path has no test: the store gives no way to make a diff read fail.
- docs/secrets.md ("Blocking") and the test-coverage row say so.

author: k-taro56
body: ## Summary Findings on #272, one round of them, stacked on it as its review asks (the commit is one per cause). Merged into the slice's branch once it is clean. Suggested branch: `fix/50-round4-native-call-results` (base `src/50-window-parameters-platform`, from `395f57ad`; one commit, signed, failing test first). Local branch `claude/r50` in `~/.cache/rs-public/wt/c-r50`. Older code, not a regression of an earlier fix of these rounds (the inputs are taken at `b704223d`, the slice's first commit, and at `395f57ad`). ### `bc4b1bb1` follow what a native call gives back to a Proxy (Codex, `compiler/proxy-origins.ts:396`) - Wrong: `callOrigins` followed a call into a source function's body and answered no origin for any other, so the result of a native call of the global namespaces was taken as holding nothing: `Object.assign({}, { p: new Proxy({}, {}) })`, `Object.freeze(new Proxy({}, {}))`, `Object.seal`, `Object.setPrototypeOf`, `Object.fromEntries([['p', new Proxy({}, {})]])`, `Array.of(…)`, `Array.from([…])` and `Object.create(null, { p: { value: … } })` were all taken, where the spread `{ ...{ p: new Proxy({}, {}) } }` is refused. - Rule now: `nativeResultOrigins` (new `proxy-native-results.ts`) reads each argument of such a call as something its result can hold. For the `Object` functions that give back their target (`assign`, `freeze`, `seal`, `preventExtensions`, `setPrototypeOf`; `assign` of its sources too) the read of the result is the read of the argument (`Object.assign({}, { p: new Proxy({}, {}), q: 1 }).q` stays taken); for any other native the whole argument, which only refuses more; a spread argument is read through its elements. A native that answers a scalar stays named apart (`SCALARS`), a call of a source function is still followed into its body, and a method of a value that is no global (`items.concat(…)`, `items.map(…)`) is not followed. - New suite `compiler-proxy-native-results.test.ts`: 21 rows, 15 fail before (six pins pass before and after: other-key read, plain `assign`/`freeze`/`keys`, `Math.max`, `String(new Proxy(...))`). Local checks: all 40 suites named `compiler-platform-*`, `compiler-proxy-*`, `compiler-settled-*`, `compiler-timed-*`, `compiler-shared-proxy-parameters`, `compiler-parameter-*` or `compiler-global-*` (640 rows) pass; `oxfmt`, `oxlint` (with and without `--type-aware`) and ESLint pass on the changed files; the package type check shows only the expected TS2307; `node tools/vocabulary/src/main.ts` finds 0 terms. No test of `origin/src/51…57` writes a `Proxy` into a call of `Object.*`, `Array.*` or `Reflect.*` that `unsettledIn` reads (the `Proxy` rows there are the error-frame suites of the framed modules). ## Standing decisions (findings not changed) The other thread of the same review (Codex `compiler/timed-events.ts:361`) is answered in the Standing decisions of #272. ## Checks - oxfmt, oxlint (with and without `--type-aware`) and ESLint pass on the changed files, and so does `pnpm check:vocabulary`. The package type-checks, but for the one expected TS2307 (until slice 51). - The 40 suites of the modules this branch changes (the new one included) pass whole (640 rows). --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the compiler so the result of a call to a native function of the global namespaces is analyzed as holding what its arguments may hold. Previously `Object.assign({}, { p: new Proxy({}, {}) })`, `Object.freeze`, `Object.seal`, `Object.setPrototypeOf`, `Object.fromEntries`, `Object.create`, `Array.of`, and `Array.from` were allowed to hold a `Proxy`, while the spread form `{ ...{ p: new Proxy({}, {}) } }` was refused. - Natives that give back their target (`assign`, `freeze`, `seal`, `preventExtensions`, `setPrototypeOf`) read the result as their argument; any other native keeps the whole argument, which only refuses more. - Adds `compiler-proxy-native-results.test.ts` with 21 rows, 15 of which fail without this change; calls of source functions still follow into the body, and methods of non-global values are not followed. Written for commit bc4b1bb1824093d896a10f2fa0015e051a4a8891. Summary will update on new commits.

author: iusetabs
body:
## Summary
Hi, thanks for the tool! While reviewing it I found a few low-severity issues in the local server and fixed them. Each is a small, self-contained commit:

1. **Local server auth**: the server generates a per-run secret. The start URL carries it as `?k=<secret>`, which sets an HttpOnly cookie and redirects to `/`. `/api/*`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/status`, `/local/calendar.json` and all state-changing requests return 401 without the cookie.
2. **GET header check**: `GET /api/*` now also requires the `X-Open-Seats: 1` header, as other requests already did.
3. **Proxy path allow-list**: proxied paths are normalised and checked against an allow-list, so `..` or encoded segments can't reach other upstream endpoints.
4. **Sign-out cleanup**: sign-out clears all token and PKCE state.
5. **Complete sign-out**: following the [Events API docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/events/latest/devguide/auth-signing-out.html), sign-out now also ends the AWS Builder ID and brokering browser sessions through `idp.awsevents.com/oidc/logout`, returning to a new `/logout` route. Without this, signing in again completes silently. If the redirect fails, the user is still signed out locally.

## Why
Without these, any local web page or process could call the localhost server and use the signed-in session, and "sign out" left the browser sessions active.

## Testing
`python3 -m unittest` runs the offline tests (`test_proxy_path.py`, `test_local_auth.py`). They are stdlib-only and never contact AWS. I also tested sign-out and sign-in in a browser: after sign out, the next sign-in asks for Builder ID credentials.

## Notes
- No new dependencies. Python 3.9+ is still enough.
- The README has a new "Tests" section and updated sign-out notes.
- Happy to split this into separate PRs if you prefer.

Closes #203.

## What changes

- `src/lib/git/RepoView.svelte`: the graph gets `active`, RepoView's flag for "this tab is the one in view, in the Git module in view".
- `src/lib/git/Graph.svelte`: a hidden tab no longer draws its canvas. When the tab comes back into view, `active` turns true and the draw effect runs again, with the current data, width and theme. A second effect draws again on the canvas's `contextrestored` event, when the browser gives back a canvas it lost (a reset of the graphics card, memory pressure).

## Why

A hidden tab is not laid out (`content-visibility: hidden`, since 2958e5f). The graph drew its lanes once and assumed the canvas kept its pixels. When its tab came back, nothing it depends on had changed, so nothing drew it again. A browser does not promise to keep the pixels of a canvas that is not shown. On Ubuntu (WebKitGTK), the graph came back empty with its rows in place: a canvas that lost its pixels and was not drawn again.

## Checks

- `npm run check` passes.
- Confirmed on Ubuntu, where the bug was seen: with this branch, the graph no longer comes back empty after switching repository tabs.
- The bug did not reproduce on the Linux virtual screen, before or after the change: 26 tab switches by mouse and Ctrl+Tab, light and dark. A copy of the hidden tabs with a canvas, in WebKitGTK and in headless Chromium, did not lose its pixels either. Software rendering there probably keeps them.
- No regression in the release build: lanes, points and bands after 3 tab round trips, after 2 round trips through the SSH module, in a tab scrolled down, and in a tab that was hidden while the theme changed to dark (it comes back in the dark palette).
- Reviewed by `design-reviewer`: compliant. Its one note, that the `contextrestored` handler drew in a hidden tab too, is applied.

author: vincentheimann
body:
Bug 137 (found by story 38's pre-production pass, row P007; the ticket and story 38's `after` are in #32).

**Problem:** a run's `processing` placeholder and its result are two rows stamped to the second, and the queries that picked a post's latest row broke no tie. A failure n8n reports within a second (a refused Anthropic key came back in about 0.4 s on n8n 2.48.5) could lose to its placeholder: the post read Processing for good, Details was disabled after a reload, and the setup dialog gave up after 3 minutes instead of showing the reason.

**Fix:**
- One rule for "the latest row": the highest `id` per post and command, in every reader that picks one — the in-flight state, the latest-result subquery behind the list, tiles and chips, the cron's selection, and Post Reviews' row order (`ORDER BY id DESC`). Ids follow write order; the plugin never back-dates `reviewed_at`.
- The trigger skips its placeholder when the run's result was already stored while WordPress was finishing the trigger after n8n's 2xx.
- No schema change, no migration, no JS change. A refused trigger still writes nothing.

**Verification:** `php -l` clean; all 25 harness files pass (every new row fails on the baseline, checked in a throwaway worktree); `npm run test:unit` 214/214. The plan's manual Local walk (a refused key from Post Reviews and from the setup dialog; same-second rows planted with WP-CLI) runs on this PR's CI Free build next; its result goes into the plan's Implementation Notes.

**Review:** two quick passes and one loopback (the list order first sorted by time, against the plan's own rule). Deferred to `deferred-work.md`: a placeholder whose callback never arrives (no server expiry), and no outcome toast for a result faster than the next list refresh (pre-existing).

**Release:** `docs/release-notes/unreleased.md` re-created with one line; ships as 4.0.5 before story 38's submission.

Plan: `_bmad-output/backlog/bug-a-run-that-fails-within-a-second-shows-processing-forever-plan.md` (status built).

body:
## What

- Pin `version: "1"` on `spec.dataFrom[].extract` for 8 ExternalSecrets under `components/multi-platform-controller/rings/ring-2/kflux-rhel-p01/external-secrets`: `aws-account`, `aws-ssh-key`, `ibm-api-key`, `ibm-ppc64be-ssh-key`, `ibm-ppc64le-ssh-key`, `ibm-ppc64le-ssh-key-wdc06`, `ibm-s390x-ssh-key-regular`, `ibm-s390x-ssh-key-large-builder`.
- Leave two unpinned on purpose: `ibm-s390x-ssh-key` (no such secret at that Vault path) and `sifive08-ssh-key` (different path, absent from the version listing).

Clusters affected: `kflux-rhel-p01`

KFLUXINFRA-5187

## Why

A credential rotation will write new versions to these same Vault paths. Unpinned, ESO serves the newest version on its next 1h refresh, which would hand the 18 IBM Z builders a private key their `authorized_keys` does not have yet. Pinning freezes what ESO serves; removing the pins later is the cutover.

## Validation

- `kubectl kustomize components/multi-platform-controller/rings/ring-2/kflux-rhel-p01/external-secrets` passes: 10 ExternalSecrets, `version` parsed as a string.
- `yamllint` clean on the directory, `git diff --check` clean.
- Every pinned version is `1`, the version ESO serves today, so merging changes no credential.
- Full cluster overlay not built: `kustomize build --enable-helm` needs binaries not installed here. Its only helm input is `host-config-chart`, which this PR does not touch.

## Risk Assessment

**Risk Level:** Low

**What could go wrong:** A pin above the live version fails the sync with `SecretSyncedError`; a pin below it silently serves an older credential. All eight are v1, the version ESO reads now, so neither applies.

**Rollback:** Revert the PR; the field disappears and ESO tracks the latest version again.

**Blast radius:** `kflux-rhel-p01` only — ring-2, `multi-platform-controller` namespace, the 8 ExternalSecrets listed above.

author: saruar-dev
body:
This PR lets LiteLLM users parse PDFs, scans, Office files, spreadsheets and email with Nace Document Intelligence through the OCR endpoint and Python SDK, returning Markdown for each page. Existing Nace users can use the same key and gateway for decisions and document parsing, with per-page spend tracking and cleanup of uploaded documents and parse jobs. I work at nace.ai, and Nace maintains this integration, with mocked tests in CI, an opt-in live test and three pricing entries to update when prices change.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `/v1/ocr` with `nace/parse-*` returns 400 `invalid provider: nace`
- Nace users must parse documents outside the gateway, with no spend tracking

How it solves it:

- New Rust OCR adapter for Nace NDI Parse, under `nace/`
- Models `nace/parse-low`, `nace/parse-medium`, `nace/parse-high` set the effort
- Public https links go to Nace as links
- Other documents upload with a one-time grant, then the file is deleted
- Each Nace job is deleted after the call, which cancels a running job
- Only a successful job with `output.include_images` is kept, for its crop links
- Cost map rows bill each processed page at the effort's price
- Shared OCR handler gets a cleanup hook and passes params on, see Caveats

## User Flow

Before: a developer whose gateway already serves Nace decision models (`nace/drex-*`) cannot parse an invoice PDF through it

1. The proxy admin adds a `nace-parse-low` deployment with `model: nace/parse-low` and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/ocr with `model=nace-parse-low` and `file=@invoice.pdf`
3. The proxy returns 400 `litellm.BadRequestError:  - invalid provider: nace` and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0`

After: the same request returns the parsed pages and is billed per page

1. The proxy admin adds the same `nace-parse-low` deployment and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/ocr with `model=nace-parse-low` and `file=@invoice.pdf`
3. The proxy returns 200 with 3 `pages`, one per PDF page, and `usage_info.pages_processed` 3
4. `x-litellm-response-cost` is `0.0105`, the same as the `cost.total_usd` Nace reports in the native response for the same file
5. A JSON request with a public `https` PDF link works the same way

## Relevant issues

Closes #52518

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. Both legs ran on one machine with the same config, proxy command, Redis setup, client commands and documents. Before ran at the merge base da8c02b9d5ac. After ran on e8a37a854a70 plus an earlier draft of the change in 9e509596, the PR's latest product commit. The draft removed `source` from the response hooks' copy of a job with `Map::remove`, which moves the last key into its place, where 9e509596 keeps the key order. It also had fewer tests and a shorter masking rule in the adapter's `AGENTS.md`. No output below comes from that hook copy, so the outputs would read the same at 9e509596. The first five rows under Focused checks ran on the tree of 9e509596.

Each leg rebuilt the Rust extension from the tree under test first, with this command from the repo root. Here and below `p` is the proof folder and `leg` is `before` or `after`.

```bash
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=<venv> uv sync --python 3.12 --frozen --all-groups --all-extras --reinstall-package litellm > "$p/build-$leg.log" 2>&1
```

The config is a copy of `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` saved as `../test-run/proof-2/dev_config.yaml`. The copy adds two Nace deployments at the top of `model_list` and points `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis` at one Redis on 127.0.0.1:6393. No other line changes.

<details>
<summary>Changes in the dev_config.yaml copy, with the existing `general_settings` and `master_key` lines kept for context</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: nace-parse-low
    litellm_params:
      model: nace/parse-low
      api_key: os.environ/NACE_API_KEY
  - model_name: nace-parse-wrong-key
    litellm_params:
      model: nace/parse-low
      api_key: os.environ/NACE_WRONG_KEY
  # ...the existing dev_config.yaml models...

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6393

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6393
```

</details>

The env vars are `NACE_API_KEY` (a working Nace key), `NACE_WRONG_KEY` (a made-up `nace_sk_` value for case 4), `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. Values are not shown. The leg script started Redis and then the proxy from the repo root with these commands.

```bash
redis-server --port 6393 --save '' --appendonly no > "$p/redis-$leg.log" 2>&1 &
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ../test-run/proof-2/dev_config.yaml \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee "$p/litellm-$leg.log" > /dev/null &
```

In both legs the proxy log shows two `Started server process` lines with different PIDs, each followed by `Application startup complete`. The proxy did not print `"workers" flag is ignored when reloading is enabled`, so the two-worker setup stayed. The log does not say which worker answered each request.

`invoice.pdf` is a synthetic 3-page text PDF (1,315 bytes) with one short block of text per page, an invoice header, a terms page and a delivery note. It holds no real data. The public link is the 1-page `dummy.pdf` test file on w3.org.

Every command in this section is copied from the script or the saved shell command that ran it, with one substitution. Local paths are shortened, so `python` stands for the full path of the virtualenv's interpreter, `uv` for a local wrapper that runs uv 0.10.9 and `<venv>` for the virtualenv's folder. The case script takes `out`, the leg's output folder, as its first argument and sets `PDF_URL=https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf`, and each command saves the response headers and body to files under `$out`. The outputs are those files pasted in full. The only edits are the Nace workspace id, file id, request ids and edge ids, which are replaced with placeholders, and the carriage returns and terminal colour codes, which are dropped.

The SDK case runs this script with the same Python environment as the proxy, with `NACE_API_KEY` and `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` set and no proxy involved.

<details>
<summary>sdk_case.py</summary>

```python
"""Case 6: parse a public PDF link with the Python SDK, no proxy. Reads NACE_API_KEY from the env."""

import json

import litellm

try:
    response = litellm.ocr(
        model="nace/parse-low",
        document={
            "type": "document_url",
            "document_url": "https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf",
        },
    )
except Exception as error:
    print(f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
else:
    print(response.model_dump_json(indent=2))
    print("response_cost:", json.dumps(response.hidden_params.get("response_cost")))
```

author: amrshadid
body:
## What was wrong

A key could still make one change after it was revoked, expired, or lost its grant, if that happened after its request was checked:

- The management calls of `internal/access` (CreateKey, RevokeKey, SetGrant, RemoveGrant) read the key and its role again just before the change, as a separate step. A revocation committed between that read and the change was missed.
- The tenant and settings handlers did not read the key again at all.

Separately, the handler that creates a tenant had to search the audit log to find out whether the registry had recorded the creation's entry.

How it showed: in the new API test, a key revoked by a hook that runs after the check and before the handler. Without the fix the change goes through, for every change of the four services. Output from `TestChangeByKeyThatLapsedAfterCheck` with the master's check and the tenant guard turned off:

```
lapse_test.go:226: SetGrant by a key revoked after the check: code_0 "", want unauthenticated "the request carries no valid key"
lapse_test.go:226: RemoveTenant by a key whose grant was lowered after the check: code_0 "", want permission_denied "the key may not do this"
lapse_test.go:226: UnsetSetting on a tenant by a key expired after the check: code_0 "", want unauthenticated "the request carries no valid key"
... (all 40 combinations of the 10 changes and 4 causes)
```

## What changed

**The master port: the actor travels with the change.**
- Every change of `master.Store` takes a `master.Actor`: one of
  - a key, plus the role it needs on a scope and the time to judge its expiry;
  - `LocalOperator()`;
  - `Server()`.
- Each driver checks a key inside the change's transaction. Changes that can fail with NotFound or Conflict run the check first, so a refused key learns nothing about the object it named. Setting changes run it last.
- On a refusal nothing is written, neither the change nor its audit entry. The error is `Unauthenticated` or `Denied` and carries a `master.Refusal` with the reason.
- `Actor.Judge` is the single statement of the rule. The drivers only do the reads it needs.
- The zero Actor is `Invalid`, so a caller that forgets the actor cannot make an unchecked change.
- A unit test makes sure only `internal/access` names `LocalOperator` and only `internal/registry` and `internal/cli/servecmd` name `Server` (test code and the contract suites excepted).

**How each driver keeps the check true until the commit.**
- SQLite: the write transaction holds the write lock from its `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` until commit.
- Postgres:
  - The key's row is held `FOR SHARE`. RevokeKey, SetGrant and RemoveGrant need `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on that row, so they wait.
  - For a role on a tenant, the tenant's row is also held `FOR KEY SHARE`. RemoveTenant needs that lock, so it waits too.
  - When a key changes keys, both rows are locked `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` in id order (`lockKeys`). Without this, A changing B while B changes A deadlocked; so did A changing itself twice at once. `CrossedKeyChanges`, run with `lockKeys` turned off, shows it: `ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)` in 66 of 80 pairs.
  - `SetTenantState` now locks `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` instead of `FOR UPDATE`. The state is not a key column, and this lock does not wait on a check's key share.
- `CheckActor` runs the same check on its own, for code that has no transaction of the master to put it in.

**The separate re-read is gone.**
- `access` no longer reads the key before a change. The change carries `Decision.Actor(scope, role)`.
- Reads (GetKey, ListKeys, ListGrants, WhoAmI) call `CheckActor` once before reading. That is one query instead of the earlier Key + RolesFor.
- `access.RefusedAtChange` maps a refusal to the check's own answer, the same kind and the same fixed message. It is recorded as refused in the installation's log with reason `"key revoked since the check"` and the like. The API's `failWith` uses it too, so a refused tenant change never writes to the tenant's log.

**The tenant port: what is honest across two databases** (decision written in `internal/tenant/doc.go`).
- A tenant's database holds no keys and shares no transaction with the master. The two may not even be the same database type.
- So a tenant change takes a `tenant.Guard`, which asks the master (`CheckActor`). The store runs it last in its own transaction: after the change and its entry are written, so after any wait for locks, and just before the commit. A Guard that refuses undoes both.
- **The window that remains, stated plainly:** a revocation that commits in the master between the Guard's read and the tenant's commit (one tenant commit) is not seen by that one change.
- Closing that window would take one of:
  - the master holding the key's row while another database commits. On a SQLite master that blocks every installation write for that time.
  - a commit protocol spanning two databases of different types.

  Neither is worth it for a window of one commit.

**Registry.**
- `Registry.Create` takes the actor and returns `(tenant, recorded, err)`. The handler records the request itself exactly when `recorded` is false. `core.written`, which searched the audit log, is removed.
- A creation is checked when its row is written. The writes that settle it are the server's own, as after a crash, so revoking the key while the database opens never leaves half a tenant.
- `Remove` takes the actor.

The API contract (`api/proto`) does not change.

## Tests and what they showed with the fix reverted

Reverting means making the drivers' `checkActor` return nil, and for tenants also disabling the Guard. Each case below failed that way and passes with the fix.

| Case | Test | With the fix reverted (SQLite and Postgres 18) |
|---|---|---|
| revoked, expired, grant removed, grant lowered, key gone, between the check and each of the 9 changes | `mastertest` `ActorChecked` | all 45 combinations fail on both drivers: `no error, want unauthenticated`, `the refused change was made`, `the refused change wrote its audit entry` |
| a refusal comes before NotFound | `ActorChecked` | `RemoveTenant of no tenant by a revoked key: kind not found, want unauthenticated` |
| role on a tenant inside a change; the grant goes when its tenant is removed | `ActorOnTenant` | `no error, want denied` |
| a change racing its key's revocation (60 rounds; 30 across two instances) | `ActorRevokeRace`, `ActorRevokeRaceAcrossInstances` | `a change begun after its key's revocation returned was made`; `the change's entry is dated ..., not before the revocation committed` (60 of 60 rounds made). With the fix, SQLite: 20 made first / 40 refused; Postgres: 8 / 52. Every made change is dated before the revocation committed |
| crossed key changes do not deadlock (Postgres) | `CrossedKeyChanges` | with `lockKeys` off: `deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)` |
| the local operator and the server are never refused | `ActorChecked`, `CheckActor` | (pass in both) |
| CheckActor answers, the expiry boundary, invalid actors | `CheckActor` | unaffected by the in-transaction revert, by design |
| a Guard that refuses writes nothing, is run once, with the change's context, before the commit | `tenanttest` `Guards` | `no error, want unauthenticated`, `its audit entry was written` |
| every API change, 4 causes, answer text and kind, refused entry in the installation's log, none in the tenant's | `TestChangeByKeyThatLapsedAfterCheck` | all 40 combinations fail |
| a change makes no store read before itself; a read makes one CheckActor | `TestChangeCarriesItsKey` | |
| Create reports its entry; Create and Remove by a revoked key write nothing | `TestCreateReportsItsEntry` | |

## Cost of the change path

Median of 6 runs, Apple M1 Pro, Postgres 18 in colima.

| Benchmark | develop | this branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| sqlite SetSettingByLocalOperator (no check) | 4.87 ms | 5.36 ms |
| sqlite SetSettingByKey (check in the transaction) | — | 5.45 ms |
| postgres SetSettingByLocalOperator | 1.54 m

body:
## Problem

Production users see React Router's developer page with `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: https://www.dshteamwork.com/assets/my-dsh-CLEtwWv1.js`.

A tab opened before a deploy still runs the previous build. When it lazily loads a page, it asks for that build's hashed chunk, which the new binary no longer embeds. The server answered the missing `/assets/…` file with the console's `index.html` (200, `text/html`), the browser refused it as a module, and no route had an `errorElement`.

## Change

- `server/internal/web/web.go`: a file under `/assets/` that the build does not hold is a 404, never the console. Covered in `TestTheConsoleKeepsEveryOtherPath`.
- `apps/web/src/app.tsx`: on `vite:preloadError` the console reloads once to fetch the current build; a second failure within a minute is left to the route. Checked in the built bundle: Vite's preload helper dispatches the event when the `import()` itself fails (`i().catch(c)`).
- Every route sits under a pathless route with an `errorElement`: a reload card in the reader's language (`common.failed` in `en` / `zh-CN`) that still logs the error to the console.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

## Verification

- `pnpm tsc`, `lint:lang`, `lint:docs`, `assets:icons --check`, `lint`, `db:drift`, `test`, `build` and the plugin's e2e all passed in the pre-push hook. Database suites ran on SQLite only locally; CI covers Postgres and MySQL.
- The deploy → stale tab → reload path was not reproduced end to end in a browser.

author: sanchitmehta
body:
## Problem
Alert **Waiting room stalled** (Sev2) fired at 2026-11-18 12:08:30Z. Since 12:01:30Z nobody has been admitted from `waitingroom-standard`: 486 guests are held, and every admission tick gets **HTTP 409 `QUEUE_NOT_CONFIGURED`** from `app-moonshot-dataplatform-api`.

## Cause
- Commit 64200a8 ("Switch admissions to the improved waiting-room queue") changed Data Platform `ADMISSION_QUEUES` from `["waitingroom-standard"]` to `["waitingroom-perf-improved"]`.
- *Deploy data platform* run [44299236835](https://github.com/sanchitmehta/moonshot-concert/actions/runs/44299236835) swapped it into production at 12:00:57–12:02:01Z. The setting is not sticky.
- `data-platform/api/src/http/app.ts` rejects any non-allowlisted queue that has waiting guests.
- Storefront `WAITING_ROOM_POLICY` still joins and drains only `waitingroom-standard`.
- Storefront PR #36, which adds the improved queue, is unmerged. It also expects standard to keep draining.

## Fix
Allow both queues: `ADMISSION_QUEUES = ["waitingroom-standard", "waitingroom-perf-improved"]`. Guests already in the standard line drain, and PR #36 can roll out safely afterwards.

## Temporary mitigation (Data Platform owner, separate from this PR)
Restore `waitingroom-standard` on production. Either swap back staging after confirming its `ADMISSION_QUEUES`, or set the app setting directly. Don't re-run *Deploy data platform* from `main` until this PR merges.

## Rollback
Revert this commit. The only effect is that the allowlist rejects `waitingroom-standard` again.

## Validation
- `terraform plan` should show only `ADMISSION_QUEUES` changing on the data-platform staging slot.
- After the swap, the Storefront `Waiting-room admission` ticks show `admitted > 0` for `waitingroom-standard`, and the 409s stop.

author: hermanhavva
body:
## Decision and behavior

Add a **separate** lifetime allowance of three distinct guest PNG exports, independent of three successful guest AI generations. Downloading and sharing a PNG file use the same export budget; unchanged artwork/pixels are free to repeat after exhaustion. Changing artwork, caption, layout, styling or included frame produces a new export. Copying an existing public meme link does not consume a PNG export. Signed-in users are unrestricted by both guest budgets; saving/favouriting still requires Google.

The operator selected a compact museum-ticket counter near headings rather than a second ribbon line. A blocked download resumes once after explicit Google login; browser-native file sharing asks for another click on return. Existing public Storage PNG URLs are not private or protected from browser tooling. The intermittent first guest bookmark/counter report was not reproducible across five hosted Chrome retries/reloads; this PR does not claim to fix a non-reproduced bug.

The selected design was validated in the real local UI. The **throwaway** three-variant prototype is preserved only on branch [`herman/guest-allowance-ui-prototype`](https://github.com/hacathon-uart/pid-sklom/tree/herman/guest-allowance-ui-prototype), not in this PR. The user chose variant A, placed closer to the content; production UI is rewritten rather than merging the prototype.

## Production rollout — migration verified, enforcement remains off until code is live

The operator applied `data/migrations/0002_guest_exports.sql` once in production. Read-only calls confirmed the prior `operation_remaining` and new `export_remaining` RPCs both work with the existing backend project/service role; both reject the public frontend key (HTTP 401). The migration preserves prior guest counts, accounts, memes, artwork and Storage. Do not rerun `data/schema.sql` or migration 0001.

The final Blueprint declares `GUEST_EXPORT_LIMIT_ENABLED=true`, but infrastructure auto-sync remains **disabled**. The production API runtime does **not** yet have the new flag set, so its default is false: merging and automatically deploying this PR does not enable export enforcement. Wait for checked main code to deploy on both services, then set the backend flag true and deploy once more. Keep the existing guest signing secret and AI/auth flags unchanged. Rollback disables only this flag without dropping migration/data.

## Validation

- 38 backend tests pass, including artwork-aware pixel fingerprints, metadata deduplication, separate quota, failure and cancellation recovery, invalid PNG/size, real-auth ownership.
- Disposable Postgres runs migration 0001 then 0002 and checks 10-way concurrent caps, independent quotas, replay, fencing, failure/expiry and role permissions.
- Real Chrome/real Supabase SDK deterministic acceptance covers 3 AI + 3 PNG, fourth export blocked, repeated export after exhaustion, public-page download and free link sharing, native-share cancellation/gesture retry, explicit OAuth download restoration, bookmark not consuming either budget and late artwork-switch authorization.
- Frontend build/typecheck, Render Blueprint validation, diff whitespace pass. Existing hosted production bookmark smoke showed no reproduction; hosted export acceptance follows flag activation.

body:
## Scope — bounded browser screencast transport contract (additive TeaVM sample)

Adds a source-pinned ten-file slice to the merged `samples/m3-viewport` Java 21 sample. Preserves original TeaVM compiler, codegen APIs, root Gradle settings and the existing Synexia compiler/workbench owners.

### What works
- `RemoteFrameInbox`: portable Java 21/TeaVM-compatible bounded latest-frame delivery, immutable pixels/bytes, session epochs, monotonic revisions, CSS viewport pointer mapping and strict authorization *after a particular frame is displayed*. Stale/unpainted/letterboxed input is refused. Frames are explicitly full-image snapshots; no false CDP dirty-region claim.
- `CdpScreencastCommands`: validated Chromium Page.startScreencast / FrameAck / mouse event command generation. CDP `sessionId` is a wire ACK token, never confused with a local session/revision.
- **JVM-only reference** `CdpFrameJson` + `CdpScreencastHost` remain under `src/test`; WebSocket listener, bounded JSON parser, compressed data admission, PNG/JPEG metadata tests, ACK after receipt rather than after paint, two-entry executor queue and negative control cases. No automatic browser process, network connection or remote input.
- `RemoteFrameInboxProof`, `CdpScreencastHostProof` and `RemoteCdpProofSuite`: headless deterministic, randomized and adversarial checks; wired into a focused Java21 JVM CI job.

### Executed local verification (2026-11-18)
```
javac --release 21 -Xlint:all -Werror ... (all 3 runtime + host + proof Java owners)
java -ea ... RemoteCdpProofSuite
M3_CDP_FRAME_INBOX_PASS assertions=118815
M3_CDP_HOST_PROOF_PASS checks=27
```
The sample `FrameWindow` remains existing and is compiled with these; compiler warnings/errors = 0. GitHub source commit `870f85c7e558bca8f4dcbcc691d8d5685094cb2a` over `master@6413f3054745e18683953837bfa6f8973b0d3ae8`.

### Security / incomplete gates — DRAFT
- CDP debugging is privileged; only a separately authenticated/isolated local or tunnel-secured endpoint is allowed. The test listener never discovers or opens a connection, and TeaVM browser code never receives a raw debugger URL.
- JVM reference adapter is **not** a production network service and does not start Chromium. No Firefox BiDi support or proven live browser-rendering acceptance.
- TeaVM JavaScript and Wasm GC code generation, actual Chrome/Firefox session, native SWT/GTK/Win32/Cocoa painting, retained frame damage, and pixel/IME/a11y parity remain **NOT_RUN**.
- Never forward legacy VNC credentials; keep existing Nebula VNC/RFB owner and Synexia compiler bridges unchanged.
- No third-party donor source copied; sample Apache-2.0.

This PR is reviewable as a portable frame-inbox plus local host-reference seam, not as completed remote-browser integration.

## Description

author: ashley-hunter
body:
Step 7 of the Linux plan, first piece: Linking, ScrollView and Image on the GTK host. Stacked on #1562.

## What it does

**ScrollView** is a `GtkScrolledWindow` filling the view, its content mounted into a document view the size of the content, as macOS mounts it into an NSScrollView's document view.
- The wheel, touchpad, kinetic scrolling and scroll bars are GTK's.
- Each scroll reports `onScroll`, updates the view's state and tells the core's hit test the offset (`ViewTree::setScrollOffset`), as `NGNScrollView.offsetChanged` does.
- `contentOffset` (applied once after the mount gives the content's size and the view's), `scrollTo`, `scrollToEnd`, `showsVertical/HorizontalScrollIndicator`, `scrollbar-width`, `scrollbar-gutter` and `scrollEnabled` (GTK's own controllers on the scrolled window turned off, so the wheel goes on to an outer scroll view).
- Classic scroll bars (`gtk-overlay-scrolling` off) take their width from the content through the core's `scrollers.h` gutter, as legacy scrollers do on macOS.

**Image** reads its source through a new core function, `loadImageSource` (`image-source.h`), which any non-Apple backend can use:
- the source's method, headers and body, as `appkit/image-request.mm` sends them;
- `cache` read as React Native iOS maps it, over an in-memory `ImageCache` in place of the system URL cache (`reload` fetches again, `only-if-cached` fails on a miss); only a GET over http(s) with no body is kept;
- files only inside the file boundary, `data:` read and never kept.

GDK decodes off the UI thread. The picture is drawn where `resizeMode` puts it (`imageContentFit`, a new core mapping onto expo-image's `placeImage`, matching the macOS layer gravity), cut to the view's rounded shape and drawn under its border. It reports load start, load (pixel size), error and load end, and ignores a late answer for a source it no longer shows.

**Linking** opens a url with `GtkUriLauncher`: asynchronous, placed against the front window (its activation token on Wayland), through the OpenURI portal inside a Flatpak or Snap. `canOpenURL` answers true for any scheme in a sandbox, where the portal decides. `openSettings` opens GNOME's or KDE Plasma's settings app.

Also: `ViewData` keeps its widget and its desktop props (`updateDesktopProps` was a no-op), and `GtkSystem` disconnects from the style manager when it goes.

## Verified

- **el9 image, arm64 in Colima:**
  - `ngn_core_tests`: 925/925, with new `loadImageSource` and `imageContentFit` cases.
  - `ngn_gtk_tests`: 36/36, with new image, scroll view and Linking cases read from pixels.
- **Tests bite:** dropping the turn check fails the late-answer test; dropping the gutter removal fails the gutter test; the border test failed before the fix that draws the picture under the border.
- **Screenshots** (canary bundle exported for `linux`, launched by deep link under Xvfb, beside the macOS host), in `~/Desktop/ng-native-linux-map/step7/`:
  - `pr1-canary-photos-{linux,macos}.png`: 12 remote picsum images loaded over libcurl, covering their thumbnails. They match macOS.
  - `pr1-canary-primitives-{linux,macos}.png`: the bundled `require()` asset sized by itself.
  - `pr1-canary-scrolling-{linux,macos}.png`: the scrolling screen inside its scroll view.
- A first try with `append_scaled_texture` streaked large downscaled photos under GSK's cairo renderer, so the plain texture node is used.

## Not here

- Deep links into a running app (`GApplication` `HANDLES_OPEN`) are step 9.
- Image `tintColor` and `blurRadius`, which the macOS host also ignores.
- The Mac Homebrew GTK loop was not built for this PR; the desktop app info lookup is guarded for it, since Homebrew's GLib has no `gdesktopappinfo.h`.

author: bpmore
body:
Part of #123.

The `text_phonetic_pair` fieldtype, its three phonetic Vue partials and the lang keys they read now ship in this add-on, as decided on UAMS-Web/uams-statamic#767. `person_name` renders with the add-on's copies of the partials instead of the host's global components.

## Approach

- **Fieldtype.** `src/Fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPair.php` is the site's `App\Fieldtypes\TextPhoneticPair` with the same settings, defaults, rules and normalization. It reads its labels from `aether-people::fieldtypes.text_phonetic_pair.*`, and the repeated config entries are built by one helper. The add-on's fieldtype discovery registers it under the `text_phonetic_pair` handle.
- **Lang keys.** `lang/en/fieldtypes.php` gains the 23 `text_phonetic_pair.*` keys (19 `config.*`, 4 `field.*`) and the 6 `phonetic_instructions.*` keys the instructions partial reads, which makes 29. The ticket's figure of 19 matches the `config.*` group alone. A host can still override any of them under `lang/vendor/aether-people/`. In `phonetic_instructions.p3_html`, the U+2014 the site's copy uses as punctuation is replaced with parentheses, per this repository's `no-em-dashes` rule.
- **Vue.** `TextPhoneticPairFieldtype.vue` and the partials `TextPhoneticPair.vue`, `PhoneticTextInput.vue` and `PhoneticTextInstructions.vue` are the site's copies. Their lang keys now use the add-on namespace. `cp.js` registers `text_phonetic_pair-fieldtype`. The partials are not registered globally. `PersonNameFieldtype.vue` registers them locally under the names its template already uses (`text-phonetic-pair`, `phonetic-text-instructions-alert`), and Vue resolves a local component before a global one of the same name. `group-fieldtype-shell` and `custom-input` are still the host's globals, as they already were for `person_name`.
- **Public form.** `resources/field-views/forms/fields/text_phonetic_pair.antlers.html` is the site's view, with one deliberate change. The site writes `include_phonetic_instructions ?? true`, and Antlers' `??` treats a literal `false` as missing, so a blueprint could never hide the IPA note. The view now uses `???`, as `person_name.antlers.html` already does. Until the site removes its override, the site keeps its own copy and its behavior.
- **Validation rules.** The `name` and `international_phonetic_alphabet` rules named in `extraRules()` stay with the host, as they do for `person_name`.
- **Alpine engines.** None are named: the view has no Alpine binding, and the partials import only `@statamic/cms/ui`.

## Files

- **add** [`src/Fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPair.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/src/Fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPair.php): the fieldtype.
- **edit** [`lang/en/fieldtypes.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/lang/en/fieldtypes.php): the 29 keys.
- **add** [`resources/js/components/fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPairFieldtype.vue`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/resources/js/components/fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPairFieldtype.vue) and the three files under [`resources/js/components/fieldtypes/partials/`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/tree/123-text-phonetic-pair/resources/js/components/fieldtypes/partials): the editor and the partials.
- **edit** [`resources/js/components/fieldtypes/PersonNameFieldtype.vue`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/resources/js/components/fieldtypes/PersonNameFieldtype.vue) and [`resources/js/cp.js`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/resources/js/cp.js): the local partials and the fieldtype registration.
- **add** [`resources/field-views/forms/fields/text_phonetic_pair.antlers.html`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/resources/field-views/forms/fields/text_phonetic_pair.antlers.html): the public-form view.
- **edit** `resources/dist/build/`: the rebuilt Control Panel bundle.
- **add** [`tests/Integration/Fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPairFieldtypeTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/tests/Integration/Fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPairFieldtypeTest.php), [`tests/Integration/Views/TextPhoneticPairFormViewTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/tests/Integration/Views/TextPhoneticPairFormViewTest.php) and [`tests/Unit/PhoneticPartialsTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/aether-people/blob/123-text-phonetic-pair/tests/Unit/PhoneticPartialsTest.php).

## Verification

All of the following were run on macOS against head `e28ed41`.

- `composer ci`: exit 0. Rector reports no changes, PHPStan reports no errors, and the suite reports 1672 passed (4217 assertions). Vitest: 103 passed.
- Mutation, run with Herd's bundled Xdebug:
  `XDEBUG_MODE=coverage php -d zend_extension=<Herd xdebug-85-arm64.so> vendor/bin/pest --mutate --class='UAMSWeb\Aether\People\Fieldtypes\TextPhoneticPair' tests/Integration/Fieldtypes/TextPhoneticPairFieldtypeTest.php`
  The first run left 1 of 119 mutants untested: removing the non-array guard in `normalizeStored()`. That change is visible only for an `ArrayAccess` value. A case for one was added, and the second run tested all 119, for a score of 100.00%.
- The view test "hides the IPA note when the blueprint turns it off" failed against the site's `??` and passes with `???`.
- `PhoneticPartialsTest` scans `resources/js` for every `__('aether-people::fieldtypes.*')` key and requires each one to exist in the lang file. Before that check it confirms that three known keys were found, so an empty scan cannot pass.
- **Not run:** rendering in a host Control Panel. The site still registers its own `text_phonetic_pair-fieldtype`, its own global partials and its own view override, so which copy a host uses depends on registration order until the site removes its copies.

## Out of scope

- Removing the site's copies (`App\Fieldtypes\TextPhoneticPair`, the Vue components, the view override and the 29 keys under `statamic::fieldtypes`): UAMS-Web/uams-statamic tracks this, after a release carries this change.
- `RoleTitle` and `Isco_08`.

## Test plan

- [x] `text_phonetic_pair` resolves to the add-on class (`TextPhoneticPairFieldtypeTest`, "resolves the text_phonetic_pair handle to the add-on fieldtype").
- [x] It renders on a public form from the add-on view, escaping both submitted values (`TextPhoneticPairFormViewTest`).
- [x] Its labels resolve from `aether-people::fieldtypes`, and a host override of the add-on key replaces them (`TextPhoneticPairFieldtypeTest`).
- [x] `person_name` and `text_phonetic_pair` import the add-on partials, and every key the CP components read exists in the add-on lang file (`PhoneticPartialsTest`).
- [x] Mutation testing on `TextPhoneticPair`: 119 of 119 tested, 100.00%.
- [ ] `text_phonetic_pair` and `person_name` render in a host Control Panel with the add-on's components. Deferred: this needs a host that no longer registers its own copies, so it is not ticked on #123 and this PR does not close it.
- [x] All remote checks green on head `e28ed41`: 38 check runs, every one success or skipped by design (the matrix jobs), including the aggregate `CI`.

author: sjqortal
body:
## Checklist

- [ ] If you changed **decentralized STUN** logic: update **both** `electron/src/stun-bootstrap.ts` and `src/lib/webrtc/stunBootstrap.ts` together, and run `npm test` (includes `stunBootstrap` golden + `electron/src/stun-udp-server.test.ts`).

Not applicable: this PR doesn't touch STUN.

## Description

Screenshots kept from the published ones aren't uploaded again from this PC: Hub reads each picture back from the node by its file name (`1.webp`, `2.webp`, …) and publishes it with its caption. If the app's screenshots were replaced since the form or the app page's editor read them (from another device, say), those names now hold other pictures, so "Change the screenshots" publishes the captions typed here with someone else's pictures. #404 fixed the same gap for the page text; this does it for the screenshots, in the publish form and in the app page's editor (develop's editor has it through the same helper).

It builds on #404, #405 and #425, which are all in develop now; develop is merged in. Beside #405's `hasDrafts()`, the page section's handle gains `noteShots()`, and the form keeps #405's rule for when it counts as saved: screenshots the check leaves out keep it unsaved until they go out.

**The check** (`AppPage/appPageDrafts.ts`)

- A screenshot read from the node remembers the signature of the set it came from. Before the fee, and again right before the screenshots go out (before and after the pictures are read back), Hub asks the node which set it has now.
- Replaced since: the screenshots aren't published, and the message says why. When the node can't say (its search fails, or it lists none although they were read from one), they aren't published either: fail closed, as for the page text.
- Taking all screenshots off, or publishing only new pictures, reads nothing back and needs no check.

**The publish form**

- Before the fee, a replaced set or a node that can't say stops the whole publish: nothing is confirmed or sent, and the error says why. After the confirmation, the app and the page text still go out and the screenshots are left in the form, still unsaved, with #404's warning and Retry. Retry checks again before its own fee.
- When the set was replaced, the screenshots part says so, with **Refresh**: it reads only the screenshots again and leaves the rest of the form as it is. Pictures added in the form stay, after the current ones (over the limit of 5, the last current ones make way for them). Captions changed on the old set have to be made again. Until Refresh is done, the form still holds the old set, so a Publish or Retry meanwhile stops as replaced rather than counting the screenshots as done.
- A form closed while the check runs asks for no fee and publishes nothing.

**The app page's editor**

- The same check before the fee and before the upload. The error has **Refresh**, which does the same as the form's. Publish is off while the check runs, so a double click asks for one fee.
- A check, a Refresh or the fee's lookup that ends after the editor was closed and opened again changes nothing in the new opening (no fee is asked for the closed one).

**After a screenshots publish from Hub**

The node numbers the files of a new set anew, and lists the new set only after the next block. Until now, both places kept the published list as drafts that read their pictures back by the old names, so:

- in the editor, when a later part failed (the icon, say), publishing again sent the screenshots a second time, read back by their old names: other pictures, or with this check a false "replaced";
- a second change in the same page visit read the pictures back by their old names too;
- in the form, when it stays open after its screenshots went out (the page text failed, or input came in during the upload), publishing again did the same.

Now the screenshots just published are held as pictures, under their new file names, and count as published: a retry sends only what's left, a second change sends the right pictures, and a form that published "No screenshots" holds none (a picture added before and set aside by it isn't sent later). The app page shows them from those pictures until it reads the node again.

`docs/app-pages.md` describes the check and what happens after a publish.

**Translations:** 2 strings (`core:app_page.edit.error_shots_changed`, `core:app_page.edit.error_shots_unverified`), in all 12 languages.

**Tests**

- New: `AppPage/appPageDrafts.test.ts` (13: the check passes the current set, refuses a replaced one, refuses when the search fails, when the node lists none, and when a picture doesn't say where it was read from, and asks nothing when no picture is read back; no picture read back from a replaced set, and none returned when the set changed while they were read; the published pictures held under their new names, edits made meanwhile kept on top, pictures taken off left out, and counted as unchanged), `AppPage/AppPageEditorDialog.shotsReplaced.test.tsx` (12: stop before the fee and Refresh; Refresh keeps added pictures; refused after the confirmation; the node can't say, before and after the confirmation; one fee for a double click; a Refresh, the check (no error, no fee) or the fee's lookup ending after a close and reopen; only the icon sent again after it failed behind the screenshots; a second change with the pictures just published).
- Added to: `__tests__/AppPublish.publishing.test.tsx` (+9: stop before the fee, then the current ones published after Refresh; Refresh keeping a picture added in the form; a set taken all off elsewhere loaded by Refresh; no fee when the form closes during the check; the node can't say; replaced after the confirmation, Retry stopping until Refresh, then publishing the current ones; a Retry while Refresh loads stopped, nothing counted as done and the form still unsaved; a second change after the form's own screenshots publish; neither the old ones nor a picture set aside sent after "No screenshots" went out), `__tests__/AppPublishPageExtras.test.tsx` (+2: stop before the fee in words; Retry checks again before its fee).
- Each of the 22 parts of the fix was taken out in turn, and each time at least one of the new tests failed.
- Full suite (`npm test`), with develop merged in: 4,691 passed, 98 skipped. `eslint` and `prettier` are clean on the changed files, and `tsc` reports no new errors.

author: ronaldtse
body:
The `@startgit` kind joins the notation — the next wave of the #455 replacement program (audit: etassia#455 comment).

## What the kind is

PlantUML's `@startgit` body is an ASCII git-log drawing: a `*` marks a commit on its rail, `|` continues a rail, `/` and `\` switch rails, and each commit keeps the name written beside it (the jar's own name rule: drawing characters stripped, up to the first space — ported verbatim from `gitlog/CursorPosition.java`).

## The implementation

- `Diagram::GitLog` keeps every line's rail positions and every commit's rail and drawing line.
- `GitLogLayout` puts one column per rail and one row per drawing line, boxes centred on their rail.
- `GitLogRenderer` draws named rounded boxes with curves down the rails between consecutive commits, matching the jar's box-and-curve structure.
- `git_diagram` joins the declared types; the tagged dispatch now returns a tag/family pair.

## Verification

New spec file (6 examples) covering detection, rail/line reading, the name rule, geometry and rendering; the full notation suite passes 5224 examples with the types-pin example updated for the new type.

body:
Fixes #1.

`vnc.Session` built the websockify URL and the `Origin` header from `urlsplit(api_url).hostname`, which drops the port. So `kasm_look`, `kasm_click`, `kasm_type` etc. always connected to 443, even when `KASM_API_URL` names another port. The API calls themselves respected the port, so only the VNC tools broke, with `websocket handshake failed: HTTP/1.1 302 Moved Temporarily`.

### Change
- `src/kasm_use/vnc.py`: use `.netloc` (`host:port`) instead of `.hostname`. `_WebSocket` already parses the port out of the URL, and the `Origin` header now matches the actual origin. URLs without a port behave exactly as before.
- `tests/test_vnc.py`: an offline test that the websocket URL and Origin keep an explicit port and stay unchanged without one. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: an "Unreleased" entry.

### Verified

author: xmejkal
body:
P892 #1266, part 2: one gate asks for every board touch. `grant.py`, `reach.py` and `live.py` now ask the board question through `KnownBoardService` before they touch a board, as the look and the deploy do since part 1 (PR #1289). A `/dev/tty.<name>` port is judged as its `/dev/cu.<name>` port.

## What changes for a person

- The kept board on USB: no new question. The three scripts run as before.
- Another board on USB: each script stops with `other_board` (exit 2) before any touch and sends to `look.py`.
- No kept board, and the board shows a serial: each stops with `no_known_board` (exit 2) and sends to `look.py`.
- A board that spark cannot tell (no serial, or a serial that its firmware set): each asks on every run, in the terminal or through `--replies`. Nothing is kept.
- A live grant on a board whose USB serial cannot be its MAC is refused from the list alone, before any read.
- After the grant's read, a MAC that is not the kept board's stops the grant before its own yes.
- `reach.py --port` lists the port once before it uses it. `reach.py --json` prints one flat line for an open question only.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Person
    participant Script as grant.py / reach.py / live.py
    participant Finder as PortFinder
    participant Service as KnownBoardService
    participant Store as KnownBoardStore
    participant Board
    Person->>Script: run
    Script->>Finder: list the boards (opens no port)
    Finder-->>Script: the row, a tty. port as its cu. port
    Note over Script: the script's own refusals first (grant: live grant and no MAC serial, the terminal. live: the grant, the pin. reach: --cure-first with no probe)
    Script->>Service: require(project, port, row, replies, replies_file)
    Service->>Store: read the kept board
    alt the same board
        Service-->>Script: go on, no question
        Script->>Board: the touch
    else another board, or no kept board and a serial
        Service-->>Script: BoardQuestionError (other_board / no_known_board)
        Script-->>Person: exit 2, the board is untouched, fix: look.py
    else spark cannot tell
        Service->>Person: the question, in the touch's own words
        alt yes
            Script->>Board: the touch
        else no, or no reply
            Script-->>Person: exit 2, answered_no / needs_reply
        end
    end
    Note over Script,Board: grant only: ComparingBoardReader stops with other_board when the MAC read is not the kept board's, before the grant's yes
```

## The design

- `known_board.py`: three more `Touch` values (`GRANT`, `REACH`, `LIVE`) with five word fields, `KnownBoardService.require`, `BoardQuestionError`, `other_after` beside `differs`, and `ComparingBoardReader`, a Decorator of the board reader.
- `board_look.py`, `board_doctor.py`, `board_start.py`: four compares use `node_name` on both sides. `PortFinder.find_listed` gives reach its listing.
- The three Operations take `--replies`, call `require` and answer a `BoardQuestionError` with `stops.question_result`.

## Existing tests that change

Fixtures only: `GrantCase`, `LiveScriptTest` and `ReachScriptTest` keep the fixture's board for the test's project. `know_the_board` moved to `tests/fakes.py`. `tests/golden_bench.py` keeps the board for `reach` and `live`. `MAY_READ` gains the three touches. No golden file changes.

Assertions that change (the plan's section 5):

- `test_reach.py`: `test_a_given_port_is_used_without_listing` is now `test_a_given_port_is_listed_once_and_then_used`. Old: no `devs` ran, and the port is in `ran[0]`. New: one `devs` ran, and the port is in `ran[1]`.
- `test_reach.py`: `test_cure_first_with_mpremote_not_a_python_package_runs_nothing`. Old: `outside.ran == []`. New: only `devs` ran.
- `test_grant.py`: `test_a_board_whose_serial_is_not_its_mac_gets_a_deploy_grant_but_no_live_one` answers the board question with a yes for its deploy grant.

Four grant tests that the plan did not name (the PO, 2026-11-18, fixtures only, no assertion changes): the two `rm` line tests keep the board in their own store. The two `store_problem` tests reach the store's write after a yes for a board with no serial. A store that cannot be read says "spark keeps no board yet": a line on P898 #1276.

## Where the build left the plan

- `stops.question_result(stopped, script, data=None)` takes the script's name.
- `board_grant.may_be_mac`: six parts joined by colons (the fixtures' MAC holds `xx`, so a hex check refuses it).
- `KEPT_FIRMWARE_WHY` is a template with the touch's verb. The look's and the deploy's text stays byte-equal.
- The grant reads `port or board.device`, the port that the person named.

## Review

- One lens on Sonnet (design craft, the interface for a person and for Claude): 12 findings. The refuter on Fable: all nine claims reproduced (36 runs with no board touch in any stop state), one false doc sentence and five small points.
- Fixed in the PR: the help and the pages hold per state of the board question and per scope, a table from `known_board.state` and `open` to the code and the next command, the paste line chosen by the Finding's code, live's answer fix asks to show the code, two fix templates, live's stop keeps its pin facts.
- A last read on Opus of the fix round found four points, all fixed: a kept record trusts no USB serial also after a board that showed none, reach's help names the three stops whose last stderr line is the fix, the pin facts for an unreadable kept record, and four mutation rows.
- Raised: the core's fix for a missing replies file names a template that these scripts do not write (a line on P913 #1293). A store that cannot be read says "spark keeps no board yet" (a line on P898 #1276).
- Dropped: `may_be_mac("a:b:c:d:e:f")` is true (such a board is asked and read, then refused with no grant). The return value and the parameter names of `require` stay as the plan wrote them.

## Verification

- The pre-push hook on 11d843cb: "story run: Ran 4,542 tests in 252.7 s (66 slow tests skipped; 87 of 123 test files ...) / OK (skipped=74)". The push before it was refused for a stale `docs/guide/map.md`, written again with `tools/map.py --write`.
- `tools/mutate.py --anchors` over all tables (the builder's run): "3628 mutation(s) in 311 table(s): 15 would be refused", the same 15 as on main (P897 #1273). No mutation run (W3): the 22 new rows wait for the sweep.
- `tools/measure.py --rules`: the same output as on main (the builder's run).
- The full run was not run again after the review's fixes. The builder's full run before them said "Ran 5463 tests ... FAILED (failures=4, skipped=2)", and those four are the grant tests that the fixtures above made green.
- Not tested on a real board. The bench check is the PO's.

Rows: `docs/observations/rows/p892-board-questions.md`.

1. **Inline task detail at 1024–1199 px.** On wide tablets the detail is now a column next to the list (the same pane as on desktops, with the resizable divider) instead of a panel that covers the right half of the list. Below 1024 px the sliding panel stays. New `NARROW_TABLET` query in `src/viewport.ts` (768–1023 px), mirrored by a `1024–1199px` media query in `detail.css`.
```text
export.zip
├── manifest.yaml        # format 1, Sode version, install UID, per router: uid, prefix, title, matrix, levels, levelOffset, levelNumbering, namesHash
├── settings.yaml        # by Settings section (the data-section names)
├── routers.yaml         # always included when an item names the router
├── users.yaml           # Role, Rights, profile; pin and len only with includePins
├── presets.yaml  filtersets.yaml  apiclients.yaml (owner user id kept)
├── panels.yaml          # panels, checkpoints by panel id, templates, Checkpoint sets
├── artwork.yaml         # Default artwork, Icon library index
├── browser.yaml         # the values of This browser, posted by the page
├── names/<router uid>.yaml
└── art/{panels/<id>,defaults,icons}/<id>.<png|jpg|gif|svg>
```

```text
POST /api/export   X-Sode-Session: <Administrator token>
  body {categories, pick{category: ids}, sections, includePins, browser}
  -> application/zip (refused when it is over the upload cap)

POST /api/import   X-Sode-Session: <Administrator token>
  cap the upload -> staging directory -> cap entries -> fixed entry names only
  -> read each entry through a size limit -> loader for the format version
  -> remove and list unknown keys -> refuse two routers with one UID
  -> answer importCheck (counts, routers, unknown keys, sameInstall), remove staging
```

References: items write the router prefix. With one router a reference (a mapping with `n`) leaves it out. A filter set's `router` and `hiddenDstsRouter` keep the prefix, because a blank value means "no router" there. The loader puts the UIDs back.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no export route, no format.
  **After:** `go test ./internal/app -run 'TestExport|TestImportRefuses'` passes:
  - `TestExportEveryCategoryReadsBack`: exports every category, reads the zip back through `/api/import` and the loader. The router UID is only in manifest.yaml, routers.yaml and names/.
  - `TestExportPicksItemsAndLeavesPinsOut`, `TestExportRoutesNeedAnAdministrator` (401 with no session, 403 for a Standard user).
  - `TestImportRefusesBadFiles`: newer format ("made by a newer Sode", 422), unknown entry name, `../`, too many entries, entry too large, upload too large, shared router UID in the manifest and in routers.yaml.
  - `TestExportFormat1Fixture`: hand-written `testdata/export-v1/`, with unknown keys listed and dropped.
  - `TestExportSectionsCoverTheConfig`: a new top-level config key must go in a section or in `exportNotSettings`.
- `go test -short ./...`, `go vet`, staticcheck: clean.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way for the file format (format 1 is frozen once files exist); two-way for the code.

**Blast Radius:** additive

Two new routes and new files only; nothing calls them yet. `/api/import` only checks a file; applying is #592.

body:
Refs #269

## Why

Courtney wants the Wave X Wrapped strip finished cleanly before release. #590 made `test_a_page_runs_exactly_one_posts_query` skip every query that names `_pkiw_wrapped_kind`, so the strip lookup stopped being counted at all. A second `Wrapped_Post::latest()` call in the strip render would pass unseen. This test counts the strip lookup again.

## What changed

`tests/phpunit/integration/NoteArchiveTest.php`, one test:

- The skipped queries go into `$strip`. The test asserts exactly one, with `posts_per_page` 1.
- It deletes `pkiw_wrapped_gen` before serving the archive. Creating notes stamps that option, and while it is set `latest()` caches its result in a transient, so a second call reads the transient and runs no query. Without the delete, the doubled call below still passed. With it, every call to `latest()` is a query.

Test only. No plugin code changes.

## Verification

Run with `WP_TESTS_DIR=~/.wp-tests/lib-x-ins` (database `wordpress_test_x_ins`) and `--filter`:

- Test as changed: 1 test, 7 assertions, OK.
- `NoteArchiveTest`, `WrappedCacheTest`, `NoteArchiveTemplateTest`: 36 tests, 291 assertions, OK.
- Mutation, not committed: I added a second `Wrapped_Post::latest( $kind, ... )` call in `Wrapped_Blocks::render_strip`. The test fails with `The Wrapped strip runs exactly one lookup query per page. Failed asserting that actual size 2 matches expected size 1.` I reverted it.
- Before the `delete_option`, the same mutation passed with the new assertions in place (the transient hit above), which is why the delete is in this PR.

Not run: the full PHPUnit suite and the CI matrix. This changes one test body.

Not covered: the test seeds no Wrapped post, so the strip stops at the lookup. With a Wrapped post the render also runs the `Wrapped_Stats` count query (`posts_per_page` 1000) through `wrapped_facts()`. Nothing pins that count.
