author: lombre33
body:
## Quoi

Limite notée dans la PR #90 (graduations de la jauge) : une jauge de 1990 à 2030 affichait « 1,99 k, 2 k, 2,01 k, 2,02 k, 2,03 k », parce que `axis` est toujours compact dès 1 000. Consigne : une valeur qui ressemble à une année, ou une colonne entière sans format, ne doit pas être compactée.

**Règle** (`GristBI.format.plainScale(lo, hi)`, pure) : une ÉCHELLE dont les deux bouts sont des entiers de moins de 5 chiffres s'écrit en toutes lettres (« 1990, 2000, 2010 », « 0, 1000, 2000, 3000 »). La décision porte sur l'échelle entière, jamais sur une valeur isolée : sur un même axe, « 1000 » à côté de « 1,5 k » se lirait comme deux unités. Pas de test « ressemble à une année » : la règle des 5 chiffres couvre les années ET les colonnes entières, sans seuil arbitraire.

- `f.forScale(lo, hi)` -> `{ axis, format }` : entiers sans compact ni séparateur de milliers (une année n'est jamais « 2 010 »), un non-entier garde `axis`, devise / pourcentage / décimales choisies / parenthèses sont conservés.
- Branché sur la jauge (bornes, graduations et valeur lues sur la même échelle) et sur l'histogramme (les bornes de classes forment une échelle).
- Au passage : les libellés de classes d'un histogramme (« 1998 – 2003 ») étaient tronqués à la largeur d'une barre (« 199… ») ; largeur fixée à 84 px, ECharts omet ceux qui se touchent.

Vérifié que `scale: true` n'est utilisé nulle part : les axes de valeurs d'ECharts partent de 0, une échelle 1990-2030 n'y existe pas, donc rien à changer côté axes ECharts.

**Non traité volontairement** : une valeur isolée (carte KPI, infobulle) qui ressemble à une année reste « 2 010 » en Automatique — on ne distingue pas une année d'un compte à partir d'un seul nombre ; le réglage « Format des nombres » de la tuile existe pour ce cas.

## Vérifié

- `node dev-tests/test-data.js` et `node dev-tests/test-audit.js` : verts (nouveaux tests : `plainScale`, `forScale` en fr/en, BigInt, `-0`, devise, pourcentage, décimales choisies, grande échelle inchangée, câblage).
- Rendu réel (`dev-tests/harness.html`, faux Grist, colonne d'années injectée) : jauge 1990-2030, jauge 0-5000, jauge 0-3,3 M (inchangée), histogramme d'années et de montants, en clair, en sombre + anglais, sur l'arbre fusionné avec `main`.
- **Non vérifié** : rendu dans un vrai Grist ou dans GFS.

Documentation : CLAUDE.md (ligne `js/format.js`), HYPOTHESES.md, TEST_PROTOCOL.md (entrée n°49).

author: guyniv
body:
### Why
`timm==0.9.16` has been pinned since the initial commit. Projects that depend on timm 1.x cannot install videoseal alongside it without overriding the pin.

### What
- `pyproject.toml` and `requirements.txt`: `timm==0.9.16` → `timm>=0.9.16`.
- `videoseal/modules/convnext.py` and `wmforger/wmforger/modules/convnext.py`: import `trunc_normal_` and `DropPath` from `timm.layers` instead of `timm.models.layers`, which is deprecated in timm 1.x and emits a `FutureWarning`. `timm.layers` already exists in 0.9.16.

### Behavior change on timm >= 1.0.12
`build_optimizer` looks names up in `timm.optim` before `torch.optim`. From timm 1.0.12, `timm.optim.AdamW` is `torch.optim.AdamW` (timm's own is now `AdamWLegacy`), so the default `AdamW` uses torch's implementation. The update rule is the same: a single step is bit-identical, and over 200 steps weights drift by about 6e-7 from float rounding. Optimizer states saved with timm's `AdamW` load and resume. `Nadam` is no longer in `timm.optim` (it is `NAdam` there and in torch); nothing in the repo uses it.

### Testing
Compared upstream `main` with timm 0.9.16 against this branch with timm 1.0.31 (CPU, torch 2.8):
- All `videoseal` modules import on both; no timm deprecation warnings on this branch.
- `videoseal_1.0` and `pixelseal` (both ConvNeXt detectors): embed and detect outputs on seeded inputs are bit-identical.
- `AdamW` + `CosineLRScheduler` learning-rate schedule over 10 epochs is identical.
- `videoseal/tests`: 7 passed on both.

author: micronizationlab
body:
## Scope

This draft PR extends the Bridge ingress foundation into an owner-controlled Android LAN HTTPS host and a JVM Desktop pairing/credential runtime.

### Android
- Android Keystore P-256 TLS identity with IP SAN, serverAuth EKU, digital-signature key usage and non-CA constraints; SHA-256 leaf pin.
- Owner-started/stopped, non-exported `connectedDevice` foreground service; private IPv4 bind only, persistent notification and Android 13+ notification permission request.
- Bounded TLS 1.2/1.3 HTTPS/1.1 server, fixed routes, strict HTTP framing/Host validation, timeouts, bounded worker pool/body/headers, per-IP and post-auth per-device rate limits.
- `POST /bridge/v1/pairing` verifies and consumes the one-time proof, then places the device into the explicit owner approval queue; requested scopes are not grants.
- `POST /bridge/v1/requests` performs credential/HMAC/scope/replay admission before dispatching only typed local operations.
- Local dispatcher supports project read, conversation read and atomic conversation append; project membership, known-agent conversation IDs, file bounds and symlink/traversal checks are enforced.
- Action approval requests fail closed until the durable owner action-approval queue is connected.
- Owner credential delivery now preserves the original `ticketId` together with the generated `approvalId`.
- The Android approval screen offers only scopes actually requested by the joining device, so the owner's issued grant remains within the request that iOS later validates. The Android owner clipboard bundle exports both identifiers; the outbox lookup joins the delivery to the durable approval record rather than inventing or regenerating identifiers.

### Desktop JVM module
- Parses owner invitation bundles with strict duplicate-rejecting bounded JSON and exact field/type validation.
- Creates one-time pairing proof and posts over hostname-verified, certificate-pinned HTTPS.
- Imports owner-issued credentials into an AES-256-GCM / PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 passphrase vault with atomic writes and owner-only file permissions where supported.
- Scope allowlist, exact bundle schema and certificate constraints are checked; vault-backed signed request transport uses the shared Bridge protocol.
- A terminal-only CLI test harness is packaged by CI for owner-approved LAN pairing and project/conversation operations; secret inputs are hidden. It is not the final Desktop messenger UI.

### CI
- Runs Android unit tests and `:desktop-bridge:test`, builds the Debug APK, packages the Desktop CLI distribution and uploads both artifacts.
- Superseded runs for the same PR ref are cancelled to avoid dependency repository throttling.

## Still required before real-device acceptance
- Physical Android Keystore certificate-signing and TLS handshake tests across supported Android versions.
- Real Android↔iOS and Android↔Desktop LAN pairing and request E2E tests, including bad pin/hostname, expired/reused ticket, denied owner approval, revoked device, invalid HMAC and replay.
- Durable owner action-approval queue and action-bound grants; no external write/financial/destructive dispatch is enabled here.
- Official ChatGPT/MCP integration path to GLAFIRA CORE. The local Android↔Desktop Bridge does not by itself make a private LAN server reachable from ChatGPT cloud; no public endpoint or relay is enabled.
- Certificate rotation with client pin rollover acknowledgement.
- Native Windows Credential Manager/macOS Keychain adapters and a user-facing Desktop UI/installer.
- Follow docs/GLAFIRA_BRIDGE_DEVICE_ACCEPTANCE.md for physical LAN validation; this has not yet been performed.

No merge, release, public endpoint, relay or paid infrastructure is included. Keep this PR Draft until CI and physical-device validation are complete.

author: slin1237
body:
## Description

**Limits:** no case holds a fence: the workspace has no weak-memory harness. None holds a take or a keep inside one naming. No fence orders a partial table's growth for a reader that began before it. Decisions hold tables from before a take until its write's publication, or a publication window's build. Under a world that still holds a row whose id was taken again, the lookup reads the pool without that row.

### Problem
#7029 left three things on its page.

| left by #7029 | here |
|---|---|
| a lookup lost a place of its cap to each id taken again | the lookup is made again without those ids |
| a run's split writes other rows' holdings past the writing lane's fence | a release fence at the split |
| a worker back on its index id inside one naming was named by another row's blocks | a row kept is asked by the count of its id's last take |

### Solution
The index counts its takes, and a pool's tables keep the count they are known whole at. The naming reads that count before its lookup, and asks after it whether the index's count still stands there. While it does, every block read under an id is the row's that the tables name. That one question replaces one ask for every holder named.

Where the count moved, each row the lookup kept is asked whether its id was taken since. The index keeps the count of each id's last take, so a worker back on its own id reads as taken. Where one was, the lookup is made again without the ids taken since, on a stream of its own, four times at most. Past that the naming names no holder.

| what orders the count after a block | where |
|---|---|
| the row's own lane | the take is said under the table's lock before the lane exists. The lane passes a release fence before a batch's blocks reach the chain |
| another row's lane, at a run's split | the chain's own release fence at the split, under the run's lock |
| another row's lane, where a partial table grows | the run's version: the writer steps it at the growth's end, and the reader loads it at its snapshot. A reader that began before the growth is turned back by the snapshot's second read of the version alone: by the letter of the memory model no fence pairs with it |
| the reader | an acquire fence in the naming, between its lookup and its question |
| a membership write that keeps a standing | it stores the tables' count by release, and the naming reads it by acquire before its lookup |

## Changes
| file | what moves |
|---|---|
| `store/index.rs` | `Index` counts its takes and keeps the count each id's last take made, in place of the worker that took it. `Tables` keep the count they are whole at, and a membership write that keeps a standing sets it again. The naming asks its one question after its lookup. `look_again` asks the rows kept whether their ids were taken since, or makes the lookup again, each round on a stream seeded by the one before it. The doc of `Index` says what orders the count after a block |
| `store/index/tests.rs` | four cases more. The two cases of an id taken again stand as written, over a helper of two layers that takes the seed beside the cap |
| `kv_index`: `chain_index.rs` | a release fence at the top of `split_locked`, under the run's lock. On x86-64 it emits no instruction: the chain's 74 functions in the counted executable are the same on both sides. On arm64 it is one barrier a split, for the gateway's use of the chain too |

## Test Plan
- `cargo test -p smg-policy-controller --features controller,kubernetes` passes 2,012 cases over its 29 test binaries.
- `cargo test -p kv-index` passes its 296 cases.
- Clippy over every target, rustdoc and the private docs pass with warnings denied.
- Eleven cuts of the change are each red by a named case.

| a case holds | what |
|---|---|
| the cap past an id taken again | the taker is the deepest of three under a cap of two. Both rows that stand are named: one lookup alone would name one |
| the rows that stand beside an id taken again | a cap of one over three rows at one depth, across 600 seeds: each of the two that stand is named about 300 times. On the first lookup's stream again the lower id is named two times of three |
| a join under a kept world | the count moved and no id of that world was taken since. The decision asks the rows it kept and names that world's rows as before |
| a standing kept through another pool's take | a row joins another pool of the model. This pool's standing is kept, and told whole at the index's new count |
| no case holds | the naming's fence; a second round of the lookup; the tables' count read before the lookup. A cut of each fails nothing: each needs a take or a keep inside one naming |

## Numbers
The one question costs 11 instructions with no holder named and four with one, and takes 145 to 158 away with sixteen.

| instructions a decision through the store | 64 workers | 512 | 1,024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| one holder named, before | 11,076.7 | 11,157.8 | 11,298.5 |
| one holder named, after | 11,080.7 | 11,161.8 | 11,302.5 |
| instructions more | +4.0 | +4.0 | +4.0 |
| sixteen holders named (a prompt every worker holds, cut at the preset's sample), before | 19,457.0 | 21,102.7 | 21,763.2 |
| sixteen holders named, after | 19,298.7 | 20,950.7 | 21,618.4 |
| instructions more | -158.3 | -152.0 | -144.8 |
| no holder, before | 9,778.1 | 9,654.0 | not read |
| no holder, after | 9,788.7 | 9,664.7 | not read |
| instructions more | +10.6 | +10.6 | |
| a publication, instructions more than main | +253.0 | +2,045.0 | not read |

The second table is the publication window's change, alone and with this change over it. There the asks cost 133 to 140 instructions with one holder and 106 to 112 with sixteen, 1.3 % of a decision at most. The compiler computes the rounds' seeds ahead of the asks: 68 of those instructions.

| a decision while one registration's build is owed | 64 workers | 512 |
|---|---|---|
| one holder named, the window alone | 11,169.4 | 11,252.8 |
| one holder named, with this change | 11,302.3 | 11,392.4 |
| instructions more | +133.0 | +139.6 |
| sixteen holders named, the window alone | 19,493.7 | 21,150.3 |
| sixteen holders named, with this change | 19,599.6 | 21,262.5 |
| instructions more | +105.9 | +112.2 |

Both sides are the crate's `store_named` bench built as its gate builds, counted by callgrind over the same calls. Before is main. The second table's two ids are in no tree.

## Release note
A decision on a store publication from before an index id was taken again now fills its cap from the rows that stand. A worker back on its own index id is no longer named by another row's blocks.

body:
## The hole (TESTER 10:40Z, advisor 10:55Z item 1)
On a new chat, the project's document panel showed a file attached in another chat, labelled "Not indexed. Stored, not searchable: Attached to this chat session", with Ask and Delete buttons.

## Route behind the panel, and why it escaped
- The panel's server feeds are `GET /v1/projects/{id}` (first page, `_owned_or_404` → `store.get_project` → `list_documents`) and `GET /v1/projects/{id}/documents` (`list_documents`). Neither binds a session scope, so `_in_scope_clause(None)` drops every session file. **The server never listed it.**
- The leak was in the client. `handleDocumentAdded` (ProjectWorkspace.tsx) put the upload **response** row into the project list. Both the composer (`onAttached`) and the DocumentsPanel upload call it, and both upload with `session_id`. The workspace reloads that list only when the project changes, so the row stayed at the top across every chat switch.

## Fix: one rule
`belongsToProjectList(doc)` (frontend/src/chat/sessionDocuments.js): a row whose `metadata.session_id` names a chat session belongs to that session, not to the project. `handleDocumentAdded` and the project load both apply it. The session strip is refreshed as before. No server change, no names.

## Why the enumeration test missed it
`test_session_scope_enumeration.py` walks the syntax tree of every server function under app/ and scripts/ that **reads** documents or chunks. This row was written into browser state from a **write's** response, so no reader walk can see it.

Closed by two tests:
- `tests/test_document_panel_holds_no_session_file.py`, through the real HTTP routes:
  - A session file is absent from the detail route and the page route.
  - It is present in its own chat's strip and absent from another chat's strip.
  - The upload response carries `metadata.session_id` for a session upload and not for a project upload. That is the field the client rule reads.
  - Two inputs each.
- `sessionDocuments.test.mjs`:
  - The predicate, on session and project rows.
  - A contract that every workspace write adding rows to the project list passes the rule. This test fails on main's ProjectWorkspace.tsx (checked locally).

## Local
- pytest (new file + test_w2_session_documents.py): 29 passed.
- All frontend `*.test.mjs`: 138 pass.
- `tsc -b`: exit 0. eslint: exit 0.
- scan_hardwiring: 0 new. Two-input lint: 0 new.

## Grader 12:50Z / advisor 12:39Z: the two open items (commits 31caf4a, and the test commit after it)

### What each by-id route did before this commit
| route | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `DELETE /documents/{id}` | project owner + "document is in the project". **No session check**: the owner could delete any chat's file from anywhere; the maker who does not own the project could not delete their own file at all | a session file: only its maker, only from its chat (`?session_id=`); else 404. A project document: owner-only, **as before** |
| ask by id (chat `document_ids`, `privileges.raise_if_inaccessible_document_ids`) | another user's session file 404; **the maker's own file was readable from ANY chat** | readable only inside the session scope the chat route already binds (its own chat, its maker); else 404. Routes binding no chat (execute, chain, mcp) reach no session file |
| fetch by id (`/preview`, `/preview/raw`, `/download`) | **anyone who can open the project, from anywhere** | the same rule via `?session_id=`; else 404. A project document needs no chat, as before |

One rule decides all three: `projects.document_in_scope` (the same one that already filters every listing). The client sends the open chat's id with preview, raw and download (`documentPath` in `sessionDocuments.js`, two-input node tests), so a cited session file still previews and downloads in its own chat.

### Tests through the real HTTP routes, two inputs each
- **Second user** on the same (shared) project: the session file is in neither panel route and in neither strip (their own chat, the first user's chat id).
- Delete: no chat, another chat, another user from the file's chat: 404, and the file is still there. From its own chat by its maker: 200 and gone. The maker who does not own the project deletes it; the owner cannot. **Negative:** a project document is deleted by its owner as before (and not by another user).
- Fetch: `/preview` and `/download` from no chat, another chat, another user: 404; from its own chat: 200. `/preview/raw` from its own chat: reached and refused as not a PDF (400); elsewhere 404. A project document: 200 with no chat.
- Ask: `document_ids` naming the session file from another chat: 404; from its own chat: 200.
- The by-id routes are pinned to their `app.routers.projects` handlers.
- Without the server change, 12 of these fail; with it all pass.
- Two existing tests asserted the old "own file from anywhere". They now assert "from its own chat" and its negative: `test_session_scope_guards.py::test_the_callers_own_document_is_not_refused` binds its chat, the new `..._from_another_chat_is_a_404` covers the other side, and `test_w2_produced_session_documents.py` downloads from its chat and gets 404 from none. No test removed.

body:
## Summary

Group 2A, step (b) of the single schema source (#2810): `server/routes/recipes.js`, `recipe-providers.js` and `pantry.js` drop the hand checks whose every refusal the schema of #2826 already makes, and the try/catch blocks that answered an unexpected error with a 500 of their own. The error now reaches the central error handler (`Internal server error.`, log line `Unhandled error: <METHOD> <pattern> -> 500`).

catch-500 removed: **recipes 7** (said `Internal error`), **recipe-providers 7**, **pantry 13** (both already said `Internal server error.`). `POST /recipe-providers/accounts` keeps a catch only around the INSERT: `UNIQUE constraint` stays 409 `recipe_providers_account_exists`, everything else is rethrown. The `LOG-PLUS-500` entries of the three files are gone from `lint-baseline.json` (13 / 8 / 7 -> 0); `tsc-baseline.json` sinks by 4 keys.

| File | Hand check dropped | Schema rule that refuses first |
|---|---|---|
| recipes | `bodyOf()` (4 routes): missing or list body read as `{}` | `requestBody.required: true`, `type: object` |
| recipes | `Ingredients must be a list.`, `null` read as none, non-object entries skipped | `ingredients: { type: array, items: { type: object } }` |
| recipes | `validateServings`: text, truth value, fraction, `""`, outside 1..99, `Servings must be a whole number from 1 to 99.` | `servings: { type: [integer, null], minimum: 1, maximum: 99 }` (Ajv strict: `1e400` is not a number) |
| recipes | to-shopping-list `num(listId, 'Listen-ID')` (required, number) | `required: [listId]`, `type: integer` |
| recipes | `quantities` not a list, entries not text or null | `type: array`, `items: { type: [string, null] }` |
| recipes | ingredient-match `pantryItemId: ''` read as clear, `num(pantryItemId)` | `type: [integer, null]` |
| recipe-providers | `SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS.includes(p) ? p : 'mealie'` (now `?? 'mealie'`) | `provider: { enum: SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS }` |
| recipe-providers | `Base URL must start with http(s)://` | `base_url` pattern `PROVIDER_URL_PATTERN`, `x-reason: recipe_providers_url_invalid` |
| recipe-providers | `External URL must start with http(s)://` (POST and PATCH, helper `externalUrlInvalid`) | `external_url` pattern, `x-reason: recipe_providers_external_url_invalid` |
| pantry | `num(quantity)`, `quantity must not be negative.` | `quantity: { type: number, minimum: 0 }` |
| pantry | `min_quantity`: `''` read as clear, `num()`, `min_quantity must not be negative.` | `min_quantity: { type: [number, null], minimum: 0 }` |
| pantry | reorder `order must be a non-empty array of IDs.` | `required: [order]`, `type: array`, `minItems: 1` |
| pantry | import `Array.isArray(items) ? items : []` (now `?? []`) | `items: { type: array }` |
| pantry | undo `Array.isArray(changes) ? changes : []`, `Number()` and `?.` on entries, the `kind` and integer filters | `required: [changes]`, entries `required: [pantry_item_id, kind]`, `kind` enum, integer/number/boolean types |

The address prefix checks fall on a probe, not by assumption: 1503 values (17 address shapes, each with all 26 whitespace characters before, after and doubled, lengths around 2000, `ſ`, Kelvin sign) against an Ajv built like `validate-request.ts` and the route's own `str()` + `/^https?:\/\//i`. Of the values the schema lets through, none fails the prefix check for `base_url`, nor for `external_url` on POST or PATCH: an address of only whitespace passes the pattern's `\s*$` branch, but `str()` answers `External URL must not be empty.` / `Base URL must not be empty.` before the prefix check, as it did before.

## What stays in the handlers

- Empty or too long **after trimming**, length in **UTF-16** (`str()`): titles, names, notes, URLs, location names. The answers table holds 150 emoji (300 UTF-16 units, 150 code points) passing the schema and refused by the handler.
- `quantities` length in UTF-16 (51 emoji pass the schema's `maxLength: 100`); `ingredientIds` required next to `quantities`, the same length, safe integers (`1e20` is an integer for the schema); 409 `recipes_ingredients_changed`.
- `Ingredient must not be empty.` after `ingredientMatchKey`; image prefix, pattern and signature; path id `0` (`Invalid recipe ID.`, `... must be a positive number.`); `Number(req.params.id)` of the providers.
- Pantry: `normalizePantryUnit` (see Not decided), `idParam` of `location_id`, `Location not found.`, `oneOf(category)` from the table, `date()` (calendar day), the import's location check, `normalizePantryQuantity`, the undo filter for an id below 1 and a `merged` entry without `quantity_added`.
- Providers: private network (literal and resolved), 502 `recipe_providers_connection_failed`, 409 `recipe_providers_account_exists`, `enabled ? 1 : 0` (identical on the booleans the schema lets through).
- The thumbnail proxy's catch: 404 `No thumbnail available.` for a provider 404, 502 `Recipe provider thumbnail proxy failed.` for every other failure, its own database read included.

## Visible change

| Route | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `GET/POST /recipes`, `PUT/DELETE /recipes/{id}`, `GET /recipes/{id}/image`, `POST /recipes/{id}/to-shopping-list`, `PUT /recipes/{id}/ingredient-match` on an unexpected failure | 500 `Internal error` | 500 `Internal server error.` |
| `PUT /recipes/{id}/ingredient-match` with `name: ""` | 400 `Zutat is required.` | 400 `Ingredient is required.` |
| same with `name: "   "` | 400 `Zutat must not be empty.` | 400 `Ingredient must not be empty.` |
| same with a name over 200 UTF-16 units that passes the schema | 400 `Zutat may be at most 200 characters long.` | 400 `Ingredient may be at most 200 characters long.` |

CHANGELOG: `[Unreleased]` / Changed (500 sentence) and Fixed (ingredient label). No existing assert read either old sentence (grep over `test/`, `public/`, `server/`, `docs/`), so no assert changed for them. Every other answer is byte-equal.

## Tests

- New suite `test:recipes-pantry-answers` (`test/test-recipes-pantry-answers.js`, in the chain after `test:small-modules-b-answers`, line in `docs/test-suites.md`): 313 requests to all 29 routes - valid, every handler refusal that stays, every input a dropped check refused (now the schema's 400), not found, gates, conflicts, 415/502 of the thumbnail proxy - with status and whole body. Expectations generated at `95b65acc5` and literal in the file; the three ingredient-match rows stand apart in `CHANGED`. Clock frozen (`mock.timers`), household zone Europe/Berlin, only SQLite's own timestamps masked. Second part: per file a forced database failure answers through the central handler (body and log line), the process answers again; the 409, the connection 502 and the thumbnail 404/502 keep their answers and never reach the central handler.
- `test:validate-recipes-pantry`: since the schema is now their only guard, the `servings` bounds are held to the CHECK of the column (insert min-1, min, max, max+1 in a rolled-back transaction), the undo `kind` enum to the kinds two take-overs answer (`added`, `merged`), and `quantity`/`min_quantity` to minimum 0.
- `test:friendly-error`: the guard "every case is named by a server" read `recipe_providers_url_invalid` and `..._external_url_invalid` from the route file; they stand only in the request schema now (`x-reason`), so the guard reads `server/openapi/paths/recipeproviders.js` too.

## Seen red first

- `test:recipes-pantry-answers` against `95b65acc5` (route files untouched): table green; the three `CHANGED` rows red (`Zutat ...`); the recipes 500 test red at the sentence (`Internal error`); recipe-providers and pantry red at the log line (their own catch answered, the central handler never logged).

author: miguelangel-nubla
body:
A review of ipv6disc together with ipv6ddns. Four commits, each builds and passes tests on its own.

**Fixes**
- Expired addresses now leave the state: before, they stayed forever, so it only grew. An address seen again just as it expires keeps its expiration events.
- A failed multicast discovery (e.g. an interface going away) called `Fatalf` and ended the process. It is now logged.
- The SSDP M-SEARCH had LF line ends, no final empty line, and the listener as its `Host`. It now follows the spec: CRLF and `HOST: [ff02::c]:1900`.
- Neighbor advertisements register their target address, as an answer can come from another address of the host, except from a proxy (no override flag).
- Data races: `Addr.Sources` was appended to while read; plugin stats were written and read without a lock; the found-address callbacks were set after their listeners started.
- A plugin interval of zero or less made the ticker panic. It is now a config error.
- The Mikrotik plugin bounds each poll with a timeout.

**Refactors**
- Shared `stats.Counters` (`atomic.Uint64`, so aligned on 32-bit for all protocols, not only NDP as in #3), and one UDP listener for SSDP and WSD.
- `plugins.Poller` and `plugins.RunSSH`: the linux and freebsd plugins differed only in their command.

**Breaking**
- `Addr.Sources` is a method, `Sources()`.
- `ListenForNDP`/`ListenForICMP`/`ListenForSSDP`/`ListenForWSD` callbacks return whether the sender counts as a host found.
- The per-package `Stats` types are replaced by `stats.Counters`.

ipv6ddns is the only known user: its PR follows.

**Tests** added for the expiry and its race, address collections, NDP message handling, the SSDP message, the UDP listener, the poller and the plugin configs. `go test -race` passes, and builds for linux/arm, 386 and windows.

## 1. Close X over the "High Scores" tab
The live site already serves the #590 fix. The live `styles.css` is last-modified 12:05:44 GMT, served `no-cache, must-revalidate`; `/play` is `no-store`. There is no service worker, and the deploy invalidates `/*`. Fresh WebKit and Chrome against `https://ffm.derschweigert.de/play` in the phone frame render the forest/gold active tab with the X clear of the tabs. The owner's screen matches the pre-#590 CSS, most likely a tab loaded before the deploy or restored from the back/forward cache. Separately, #590 only reserved a corner with a 44px margin on the tab rows, and the owner asked for a real safe space.

Fix: the close X of the account, login, checkout and status dialogs is now the first row of its card: `position: static`, right-aligned, 44px square, a flex item in the card's column. No content can be laid out under it, however the 5 account tabs wrap or the card scrolls. The tabs use the full width again. The app's help overlay already had its own header row.

Checked with headless Chrome against the real `index.html`/`styles.css` (logged-in mock: Profile and Billing tabs, plus login, checkout and status dialogs) at 390x844, 390x600, 320x568, 844x390 and 1440x900 in the frame. At every size the X sits above every other child of its card, overlaps no tab, and no blue/indigo is left.

## 2. "1 4 = ? 8" in the fiend's speech bubble
The canvas pixel font had no glyph for `/ − ( ) √ ∛ ^` or the superscript/subscript digits, and a missing glyph draws as a space. Campaign II question text is correct ("1/4 = ?/8", "(2/3)⁻² + log₁₀ 100 = ?"), but the bubble dropped the fraction bar, the maths minus, exponents, roots and log bases. Fix:
- The font gains the missing glyphs.
- `−` draws as the hyphen glyph, and `∛` as a raised small 3 before `√`.
- Exponents and log bases draw as smaller raised or lowered digits.
- The bubble is sized from what is drawn (`measurePixelText`).

Campaign I bubbles are unchanged: same glyphs, same width (asserted over all 60 levels). The top question line, answer buttons, level intro, practice and mistake lists render HTML or Unicode text and were not affected.

- `static/game/bubble-glyphs.test.js`, which fails on the old code:
  - every character of all 40 Campaign II levels' questions and reveals (40 seeds each) has a glyph;
  - Campaign I questions and reveals for all 60 levels are drawable and keep their width;
  - fraction bars, minus, super/subscripts and the cube root are covered;
  - the bubble is measured from what is drawn.
- `static/game/dialog-palette.test.js`: each X is the first child of its card in the real `index.html`, and is a static, right-aligned, order -1 flex item; the old tab-margin trick is gone.

author: fiunchinho
body:
## Problem

The release watch reads CircleCI without a token on gazelle. Without a token, CircleCI lists a public project's pipelines, but answers a pipeline's workflow listing `404 Pipeline run not found`. So the watch found each tag pipeline, could not read its workflows, and kept the release in `watching` (159 releases on gazelle today).

The pipeline lookup reads only the 60 newest pipelines of a project. On a busy project the tag pipeline leaves them after some days. The watch then found no pipeline and settled the release `unbuilt`. This gave a false "has no CircleCI pipeline" notice: crossplane-fn-irsa v0.4.0, 11270 minutes after the tag, while its pipeline 1025 was green.

## Change

- Without a token, CircleCI answers a job and a workflow by id. When the workflow listing is refused, the watch follows the target URLs of the tag commit's `ci/circleci:` statuses: an OAuth follow's job URL (read for its workflow) or a GitHub App pipeline's workflow URL. It keeps only the workflows of the tag's own pipeline, by pipeline number. Statuses of a branch pipeline or a candidate tag's pipeline at the same commit change nothing. The workflows then decide the release by the same rules as with a token (`collect.ReadTagPipelineByTargets`).
- The watch never settles a release `unbuilt` when an earlier pass found its tag pipeline. When that pipeline is no longer listed, the watch reads it through the statuses in the same way. If no status leads to it, the release settles `unchecked`, and nobody is told.
- The record keeps the target URLs of a release's tag commit statuses (`HeadStatus.Targets`). Both GraphQL queries that read the tag commit now read `targetUrl`.
- With a token, when the workflow listing works, nothing changes.

After the deploy, the releases that are stuck in `watching` settle on the next passes. A release whose record has no target URLs yet settles after the next inventory read of its repository.

## Tests

- `TestReadReleaseDecidesFromTheTagPipeline`: new cases for a refused workflow listing (built, with a branch pipeline's red job at the same commit left out; red through a GitHub App workflow URL; no status yet keeps watching), and for a pipeline that left the listing (built through the statuses, `unchecked` without them). On the old code these cases fail with the real symptoms: `watching` and `unbuilt`.
- `TestReleaseWatchReadsTheTagPipelineWithoutAToken` (e2e): the GraphQL rollup carries `targetUrl`, the fake CircleCI refuses the workflow listing, and the release settles `built` with no notice. It fails on the old code (`Watching:1 Settled:0`).

## Review

| ID | Severity | Outcome | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | blocking | fixed | Settling from the statuses' states can close a release too early or falsely red, because statuses can come from another pipeline at the same commit. Fixed by the redesign: the watch reads the tag pipeline's own workflows. |
| F2 | blocking | fixed | Paths of the status fallback had no tests. The fallback is gone; the new paths have tests. |
| F3 | non-blocking | fixed | The `unchecked` reason named a missing token when a token was set. The new reason does not name a token. |
| F4 | non-blocking | fixed | A gone pipeline with no statuses: code and spec disagreed. Both now say `unchecked`. |
| R1-1 | important | accepted | Statuses older than the last inventory read: with the exact read, they can only lead to an earlier run of the tag's own workflow. Rare. |
| R1-2 | important | accepted | A status list cut at 40 contexts can miss a workflow. Rare. |
| R2-1 | important | deferred | A later branch pipeline can overwrite every status of one tag workflow, so that workflow is not seen. giantswarm/giantswarm-repo-manager#318 |

`watch_repository` (`internal/tools/watch.go`) has the same refused read; it is item 2 of giantswarm/giantswarm-repo-manager#318.

author: chibenwa
body:
Closes #649

## Problem
Saving a contact `PUT` the whole card with no precondition, so a change saved meanwhile (by a sharee of the book, or by a phone/desktop CardDAV client) was silently overwritten.

## Fix
- `Contact` keeps the `etag` of the card it was read from: the `etag` of the listing item, or the `ETag` header of `fetchContact`.
- `saveContact(userId, bookId, contact, mode)`:
  - update: `If-Match: <etag>`. A contact with no known ETag is still updated without a precondition, as before.
  - create: `If-None-Match: *`.
  - resolves with the ETag of the saved card. esn-sabre answers a JSON `PUT` without `ETag`, so the card is read back once (a failure of that read does not fail the save). Without this, the second edit made without reloading would be unguarded again.
- `updateContact` / `createContact` keep that new ETag in the store. A `412` on update shows the new message `contacts.errors.changedMeanwhile` (7 locales): "This contact was changed by someone else since you opened it. Reload the page to see the changes, then edit it again." The form keeps the user's edits.
- `EditContactPage` saves against the ETag of the version **the form was opened on** (`useOpenedEtag`). Otherwise a realtime refresh (websocket push → `fetchUpdatedContacts`) would put the other user's version in the store, and its ETag would be used, overwriting it silently.
- Move after edit passes the saved contact, with its new ETag. MOVE/COPY keep the card data, and esn-sabre's ETag is `md5(cardData)`, so the ETag stays valid in the destination book.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: documents the precondition handling.

No other code path `PUT`s a card (`saveContact` is the only `api.put`).

## Upgrade / deployment notes
- twake-calendar-side-service must forward `If-Match` / `If-None-Match` to esn-sabre. Its `DavProxy` does on `main`; older versions drop these headers, and saves then behave as before.
- If the side service is served from another origin than the app, it must expose `ETag` (`Access-Control-Expose-Headers: ETag`) so a contact opened directly by URL is guarded. Contacts loaded from listings carry their ETag in the JSON body and are guarded in any case.

## Checks run
- `npm run typecheck`: OK
- `npm run lint`: OK
- `npm run lint:fmt`: OK
- `npm test`: 73 files, 1050 tests passed, including the locale consistency and translation key tests
- New tests: DAO preconditions and ETag read-back (`ContactsDao.test.ts`), the store keeping the ETag plus the 412 message (`ContactsSlice.test.ts`), and the edit page saving against the ETag it was opened on after a refresh (`ContactFormPage.test.tsx`).
- Not run: Playwright e2e.

Fixes the three tool defects filed as #72, #73 and #74, and adds the `[raw]` inbox.

- **#72** `fr amend RID PATH --delete` removes one key (or list element) from the raw record, never from the store's projected `doc`; the ledger line keeps the old value with `"deleted": true`. A top-level field and an absent key are refused.

author: 4phyra
body:
The render walk visited every item on each frame, also the children of items it didn't draw.
Each item's cache entry now holds a subtree rect: the clipped screen rects of the item and all its descendants.
The new `ItemRenderer::skip_subtree()` returns true when that rect misses the dirty region, and `render_item_children()` then skips the item and its children.

On the ESP32-P4 lamp scene, the render walk drops from about 290 to 36 visits and from 12.0 ms to 5.1 ms per frame.

Stacked on #15028.

== Implementation Notes ==

The full dirty walk resets an item's subtree rect to its own rect and grows its ancestors' rects by it.
The walk over the changed items only grows the rects of the items it marks dirty, and of their ancestors, until the next full walk.
A rect may be too big, but never too small.

The rect is a `PackedLogicalRect`, a `u16` `Box2D` rounded outward to whole pixels, so it adds 8 bytes to each cache entry.

## Purpose

Prepare MathOS for an intentional, evidence-scoped software or academic publication decision **without publishing anything yet**.

## Changes

- Add `docs/PUBLICATION_READINESS.md`: maintainers' decision checklist for licensing, citation, code and research reproducibility, claim boundaries, security/provenance, release artifacts, and separate SAT1 manuscript review.

## Audit observations at baseline main 245e94a9

- `LICENSE` already contains Apache License 2.0.
- `v0.1.0` is an unpublished GitHub Release draft describing Experiments 001–022; current main contains substantially more modules, so version and release scope need a human decision.
- Relevant GitHub Actions runs on main reported success on Nov 18 for TOPO-406, EFO integration, R3B, TECT and PEA; those results do not validate a future release commit, complete all other checks or constitute external scientific replication.

round-20261118-142138-9c0p  item 1.1  open, only local  started 18-11-2026 15:21
round-20261118-111023-okmt  item 2.1  closed, merged  started 18-11-2026 12:10, took 3h 00m

history whether a draft pull request is open — the state does not keep the draft. The decision is a pure function,

One pull request.

author: metrologymaven
body:
Implements leaf **TRUST.SIGN.DSSE** as the new crate `fid-sign-core` (layer `model`, no OS or network dependencies, added to the wasm32-wasip1 CI test job).

## What it does

- `pae()`: DSSE v1.0 pre-authentication encoding.
- `Envelope::{from_json, to_json}`: `payload` (base64), `payloadType`, `signatures[{keyid, sig}]`. Parsing is bounded (64 MiB, 1 to 64 signatures, canonical padded standard base64, duplicate members rejected via the `fid-trust-canon` bounded parser); output is RFC 8785 canonical JSON.
- `PublicKey::{from_spki_der, from_pem, ...}`: ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 and Ed25519 only; any other SPKI algorithm or curve (RSA, P-384, ...) is `sig.unsupported_algorithm`.
- `PublicKey::verify_raw`: P-256 requires strict DER (minimal lengths and integers) and low S, else `sig.invalid`; Ed25519 uses `verify_strict` (rejects small-order keys and R, non-canonical S).
- `Fingerprint`: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the SPKI DER; `sign_envelope` sets every `keyid` to it.
- `verify` / `verify_json`: verify over PAE(payloadType, decoded payload) and return the fingerprint.
- `trait Signer { algorithm, public_key, sign_pae }`, `sign_envelope` (verifies each produced signature before accepting it), `p256_signature_to_der` (low-S + DER for keystores that return raw r||s).
- `SoftwareSigner` exists only with the `test-signer` feature (enabled for tests through a self dev-dependency).

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Covered by | Status |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1 PAE vectors byte for byte | `ac1_pae_vectors_match_byte_for_byte` (9 vectors in `fixtures/dsse/vectors/pae.json`), `ac1_pae_worked_example` | covered |
| AC-2 Ed25519 golden byte for byte | `ac2_ed25519_golden_is_byte_exact` (test key `keys/ed25519-test.pem`, `statement.json`, `golden/ed25519.dsse.json`) | covered |
| AC-3 P-256 and Ed25519 goldens verify, fingerprints match `keys/*.fingerprint` | `ac3_goldens_verify_and_report_fingerprints` (also a two-signature envelope) | covered |
| AC-4 RSA gives `sig.unsupported_algorithm`; high-S gives `sig.invalid` | `ac4_rsa_is_unsupported_algorithm`, `ac4_high_s_and_non_canonical_der_are_invalid` (high S, non-minimal INTEGER, long-form length), `ac4_rfc6979_sample_high_s_rejected_low_s_accepted` | covered |
| AC-5 single-bit flips never valid | `ac5_bit_flips_in_decoded_fields_never_verify` (every bit of decoded payload, payloadType, sig) and `ac5_bit_flips_in_envelope_json_never_verify` (every bit of the three JSON string values; each result is `sig.invalid` or `sig.malformed`) | covered |
| REQ-006 limits | `signature_count_limit`, `size_limit`, `invalid_base64_and_structure_are_malformed` | covered |

## Independent test data

All expected values come from `fixtures/dsse/make_fixtures.py` (stdlib-only Python, committed, `--check` mode added to the CI Python step). It has its own PAE, Ed25519 (RFC 8032) and ECDSA P-256 with RFC 6979 nonces, plus DER/PKCS#8/SPKI encoders. It self-checks against RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 1 and 2 and the RFC 6979 A.2.5 P-256 "sample" signature (typed in as hex test data) before writing. I also checked the fixtures locally with OpenSSL: the PKCS#8 keys derive exactly the committed public PEMs, and `openssl dgst -verify` / `pkeyutl -verify` accept the P-256 and Ed25519 golden signatures over the PAE. No expected value was produced by the Rust code.

**Test keys only:** the private keys are the published RFC 8032 TEST 1 seed and the RFC 6979 A.2.5 P-256 key, labelled in `fixtures/dsse/keys/README.md`. The RSA key is a made-up modulus with no private key.

## Deviations and judgement calls (stated openly)

1. **`Sig.keyid` is a `String`, not `Fingerprint`.** DSSE makes `keyid` optional and free-form, so parsed envelopes may carry an empty or foreign keyid. Emitted envelopes always use the fingerprint. `verify` tries signatures whose keyid is empty or equals the key's fingerprint and skips the rest.
2. **Base64 is standard alphabet, padded, canonical only.** The DSSE text allows URL-safe too [unverified]; the build prompt asks for strict base64, so URL-safe input is `sig.malformed`. `TRUST.SIGN.INTEROP` may need to revisit this.
3. **P-256 SPKI must use the uncompressed point**, so each key has exactly one fingerprint; compressed points are `sig.malformed`.
4. **Unknown JSON members are ignored** (top level and in signature objects); only `payload`, `payloadType` and `sig` are authenticated anyway. An envelope with zero signatures is `sig.malformed`.
5. **`SignError`** is an extra type: `Backend` (code `sig.sign_failed`, not in the leaf's error list) for a key handle that fails, and `Rejected(SigError)` when the handle's output does not verify.
6. **AC-1 vectors are generated, not copied** from the DSSE repository (the leaf allows a pinned reference implementation); the reference is the committed Python encoder plus the hand-checked `http://example.com/HelloWorld` example.
7. **Extra public helper** `p256_signature_to_der` for keystore backends (low-S normalisation + DER).
8. Performance budget (1 MiB verify under 5 ms) is not measured here; it stays [unverified].
9. `fid-types` is not used: the fingerprint is bare lowercase hex (REQ-005), not a `sha256:` digest.

## Dependencies added

- `p256 0.14` (RustCrypto, `ecdsa` feature only, no default features; pulls ecdsa 0.17, elliptic-curve 0.14.3, crypto-bigint 0.7.11): P-256 point validation, ECDSA verification, RFC 6979 signing for the test signer. Apache-2.0 OR MIT.
- `ed25519-dalek 2` (dalek-cryptography, no default features; `fast`, `zeroize`): `verify_strict`. BSD-3-Clause.
- `sha2 0.10` (already in the workspace) for fingerprints. Not moved to 0.11: `fid-trust-canon` and a dozen other workspace crates use 0.10, so moving only this crate would not remove the second copy (p256 0.14 brings 0.11); a workspace-wide sha2 move is a separate change.
- `fid-trust-canon` (same layer) for the bounded JSON parser and RFC 8785 serialiser.
- Base64, DER (SPKI, ECDSA signature) and PEM handling are small strict in-crate code so the accepted forms are exact.

## MSRV raised from 1.81 to 1.87 (maintainer decision, 2026-11-18)

p256 0.13 depends on crypto-bigint 0.5, affected by RUSTSEC-2026-0387. The fix (crypto-bigint 0.7.6+) needs p256 0.14 (rust-version 1.85) and crypto-bigint itself needs rust-version 1.87. The maintainer approved raising the MSRV so the advisory is **fixed, with no `deny.toml` ignore**. Changed: workspace `rust-version`, the `msrv` CI job toolchain, the `.cargo/config.toml` comment, `platform/support-matrix.toml` notes, and the repository template (`templates/repo/code/Cargo.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`) for consistency. The decision is also noted in the leaf's Design.

Two workspace clippy allows were added in `Cargo.toml`: `manual_is_multiple_of` and `unnecessary_map_or`. Both are style-only lints that start firing only because the MSRV now permits `is_multiple_of` / `Option::is_none_or`; they would otherwise force edits in unrelated crates (including fid-xtask and fid-outreach). Removing them is tracked as a follow-up.

`Cargo.lock` is regenerated by the lockfile workflow on cargo for the new MSRV, which moves it from lockfile format v3 to v4 (supported by cargo 1.78+).

Other changes: `layers.toml` entry, `built_in: [fid-sign-core]` / `built_pr: 126` on the leaf, regenerated `generated/`, CI: `-p fid-sign-core` in the wasm32 job (also listed in the support matrix notes) and `python fixtures/dsse/make_fixtures.py --check`.

author: ivanmanfre
body:
## Content Desk: a content chat in the Claude place

A separate desk thread for content work. It answers from a preloaded brief (calendar, Review drafts, call lines, beliefs, quotas, recent posts), so most answers need no tool calls. Replies can act through the app's own write paths, with an echo and Undo. Heavy jobs open a T3 Code cloud thread and post the result back.

### What is in here
- `supabase/functions/content-desk/`: edge function (brief, prompt, streaming model call through the Railway proxy, typed actions, proactive trigger tick, T3 queue). `verify_jwt = false` in config.toml; the function checks the user JWT itself.
- `supabase/functions/_shared/desk-t3.ts`: T3 job queue helpers.
- `db/20261118m_content_desk_*.sql`, `db/20261118n_desk_t3_report.sql`: desk tables, flags (`desk_config`, all off), brief functions, locked write functions (`desk_set_date`, `desk_set_photos`, `desk_pull`, `desk_approve`, `desk_keep`, `desk_delete`, `desk_redo_claim`/`release`, `desk_undo_*_v3`, `desk_live_drafts`), trigger claim, the tick cron (inert until armed). Each file has a `_rollback.sql`.
- `src/d/desk/`: the desk UI (stream, composer with voice/photo/link, held actions with server-side commit and Undo, chips), plus one-line entry hooks in the Claude place, Content tab and shell nav.

### Safety
- Writes only through the app's own RPCs, wrapped in desk functions that take the publisher's lock order and check the shown revision, status and date under the lock.
- The target draft is resolved on the server from Ivan's own words (a list number the desk showed, or a phrase that matches exactly one draft); otherwise nothing is done and the matches are shown as chips.
- Every draft write (approve, delete, pull, redo, move, remove date, photo) is held: it runs only when Ivan taps "Do it now" on a card that names the exact draft and, for a move, the exact instant. Move, remove date and photo keep an exact Undo after the tap.
- Every draft action needs Ivan's explicit message; proactive turns are read-only.
- One-flag rollback: `desk_config.desk_enabled = false` (also stops the tick).
- The ops bot (`inbox-bot-tick`, `inbox_threads`/`inbox_turns`) is untouched.

### Tests
- `deno test` in `supabase/functions/content-desk`: 106 pass (incl. a 67-row grammar table).
- `npx vitest run src/d/desk`: 96 pass; shell/claude/content suites green; `npm run build` clean.
- Fixtures and tests use invented data only.

author: pablotasuyuk
body:
## O problema
Em Treinamentos › Novo treinamento, vídeo de ~100 MB dava erro, embora a tela diga "Até 200,0 MB".

Duas causas no cluster próprio:
1. **Teto global do Storage de 50 MB** (`FILE_SIZE_LIMIT: 52428800` em `infra/failover/docker-compose.cluster.yml`) — acima disso o storage responde 413 "The object exceeded the maximum allowed size", não importa o limite do bucket (`treinamentos` = 200 MB, `trn-midia` = 500 MB).
2. **Upload retomável (TUS) quebrado**: o storage-api devolve o endereço dos pedaços como `http://api.grpnascimento.com.br:8000/upload/resumable/<id>` (porta do Kong, sem `/storage/v1`). Todo arquivo > 6 MB enviado por TUS (inclusive na Plataforma de Treinamentos) morria no 2º pedaço.

## O que muda
- `src/lib/uploadRetomavel.ts` (novo): upload simples até 6 MB, TUS em pedaços de 6 MB acima disso, com a base do endereço dos pedaços corrigida e erro em português (tamanho / permissão / queda de rede).
- `TreinamentoEditor.tsx`: vídeo, material e capa usam o helper; barra "x MB de y MB · %" no modal e erro fixo no rodapé (não só no toast).
- `useTreinamentosPlataforma.ts`: `uploadMidia` usa o mesmo helper (corrige o TUS da Plataforma também).
- Infra: `FILE_SIZE_LIMIT` 50 MB → 500 MB. O limite de cada bucket continua valendo (mig 20261103009300 deixa os demais em 10/25 MB).

## ⚠️ Depois do merge
O compose **não** é aplicado pelo CI. Para os 100–200 MB passarem, rodar fora do pico:
```
bash infra/ha/aplicar-pilha.sh            # mostra a diferença
bash infra/ha/aplicar-pilha.sh --aplicar  # recria só o storage, banco2 e depois banco1
```
Até lá, acima de 50 MB a tela mostra o erro claro de tamanho.

## Testado (localhost:8080, logado, contra o cluster)
- 60 MB upload simples → 413 (reproduz o bug).
- TUS sem correção → falha no pedaço 2 (offset 6291456); com correção → 13 MB e 40 MB OK, progresso 11% → 100%.
- 100 MB pela tela → mensagem "O servidor recusou o arquivo por tamanho (limite anunciado: 200 MB)…" no rodapé e no toast.
- Treinamento/arquivos de teste apagados depois.

body:
## Problem and behavior

Refs #36（S12-03，SDK driving adapter／共享应用服务／质量）。过去文档样例和兼容说明容易与实际安装行为脱节。本 PR 从 guide 原字节提取唯一具名 Python 函数，在独立安装的 core wheel 和新 owned roots 下真实调用；README 命令模板绑定受控消费者的实际逻辑参数，并保留 source、hash、argv、输出和持久回执。补齐 SDK 契约回归、分版本支持矩阵和按稳定错误代码排查的自助文档。

文档合同 `7aab69e10c636e76c331d3a02d887abe3af7749e`／ADR0043 已先提交推送，再实现最终候选 `4b5e98d01d62f489dcf56142c8177adfaba6c114`。生产 SDK、领域／应用规则、依赖和工作流不变，保留 SDK v1 五方法／七名称。没有新增验证器、receipt 解析器或执行桥。

## Evidence

四档新 SDK 功能／类型 FULL DATA 审计（core、Ubuntu、macOS、source-wheel）均完成并经 root 复核，制品 ID 分别为 `14439731204`、`14438683145`、`14438963630`、`14438882855`。每档实际 27 次受控功能调用＋4 次类型检查，共 31 次，继续共用原 max32／functional28／typing-reserve4／普通等待30秒／原180秒期限。没有新增研究或 native 槽；直接子调用／期限检查不构成内核进程树或物理回收硬期限认证。

具名 guide 函数、README 逻辑参数、运行时 wheel SDK／py.typed 和源码包字节相互绑定；README 不宣称 verbatim shell execution。同一份已执行的 Python 样例进入既有正向严格类型命令；三份故意错误类型诊断精确核对，负例程序没有执行。安装批次实际覆盖七类 schema／shape 拒绝及两个新增代表性 CLI 拒绝；版本／报告扩展由源码 SDK／CLI 回归覆盖，二者不混称。

每档完整核验 11 个新 Catalog、21 行／manifest、63 个 CAS 引用、6 个 registry roots／8 份 protocol 副本。SQL 仅在无 sidecar 预检后只读 immutable／query_only 打开新 SDK 数据，全部原始载荷前后 hash 不变；三处故意损坏的 raw 副本保留损坏字节及相应拒绝。原 controls／retention／faults 三类实际制品仅逐文件对比 before／after 哈希，未打开旧 DB，不称为 16 份新 DATA 语义审计。

实际 sdist 的 14 项变更与本候选逐字节一致，wheel 全部 166 个生产包文件（165 Python＋py.typed）匹配；载体 API／实际 ZIP 和三个包内校验和通过。所有项目测试、构建、安装、格式、类型及 native 执行均在远端 GitHub Actions CPU 完成。

首候选 c9c497b 的[真实格式失败及取消检查](https://github.com/Darrenus/tickwitness/actions/runs/44330269717)单独保留，不计通过。最终仅按已审阅的 CI 817 字节 patch 修正一处断言排版；原始载体 SHA `4a7352a452d67f703360ed9df1e62dd7d3cb9c6bc29930b1b845fe0563cba4ec` 已核对，localdiff 与 patch 逐字节一致。未使用本机格式器或通过盲目重跑隐藏失败。

author: patel-om
body:
<!-- review:founder-class -->Founder class: control-plane (Control plane); the Founder Proxy (agent) reviews it after key 2.<!-- /review:founder-class -->

Founder classes: control-plane (Control plane: `.github/**`); the Founder Proxy (agent) reviews it after key 2.

M89, live evaluation seat account (gates WF9 and WF17 of `council/records/2026-11-17-g3-whole-flow-cases.md`; WF17 is stated by the second addendum, ip#337): seat code in the live evaluation runs as an account of its own, a reach test proves what it cannot reach before any trial, and the counting re-judge runs in a separate job on a fresh checkout.

Why: in `.github/workflows/live-eval.yml` on main, the trials run model-written code (cocotb test modules, inside `vvp`) as the runner user. That user has passwordless sudo, owns the checkout, the installed package and the records, and its `nirmaan` process holds the plan token in its environment, which any same-user process can read in `/proc/<pid>/environ`. The re-judge then ran in the same job, on the same checkout, after the trials. Nothing checked that the checkout was unchanged, and nothing tested what a credential-holding environment exposed. So seat code could have changed the judge or the records and forged a verdict. W2-L1's 9 cocotb CI trials ran on that path.

What changes:
- **The seat account** (`scripts/live_eval_seat.py`, `.github/actions/live-eval-seat`, new). Every job that runs seat code makes `nirmaan-seat`: a system account with no password, no sudo rule and no group but its own. It then puts a root-owned `vvp` first on `PATH`. That `vvp` runs the real one through `sudo` to a root helper, which runs it with `setpriv` as the seat account. The seat process gets:
  - `no_new_privs`, so no setuid program gives it more (sudo included);
  - an environment that holds only cocotb's own settings (`env -i` plus an allow list; no name that could hold a credential);
  - write access (ACL) to the run's own directory only. That directory must be one the harness made under `/tmp/nirmaan-*`, owned by the runner, reached without links.
  
  When the run ends, or the harness stops it, the helper:
  - kills every seat process;
  - removes any link, pipe or other non-regular file the seat made in the run directory, and gives every other file back to the runner;
  - takes back every grant;
  - removes what the seat left in `/tmp`, `/var/tmp` and `/dev/shm`.
  
  A lock serialises runs, and a recorded grant list lets a crashed run be cleaned up by the next one. No harness code changes: the wrapper sits on `PATH`.
- **Hardening the runner image.** The hosted runner's tool cache (the Python the package is installed in, its `site-packages`, the editable `.pth`, the `nirmaan` console script and cocotb) and `/usr/local/lib/node_modules` (npm) are writable by every account. The first replays' reach tests found both. The action takes write access for other accounts away from those trees and from every folder on `PATH` (sticky folders such as `/tmp` are left alone).
- **The reach test** (`scripts/live_eval_reach.py`, new). It runs in every job that runs seat code, before any trial or re-judge, through the real path: a cocotb module run by `simulator.run`'s cocotb backend (`eda.execute`), so through the same `vvp`. Its six tests:
  - `reach_identity`: it runs as the seat account, not the runner, with no other group;
  - `reach_no_sudo`: `sudo -n true` and `sudo -n -u runner true` fail;
  - `reach_no_write`: it cannot write any of these:
    - the checkout;
    - the installed package (the `nirmaan` package, the Python, `site-packages`, the editable install files, the console script, cocotb);
    - every folder on `PATH` and every program a gate or the harness runs;
    - the seat account's own wrapper and helper;
    - the records folder and `RUNNER_TEMP`;
    - `GITHUB_ENV`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `GITHUB_PATH` and `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`;
  - `reach_no_credential`: two canaries (one under `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, one under a plain name) are absent from its environment and from every `/proc/<pid>/environ`; the harness's environ is unreadable; a runner-only file is unreadable;
  - `reach_no_signal`: it cannot signal the harness;
  - `reach_own_directory`: the control. It can write its own run directory.
  
  A probe counts as denied only on EACCES, EPERM or EROFS. The test fails closed: it fails when it cannot determine a target (the package file, cocotb, a gate program, the wrapped programs, or in Actions the step files) or a target does not exist, rather than shrinking the target list. It passes only when cocotb's verdict is a pass and all six tests are in the results, passed. Otherwise the job stops before any trial.
- **Seat C waits.** `fw.build` and `fw.test` run seat C by path, so the account does not reach them yet. A live trial of a case whose seat is `firmware`, or whose held-out checks use either tool, is refused before any trial (`scripts/live_eval_ci.py`, exit 6; today that is `firmware/axi4-lite-driver`). A replay of it still runs, because its code is the reference answer. The `fw.test` probe lands with that confinement.
- **The tree hash** (`scripts/live_eval_ci.py tree`, new mode). It covers the commit, every file git tracks or would add, and every file under `src/`, `scripts/` and `evals/`, ignored files included, by path, type, mode and content. It is taken before and after the trials. `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` is set, so no bytecode appears. On a change the job fails and prints the diff.
- **The counting re-judge** (new job `rejudge`, `needs: [replay, live-eval]`, no environment, no secret). It ran no seat code before it. In order, it:
  - refuses the records unless the trial job's before and after hashes are equal and it ran `github.sha`;
  - checks out `github.sha` afresh;
  - installs the tools and makes the seat account;
  - downloads the records artifact, the only way they reach it;
  - runs the reach test with the records folder as a target;
  - runs `nirmaan eval rejudge <record> --write` on every record, between two tree hashes of its own checkout;
  - uploads `live-eval-rejudged-<run id>`, the records with their `rejudge.json`.
  
  Re-judging replays the recorded answers through the real gates, so seat code runs again there, as the seat account. Any difference fails the job. The old in-job re-judge step is removed.
- **Replay** now goes through the same account, reach test, tree hashes and `rejudge` job.
- `.github/actions/live-eval-setup`: also installs `acl` (for `setfacl`).
- **Milestone M89** is reserved in `docs/ROADMAP.md`, with `docs/history/M89-live-eval-seat-account.md` and its line in `docs/history/README.md`.
- **WF17, as this PR reads it, for security and the Founder Proxy to confirm.** Re-judging replays the recorded answers through the real gates, so a cocotb case's re-judge always runs seat code. This PR reads "a job that ran no seat code" as "no seat code before the re-judge". The seat code the re-judge itself runs does so as the seat account, after that job's own reach test, between two tree hashes. `docs/LIVE_EVAL_EVIDENCE.md` section 6 says so.

body:
Closes #4963

## Summary

A Resource History record of a command run by `booley flow fpga`, `lint` or
`synth` now has outcome `exit_zero` when the Flow, after reading the command's
output, judged it succeeded, and `exit_nonzero` when it judged it failed. The
raw exit code stays in `returncode`; `timeout`, `oom_kill` and `host_oom_kill`
are unchanged. A command the Flow never judges keeps the raw-exit outcome.

- `src/booley/flows/job_resources.py`: `judged_commands()` holds the records
  of the commands run in its block and writes them when it ends;
  `JudgedCommands.judge` records the Flow's verdict per command (an index with
  no held command is ignored, so judging never raises).
- FPGA: judged from `FpgaMetrics.returncode` (the exit the Flow assigns).
- Lint: judged from `LintConfigResult.error`.
- Synth: `_judge_stage_commands` fails only the command whose own output
  failed the run (Yosys for its own error lines, missing outputs and
  structural checks; otherwise OpenROAD); the other keeps its raw outcome.
- `changelog.d/4963.md`: the user-visible change. `docs/user/CONFIG.md` is
  unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1, AC3, AC6: `test_fpga_impl_record_outcome_follows_route_completion[boardless]`
  (exit 2, route completed: `exit_zero`, `returncode` 2).
- AC2: `[no-route]` (route not completed: `exit_nonzero`).
- AC4: `test_judged_commands_follow_the_judgment_except_for_stops`
  (`timeout`, `oom_kill` kept when judged succeeded).
- AC5 (amended by the maintainer, decision d4963-1 option A): the changelog
  fragment states the user-visible change; the code docstrings state what an
  outcome means; the user docs are unchanged.
- AC7: `test_lint_record_outcome_follows_the_linter_error`
  (`warnings-only`: `exit_zero`; `exit-zero-error`: `exit_nonzero`).
- AC8: `test_synth_record_outcome_follows_the_failing_stage[logical]` and
  `[physical-structural]`.
- AC9: `[physical-yosys-log]` (Yosys `exit_nonzero`, OpenROAD `exit_zero`).

author: re-haiyan
body:
## UI-only refinement of the deployed five-stage DeFaketive panel flow

**Production baseline:** `147eccbfcf206b37550ce9e8b0a71bba626dacc3` (pc7, context-v2). **NOT DEPLOYED.** This is intentionally separate from PR #48 concern-wording changes and PR #50 research intake.

### Why
The live summary displays technical text such as "0 of N matched examples", which may be misunderstood as a poor model score or as failed product safety analysis. Category context is an **informational phrase matching stage**, not a validated second sentiment classifier.

### Improvements
- Replace the always-visible technical summary with an accessible expandable **"How product context was checked"** disclosure beneath the saved Category label, leaving the result and highlights first on mobile.
- Explain clear category phrase matches, **expected behavior (not automatic praise)**, ambiguous text, mismatches from XLM-RoBERTa (not proof of error), unavailable/unclassified contexts, and old saved reports. When there are no exact examples, explain that reviews still receive normal sentiment and hazard analysis.
- Add an explicit **five-stage panel explanation** inside the existing "How was this result reached?" dialog: title-derived category → shared XLM-RoBERTa sentiment → informational category context → independent five concern categories → cautious conclusion.
- Guard the JavaScript aggregation against new/malformed context statuses: unknown codes can no longer be silently treated as `no_signal` and inflate reviewed counts.
- Preserve the existing full DeFaketive disclaimer and historical report recheck messaging. All explanations distinguish review reports from verified safety/authenticity claims.

### Guardrails
- **No backend code, classifier model files, hazard rules, thresholds, version stamps, saved reviews or databases changed.**
- No sentiment override; expected trait **does not** imply Positive and context contradiction **does not** imply XLM-RoBERTa wrong.
- No new model accuracy or F1 claim. This is a clarity/usability improvement only.
- New frontend regression tests cover unknown metadata, hidden vs expanded context, five-stage dialog, and unchanged shopper-verdict/safety text.
- CI checks Node tests, `svelte-check`, production build, and a repo diff guard for all backend, model, research and deployment paths.

### Release gate
After all checks pass, review mobile/desktop report with: saved current context, no explicit phrase matches, expected trait, conflicting context cue, stale saved report, and older report without context. No VM deployment or PR merge until explicitly authorized.

author: milescoviello
body:
### What

`sceUsbdAllocTransfer` returns a host `calloc` allocation and records it with its iso packet capacity. `sceUsbdFreeTransfer` frees it and drops the record. The calls that fill or read a transfer wrote and read its fields through the caller's pointer without looking at that record. A pointer that `sceUsbdAllocTransfer` didn't return, or one already freed, was therefore written as host memory: a stray pointer crashed the host, and a freed one corrupted the host heap.

Changes:
- `sceUsbdFillInterruptTransfer`, `sceUsbdFillBulkTransfer`, `sceUsbdFillIsoTransfer`, `sceUsbdFillControlTransfer`, `sceUsbdControlTransferGetData`, `sceUsbdControlTransferGetSetup`, `sceUsbdSetIsoPacketLengths` and `sceUsbdGetIsoPacketBuffer` check the pointer against the allocated transfers before touching any field.
- An unknown or freed transfer throws "the transfer was not returned by sceUsbdAllocTransfer or was already freed". That follows the existing messages for a device not returned by `sceUsbdGetDeviceList` and a handle not returned by `sceUsbdOpen`. A null transfer still throws "null transfer".
- `sceUsbdFillIsoTransfer` and `sceUsbdSetIsoPacketLengths` already treated an unknown transfer as having no iso packets, so an iso fill of one already threw. The check now runs before the capacity check, in the same locked block.

Allocated transfers behave as before. `sceUsbdSubmitTransfer` and `sceUsbdCancelTransfer` are left alone, since #21530 and #21195 edit them.

### Tested

Windows 11 VM (GeForce GT 1030, WinLibs GCC 16.2.0 POSIX UCRT, Ninja, Release):
- `guest_usbd`'s transfer filler check gains a stack `UsbdTransfer`, a freed transfer and a null one, passed to all eight calls. Each call throws, and the stack transfer's fields stay zero. An allocated transfer is filled normally after the refusals.
- `guest_usbd` passes, 3 runs, on `6d27fa0a3e`, the pre-squash commit with this tree.
- Negative control: `main` with only the new test (`69de86f3d5`) fails `guest_usbd` with `a transfer sceUsbdAllocTransfer did not return was accepted`, 3 of 3 runs.
- `git merge-tree` against `main` is clean, and with #21530 and #21195, which edit both files. #9803 already conflicts with `main` in both files; this branch adds no conflict hunk to either.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` passes on the branch and this body. `tools/debt_fold.py --check` reports nothing for this fragment.

Linux (Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0), GCC 15.2, Ninja, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:
- `guest_usbd` passes, 3 runs, on `09a93376e3` (this PR's head).
- Negative control: the same tree with `main`'s `Export.cpp` fails `guest_usbd` with an abort from `a transfer sceUsbdAllocTransfer did not return was accepted`.

### Checklist
- [x] Based on current `main`; no other open PR implements the same functions
- [x] One topic per PR; follow-ups go in a new PR
- [x] No comments in code except [technical debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md) and the licence notice of code adapted from upstream (see AGENTS.md)
- [x] Unimplemented paths throw (`NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`); silent stubs are listed under Silent stubs in their library's [technical debt](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/tree/main/docs/dev/debt) file
- [x] No notes, investigation `.md` files or images added to the repository (attach them to this PR)
- [x] New third-party code is a submodule built from source
- [x] Generic behaviour, not specific to one title
- [x] Depends on: none
- [x] Fixes: none
- [x] Unblocks: none
- [x] GPUs tested: n/a
- [x] AI-assisted: yes

author: fishbowler
body:
## Why

The `waitForAnimationToEnd` e2e flow fails intermittently on Android, ending the wait while the demo app's animation is still running. Run on its own on a local emulator, it passed 1 in 8 on API 33 and 2 in 8 on API 34, and it failed on every level from 34 to 37 in full-suite runs. CI on API 32 hasn't shown it, but only because its slower emulator hides the race; it stands in the way of moving CI to a newer Android version.

## Approach

`waitForAnimationToEnd` takes two screenshots back to back and treats the screen as settled when they match. The Animation Test screen's countdown and globes change only every 100–125ms, so on a fast emulator both screenshots often land between changes.

The globes and the milliseconds counter are replaced by a block that slides across a track on every frame while the animation runs. Its position comes from the animation controller's time-based value, so a dropped frame still moves it. It is hidden when idle, so the flow's no-animation check still sees a static screen, and it is excluded from semantics, so the view hierarchy is unchanged. The countdown stays, because `extendedWaitUntil.yaml` waits for it to reach `0.0s`. Maestro itself is unchanged.

## Verification

On arm64 emulators configured like CI's (4 cores, 4192 MB, swiftshader, 606×1280), with a fresh demo app build, `commands/waitForAnimationToEnd.yaml` run alone 10 times on each level:

| API | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 33 | 1/8 | 10/10 |
| 34 | 2/8 | 10/10 |
| 36 | — | 10/10 |

`commands/extendedWaitUntil.yaml`, which uses the same screen, passed on each. After removing the globes and counter, both flows were rerun on API 34: 10/10 and a pass. Not run on iOS.

author: kanikabreed
body:
## What it is for

A bot can now use the land tools: subdivide and join parcels, and terraform, as the viewer does. It also reads what a viewer sees of the land: the ground's height from the region's terrain patches, and the parcel overlay (who owns each 4 m cell, and where the property lines are). `ferro-probe` uses this to test a region's land management as the owner, as a visitor, and with messages a viewer never sends. On Tranquillity's develop branch this found two bugs that damage a region.

## References

- **Aurora Viewer** `crates/aurora-net/src/terrain.rs`: the LayerData land patch decoder (`BitReader`, `Tables`, `decode_land_layer`), ported to `crates/client/src/land.rs` (a NOTICE.md row).
- **Aurora Viewer** `crates/aurora-net/src/build.rs` and `session/build_cmds.rs`: `land_action`, `brush_index`, `ModifyLand`, `ParcelDivide` and `ParcelJoin`.
- **Viewer** `LLToolBrushLand` (`modifyLandAtPointGlobal`, `modifyLandInSelectionGlobal`), `LLViewerParcelMgr::subdivideParcel` / `joinParcel`, and `LLViewerParcelOverlay` (the owner bits and the west and south lines).

## What changes

- **Land tools** (`ParcelAction::Divide`, `Join`, `ModifyLand`):
  - ParcelDivide and ParcelJoin of a selection.
  - ModifyLand with the old brush index plus the real size in ModifyBlockExtended. `local_id` is -1, as the viewer sends it, or a parcel to keep the change to.
- **The ground:**
  - LayerData land patches are decoded into `State::terrain`, read with `Client::ground_height`.
  - ParcelOverlay parts go into `State::overlay`.
  - Both are forgotten when the bot leaves the region.
- **Faults:** `Faults::claim_agent` sends ParcelAccessListUpdate naming another agent: a client that lies about who it is.
- **`ferro-probe`** (`--land-at X,Y` places the 32 m square, default 16,16):
  - `land`: the owner divides off a 16 m square and another at the region's east edge, checks the overlay's property lines, and joins both back. It then bans a stranger and lifts the ban, and raises, lowers and reverts the ground, judging each step by the region's own patches.
  - `land-guard`: a visitor tries divide, join, terraform and a ban-list change in the owner's name. Nothing may change.
  - `land-faults`: a divide of no land, which must make no parcel, and a terraform kept to a parcel that does not exist, after which the land tools must keep working. It may leave the region damaged, so it is not in `all`.
- **Test grid:**
  - It records divide, join, ModifyLand, and whom an access list change claims to come from.
  - `send_ground` and `send_overlay` let a test send ground patches and overlay parts.

## Tests

- `check.sh` is green.
- **Test-grid tests:**
  - The land tools are sent as the viewer sends them.
  - Ground patches and the overlay become known.
  - An access list change can claim another agent.
- **Unit tests:** the patch decoder, the overlay, the brush index, and `--land-at`.
- **NGC** (2026-11-18), four local Tranquillity regions on develop:
  - `land` as the owner: every step right.
  - `land-guard` as another account: everything refused. The ban-list change in the owner's name never reaches the land module: OpenSim's LLUDPServer drops a packet whose AgentData is not the circuit's (`Packet.ValidIDs`). The region was checked with a temporary log line.
  - `land-faults`, reproduced twice:
    - A divide of no land leaves a stored parcel with no land.
    - A ModifyLand kept to a parcel that does not exist leaves `TerrainModule`'s lock held. After that nobody can terraform, and new arrivals get no ground patches until the region restarts.

## Limits and follow-up

- The ground is read at the patch's nearest sample, which is enough to judge a change of 0.2 m or more.
- ⬜ lines added to TASKS.md:
  - a terraform kept to a parcel with a selection off the 4 m grid;
  - the region's Block Terraform and Allow Land Join/Divide flags;
  - a single raised point on a patch's last row.

author: quntao-z
body:
## What

The writer's `missing-research-page-coverage` gate refused written bodies that restate their research page's own research sentence.
On profile pages, the two existing arms (frequent terms and headings) are led by the person's name, title, contact, degree, award and citation-list words, which repeat across the page, while the research sentence appears once.

This adds a third, loosen-only arm, `coversResearchPageStatements`.
A body covers the page when it restates one of the page's research statements in at least 4 of that statement's own terms, and it names a term repeated across the page's prose sentences, if any term repeats.
Research statements are prose sentences with a research cue.
The arm reads them without contact, degree and award sentences, and without the lead's name tokens (from `leadPersonName` and an "About <name>" line).

The two existing arms are unchanged, so no body they accept can be refused.
`researchPageHeadings` is unchanged, so no writer input hash or evidence fingerprint moves and every cached v2 derivation stays valid.

## Measurement (offline, no fetch, no model call, no write)

Replay of `research-entity:coverage-synthesis --import-derivations <v2 bodies> --validate-only --evidence-file <v2 capture>` over the 3,778 v2 bodies:

| | beta | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| accepted | 2,765 | 2,806 |
| refused `missing-research-page-coverage` | 72 | 24 |

- 41 of the 72 are now accepted, and 7 move on to the later `refused-by-serving-bar` arm.
- 0 bodies change from accepted to refused, and no other refusal reason moves.
- Precision: each body was paired with another row's research page (2,982 mismatched pairs).
  The new arm alone admits 10 of them, against 724 the two existing arms already admit.
- A read-by-hand sample of the newly accepted bodies restates its page's research sentence, often nearly word for word.

Other variants measured before choosing this one:
- A 3-term floor admitted 59 extra mismatched pairs.
- Dropping the repeated-term condition recovered 58, but admitted a restatement that omits the subject the page repeats, which an existing test pins as uncovering.

## Kind of fix

Writer gate, not serve-time: merging changes nothing a student sees.
The 41 bodies take effect when their v2 derivations are re-imported through the derivation cache and resolved cache-only, with the OpenAI key blank.
That data step is owned by the description tooling, and no model call is needed because the drafts already exist.
Because this loosens a gate, the 41 newly accepted bodies get a blind accuracy grade against their research pages before the re-import.
The graders run inline, and the bar is 0 bodies unsupported by majority.

## Verification

- New tests in `writtenDescriptionChecks.test.ts`:
  - the #6464 synthetic profile page, where the older arms still refuse and the new arm admits;
  - an off-subject body and an award-only body, both still refused;
  - a restatement that omits the repeated subject, still refused;
  - end to end through `coverageSynthesisDecision`.
- Focused suites (`writtenDescriptionChecks`, `writtenDescriptionReadTimeFixes`, `coverageSynthesis*`): 60 pass.
- eslint and prettier are clean on the changed files.
- The full suite runs in CI, because local memory is below the 40% floor.

Refs #6464

author: arithman34
body:
## Summary
- Add `cube/cubies.py`, which reads the 54 stickers into a `CubieCube`: 8 corners and 12 edges, each with a permutation and an orientation, using the standard Kociemba slot order (URF, UFL, … / UR, UF, …).
- Raise `ValueError` from `from_stickers` when a piece has a colour combination that doesn't exist or appears twice.
- Add `permutation_parity`, which counts cycles to decide whether a permutation is even or odd.
- Add `cube/validation.py` with `find_errors` and `is_solvable`. Checks run in this order:
  1. Centers in place (`BAD_CENTERS`)
  2. 9 stickers of each colour (`BAD_COUNTS`)
  3. Every piece real and unique (`INVALID_PIECE`)
  4. Corner twist sum divisible by 3 (`TWISTED_CORNER`)
  5. Edge flip sum even (`FLIPPED_EDGE`)
  6. Corner parity equals edge parity (`SWAPPED_PIECES`)
- Checks 1–3 stop at the first failure. Checks 4–6 are reported together.
