author: shifatmasud
body:
## What was wrong

The Web Slingshot (tap web / RMB / Shift) did two things wrong, and both are visible in the same second of play:

* **The launch fired before the coil could play.** `src/sim.ts` set `sim.spring = 0.4`, `sim.grappleFlight = true` and wrote the **full slingshot velocity on the trigger frame**. Measured 0.13 s after the trigger, the hero was already **9.4 m up at 65 m/s** - the 90 ms coil pose (`src/heroSlingshot.ts`) had barely started and was never seen from the ground.
* **The webs stayed on the anchor for the whole flight.** `src/Scene.tsx` held `tethering = sim.spring > 0 || (grappleFlight && !web && !ground && !wall)`, so the two lines stayed drawn to `sim.anchor` for the entire `grappleFlight`. Measured on `main`: both lines drawn in **13/13 frames** of the move, **5 of them past 0.2 s** with the line end **0.00 m** from the anchor - two webs stretching metres behind a hero who had already flown past the anchor.

## What changed (Option B: true 2-beat pull -> launch, webs released)

* **PULL beat, `src/sim.ts`** (`SLINGSHOT.PULL = 0.12 s`, `PULL_V = 12 m/s`). The trigger no longer launches: the webbing goes taut and the hero is **drawn ~1.4 m along the line** (peak 12 m/s), so the coil has time to read. The ground snap is held off during the pull so the lines, not the street, carry him.
* **LAUNCH beat.** At 0.12 s the full slingshot velocity is written - the **roof arc is re-solved at that moment from where he is then** (it still lands on the roof), and the air-anchor launch keeps the speed he brought in (`springV0`), so the launch power is unchanged. If he is carried through the anchor plane before the pull ends, the launch fires early. `sim.springRel` stamps the release.
* **Release + retract, `src/Scene.tsx`.** The lines hold the anchor through the pull only. At the release they **snap back into the fists over `SLINGSHOT.RETRACT` (0.12 s)** and disappear; the permanent `grappleFlight` hold is gone. The fists come off the line over `AIM_OUT` (0.16 s) so the arms ease out of `aimHandsOnLine` into the flight pose instead of snapping.
* **`src/Ghost.tsx`** draws her two lines on the same two beats (anchor through the pull, released and retracted after it).
* **`src/audio/director.ts`** plays the spring whoosh at the launch beat instead of 120 ms early, during the pull.
* **Constants** live in `SLINGSHOT` (`src/heroSlingshot.ts`): `PULL`, `PULL_V`, `AIM_OUT`, `RETRACT`.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass. `test/web-spring-pose.mjs` is rewritten around the two beats and passes on a `VITE_DBG=1` preview (headless Chromium + SwiftShader, real `grabQ` trigger, frames pinned by the `__ts` hook):

| | main (5974edc) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| pull beat, 0.13 s after the trigger | **9.4 m up, 65 m/s** (already launched) | **1.7 m up, 10.6 m/s** (drawn in) |
| hands on the line during the pull | - | arms 0.4-1.9 deg off the anchor, both sides |
| lines on the anchor during the pull | yes | yes (35.1 m line, end 0.00 m on the anchor) |
| launch | on the trigger frame | **0.121-0.131 s**, 66-73 m/s |
| lines after the release | **13/13 frames drawn, 5 past 0.2 s on the anchor** | **0 frames drawn** after release + 0.14 s retract |
| roof landing | y = 35.2 m | **y = 35.2 m** (unchanged) |

The test asserts: both fists within 10 deg of the anchor and both lines ON the anchor through the pull; pull speed under 20 m/s (no launch velocity before the launch); the release inside 0.09-0.16 s; the catapult only after the pull; and **zero web lines drawn in any frame more than 0.14 s after the release**, plus nothing drawn once the move is over.

A/B sheet (same fixture, camera and frame marks; UI hidden): **`/workspace/downloads/slingshot-release-ab.png`** - pull with the webs anchored -> launch with the lines letting go -> free flight with no webs.

## Not claimed

* SwiftShader runs at well under 10 fps here: this is a look/timing verification, not a performance result; no device run.
* The capture fixture is a downtown street 25 m off a 34 m facade, so the ground pull is in the street's shadow; the webs read as clear lines, the body is small in frame.
* Nothing merged.

author: nicolasbonilla
body:
## What changed and why

A reader-study researcher commenting on the public demonstration pointed out two gaps in how the AI lesion draft is reviewed:

1. An accept/correct/reject log only sees what the model drafted. The lesions a reader **adds** (the model's misses) never appear in it.
2. When the draft is on screen first, independent agreement cannot be told apart from a reader going along with the draft. A small set of cases read **before** seeing the draft is needed to measure that.

Until now the confirmation of an AI review recorded *who* confirmed *which* final mask, and nothing per lesion. The original draft was not even kept: corrections made before the first save overwrote it.

### RC-131 — lesion-by-lesion record (Implements REQ-FUNC-119)
- The in-browser AI draft is kept exactly as the model produced it. It is a write-once object stored at the first save, before the clinician's version is uploaded.
  - The server refuses it unless its marked voxels equal the draft's own record (`annotated_voxels`), and only for the user who saved the draft.
  - The object carries who stored it, when, and its digest.
- At each confirmation of the AI review, the server compares the original with the confirmed mask lesion by lesion (18-connected lesions, RC-030). Each draft lesion is **kept**, **corrected** (outline changed, split or merged) or **removed**, and the reviewer's own lesions are counted as **added**.
- The counts appear in the AI-draft banner (en/es/de) and are reset with the review.
- Every record is also kept as a write-once object, and no names are stored in it.
- **Evidence only:** the record is never a condition of the confirmation. A draft without its original is confirmed with the record stated as not available.

### RC-132 — reading before the AI draft (Implements REQ-FUNC-120)
- **Reader-study set:** a fixed share of images chosen by a keyed hash of the image id (`READER_STUDY_UNAIDED_FRACTION`, **default 0 = off**; `READER_STUDY_KEY`).
- **Order on such an image:** the in-browser AI is offered only after the radiologist records their own saved reading. That reading is write-once and bound to the saved mask, and it is refused once the radiologist has saved an AI draft of the image.
- **At the confirmation** by the same radiologist, every final lesion is related to the reading recorded before the draft was created (server times). Each falls into one of four groups: reader and draft, reader only, adopted from the draft, or added later. The reader's own lesions that were dropped after seeing the draft are listed, along with the Dice of each pair.

### New routes
Each route has object authorization and an audit mapping, both added to the existing route maps.
- `PUT /segmentation/{id}/ai-draft/original`
- `POST /segmentation/{id}/unaided-read`
- `GET /segmentation/reader-study/assignment`

## Traceability
- **Requirements:** REQ-FUNC-119 and REQ-FUNC-120 (SRS Addendum D, SRS 1.20 draft).
- **Risk:** HAZ-001 cause (m), "the reader goes along with the AI draft", with measurement controls RC-131 and RC-132 (RMF 1.23 draft). They make the cause measurable; they do not by themselves reduce it.
- **Manifest:** both controls are marked `unverified`. This is the research stage (owner decision 2026-11-14): CI, one review and the owner's sign-off, with no negative-control campaign.
- **Residual risk (stated in the RMF):**
  - An in-browser run is not seen by the server until its draft is saved, so the viewer enforces the order.
  - If the assignment cannot be read, the AI is offered as before.

## Verification
- Backend: `tests/unit/test_rc131_rc132_lesion_review_record.py` (23 tests). Related suites also pass locally: RC-047, CAPA-009, CAPA-015, PRB-029/030 and the risk-control manifest (882 + 740 passed).
- Frontend:
  - `LesionReviewRecord.test.tsx` (9 tests);
  - `useSegmentationData.flamesDraft.test.tsx` (+2: the original goes first, and a failed original never blocks the save);
  - related suites: 82 passed;
  - `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Tests ran locally in the offline, no-credential environment (PRB-002).

## Independent review and fixes (one review, one fix round: research stage)

The review found no blocker, and found 4 major and 7 minor issues. All 11 were fixed in `0d358f2`, and CI follow-ups in `e889ff7`.

- **RC-132 integrity.** A reading is now refused in three situations:
  - outside the set;
  - while anyone's AI or automatic segmentation of the image is saved;
  - once the caller has ever saved an AI draft of it. A write-once mark records this and survives deletion of the draft.

  When the set cannot be checked, the viewer holds the AI back and offers a retry.
- **Comparison with the reading.** It now works by lesion site: a connected region of reading, draft and final mask together. Lesions are followed through outlines that touch or only partly overlap, merges show as part counts, and draft-only sites are counted as `draft_removed`.
- **Minimum lesion volume.** Lesions now follow the 3 mm³ minimum of the lesion table. The voxel volume comes from the affine already read by the displayed-image check, so the image is not read a second time. Smaller components are counted apart. The draft can no longer be recorded once a version is saved.
- **Who is held back.** Only radiologists. Once shown, the AI card is not withdrawn mid-run.
- **Failures.** "Unreadable" and "not stored" are told apart, and a failed reading comparison never discards the draft comparison. A record that could not be made is recomputed on a repeat confirmation.
- **Who sees the reader data.** Radiologists and administrators only. Listings omit the per-lesion lists, and the banner wording is neutral.
- **Record lifetime.** The record is cleared with the review; its write-once object is written after the confirmation is stored. The draft copy is cleared only after the save succeeds.
- **Server load.** The record is computed off the event loop, and readings are found from small sidecar files.
- **Configuration and docs.**
  - `READER_STUDY_KEY` now defaults to empty: the study set stays off without a key.
  - New `DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md` section.
  - The cause label is now `(m)`, so it no longer clashes with an existing one.
- **CI fixes.**
  - The new route was added to the RC-029 route map.
  - The PRB-003 C1 negative-control anchor is unique again.
  - The PRB-030 R1 anchor was updated to the confirm call, which now also returns the affine. The mutation is unchanged.

## Not changed
- No Class C module from the CLAUDE.md list was modified.
- `edgeAI.worker.ts` and the lesion analysis are untouched; the record reuses `lesion_metrics.label_lesions`.

**PENDING owner approval. Not merged, not deployed.**

body:
## Summary
`tokens::revoke` parsed the stored `oauth_tokens.kind` with `.expect()`, so a hand-edited row would panic the request. It now returns an error instead, and revokes nothing for that row.

## Changes
- `src/store/oauth/tokens.rs`: `revoke` runs in a transaction; an unparseable kind becomes `OkfError::Database` (a `sqlx::Error::ColumnDecode` on column `kind`, the error the driver itself gives for an undecodable column; no new variant). The error drops the transaction, so the `UPDATE ... revoked_at` is rolled back and the row is not partly revoked.
- Test `revoke_answers_an_error_and_revokes_nothing_for_a_corrupt_kind`: drops the CHECK in the throwaway DB, sets `kind = 'bogus'`, asserts `Err(OkfError::Database)` and `revoked_at IS NULL`. It fails (panics at the old `.expect`) when the fix is reverted.
- Changelog entry.

## What the caller sees
`POST /oauth/revoke` calls `revoke` with `?`, so the `OkfError::Database` becomes `OAuthError::Server`: HTTP 500 with `server_error` and no detail in the body (the other store failures take the same path). No production path other than `POST /oauth/revoke` calls this function (the other callers are tests).

## Not changed
Other store readers use a similar `.expect` on a parsed column in other files (`ceiling.rs`, `changesets.rs`, `teams.rs`, `unlocks.rs`, `keys.rs`, `oauth/clients.rs`, `oauth/codes.rs`, `sign_in_events.rs`). There is no existing mapping to follow; they are out of scope for this PR.

## Validation
Through `tools/agentic/gate.sh`: fmt, lint, dylint and test each exited 0 (logs in the worktree) (lib: 2276 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored).

## Claims
This repository has no claims ledger; these findings were not recorded. Audit (table-only): 14 supported, 0 refuted, 1 not_enough_info (gate exit codes, which the implementer observed as 0), 1 wording fix applied (callers; the `sign_in_events.rs` pattern is similar, not identical). Supported: no panic and no new `.expect`/`.unwrap` outside tests; `OkfError::Database` via `ColumnDecode`; rollback on a bad row; the test fails when the fix is reverted (panics at the old `.expect`); `POST /oauth/revoke` answers 500 `server_error` without detail.

Closes #266

body:
## Summary

The task sheet draws a task's body and comments as markdown, with the message renderer (ADR 0002): nothing is fetched or run, and links open as in a message (a bare link at once, a labelled one after a confirmation naming "this task"). Both are selectable to copy. The title, history and every other text of a task stay plain.

```diff
 <TaskSheet>
   TaskDetailSections
-    Text(body, Type.message)
+    SelectionContainer { MarkdownText(body, place = "this task") }
     Section("Comments")
-      Text(comment.text, Type.small)
+      SelectionContainer { MarkdownText(comment.text, place = "this task") }
 MarkdownText(text, color, modifier,
+             place = "this conversation")   # the website confirmation: "The link leaves this task for the browser."
   Blocks → Block
+    depth ≥ Markdown.MOST_DEPTH (8) and a quote or list → Text(Markdown.flatWords(node))   # its words, plain, read without recursion
```

Docs: `docs/spec.md` (A task's sheet: Body, Comments, Untrusted text; the element table; Web links; To verify) and ADR 0002 (proposed), a consequence: a task's body and comments are drawn the same way.

Pairs with enclos#330: the protocol says the body and comments are markdown, and the Hermes plugin tells every agent whose tasks the app shows. So it comes with the plugin at install.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a body shows raw: `# #298 S1d — approved run177 validation continuation, SAME card`, then a wall of text with its marks.

New JVM test `MarkdownTest.text_nested_past_what_is_drawn_reads_as_its_words_however_deep`. author: carvalinh0
body:
## What and why

After finding what fills the disk, the user still had to delete it somewhere else. `d` now moves the selected entry to the trash, after an explicit confirmation. This drops the "only reads" promise, so docs and the privacy policy change with it (Store texts are updated by hand by the maintainer).

**Behaviour**
- `d` in the tree or in the largest files list (`f`). The footer asks `Move <path> (<size>) to the Recycle Bin?`; only `y` proceeds, any other key cancels. Mouse events are ignored while asking.
- Never a permanent delete: the [`trash`](https://crates.io/crates/trash) crate (5.4, pure Rust: `windows`/`objc2`, no C toolchain, MSRV 1.87) uses the Recycle Bin on Windows, `NSFileManager` on macOS, and the freedesktop spec on Linux, including a mount's own `.Trash-<uid>`. Everything can be restored.
- Afterwards the entry leaves the tree and the list, and its size is subtracted from every ancestor. The title says `Moved … to the Recycle Bin: empty it to free the space` (green, until the next key).
- Refused, with the reason in the title:
  - while the scan runs (it would keep adding to the entry);
  - the scanned folder itself;
  - drive and filesystem roots and the home folder;
  - system folders (`platform::system_folders`): `%SystemRoot%` and the `Program Files` folders on Windows; `/usr`, `/etc`, `/bin`, `/boot`, `/var/lib`… on Linux; `/System`, `/usr`… on macOS.

**Implementation**
- `Node::remove` flags the node and subtracts its size. Children cannot be taken out of the `OnceLock` slice, because workers hold `&Node`s into it, so `tree::build`, `largest_files` and `can_expand` skip removed nodes. `tree::find` maps a path back to the chain of nodes, for both views.
- `App::trash` is a function pointer (`platform::trash`), so tests use a fake and never touch the real trash.
- `platform::home_dir` is now shared (it moved from `app.rs`).

**Docs**: README (key table, the "only reads" paragraph), `PRIVACY.md` (the `d` exception), the bug report template.

## How it was tested

- [x] fmt, clippy (Linux, `cargo xwin` Windows, `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`), `cargo +1.95 check`, 44 tests:
  - `Node::remove` and `tree::find`: sizes of the ancestors, rows, largest files;
  - the `d`/`n`/`y` flow with a fake trash; the scanned folder refused; `d` in the `f` list; `/usr` refused (Unix);
  - protected paths (roots, home, system folders; case-insensitive on Windows);
  - the confirmation footer.
- [x] In tmux on Linux, with the real trash:
  - a 300 KB file went to `/tmp/.Trash-1000` with its `.trashinfo` (restorable); the tree dropped to the remaining 4 KiB;
  - refusals: during a scan ("wait for the scan to finish"), on `/etc` (system folder), on `/` (the scanned folder).
- [ ] Recycle Bin on Windows and Trash on macOS: covered by the crate and CI builds; not tried by hand (Smart App Control blocks unsigned builds on the dev machine).

author: grimicorn-agent
body:
## What changed
Internal link line numbers drifted early after a wrapped code span, link title or reference label, because newlines inside those constructs leave no softbreak token. `extractInternalLinks` now derives each inline child's line from its offset in `inline.content` instead of counting break tokens.

## Implementation notes
- markdown-it keeps no source position on inline tokens, so `.vitepress/theme/utils/internalLinks.ts` subclasses the parser's `inline.State` (on the module's private `MarkdownIt` instance only) to record `state.pos` for every pushed token and flushed text token in a `WeakMap`.
- A child's line is the first line plus the newlines in `content.slice(0, offset)`. Tokens created after parsing (core linkify) have no offset and take the line of the next token that has one; a text token never spans a newline, so that is the same line.
- Removes the `@todo` that described this bug and the now-unused `extraLines` helper.
- No new dependencies, env vars or services.

## Tests
New regression tests in `.vitepress/tests/posts/internal-links.test.ts`: a multi-line code span, link title and reference label each followed by a link, and a linkified URL after a wrapped code span. Both fail on `main`.

## Where to see it
Not user-visible (build/CI link-check line numbers).

Closes #610

body: `npm test` is 113 tests. `npm run test:e2e` adds 4 against the built stdio and HTTP servers. Coverage is from `npm run test:coverage` on Node v22.23.4. ## Coverage | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Tests (`npm test`) | 45 | 113 | | Lines | 91.33% (696 / 762) | 99.61% (771 / 774) | | Branches | 78.02% (419 / 537) | 96.88% (528 / 545) | Core, same run: | File | Lines | Branches | | --- | --- | --- | | `src/domain/**` | 100% (185 / 185) | 99.11% (111 / 112) | | `src/domain/scoring.ts` | 100% (75 / 75) | 98.52% (67 / 68) | | `src/db/repository.ts` | 100% (149 / 149) | 100% (116 / 116) | | `src/mcp/server.ts` | 100% (133 / 133) | 95.65% (88 / 92) | | `src/mcp/format.ts` | 100% (17 / 17) | 100% (8 / 8) | `vitest.config.ts` fails the build under 98% statements, 95% branches, 98% functions, and 98% lines. Domain files are gated per file at 100% lines and 95% branches. `repository.ts` is gated at 98% lines and 95% branches. `server.ts` is gated at 100% lines and 95% branches. ## What the new tests drive - Every MCP tool: invalid and boundary input, unicode, very long strings, missing and unknown ids, duplicate and idempotent calls, follow-up instants, an empty pipeline, and CSV cells with commas, quotes, newlines, and formula prefixes (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`), including after leading whitespace. - fast-check properties for the scoring rubric: the score stays in 0–100, the factors sum to it, and source, urgency, value, open stage, recency, and reachability are monotonic where the rubric says they are. - Contract snapshots of `tools/list`, `resources/list` (plus resource templates), and `prompts/list`. - Migrations on an empty database, a second idempotent run, and the same round trip on `node:sqlite` and Miniflare D1. No Cloudflare credentials. - A real MCP client against `dist/bin/stdio.js`, the built Streamable HTTP server including bearer rejection, and the Worker `fetch` entry on a Miniflare D1 binding. ## Mutation score Stryker 10.1.1 on `src/domain/**/*.ts`, Vitest runner, 4 minutes 6 seconds: **82.07%** (619 mutants, 508 killed, 110 survived, 1 with no coverage, 0 timeouts, 0 errors). `scoring.ts` was 73.36% (223 killed, 80 survived). Most of those survivors are detail-string edits. The CI job fails below 80. ## Bugs fixed - Follow-up due times and interaction timestamps were ordered as raw text. `16:00+01:00`, and a `Z` timestamp with no milliseconds, did not mean the instant they spelled, so a due item could be missing and `MAX(occurred_at)` could pick the earlier conversation. Writes now store `Date#toISOString`, and the idempotency hash uses that same instant. - Logging an interaction set `updatedAt` to the conversation time, so a backdated note sank the lead in the recently-updated scan. `updatedAt` is the server clock. - Recency treated an age of exactly 2 days as "under 2 days" and exactly 7 days as "under 7 days". The published rubric says under 2, under 7, then 7 through 14 days at 0. - A closed-lost summary said the score was capped when the raw total was already under 15. - CSV formula neutralization missed a cell whose first non-whitespace character is `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@`. Spreadsheets still execute those. - Setting a follow-up to the status it already had rewrote the lead and could fail a concurrent update. The same status is now a no-op. - `daily_follow_up_briefing`'s `staleAfterDays` was a number schema. Prompt arguments arrive as strings, so a client could not set it. The value is coerced. - The Worker migration sent the formatted SQL script through D1 `exec`. Miniflare's D1 ends a statement at a newline, so `CREATE TABLE` never completed and `/mcp` could not bootstrap. `migrate` now runs one flattened statement at a time. - Log fields named `reason` were redacted, which hid why a seed was skipped. Those diagnostics are logged as `cause`.

author: krasotinpa
body:
## What

Issue #9 (automatable part): `scripts/install.py` + README install section +
headless tests. **The live cutover itself was NOT run** — only a read-only
`--dry-run` (below). Merging and the manual acceptance stay with the
maintainer; this PR does not close the issue.

- `scripts/install.py` — stdlib + reuse of the `autostart` core and
  `settings._startup_dir()` / `settings.TRAY_ARGUMENTS` (importing settings
  has no side effects). No new dependencies.
- `tests/test_install.py` — 17 tests, every seam fake (subprocess runner,
  CIM enumeration, shortcut switch, Popen, socket probe, clock); shortcut
  behaviour additionally exercised on real `.lnk` files in `tmp_path`
  (same convention as `test_autostart.py`). Live processes, the real
  Startup folder, 8118/9090 and the user's Config are never touched.
- `README.md` — Install section: prerequisites, command, what the script
  does, client env (`HTTP_PROXY=HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8118`, no
  `ALL_PROXY`), curl verification, rollback note.

## Design decisions

- **Order**: `uv sync` strictly BEFORE stopping the old bridge — broken
  deps must never kill a working bridge. Pinned by
  `test_sync_runs_before_stop_and_the_rest` and
  `test_uv_sync_failure_aborts_before_stop` (sync fail → abort, no
  taskkill / shortcut / launch).
- **uv discovery**: `UV_BIN` env → `shutil.which("uv")` → known fallback
  `C:/Users/krasotin/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.15-64/Scripts/uv.exe`.
  `uv sync` gets `--python C:/Users/krasotin/AppData/Local/Python/bin/python.exe`
  when that shim exists (AGENTS.md: uv may not find the install-manager
  Python on its own).
- **Process matching**: PowerShell CIM enumeration of python/pythonw only;
  command line must match `tools[\/]socks-http-bridge[\/]bridge.py` —
  separator-tolerant, case-insensitive, whole filename (`bridge.py.bak` /
  `bridge.pyw` do NOT match). Unrelated python is never killed (pinned with
  live-like command lines).
- **Stop strategy**: graceful `taskkill /PID` first (WM_CLOSE; a windowless
  pythonw usually refuses — expected), wait up to 5 s, then `taskkill /F`
  and wait up to 3 s. Force failure or still-alive → `InstallError`, abort
  BEFORE touching the shortcut or launching the tray (pinned).
- **Shortcut cutover**: old `.lnk` identified by target/arguments content,
  never by name (an old bridge under `SocksHttpBridge.lnk` is still
  replaced); unrelated `.lnk` untouched (pinned). New shortcut via
  `autostart.create_shortcut(startup, .venv/Scripts/pythonw.exe,
  arguments="-m socks_http_bridge --tray")` — identical to what Settings
  syncs, so the Autostart checkbox stays in sync.
- **Idempotency**: no old process → skip stop; shortcut already correct →
  skip (mtime pinned); tray already running → skip launch (the
  single-instance mutex would exit a second instance anyway); tray up +
  Listener answering → "Already installed" report.
- **`--dry-run`**: read-only discovery only (CIM, `.lnk` reads, Config
  read), prints the plan; no sync/stop/writes/launch (pinned).
- **Verification**: TCP-connect the first configured Listener (default
  `127.0.0.1:8118`) for up to ~10 s; on failure print the log path and a
  Stop/Start hint.

## Checks (local, `env -u PYTHONPATH`)

```
uv run pytest        → 152 passed in 84.35s (0:01:24)   [135 baseline + 17 new]
uv run ruff check .  → All checks passed!
uv run mypy src      → Success: no issues found in 10 source files
```

`pyproject.toml` sets `[tool.mypy] files = ["src"]`, so `scripts/` is
outside mypy scope by project config; ruff covers it.

## Live reconnaissance (read-only, 2026-11-18)

Old bridge processes (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, python/pythonw with
`tools\socks-http-bridge\bridge.py` in the command line) — **3 alive**:

| PID | CommandLine |
|-----|-------------|
| 24040 | `C:\Users\krasotin\AppData\Local\Python\bin\python.exe C:/Users/krasotin/tools/socks-http-bridge/bridge.py --listen 0.0.0.0:8119 --log C:\Users\krasotin\AppData\Local/socks-http-bridge/test8119.log` |
| 26380 | `"C:\Users\krasotin\AppData\Local\hermes\installs\79bb02a9af50deb5\environments\283b0f6b505746178cc6aeda1b1ba495\venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe" C:\Users\krasotin\tools\socks-http-bridge\bridge.py` |
| 12864 | same as 26380 (second instance) |

Note: PID 24040 is a leftover `0.0.0.0:8119` test instance with mixed
separators — it matches the old-bridge pattern and WILL be stopped by the
cutover (by design; the matching test pins separator tolerance).
`tools/socks-http-bridge/HANDOFF.md` claims the bridge was stopped on
18.11 — live CIM state contradicts that; live state wins.

Startup folder (`%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`,
targets read via WScript.Shell): only `Cloud.lnk` (Mail.Ru Disk-O) and
`Telegram.lnk`. **No old bridge shortcut exists** (HANDOFF.md: removed on
18.11; HKCU Run key and scheduled tasks also clean). The remove-old step
is therefore a no-op on this machine; it is implemented and tested for
the general case.

uv: not in PATH; known fallback
`C:/Users/krasotin/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.15-64/Scripts/uv.exe`
exists. `.venv/Scripts/pythonw.exe`: created in this worktree by
`uv sync --python C:/Users/krasotin/AppData/Local/Python/bin/python.exe`.

Real `--dry-run` output (read-only, no side effects):

```
dry-run: planning only, no changes will be made
  would run: ...\uv.EXE sync --python C:\Users\krasotin\AppData\Local\Python\bin\python.exe
  would stop old bridge PID 24040: ...bridge.py --listen 0.0.0.0:8119 ...
  would stop old bridge PID 26380: ...pythonw.exe" C:\Users\krasotin\tools\socks-http-bridge\bridge.py
  would stop old bridge PID 12864: ...pythonw.exe" C:\Users\krasotin\tools\socks-http-bridge\bridge.py
  would create Startup shortcut SocksHttpBridge.lnk -> ...\.venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m socks_http_bridge --tray
  would launch: ...\.venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m socks_http_bridge --tray
  would verify Listener 127.0.0.1:8118 via TCP connect (up to 10 s)
```

## Manual acceptance checklist (after merge, with the user)

Run from the merged checkout root: `uv run python scripts/install.py`
(recommended: `--dry-run` first). Then:

1. [ ] Install script runs cleanly; old bridge processes stopped; tray app
   running with a **green** icon.
2. [ ] `curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8118 https://api.ipify.org` returns the VPN
   exit IP (185.77.216.16 per HANDOFF).
3. [ ] Codex test:
   `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8118 HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8118 NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Reply with exactly one word: OK"`.
   Windows codex.exe: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9e1da79431da526b\codex.exe`.
   **WSL caveat**: codex may be the WSL one (`/home/user/.local/bin/codex`);
   WSL2 NAT cannot see the Windows loopback bridge without mirrored
   networking (`.wslconfig` `networkingMode=mirrored`) or a non-loopback
   Listener — decision for the user, out of scope here.
4. [ ] Startup shortcut targets `.venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m socks_http_bridge --tray`;
   Autostart checkbox in Settings in sync.
5. [ ] Exit IP Test popup, Settings Apply, Stop/Start verified manually;
   record results in issue #9.
6. [ ] Logoff/logon (or reboot): tray starts without any console window.

## Known gaps / notes

- If the tray was already running but the old bridge held 8118, the tray
  stays in Error after the cutover until the user does Stop → Start in the
  tray menu; the failure message says so. (Not reachable on this machine
  today: no tray process is running.)
- `scripts/` is outside mypy scope per `pyproject.toml` (`files = ["src"]`).
- No `src/` module, existing test, or AGENTS.md was modified.

Base: `multi-session/prerelease`, parent `43435dfc9d9c83bf8806afa957b231654ddd19b3`. Four files, +11/-9. Existing image generation, web search and asynchronous user messaging settings are untouched. Claude and agy are unchanged; this PR does not include #1453.

## Whole-PR Self-Review

| Finding | Product fix | Existing test | Contract / mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime Codex argv does not disable goals/apps | `cli/lib/runtime/session-command.js:47` | `cli/lib/runtime/__tests__/session-adapter.test.js:84` | Add exactly the two approved `-c features.*=false` overrides next to the existing override, before the startup prompt and independently of bypass. No new mechanism. |
| Docker Codex args omit the same overrides | `docker/entrypoint.sh:170` | `test/docker-dashboard.test.js:106` | Same overrides before the existing bypass conditional. No new mechanism. |

Reviewed the entire parent-to-head diff. Only these two product lines and the two existing expectation blocks change. The existing four model/bypass combinations iterate the expanded expected settings list; no new test cases. Existing checks retain rejection of duplicate/misplaced settings, preservation of bypass behavior, and exclusion of Codex settings from Claude/agy. No `--disable`, new flags, environment variables, configuration options, settings migrations or unrelated cherry-picks. New cases: 0. Removed negative controls: 0. No source re-evaluation or runtime source mutation.

## Validation

- `env TMPDIR=/dev/shm node scripts/run-node-tests.js '--test-name-pattern=Codex disables interactive tools' cli/lib/runtime/__tests__/session-adapter.test.js`: 4 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Calls real `buildRuntimeArgs`; covers default/override model x permission bypass on/off, unique paired `-c` values, ordering before the prompt and other-runtime exclusion.
- `env TMPDIR=/dev/shm node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/.bin/jest --runInBand --runTestsByPath test/docker-dashboard.test.js --testNamePattern='Docker Codex launch arguments'`: 1 passed, 12 unselected/skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Static check of the actual entrypoint; no container or services launched.
- `bash -n docker/entrypoint.sh`: exit 0.
- `git diff --check HEAD^..HEAD`: exit 0.
- `codex --version`: `codex-cli 0.166.0`, exit 0. No runtime installation, upgrade or configuration change.

### Real Request Comparison

One-off evidence harness outside the repository: `node /home/agent/zylos/workspace/codex-unused-tools-capture.mjs`, exit 0. Uses the installed Codex binary and real `buildRuntimeArgs`, `exec --ephemeral`, a fresh HOME/CODEX_HOME/ZYLOS_DIR/PM2_HOME/short TMPDIR under `/dev/shm`, and a local HTTP fixture bound to `127.0.0.1`. Actual paths, argv and loopback endpoint are printed before each launch. Child environment is an explicit allowlist without inherited credentials/session IDs. A custom Responses provider points only at that fixture, requires no authentication and returns a deterministic assistant message; the memory MCP server is disabled identically in both controls. No live login state is copied, no headers are recorded, and no requests are sent upstream. No tmux or database is used; each child has a 25-second kill deadline, response capture is bounded, and children/server/temporary directories are cleaned in `finally`. Evidence remains outside Git.

| Case | Exit | Request bytes | Tool count | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Existing launch argv without the two new overrides | 0 | 38,120 | 8 | exec_command, write_stdin, view_image, multi_agent_v1, get_goal, create_goal, update_goal, web_search |
| Candidate launch argv with both overrides | 0 | 34,907 | 5 | exec_command, write_stdin, view_image, multi_agent_v1, web_search |

Only `get_goal`, `create_goal` and `update_goal` disappear. Added tools: 0. All five retained tool definitions are JSON-identical, including web_search. Both Codex processes consume the local response and finish normally. Request bytes include the fixture prompt and per-case paths; this is not a general token-saving estimate. A first run confirmed tool names; a second run added an explicit identical-definition assertion and passed.

The fresh local-provider control exposes no apps connectors, request_plugin_install, image_gen or send_message_to_user_async. Their removal/preservation is **unverified**, not inferred from absence in both controls. No ChatGPT login state was available or accessed. These require reviewer verification in a suitable environment, particularly Codex 0.169.1 with an enabled apps control. If either approved `-c` override fails to remove its exposed group there, stop and report in the topic; do not substitute `--disable` or another mechanism.

| Existing integration files/cases required by this PR | New integration files/cases and coverage |
| --- | --- |
| 0 committed integration files/cases. Any integration execution must isolate HOME, ZYLOS_DIR, PM2_HOME, short TMPDIR, private tmux socket and test database; read back actual paths/argv, prove separation from production, and clean up owned resources. | 0 committed integration files/cases. The one-off local request comparison above is outside the repository. Any integration execution must isolate HOME, ZYLOS_DIR, PM2_HOME, short TMPDIR, private tmux socket and test database; read back actual paths/argv, prove separation from production, and clean up owned resources. |

## Acceptance

1. **Passed locally:** all four Codex model/bypass combinations carry both overrides before the startup prompt; product diff and existing tests confirm Claude/agy exclusion. Docker expectation passes.
2. **Partially passed:** three goals tools disappear from actual Codex 0.166.0 requests and all five other exposed definitions remain identical. **Reviewer-run:** apps connectors/request_plugin_install disappearance with an enabled ChatGPT control; image_gen and send_message_to_user_async preservation in an environment that exposes them; repeat on 0.169.1. No blanket claim of scenario completion.
3. **Reviewer-run:** full Zylos Codex session launch and message receipt. The local ephemeral fake-response run is not evidence of IM delivery.

Full Node/Jest suites, other integration/e2e suites and the tmux matrix were not run by Piper. No tmux protocol changes. No merge, deploy or restart. The issue body has no numbered scenarios beyond the topic's dispatch; the three dispatch scenarios above are the acceptance checklist.

## Summary
`argocd-server` redirects HTTP to HTTPS (307), and Homepage's `siteMonitor` doesn't follow a redirect to another protocol (`ERR_FR_REDIRECTION_FAILURE`). The Argo CD tile therefore showed an error.

- `siteMonitor` now points at `https://argocd-server.argocd.svc.cluster.local/healthz`. Homepage's proxy uses `rejectUnauthorized: false` for HTTPS, so Argo CD's self-signed certificate is accepted.
- `href` now uses `https://192.168.2.53/` so clicking the tile skips the redirect.

## Test plan
- [x] `kubectl kustomize homepage` builds
- [ ] After syncing, `/api/siteMonitor?groupName=Infrastructure&serviceName=Argo%20CD` returns 200

author: ramiroveloso
body:
## Descripción
Implementa el cálculo puro de saldos pendientes, el encadenamiento de remanentes entre entregas parciales sucesivas y la actualización del monto ejecutado en la partida presupuestaria al confirmar recepciones físicas (**Refs: #91**, siguiendo `DECISION_PARTIDAS_PRESUPUESTO_154.md`).

### Cambios principales

1. **Dominio (`ObraSync.Recepcion.Domain`):**
   - Se agregaron en `OrdenCompra.cs` los métodos puros `CalcularSaldosPendientes`, `ObtenerSaldoPendienteArticulo` y `EncadenarEntregas` para calcular el saldo remanente por artículo y validar la secuencia de entregas sucesivas sin superar el saldo vigente en cada eslabón.

2. **Aplicación y Contratos (`ObraSync.Recepcion.Application` & `contracts/`):**
   - Se incorporó `CantidadPendiente` en `ItemOrdenPendienteDto` y en el contrato OpenAPI (`contracts/openapi/recepciones-openapi.json`) para exponer explícitamente el saldo pendiente (`cantidadEsperada - cantidadRecibida`) en `GET /api/recepciones/ordenes-pendientes`.
   - Se unificó el cálculo de saldos pendientes en `CrearRecepcionCommandHandler` y `ObtenerOrdenesPendientesQueryHandler` delegando en `OrdenCompra.CalcularSaldosPendientes(...)`.
   - En `CrearRecepcionCommandHandler`, al confirmar una recepción sobre una orden con partida presupuestaria asignada (`!SinPartidaPresupuestaria`), se empareja la partida (`EmparejadorPartidaPresupuestaria`) y se invoca `partida.EjecutarMonto(...)` por el monto efectivamente recibido ($\sum \text{CantidadRecibida} \times \text{PrecioUnitario}$), manteniendo el remanente en `MontoComprometido`.
   - Se agregó manejo de `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` relanzando `RecepcionConflictoException` (`409 Conflict`) ante colisiones optimistas sobre `PartidaPresupuestaria`.

3. **Pruebas (`ObraSync.Recepcion.Tests`):**
   - **`OrdenCompraRemanentesTests.cs`:** pruebas unitarias de dominio puro para saldo pendiente (`100` pedidas / `75` recibidas $\to$ saldo `25`), cadenas de entregas sucesivas, validación de excesos sobre el saldo vigente y órdenes multi-ítem asimétricas.
   - **`CrearRecepcionEndpointTests.cs` y `FlujoIntegracionRecepcionTests.cs`:** pruebas de integración end-to-end verificando una cadena de 3 entregas sucesivas (`40` $\to$ `35` $\to$ `25`), la evolución de `cantidadPendiente` en `GET /api/recepciones/ordenes-pendientes` hasta desaparecer al completarse, y la actualización progresiva de `PartidaPresupuestaria.MontoEjecutado`.

### Verificación
- Compilación sin errores ni advertencias (`0 warnings`).
- `ObraSync.Recepcion.Tests`: **441/441** pruebas pasando.
- Regresión completa en `Requisiciones`, `Licitaciones` y `Usuarios`: **100%** pasando.

author: jaswanthcherukuri1-ai
body: Release Notes ------------- Bug Fixes - Fixed `confluent flink query -o json` and `-o yaml` printing a stray `[]` to stdout before the error when the statement fails (or is stopped or deleted) before returning any rows. Stdout is now empty and only the error is reported. Checklist --------- - [x] I have successfully built and used a custom CLI binary, without linter issues from this PR. - [x] I have clearly specified in the `What` section below whether this PR applies to Confluent Cloud, Confluent Platform, or both. - [ ] I have verified this PR in Confluent Cloud pre-prod or production environment, if applicable. - [ ] I have verified this PR in Confluent Platform on-premises environment, if applicable. - [x] I have attached manual CLI verification results or screenshots in the `Test & Review` section below. - [x] I have added appropriate CLI integration or unit tests for any new or updated commands and functionality. - [x] I confirm that this PR introduces no breaking changes or backward compatibility issues. - [x] I have indicated the potential customer impact if something goes wrong in the `Blast Radius` section below. - [ ] I have put checkmarks below confirming that the feature associated with this PR is enabled in: - [ ] Confluent Cloud prod - [ ] Confluent Cloud stag - [ ] Confluent Platform - [ ] Check this box if the feature is enabled for certain organizations only What ---- Applies to Confluent Cloud (`confluent flink query`). With `-o json` / `-o yaml`, results are streamed and `streamer.close()` always writes the document terminator. When a statement ends in a failed terminal phase (FAILED, STOPPED, DELETING) with zero rows written, `close()` emitted a bare `[]` on stdout ahead of the error. Consumers piping stdout (e.g. to `jq`) got an empty array that looked like a successful empty result. Fix: in `emitResult`, if there is a phase error and no row was written, skip `close()` and return the error. This needs an `isOpened()` method on `resultStreamer` (true once the first row is written). Behavior kept as before: - A successful statement with zero rows (including schema-less DDL) still emits `[]`. - A phase error after rows were already streamed still calls `close()`, so the array stays valid JSON. - `-o human` is unchanged. Not a breaking change: no flags, fields, or serialized formats change. The only difference is that a failing run no longer prints a misleading empty array on stdout. Blast Radius ---- Confluent Cloud customers who run `confluent flink query -o json` or `-o yaml` and parse stdout. On a failed statement with no rows they now get empty stdout plus a non-zero exit instead of `[]`. Scripts that treated `[]` on stdout as "no rows" for a failed statement would change behavior, but that output was misleading. Successful runs and `-o human` are unaffected. References ---------- - SQL-5506 Test & Review ------------- - Unit: `TestEmitResultStreamedPhaseError` covers FAILED/STOPPED/DELETING with no rows (empty stdout), FAILED after rows (valid JSON array), and a successful empty run (`[]`). With the guard removed, the no-rows cases fail. - Integration: two new `TestFlinkQuery` cases run `will_fail` with `-o json` and `-o yaml` and expect exit code 1. They use a new anchored golden, `failed-serialized.golden`, so any stdout ahead of `Error:` fails. They fail without the fix. - `golangci-lint` (v1.64.8) and `make lint-cli` are clean on Go 1.26.10; `TestCLI/TestFlinkQuery` and `internal/flink` unit tests pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: ductm54
body:
## Summary

Adds a new solving method, **Beginner guide (Learn tab)**. It solves using only the moves the Learn tab's beginner guide teaches. A **Faster tricks** setting switches on the Learn tab's "Go faster" shortcuts for any of: Cross, First-layer corners, Middle layer, Last layer. With none picked (the default), it gives exactly the guide's moves.

**How it solves:**
1. Hold the cross colour on top and build the cross one edge at a time: D to line up, F2 to lift, `F U' R U` to flip, `R' D' R` to drop a middle edge.
2. Turn the cube over, then insert the corners with the right or left 4-moves.
3. Put the middle edges in with the two-sets-of-4-moves algorithms.
4. Solve the yellow cross, then the yellow edges, then the yellow corners.
5. Turn the cube over again and twist the corners with `R U R' U'` and D turns.

**What each trick setting changes:**

| Setting | Shortcuts |
|---|---|
| Cross | A middle-layer edge slides straight up (`U' R U`) instead of being dropped first |
| First-layer corners | White on top in two sets, stuck corners taken out with the left hand, and a middle edge that's already solved is kept |
| Middle layer | `R2 U2 R2 U2 R2` swaps the two right edges; `R U2 R' U R U2 R' U F' U' F` flips an edge in its slot |
| Last layer | `f R U R' U' f'` from the backwards L, the opposite-edges case done in one step, the left-hand corner cycle once instead of twice, and two backwards 4-moves instead of four |

Each step is chosen by trying the allowed moves on the cube and keeping the shortest that works. Steps that use a shortcut are labelled "Faster trick".

**Other changes**
- Multi-choice settings can now allow an empty pick (`allowEmpty`). An empty pick shows as "none" in the settings line above the solve.
- Learn tab: a playable demo of the flipped middle edge fix. The "Solved!" card and the "Go faster" intro now point to the new method.
- New text is in English only, like the rest of the Learn content.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 108 tests pass, and `tsc` passes.
- New `tests/guide.test.ts` solves random scrambles with every combination of tricks and all six cross colours. It checks that each layer is finished at the end of its own stage, that no B turns are used, and that each trick only appears in its own layer. It also checks that turning tricks on gives shorter solves, and the swap and flip cases.
- Checked a full solve in a production build (`vite preview`), with corner and last-layer tricks on.

body:
Plain OpenAI-compatible generation substitutes a 600-second request timeout when the caller omits one. That request override prevents the shared client from honoring the provider profile timeout and lets a delayed gateway response determine the result.

Pass the optional request timeout through to the shared client. Explicit request timeouts retain precedence, the client still defaults to 600 seconds when configuration is absent, and existing profiles require no migration.

The native regression and the browser model check fail before the fix and pass on SQLite and PostgreSQL with Wippy v0.3.65a. A loopback gateway verifies that the configured timeout yields a retryable Timeout, HTTP 502 yields a retryable Unavailable, and the configured retry count bounds the number of requests.

author: sentfromthefuture
body:
## Summary
- Add a service-role-only `dr_blueprint_finalize` RPC that stores the validated Blueprint and commits its quota reservation in the same Postgres transaction.
- Make finalization idempotent for a retry after a lost response: an already-committed reservation returns its existing result.
- Add a result-store adapter method that calls the RPC and re-reads/revalidates the stored result.
- Add a synthetic adapter test for the atomic finalize path.

## Why
Separate result persistence and quota commit calls create a failure window: a completed result could be uncharged, or a reservation could be charged without a saved result. This RPC makes both changes atomic.

## Safety
- Migration only; not applied to hosted Supabase.
- Synthetic fetch tests only; no provider calls, DB writes, secrets, or deployment.
- Provider execution remains hard-disabled pending privacy review.

author: alegruz
body:
Part of #1307 (managed render passes and pipelines, first migration).

## What changed

- **`RenderGraphProgramCache`** (new public type in `render_graph.hpp`): a device-scoped, owner-thread holder for the bilinear upscale pass's immutable dependencies: vertex/fragment stages, binding layout, linear sampler and full-target quad. Graphs lease a set by the **complete canonical description** of the composite stages. That covers the stage, every target artifact and entry point, reflected inputs, bindings, uniform members and GLSL ES names. Pointers and hashes never select a set. The final lease destroys the set, and no idle set is kept.
- **`RenderGraphUpscaleProgram`** now leases from the cache and gets its pipeline through `rhi::RequestPipeline` instead of `CreateRasterPipeline`. Equal shader/layout incarnations and fixed state share one native pipeline. The surface and RGBA8 targets stay distinct. Source views and binding sets stay per-graph, so a resize or input rebind issues no new request. The MetalFX surface copy uses the same program.
- **`RenderGraph::Initialize`** takes an optional trailing `programCacheOrNull`. With null, the graph gets a private cache, so it behaves as before.
- **`RenderGraphActivation`** owns one cache shared by its active and candidate generations, and exposes `GetProgramCacheReport()`.
- **Reporting:** `RenderGraphPipelineReport::Upscale` gives per-graph requests, shared requests, ready requests and prewarm/queue seconds. This is separate from frame time and from the device totals.
- Docs: renderer-systems "First migration and acceptance" status, plus the "Device pipeline preparation" guide with measurements.

## Acceptance status

| Criterion | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Two compatible instances and overlapping active/candidate generations share one backend creation | ✅ reference-backend test plus native Metal test (candidate `SharedRequests == 1`, no extra pipeline or shader creation) |
| Incompatible targets get distinct pipelines | ✅ surface vs RGBA8 test |
| Extent-only resize and input rebinding reuse the pipeline | ✅ no new pipeline or shader creation, no new shared request |
| Cancellation releases the candidate's request; pending replacement keeps the active drawable | ✅ pending candidate reset; `PreparingPipelines` returns to baseline; active keeps rendering |
| Accepted frame retains its pipeline until completion | ✅ native pipeline and shaders are destroyed only after the submission completes |
| Native pixels match the current pass | ✅ Metal: shared active and candidate graphs are byte-identical to an unshared graph |
| **Browser pixels** | ❌ **Not done.** No browser fixture draws the bilinear pass (renderer GPU tests are native-only). Needs a separate WebGPU fixture, so the issue stays open. |
| Creation counts and preparation time separate from frame time | ✅ see below |

Measured on 18 Nov 2026: Apple M5, Metal, `macos-clang-debug`, load average ~40–50, 3 runs, 48×32 → 96×64 surface upscale.

| | Active | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upscale requests / shared | 1 / 0 | 1 / 1 |
| Native upscale creations | 1 | 0 |
| Upscale native preparation | 0.25–0.28 ms | shares the active creation |
| Upscale queue time | 0.04 ms | shares the active creation |
| `Render` CPU time | 0.39–0.49 ms | 0.39–0.49 ms |

Scope note: only the bilinear program is migrated. Scene-stage and other renderer-owned pipelines are still created directly per graph. Equality for explicit attachment formats, MSAA and stencil stays with #1313.

## Verification (local, macOS arm64)

- `cmake --build out/build/macos-clang-debug` (with `LUDUS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON`): `ludus_graphics_renderer`, `ludus_renderer_tests`, `ludus_renderer_render_tests` all build clean.
- `ludus_renderer_tests`: **all 315 cases pass**, including the 5 new `[managed-pipeline]` cases.
- `ludus_renderer_render_tests "[bilinear],[metalfx]"`: 5/5 pass on Metal (new pixel-parity case included).
- `ludus_renderer_render_tests "[render-graph]"`: 39/39 pass on Metal.
- `./scripts/check --format-changed --base origin/develop`: clean.
- `python3 scripts/python/source_policy.py --base <merge-base>`: clean.
- `./scripts/check macos-clang-debug --tidy-changed --base origin/develop`: clean. Full `.clang-tidy` on `render_graph_program_cache.cpp` and `render_graph_upscale.cpp`: clean.
- `python scripts/check-docs`, `mkdocs build --strict`, `python scripts/build-api --bootstrap` (no new API documentation gaps), `python scripts/check-wiki --documentation-only`, `test_docs.py`: all pass.

**Not run locally:** Linux/Vulkan, Windows/Direct3D 12 and browser builds; these first run in CI. The field-coverage `static_assert`s on the RHI description sizes are checked only on 64-bit targets.

author: rulogb
body:
## Problem

In OpenCode, a subagent finished, and its parent was told so, before its task-end checks ran. The plugin ran the checks on the subagent's turn end, 2 or 3 minutes on a real project. When they failed, it resumed the subagent while the orchestrator already took its work as done. OpenCode 2.3.0 now runs every subagent in the background, so this hit every delegated task.

## Change

- On OpenCode 2.2.1 and later, the plugin uses the `experimental.idle` session hook. OpenCode awaits it just before a session goes idle, and input it admits runs in the same execution.
- For a subagent that changed files, the hook runs its task-end checks there. On failure it gives the subagent the failures to fix, up to 3 attempts. Its answer, in the foreground or in the background, reaches the parent only after that.
- If it still fails, or stops, the failures go to the parent: in the `subagent` tool's answer, or in a message for one in the background.
- Every message admitted to a session is input, even with `resume: false`, so the line for the user waits for the subagent's turn end.
- Without the hook, as on older OpenCode, the checks still run at the subagent's turn end, as before.
- A second commit fixes two issues a review found: a held subagent could be released twice, and its background mark never cleared.

Claude Code, Codex and Copilot need no change: their `SubagentStop` hooks already block the subagent before it finishes.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm test` pass (1175 tests). 13 new tests cover the held paths.
- Tried by hand in OpenCode 2.3.0 on a multi-module Maven sample, with a background subagent told to write code that fails Checkstyle. OpenCode's database shows the subagent getting the failures 0.5 s after its first answer, in the same execution, and fixing them. It went idle 84 s later, and its parent got the notice 22 ms after that, with the fixed answer. Interlint's metrics show the same order.

`experimental.idle` is marked experimental by OpenCode and may change.

author: seanldnet
body:
## Scope (PR C only)
Implements Dujiao-Next purchase forwarding on an isolated branch. This PR does not include PR D or PR E and does not claim real-upstream integration.

- Enqueue procurement atomically with verified TRC20/wallet payment confirmation; snapshot upstream product/SKU identity at local order creation.
- Re-read live order and product immediately before supplier purchase; skip canceled/refunded/non-upstream/unlisted orders. A public HTTPS callback URL must be configured in the admin UI before the Telegram shop allows upstream checkout.
- Persist local/downstream order mapping and supplier order ID/no with unique constraints.
- Signed Dujiao-Next purchase and order lookup client; configurable poll interval/timeout.
- HMAC-SHA256 callback verification, semantic callback idempotency, encrypted fulfillment persistence, and Telegram delivery through the existing delivery pipeline.
- Failed/uncertain procurement enters the admin manual queue; manual recovery queries a known supplier order ID first, otherwise reuses the original local order number as the idempotency key. Confirmed failures can be refunded to buyer wallet with a separate ledger record and admin audit; original payment reference is unchanged.
- Supplier balance snapshots, low-balance alert threshold, and daily reconciliation report inclusion.
- Manual-form fulfillment products remain blocked until buyer form-data collection is implemented; auto-fulfillment SKUs are the supported self-service purchase path.

## Upstream contract boundary
The verified Dujiao-Next Open API documents idempotency by API Key + `downstream_order_no`, but does not document a lookup endpoint by downstream order number. If the initial POST times out before returning an upstream order ID, the worker parks the order as `uncertain` for human verification and does not automatically resubmit. A manual retry uses the exact same idempotency key, so an accepted first request resolves to the existing supplier order instead of creating a second one. If an upstream order ID is known, the worker queries `GET /orders/:id` before further action. Non-2xx supplier business responses (including HTTP 402/404) are parsed separately from transport failures.

author: francomarin
body:
## Criterio de actividad

Solo reinician el contador las acciones del dueño: editar el reporte, "Seguir mostrando", cerrarlo, confirmar una coincidencia y escribir en un chat de su reporte. No cuentan los mensajes de la otra parte, las coincidencias sugeridas por la IA ni las escrituras del sistema (moderación, flyer). Decisión registrada en ADR-0028.

## ADR-0028: cierre por inactividad

**Decisión.** La inactividad se mide con una columna propia, `lastActivityAt`, que solo reinician las acciones del dueño: editar el reporte, "Seguir mostrando", cerrarlo, confirmar una coincidencia y escribir en un chat de su reporte. Una tarea periódica en el backend avisa a los 30 y 37 días y cierra a los 38, con al menos 24 h entre el segundo aviso y el cierre.

**Motivo**
- Las actividades que reinician los días son las que involucran al dueño, así se sabe que sigue activo (criterio del equipo).
- `updatedAt` se actualiza con cualquier escritura, incluidas las del sistema (veredicto de la IA, ocultamiento automático, restauración, flyer), por lo que reiniciaría el contador sin que el dueño actúe.
- El backend ya ejecuta tareas periódicas en proceso, por lo que no se suma infraestructura nueva.

**Alternativas descartadas**
- `updatedAt`: mezcla escrituras del sistema con acciones del dueño.
- Contar coincidencias sugeridas por la IA: no involucran al dueño y exigiría modificar el servicio de IA.
- Máximo calculado con uniones sobre mensajes y coincidencias: encarece cada barrido.
- Cola o cron externo: suman infraestructura.

**Consecuencias**
- Cada acción del dueño que cuenta como actividad actualiza `lastActivityAt` de forma explícita y se agrega una migración. Los mensajes del otro usuario y las confirmaciones de la otra parte no reinician el contador.
- La tarea corre en cada instancia del backend sin bloqueo entre instancias, por lo que los avisos y el cierre se reclaman con escrituras condicionales para no duplicarse.
- Los reportes ocultos no se cierran automáticamente: el cierre solo es válido para reportes publicados.

## Cambios

- **ADR-0028**: columna propia en vez de `updatedAt`, tarea periódica en el backend, motivo del equipo.
- **Backend**:
  - Migración con `last_activity_at`, `inactivity_warned_30_at`, `inactivity_warned_37_at`, `closed_reason` y `closed_at`.
  - Barrido idempotente cada 1 h, con escrituras condicionales para que no se duplique entre instancias.
  - Notificaciones `inactivity_warning` e `inactivity_closed`.
  - `POST /api/reports/:id/keep-active`. "Caso resuelto" reutiliza `POST /:id/close`.
  - Los avisos pendientes se marcan como leídos al actuar.
- **Frontend**: botones "Caso resuelto" y "Seguir mostrando" en la notificación, con estados de carga y error y manejo del 409.

El cierre automático deja el reporte en `resolved` con `closed_reason = inactivity`, s

## Pruebas

- Backend: 44 tests de #264 pasan, incluidos 23 contra base real con la migración aplicada. `typecheck` limpio.
- Frontend: `vitest` 1162/1162, `tsc` y `oxlint` limpios.
- Cada commit del backend se probó aislado.
- La suite completa del backend tiene fallos que parecen del entorno (timeouts de bcrypt en `auth` y los e2e, y la tabla `layer` de PostGIS en `cascade-user-deletion`). No los comparé contra `main`.
- No se hizo prueba manual del flujo completo ni e2e de Playwright.

## A decidir antes de desplegar

La migración rellena `last_activity_at` con la fecha de publicación. En producción, los reportes publicados hace más de 37 días recibirían el segundo aviso en el primer barrido y se cerrarían unas 24 h después, sin aviso a los 30 días. Habría que rellenar con la fecha del despliegue.

Closes #264

author: ker2xu
body:
## Problem and change

After an OpenCode background sub-agent round, clicking the "Load background activity" pill (the out-of-turn wire-content notice) rendered the newest messages ABOVE a duplicated copy of the old round — the timeline looked like the latest messages "jumped to the top".

Mechanism (traced to the real local store data, opencode session `ses_e117f284affeNxE0ryo9ujXPRm`, 2026-11-18):

1. 11:55:01 user asks; 11:55:18 the parent turn ends with a `subagent(agent: explore)` launch + background ack, and codeg promotes that round into `localTurns`.
2. The child session runs 11:55–12:02:50 out-of-turn; when it finishes, opencode continues the parent with a synthetic notice + a new assistant turn and **no user prompt**, so codeg's out-of-turn wire guard drops it and arms the pill.
3. The pill refetches with `preserveLive: true`. The re-parse (`ORDER BY seq ASC`) is correctly ordered, but `FETCH_DETAIL_SUCCESS` keeps `localTurns`, and the timeline appends them AFTER the persisted tail. The old round's persisted twin carries a parser id (`msg_…`) that `dedupeTimeline` (exact `(role, id)`) can never match against the promoted `live-<cid>-…` id, so the whole old round renders twice — below the new tail.

Change: in `FETCH_DETAIL_SUCCESS`, when `keepAllLiveBuffers` preserves `localTurns`, retire a local turn the response **provably** covers (`retireDetailCoveredLocalTurns`): the detail is a settled (non-in-flight) response whose window holds a **strictly newer** turn than it, and whose uncovered prefix (`uncovered_prefix_max_ts`, the same guard `retireCoveredBackgroundTurns` applies to overlay turns) cannot be holding its twin. Mid-flight responses, an attached `liveMessage`, and the sub-agent dialog (`liveOwnsActiveTurn`) keep every local turn — a reply's transcript write can still be in flight there (`completeTurn`'s documented write race), and the dialog owns its own promotion/dedup path. Unparseable timestamps keep the turn. The failure direction of every ambiguous case is a recoverable transient duplicate, never a vanished message.

## Validation

- New regression `src/stores/runtime-out-of-turn-pill-order.test.ts` (8 tests, seeded from the real failure's turn ids/timestamps): the pill refetch now yields exactly the parsed transcript `[user, a1, a2, background]` with `localTurns` emptied; protective cases keep the promoted round for the write race (round newer than everything parsed), an in-flight detail snapshot, an attached live message, the sub-agent dialog, an uncovered-prefix windowed response, and an unparseable timestamp. Before the fix, the first test failed with the duplicated round below the new tail (verified against the pre-fix store: repro test documented `[user_p, a1_p, a2_p, NEW_p, user_l, a1_l, a2_l]`).
- Blast radius (every test file importing `conversation-runtime-store` or `message-list-view`, on a clean worktree of this branch): **32 files, 771 tests, all passing** (31 files / 599 tests + `acp-connections-context.test.tsx` / 172 tests).
- Full frontend suite on a clean worktree of this branch: **8,813 / 8,888 passed, 75 failed across 17 files — none in the blast radius**; 64 of the 75 are `Test timed out in 5000ms`. Control experiments on the same machine:
  - The same 17 files on clean `main` (`e21eb6b38`) also fail under the same load (24 failed, 20 timeouts), and the failing test sets differ run-to-run on both sides — the signature of load flakes, not regressions.
  - The worst offender (`task-editor-dialog.agent.test.tsx`: 7 timeouts in both loaded branch runs, green on main's loaded run) passes **11/11 in isolation on both `main` and this branch**.
  - CI's Linux runner is the authoritative signal for these files.
- Changed-file ESLint/Prettier clean; `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; `git show --check` clean.

## Evidence boundary

The retirement proof relies on the parser walking the transcript in append order (`seq ASC` for the OpenCode 2.x store, JSONL append order for Claude), so a strictly newer parsed turn implies the older round's write completed; clock skew between the client-stamped promoted timestamps and parser timestamps can delay retirement of the newest round (transient duplicate until the next refetch), never remove an unpersisted one. The pill's own `preserveLive` contract for a turn the user started in the meantime (liveMessage/optimisticTurns) is unchanged.

author: ahoo-wang
body:
The third of #6468's candidates, decided yes: a Java record command names its aggregate by a component marked `@AggregateId`. #6468 stays open until all three candidates are settled.

## What KSP shows of a record (probed, KSP 2.3.14)

A Java record has no properties in KSP, only its canonical constructor and its accessors. The mark therefore shows up in a different place depending on where the record is compiled:
- **Compiled in this module:** on the canonical constructor's parameter (`<init>`'s `id`); the accessor shows nothing.
- **Compiled in a library** (an api module's jar): on the accessor `id()`, once the annotation targets functions. javac carries a component's annotation to its accessor only for a `METHOD`-targeted annotation.

Before this change, the first case was refused (the parameter is no property) and the second was never seen.

## The change

- **`@AggregateId` gains `AnnotationTarget.FUNCTION`** beside `PROPERTY` and `FIELD`, so javac carries a component's mark to its accessor. This is public API: an annotation's targets are part of its contract.
  - The ABI dump does not record targets, so its line is unchanged: `public abstract interface annotation class me/ahoo/wow/api/annotation/AggregateId : java/lang/annotation/Annotation`.
  - The annotation's KDoc, and the generated annotations reference (en, zh), say what the target is for.
- **The compiler reads the mark from a record's component** (new `JavaRecords`):
  - the components are the canonical constructor's parameters that have an accessor of the same name;
  - the mark is read from the parameter or the accessor, whichever KSP shows;
  - the generated model reads it as Kotlin reads a component (`aggregateId<Tally> { it.id }`), and the Manifest names it (`idProperty`);
  - a component that is no `String`, or an `@Unaddressed` record, is refused as a property is;
  - a record with a marked component and another marked property has "several @AggregateId properties".
- **On any other function, the mark is a compile error** naming where it may go: "…which only a property of a command an aggregate decides takes: a Kotlin property, a Java field read by its public getter, or a Java record's component". It is checked module-wide (`AggregateIdResolver.reportMisplaced`), so a function of any class is covered, not only the model's types.
- **The report of an unmarked record** (`UnmarkedAggregateId`) now says "mark the component @AggregateId (record Tally(@AggregateId String id, …))", instead of "write the command as a class".

## Tests

- **`InheritedAggregateIdTest`:**
  - The canonical constructor is the one whose every parameter is a component, of the most parameters, pinned with a record that has a wider second constructor.
  - The three refusals, one case each with its text: a component that is no `String`, an `@Unaddressed` record, and a marked component beside an interface's marked property.
  - A creating record command with a marked component, compiled here and compiled in a library: both build, the model reads `id`, and the fragment names `idProperty = id`.
  - A Kotlin function marked `@AggregateId` is a compile error with the new text.
  - The unmarked-record report pins its new way out.
- **java-smoke** gains `RenameAccount(@AggregateId String id, String owner)` and its event `AccountRenamed`.
  - `AccountSpec` runs it end to end.
  - `JavaManifestTest` pins its `idProperty`.
  - `guide/java.md` (en, zh) carries the updated `Account.java` and `AccountState.java` samples.

## Docs

`guide/aggregates.md` (en, zh): a Java record marks its component, compiled in the domain module or the api module alike, and the mark on any other function is a compile error.

A move-only commit first takes the reason a module has no context (`noContext`) out of `ModelSymbolProcessor.kt` into `BoundedContexts`, so the file ends at 588 lines with the new call. The check itself lives in `AggregateIdResolver`, and `JavaRecords` (in `model.symbol`) is the one reader of a record.

Refs #6468.

## Verification (JDK 25, `-Pwow.test.java=25`)

- `:api:check` (251 tests, the ABI check), `:compiler:check` (334), `:java-smoke:check` (7) and `:architecture:check` (159): green.
- The four docs scripts: clean.

body:
## What

Moves the last local release step into GitHub Actions. Publishing already runs there; creating the `<pkg>-v<version>` tag and the GitHub Release did not.

- **New `Release` workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`). You start it by hand, pick a package (`vscode`, `intellij`, `nxls` or `nx-mcp`) and choose whether it's a dry run (the default). It only runs from `master`, in a new `release` environment, and calls the existing `tools/scripts/release.js`. The GitHub Release it creates triggers the existing `publish-*` workflows, which still wait for approval in `release-approval`.
- **GitHub App token instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN`.** The tag ruleset only lets admins and its bypass actors create tags. Releases created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` also don't trigger other workflows. The workflow requests a one-hour App installation token limited to `contents`, `issues` and `pull-requests` write. It does so after `yarn install`, so dependency install scripts never see it. Checkout runs without persisted credentials, and Nx Cloud is off for the job.
- **Publish workflows refuse tags that aren't on `master`.** Each `publish-*` workflow first checks that the release tag points at a commit on `master` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). A tag created or moved onto another branch can't publish, even if the deployment gets approved.

## Why these App permissions
- `contents: write`: push the tag and create the GitHub Release.
- `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write`: semantic-release (vscode, intellij) posts "released in vX" comments and adds the `released` label to the issues and PRs that shipped.

## Before merging (repo/org settings, not in this PR)
1. Create a GitHub App in nrwl with Contents, Issues and Pull requests set to read & write and no webhook, and install it on nx-console only.
2. Create the `release` environment: required reviewers Console Admins, prevent self-review, deployment branch `master`. Add the variable `RELEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` and the secret `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Create it **before** merging: a job that names a missing environment creates it without protection.
3. Add the App as a bypass actor on the "Auto-imported tag create protections" tag ruleset.

Until those exist the workflow can't get a token, so it does nothing. Nothing publishes without the existing `release-approval` approval.

## Testing
- actionlint passes on all workflows.
- The master check passes for the latest `vscode`, `nx-mcp`, `intellij` and `nxls` tags and rejects a commit that isn't on `master`.
- The release workflow can only be tested end to end once the App exists. After merging: Actions → Release → `vscode`, dry run.

```
A student signed out and deleted the account on "Dieses Gerät", the old diagnostics screen behind a pill on the Übersicht. It showed "Arbeitskopie · localhost:3000", "21 von 21 bestanden" and a SQLite version, and on the web it had no way back. The app had one tab.

Now there is a second tab, **Profil**, built from D83's slim profile (`profile-v2.html`, direction 2). It shows the initials in a blue circle with the name, Jahrgang and Klasse. Below that come a card with Schule, Jahrgang and Klasse, the Notizbuch-Schlüssel row, a Diagnose row, then Abmelden and Konto löschen. The old screen is now "Diagnose", a page under Profil with "Zurück" on every platform. The Übersicht's person button leads to Profil. On the wide web, the side rail has the app icon on top.

Preview: https://pr-138.studienbuch.schnau.dev/app/profil (sign in as a persona there; beta has none).

## Screens

Legacy Flutter, D83's mock, and the result at 390 px:

![Side by side](https://files.schnau.dev/html/studienbuch-roadmap/design/assets/m1-10-profile-side-by-side.png)

Before and after on the web at 390 px and 1280 px, light and dark:

![Before and after, 390](https://files.schnau.dev/html/studienbuch-roadmap/design/assets/m1-10-profile-before-after-390.png)
![Before and after, 1280](https://files.schnau.dev/html/studienbuch-roadmap/design/assets/m1-10-profile-before-after-1280.png)

Android (tower emulator, API 36, release APK) and iOS (iOS 27 simulator, Release build). Each shows the tab bar, Profil, Diagnose with its way back, Konto löschen and dark mode:

![Android](https://files.schnau.dev/html/studienbuch-roadmap/design/assets/m1-10-profile-android.png)
![iOS](https://files.schnau.dev/html/studienbuch-roadmap/design/assets/m1-10-profile-ios.png)

All of it on one sheet: https://files.schnau.dev/html/studienbuch-roadmap/design/assets/m1-10-profile-contact-sheet.png

## Decisions for Hauke

- **Only what the device holds.** The name comes from the encrypted profile, Jahrgang and Klasse from today's term's course choice, and the school from its row. A missing fact is left out, so the hero says "Profil" on a locked device and there's no Jahrgang between terms. E-Mail is left out because the device doesn't keep it.
- **Left out until their features exist:** Profil & Kurse bearbeiten (M3.1), Geräte, Aussehen, Über die App, Feedback, and the "Unterschriften" fact (signatures don't exist yet). The Sync Lab row from m1-screens is also out, because it wasn't on "Dieses Gerät" either.
- **Konto löschen** stays a quiet button under Abmelden. D83 doesn't show it.
- **Tab label "Profil"**, as D83 names it (legacy said "Mein Profil"). The person button stays on the Übersicht and switches to the tab.
- **The addresses stay.** `/diagnose`, `/selbsttest` and `/konto-loeschen` move into a `(profil)` group, which adds no path, so old links still open, now on top of Profil.
- **iOS had no way back from Notizbuch-Schlüssel** (from "Dieses Gerät" before, an older iOS screenshot shows it too). iOS's header shows a back button only above another screen of the same stack, and the key screens come first in theirs. `HeroScreen` now gives such a screen its own button. Its proof on the simulator follows in a comment, since m1 is slow tonight.

## Hit every surface

- **Platforms:** web in Chromium at 390 and 1280 px, light and dark, on a dev instance. No click reloads the page: tab switching, the person button, Diagnose and back, Notizbuch-Schlüssel and back, Konto löschen and back, and the deep links `/diagnose` and `/konto-loeschen` with "Zurück" to Profil. Android checks the same routes, back by "Zurück" and by the system's back. iOS checks the same routes with the native back. Screen readers hear which web tab is selected (`aria-selected`, verified in the DOM).
- **Apps:** the Expo app only. The landing page's phone frames are stand-ins with the planned four tabs and stay as they are.
- **Offline:** Profil reads local SQLite only (onboarding's reading and the key summary) and adds no network call. Sign-out still asks first when something would be lost (D86): a fresh account without a passkey got "Abmelden?" with "Notfallkarte erstellen" from Profil.
- **Two devices:** no new state.
- **Table class:** none. No table, field or mutator changes.
- **Old clients:** app only, and the old addresses keep working.
- **Reverse states:** every page under Profil has a way back on every platform. Signing out returns to the sign-in screen. Deleting a fresh account from Profil removed it from the server (`auth_user` empty for its address) and returned to the start.
- **Docs:** the atlas (the `(tabs)` routes, the new `features/profile`, `features/diagnostics`, UI pieces). The sign-up's "Geschafft!" text now points to "im Profil unter „Notizbuch-Schlüssel“".

## Docs outside the repository

- `m1-screens.md`, "Meine Woche and Mein Profil" and rule 18 ("Mein Profil is a list of rows"): the tab is "Profil" in D83's slim shape, with no E-Mail row, and Diagnose and the Sync Lab are not rows on it as described.
- `m1-6-m1-10-gaps.md`, slice A, is done, except that the pill stays (the brief asked for it) and there is no Sync Lab row.

## Review

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with GPT 6.2 Sol. Sol verdict: approved.

- S1 (should): the web tabs didn't tell screen readers which tab is selected. Fixed with `role="tablist"` and `aria-selected`.
- S2 (nit): after a failed read Profil keeps the last facts it read. That is intended offline, so only the comment changed.
- S3 (design): Profil shares onboarding's read, which loads tables it doesn't need and keeps last term's Jahrgang if the app stays open offline across a term boundary. Declined here, as a follow-up: a smaller read keyed on `DeviceStatus.today`.
- S4 (nit): a stray screenshot in the commit. Removed.

Proof: the web, Android and iOS routes above on a dev instance, sign-out and deletion from Profil, `vp run check:changed` and `calder check` green.

Created with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code). Reviewed by GPT 6.2 Sol in Codex.

```
