author: junebug-junie
body:
Fixes the live-proof gap on #3463: page:lately's first two live folds were thrown away for length.

## Summary

- page:lately's first two live folds (`dry_run=false`) were rejected at 353 and 354 words, against the 350-word cap. Nothing was written.
- Every core page (juniper, origin, lately) now ends its prompt rules with the same length rule: about 280 words, at most 12 sentences, and a page over 350 is thrown away. The cap is unchanged.
- After a page is rejected for length, the next attempt that day says how long the last page was and asks for a shorter one. The sentence budget is scaled from the last page. This works in the nightly fold and in the dry-run script.
- The note only lasts while it is true. A later reject for another reason clears it, a successful fold clears it, it is ignored on another day, and a dry run never sets it.

## Outcome moved

**Live dry runs of page:lately** (read-only, nothing written, `memory_distill`, 243 sources):

| Prompt | Runs | Words per attempt (cap 350) |
|---|---|---|
| "about 280 words", no sentence budget (first commit) | 3 | run 1: 389, 435, 380, all rejected · run 2: 389 rejected, then 349 passed · run 3: 322 passed |
| "about 280 words, at most 12 sentences" (final) | 3 | 291 (12 sentences) · 303 (12) · 331 (13), each passed on attempt 1 |

- A word target alone does not hold the model to the cap: its sentences ran 21 to 27 words, and a higher target made pages longer.
- A sentence budget does hold it: all 3 final runs landed under 350 on the first try.
- The retry note was exercised with the first-commit prompt (run 2: 389 words, then 349 after the note). With the final prompt, no retry was needed.

The page text stays host-side (`~/.orion/core_pages/`, mode 600). The repo is public.

## Current architecture

- Each page wrote its own length line: juniper and origin said "At most 300 words", and lately said "about 220 words in 10 to 14 sentences".
- A rejected fold retried with the identical prompt on the next tick, up to 3 attempts a night.

## Architecture touched

- `orion/memory/pages/fold.py`: `TARGET_WORDS`, `TARGET_SENTENCES`, `length_rule()`, `retry_note()`, `with_retry_note()`.
- `services/orion-durable-runs/app/core_page_fold.py`: a per-folder, per-Denver-day retry note.
- `scripts/core_page_dry_run.py`: the same retry note between attempts.

## Files changed

- `orion/memory/pages/fold.py`: the shared length rule and the retry note.
- `orion/memory/pages/juniper.py`, `origin.py`, `lately.py`: use `length_rule()`.
- `services/orion-durable-runs/app/core_page_fold.py`: carry the note between attempts.
- `scripts/core_page_dry_run.py`: same, in the attempt loop.
- Tests:
  - `orion/memory/pages/tests/test_core_page_length.py` (new)
  - `services/orion-durable-runs/tests/test_core_page_fold.py` (2 tests)
  - `orion/memory/pages/tests/test_core_page_origin.py`

body:
## Intent

Make the window tests run hidden on the Mac, so the app stops popping up during test runs.

Context: the test files for the screens, the editor, the check screen and the speed tests (test_screens.py, test_editor_screen.py, test_check_screen.py, test_speed.py, and any other test that builds the app) open real app windows, roughly 70 tests; only two withdraw their window. The full suite runs several times per change (while a worker iterates, in the review pipeline's test step and after each fix round), so every change flashes the app on screen for many minutes. Make them run hidden or off-screen locally by default, while the Windows CI run keeps checking the real window geometry (MIN_WINDOW and the -17 px font checks).

## What Changed

- Added `capacity_egress_app/conftest.py`, a session-scoped autouse fixture that wraps `tk.Tk.__init__` and `tk.Toplevel.__init__` so each new window is set to `-alpha 0` as soon as it is created. The windows are still mapped and laid out, so the geometry checks (MIN_WINDOW, the -17 px font) measure the same real sizes. If the `-alpha` call fails, the test fails instead of the error being swallowed. The original constructors are put back when the session ends.
- Set `CAPACITY_TEST_WINDOWS: real` on the pytest step in `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, so CI turns the fixture off and runs the tests with visible windows.
- Added a line to the README's test instructions: test windows are transparent by default, and `CAPACITY_TEST_WINDOWS=real` shows them.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is test-only: a session conftest makes each Tk root and Toplevel transparent (-alpha 0) when it is created, and the CI test step sets CAPACITY_TEST_WINDOWS=real, so CI on Windows and the Mac still shows real windows and checks real geometry. The round-1 fix (no try/except around -alpha) is in place.

## Testing

I ran the four window-test files on this Mac with an observer plugin (kept in the evidence folder) that records every live app window after each test. In the default mode all 104 tests passed, and all 94 windows across 67 tests were transparent (alpha 0) while still mapped. With CAPACITY_TEST_WINDOWS=real all 104 passed with alpha 1.0, and window size, requested size, minsize and mapped state matched the default run exactly (0 differences), so MIN_WINDOW and the -17 px font checks measure the same sizes. Values other than exactly 'real' (REAL, empty, yes) stayed hidden. When Tk is made to reject -alpha, the hidden run errors out instead of quietly showing windows, and the real run is unaffected. I tried to take screenshots during the runs, but the screen was locked, so they only showed the lock screen and I discarded them; the evidence is the probe's per-window alpha and geometry data. I could not run the Windows CI job here; remote CI covers it.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product

| Local default run of the window tests on the Mac opens every app window transparent (alpha 0) and the tests pass | ✅ pass | live | pytest_hidden.log (104 passed, exit 0); windows_hidden.json: all 94 observed Tk/Toplevel windows have alpha 0.0 |
| CAPACITY_TEST_WINDOWS=real (the CI setting) shows the windows at full opacity and the tests pass | ✅ pass | live | pytest_real.log (104 passed, exit 0); windows_real.json: all 94 windows have alpha 1.0 |
| Hidden windows have the same geometry as real ones (MIN_WINDOW and -17 px font checks still measure real sizes) | ✅ pass | live | Comparison of windows_hidden.json vs windows_real.json: same window set, 0 differences in size, requested size, minsize, mapped state or wm state; test_screens geometry tests passed in both modes |

body:
Design step 7 (docs/dev/drafting-design.md §3.3), part of #4.

**What**
- `core/src/draft/pat.rs`: AutoCAD `.pat` parser (headers, families, dashes, comments, `;%UNITS=`), capped (256 KB, 256 patterns, 64 families, 16 dashes, finite numbers), never panics; our own CC0 built-ins (diagonal, cross, steel, grid, dots, brick, concrete, earth, insulation, wood, sand). No Autodesk patterns.
- `core/src/draft/hatch.rs`: generator (even-odd clipping with holes, dash phase from each line's origin, angle/scale, paper or model scale); degrades to a tint with a reason over 200k segments / closer than 0.05 mm.
- IR `Prim::Hatch`: PDF and SVG clip to the region (even-odd) and stroke the lines; DXF writes a native pattern `HATCH` (76=2) that regenerates the same lines.
- Plans and section viewports hatch each cut region whose tag has a cut hatch (`project::cut_region`, the hook for #5). Export `warnings` lists tinted hatches.
- Commands: `tag_style {hatch: {...}}`, `hatch_pattern {name, text, units?, delete?}`, `hatch_patterns {text?}` (read-only). MODEL policy, one undo step each, saved in the model (format 2).
- On screen: the `section` command returns per-tag hatch lines + paper fill; Viewport draws them.
- UI: Hatch button + editor per tag in Outliner > Tags (swatch preview, hint, pattern, colour, weight, scale, angle, paper/model size, Import .pat…).

**Tests**: `core/tests/hatches.rs` (19, incl. 1,500-case fuzz and DXF round trip), `app/tests/hatchswatch.test.ts` (7), `tools/ui-tests/hatches.mjs` (25 checks, registered in run.mjs). Full `cargo test`, clippy (no new warnings), tsc, `npm run check`, vitest, and the hatches + line-styles browser suites pass locally.

author: jaimemonster
body:
Resuelve el Reto 2 como un proceso desplegado en Cloud Run que se ejecuta solo cada día a las 00:00 (Europe/Madrid) y deja la propuesta en el Google Sheet que revisa Compras. El informe del Reto 1 enlaza al servicio.

Previsión de demanda (src/demand.py)
- Se predice el nivel por sección × categoría y se reparte a SKU. A nivel de SKU la demanda semanal es ruido: 0,79 uds de media y 62 % de semanas a cero. Dándole al método el total de categoría correcto, el sesgo cae del 44 % al 8 % sin tocar el reparto: el problema era el nivel.
- Modelo: HistGradientBoostingRegressor entrenado con las diez categorías a la vez, lo que permite estimar la estacionalidad con diez veces más datos.
- El método se elige por backtesting entre cuatro candidatos (12 cortes, origen móvil). Gana con MAE 6,02 y desvío 24,9 %, frente a 6,36 y 37,9 % de la media móvil. Prophet se probó en cinco configuraciones: su mejor versión da 14,69 y 74,4 %.
- El error se mide en valor absoluto. Con signo, +103 % en un corte y −62 % en otro se cancelaban y el método parecía bueno.

Calidad del dato (src/clean.py)
- Se reconstruye el stock semanal caminando hacia atrás desde la foto de cierre, contando los regalos a influencers como salida de almacén. Permite distinguir una semana sin ventas por falta de demanda de una por rotura: afecta al 4,9 % de las semanas sin venta, en 45 SKUs.

Reposición (src/replenishment.py)
- necesidad = demanda(14 sem) − stock − compras que llegan dentro del horizonte. Las compras vencidas sin confirmar no cuentan, igual que en el Reto 1.
- El stock parado se detecta por ventas observadas, no por demanda prevista: al repartir el total de una categoría, hasta un producto muerto recibe una brizna de previsión. Recupera 41 SKUs con 19.276 € inmovilizados.
- El entregable se reduce a cuatro pestañas y once columnas, con glosario.

Servicio (service/)
- FastAPI con cinco páginas: propuesta filtrable, cómo funciona, esquema de producción, decisiones y el histórico de ejecuciones.
- Escribe en Sheets sin ninguna clave descargada: en Cloud Run corre como su cuenta de servicio y en local se impersona. La organización prohíbe descargar claves y la solución correcta es no necesitarlas.
- La página de decisiones se genera desde docs/decisiones.md, no a mano.

Infraestructura
- Dockerfile con versiones fijadas: el contenedor corre Python 3.11 y el entorno local 3.9, y sin fijarlas el despliegue fallaba por una incompatibilidad entre numpy y scikit-learn que no se reproducía en local.
- .github/workflows/desplegar.yml queda escrito pero SIN activar: el disparo por push está comentado porque el proveedor de Workload Identity todavía no existe.
- El informe del Reto 1 deja de estar en .gitignore: es el entregable que se reparte y lleva dentro el enlace al servicio.

body:
Replace Dagger with ServiceLoader-discovered application factories and utility services. CLI parsers retain fresh command instances; desktop windows retain independent state, lazy updates, and explicit executor/plugin cleanup. Missing or ambiguous single-provider registrations fail with service/provider diagnostics.

`ApplicationPaths` and `UserConfiguration` are replaceable interfaces backed by `SystemApplicationPaths` and `FileUserConfiguration`. Translations accept scoped configuration/paths, and the updater discovers `ReleaseSource`. Providers expose public no-argument constructors and explicit dependency constructors. Explicit file configuration construction now uses `FileUserConfiguration(path)`.

Remove injection annotations/processors, generated-code exclusions, runtime packaging expectations, and obsolete licenses. Packaging checks verify application factory registrations. The device-dialog E2E test waits for asynchronous save completion before checking dialog removal. The native plate-reorder test moves gradually and waits for the target drag-over event before releasing; its focused Windows check passed.

## Validation

Passed locally on Windows with Java 21 and matching master API source snapshots/local BOM:
- All application unit tests and `basicChecks`, including SpotBugs and workflow tests.
- All `:util:integrationTest` tests, including packaged service registration checks.

CI passed on the single squashed commit. Earlier revisions exposed a UI synchronization race (fixed here) and intermittent build-plugin dependency downloads; successful local checks apply to the unchanged squashed tree.

## CI runtime

Cap each runner job at 20 minutes or less. Run the CAD matrix on PR updates and master pushes, with manual dispatch for branch builds. Ubuntu jobs share cached package downloads and install the pinned slicer and desktop dependencies in one APT transaction. Gradle reuses cached build outputs and keeps checking changing snapshots. Native test results are excluded from the Gradle build cache.

Local verification passed with the master API composite using `spotlessKotlinGradleCheck spotlessWebAndDocsCheck :util:test :gui:compileE2eTestJava --build-cache`. Bash syntax and `git diff --check` also passed. Hosted timings depend on runner availability and cache state.

author: gtguerreiro-max
body:
Fixes #602.

## Problem

`FindRecompiledModule` compares the normalized path of a module being loaded with the registered paths, which are relative to `game:`. `NormalizeGuestPath` strips `game:\`, but not `\Device\Harddisk0\Partition1`, the partition that `game:` and `d:` link to. A title that loads a module through that partition (From Dust loads all of its DLLs as `\Device\Harddisk0\Partition1\x.xex`) matched no registered module and ran it without its recompiled code.

## Change

- The game partition's path is now a public constant, `rex::filesystem::kGamePartitionPath` in `rex/filesystem/mount.h`, which `FileSystem` mounts and links as before.
- `FindRecompiledModule` strips that partition from the normalized path before comparing, so `\Device\Harddisk0\Partition1\x.xex` finds the module registered as `x.xex`, as `game:\x.xex` does.
- The manifest reference says that `guest_path` is compared without the partition too.
- A cross-module test loads the importer through the partition path and calls its recompiled function. Without the change it fails at the lookup of that function.

## Testing

- On `development` (115171b4), with clang 20 (`win-amd64`), unit and cross-module test binaries rebuilt: `ctest` 2208 of 2213 pass, with the new test passing. The 5 that fail are the "base memory module" cross-module allocation tests, which fail the same way on plain `development` in this Windows build.
- Our From Dust port has carried an equivalent lookup on v0.11.0, where its DLLs (`GalileoKernel.xex`, `GalileoTexture.xex`, ...) load with their recompiled code.

author: tc-wilson
body:
## Summary

Crucible records tool metrics (mpstat CPU, sar-net, procstat, ...) continuously
across a run, but a benchmark is only executing inside its *periods*
(`run → iterations → samples → periods`). The idle gaps between periods carry no
benchmark load, so averaging a metric over a whole run span dilutes real
busy-time utilization with idle time and reports an inaccurate figure (e.g. CPU
usage looks lower than it actually was).

Previously the review agent's `cdm_api_request`/`cdm_api_requests` tools were
thin passthroughs; correct time-windowing was LLM-driven. This PR makes it a
code-enforced invariant, per the project's "LLM decides intent; code enforces
invariants" and "guardrails at every LLM/infrastructure boundary" principles.

## Changes

Two layers so reported metrics exclude inter-period idle time:

- **Guardrail** (`validate_cdm_metric_data_request`): rejects unbounded
  `POST /api/v1/metric-data` queries. A run-scoped query must carry a `period`
  id or a `begin`/`end` window; otherwise it is refused before the HTTP request
  is issued. Wired into `cdm_api_request` after the existing host/port/path
  validation, so both the singular and batched paths are covered.

- **Deterministic tool** (`get_run_metric_by_period`): resolves each sample's
  primary period in code (`iterations → samples → primary-period-id →
  periods/range`) and queries `metric-data` bounded to that period, returning
  period-bounded per-sample values plus mean/min/max/stddev. The LLM supplies
  only `source`/`type`/`breakout`, never the time math.

Also:
- Registered the tool in the review agent's crucible-only scoping set and the
  tool-audit policy (read-only).
- Documented it in the CDM skill (`skills/crucible/cdm-query-guide.md`) and API
  reference (`docs/cdm-api-reference.md`) as the preferred path for CPU and
  other continuously-sampled tool metrics.
- Added regression tests for the validator, aggregation helpers, and the
  deterministic query flow (mocked via `httpx.MockTransport`).
- Updated the existing CDM HTTP error-passthrough test to scope its
  `metric-data` probe to a period so it still reaches the server.

## Testing

- `test_review_cdm_period_scope.py` (28), `test_review_cdm_http.py`,
  `test_tool_scoping.py`, `test_review_prompt_guidance.py`: all pass.
- `test_tool_audit_policy.py` (tool-registration completeness): pass.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean.

## Notes

Code can't verify that a supplied `begin`/`end` is the *correct* period range
without extra round-trips, so a hand-constructed window that itself spans
multiple periods would still pass the raw-query guardrail. The guardrail is the
floor; `get_run_metric_by_period` is the fully-deterministic path that
eliminates that gap for CPU/tool metrics.

Closes #1390

author: code19m
body:
The branch of `finish` that completes the task of `RunTask` repeated
`completeWaiting` line for line. It differed in one point: it set
`completedDirectly` inside the transaction, before the commit was known.

`completeWaiting` now returns the tasks that it completed, and none if
its transaction did not commit. `finish` sets `completedDirectly` from
that, so the flag says what its comment says: the completion is
recorded.

`RunTask` reads the flag only if the task is gone afterwards. Its value
can differ only when every try to complete failed: a try whose commit
failed left it set, and it is false now.

author: fikrifirat
lbarzanti
body:
An NVIDIA card gets used automatically today; on an AMD machine the clips were encoded on the CPU and the captions were made on the CPU too. This makes the AMD path first-class, so both vendors use the GPU.

**What changed**

- **Encoding** — the encoder is probed once at startup (`h264_amf` → `h264_nvenc` → `libx264`) instead of hardcoding `libx264`.
- **Captions** — on an AMD-only machine the script restarts itself under [ZLUDA](https://github.com/vosen/ZLUDA) so CTranslate2 sees the Radeon as a CUDA device. On NVIDIA nothing changes.
- **New flags** — `--encoder {auto,amf,nvenc,x264}` and `--cpu-only`.
- **`setup_zluda.py`** (new) — installs ZLUDA into `./zluda`, checks the HIP SDK, then verifies the whole chain: ZLUDA's own `cuda_check` plus a probe that Whisper really sees the device. `--check` reports without downloading. It also explains what to do on cards the official HIP SDK doesn't cover (RX 6000 cards are `gfx1032`, which needs a nightly ROCm SDK).
- **README** — short "Using your GPU" section covering both vendors.
- **`.gitignore`** — `venv/`, `zluda/` (the latter is an 86 MB download, not source).

**Why a restart under ZLUDA**

CTranslate2 only speaks CUDA and ZLUDA must be loaded *before* the process starts to translate those calls. So `main()` relaunches the script through `zluda.exe` when it finds an AMD-only machine, a ZLUDA install and a HIP SDK. If any of the three is missing it logs a single line and captions on the CPU exactly as before.

**Tested**

On a Radeon RX 6600 XT (gfx1032), Windows 11, on a live Twitch stream:

- `encoder: h264_amf (GPU)` and `whisper: loading 'small' on cuda (AMD GPU via ZLUDA)`
- 30 s clip: 1080x1920, video stream tagged `encoder=Lavc63.1.102 h264_amf`, word-by-word captions burned in
- ~94% GPU compute utilisation while Whisper ran
- `--cpu-only` still produces the same clip with `libx264` and CPU captions
- no new Python dependencies: ZLUDA is a separate download, the HIP SDK is a driver-level prerequisite

**Caveats**

- The current ZLUDA build panics in its thread-local destructors while unloading (exit code 127, *after* all the work is done). `os._exit(0)` when `ZLUDA_RUNNING` is set skips that teardown; without the marker nothing changes.
- ZLUDA compiles kernels on first use, so the first clip is slow and the following ones are quick (36 s → 4 s for the same audio here).
- ZLUDA is a pre-release. If the chain breaks, the clipper falls back to CPU captions instead of failing.

author: aitrawog
body:
## Summary

**Successor to #1115, which the validator auto-closed at five rounds.** That PR's last finding was that R3's *"three hunks"* no longer matched the diff — because the same round's fixes added a fourth. **The hunk count is now stated as four, and it is the count `git diff | grep -c '^@@'` produces on this head**, not the count from the round before.

**`PROGRAM/design-implementation.md` is the objective's single durable record of package state — and on `main` it was 551 lines: the 2026-11-13 opening state, with no rule learned since.** This lands the **4063-line** record a later session resumes from.

**The six deleted lines are stale, measured rather than assumed:**

```console
$ git diff origin/main HEAD -- PROGRAM/design-implementation.md | grep -E '^-' | grep -v '^---'
| programme state | `planned` — goal armed 2026-11-13; no package started |
| agents spawned | 0 |
| round budget | 600 rounds, sized to the work (44 packages, roughly 150 PR legs across the five la… |
| last measurement | 2026-11-13 (§7) |
| P01 | Kind bodies into their plugins (3 units left: `candy`, `android`, `deploy`) | ...
| P26 | Pipeline stages, attempts and asks | 2.21, 2.22, 2.23 | plugin-pipeline > spec | ...
```

**Every one is stale, and stale in the direction that matters**: a state block claiming no package had started, and two package rows that have since landed. **A ledger whose opening page is wrong is worse than no ledger, because a later session reads it first.**

## What it carries now

| | |
|---|---|
| sections | **94** |
| rules | **1–27** — each derived from a measured failure |
| the census | the four groups below, which close on the row count |
| packages | **44** (`P00`-`P43`) |
| package table rows | **48** — four packages carry a **second** row recording their landing |
| rows still reading `planned` | **42**, and 42 + 2 moved = the 44 packages |

**The census, with its arithmetic shown — the four groups must sum to the measured rows:**

```console
$ git show origin/main:TODO.md | grep -cE '^\| [0-9]+\.[0-9]+ \|'
147
```

Of those, **125 are the rows the census measured** and **22 it did not**. **This document does not partition the 22**: sections 0 and 1 hold 6 of them, and the remaining 16 lie inside sections 2–14 — the census's scope was row-by-row, not section-by-section, so asserting "the rest are sections 0–1" would be a claim its data does not support. **An earlier draft of this body did assert exactly that, and it was wrong**: 147 − 6 = 141 rows sit in sections 2–14, so 125 cannot be "sections 2–14" either. The 125 divides as:

| group | count |
|---|---|
| already `done` | **9** |
| `stale`, corrected | **20** |
| `stale`, reproducing unchanged | **3** (2.2, 2.5, 2.8) |
| genuinely `open` | **93** |
| **total** | **125** |

**3.24 is a fourth reproducing row whose CLAIM reproduces while its EVIDENCE was wrong** — it moves to `corrected` when `audit-protocol`'s row lands, and is listed apart here rather than folded into a count it would make wrong.

## What the package rows honestly carry

**`state` is a work list, not a verdict.** Measured: of the **44** packages, **42 package rows still read `planned`** — the file holds **48** rows because `P01` and `P26` carry a **second** row recording their landing, and so do `P05` and `P07` — whose second rows are dated-section landing records, not package-row state changes — because those packages have not been dispatched. **The evidence for what HAS landed lives in the dated sections** — §1i records P05 merged, §1q P06's first two legs, §2h P09, §2m P07's four of six, and the P26 row records unit 1. Only P01 and P26 have state that moved off `planned`.

**Consolidating those section verdicts into the 42 cells is real work that this PR does not do**, and the ledger says so in its own words, so that a later reader cannot mistake an un-dispatched package for an unmeasured one.


### This round: five findings, and they were one sentence written four times

The previous round raised five, and **the first four were the same defect**: a summary sentence that restates a table, written from memory instead of re-derived.

| finding | the claim | what the measurement says |
|---|---|---|
| line count | a total the diff did not produce | **4063** — `+3518 −6` from a 551-line base |
| package state | "the four whose state moved off `planned`" beside "42 still read `planned`" | **four carry a second row; only `P01` and `P26` moved off it.** Four moved would leave 40, not 42. |
| census partition | "125 are the measured rows (sections 2–14)" | **147 − 6 = 141 sit in 2–14**, so 125 cannot be "sections 2–14"; and the 22 unmeasured are **not** "sections 0–1" — 6 are, and 16 lie inside 2–14 |
| prose in a fence | — | a bold paragraph rendered as monospace; the fence now closes after `box validate` |

**The fifth is the RCA, and the missed control is the same one every time**: nothing re-derives a sentence that restates a table. **The fix is not to write more carefully — it is to delete the restatement**, which is why the partition sentence now states the pair it measured and **declines to partition the 22**, rather than asserting a composition the census's row-by-row scope never produced.

## Head

```console
$ git rev-parse HEAD
f736d294d6ea0ec857ad80888f4d4980e5892617
```

## How tested

**This diff touches two `PROGRAM/*.md` files and nothing else, so its owning class is `documentation-only` — the non-runtime standards, not a bed and not the pin gate.** All of them, on the committed tree:

```console
$ bash scripts/design-check.sh; echo $?
design-check: all controls pass
0
```

```console
$ bash scripts/design-consistency.sh; echo $?
consistency: tables, table shape, word lists, rule tags, ids and § references, vocabulary, grammar — all agree
0
```

```console
$ node scripts/check-harness-config.mjs --self-test; echo $?
check-harness-config --self-test: OK (30/35 arms live)
0
```

```console
$ ./charly/bin/charly box validate; echo $?
charly box validate: OK — checked 553 candies, 188 boxes, 6 distros, 7 builders; 0 warnings, 0 errors
0
```

**That 553 is a SESSION-WORKTREE count** — the ledger's own §1b records 610 from a full clone, and **the two numbers are not comparable**: `charly box validate` walks the submodules that are CHECKED OUT. This body states the tree it ran on because a `box validate` figure without one is not a measurement.

**Two notes on the gates, both learned the hard way in this session:**

- **`design-check`'s `design-pintag` step failed on the first run with THREE findings about `layer-openclaw`, `layer-strata` and `charly` — all "a CHANGELOG commit with no parent", all caused by materializing those submodules with `--depth 1`.** A shallow commit has no parent, so the tag map cannot be built and the gate reports a phantom defect in repos it never examined. **`git fetch --unshallow` on each fixed all three, and the gate then passed.** That is `AGENTS.md` Part II #2's warning in its exact words: *"`--depth 1` is NOT a substitute, because a shallow clone answers 'not an ancestor' for a healthy pin."*
- **`charly task verify` is not this change's gate**, and its transcript in this worktree prints `charly.yml` as that branch has it — which is *before* `#1117` rewords the branch-audit step. Running it here would paste a description another PR is changing, so it is deliberately not the evidence for a docs diff.

## Rulebook compliance

- **R0** — `/charly-internals:agents` (the session ledger) and `/charly-build:docs` loaded.
- **R1** — five anomalies, each RCA'd: the durable record was 87% absent from `main`; the opening table contradicted the body; the census arithmetic did not close; three findings sat under banned framings; and two irreconcilable `box validate` counts lived in one file. **Missed control:** nothing ever asserted that the ledger on `main` matches the ledger a session writes, so six weeks of rules lived only in closed branches.
- **R2** — one ledger, at the path the objec

author: jejjohnson
body:
Today (bug): every PR on vardax fails its fast tests, because CI now resolves jax 0.12.1 (released 18 Nov 2026, after `main`'s last green run on jax 0.12.0.1) and two tests fail on it: `test_gradient_nonzero_outside_box` and `test_basis_path_matches_pre_pr_reference`. vardax commits no `uv.lock`, so `main` fails the same way.

After this PR: both pass on jax 0.12.0.1 and 0.12.1.

- **`SoftBoundedForward` lost its gradient far outside the box.** It wrote the saturation as b + b u / (1 + u). The quotient rule on u / (1 + u) subtracts two nearly equal float32 terms, so at x = −1e9 the gradient came out as 7.1e-16 instead of 1e-16 on jax 0.12.0.1, and exactly 0 on jax 0.12.1. The same map written 2b − b / (1 + u) differentiates to the single term b / (1 + u)², with nothing to cancel. Its values differ from the old form's by at most 9.5e-7.
- **The basis-path test pinned a float32 BFGS iterate.** With the same data and code, jax 0.12.1's numeric changes (new `log` kernels, fused multiply-add in `lax.polynomial`, among others in its changelog) move the iterate by 6.2e-5 against a 1e-5 tolerance. The result is still 1.1e-4 from the float64 optimum, inside the 0.017 bound the same file derives from BFGS's stopping tolerance. The test now checks against that closed form and bound, which moved into a helper shared with the slow test.

## Reproduction on main

Commit `b9bcfcf`, jax 0.12.1: `pytest -k "test_basis_path_matches_pre_pr_reference or test_gradient_nonzero_outside_box"` gives 2 failed; with jax and jaxlib pinned to 0.12.0.1, 2 passed. Between `main`'s green CI run (44156355953) and the failing one on #299 (44367921946), the resolved packages differ only in jax and jaxlib (0.12.0.1 to 0.12.1) and five tooling packages.

## Evidence

| | jax 0.12.0.1 | jax 0.12.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Old form's gradient at x = −1e9 | 7.1e-16 | 0 |
| New form's gradient at x = −1e9 | 1.0e-16 | 1.0e-16 |
| Basis path, distance from the float64 optimum | 2.3e-6 | 1.1e-4 (bound 0.017) |

**Not shown:** GPU and macOS runs; CI's macOS job covers the latter.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/test_parameterization.py tests/test_utils/test_forward.py` (slow tests included) passed on head under jax 0.12.0.1 and 0.12.1, 23 of 23 each.
- `ruff format --check .`, `ruff check --no-fix .` and `ty check src/vardax` pass.

## Not in this change

- A `uv.lock` or a jax upper bound: the stack resolves fresh on purpose, and this fixes the code rather than freezing jax.

#299 and #300 fail the same two tests. GitHub does not allow their stack's base to change, so once this merges, `main` is merged into their branches to rerun their checks with the fix.

```ts
  const window = new BrowserWindow({
    icon,
    show: false,
    backgroundThrottling: false,
```
This is the wrong place to initialize `backgroundThrottling`. That option is in `webPreferences`.

Ref: https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/browser-window

After setting it in `webPreferences`, we can remove `window.webContents.backgroundThrottling = false`.

Alternatively, we can skip defining `backgroundThrottling` in `webPreferences` and keep `window.webContents.backgroundThrottling = false`.

author: moodiness
body:
A request whose forwarded headers do not tell who its client is no longer counts as on the local network: one that comes through a reverse proxy missing from **Known proxies**, and one from a known proxy whose headers disagree or cannot be read. System › Health still names the address to add, and now says what its requests count as until then.

**The local network** (`internal/forwarded`, `InLocalNetwork`):
- **A connection that is not from a known proxy:** a request that carries `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP` or `Forwarded` is not local, whatever the connection's address. Its client stays the connection's address, for the limit of failed sign-ins and for devices. Without these headers, the connection's address decides, as before.
- **A connection from a known proxy, headers that cannot both be the proxy's:** when `X-Forwarded-For` names a client and `X-Real-IP` names another address that is not a known proxy, the request is the proxy's own, and not local. A proxy passes on the header it does not set as its client wrote it, and nothing tells which one it sets.
- **A connection from a known proxy, a header that cannot be read:** an entry of `X-Forwarded-For` that is no address makes the request the proxy's own, as before, and it is no longer local. The same holds for an `X-Real-IP` alone that is no address, and for a request that names its client in `Forwarded` alone, which Polyfin does not read, as DLNA already judges it.
- **Read as before:** a proxy that appends to `X-Forwarded-For`, with or without an `X-Real-IP` naming the same client or a known proxy; several known proxies in a row; `X-Real-IP` alone; addresses with a port, in brackets, IPv4-mapped or with a zone.
- No new setting, and no caller changed. What reads the local network follows by itself: sign-in and requests of users who may not connect from outside it (Jellyfin apps, the admin app, the identity provider, two-step sign-in, Silo's apps), `/Users/Public`, password reset PINs, `/System/Endpoint` and the qualities offered outside the local network.

**Texts** (`internal/admin/healthproblems.go`, `web/src/i18n`, six languages):
- **The Health warning** names the address as before, then says that requests through it count as coming from outside the local network, that users who may only connect from the local network are refused through it, and that its clients share one limit of failed sign-ins.
- **The note under a user's remote access switch**, shown while Health sees such a proxy, said everyone through it looked local. It now says the user is refused through it.
- **The help of Known proxies** said the headers of any other address are ignored. It now says they name no client, and that a request carrying them counts as outside the local network.

**Docs:**
- `docs/reverse-proxy.md`: what an unlisted proxy's requests count as, the rule for a known proxy whose headers disagree or cannot be read, and that the proxy should set the header it names the client in, or both.
- `docs/health.md`, `docs/user-limits.md`, `docs/transcoding.md`, `docs/metrics-and-api-keys.md`, `docs/jellyfin-api.md`: the sentences that said clients behind an unlisted proxy look local.

**Tests:**
- **`TestClientAndLocalNetworkBehindProxies`:** a table of connection, known proxies and headers, giving the client and whether it is local. An unlisted local address with each of the three headers is not local, and is without them. A known proxy names its client through `X-Forwarded-For`, a chain, or `X-Real-IP` alone. Headers that disagree or cannot be read give the proxy's own address, not local.
- **`TestOnlyLocalConnectionsCountAsLocal`:** without forwarded headers only loopback, private and link-local connections are local, in no IPv6 form of a public or translated address. With any of the three headers, none is.
- **`TestRequestsThroughAnUnlistedProxyAreOutsideTheLocalNetwork`:** through the Jellyfin handlers, from an unlisted proxy on a private address, a user without remote access gets 403 and a forgotten password makes no PIN, whichever header the proxy sends. The same address without them signs in and gets a PIN.
- **`TestAClientsOwnForwardedForNamesNoClientBehindAKnownProxy`:** behind a known proxy that sets `X-Real-IP` alone, an `X-Forwarded-For` the client wrote does not make the request local (403, no PIN), and wrong passwords sent with a new `X-Forwarded-For` each time meet the limit of failed sign-ins at the third.
- **Existing tests that held the earlier rule, changed:** `TestResolve` (the row where `X-Forwarded-For` won over another `X-Real-IP`), `TestLocalNetworkBehindAKnownProxy` (`/System/Endpoint` and PINs behind an unknown proxy) and `TestRemoteAccess` (its last lines, where the internet looked local behind an unknown proxy).
- **Without the fix:** each fails, checked by undoing its lines.

**Shots:** System › Health with the warning, a user's page with the note, and the help of Known proxies, at 1440 and 390 px, in English and French.

**Upgrading:** behind a reverse proxy that is not listed under **Known proxies**, in **Settings › Security**, every request now counts as coming from outside the local network. Until the proxy is listed:
- users who may not connect from outside the local network can no longer sign in or play through it, from the local network either;
- a forgotten password asked through it makes no PIN;
- Jellyfin apps that reach the server through it are told they are outside the local network (`/System/Endpoint`): an app that keeps a quality for the internet applies it, and **Several qualities when converting** set to **Outside the local network** applies to them;
- **System › Health** names the address to add.

An administrator whose own account may only connect from the local network, and who reaches Polyfin through such a proxy alone, opens Polyfin at its own address and port once to add the proxy. A known proxy that sends both `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-IP` must name the same client in both, as proxies that set both do.

**Checks:** gofmt, `go vet ./...` and the Windows build pass. So do the race tests of `internal/forwarded`, `internal/admin`, `internal/silo` and `internal/jellyfin` (whole, in two halves), the `paralleltest` and `tparallel` lint on the changed test lines, the web typecheck, format check, i18n check and French spacing, and the docs checks.

body:
Advances: A4, step 5e. It brings into the corpus audit the check of `repeated` that the `interfaces` tests make only with doubles. The session that reviews the work asked for it after #138.

## What

- **CORPUS-055:** when the gate `repeatability` ran in a case's audit (its status in the predicate is `run`), the evidence carries `repeated` with `runs` 2, the default policy, and `consistent` true. When it did not run, there is no `repeated`. Whether it ran is read from the status of `repeatability`, which is what decides `repeated` (ADR-0069), and not from another gate of the state.
- **`test_corpus_audit.py`** reads `repeated` from the evidence it already reads back.

## Result

I ran it here on the ten cases with podman and the clones: 10 passed in 758 s. All ten cases reach `verifying`, and their evidence carries `repeated` with `{"runs": 2, "consistent": true}`. No case of the corpus stops before `verifying`, so the branch "with no `repeated`" is not exercised by the corpus. The `interfaces` test covers it (#136).

The `corpus` job of this PR runs the same test in CI.

## The check can fail

I changed the expectation to `runs` 3 and ran a single case. `python-semver/replace-keeps-the-constructor-error` failed in 39 s with `{'runs': 2} != {'runs': 3}`. I restored the expectation and the case passed again. The full corpus was not run a second time.

Gates: `uv run python -m tools.gates` passes.

author: dbeasty
body:
## What

- **One game at a time.** The Moves history held the whole match, so earlier deals/hands in the series stayed above the current one. Each logged move now carries its round (`Move.Round`). The server starts a seat's log again when a new round begins, and the client (`joinMoveLog`) keeps only the newest round's lines. Games without rounds are unchanged.
- **Between rounds** the round that just ended stays in view. Seats pressing "continue" during the pause still count as part of that round; the next round begins with the first move after play resumes (`logMarkFor`).
- **Start/end notes**: `moves.roundBegins` / `moves.roundEnds` ("Hand 2 begins" / "Hand 2 is over", in the game's own word for a round), and `moves.gameBegins` / `moves.gameEnds` for games without rounds. They have no player and are shown in italics. Wording is in all 24 locales, and `go generate ./internal/gamemcp` has been re-run.
- **Player filter**: when the list is open, a row of chips (All, then each player, yours marked) shows only one player's moves, keeping the notes for context.

## Testing

- `ZOLIK_TEST_DB_ENGINE=kdb go test ./internal/match ./internal/module ./internal/gamemcp`: pass. New tests: `TestLiveLogStartsAgainEachRound`, `TestLiveLogNotesRoundBeginAndEnd`, `TestLogMarkKeepsTheEndedRoundThroughThePause`.

## Known gap

Siete y Medio has no `NarrateEvent`, so its history shows only these notes and no player moves. Not addressed here.

## Summary

Adds the frontend's security scans and its OIDC deploy pipeline: automatic publish to staging after CI passes, and production after approval. It completes SIL-220 together with the infra and backend PRs.

Closes SIL-220

## Changes

- **`security` job:** Semgrep 1.183.0 (`p/typescript`, `p/react`, `p/secrets`; ERROR fails), npm audit on the runtime dependencies (HIGH and CRITICAL fail; the 4 moderate findings in the shadcn CLI's `minimatch` are reported), and gitleaks 8.30.1 over the full history.
- **`deploy.yml`:** runs after CI succeeds on `main`, or manually. For each environment, it builds with that environment's `VITE_API_BASE_URL` and then:
  1. Syncs hashed assets with `max-age=31536000, immutable`.
  2. Uploads `index.html` with `no-cache`.
  3. Invalidates `/index.html` and `/` and waits for the invalidation.
  4. Smoke-tests the site.
- Staging runs automatically; prod waits for approval. Old assets are kept, so open tabs can still load their lazy chunks.
- OIDC only (the environment's `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`); actions are pinned by SHA.
- An unused shell variable in the e2e job was fixed (actionlint/shellcheck).
- **e2e in the official Playwright image:** the job runs `scripts/e2e-docker.sh` (the same command as locally) instead of installing Chromium and its system libraries with apt. A guard fails early if the image tag and the lockfile's `@playwright/test` version differ.
- README: CI table and a new Deployment section.

## How to test

1. This PR's CI shows `security`.
2. After merge, Deploy publishes staging and waits for approval for prod.

CI on `a748829`: [CI run 44372600471](https://github.com/victorkauan/silver-proposals-frontend/actions/runs/44372600471): quality ✅ 37s, security ✅ 35s (Semgrep, npm audit, gitleaks), e2e ✅ 1m22s, build ✅ 23s; [PR title](https://github.com/victorkauan/silver-proposals-frontend/actions/runs/44372600421) ✅.

author: meerq1
body:
Work in progress: the twelve items from the review ("what can we improve, add or fix"), and making the game snappier. This description is updated as items land.

## Done so far

**Real per-province sizes (redrawn maps, revision 3).** Each province and sea zone of Europe 1914/1936 and the World 1914/1936 records its width, measured against revision 1 on the same ground (`tools/mapwidths.ts`: both revisions rasterised on one grid). A step counts the mean of the widths of its two ends — marching, supply, reach, integration distance, loose-army threat range; fleets' voyages and estimates count the sea each zone covers. Railways are revision 1's on the same ground (the redraw had laid none on land split from a city). The World, 1936 has its Bab-el-Mandeb crossing again. Marching between capitals against revision 1: Europe 1914 +2% (was +4%), Europe 1936 +1% (+3%), World 1914 +2% (+5%), World 1936 +4% (+10%). Revision-2 saves continue with a notice.

**Occupation pace.** On a redrawn map an undefended province takes the time its ground takes (2 weeks per old province's worth), and a week's work beyond the 100 carries to the besiegers' next undefended province.

**Coalition wars.** Three planner faults fixed (detachments that left the rest too weak, armies gathering alone where a stronger enemy could reach them, a conquest that ignored a second enemy army in our land). Germany v Poland with France and Romania in, 16 seeds, 40 weeks, share of Poland taken: Auto-conquer 26% → 32%, delegated 23% → 32%; Poland alone 56% → 55% and 51% → 52%; revision 1 unchanged or better.

**AI armies at peace.** The standing army follows what is around a realm (its starting army, a share below one of its neighbours', the enemy side at war), not its treasury. Six years of Europe 1936: France 64 → 88 regiments (152 before), USSR 113 → 131 (216), Britain 27 → 35 (86).

**Money trouble told before it bites.** Orders that leave upkeep above income are flagged; a treasury running dry within three months is forecast; bankruptcy names the armies whose regiments deserted; an army that runs out of supply is reported once with why.

## Still to come in this PR
Sea-zone regrouping in operations, renderer and simulation speed (World 1914 medium zoom, Europe 1936 week cost, load, ledgers), tutorial steps, victories on the historical maps, technologies beyond 1936, cross-browser and phone checks with a steadier browser performance probe, and the before/after measurements.

body:
## Summary

Adds a minimal `vercel.json` at the repository root so the Angular SPA works correctly on Vercel.

Angular Router uses client-side routing, so deep links and page refreshes on routes such as `/login` or `/students/123` would otherwise return a 404. The rewrite below routes any unmatched request to `index.html`, letting Angular Router handle it.

```json
{
  "rewrites": [{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html" }]
}
```

Vercel serves static files from the build output first and only applies the rewrite when no file matches, so real assets are unaffected.

## Scope

- Single new file: `vercel.json`.
- No other files, dependencies, or configuration changed.
- No deploy performed by this PR.

author: ahmedabu98
body:
Follow-up to #41408.

The live view takes over the whole terminal, but pipelines keep logging to that same terminal while it's open. The Iceberg CDC source logs at INFO on every poll, so a streaming `CHANGES()` query buries the view under log lines within seconds.

This PR makes two changes:

* While the live view is open, the shell holds back console logging. Warnings and errors print once the view closes, and the closing line says how many other messages were hidden, for example "Live view closed after 3 rows in 00:32. Hid 9 log messages while it was open."
* The Iceberg CDC source logs its per-poll messages at DEBUG instead of INFO: "Skipping scan: nothing new since last poll", "Sitting idle... Bumping watermark", and the full "Collected snapshots" dump. "Emitted snapshot" stays at INFO.

I tried it by streaming `CHANGES()` from an Iceberg table in a real terminal while another process committed rows. No log lines landed on the view, and the new rows showed up within two seconds.

author: perfecto25
body:
Closes #1321.

## Summary

A lazily opened 17000² PSD now reaches its settled fit-to-screen picture in **24 % of the eager open's time** (M12: 9433 ms eager; master 3837 ms → **2263 ms**). The issue's target was 25 %.

- **Coarse tiles fold from finer ones** (`pictura-render/src/tile_build.rs`, new). A missing tile with current finer tiles under it is folded from them one level at a time; only the parts with no finer tile read level 0. The tile worker gets a `TilePyramid::snapshot` taken with its ticket, lands the levels it folded through, and `build_now` uses the same builder. The Navigator/Histogram coarsest level no longer runs a second level-0 pass.
- **Fresh tile rows build as one strip.** After the folding, gdb sampling showed one worker in serial `decode_packbits` with the rayon pool idle. A fit tile read a 4096-wide footprint, but the merged preview decodes 17000-wide bands into a 32 MiB LRU, so each band was decoded about four times. Adjacent fresh tiles of one row now build from one read, and `MergedPreview::region` decodes a band's channels side by side.
- **`Region::halved` interior fast path**, same bytes.

Every tile stays byte-identical to the direct build (`compositing/tile-pyramid`).

## Measurements

M12 (`scripts/profile-tools.py --scenarios M12 --peak`), master `bb911b80` vs this branch built side by side, runs alternated, medians of three, load average ~10 from other work:

| Build | Total | Of eager | Peak | RSS after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| master | 3837 ms | 41 % | 647 MiB | 588 MiB |
| this branch | 2263 ms | 24 % | 724 MiB | 677 MiB |

App CPU time over the open: 11.0 → 5.5 s.

**Memory trade-off (owner decision).** Peak is 77 MiB above master's. It is not live data: the strip's ~31 MiB chunk buffers sit just under glibc's largest mmap threshold, so the thread arenas keep them after they are freed (`MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` removes the difference). A tile job now ends with `eviction::trim` (`malloc_trim`), which lowers the RSS after the open but not the peak. Follow-up: #1423. Band-tall chunks kept master's peak but took 4.4 s.

## OpenSpec

`coarse-tile-folding`, archived. New capability `compositing/coarse-tile-folding`. Scenarios `ctf_fold_cached`, `ctf_partial`, `ctf_same_job`, `ctf_stale`, `ctf_strip`, `ctf_halve` (render) and `ctf_worker` (app) have tests.

## Test status

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean; self-test 467 passed, 0 failed.
- `verify-fast` with `TMPDIR` under the repo: the control-socket suites, `pictura-mcp` and `core::mcp_control_server` failed on socket paths over 108 characters. Re-run with the default `TMPDIR`, they pass.
- Still failing, and failing the same way on master `bb911b80` built on this host: `tst_present_cache::frameBoundedPaintMatchesCpu(gpu)` and `tst_large_document::cancellingATransformEndsIt`.

## Reviewer checklist (manual test-plan rows)

- [ ] `ctf_m12`: M12 at 17000² on an idle machine, master vs this branch (`profile-tools.py --scenarios M12 --peak --fixture-dir <dir>`); expect about 24 % of 9433 ms and a peak about 75 MiB above master's.

body:
Fixes #2382.

## lvcharts.com
`lvcharts.com` was the docs site until 2023. Commit `93db2e379` ("update site url") moved the docs to `livecharts.dev`, but **16 links in 4 files** still pointed to the old domain, which now serves spam:

| File | Links |
|---|---|
| `docs/overview/1.5.mappers.md` | 9 (one also hard-coded version `2.0.0-beta.710`) |
| `docs/samples/lines/zoom/template.md` | 4 |
| `docs/cartesianChart/axes.md` | 2 |
| `docs/samples/events/cartesian/template.md` | 1 |

They now point to `livecharts.dev`, with the same paths. Rendered, that was 120 links, one copy per platform. The README link was already fixed on master by a contributor's commit (`99095840d`). `release/v2.2.x` still has it, so the backport has to cover the README too.

**Guard:** a new `Docs links` workflow fails if `docs/**` or `README.md` links to `lvcharts.com` again. It has to be its own workflow, because the main workflow only runs on code paths.

## Other broken links found by building the docs
I built the docs with docr (896 articles) and checked every `livecharts.dev` link against the generated pages and the types in `src/`:
- **API links to types that lost their generic parameter:** `IChartElement-1`, `ICartesianSeries-1`, `IPolarSeries-1`, `IChartLegend-1` and `IChartTooltip-1` now link to the non-generic types.
- **Renamed type:** `IAnimatable` now links to `Animatable`.
- **Series property pages:** they linked their API page as `<Title>Properties-3`, e.g. `StepLineSeriesProperties-3`. `shared/series.md` now strips "properties" from the title. It also maps the three pages whose title differs from the type:
  - Candle Sticks → `CandlesticksSeries`
  - Stacked (Step) Line → `Stacked(Step)AreaSeries`
- **Polar chart overview:** it linked the polar line series page under `CartesianChart.`; it now uses `PolarChart.`.

After the fix, the rebuilt docs have **no** `lvcharts.com` links and **no** API links to missing types. I spot-checked the corrected links against the live site (`livecharts.dev`, version 2.0.4), and all ten return 200.

**Not in this PR:** five "related articles" links that come from docr's `config/settings.json` (a separate repo) and point to pages that don't exist:
- `CartesianChart.Row Series properties`
- `CartesianChart.Scatter Series`
- `PolarChart.Polar line series properties`
- `TreemapChart.Treemap chart control`
- `TreemapChart.Treemap series properties`

author: nlundee
body:
## What and why

The portal rework needs data the API did not give. This adds it, generic for any service and engine:

- **Dataset documents** (`GET /tenants/{tenant}/datasets/{id}/documents`): `total` always present (`totalExact` false for an estimate), `query` and `sort`/`order` where the engine declares them in `listing` (pgvector declares none; Typesense searches titles and sorts by the fields a dataset names in `options.sortFields`), `status=indexed|failed|pending` with `statusCounts` (failures merged from the latest run of every pipeline), and `chunkCount` per document on Typesense. `GET .../documents/{doc}?chunks=from-to` reads up to 50 chunks in order.
- **Models** (`GET /models`): `contextWindow`, `releaseDate` (catalogue field and discovery `releaseDates`), `recommended` from the new setting `models.recommended` (falls back to `services.defaultModel`), and `available`. Models the tenant's block policy refuses or holds for approval are now left out; `?all=true` lists them with `available: false` and `reason`. The portal's building block detail, usage and run pages and the admin MCP `list_models` read `?all=true`, so they still show those models' facts and names; `list_models` shows `available` and `reason`.
- **Service tabs**: `latency` (p50/p95) per service in the usage report; `GET /tenants/{tenant}/service-failures` with failure causes per service since the start of today in Norway; `offset` and `q` on `GET /tenants/{tenant}/tasks`; `GET /tenants/{tenant}/services/{service}/shared-with`; `GET /tenants/{tenant}/services/{id}/draft/checks` runs the publish checks on the saved draft without publishing and without model calls. on_publish hooks are not run; `hooksSkipped: true` says when the organisation has enabled ones that could still refuse.

OpenAPI and docs/api are updated for every route.

## Risk

Sensitive: touches tenancy and rights on read routes.

- Failed and pending documents are shown only for the tenant's own datasets, never a shared dataset's runs.
- Task search matches question text only for callers with `manage-services`, and never an erased run's question.
- `shared-with` is readable by any member; it lists key names and prefixes, never secrets, and leaves out revoked and expired keys.
- `/models` now hides models the block policy holds back by default. A client that listed them before must pass `?all=true`.
- Draft checks skip the `hooks` module, so a check never calls an organisation's on_publish hooks or writes their audit entry; it only reads the hook config to set `hooksSkipped`.
- Typesense is read only through the search client (`multiSearch`).
- `packages/port-knowledge` only gains optional fields; the knowledge worker, reconciler and ingest writers are untouched.

## Undo

Revert is enough. No migrations; the new setting has an empty default.

## How it was tested

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, eslint on touched files, `npm run boundaries`, `npm run atlas:build` and `npm run atlas:test`.
- Full suites: `apps/api` (2398 passed), `packages/port-knowledge`, `providers-typesense`, `port-model`, `definitions` and the portal settings screens (485 passed).

author: guanting112
body:
A GitHub release here has carried only its notes, so OpenSSF Scorecard's Signed-Releases check found no release with files and left itself out of the score ("no releases found").

`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs when a release is published:

1. `git archive` of the tag, as `httpdog-house-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz`
2. `actions/attest-build-provenance` (v4.2.2, the same pin as httpdog) attests where that archive came from
3. `gh release upload` attaches the archive and the attestation bundle, under two names with the same content, as httpdog does: `httpdog-house.sigstore.json` and `httpdog-house.intoto.jsonl`, the name Scorecard looks for to see provenance

The workflow reads by default; only its job may write (`contents`, `id-token`, `attestations`), as in httpdog, whose Token-Permissions score is 10. The files are added after publishing, so the repository's immutable releases setting has to stay off (it is); `docs/development.md` and its Traditional Chinese twin say so, and list the workflow. `CHANGELOG.md` gets a line under Unreleased with the command to verify an archive.

Checked locally: the same `git archive` on `v0.1.2` holds the 147 tracked paths and none of the local-only files; the workflow parses; `actions/attest` writes its bundle as one JSON per line. The workflow itself first runs on the next release, and Scorecard scores the check from then on.

La búsqueda administrativa recortaba entradas largas y el listado agrupaba avisos junto con todas las publicaciones, cargando además campos de cuenta del autor que no necesita. Ahora valida búsqueda, audiencia y estado de correo; una entrada inválida muestra errores y cero resultados. Primero pagina 20 publicaciones con identidad mínima del autor y grupos precargados, y después calcula sus métricas en una agregación limitada a esos identificadores.

Los filtros de audiencia y correo utilizan EXISTS: seleccionar un estado conserva los demás conteos de la novedad y varias pertenencias a grupos no los multiplican. Las tarjetas muestran avance de lectura, audiencia configurada y estados de correo, con fecha explícita de Colombia. La cola general y la lista se actualizan conjuntamente mediante el controlador existente; los filtros y la paginación funcionan sin JavaScript. El reintento de errores mantiene su alcance global y sus controles POST/CSRF.

Validación: 463 pruebas completas con MySQL; 18 regresiones nuevas también con SQLite en memoria y repetidas con MySQL tras ajustar los textos. 37 comprobaciones de Chromium: 33 funcionales y cuatro finales de texto/diseño, con filtros combinados, métricas completas, 35 publicaciones en dos páginas, publicación dirigida a cuatro destinatarios temporales, seis roles y anchos de 320 a 1.440 píxeles. El contexto de 1.200 publicaciones usa cuatro consultas y métricas de 20 filas; la medición excluye autenticación, middleware y cola general y no afirma una mejora de latencia.

Ruff, formato, migraciones, producción, estáticos, diagnóstico SQL estricto y auditoría de dependencias correctos. No hay cambios de esquema, permisos SQL ni dependencias. Se retiraron 36 novedades ficticias, cinco cuentas, un grupo y nueve sesiones junto con sus datos relacionados. El correo local permanece en Mailpit y no se reintentó la cola general.

author: steveapo
body:
## What changes

- **Parallel full tier.** The single 38-minute `full` job becomes three `suite` jobs that run at the same time, each on its own runner with its own PostgreSQL, Valkey and object store: `integration 1 of 2`, `integration 2 of 2` (`vitest --shard`) and `end-to-end`. `fail-fast: false`, so a failed part can be re-run alone.
- **`full` keeps its meaning.** A final job named `full` `needs` `quick`, `changes` and `suite`, runs with `always()` wherever the full tier was asked for, and succeeds only if `quick` succeeded and either every `suite` part succeeded or the path rule applied. It **fails (it is not skipped)** when a part fails or is cancelled. `release.yml`'s gate (`select(.name == "full")` with conclusion `success` on a successful push run of main), the label `ci:full`, and any required check on `full` need no edit.
- **Free speed-ups.** The Playwright browser is cached by Playwright's version (system libraries still installed each time). Next.js's `.next/cache` is cached by lockfile, with the run's sha at the end of the key. The separate `pnpm build` step is gone: Playwright's `webServer` already runs `pnpm build && pnpm start` (`playwright.config.ts`), so CI was building twice. The build still runs, and its failure still fails `end-to-end`.
- **Sharding the integration tests is safe.** Every file gets its own database (`tests/integration/database.ts` `createDatabase`, a random name for each file), files already run one at a time (`fileParallelism: false`), and each shard has its own services. No retries were added and no test was skipped.

## The path rule (security-relevant: please review this wording)

> The job `changes` runs wherever the full tier is asked for (a push to `main`, a run by hand, or the label `ci:full` added to a pull request that is not a draft). The diff that decides is `git diff --raw --no-renames` over: **on a pull request**, `base...head` (from where it left `main`); **on a push to `main`**, from the most recent commit of `main` that is an ancestor of the pushed head, is not the head itself, and has a successful push run of `ci` whose job `full` concluded `success`, to the pushed head; **by hand**, no diff (always the full tier). The change is content alone, and the full tier is satisfied by `quick`, only if the diff is not empty and **every** line is a regular file (new mode `100644` for A and M, and old mode `100644` as well for M; old mode `100644` for D: a symbolic link `120000`, a submodule `160000`, an executable `100755` or a change of type needs the full tier) and is one of:
>
> 1. status A, M or D, path matching `^docs/[^"]*\.md$`: Markdown documentation outside the application's source;
> 2. status A, M or D, path one of `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `TRADEMARKS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` at the root;
> 3. status A or M (not D), path matching `^public/images/[^"]+\.(png|jpe?g|webp|avif|gif)$`: a raster image added or replaced under `public/images/`.
>
> Anything else needs the full tier, and so do: an empty diff, a rename (split into a delete and an add by `--no-renames`), any other status, a path git quotes, no earlier commit of `main` with `full` passed, any error in computing the diff (`set -eu` fails the job, and a failed `changes` has no output, which the `suite` condition reads as "run"), and any answer from the script other than `full=true` or `full=false`. Where the rule applies, `full` concludes `success` and writes "The full tier was satisfied by the path rule" in the run summary; `changes` writes the diff it judged.

Why each entry:
1. `docs/**/*.md`: nothing under `src/`, `scripts/` (apart from `record.ts`, a by-hand command), `tests/integration/` or `tests/e2e/` reads these files (checked by grep; the hits are comments). The unit tests that read them (`storage-match`, `advisories`, `processors`, `dependency-patches`, `procedures`) and the Markdown format check run in `quick`.
2. Root Markdown: read by nothing that runs; the names in `src/` are in comments. `data/common-passwords.md` is **not** on the list: it is data.
3. `public/images/` rasters: served as static files by Next.js; no route of the application is under `/images` (no `src/app/**/images` route segment), so a file there shadows nothing. SVG is excluded (it can carry script), and deletion is excluded (a page may name the file). `public/` does not exist yet; this entry is for the owner's example of adding an image.

Transitivity on `main`: a base that itself passed by the rule is fine, because its own diff to an earlier fully tested commit was content alone, so behaviour equals that commit's.

Known limit: the rule is only as strong as the review of its own files. A pull request runs its own copy of `ci.yml` and `scripts/ci/scope.mjs`, and once merged, the push run on `main` for that merge commit runs the merged copy too. So a pull request that widens the allowed list gates its own push run on `main`, and with it the deploy gate. That is no worse than a pull request that deletes tests, and the defence is the same: review every change to `.github/` and `scripts/ci/`. No CODEOWNERS file or setting is changed here; that is the owner's call.

Nit: when the suite is skipped (path rule), its jobs show as `matrix.part` in the checks list, because the matrix is never expanded. That does no harm unless one of the part names (`integration 1 of 2`, `end-to-end`, …) is made a required check. Require `full` only.

## Proof in Actions

| Run | Head | What | Wall-clock | Jobs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 44323414114 (before, `main` push) | `8cf0209` | old single `full` | **38m46s** | one job in sequence |
| 44371476048 | `b78ee0b` | new full tier, cold caches | **17m35s** | quick 1m38, changes 7s, integration 1 of 2 9m51, integration 2 of 2 15m48, end-to-end 14m18, full 3s |
| 44377110825 | `0a2648f` (final head) | new full tier | **22m19s** | quick 2m47, changes 5s, integration 1 of 2 10m27, integration 2 of 2 14m59, end-to-end 19m23, full 3s |
| 44375054683 (throwaway #104, docs-only on top of this branch, closed unmerged) | `40e1df9` | path rule | **2m44s** | quick 2m36, changes 6s, suite skipped, full 2s "satisfied by the path rule" |

In 44377110825, `playwright install-deps` (the apt packages; the browser came from the cache) took 6m32s, against 15s for the whole install in 44371476048. The PostgreSQL client's apt step was also slower (28s against 8s). That points to a slow apt mirror on that runner, not to this change. Without it, end-to-end took about 13 minutes.

## Not verified

- The push run on `main`, and in it the `changes` search for the last commit of `main` with `full` passed: it can run only after merge. If the search fails, the full tier runs.
- The Next.js build cache is saved and restored. Whether it shortens the build measurably has not been measured.

author: anna-germ
body:
## Problem

Germ sign-in on a tranquil PDS (e.g. tranquil.farm) ends at "Almost done. Try again later." For a missing record, tranquil returns HTTP **404** `{"error":"RecordNotFound"}`; the reference PDS returns **400** with the same error name. `parse` types only the 400, so the 404 surfaces as `.unrecognized(404)` with the body dropped, and AtprotoClient's `callExpectingOptional` can't read it as absent.

## Change

`ResponseParsing` gets a `notFoundErrors` requirement, empty by default. For an `OptionalResultRequest` (getRecord, getBlob, resolveHandle) it defaults to that endpoint's `notFoundCodes`. `parse` types a 404 as `.xrpcError(status: .notFound, …)` only when its body is an XRPC error naming one of those codes. Every other 404 (other error names, HTML, endpoints without not-found codes) stays `.unrecognized`, as today.

## Tests

`NotFoundParsingTests` runs canned responses through the real `GetRecord` (so the constrained default is the one its conformance picks up): a 404 or 400 `RecordNotFound` is typed; a 404 `RepoNotFound`, a 404 HTML page, and a 404 on `PutRecord` stay `.unrecognized`. With the source change reverted, the 404 case fails. Full suite passes locally.

With AtprotoClient germ-network/AtprotoClient#69 pointed at this branch, its suite passes and a live `getRecord` of `com.germnetwork.declaration/self` comes back absent for both a tranquil account (404) and a bsky-hosted one (400).

**Found by the live Cencori test (18 Nov 2026).** Lodestone estimated a call's cost from OpenRouter's catalogue only. A fallback that does not report its own cost (Cencori, Requesty and others) was therefore counted at the flat hold ($0.01 by default) even when its own model list has prices: one `gpt-4o-mini` call of 26 tokens was counted as $0.01, so a spend limit was far stricter than needed for cheap calls. Safe (it over-counts) but wrong.

**Fix:** `estimateCost` now reads the calling provider's own catalogue when it has one (OpenRouter's otherwise). With no price listed, the hold still counts. Two tests (priced and unpriced).

**Docs:** the Providers page and README move Cencori from "partly" to checked, with what was actually seen: a live chat answer (gpt-4o-mini, ~4 s), the list read (63 available chat models of 95), failover, a withdrawn model dropped using the list, discovery with a price limit, and the `private` rule. Changelog entry under Unreleased.

TypeScript 275 tests and Python 65 pass. TypeScript only: the Python port does not read other providers' price lists.

author: keejkrej
body:
## Summary

M1 public SDK + persistence increment for QuickPy. This adds the public Go
package, explicit execution state, the ABI 2 guest state slice, and a
real-artifact integration suite. It is a coherent, independently verified
increment — **not** a full M1 acceptance or production release.

Base: `main` at `1100618` (M0 merge). Head: `m1/public-sdk`.

## What is included

- **Public root package `quickpy`:** `New`, `RuntimeOptions`, `ArtifactSource`,
  `RegisterTool`/`UnregisterTool`/`ToolNames`, `Execute`,
  `Execution.Wait`/`Cancel`/`ID`, `Close`, `Value`, `ToolCall`/`ToolHandler`/
  `ToolError`, `Event`/`TextEvent`/`ConsoleEvent`/`ImageEvent`/`ToolEvent`,
  `Result`, `Status`, `Error`/`Kind`, `GuestInfo`.
- **Explicit persistence:** `quickpy.get_state()` / `set_state()`, catchable
  `StateError`, last-write-wins, commit only on successful completion,
  `StateWritten` distinguishing `set_state(None)` from no write, deep-copy
  semantics, and IEEE 754 binary64 float fidelity.
- **ABI 2 guest:** state slice, zero WASI imports, one EH tag, 64/1024 memory
  pages, 4 MiB MicroPython heap.
- **Host hardening:** ABI 2 handshake, state decode, observer, cancellation,
  close, registry snapshots, event sinks, and the capacity-release race fix.
- **Integration suite:** `integration/` gated by `QUICKPY_TEST_ARTIFACT`; plain
  `go test ./...` skips cleanly.
- **Docs:** `docs/M1_STATUS.md`, `guest/M1_NOTES.md`, updated `README.md`,
  `docs/HANDOFF.md`, and `docs/SPEC.md`.

## Architecture

```
Go application
  └─ public quickpy package        api.go, runtime.go, execution.go, events.go, value.go
       └─ engine boundary          engine.go, wasmengine.go
            └─ internal/wasmguest  ABI 2 host adapter, protocol, state, observer
                 └─ WASM guest     guest/build/quickpy.wasm (generated, ignored)
                      └─ C adapter + MicroPython v1.29.0
```

The public package owns lifecycle, tool registry snapshots, events, results,
errors, and state. `internal/wasmguest` owns the ABI 2 protocol and wazero
integration. The guest artifact is generated and gitignored.

## Artifact

- **220,134 bytes**
- sha256 `be1b8e48b6884e3e9e2a59c758a2abceac564adb5162b691e5a6b6cd3eac9c4d`
- ABI 2, **0** WASI imports, **1** EH tag, memory 64/1024 pages
- Byte-identical rebuild independently reproduced

## Independent verification (2026-11-18)

**GO, no blockers.** The independent verifier reported:

- Root: **48** test functions pass, including the race suite.
- Internal: **83** test functions + **1** fuzz target = **84**.
- Real-artifact integration: **40 top-level tests + 14 subtests PASS**; race
  run PASS; **3 repeat integration runs PASS**.
- Guest smoke: **66/66** checks pass.
- Default root tests skip integration cleanly when the artifact is unset.
- Artifact rebuilt byte-identically at the size/hash above.

## Test commands and results

```sh
gofmt -l *.go cmd internal integration        # clean
go vet ./...                                  # PASS
go build ./...                                # PASS
go test -count=1 ./...                        # PASS (integration skips cleanly)
QUICKPY_TEST_ARTIFACT=guest/build/quickpy.wasm go test -count=1 ./integration
                                              # PASS, ~6.7 s
cd guest/smoke && go run . ../build/quickpy.wasm
                                              # PASS, 66/66
```

The longer race run was independently verified and was not re-run for this
packaging pass.

## Security and memory boundaries

- Guest imports **zero** WASI functions; host allowlist is empty and
  default-deny.
- No host filesystem, network, environment, or process access.
- WASM is a guest memory/capability boundary, not OS process isolation.
- Tool implementations are trusted; a malicious trusted tool can do anything
  the host permits.
- `MaxMemoryBytes` is enforced at the wazero runtime level, not per instance.
  A lower per-execution value is rejected before admission rather than applied.
- Guest entry is serialized; concurrent async tools are host-dispatched but only
  the owner re-enters the guest.

## Known deviations from SPEC targets

These are implementation constraints, not spec rewrites:

- SPEC names distinct `ToolNotFoundError`, `ToolArgumentError`, and
  `ToolLimitError` classes. The current guest exposes a single
  `quickpy.ToolError` with a `code` field; a `MaxToolCalls` overrun is currently
  host `LimitExceeded`, not a catchable `ToolLimitError`.
- A runtime-level WASM memory-cap trap currently maps to `GuestFault`, not
  `LimitExceeded`, because the host cannot attribute it to a configured
  per-execution limit at that boundary.

## Non-goals and remaining M1 gates

- No full M1 acceptance or production-readiness claim.
- No `ToolCause` population on `Error.Tool` yet.
- `GuestInfo.Version` is blank.
- `ConsoleEvent`/`ImageEvent` are API surface only; the real guest emits text.
- No host wall-clock timers; no top-level `await`/`return`.
- No per-instance memory enforcement.
- No stable artifact distribution/embedding contract.
- No complete normative `asyncio` subset/failure matrix.
- No dedicated soak/resource-leak trend.
- No pi-go integration and no Zig rewrite.
- Remaining request-specific caps and real protocol/guest-fault coverage are
  incomplete.

## Licensing

No project license has been selected for original QuickPy code. Third-party
notices are unchanged in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (MicroPython MIT,
wasi-libc/musl MIT, wazero Apache-2.0, `golang.org/x/sys` BSD-3-Clause).

author: denguzov
body:
## Why

Part of MT-2419. Before this PR, `CollectDispatcher`:
- Leaked sockets. On an HTTP error, the error stream was neither read nor closed, and `disconnect()` wasn't called.
- Never reused connections. On success, it called `disconnect()` without reading the body. Collect replies with an empty chunked body, so every dispatch opened a new TLS connection.
- Could send a POST twice. When the server closed the connection after reading the request, the JDK resent the POST (`sun.net.http.retryPost` defaults to `true`), and the SDK reported success.
- Counted only exactly 200 as success.

## What

- 2xx success. Any 2xx counts as success. An `x-error` header still makes it a failure.
- No resend. The body is sent with `setFixedLengthStreamingMode`, and the JDK doesn't resend streaming requests. A lost response now gives a failure callback instead of a silent resend and a success.
- No redirects. `setInstanceFollowRedirects(false)` makes a 3xx an ordinary failure. In streaming mode the JDK couldn't follow it anyway.
- Body release before the callback. `releaseConnection` reads the body from the input stream (status < 400) or the error stream: a success body to the end, at most 8 KB of a failure body. It then closes the stream. On close, the JDK reuses the connection if the rest has arrived, drains up to 512 KB in the background, or closes the socket, so no socket is left open. If reading fails, it calls `disconnect()`. The outcome still comes from the status and headers.
- `disconnect()` when connecting, writing or reading the status fails.
- Tests. A new `CollectDispatcherConnectionTests` covers:
  - connection reuse over chunked bodies, as Collect sends them;
  - open connections after bursts of failures, counted on the server;
  - cut-off and slow bodies;
  - exactly one POST when the server closes after reading it;
  - 204, 200 with `x-error`, and 302;
  - a unit test of the 8 KB read limit.

  The reuse and burst tests fail against the code before this PR.

### Not in this PR

- Error detail in the callback (status code, `x-error`, body and cause in the error string). That's PR 3 of MT-2419.
- A time limit for the whole send. The read timeout applies to each read, so a server that trickles bytes can still block `track()`. This goes to MT-2440, with asynchronous sending and retries.
- README and change log (MT-2421).

author: leon-liang
body:
## Problem

Clicking **Resolved** in the inbox with 67+ items made the Running and Resolved headers jump from the bottom of the list to the top in about 40 ms.

`Disclosure` animated `grid-template-rows` from `0fr` to `1fr` in a fixed 300 ms. For a long list that is about 3,400 px, nearly all of it off-screen, so the visible part filled almost at once.

## Change

`Disclosure` (`web/src/components/shell/layout/Disclosure.tsx`) now:

- animates the measured height, only up to the part that is visible when open. The off-screen part appears at the end, below the fold.
- scales the duration with the distance: 180 ms for short lists, up to 400 ms for long ones.
- uses the standard ease-in-out curve. A fast-start curve showed a 75 px jump on the first frame, because the click's render takes about 30 ms.
- fades items in over 300 ms on open and out over 150 ms on close.
- reverses from the current height on a second click mid-way.
- skips the animation when reduced motion is set.

This also applies to board station sections, Runs age groups and the team navigation.

## Verification

- Storybook `Inbox/Items` at 450×900, Open collapsed, header position sampled every frame: the header now travels 570 px over about 330 ms, at most 33 px per frame. A mid-way reversal continues from the current height.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` passes. Vitest for shell layout, Inbox, board and Runs: 243 tests pass.
