author: eregon
body:
Follow-up to #4553, addressing @nirvdrum's review there, which arrived after the merge. Two commits.

## 1. Make PTY.spawn closer to CRuby

`PTY.spawn`:
- The redirections given in the options take precedence over the pty, like on CRuby. Before, the pty always won:
  ```ruby
  PTY.spawn("sh", "-c", "echo to-stderr >&2; echo to-stdout", err: File::NULL)
  # CRuby and now TruffleRuby: "to-stdout\r\n", before: "to-stderr\r\nto-stdout\r\n"
  ```
- `spawn-helper` opens the terminal by its path to make it the controlling terminal, so this no longer depends on stdin, which the user can redirect.
- `spawn-helper` drops privileges with `seteuid(getuid())` once the terminal is acquired, like CRuby's `drop_privilege()`.
- `pgroup:` raises `Errno::EPERM` (`setpgid`), like on CRuby: the command is a session leader.
- `spawn` and `getpty` are module functions, so they are also private instance methods of `PTY`.
- With no command and no `$SHELL`, the shell is looked up with `$USER` or `getlogin`, and falls back to `/bin/sh` if there is no passwd entry, instead of raising `ArgumentError`.
- The result of the `fcntl()` duplicating the master is checked.

`PTY.open`:
- The master is opened with `O_CLOEXEC` directly, closing the window where another thread's spawn could inherit it.
- Both file descriptors are closed if the `chmod` fails.

Others:
- `rb_ary_resize()` raises `IndexError` for a too big length.
- The `[command, argv0]` spec is guarded for BusyBox, like in `core/process/spawn_spec.rb`.
- The `rb_io_gets()` ChangeLog entry moves to Compatibility, as it used to raise.

## 2. Report spawn-helper failures to the parent through a pipe

`posix_spawn()` succeeds as soon as `spawn-helper` is executed, so a failure in it (`setsid`, `chdir`, `execvp`, ...) was only printed and seen as the exit status of the process.

`spawn-helper` now writes the failed step and `errno` to a close-on-exec pipe and the parent raises the corresponding `SystemCallError`, similar to `rb_fork_async_signal_safe()`. The read end is at end-of-file once the command is executed, so spawn only waits until the exec.

This applies to `PTY.spawn` and to `Process.spawn` with `chdir:`, which goes through `spawn-helper` and had the same gap. E.g. a script whose shebang names a missing interpreter now raises `Errno::ENOENT`, like on CRuby, instead of returning a pid.

This is a separate commit so it can be dropped on its own: without it the rest still works, and such a failure is an exit status of 127/126/125 from `spawn-helper`.

## Testing

- New specs for the redirection precedence, the controlling terminal with stdin redirected, `pgroup:`, a missing interpreter (for `PTY.spawn` and for `Process.spawn` with `chdir:`), and the module functions. They pass on TruffleRuby and on CRuby 3.3.
- `TestPTY` and `TestIO_Console` from the MRI tests pass.

Not tested: macOS (including `O_CLOEXEC` for `posix_openpt()` there), the privilege drop (needs different real and effective UIDs), and the `chmod`/`fcntl` failure paths.

- [x] ChangeLog entry added for the `Process.spawn` `chdir:` change. The `pty` changes are covered by the existing entry for this unreleased version.

author: kalebgore28
body:
## Summary
A frontend pass against current web platform guidance (accessibility, forms, dialogs, tables, dark mode, performance), plus the mobile issues found along the way: the nav was small on phones, choosing a page didn't close the nav drawer, and much of the text was 12–14px.

### Dark mode
- The theme is now applied by a small inline script in `<head>` before first paint, instead of in a `useEffect`. Dark mode no longer flashes light on load.
- `color-scheme` is declared in a `<meta>` tag and in CSS, so scrollbars and native controls match the theme.
- "System" is now the real default and follows the OS when it switches. Previously the first visit saved `light` or `dark`, so the page never followed the OS again.
- Toasts follow the app's theme. They used `next-themes`, which was never set up, so that dependency is removed.
- The theme menu shows which option is selected.

### Mobile
- Choosing a page in the nav drawer now closes it.
- On phones, nav items are 44px tall with 16px text, up from 28px and 14px, and the current page is highlighted.
- At phone widths, Tailwind's `text-xs` and `text-sm` are raised to 14px and 16px in `spacing.css`. Desktop is unchanged.
- Adds `<meta name="text-scale" content="scale">` so supporting phones apply the OS text size.

### Accessibility
- Clickable table rows (advisees, instructors, an instructor's sections) were `<tr tabIndex=0>`, so screen readers announced plain rows and they couldn't open in a new tab. Each row now has a real link in one cell, and clicking anywhere else in the row follows it.
- The user modal is now a real `<form>`:
  - It stays open until saves finish, so a failed save keeps your edits.
  - Esc, clicking outside, Cancel and the close button ask before discarding unsaved changes.
  - Missing fields are flagged and focused when you try to save, instead of Save being disabled.
- Screen readers now hear the student lookup result count, import progress steps, and import results and errors.
- Each page has its own title, like "Student Lookup | COBIS", instead of "COBIS App" everywhere.
- Adds a skip link to the main content, and there's now one `<h1>` per page.
- Every table has a screen-reader caption, and `SortableTable` and `EditableDataTable` now require one.
- Header cells default to `scope="col"`. The permissions table uses row headers, so each checkbox is announced with its data category.
- The editable table's filter and bulk-edit popovers are real forms with unique ids. Student lookup filters are wrapped in `<search>`.
- On the error page, the heading is now an `<h1>`, the icon-only copy button has a label, and copying is announced. Dev login now shows an error when it fails.

### Performance
- Fonts load from one preconnected `<link>` with only the families in use (Oxanium, Fira Code). Before, three chained CSS `@import`s also pulled in Merriweather and Oswald, which nothing used.
- The logos were 3001px PNGs of about 72 KB each, displayed around 240px wide. They are now 800px AVIF files of about 14 KB, with set dimensions so the page doesn't shift as they load.
- The login logo is fetched first, and the sidebar only downloads the logo for its current size and theme.
- Removes the unused PNG logos and the 24 unused Freight web font files.
- TypeScript and the Vite build now target ES2024.

## Things to know
- **Saved themes:** anyone who used the app before this keeps the `light` or `dark` value the old code saved automatically. Their browser won't follow the OS until they choose "System" in the theme menu.
- **Clickable rows:** they use a row click handler instead of a link stretched over the row with `::after`. The stretched link needs `position: relative` on `<tr>`, which Safari long ignored ([WebKit bug 240961](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=240961)), and could have made every row open the last row. I haven't tested this on a real iPhone.
- **shadcn files:** two generated components in `src/components/ui/` are edited:
  - `table.tsx` defaults header cells to `scope="col"`.
  - `button.tsx`: the small button size uses the larger phone text.

  Regenerating either component would drop these changes.

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit`, `vp lint --type-aware` and `vp build` all pass. The project has no automated tests.
- Checked in the browser at desktop (1280×800) and phone (375×812) widths, in light and dark mode:
  - row clicks, user modal (Esc, outside click, Cancel, discard prompt, focus)
  - nav drawer closing, skip link, editable table filter on Enter
  - page titles, table captions, theme switching
  - no horizontal scroll on the main pages
- Not tested: an actual save in the user modal, the error page, a failed dev login, and Safari.

body:
The first piece of using the model's own probabilities: \`Runner::score(target)\` returns the bits (\`-log2 p\`) the model needs for each token of a text after what the live sequence holds. No request kind and no use by the seat yet; the design page records what was measured and what was not.

Two commits, red then green. Red: a stub and the real-model check (\`tests/score_model.rs\`, needs \`MEMBRAMA_TEST_MODEL\`, skips loudly without it) failed on its first assertion. Green: it passes. On \`qwen3:8b\`, five invented entities (three facts each), ten questions, the answer scored as the model writes it: mean bits for the answer **15.3 with no facts, 1.0 with the entity's own facts, 37.8 with another entity's facts**; for every question the right facts were cheapest and another's facts were worse than none.

A correction in my own test: its first version scored lowercase answers (\`hamster\`), and the pets and instruments showed almost no drop, one of them slightly worse. The model writes \`Hamster\`; the target must be what the model would write. The design page says so.

What this does not show: that it improves recall. The facts here fully determine the answer and the names are invented; a real memory is rarely a literal answer; and at recall time the answer is not known yet, so it cannot be scored then. One model, ten questions.

Local run: all membrama tests pass without the model; with the model, the turn, splice and score tests pass.

The release's gesture-phase profile observed short cancellation interactions for only 149/246 ms. Device orientation arrived after the native interaction ended, and the raw phase assertion correctly blocked publication even though XCTest itself passed.

Hold pointer input for two seconds only in the gesture-phase profile so asynchronous orientation delivery has an explicit input window. The default-transition/content-Back profile retains 0.3 seconds. Distances, velocities, observation deadlines and every native assertion remain unchanged. Orientation must still reach the app while the same coordinator and recognizer are interactive; no gesture is retried.

Validation: normal iPadOS 26.2, normal 18.6 and a real one-second delayed-orientation control on 26.2 each pass three XCTest methods and the native phase checks. The delayed control records the request timestamp after waiting and receives orientation 1.17–1.31 seconds before cancellation decisions. The temporary delay was removed. All 69 harness tests pass. All nine source hashes per run are verified against the final fixture/control patch.

The 18.6 profile retains its two known missing inset gestures. Gesture intent and actual UIKit outcome remain distinct; mandatory actual inset cancellation stays enforced by the unchanged default profile. These runs still show deferred visual rotation, not proven visual overlap. Package/runtime contents are unchanged.

[Evidence report and original hosted failure](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/blob/b9f78d0aaf4598f7fb33bf999ef589fa23e2f08d/test/stable-010-gesture-window.md).

This records the normal final fixture without injected delay, including rotation, retained state and modal controls. Native JSON supplies the timing and actual outcome evidence.

[Focused hosted validation](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/actions/runs/44397342759) uses the identical native source. Its [26.2 job](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/actions/runs/44397342759/job/135130675370) failed before XCTest: `simctl install` exceeded the existing installation timeout and was killed without output. No native result artifact was produced, and this is not counted as acceptance. The [18.6 sibling](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/actions/runs/44397342759/job/135130675910) passed all three profiles (three gesture, two programmatic-overlap and four default XCTest methods). All nine native source hashes per profile match the final main fixture. The workflow overall retains the 26.2 setup failure; it is not described as fully passing.

The [complete release gate on final main 1064891](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/actions/runs/44398468421) includes a fresh execution of every applicable profile and must pass before publication.

Final main [iPadOS 26.2 validation](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/actions/runs/44398468421/job/135135581865) passed all three profiles: three gesture, two programmatic-overlap and four default-transition XCTest methods, with zero failures or skips. Native phase assertions also passed, including real inset Back cancellation in the default profile. All nine recorded source hashes per profile match clean main `106489195ef2bc860104ebac2b828dd5d03fc0cc`. The separate content-Back job initially encountered an installation timeout before XCTest. Its [same-commit rerun](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/actions/runs/44398468421/job/135179476483) passed all four XCTest methods with zero failures/skips, including actual inset Back cancellation. All nine source hashes match the final main fixture.

Final main [iPadOS 18.6 validation](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/actions/runs/44398468421/job/135135581844) also passed the three gesture, two programmatic-overlap and four default-transition XCTest methods, with zero failures or skips. All nine recorded source hashes per profile match clean main `106489195ef2bc860104ebac2b828dd5d03fc0cc`; the known missing inset gesture cases remain explicitly reported.

The full release workflow completed successfully on `106489195ef2bc860104ebac2b828dd5d03fc0cc`: 38 successful jobs, retaining the 35 successful jobs from attempt one and rerunning only the setup failure and its dependent gates. [Stable v0.1.0](https://github.com/rafaelaugustos/vue-router-ns/releases/tag/v0.1.0) was created after the complete native gate and final-tarball installation checks passed.

body:
Version 4.52: Im KI-Training gibt es eine neue Seite »Die Wunsch-Methode« – das Modell »Vier Sätze, drei Kreise« als Zeichnung zum Antippen.

**Freigabe/Anlass:** Auftrag Mario (18.11.2026): das Modell perfekt visualisiert in Kidu umsetzen, als Pull Request. Zusammengeführt wird erst auf deine ausdrückliche Freigabe. Einzelheiten: `docs/version-4-52.md`.

## Was du freigeben musst

1. **Der Name der Seite: »Die Wunsch-Methode«.** Nicht »Die vier Sätze« – Kidu hat schon »fünf Sätze«. »Vier Sätze, drei Kreise« steht als Marker darunter.
2. **Neue Namen, die danach eingefroren sind:** Wissen · Sagen · Prüfen · Verantworten; Für mich · Für meine Lernenden · Für andere; Grundausstattung; »Wo stehst du?«; »Was in der Lampe wirklich steckt«.
3. **Die Texte der zwölf Felder:** was du kannst, erster Schritt, Beispiel, Übung, Kniff. Alle Beispiele sind ausgedacht – so steht es auf der Seite.
4. **Die Reihenfolge für »Das lohnt sich anzusehen«:** erst die Grundausstattung (zuerst Prüfen), dann »Für meine Lernenden«, dann »Für andere«. Ein Vorschlag, kein Befund.
5. **Der Platz:** KI-Training · Phase 1 »Grundlagen«, siebtes Werkzeug; auf der Karte der Phase die Hilfe »Den Überblick bekommen«.
6. **Das Bild:** ein Halbrund aus zwölf Feldern, unten die Lampe. Der Geist ist nur Rauch. Die Bratwurst steht im Text.

Das Modell ist ein Vorschlag und noch nicht erprobt. So steht es an der Zeichnung.

## Was sich ändert

- **Neue Seite `wunsch-methode.html`:** links die Geschichte von der Lampe mit zwei Merksätzen, rechts die Zeichnung. Vier Fächer (die Sätze), drei Bögen (die Kreise), zwölf Felder. Ocker gefüllt ist die Grundausstattung. In der Mitte steigt der Rauch auf: »Hier endet das Märchen« – links wünschen, rechts prüfen und verantworten.
- **Ein Feld antippen** öffnet das Arbeitsfenster neben der Zeichnung: was du kannst, »Dein erster Schritt«, ein Beispiel, »Die Übung dazu«, »Der Kniff dazu«. Escape oder »Schließen« schließt; die Adresse merkt das Feld; »Zurück« funktioniert.
- **»Wo stehst du?«:** drei Bilder, eines je Kreis. Danach steht an jedem Feld ✓ »mache ich schon« oder ○ »noch nicht«, dazu bis zu drei nächste Schritte. Keine Stufe, keine Zahl, kein Balken. Gespeichert wird nur in diesem Browser; »Eingaben löschen« entfernt es.
- **Liste aller zwölf Felder** als Rückfall: am Telefon, ohne Skript und im Druck.
- **Drei Aufklapptexte:** was in der Lampe wirklich steckt, was »Grundausstattung« heißt, worauf das Modell beruht (mit Belegstand).
- **Fahrplan KI-Training:** neues Werkzeug in Phase 1, neue Hilfe auf der Startseite. Phase 1 zeigt »6 Hilfen · 7 Werkzeuge«.
- **Technik:** eine Datenquelle `assets/daten/wunsch.js`; `tools/wunsch.py` setzt beim Bauen Zeichnung, Liste und Lampentext ein; `tools/pruefen.py` prüft die Seite. Alle Wörter der Zeichnung sind Text, kein Bild.
- **Dokumente:** `DESIGN.md` (neuer Abschnitt mit Schaubild-Zeile, Bedeutungs-Check, Messwerten), `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, »Über Kidu«, `docs/version-4-52.md`.

Die vielen geänderten `*.html` im Hauptordner sind neu gebaute Seiten: Nur die Prüfsumme der CSS-Datei hat sich geändert.

## Prüfung

Gelaufen:
- Projektprüfung (`tools/bauen.py`, `tools/pruefen.py`): keine Verstöße
- Unit-Tests: 204 von 204 (zehn neu in `tests/wunsch.test.js`)
- Browser-Tests: 938 von 938 (50 neu für 4.52, zwei alte Zählungen angepasst)
- Mindestprüfung 5a für `wunsch-methode.html`, `ki.html`, `ueber.html`: 0 Probleme
- Bildschirmfotos angesehen: Beamer, 1920, iPad quer und hochkant, Telefon, Beamer-Ansicht, Tastaturfokus, Druck

Gemessen:
- Beamer 1280 × 720: Zeichnung bis 544 px, »Wo stehst du?« bis 618 px; bei jedem der zwölf Felder steht der erste Schritt im ersten Bildschirm (höchstens 705 px).
- Felder 44,8 bis 61,1 px dick (iPad quer bis 1920 px). Kein Text unter 16 px. Kein waagerechtes Scrollen. Nach dem Laden läuft keine Animation.
- Beamer-Ansicht: Wörter auf Grund 21:1, auf Ocker 6,2:1, Kanten der Felder 9,2 und 9,4:1.
- Druck: 7 Seiten A4.

Eigene Kritik nach den Bildschirmfotos: **84 von 100** (Design 34/40 · Bedienung 25/30 · Eigenständigkeit 17/20 · Inhalt 8/10). Schwächen: Am Telefon gibt es die Zeichnung nicht. Am Beamer steht bei einem offenen Feld nur der erste Schritt im ersten Bildschirm. Auf sehr breiten Bildschirmen bleibt unter der Zeichnung Platz leer. Der Druck ist lang.

Nicht gelaufen: axe-core (`tests/vendor/axe.min.js` fehlt, Paketinstallation gesperrt) · Impeccable audit/polish und Taste Skill (Plugins fehlen) · echtes iPad mit Safari · VoiceOver · Druck auf Papier.

## Bewusst nicht übernommen / offen

- »Wo stehst du?« steht nur auf dieser Seite, nicht in »Mein Fortbildungsbogen« – deine Entscheidung, noch offen.
- »Wissen · Für andere« hat in Kidu noch kein eigenes Werkzeug. Das steht auf der Seite so da. Neue Werkzeuge wären ein eigener Schritt.
- »Vier Wochen KI-Training« nennt die Wunsch-Methode noch nicht.
- Kein Geist als Figur, keine Bratwurst als Bild (Begründung in `DESIGN.md`).
- »Was ist neu?« in »Über Kidu« nennt 4.49 bis 4.51 nicht; ich habe nur 4.52 ergänzt.

- Die Texte der zwölf Felder lesen: Stimmt jeder Satz für deine Schule? Besonders die Sätze zu Daten, Bewertung und Kennzeichnung.
- Auf dem iPad hoch und quer und am Beamer durchtippen: Feld → erster Schritt → »Wo stehst du?« → Karte → »Eingaben löschen«.

Die Quellen im Aufklapptext »Worauf das Modell beruht«: Drei habe ich für diesen Stand gegengelesen (Bastani u. a. 2025, Aalto-Universität 2025, Hebel 1811). Die übrigen stammen aus dem Bestand von Kidu und sind hier nicht neu gelesen.

## Brief description

Adds `ids/hali/` for the namespace of [hali](https://github.com/natemarks/hali), an open-source command-line tool that keeps a SKOS/OWL/SHACL description of local files. Its ontology IRI is `https://w3id.org/hali`, with terms such as `https://w3id.org/hali#Resource`. The tool does not fetch these IRIs, so nothing depends on the redirect at runtime; it makes the IRIs dereferenceable.

- `https://w3id.org/hali` with `Accept: text/turtle`: 303 to the core ontology, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/natemarks/hali/main/src/ontology/core.ttl`.
- `https://w3id.org/hali` with any other `Accept` (browsers, `*/*`): 303 to the project page, `https://github.com/natemarks/hali`.
- Any other name under `/hali/` (graph names, media types): 302 to the project page. These are identifiers only.

Only `ids/hali/.htaccess` is added. No other file is touched. Maintainer contact, with GitHub username, is in the file's comment block.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ifiokjr"} -->
_Requested by **ifi** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_014zNNNChuBzmX1c51HQXWjr?thread=cmsg_014zNNNChuBzmX1c51HQXWjrAt96eux4ZLWZ7RDzNg8q7t)_


## What changed

- **Flow recipes.** The six `// When your version has it` notes are gone. Each now uses the real feature:
  - `three-tries`: the insight page stages a flower and the star does `notice see=flower.1`.
  - `there-and-back`: the turn is `notice see=left` (home is leftward). The souvenir is held with `hold holds=parcel see=mine`.
  - `wrong-end-of-the-stick`: the star looks `see=away` while the half-sentence goes by.
  - `gag-short` and `wrong-end-of-the-stick`: the double-take is written with what exists. A glance, a pause, a look away, a pause, then `notice … shocked`. I rendered a preview of the gag-short scaffold and it plays as two looks and a take.
  - `there-and-back`: the setting-out page no longer frames `on={{star}}` after the star has left. On `main` that made `fables review` stop with an error on a fresh scaffold.
  - Where a recipe sets a `see=`, the next page says where the eyes go, with a one-line note that a `see=` holds over the page turn.
- **The nine flow books.** Things the words name are now in a hand or on the stage, and eyes are directed.
  - *The Letter with No Address*: Clem holds a `letter` (it was a `parcel`), reads it with `see=mine`, hops with `hop`, looks back with `notice see=left`, and props the letter on the counter as a stage prop.
  - *The New Kid*: Nan holds a `basket` (it was a `parcel`), sits, puts it down as a stage prop, and stares with `notice see=mo`. Mo waves, looks `see=away` at the half-sentence, and carries the basket on page 11.
  - *Mo and the Jar of Words*: Mo holds a `jar` (it was `jam`) and looks at it, at the bird, at the tree and at the hilltop sky.
  - *The Whole Street Hums*: everybody looks at each newcomer, and up when the bunting snaps.
  - *Otto and the Wobbling Tower*: Otto holds a `ruler`, Mochi holds a `cake`, a big cake stands for the tower, and the ruler and a cake lie on the ground after the row.
  - *A Feather Round Teacup Town*: Mochi's eyes follow the chain (dog, bird, flower, dog).
  - *Mochi and the Fireworks*: `point`, `hold`, `sit`, `see=up`, and `notice see=flower.2` on the insight page.
  - *Mochi Nibbles*: cakes at last. Held cakes, a cake on the stage, a huge one for the WHOOSH page, a cake to hide behind, and a `spoon` at the end.
  - *Zia and the Pigeon*: Zia holds a `bell`, then a `drum` for the band, and looks at the pigeon throughout.
- **The town's lit windows glow.** `settings/town.svg` gains one `data-glow` circle per lit window (eleven far, six near), shown at `dusk`, `night` and `moonlit`. The lit panes used to be flat fills that the light dimmed to brown. A glow is not dimmed, so the windows now read as lit. No new mechanism.
- **Review.** A prop standing on the stage is no longer reported as an idle arrival ("give them a beat, `@letter talk`"). A thing is only ever placed. One unit test covers it.

No story text changed. The only non-direction line that changed is the letter book's cover pose (`holds=parcel` to `holds=letter`).

## Existing books

Compared with `main` at da4e985, every page of every book.

- **Kerfuffle: no page changed.** Every proof of *Stinky McStinkbreath* is byte-identical. Its town pages are bare day and bare night, which the new glows do not touch.
- *The Visitor*: page 8 only. The town at `moonlit` now has glowing windows. Characters are identical.
- The three new worlds from #13, *Hana and the Wind*, *Ren Runs*, *Mo Mumble*, *Camera Test*, *Otto Measures the Sun*, *Zia Rings the Bell*: unchanged.
- The nine flow books changed because their scripts changed:
  - *The Letter with No Address*: cover, title page, pages 2 to 15 (letter in hand or on the counter, eyes, hops).
  - *The New Kid*: pages 1 to 9 and 11 (basket, wave, sit, eyes; page 7 is now a full shot so the basket on the grass is in the picture; page 11 ends full so the basket Mo carries is in the picture).
  - *Mo and the Jar of Words*: pages 2 to 13 and the back cover (jar, eyes; the back cover star looks out because the book ends on `see=front`).
  - *The Whole Street Hums*: pages 2 to 11 (eyes).
  - *Otto and the Wobbling Tower*: pages 1 to 15 (ruler, cakes, eyes).
  - *A Feather Round Teacup Town*: pages 2 to 9 (eyes).
  - *Mochi and the Fireworks*: pages 2 to 14 (poses and eyes).
  - *Mochi Nibbles*: pages 1 to 15 and the back cover (cakes, spoon, eyes).
  - *Zia and the Pigeon*: pages 1 and 3 to 7 (bell, drum, eyes).

Many of those pages changed only in where a head and eyes point. That is deliberate, and it has a cause worth knowing: see "What is weak".

## Review findings, before and after

`fables review`, `main` binary against this branch. "Text-picture" counts the "The text says/names …" considers.

| Book | Text-picture | All findings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Letter with No Address | 5 → 0 | 6 consider → 1 |
| The New Kid | 2 → 0 | 3 → 1 |
| Mo and the Jar of Words | 0 → 0 | 1 → 1 |
| The Whole Street Hums | 0 → 0 | 3 → 3 |
| Otto and the Wobbling Tower | 1 → 0 | 4 → 2 |
| A Feather Round Teacup Town | 0 → 0 | 2 → 2 |
| Mochi and the Fireworks | 3 → 0 | 5 → 2 |
| Mochi Nibbles | 1 → 0 | 2 → 1 |
| Zia and the Pigeon | 0 → 0 | 2 → 2 |

Twelve text-picture considers became none. No book gained a finding it did not have. Every other book's review is unchanged.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test`: all pass (454 unit tests and every integration suite).
- `scripts/check-worlds.sh`: passes.
- `fables flow list`, `fables flow show <name>` for all nine, and `fables new --flow <name>` for all nine: each scaffold passes `fables check` and `fables review` (one consider each: the unwritten lines).
- The town was rendered before and after at day, dusk, bare night, `light=night`, moonlit, golden and storm, in the `riso`, `clear`, `tv`, `shadow` and `card` skins. Day, bare night, golden and storm are byte-identical.

## What is weak

- **`see=` holds across page turns, and nothing gives the undirected look back.** A `see=` set on page 2 still aims the head on page 9, and on the back cover. `see=front` turns the head square to the reader, which is not the three-quarter look an undirected figure has. So a book that uses `see=` once has to say where the eyes go on every later page, which is why so many pages changed. The books now do that on purpose, and the recipes carry a one-line note. A value that hands the eyes back to the engine, or a page turn that resets them, would be a small engine change. I left it for the owner to decide. `docs/directing.md` says `see=front` "lets the room pull the eyes again", which is not quite what a still shows.
- **`see=` does nothing for critters** in a still (dog, bird, worm). "The dog was awake, and looking at Mochi" is still not drawn. I removed the critter `see=` I had tried.
- **`@camera … on=` ignores a stage prop.** `on=clem,letter` frames Clem alone. I stood Clem by the counter instead.
- **A stage prop cannot have copies** (`@cake.a` is an unknown actor). The cake tower is one big cake.
- **A close shot crops a held thing.** In close and medium shots on a kid, a prop held at the hip is below the frame, so several pages add `hold` to raise it. On two last pages the still ends on a wider shot than the video does: the trailing `@camera` after the close has no time left in the video, so the film ends close and the book page shows the prop.
- **A held cake sits near the chin** with `hold` on a small figure; a candle can touch the mouth (Otto pages 3, 5, 13, 14). Without `hold` the chibi carries it flat against the chest, which read worse there, though it is what Crumb does.
- **Nearest props, not exact ones.** The jar is drawn with sweets in it although the text says "empty jam jar". The basket has apples, not wool. There is no sock,

author: hixie
body: PROBLEM The toolshed binary is compiled with the V8 flag `--perf-basic-prof-only-functions`, which also switches on V8's event log. V8 writes that log to a file named after each isolate, in the process's working directory: isolate-0x953908000-65537-v8.log isolate-0x954088000-65537-v8.log The integration test lanes start the compiled toolshed with the checkout as its working directory, so a local test run leaves these files untracked in the checkout. A deployed toolshed writes them into its own working directory, one per thread that runs JavaScript. SOLUTION Build the binary with `--no-logfile-per-isolate` and `--logfile=+` as well. `+` is V8's name for an unnamed temporary file, which the system frees when its isolate ends: a serving worker's when the worker ends, and the main thread's when the process ends. The perf map that the profiling flag exists for is still written to `/tmp/perf-.map`. A new test runs Deno with the toolshed's V8 flags, from an empty directory, on a script that starts a worker. It checks that the directory stays empty and that the perf map is written. A companion test drops the two new flags and checks that V8 then writes its log files into the directory, so the first test can tell the difference. DESIGN DISCUSSION V8 cannot turn the log off while the perf flag is set: `--perf-basic-prof` implies `--log`, and `--no-log` is overridden. `--logfile=/dev/null` does not work either, because V8 opens only regular files as log files and falls back to standard output for anything else, which would interleave the log with the server's output. The temporary file still grows for as long as its isolate runs, as the perf map does, and on Linux it takes space in `/tmp` that a directory listing does not show. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

body:
Benny, 2026-11-18 15:55: "I want you to finish building it." App 1.4 puts the catcher in the notification shade, so it can be read and switched without leaving the game. It also carries the weather wording that came in after #171 was merged.

## What is in it

**1. The weather wording** (Benny 15:36: "yes include weather boosted too")
- All: "only what pays more than the normal 100 stardust: 476 species and anything weather-boosted, plus every shiny"
- a level: "only catches worth 700+ stardust: 20 species: <names> (weather boost counts), plus every shiny"
- without the catcher's levels file: "only what pays more than a normal catch, weather-boosted included, plus every shiny" / "only catches worth N+ stardust, plus every shiny"
- fold-out: "Catches only what pays more than a normal catch - evolved forms, bonus species and anything weather-boosted - plus every shiny. The list updates itself."
- The Auto-Catch tile for `only=1` stays "ON - only high-stardust Pokemon and shinies".
- A long `why=` wraps under the status card and is never cut (four lines in the picture of demo 3).
- README and the comments in `catcher_ctl.sh` say the same (`catcher_ctl.sh`: comments only).

**2. One ongoing notification** (`StatusService`, a foreground service of type `specialUse`)
- Title: the catcher's own line, e.g. `964 caught - 13.2/min - Star Piece OFF`.
- Under it: the `why=` problem, then the gym runner's line while Gym is on, the high-stardust mode when the catcher reports `only=`, the stardust and the balls.
- Three buttons: Catch, Spin, Gym. A label says what a tap will do (`Catch off`). A tap runs the same `catcher_ctl.sh` verb as the app's tile and is verified the same way (the flag file must hold the new value, three tries). A newer tap on the same button ends an older one.
- The app's screen starts it while a switch is on. It stops itself 2 minutes after Catch, Spin, Perfect Throw, Tap to Move and Gym are all off.

**3. Alerts** (a second channel: heads-up, with sound), one per change, never again while the state holds
- `why=` turning into a reason that stops the catching: storage full, no balls, every throw fleeing, the game not answering, a game version the catcher cannot hook, the safety pause, the daily spin limit.
- Never an alert: "no Pokemon in range", a paused map, refused spins, "PoGo is not open", starting, "can't reach the game".
- `sp=` going 1 -> 0 (the Star Piece ran out).
- The gym status line starting with `STOPPED`.
- An Alerts switch on the screen (the app's own SharedPreferences) turns the alert posts off; the status notification stays.

**4. Around it**
- versionCode 5 / 1.4. Permissions: `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. The service is not exported.
- `build.ps1` compiles every source file under `src` (three now).
- README: one row for the notification and the alerts.

## It needs one thing from him

Android 13+ shows no notification from this app until he allows it. The screen asks once, the first time 1.4 is opened. Until then the Alerts tile is amber and reads "NOT ALLOWED YET - Android has to allow this app's notifications first. Tap here to allow them." I did not grant it for him (`pm grant` was not used).

## Checked

On the PC:
- 202 + 123 plain-JVM checks: the notification's words, every real `why=` text of `catch_loop_fast.py` sorted into alert / no alert, the alert sequences (a hold that lapses and comes back, a Star Piece that ran out, a stop line rewritten with a newer time), save and load.
- The `catcher_ctl.sh` sandbox run: ALL OK.

On the phone (he was playing; no Activity was opened, no input was sent, no switch was flipped, nothing was granted):
- `adb install -r` of this build: versionCode 5 confirmed, same signer as 1.2 and 1.3.
- The screen drawn off screen with RenderProbe: the real state, demo 1, demo 2, the fold-out. PoGo stayed the focused window.
- ONLY the service started, as root (`am start-foreground-service -n com.benny.autocatcher/.StatusService`):
  - `dumpsys activity services`: `isForeground=true`, `types=0x40000000` (specialUse), a notification on channel `status` with `actions=3` and a BigTextStyle.
  - the app's log line: `status: in the shade: 964 caught - 13.2/min - Star Piece OFF | +542,950 stardust - 7.4K/min - Balls 2,975 / 5 / 5 | buttons: Catch off, Spin off, Gym on -- HIDDEN: notifications are not allowed for this app yet`
  - `dumpsys notification`: both channels registered (`alerts` importance 4, `status` importance 2); no posted record, because notifications are not allowed yet.
  - the alert state the service saved holds the phone's real `sp=0`.
- `catcher_ctl.sh` deployed without a restart (comments only changed), its `status` verb read back.

## Not proven on the phone

- A notification on the screen, a tap on one of its buttons, and a heads-up alert: all three need his "Allow" first, and the last two need the screen.
- Every tap on the app's screen (no input was allowed). The pictures are off-screen drawings of the real views.
- After a phone restart, or 2 minutes after every switch went off, the notification comes back when the app is opened again; nothing starts it at boot.

author: braghettos
body:
All three axes are measured at or through 0.84.0, so the pin moves.

**Why it moves at all:** 0.67.0 was clean on oasgen#818 only because it **predated** the defect. That is luck, not coverage. 0.84.0 carries #825, the fix, and the `0.75.0–0.83.1` boundary becomes history.

| axis | result |
|---|---|
| shape | 0.67.0 ≡ 0.83.1, 51 assertion lines byte-identical |
| reconcile | fresh install at **0.84.0**: 4 created and observed, drift corrected, 4 deletes verified 404, residue 0, `pin_verify exit=0` |
| in-place upgrade | 0.67.0 → 0.84.0: `generatorBuild` moved 4/4, 8/8 CRD schemas byte-identical, 4/4 CRs survived with the same uid and `generation` 1, 4 drifts corrected, 4 deletes verified 404 |

### This is not a find-and-replace

54 occurrences across 15 files, read and classified individually — because **four are measurements at 0.67.0**, and bumping those would convert a measurement into a claim about a version nobody measured.

**Moved:** the workflow's `CURRENT PIN` + `OASGEN_VERSION` (which `validate.py` cross-checks), `pin_verify.sh`'s `PIN` default, 8 `helm --version` args and 19 prose pin references across README, usage, getting-started, troubleshooting, authentication and the example README.

**Deliberately not moved**, each read before being left alone:

- `tests/compositions/*` — *"At the 0.67.0 pin LoadBalancer settles at…"* is a measurement. Relabelled as measured-at-0.67.0, **not** re-measured at 0.84.0.
- `composition_rollup_probe.sh` — its pin paragraph argued for running at the pin rather than at oasgen's newest, which the move invalidates. Rewritten: the probe follows the pin, and its one result is 0.67.0 + cdc 2.13.114 **history**, not a statement about the pinned version.
- `check_retracted.py` — a historical illustration, relabelled "then-current".
- `validate.py` — regex **fixtures** using 0.67.0 as sample data, plus prose about a past bug.

### The six frozen-field statements are retired — on a measurement, not on #837's changelog

`docs/release.md` said they may be retired by a release carrying #837 **"and not before"**, and that the current claims were *measured from the served schema*. So I read the served CRD at 0.84.0 field by field, with `spec.resource`'s ten rules as the positive control:

| field | rule at 0.84.0 | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `spec.resourceGroup` | `self == oldSelf` | immutable |
| `spec.resource.kind` | `self == oldSelf` | immutable |
| `spec.resource.identifiers` | `self == oldSelf` | immutable |
| `spec.resource.additionalStatusFields` | `size(self) >= size(oldSelf) && oldSelf.all(i, v, self[i] == v)` | **append-only** |
| `spec.resource.includedSpecFields` | the same rule | **append-only** |
| `spec.resource.excludedSpecFields` | none | mutable (0.72.0, #666) |
| `spec.resource.configurationFields` | none | mutable (0.84.0, #837) |

**Two of the six were wrong in a second way nobody had noticed:** `additionalStatusFields` and `includedSpecFields` are append-only, never immutable, and three sites called them immutable. `docs/live-cluster-test.md` already had the first one right.

`identifiers` stays immutable **deliberately** — adding one can orphan a live CR, removing one is oasgen#444's measured case where a CR adopted another object, reported `Synced=True` and deleted it. No safe direction.

`pin_verify.sh`'s directory-vs-overlay rationale **rested on the retired rule**. The directory is kept on a reason that doesn't: an overlay leaves the cluster holding both definitions, so which one a controller used becomes an inference from ordering. Switching to an overlay is now a separate decision, not something #837 forbids.

### And a correction to a doc merged hours ago

`docs/safe-observation.md` (#107) said the runtime behind a release *"cannot be read from the RDC source repositories"* and was *"a question to answer on a cluster"*. core-provider answered it from the image itself:

```
rest-dynamic-controller:0.84.0  ->  unstructured-runtime v1.27.1
```

**So the management-policy create/update gate is NOT live at this new pin** — only delete is honoured. A reader setting `management-policy: observe` here still gets creates and updates, and the doc now says so under the pin it applies to.

The live source **is** readable: the monorepo `krateo-platformops/oasgen-provider` under `go/rest-dynamic-controller/`. I had been reading two frozen repositories and generalised "neither is the source" into a claim about all of them. Boundaries differ per surface — REST waits for an RDC carrying v1.28.1; compositions have the gate from core-provider **2.13.115** (2.13.114, which our probe pins, is v1.27.1).

author: jafargas
body:
## Summary

SQLite flattened the FROM-clause KNN subquery in the sqlite-vec backend into its join with `vec_index`. The plan then put `vec_index` (searched by tenant) in the outer loop and ran a full KNN scan of `vec_artifacts` once per tenant row. That made each query O(n²) in the number of vectors.

The problem showed up in a sandbox with 3,993 skills. The semantic overlap startup pass stored nothing after 12 minutes at 98% CPU, and a goroutine dump showed it inside `SQLiteVec.QueryModel`. Measured against that database:

| Query | Plan | Time |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Before | `SEARCH vi`, then `SCAN vec_artifacts` per row | 19.4 s |
| KNN alone | `SCAN vec_artifacts` | 4.7 ms |
| After | `MATERIALIZE va`, then `SEARCH vi` | 15.8 ms |

`Query` (hybrid search) and `QueryModel` (search during a model switch, and every semantic overlap computation) now share `knnJoin`, which runs the KNN in a `MATERIALIZED` common table expression. Results are unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestSQLiteVec_KNNRunsBeforeTheTenantJoin` pins the query plan: the KNN is materialized and scanned before the `vec_index` search. Against the old query the plan leads with `SEARCH vi` and has no `MATERIALIZE` step, so the test fails. It also checks the nearest match.
- The `pkg/vector` conformance suite, plus the `SemanticOverlap`, `Hybrid`, and `Search` e2e suites, pass. `make lint` is clean.

author: jesusmanuelrg
body:
Fixes #46.

`download_datasets` writes to a `.tmp` file through `tqdm.wrapattr(open(...))`. `wrapattr` closes the progress bar but not the stream it wraps, so the file is still open when `os.rename` runs. Unix allows that. Windows does not and raises `PermissionError: [WinError 32]`.

The file is now opened in its own `with` block and closed before the rename. The `with` blocks are nested because `requires-python` is `>=3.8`, which rules out parenthesized context managers.

I have not run this on Windows. On Unix I checked, with the download mocked, that the temp file is still open at the `os.rename` call on `master` and closed with this change. The repo has no test suite, so I did not add one.

author: juanlo7
body:
Closes #233

**Stacked on #238** (needs `LLM_MODE=auto` and the Groq settings): review after it; GitHub retargets this PR to `main` once #238 merges. Suggested merge order: #237, #238, this, #235.

## What and why
Aiven (API + Valkey) runs on trial credits, and Vercel cannot host the backend (no scheduler, writes only to a per-instance temporary folder, 300 s limit). Everything moves to **one free Render web service** that builds the existing `Dockerfile` and serves the web app and the API, so anyone on the team can deploy their own copy in one click.

- `render.yaml`: Docker, free plan, health check `/api/health`, `CALA_MODE=replay`, `LLM_MODE=auto`, `DEMO_MODE=1`; asks for `DEMO_DB_URL` and the two optional free AI keys.
- `Dockerfile`: downloads the Cala snapshot from `DEMO_DB_URL` (Render passes env vars as build args), else keeps using a local `data/grabbit.db`; `LLM_MODE` now comes from the settings default.
- `.github/workflows/keepalive.yml`: optional, off unless the `KEEPALIVE_URL` repository variable is set; pings every 14 min to skip the ~1 min cold start.
- `docs/deploy.md`: deploy your own copy, pointing grabbit.cloud at Render (DNS steps in IONOS), Vercel and Aiven as legacy.

Checked with the real image (this branch plus #237), built with `DEMO_DB_URL` served locally and run with `-m 512m` and no keys: health lists `["scripted"]`, the web app serves, the 3 demo steps answer with no errors, report of 5 startups, **about 70 MB of the 512 MB**.

**To go live (needs Render and IONOS access):** create the Blueprint from `main` after the merges, add the custom domains in Render, then change the DNS in IONOS as `docs/deploy.md` > "Custom domain" says.

## Tests that protect this
`backend/tests/test_render_blueprint.py`: every env var in `render.yaml` is a setting the app reads (it failed on `main` before #238, as it should), the health check is a real route, and the service port matches the image's.

## Checklist
- [x] `make test lint` passes
- [x] Contract, mocks and `.env.example` updated if affected (not affected)
- [x] New dependency or service added to README "Built with" (Render: in #234 with the README rewrite)

author: manuel-bot-user
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [cert-manager](https://cert-manager.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager)) | HelmChart | patch | `v1.21.0` → `v1.21.3` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>cert-manager/cert-manager (cert-manager)</summary>

### [`v1.21.3`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/tag/v1.21.3)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/compare/v1.21.2...v1.21.3)

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

v1.21.3 removes trust in the compromised eMudhra CA (see [eMudhra Compromise](https://cert-manager.io/docs/trust/trust-manager/#emudhra-compromise)). The updated base images no longer include the "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" root certificate. Go 1.26.10 also makes `crypto/x509` reject certificate chains that pass through the compromised intermediates ([CVE-2026-111943](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6809)).

It also fixes an ACME ARI renewal loop, stops the controller copying a private key from a Secret that the Certificate does not own, and quotes the proxy values in the Helm chart. It updates Go and several dependencies to fix reported security vulnerabilities.

All users should upgrade.

#### Changes by Kind

##### Bug or Regression

- Added `status.acme.ari.certID` to track issuance of new certs and re-fetch ARI from CA. This fixes a renewal loop where a stale ARI window from the previous certificate triggered repeated re-issuance until the CA rate limit was hit. ([#​9292](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9292), [@​hjoshi123](https://redirect.github.com/hjoshi123))
- Helm chart: quote the `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` and `no_proxy` values when rendering the controller Deployment env vars, so values like `*.example.com` no longer break the manifest. ([#​9407](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9407), [@​pujitha24](https://redirect.github.com/pujitha24))
- The `requestmanager` and `issuing` controllers now only consume the Secret named by `status.nextPrivateKeySecretName` when it carries the `cert-manager.io/next-private-key` label and is owned by the Certificate, matching the invariant the `keymanager` controller already enforces. Previously a principal able to write the `certificates/status` subresource, but not to read Secrets, could name any Secret in the namespace and have its private key copied into `spec.secretName`. The `keymanager` controller no longer creates the next private key Secret under the name in `status.nextPrivateKeySecretName`. It always uses a generated name, records a `NotOwned` Warning event when the field names a Secret it does not own, and repoints the field at the Secret it owns rather than deleting that Secret when the two disagree. The Secret named by `spec.secretName` is never treated as a next private key Secret, even if `spec.secretTemplate` labels it as one. ([#​9368](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9368), [@​wallrj](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj))

##### Other (Cleanup or Flake)

- Upgrade Go to 1.26.9, fixing CVEs in the crypto/tls, net/http, net/textproto and html/template packages. ([#​9444](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9444), [@​wallrj-cyberark](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj-cyberark))
- Upgrade Go to 1.26.10, fixing a CVE in the crypto/x509 package. ([#​9501](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9501), [@​wallrj-cyberark](https://redirect.github.com/wallrj-cyberark))
- Bump `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0 to fix reported security vulnerabilities ([#​9451](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9451))
- Bump `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace` and `otlptracegrpc` to v1.45.0 to fix a reported security vulnerability ([#​9374](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9374), [#​9375](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9375))
- Update distroless base images, removing the compromised "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" root certificate ([#​9351](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9351), [#​9414](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9414), [#​9493](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9493), [#​9495](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9495))

### [`v1.21.2`](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/tag/v1.21.2)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/compare/v1.21.1...v1.21.2)

cert-manager is the easiest way to automatically manage certificates in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

v1.21.2 fixes controller and webhook panics, data races, ACME renewal and HTTP-01 solver bugs, and a Gateway API dnsNames bug. It stops the ACME and Vault issuers copying untrusted HTTP response bodies into status conditions and Events, and tightens ambient AWS credential use for namespaced Vault Issuers. It also updates Go and several dependencies to fix reported security vulnerabilities.

All users should upgrade.

#### Changes by Kind

##### Bug or Regression

- ACME Issuer response bodies are no longer reflected into Issuer status conditions or Kubernetes Events. Only ACME problem documents are surfaced (bounded in length); other responses are reported by HTTP status code alone, with the full error available in the controller logs. ([#​9239](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9239), [@​FelixPhipps](https://redirect.github.com/FelixPhipps))
- Cap ACME server response bodies at 16 MiB to guard against unbounded-body denial-of-service. ([#​9222](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9222), [@​FelixPhipps](https://redirect.github.com/FelixPhipps))
- De-duplicate dnsNames when multiple Gateway/ListenerSet listeners share a Secret ([#​9234](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9234), [@​speer](https://redirect.github.com/speer))
- Fix certificate renewal windows using February 29 cron schedules across non-leap century years. ([#​9240](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9240), [@​wieghx](https://redirect.github.com/wieghx))
- Fix validating webhook panics when AdmissionReview requests omit optional fields, by routing identity, approval, and resource validation on the always-present Resource/SubResource fields and denying (rather than silently allowing) requests with an unset or mismatched resource. As a side effect, validation is now also enforced for equivalent-converted requests on non-v1 API versions, which previously could skip validation. ([#​9235](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9235), [@​lunarwhite](https://redirect.github.com/lunarwhite))
- Fixed HTTP-01 solver cleanup so that a solver ingress, pod or service that has already been deleted no longer fails the cleanup with a NotFound error. ([#​9278](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9278), [@​arpitjain099](https://redirect.github.com/arpitjain099))
- Fixed a bug where `replaces` field was being populated for the wrong issuer on issuer changes ([#​9236](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9236), [@​hjoshi123](https://redirect.github.com/hjoshi123))
- Fixed a data race in the ACME HTTP-01 self-check that could occur when custom DNS servers were configured. ([#​9313](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/9313), [@​shashankvarma499](https://redirect.github.com/shashankvarma499))
- Fixed a panic in the certificates-issuing controller when a CertificateRequest has a failure time set but no Ready c

author: jdeast
body:
## Problem

On the ubuntu Python 3.14 legs, all three tests in `tests/test_sbc_smoke.py` keep erroring at setup with `Failed: Timeout (>600.0s) from pytest-timeout`. Master runs 43909944076, 44372891494 and PR #611's run 44382820961 all show it, and so do several nightly runs on the unchanged e89acdae (11-11, 11-13, 11-14). The failure follows whichever shard holds the file.

## Root cause

Python 3.14 changed the default `multiprocessing` start method on Linux from `fork` to `forkserver`. The module fixture calls `pm.sample` 21 times with `cores=2`: one prior run plus 20 replicates. pymc passes `mp_ctx=None`, so each call starts two worker processes with the platform default. A forkserver worker re-imports pymc/exozippy and rebuilds the compiled model on every call.

Evidence:

- Fixture setup time from the `--durations` transcripts of the last ~30 master runs:
  - ubuntu 3.12: 112-387 s
  - ubuntu 3.14: 226-606 s, with roughly 2.5-4x the 3.12 time in the same run
  - 3.14 has been within ~100 s of the limit since at least 2026-11-08 (599.31 s on b567b749; 600.33 s timeout on c71244d3).
  - The pass or fail outcome on 3.14 is just runner variance around 600 s. It is not a regression in the fixture, and it is not caused by the #607 durations refresh.
- Per-replicate fit times printed by the failing 3.14 jobs: 20-34 s each, and 67-88 s for replicate 0.
- Local reproduction on CPython 3.12, same model, with only `mp_ctx` forced:
  - `fork`: 2-4 s per `pm.sample` call
  - `forkserver`: 44-49 s per call (5 replicates: 81 s vs 239 s)
- Dependency versions on the 3.14 legs (pymc 6.3.2, pytensor 3.3.6, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.18.1) are the same in passing and failing runs.

## Fix

Set `cores=1` in the fixture so the two chains run sequentially in the test process. This model samples 2 x 600 iterations in a second or two, so worker processes only ever cost time here. The fixture now runs 123 s locally (3.12, all 21 calls "Sequential sampling"; all three tests pass), and its cost no longer depends on the start-method default.

`examples/validation/sbc.py` itself is unchanged. The full cluster runs choose their own `--cores`.

author: krisztiankoos
body:
## Outcome

Read-only AGY review tasks with a complete findings response now settle as done when AGY exits zero with a clean terminal ERROR. The task record retains the sanitized terminal error in `transport_warning`. Missing, truncated, schema-invalid, or model-mismatched results stay failed.

The adapter already preserved the terminal response. The worker rejected it solely because the terminal status supplied an error. The worker now validates the response with the existing findings validator and applies the normal settlement gates before recording the warning.

## Proof

- Before the change, the record-based stream fixture reproduced failed settlement for both terminal error classes. After the change, the focused pytest run passed all 107 selected AGY tests, including the new settlement cases.
- Ruff passed using the CI configuration. The local tree scan covered 1,860 files and reported zero findings.

## Design charter

The tests own their input data and use a temporary checkout. The recovery uses the existing review schema and provider diagnostic classifier. It fails closed on malformed streams, incomplete work, invalid findings, and existing boundary or model checks.

## Review

- Round 1 of the review of record was Claude Opus 5.5 via native Claude, at `11bf5825` (2.47 minutes). It approved and raised one P3 coverage gap. The updated fixture covers incomplete commands, model-selection refusals and unrecognized terminal statuses.
- Round 1 advisory review was Gemini 4 Carbon via AGY at `11bf5825` (16.85 minutes). It found three issues, all fixed at `8fc0ba2b`. F1 (P1) now requires the actual process to exit zero without a linger kill. F2 (P2) keeps over-deep response JSON on the failed path. F3 (P2) makes the fixture supply its own interpreter. The review of record did not raise these three findings.
- Round 2 of the review of record was Claude Opus 5.5 via native Claude at `8fc0ba2b` (1.45 minutes). It approved with no findings and independently passed all 12 settlement cases. The focused run at this head passed all 112 selected AGY tests, including 12 settlement cases.
- The first merge-group run failed three existing AGY boundary-receipt tests. The supervisor gave injected providers a keyword outside the parser contract. The repair at `66890f0c` preserves that contract and keeps the read-only, actual-zero-exit and linger checks in settlement.
- Round 3 of the review of record was Claude Opus 5.5 via native Claude at `66890f0c` (2.13 minutes). It approved with zero findings and independently passed all 12 settlement and three boundary-receipt cases.

author: patrickdereuver98-lab
body:
Dit is de rest van de UX-audit van november. Het rapport staat in [`docs/audit-ux-2026-11.md`](docs/audit-ux-2026-11.md); G1, G2 en K1 zitten al in 0.9.1. Deze PR verandert geen data of schema: er zijn geen migraties en geen edge functions.

`origin/acceptatie` (0.9.1) is in deze branch samengevoegd. De conflicten in de plekpagina zijn opgelost in de lijn van #157:
- Delen zit in de actierij en stuurt nu ook tekst mee.
- Het kaartpaneel houdt het omhoog en omlaag vegen van #157 en krijgt daarnaast opzij vegen naar de vorige en volgende plek.

**Voor bezoekers** (alles blijft op het toestel, er gaat niets naar de server)
- **Zoekvak**
  - Eerder gezocht en laatst bekeken, met de knop "Wis geschiedenis".
  - Filters in gewone taal, zoals "gratis texel met stroom" of "zonder vertrektijd zeeland". Wie alleen "honden" typt, krijgt de suggestie "Filter: honden welkom".
  - Kopjes in de suggestielijst en het getypte deel vet.
  - Tikfouten werken ook bij plekken; een exacte plekmatch staat bovenaan.
  - `/` opent het zoekvak en Home/End werken in de lijst. Een postcode wordt meteen opgezocht.
- **Zoeken**
  - Het tabblad Zoeken gaat naar je laatste zoekopdracht met filters.
  - De zoekbalk schuift weg bij omlaag scrollen.
  - Meer plekken laden vanzelf.
  - Bij meer dan 40 plekken: "Zoek in deze plekken".
  - De kaartknop toont het aantal: Kaart (n).
  - "Gegevens van … Ververs" als de plekken uit de cache komen (ook op Dichtbij); de service worker gaat dan langs het netwerk.
  - In de lege staat staat "Binnen 50 km" voorop.
- **Kaart**
  - Knop naar mijn locatie.
  - "Zoek in dit gebied" na zelf schuiven.
  - Vorige en volgende plek in het kaartpaneel.
- **Plek**
  - Foto's schermvullend: vegen, dubbeltik zoomt, terug sluit.
  - Vorige en volgende uit je laatste zoekresultaten.
  - "Nog x uur om vandaag aan te komen", alleen als de laatste aankomsttijd bekend is.
  - Delen stuurt de vertrekregel en de prijs mee.
  - Kopieerknop bij het adres.
  - Snelmenu door lang indrukken of rechtsklikken op een plek in de lijst.
- **Mijn reis**
  - Ongedaan maken na weghalen.
  - Volgorde slepen aan het greepje; de pijltjes blijven. Dit lost open punt 129 op.
  - Delen als tekst.
  - In je agenda zetten (.ics).
  - Op een reisdag bovenaan wat er vandaag speelt.
  - Aantal stops op het app-icoon.
- **Dichtbij** onthoudt zijn keuzes.
- **App**
  - Delen vanuit Google Maps naar VrijStaan (Android, `/delen`).
  - Een eenmalige tip voor het beginscherm op de iPhone.
  - Een duidelijkere offlinebalk.
  - De Enter-knop op inlog- en codevelden zegt wat hij doet.

**Wat anders is dan het rapport voorstelde**
- De statusbalk `black-translucent` is niet gedaan. Die wacht op een test op een echte iPhone (LANCERING 3.2).
- Het snelmenu heeft geen eigen ⋯-knop, zodat de vertrekregel niet smaller wordt.

**Controle**
- `npm run check` is schoon.
- `npm test`: 535 geslaagd.
- `VRIJSTAAN_OFFLINE=1 npm run build` slaagt.
- Volledige e2e: 280 geslaagd en 16 overgeslagen. Nieuw zijn `e2e/ux-audit.spec.ts` en de bijgewerkte `e2e/gestures.spec.ts`.
- Bij het testen kwam er een echte fout boven: "Toon meer" en het vanzelf laden konden elkaar overschrijven. Die is gerepareerd.

**Documenten:** CHANGELOG (0.9.2), App Flow, het auditrapport, LANCERING 2.8 en open punt 129 zijn bijgewerkt.

author: amalsaidov
body:
**Reason for Change**:

`SelectNodes` ranks nodes created by gpu-provisioner or karpenter above plain/BYO nodes, then falls back to an alphabetical tie-break so the choice is deterministic. The provisioner check compared the two labels (`kaito.sh/machine-type` and `karpenter.sh/nodepool`) as independent dimensions:

```go
if (iCreatedByGPUProvisioner && !jCreatedByGPUProvisioner) ||
    (iCreatedByKarpenter && !jCreatedByKarpenter) {
    return true
} else if (!iCreatedByGPUProvisioner && jCreatedByGPUProvisioner) ||
    (!iCreatedByKarpenter && jCreatedByKarpenter) {
    return false
}
```

This is not a valid strict weak ordering. For a gpu-provisioner-only node `A` and a karpenter-only node `B`, both `less(A, B)` and `less(B, A)` return `true`. `sort.Slice` is then free to order the pair arbitrarily, so the intended alphabetical tie-break is skipped and the selected node depends on the input order rather than being deterministic.

Both labels describe the same thing here ("created by a provisioner, more likely to be empty"), so this collapses them into a single provisioner-created tier. The comparator is then antisymmetric and any two provisioner nodes fall back to the alphabetical tie-break, regardless of which provisioner created each one. No behavior changes for the provisioner-vs-plain, preferred, or previously-used tiers.

**Requirements**

- [x] added unit tests and e2e tests (if applicable).

Added a unit test with a gpu-provisioner node and a karpenter node, asserting the same deterministic alphabetical result for both input orders. It fails on `main` (returns the wrong node for one order) and passes with this change.

Scoped to `internal/k8s/nodes`. `go test -race ./internal/k8s/nodes/...`, `gofmt`, and `go vet` pass.

author: victortodoran
body:
Closes #319

## Summary

- `composer ci:check` now starts with `bin/ci-stamp.sh start` (drops any old stamp, notes HEAD if the tree is clean) and ends with `bin/ci-stamp.sh pass`. `pass` stamps the commit only if HEAD and the tree haven't changed and no extra arguments were passed. Composer passes `-- --filter=...` to every step, so a filtered run is never stamped.
- The stamp lives in `$(git rev-parse --git-dir)`, so each worktree has its own.
- `.githooks/pre-push` skips the checks, and prints one line saying so, only when `bin/ci-stamp.sh covers <sha>` holds for every pushed sha. That means the sha is the stamped commit and `git status --porcelain` is empty. Any other push runs `composer ci:check` as before.
- `implementing-an-issue.md` step 5 gains the one-line note.

## Evidence

- Full `composer ci:check` passed on a8f3908 (1125 tests) and wrote the stamp. Pushing that commit printed `pre-push: composer ci:check already passed on a8f3908; skipping the checks.`
- Stubbed hook runs: a different sha and an untracked file both started `composer ci:check`, and a branch deletion exited without running anything.
- Direct stamp checks:
  - `start` without `pass` (a failed run) leaves no stamp.
  - A dirty tree at `start` leaves no stamp.
  - `pass --filter=Foo` leaves no stamp.
  - `covers` is false for HEAD~1 and for a tree with an untracked file.
  - The main checkout's git dir has no stamp.

author: datmoser
body:
## Summary
`speakVoiceReply` (used in 3 of this file's 5 tests) starts `useTeleprompter`'s `requestAnimationFrame` loop. Nothing in this file, or anywhere in the project's vitest setup, ever unmounts the hook afterwards: `@testing-library/react`'s automatic cleanup only registers itself when `afterEach` is a real global, and this project doesn't set `test.globals: true` (every test file imports `describe`/`it`/`expect` from `vitest` explicitly).

The hook's own unmount cleanup is correct — it cancels the pending `requestAnimationFrame` and clears its `setInterval` — it just never ran. With the hook staying mounted, a leaked rAF is still scheduled on this file's jsdom `window` when vitest tears that environment down. If the worker running this file is reused for whatever runs next (likely under CI's lower parallelism), that pending callback fires against a torn-down environment and throws `ReferenceError: window is not defined` from unrelated code — exactly the symptom in #987 (run 44400429940), including that it's a true race: didn't reproduce locally across the many repeated runs below, consistent with "passed locally and on the next head."

Fix: explicit `afterEach(cleanup)` in this file (imported `afterEach` from `vitest`, `cleanup` from `@testing-library/react`), so each `renderHook` actually unmounts before the next test runs. Checked the other two `useTeleprompter.*.test.ts` files — neither calls `applyProgress`/starts the rAF loop, so they aren't at risk of the same leak and don't need the same fix.

Based on `chore/s7-batch` since the file this fixes was added there by #149 and isn't in `development` yet.

## Test plan
- `npx vitest run src/hooks/useTeleprompter.sleep.test.ts`, looped 50 times: clean every time.
- Full frontend suite, looped 15 times (once with `--no-isolate` to force a shared worker across files): clean every time, 50/50 files / 400/400 tests.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

— @orbit

## What

Adds hooks to the shared template features, so one template can have its own look without editing or bypassing a shared page. Every hook is additive: a template without the file or the CSS builds and renders exactly as before.

| Hook | Where | Default without it |
|---|---|---|
| `site/HeaderActions.vue` | site `Header.vue`, between the navigation and the language switch, at every width | nothing |
| `data-header`, `data-header-bar`, `data-site-name` | site `Header.vue`, `Logo.vue` | no change |
| `data-notice`, `data-notice-item` | site `Notice.vue` | no change |
| `data-footer`, `data-footer-name` | site `Footer.vue` | no change |
| `data-dish-name`, `data-sold-out`, `data-dish-price`, `data-allergens`, `data-lunch-dish` | menu `Dish.vue`, `Allergens.vue`, `LunchDays.vue` | no change |
| `menu/Top.vue`, `menu/LunchTop.vue` | menu and lunch pages, after the page header | nothing |
| `event/List.vue` (`items`) | events list page | the cards |
| `event/Header.vue` (`event`) | event page; the booking actions render after it | back link, title, facts, photo |
| `pages/Header.vue` (`id`) | free pages; the action button renders after it | page header and photo |
| `blog/List.vue`, `people/Cards.vue`, `downloads/Rows.vue` | inside `BlogPostList`, `PeopleList`, `DownloadsList` | the rows or the grid |

Also:

- `EventActions` is a new shared component: the event page's booking block (sold out, booking closed, book, phone and email), moved out of the page unchanged so it can render after a template's own header.
- `templates/_features/ui/DESIGN.md` gets a section "A template's own look": a template may set its own neutral colours, radii, fonts and type sizes in its `main.css` if it keeps the contrast rule, and the list of names and hooks.
- Decision D66 in `internals/decisions.md`.
- `pnpm templates sync` copied the changed sources into the templates. The `package.json` range rewrites that the sync also makes are not part of this change and were reverted.

## Why

The restaurant and nonprofit templates are also Lupinum's live demos and get their own designs next. Only the home page is a template's own file; every other page, the header and the footer are synced copies, and `pnpm templates sync --check` fails on any edit. Without hooks the only ways were long CSS overrides on utility class names, or a plugin that replaces the shared pages. Both go around the feature system. The hooks follow the pattern the features already use (`projects/List.vue`, `pages/Top.vue`, `event/Programme.vue`: an optional component found with `import.meta.glob`).

The two design changes come as their own pull requests on top of this one.

- `pnpm templates sync --check`: only the lines `main` shows too (the `@lupinum/*` ranges per template, the sample dates of saas and starter). No drift.

author: vv01t3k
body:
Rebuilds the web UI as the owner's **Trader Terminal** design (Remix `01 Terminal`), adapted to real data. Starts from `v2`; unrelated to #27.

## What changed

- **Layout (owner's correction applied):** full-width table with full-width source tabs under the header. The sidebar is an overlay drawer opened from the menu button (`v1-sidebar.jsx`) and is closed by default. No docked sidebar and no dead space beside the table.
- **Source tabs:** all four sources (mBank funds, CoinGecko, CoinPaprika, CoinMarketCap). Each tab shows a freshness badge from the API: `LIVE`, `CACHED 06H` for funds, `STALE` or `NO DATA`.
- **Header:** wordmark, search (`/` focuses it), live/freshness stamp in Warsaw time (`18.11.2026 · 06:02 CET`), and a sign-in stub.
- **Table controls:** mBank category chips, or crypto "Highlight <period> >" threshold chips, then the row count and a TABLE settings popover (density, sparkline on/off, visible columns).
- **Threshold highlight:** keeps every number on the same right edge. The whole cell is tinted and bolded with no badges, and the row gets an amber edge. One rounding rule drives the printed value, the colour and the threshold.
- **Table:** sortable with `aria-sort`, a sparkline per row, and pl-PL numbers (`412 840,00`, `+9,15%`, `384,00B`).
  - Rank is folded into the ticker on phones.
  - Descriptive columns drop out at tablet widths, and everything except the figures at phone widths (container queries).
  - The name column absorbs spare width, so the table never overflows from 320 to 1440px and never leaves a gap.
- **Instrument page** (`/$kind/$source/$externalId`): price, return tiles, a range-selectable price chart, and facts (mBank's named risk scale, never SRI). It resolves through history, so delisted instruments still open.
- **Drawer:** source status, the threshold slider, auto refresh (off/30s/1m/5m driving React Query `refetchInterval`), force refresh, API docs, and the stub features.
- **Footer:** API health and round trip measured from the browser, collector on/off, repo link and version.
- **Phone layout** from `mobile.jsx`: compact source switcher, headline figure (total cap + 24h for crypto, median for funds), compact table, bottom bar.
- **Stubs:** Dashboard, Watchlist, Portfolio, Alerts, Reports, Export CSV, API Keys, Preferences and sign-in are visible but disabled, each with a "coming soon" tooltip. There are no dead links and no fake data.
- **Preferences** (density, sparklines, columns, auto refresh) live in a cookie, so the server renders them on the first paint. View state (search, sort, category, threshold) stays in the URL. The search box keeps a draft; only trimmed text reaches the URL, with `maxLength` 100.
- **API:** one batched read-only endpoint, `GET /api/v1/sources/:source/sparklines?points=N` (2–200, default 24). It returns the last N values, oldest first, for every instrument in the latest snapshot, in one query. Covered by `apps/web/test/api.test.ts`.
- **Radix → Base UI** (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0) for tooltips and the settings popover. `radix-ui`, the shadcn components, cva and tw-animate-css are removed. JetBrains Mono is self-hosted (`@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono`).

## TanStack libraries considered

| Library | Decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start, Router, Query, Table | used (already) | pages, URL state, server data, column/sort model |
| Charts (`@tanstack/charts` 1.5.0) | **used** | Instrument chart: `lineY` with crosshair, tooltip and built-in pointer and keyboard inspection. Sparklines are `createChartScene` + `renderChartSvg` static SVG (no live host per row). Replaces ~300 lines of hand-drawn SVG. |
| Hotkeys (`@tanstack/react-hotkeys` 0.25.1) | **used** | `/` search, `j`/`k` and ↑/↓ row navigation, Esc clears the search. Replaces hand-written keydown listeners. |
| Pacer | rejected | Effect covers debounce and throttle; in-memory search over ≤257 rows needs no debounce. |
| Store | rejected | Prefs are a small context plus a cookie the server reads. Effect's Ref/SubscriptionRef cover shared state if it ever grows. |
| Form | rejected | Settings are a handful of toggles that apply immediately. No form submits anything. |
| Ranger | rejected | Its peer range excludes React 19 (`^16.8 \|\| ^17 \|\| ^18`), 0.0.5 is unmaintained since 2025-12, and a native range input already gives role, keyboard and value text. |
| Virtual | rejected | 257 rows lay out in 2–5 ms. Virtualizing a `<table>` breaks Ctrl+F and screen-reader row counts and complicates the sticky header. |
| DB (1.0 RC) | rejected | Read-only snapshots with no mutations or sync to manage, and still a release candidate. |

`@tanstack/charts` is used instead of the `@tanstack/react-charts` wrapper, which its own README calls a compatibility package; `@tanstack/charts/react` is the adapter. All versions are pinned exactly and are older than the bunfig `minimumReleaseAge`.

## Modern Web Guidance applied

- **Native modal `<dialog>`** for the drawer: `showModal()` and `closedby="any"`, with no hand-made focus trap or Esc handler. Backdrop and drawer use `overscroll-behavior: contain`. Entry and exit animate with `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` (`overlay`, `display`).
- **Container queries** (`container: market / inline-size`) decide which columns show from the table's own width, not the viewport.
- **`:has()`** puts the keyboard focus ring on the row whose link is focused.
- **View transitions:** `viewTransition` on source switches gives a 160 ms crossfade, disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Motion:** only transform and opacity animate. The LIVE pulse runs only with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
- **Scrolling:** `scrollbar-gutter: stable` and `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the table scroller.
- **Browser surfaces:** themed scrollbars, selection, caret and focus ring.
- **`content-visibility` was not applied to table rows.** Measured in Chrome: `content-visibility: auto` never skips an offscreen `<tr>`, because containment doesn't apply to table-internal boxes. A full relayout of all 257 mBank rows takes 2–5 ms anyway.
- The page uses Base UI's popover and tooltip, which handle collision and anchoring, so CSS anchor positioning wasn't needed.

## Learnings from #27 reused

- pl-PL formatting with one rounding rule for text, colour and threshold.
- Warsaw time.
- mBank's named risk scale.
- The most common valuation date shown dim, with exception dates in amber and never truncated.
- Freshness and stale states, with a visible notice when the last run failed.
- URL search params validated leniently, and a search draft that keeps its spaces.
- The detail page resolves via history.
- 44px targets on phones.
- No page-level horizontal scroll from 320 to 1440px. The resize sweep checks every 40px on every route, including the table's own overflow.

## Where it deviates from the design, and why

- `--dim` is `#7d858e` instead of `#6a727b`, so 10–11px labels pass 4.5:1 on the background.
- The highlight tints the cell instead of a ragged badge, per the owner's correction.
- Columns follow our data. There's no VOL 24H, which no source provides. Funds get TYPE / AS OF / 1M–1Y / MOM / UNIT; 1D, 3Y, 5Y, MAX and RISK can be turned on in TABLE settings.
- No Fullbleed/Centered layout toggle. The owner picked the full-width layout.
- The header and phone search appear on every page; the phone design has none, but search is a real feature.
- The "LIVE" stamp means "this source's data is current". Collection still runs on the source's interval.

## Verification

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run check`, `bun run test` (245 tests) and `bun run build` are all green locally.
- **New tests:**
  - the sparklines endpoint (Postgres);
  - formatting, URL search state, filters, the highlight rounding boundary, and prefs cookie round trips (`views.test.ts`);
  - a DOM test of the table (`table.test.tsx`): visible columns, settings, sort and `aria-sort`, missing values last, t

author: popematt
body:
**Issue #, if available:**

#1063 

Part of #1092 


**Description of changes:**

#1115 added `CompactText`, `LinesText`, and `PrettyText`, but only the raw text writer could use them, and that's crate-private. Users write through the managed `Writer`, so this is the change that makes the styles usable at all.

A writer with a fixed (in this case, monomorphized) style doesn't look up its whitespace at run time, and Compact and Lines writers don't track indentation. With the rest of the series applied, compared to using `RuntimeStyle` (from #1114), a writer built with a specific style is 24–37% faster for Compact and Lines, and 6–20% faster for Pretty (measured on m8g.4xlarge).

  - `Writer<E, Output, S>` gains a style parameter, `S: WriterStyle`, which defaults to `RuntimeStyle`. `Writer<E, W>`, `TextWriter_1_0`, and `BinaryWriter_1_0` all mean what they meant before.
  - `Writer::new`, `Writer::idle`, and `Writer::set_config` take an `impl IntoWriterConfig<E, S>`, which is a sealed trait. A `WriteConfig` (or anything that converts into one) infers `RuntimeStyle`, and a marker infers its own style, so neither case needs a turbofish.
  - `StyledEncoding` is a crate-private supertrait of `Encoding` that names each encoding's raw writer for a given style. Binary ignores the style.
  - The three markers, `WriterStyle`, and `IntoWriterConfig` are exported under `experimental-reader-writer`. The stable API is unchanged; the `api/` snapshots don't move.
  - The `text_write` bench gets `writer_styled/*`, and the compact `writer_per_value` and `writer_reused` cases now use `CompactText`.

The tests cover style inference for `new` and `idle`, reuse (`idle`/`attach`/`detach`) with each marker, and the existing output-pinning tests run once per marker.

Switching `encode_as`, `encode_to`, and serde to use the static styles will be a followup PR.
