author: sam-mfb
body:
Audit B1: the `ClientCommand` contract and kkt-llm-agent-command, proposed in message 4594 and approved in 4595. It is the last step of the list in 4500, and it gives `ClientConfigError::Command` a kind in place of text. The tip of `refactor` (faf98c1) is merged in, and the map data is regenerated on it.

## Already pinned
kkt-llm-agent-command's three messages were already pinned exactly in its tests. kkt-llm-agent-config's 46 messages were pinned in #643, including "claude mcp failed" through its fake host. So this pull request has no separate pin commit. Both pins pass unchanged; they now compare the error's text.

## The types
- **kkt-llm-agent-command:** `Claude::remove_server` and `add_server` return `ClaudeError`, with today's text for each kind:
  - `NotFound { retry }`: "claude was not found on PATH; install Claude Code, then retry <retry>";
  - `NotRun(io::Error)`: "could not run claude: <e>";
  - `Failed { status }`: "claude mcp failed with <status>".

  As before, it holds only the exit status, never the command's output, which may hold credentials.
- **The contract, in kkt-llm-agent-config:** `ClientCommand`'s methods return `CommandError { kind, cause }`.
  - `kind` is a `CommandFailure`: `NotInstalled`, `NotRun` or `Failed`.
  - `cause` is the implementation's own error, boxed. The error's text is the cause's.
- **`ClientConfigError::Command`** carries a `CommandError` in place of `String`. That removes the last text field 4484 left.
- **`apply_claude`:** `NotRestored` and `NotRemoved` used to clone the command's text. They now take the command's error itself. When undoing the change fails too, the error moves into whichever of the two applies. The words are the same.
- **`testing::Recorder`:** `fails` is now the `CommandFailure` to fail with, or `None`, as 4595 asked, so a caller's tests can choose the kind. The crate's fake host fails as `Failed`.
- **The program:** its `ClaudeCommand` maps each `ClaudeError` to its kind and boxes it as the cause. A new test checks each mapping and its words. kkt-install-commands' lifecycle test stand-in returns a `CommandError`.
- **New dependency:** kkt-llm-agent-command gains `thiserror`, a language-shaping library (RUST.md 7).
- **Notes:** the CHANGELOG and both crates' CLAUDE.md rows say what changed.

## Effect on existing installs
None. Every message is the same, and the command runs with the same arguments. This changes the shared Rust API only.

author: benfoster-dev
body:
Closes #750
Closes #751
Closes #752
Closes #753

## What changed
- **#750 `analytics.ts`:** `trackEvent` now queues events instead of calling the provider once per event. The queue flushes when it reaches `ANALYTICS_BATCH_SIZE` (10), `ANALYTICS_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS` (5s) after the first queued event, or on `pagehide`/`visibilitychange: hidden`, so queued events aren't lost on navigation. `flushAnalytics()` is exported, and public-key hashing is unchanged. New `analytics.test.ts`.
- **#751 `pool-slugs.ts`:** new `generateUniquePoolSlugs(pools)`. Pools with a unique short slug keep it unchanged; pools that share one get the shortest longer id tail that tells them apart. That depends only on the colliding ids, not on list order, so slugs don't swap when the list is reordered. `extractPoolIdFromSlug` and `generateStaticParams` use these slugs, and a short slug shared by two pools no longer resolves to whichever was listed last. Tests added.
- **#752 `share-url.ts`:** `buildShareUrl` adds the visit's `utm_*` params to the link unless the link already sets them. `rememberUtmParams()` stores the landing page's UTM params in `sessionStorage`; `AppShell` calls it on each navigation, so attribution survives moving away from the landing page. New `share-url.utm.test.ts`.
- **#753 `feeBumpGuard.ts`:** adds `HIGH_FEE_BUMP_STROOPS` (1 XLM), `isHighFeeBump` and `highFeeBumpWarning`. `/api/sign-fee-bump` logs an unusually high bump fee server-side and returns a `warning` field, which `requestFeeBump` logs. The bump fee scales with the caller-supplied inner fee, so this flags inflated inner fees. Tests added; the route test's `feeBumpGuard` mock gains the new export.

## Why
- One provider call per event.
- Two pools could share a URL.
- Campaign attribution was lost after the first navigation.
- An inflated sponsored fee passed silently.

## How to test
- `npm test -- src/lib/analytics src/lib/pool-slugs src/lib/share-url src/lib/feeBumpGuard src/app/api/sign-fee-bump`

Note: not run locally; I'm relying on CI. Three choices worth calling out:
- **Pool slugs:** `FarmPoolRow` still builds its links row by row from `symbol` and `contractAddress`, so for a colliding pair the list link now resolves to "not found" rather than the wrong pool. A full fix needs the farm page to pass list-aware slugs into `FarmPoolRow`.
- **Fee warning:** the high-fee warning is logged, not shown in a dialog; a UI prompt needs changes to the submit flow.
- **Pre-existing fix:** `AppShell.tsx` on `main` rendered `<ServiceWorkerRegistrar>` without importing it; the import is added here because this PR edits that file.

Also seen on `main` and not touched: `src/app/layout.tsx` imports `AppShell` twice and renders it twice, which looks like a merge leftover.

author: jakobsaadbye
body:
## Mads never stops (Rolling)
- With nowhere to go, or when told to stop (S), he rolls on the way he faces.
- If he rolls straight into a wall, he bounces off and rolls back the way he came, losing most of his speed.
- Only things that hold him stop him: stun, freeze, sleep and the like. When they end, he rolls on again.
- Mads is the only hero with the `momentum` trait, and the trait now carries this behaviour.

## Speeds
| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Base speed | 7.6 | **6.4** |
| Most bonus going straight (`MomentumBonus`) | 35% | **90%** |
| Gain per second going straight (`MomentumGain`) | 0.5 | 0.4 |
| Top speed | 10.3 | **12.2** |

He's slower to start and after turns, and faster than before once he's going straight. The tooltip and readme are updated.

## Bots
A bot playing Mads can't wait for a gap by standing still, so it rolls to and fro over the spot it would wait on, along the road rather than into it (`Bot.pace`). In a quick scratch check (3 games × 3 bots × 2 minutes), bots playing Mads crossed as often as bots playing Allan (2 against 2), with slightly more deaths (11 against 9).

## Checked
- The game compiles and all simulation tests pass.
- A new test checks that a stop order doesn't stop him, a stun does, and he rolls on once it ends.

author: kovashikawa
body:
The plugin now reads the times in a Claude Code session file as real instants. Before, it compared them as text, which gives the right order only while every time has exactly the same form. Sessions written by today's Claude Code are sent exactly as before.

This is the first of the sender hardening changes that go in before the plugin starts reading reports back from Emet.

## What changes

- A new module, `timestamps.py`, turns each time into a UTC instant once. Span building compares instants, never text
- The parser is written by hand. `datetime.fromisoformat` accepts different forms on Python 3.9 and on 3.11 and later, so the same session could be read two ways
- It reads 1 to 9 fraction digits, `Z`, and numeric offsets (`+02:00`, `+0200`, `+02`). A time with no time zone is treated as unreadable, not assumed to be UTC: Emet refuses such times, and guessing could move a trace by hours
- Every time is sent in one form, UTC with milliseconds and `Z`, which is what Claude Code writes today
- Order still follows the position in the file. Nothing is sorted by time
- An entry with no readable time takes the time of the entry before it
- A turn that cannot be built is skipped, written to the log as `turn skipped <error type>`, and counted in the status file (`skipped_turns`, `last_skipped`). `/emet:status` reports it. The session keeps advancing, and what is added later to a skipped turn is not attached to the turn before it. The guard covers any error while building a turn or a later addition, not only a missing time
- A turn whose first entry has no id gets a stable id from its byte position in the file (`turn-at-<offset>`)
- A skipped turn or addition also adds a `skipped` line, with the error's type, to the session's pending file, so a later reader does not take a turn that was never sent for a clean one
- A turn's span starts at its earliest time and a subagent's ends at its latest, so no span starts before the turn it belongs to when the clock steps back
- A session line nested too deep for the JSON reader is passed over like any other unreadable line
- A saved tool output or a subagent file that cannot be opened no longer costs the whole turn. The turn is sent with the result the session file holds, or without that subagent

## What it fixes

Three faults in the same code, none seen in real use so far. They guard against a change in the session file format, which Claude Code does not promise to keep stable.

- A turn with no usable time raised an error on every run. The session's progress was never saved, so nothing after that turn was sent
- An empty or badly formed time could be sent as is. Emet answered `400` and the whole batch, up to 500 spans, was dropped
- A turn with no id was sent under the literal id `None`, so every such turn of a session would have merged into one trace

## What is sent

No change for sessions as Claude Code writes them today; the existing tests pass unmodified. A turn that cannot be read is now left out and recorded, where before it blocked the session. Nothing new is logged beyond the error's type name, never content.

## Testing

- 68 tests in `tests/test_timestamps.py`: every fraction length from 1 to 9 digits, `Z` and numeric offsets, a turn with mixed offsets, a time with no zone, unreadable values, an entry and a prompt with no time, a turn with no times at all, a subagent with no times, any other error while building a turn, a later addition that cannot be built, a turn with no id, the time of the entry before against the first time of the turn, a clock that steps back, skips adding up within and across runs, a line nested too deep, side files that cannot be read, and the plugin's own file times
- Thirty deliberate breakages of the new code: twenty-nine were caught by a test. The one that passed swaps an instant comparison for a text comparison of two times already in the fixed UTC form, which gives the same result
- The full suite passes (271 tests), with `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` clean

## Known limits

- A skipped turn is not sent later. The count and the log line are the record of it
- The offset `-00:00` and a time zone name such as `UTC` in place of `Z` are not handled specially: the first is read as UTC, the second is unreadable

author: dutchmaxwell
body:
## What

Plan G step 11 asked: does the Rust self-play plan each seat on a fogged state (the twin of `tools/core_selfplay.gd` `_seat_view`)? **It did not.** `selfplay._pick_for` handed the one shared state straight to `plan_with_rollout` for both seats, so in a Smash & Grab game the attacker's planner could read which marker is the relic and which is the trap. Lead decision O5: fix the leak before the regression pin is recorded, so the fix is part of this PR.

## Root cause

`BattleSim.capture(viewer)` masks the attacker's view of an unrevealed secret marker (no `secret` / `carry` / `carried_by`, `secret_hidden` instead). The GD oracle kept that per seat in `_seat_view`; the Python harness dropped it. `score.rs` `role_term` reads `secret == "relic"` straight off the state, so the attacker's value and its picks depended on the hidden kinds.

## Fix

`selfplay._seat_view(core, state, player)`: the attacker's view of an unrevealed secret marker drops `secret` / `carry` / `carried_by` and says `secret_hidden` (already priced 1/n relic, 1/n trap by `role_term`). The defender, a revealed marker, and every game without a hidden marker get the very same state object. Used by `_pick_for` (planner call plus its R4 hooks) and by the fork continuation's policy steps (the twin of the GD `_fork_pick`). The shared state is never edited. A cheap gate (`state.scoring in FOG_SCORINGS`, i.e. "extract") skips the state read for every other game; a test pins that every secret-marker mission in `missions.json` is covered by that set.

## Evidence

Real game, `smash_and_grab`, seed 27, spy core around `plan_with_rollout` (robot_legions_1000 vs blessed_sisters_1000, top_k 2, horizon 1):

| | attacker planner calls that saw an unrevealed marker kind | defender calls that saw one |
|---|---|---|
| origin/main | **11 of 28** | 12 of 23 |
| this PR | **0 of 28** | 12 of 23 |

On the shared state the attacker's hand value moved 0.267 -> 0.183 when the relic and the trap swapped places, and its planned pick changed. Through its view it does not (test below).

Default games are untouched: `duel` seed 27 result digest `013f8f032589c1d7` before and after. Only `smash_and_grab` carries secret markers (checked in `assets/solo/missions.json`); its digest changes (`a8d6a43e...` -> `e690ec75...`), as it must.

## Red / green

`tests/python/test_seat_fog.py` (11 tests; 10 hermetic on the in-repo `acts_25.jsonl` board, 1 whole-game test that skips without the lists + terrain bank). Seen red by temporary plants, then reverted:

| plant | red tests |
|---|---|
| `_seat_view` returns the state untouched | 7: attacker view, revealed-marker, markers-only diff, value, pick_for hand-off, pick equality, fork |
| `_pick_for` does not call `_seat_view` (= origin/main behaviour at the planner) | 2: hand-off, pick equality |
| fork policy steps do not call it | 1: fork |
| `FOG_SCORINGS` empty | catalog pin plus every view test |
| whole game vs origin/main `selfplay.py` | `test_a_played_smash_and_grab_game_never_shows_the_attacker_a_hidden_kind` fails with "the attacker's planner read a hidden marker kind" |

Named twins of `test/core_selfplay_fog_test.gd`: `test_the_attacker_seat_cannot_read_a_hidden_marker`, `test_the_defender_seat_keeps_its_secrets`, `test_a_game_without_secret_markers_gets_the_same_object` (the GD file is deleted in step 15a, not here).

## Tests run

- `test_seat_fog.py`: 10 passed + 1 whole-game passed with `NML_AI_LISTS_DIR` set (10 passed, 1 skipped without).
- Full `core/nml-core-py/tests/python`, CI-style (`PYTHONPATH=core/nml-core-py/python`, no lists): 796 passed, 28 failed, 4 errors. The other 31 failures all also fail on unmodified origin/main code (corpus-dependent tests against local `~/selfplay_out`, same set); one more, `test_fitted.py::test_net_player_decides_which_seat_takes_the_fitted_leaf`, was caused by this change (its stub state had no `scoring`) and is fixed here (`_StubState.scoring = "end"`).
- The 61 test files that play games or touch `_pick_for`, with `NML_AI_LISTS_DIR` set (real games): 392 passed, 24 failed, 7 skipped. The same 24 node ids fail identically on unmodified origin/main code (re-run of exactly those ids on a tree with main's `selfplay.py`); they are the byte-identity / legacy-corpus tests the plan already reports red on main (m3_ref_v4/v5 etc.).
- Core under test: `nml_core.BUILD_COMMIT == 4f07db57b`, not dirty, `CURRENT_RULES_EPOCH 90` (Rust untouched in this PR).

## Not verified / notes

- No rules epoch: the change feeds the planner, it alters no rule outcome. Fresh smash_and_grab games differ from older recordings of the same seed; replays use forced picks and are unaffected. If the lead wants an epoch stamp for that, say which number.
- Sidecar rows (`features`, `board`) are still computed on the shared state, as in the GD tool. Measured on one smash_and_grab position: `core.features(...)` and `core.board_rows(...)` are identical under a relic/trap swap, so they carry no kind; not proven for every position.
- No GitHub ticket opened: the leak is fixed in this PR.

## Summary

Introduce one advisory agent workflow and a lightweight evidence-based PR handoff, preserving all existing contribution and verification hard gates.

Two record-only gotchas are included because they cost real time during this change's own verification: a stalled `flutter test` signature (disk-full host) and stale untracked bundled plugin bundles that masquerade as baseline test failures. Neither adds a check or changes behaviour.

body:
Part 1 of #205: fetch images never answers with a server error when the search comes up empty. The image source is unchanged; replacing it is a later piece of work.

## Change
- `POST /api/v1/watches/{id}/fetch-images`: when the search finds nothing, the offset is past the last result, no image downloads, or the image source raises, it answers **200** `{"message": "No images found; you can upload your own", "images": []}` and saves nothing. Found images still answer 201 as before. Unknown watch is still 404.
- `google_images.fetch_watch_images` returns `[]` for the three "nothing found" cases instead of raising.
- Watch page: the message shows under the fetch button (was a browser `alert`); the offset only advances when images arrive. Other errors (for example the rate limit) show their text in the same place.

## Tests
New `TestFetchImagesNothingFound`: search finds nothing, offset past the end, every download fails, image source raises. Each answers 200 with the message and stores no image. Backend image tests pass, lint clean; frontend lint, tsc, vitest, build pass.

Checked in a browser against a local server with no internet access (the "source fails" case): the API answered 200 with the message, and the page showed "No images found; you can upload your own".

author: lvyufeng
body:
## AI Agent Information

- **Agent/Tool**: Codex desktop.
- **Model**: GPT-6.
- **Human Reviewer**: @tengqm (review requested; no approval is implied).
- **Session Summary**: The maintainer requested a working Enflame native-host adapter, complete-model comparison against original vendor PyTorch, at least 80% relative performance, and an audit of accuracy and CPU fallbacks. The requested policy is to use FlagGems whenever qualified and vendor-generated operations for measured gaps.

## Summary

Raw JSON result payloads are archived in a [separate evidence branch on the contributor fork](https://github.com/lvyufeng/Torch-FL/tree/codex/enflame-native-host-evidence-20261119/benchmarks/host_compiler/results), pinned at `9b409b67`. The implementation diff contains code, tests, generated configuration and readable documentation only. Existing measurements remain accessible through immutable links.

Add the experimental Enflame TOPS adapter to the shared source-generated FlagGems host runtime, including its published GCU300 pointwise ABI and ordered mixed-producer submissions. Complete BF16 Qwen3-0.6B runs with nine direct FlagGems operations plus an FP32 square composition through FlagGems multiply; generated topsaten paths cover the measured precision/compiler/integer gaps. The rebased installed wheel preserves bitwise-identical full-model logits, but the 80% performance gate remains open: the reverse-order control reaches 81.85% prefill / 79.40% decode; pooling both retained runs yields 81.38% / 78.60%. The initial slower run (69.43% / 67.01%) is retained and explicitly reported.

The model config is explicit opt-in and qualifies the measured published-wheel cohort and shapes. This PR preserves all existing NVIDIA, Hygon, MetaX and Ascend adapter changes when rebasing onto `5ba9b564`.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug Fix
- [x] New Feature
- [x] Performance Optimization
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Testing
- [ ] Breaking Change

## Platforms Affected

- [x] Enflame GCU (TOPS native host, vendor codegen and model qualification).
- [x] Platform-agnostic shared host compiler/runtime and admission tests.
- [x] NVIDIA / Hygon / MetaX / Ascend: existing adapters retained; shared host behavior covered by Linux unit suites. No new hardware qualification is claimed for those platforms.

## Problem Analysis

### What was broken/missing?

The shared launcher lacked an Enflame TOPS adapter. A naive integration spent most time in Python pointwise preparation and repeated host stream drains; earlier vendor-only execution completed the model but did not prove FlagGems numerical execution. Some full-model operations also copied tensors to CPU or disagreed with vendor scalar opmath / BF16 logit rounding.

### Why did it happen?

The published Enflame driver has a distinct kernel launch, descriptor and pointwise schedule ABI. Ordinary topsaten calls conservatively synchronized both before and after submission to prevent a measured Triton-to-vendor producer race. Generic FlagGems wrapper preparation does not express all GCU300 scheduling metadata in the existing shared C++ path. In addition, the vendor library lacks general int64 arithmetic; treating it as unsupported forced host round trips. Floating scalar staging rounded attention's scale too early, while independently substituted mean/rsqrt/mm changed the model's fixed logit contract.

### Investigation process

1. Inspected the pinned published FlagGems/FlagTree wrapper and driver sources, validated their metadata/signature ABI, and built the installed wheel with CPU Torch and the verified SDK.
2. Measured complete-model runs and isolated each candidate FlagGems operation. Counted **successful SDK enqueues**, separate from launcher construction; a zero-enqueue ATen redispatch control was rejected.
3. Used separate TOPSPTI device traces and a TOPS API/transfer observer to split kernels, copies and host/submission/device-idle remainder. A warmed nine-forward audit found no tensor numerical CPU fallback, with only scalar validity/bounds checks transferred to the host.
4. Independently reproduced the strided add and cat compiler failures on **original torch_gcu + unmodified published FlagGems**, without importing Torch-FL. Direct norm/pow/mm differences remain within per-op `atol=rtol=1e-3`, so those are reported as a precision compatibility request rather than asserted upstream defects.

## Solution Design

### Implementation approach

- Package a fingerprinted TOPS launcher/module utility at build time; use the shared versioned backend manifest and preflight. Fail explicitly on unsupported compiler/descriptor/scratch/grid metadata, and forbid runtime C/C++ launcher compilation.
- Extend the shared C++ pointwise preparation with the published GCU300 schedule, preserving strides, DMA predicate, tile/MMU limits, warp rule and int64 flags. Keep the compiled published fallback for unsupported host preparation. Safely unroll the read-only variadic dtype predicate to admit source-derived C++ host entries.
- Use stream interop **ABI 2** to serialize producer submissions and record/wait per-stream TOPS events at topsaten/Triton transitions. ABI 1 transition drains and untracked-build legacy pre/post drains remain covered; errors release the submission lock and stream destruction destroys the event.
- Express device integer/argmax/scalar/pow behavior in **GCU codegen**, regenerate its artifacts and require a second generation to leave their hashes unchanged. No handwritten numerical device kernel or dependency source patch is added.
- Generate an opt-in model config with FlagGems `mul.Tensor`, `add.Tensor`, `neg`, `cos`, `sin`, `where.self`, `silu`, `_softmax` and `bmm`. Generated FP32 `pow(2)` composes through selected multiply. Mean/rsqrt/mm/cat and Int32/Int64 add keep measured topsaten paths. Only independently qualified SiLU is restored in the default config; other older-cohort/large-grid holds remain.

### Key design decisions

The runtime owns the producer boundary before removing repeated host drains, and event ordering is not enabled for ordinary untracked launchers. The measured model config stays opt-in because small softmax grids and one inference workload do not establish general platform coverage. Numerical fallback integration belongs in the platform generator, and published dependencies remain unchanged so the comparison uses the pinned cohort.

### Code changes by file

- `README.md`: Describe the experimental Enflame adapter and measured model qualification.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/configs/enflame_native_host.conf`: Ship the generated, explicit opt-in FlagGems-first Qwen3 experiment.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/enflame_api_trace.cc`: Observe TOPS API calls/transfers separately from acceptance timings.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/enflame_flaggems_probe.py`: Add strict-eager GCU comparison, operator isolation and successful-enqueue provenance.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/enflame_profile_summary.py`: Separate measured device kernels, copies and profiled wall-time remainder.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/enflame_published_gems_probe.py`: Reproduce upstream precision/compiler/layout findings with original torch_gcu.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/enflame_strided_add_probe.py`: Minimize and sweep the independent sliced-broadcast add correctness failure.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/qwen_eager.py`: Add strict-eager GCU comparison, operator isolation and successful-enqueue provenance.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/qwen_operator_census.py`: Add strict-eager GCU comparison, operator isolation and successful-enqueue provenance.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/qwen_operator_snapshot.py`: Add strict-eager GCU comparison, operator isolation and successful-enqueue provenance.
- `benchmarks/host_compiler/qwen_strict_eager.py`: Add strict-eager GCU comparison, operator isolation and successful-enqueue provenance.
- `csrc/aten/backends/enflame/gcu_copy.cc`: Preserve int64 storage through vendor 32-bit word copies and guarded device casts.

author: nikos-d
body:
## Problem
#82 keeps the tightened position band and, when a pinned start or goal lies outside it, makes the
first/last segment target that endpoint. The pinned sample then sits exactly on its bound: an active
row (c = 0) with zero gradient, since the endpoint cannot move. NLopt's SLSQP mishandles such a row:
when the linearised subproblem is otherwise consistent, its step is wrong, and the solve can stall
far from the subproblem's solution. Any task whose start or goal is near a joint limit (for example
a wrist at ±π with limits of ±3.1416) has such an endpoint.

## Change
- `tighten_for_success_tolerance`: besides tightening the limits (unchanged), computes once the
  position bounds the solver enforces, `Optimization::solver_position_min/max`. A side whose
  tightened bound the pinned start or goal lies on or outside is widened, for the whole trajectory,
  to halfway between that endpoint and the true limit. An endpoint at (or within a few ulps of) the
  true limit is not widened: there is no room, and no trajectory from it passes the true-limit
  validation. `solver_position_min/max(opt, joint)` return these while tightened and the limits
  otherwise.
- `position_constraint_params(opt, joint)`: `c = max(p - upper_bound, lower_bound - p) * inv_half_range`,
  with `inv_half_range` from the tightened limits. c is continuous, 0 at each bound, and has the
  same slope on both sides. On a side that is not widened, c = `success_tolerance` exactly at the
  true limit. On a widened side the pinned endpoint is strictly inside (c < 0), and the solver may
  accept a position past the true limit by less than the tightening; the validation on the true
  limits decides there. The same for every segment and sample: computed once per evaluation. The
  `segment` / `n_segments` parameters, `target`, and `position_constraint_params_at_point` are removed.
- `decision_bounds`: the control-point box uses `solver_position_min/max`.
- The success check is unchanged: the output trajectory is still validated on the true limits and
  geometry every `output_steps_ms`.
- `docs/guides/constraints.md` describes the new rule.

## Tests
- `test_optimization_tightening_contract`: per joint, the bounds are the tightened or widened ones,
  c = 0 at the bounds with the same slope on both sides, c = `success_tolerance` at the true limit
  on a side that is not widened, start and goal strictly inside. Also: asymmetric limits with the
  start at the true limit (not widened, finite), an endpoint on the tightened bound (widened), and
  a goal 3.6e-9 rad inside the limit (widened). Fails on main, passes here.
- `test_decision_bounds`: the box follows `solver_position_min/max`.
- `ci-gcc` and `ci-float`: 25/25. ASan + UBSan: 25/25, no reports (with #96; on main alone every
  test aborts on the aligned_alloc bug that #96 fixes).

## Impact
Only the tightening of position limits changes. Dynamics and forward kinematics are untouched, so
blast-playground is not affected. No Python API change.

author: dannyroberts
body:
Deploys could only use the public `dimagi/commcare-hq` repo. This adds `cchq <env> deploy --private-repo --commcare-rev=<branch>` (and the same options on `deploy-diff`), which deploys a branch of the repo set as `private_code_repo` in the env's `fab-settings.yml`. Deploys without the flag are unchanged.

How it works:
- **Servers** authenticate with a read-only GitHub deploy key stored as the `private_code_repo_deploy_key` secret. The key is used only for the top-level clone (deploy keys are single-repo), with strict host key checking against the bundled `github_known_hosts`. The private mirror is seeded from the existing commcare-hq mirror so the first clone isn't a full fetch.
- **The control machine** uses the deployer's own GitHub SSH key (via the forwarded agent) and plain git, not the GitHub API, so no token is needed for the private repo. It keeps a commit-only cache of commcare-hq history (~55 MB, at `~/.cache/commcare-cloud/`), fetches the private revision into it, and finds the public commit the branch is based on. Missing config or an unfetchable revision fails before anything is recorded or announced.
- **Deploy diff** compares public commits as usual, so it lists the public PRs being deployed; commits only in the private repo are not listed. For these deploys the diff link is labeled "Public changes only", with the number of private-only commits and the commit that was actually deployed. Sentry gets the same public commit list. The next normal deploy after a private one also gets a real diff, by mapping the deployed commit back to its public base.
- **Release tags** are pushed to the private repo.

Things to flag in the diff:
- `git_setup_release` now applies `key_file` only to the top-level repo, not submodules, and adds `IdentitiesOnly=yes`. No environment uses the existing `deploy_keys` mechanism today, so this shouldn't change any current behavior.
- `deploy-diff` previously had no `--commcare-rev` and silently ignored it. It now accepts it.
- The first private-repo deploy on each host copies the commcare-hq mirror's objects (`--dissociate`), which takes a few minutes and uses roughly double the mirror's disk.

Testing: unit tests cover the CLI routing and early exits, key scoping and mirror seeding in `git_setup_release`, and the private/public commit resolution (against local git repos). The resolution was also checked against the real private repo, and a `--private` release was built on staging from a private branch. A full staging deploy hasn't been run yet.

##### Environments Affected
staging, production, india, eu (`private_code_repo` added to `fab-settings.yml`; no behavior change unless `--private-repo` is used)

- [ ] If the changes affect multiple environments, I will ensure they are rolled out consistently across all environments.

author: limincode
body:
## Summary

The user asked for the rarely used animation controls to leave the root of the right-click menu: **Play animation, Switch character, Playback speed, Size**, together with **Fish controls**.

The menu layout allows only one level of submenus; a deeper tree makes the resolver fall back to the two-item safe menu. So the four items are not wrapped together with Fish controls in a new submenu. Instead they move **into** the existing "Fish controls" submenu as its first group, separated from the original controls by a divider. The root menu loses four items, and all five things the user named now sit in one secondary menu.

## What changed and why

- **`pet/menu_templates/modern-default-v1.json`**: removed `animations_hub`, `character`, `playback_speed` and `size` from the root. Added them, in that order, at the top of `pet_controls`, followed by a new separator `default.separator-animation`. The original ten controls keep their order.
- **Saved layouts are not rearranged.** The resolver keeps every action a saved layout already has where the user put it, and only inserts actions that are new to the default. So the new default reaches users who never saved a layout; a saved layout stays as it is. A test now pins this.
- **Tests:**
  - `test_menu_layout.py`:
    - **New:** the default tree and the real `QMenu` have the four items at the top of "Fish controls", followed by a separator; each still opens its own submenu; the root has none of them.
    - **New:** a saved layout with the items at root keeps them at root.
    - **Updated:** the default-template, resolved-node and rendered-menu expectations.
  - `test_desktop_pet_features.py`: the animation submenu and its lazy leaf-icon test now reach "Play animation" through "Fish controls".
  - **Leftover from #81, fixed:** the `compact_semantic_groups` baseline still monkeypatched `registry.QDesktopServices`, which #81 removed. So it failed early with `AttributeError` instead of its known baseline reason (`列队`, the "line up" item). The stale patch is gone, and the test fails only for its old reason again.
- **Docs:** `docs/settings-and-menu.md` describes the default grouping and that editing the default does not move items in saved layouts; `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Performance

- **Opening the menu:** the default menu builds the same actions as before. Four of them now sit one level down, so opening the root menu creates four fewer top-level entries. The animation and character submenus still fill lazily on open; the lazy-icon test asserts no animation is decoded when the root opens.
- **Other costs:** nothing new on any timer, thread, disk or network path. This is a template data change, so no number was measured.

## Real-machine run

**Pet started from this branch:** pid 22232, confirmed in `pet-overlay-gate.log`. 0 ERROR lines; 1 WARNING, a startup slow tick.

**The real config's layout, resolved read-only with this branch's code:**

```
source user
root ['ojingjing', 'rally_pets', 'lineup_pets', 'chat', 'animations_hub', 'character', 'playback_speed', 'size', ...]
```

**Finding:** the user's config now holds a saved `context_menu_layout`. It was written at 11:30 today and is node-for-node identical to the current default. Earlier today it had none. With this PR alone the user's menu would therefore not change.

**Investigation:** I tried to reproduce how an unchanged default became a saved layout, using this branch's code:

- a fresh config;
- a copy of the real config with the layout cleared;
- `include_ai` both off and on;
- in each case, opening the settings window and saving without changes.

Every attempt stored `None`, as intended. The likely source is a settings window that was opened earlier and still ran older code; it is a separate process that outlives pet restarts. The cause was not reproduced.

**After merge (follow-up on the machine):** the plan is to clear that identical saved layout while the pet is stopped, so the user follows the new default. Nothing is lost, because it equals the default. The outcome is reported to the user, not in this PR.

**Not opened by hand:** the right-click menu, because that needs real mouse input. The real `QMenu` is built from the template in the new test.

## Tests

- `ruff check pet tests scripts`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- **Red first:** before the template change, the new grouping test failed (the root still had all four ids).
- **Affected families** (39 files: every `*menu*`, `*context*`, `sprite_menu*`, tray, i18n/English, config, architecture and PR-report test, plus desktop-pet features and the animation-path tests): 511 passed, 3 failed. All 3 also fail on `main`:
  - `compact_semantic_groups` (now failing again at its known `列队` index);
  - `three_column_masonry`;
  - `test_compact_ai_provider_controls_stay_inside_their_setting_row`.
- **Full suite skipped:** this is a menu template change and its tests. No config migration, lifecycle, threading or platform branch changed, and every family that builds or resolves the menu is in the set above.

## Docs

- [x] CHANGELOG.md
- [x] Topic doc under docs/ updated (`docs/settings-and-menu.md`)
- [ ] ADR: not needed. This regroups the default menu; no feature or boundary changes.

body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #25248
* #25247
* #25246
* #25245
* #25244
* #25243
* #25242
* #25241
* #25240
* #25239
* #25238
* #25237
* __->__ #25236

With layout optimization off, which Inductor decides for a graph with few convolutions (fewer than one per 300 nodes), a stride-1 1x1 convolution is lowered as a convolution, and Inductor's autotuning offers `conv1x1_via_mm`: a Python function with no C++ shim. AOTInductor's C++ wrapper cannot emit it, so whenever it is the fastest choice the compile fails in wrapper codegen with "Expected name is not None". A single strict-FP32 512-to-32 1x1 convolution on a 5x512x3x3 input reproduces it. In a full model it appears once enough convolutions are routed to `triton::convolution` that the remaining ones fall below Inductor's threshold.

The CUDA backend gains one more scoped compile patch, like its existing Inductor workarounds: during its AOTI compile, the convolution lowering's autotuning drops extern choices without a C++ kernel or a fallback kernel when the C++ wrapper is in use. Only threads inside the backend's compile get the change, and the patch is removed when the last one leaves. Inductor offering such Python-only choices under the C++ wrapper is filed upstream as https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/204342; the patch goes once the pinned PyTorch has the fix.

`test_cuda_export.py` checks that the patch drops only those choices and only for the C++ wrapper, and lowers the reproducing 1x1 convolution with layout optimization off, which failed before.

This diff was authored with Claude Code.

## Summary

After #21 and #22, the field agent still cannot sign in. When the corrected variables were pasted into Render, `STAFF_FIELD_AGENT_PASSWORD_HASH` lost its last character: 59 of the 60 characters of a BCrypt hash. V1_3_1 copied that truncated value into `identity_access.users`, so every sign-in of `fieldstaff@inmonode.dev` fails with 401, and the failed attempts may already have locked the account.

The Render variable now holds the complete hash (saved without a deploy). Since V1_3_1 already ran, the account needs one more migration.

## Change

One production-only migration, `db/seed-prod/identity_access/V1_3_2__fix_prod_field_agent_password.sql`:
- **Guard:** while `STAFF_FIELD_AGENT_PASSWORD_HASH` is not 60 characters long starting with `$2`, it aborts with `STAFF_FIELD_AGENT_PASSWORD_HASH must hold a complete BCrypt hash before V1_3_2 runs`. This is the check V1_3_1 lacked: a truncated hash now stops the deploy instead of being stored.
- **Update:** the `FIELD_AGENT` user with `STAFF_FIELD_AGENT_EMAIL` takes the current hash, with its failed attempts and lock cleared.
- **Version 1.3.2**, applied out of order after 5.3 like V1_3_1. Only the `prod` profile loads `seed-prod`.

## Verification

Replayed with Flyway 12.4.0 on PostgreSQL 18.6 with the prod settings, starting from today's prod state: V1_3 with the template e-mail, V1_3_1 with the truncated hash, and the account locked after 5 failed sign-ins.

| Deploy | Result |

| Variable still truncated | Fails with the guard message; account and history unchanged |
| Variable corrected | Applies 1.3.2; 60-character hash that matches the password, failed attempts 0, lock cleared; V1_3 and V1_3_1 still validate |
| Next deploy | No migration pending |

body:
## Summary

Slack, both ways, behind `serve --slack`, which is off unless an operator gives it. A person files a Slack message as a note or writes one, and asks the bot to find something; the bot answers only the person who asked. Decision 165.

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| The switch | `serve --slack` with `--sign-in`, an `https://` `--public-url` and `CAIRN_SLACK_KEY`. Refused under a brand in this version. |
| One app for each workspace | The workspace's owner creates the Slack app in their own Slack workspace from a manifest cairn generates, and pastes its two secrets into cairn once; both are sealed. |
| What Slack sends | Only what a payload carries: a message shortcut's message, a slash command's text, a direct message to the bot. Four permissions; the client has no call that reads a conversation's history. |
| Who acts | A Slack user is linked to a person in two steps: the person who opens the Slack user's one-time address signed in and says yes is shown a code, once, and the same Slack user types it in Slack. A link is never moved to another person. Every action runs with that person's reach; answers are private. |
| Whose message | A message is filed only when Slack shows its author to be of the same Slack team. |
| The three addresses Slack calls | Body cap, install, then timestamp and signature for every request, before anything is parsed. A request whose signature holds is never refused; failures are counted per install and client address. |
| Not to a model unless chosen | A note from Slack is not sent to a model that arranges pages unless the operator sets `<PREFIX>_SLACK_NOTES=send`. |
| When the app goes | Secrets and links deleted at once; every note Slack created forgotten 10 days later. A removal Slack never reported is found by asking `auth.test` every 6 hours: two ended answers switch the install off, and 3 days without a bot token remove it. |

## Off means off

With the switch off there is no route, no block on the Sources page and no read of the Slack tables. The exception is the schema, which moves to step 29 for every install: an older build refuses a database a newer one opened, so going back means going back to a backup.

Existing tests changed: the pins of the schema version and table lists, one line of the reach test, one sentence of a guide test that the privacy guide's new text made untrue, and the journey's `Server` class, which gained a way to start a launcher. Nothing else.

## How it was built

Contracts first, as three acceptance files whose docstrings state the behaviour; four implementers and a second agent in separate files; the Slack facts each test relies on checked against Slack's own pages into `docs/slack-api.md`. Three things in the first plan were wrong and were changed before code was written: a claim of no history permission while asking for the one direct messages need, taking the invoker's team for the author's, and keeping notes after the app is removed.

## Outside review

A reviewer with no part in the build read the branch against Slack's published pages. First pass: two blocking faults and five lesser ones. Second pass, over the fixes: no blocking fault, one more lesser one, fixed with it.

| Found | Fixed by |
|---|---|
| Failures were counted per client address across installs, before the signature was computed: one install with a mistyped secret answered 429 to every other install's signed requests | The signature is computed for every request; a signed request is never refused; failures are counted per install and address |
| A Slack user could send their one-time address to a member, whose single yes linked the member's account to that Slack user | The yes only shows a code; the same Slack user must type it in Slack |
| The same message filed by two people at once stored a second note that removal never forgot | A message is claimed before anything is asked or written |
| A missed uninstall was never noticed | The loop asks Slack whether each bot token still works |
| An HTTP client per call, never closed | One client, made at start and closed at shutdown |
| "Ready" claimed the signing secret was proven | The page says what is proven and when, and takes both secrets again in any state |
| Sentences in the guides and decision 165 that were not true of the code | Rewritten, each with its test |

Three more implementers made the fixes to contracts written first; each finding the reviewer had reproduced with a test became the first failing test of its fix.

A second agent then reviewed the fixed branch on its own and found three more, each fixed the same way:

| Found | Fixed by |
|---|---|
| Pasting another Slack team's token into an install moved it to that team and left the first team's notes with no day to be forgotten | An install belongs to its team: another team's secrets are refused; every record keeps the team it came from; setting up again cancels the forgetting only for that team; a request keeps the team it was verified for and is refused once the install holds another |
| A note and the record that it is Slack's were two writes, so a stop between them left a note no removal finds | One transaction, through a general hook inside the store's write of a note |
| Notes from Slack fell outside the default hold that keeps source-brought text from a model that arranges pages | Held by default; sent only by a setting that names Slack |

Its patch for two of the bot's answers is in too: `unlink` says the link is undone and how to link again, and a note still waiting for its page says so.

## Evidence

- Whole suite on this branch: 10,936 passed.
- A journey on the real server process, from set-up to removal and both orders of Slack's two removal events, against a stand-in Slack on loopback.
- Not done: a run against Slack itself. No Slack app or workspace was created or used.

## Known limits (decision 165 lists them)

The compile inside a turn is not bounded, so one slower than Slack's three seconds leaves the note stored and Slack showing its own timeout; a backup made before a removal holds the notes until it ages out; an event whose handler fails after more than three seconds is lost; an install whose checks never get a clear answer is never acted on; the day an install without a token is removed is said on the Sources page only; not tried with an Enterprise Grid organisation or GovSlack; HTTP only, so a local install on 127.0.0.1 cannot be reached by Slack.

## What failed

`test_picks_saved_before_the_world_had_its_own_titles_are_drawn_again` failed once on macOS on `release/v1.5.0` and passed on the next run.

## Cause

The test put a title from the shared bank on the companion's current book, then checked that the redraw no longer showed that title. A fresh draw in a made-up city with no list of its own comes from the shared bank about four times in ten, and the timeline's seed is new on every run. So now and then the redraw picked the very same shared title again, which is correct behaviour, and the test failed.

Measured: 2 failures in 1,500 runs of the test, and 0.2% in a 20,000 seed simulation of the pick. It is not tied to the storyline bank or to macOS.

## Fix

Test only. The stale pick is now a title that no bank or city holds, so the redraw can never land on it. The app code is unchanged.

## Checked

- The test run 1,500 times after the change: 1,500 passed.
- `tests/test_media_world.py`: 9 passed. Ruff clean.

The same change goes to `release/v1.4.2` in a second PR, since the test file is identical there.

_Requested by **Andreas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Ww6NQLWNNnN3oUNMMDoMfo?thread=cmsg_01Ww6NQLWNNnN3oUNMMDoMfoW2LfsEieys79JN7wjfH5Db)_

This is the last item of workstream P (docs/handoff/APP_PARITY_PLAN_2026_11_14.md): "a tab or pane running on another machine via K7".

## What changes for the person
- Typing `ssh USER@HOST` (or `ssh -p PORT …`) in a Spindle pane logs in to that machine right in the pane:
  - the remote shell gets a real `xterm-256color` PTY at the pane's size;
  - keys go through as they are typed, Ctrl+C included;
  - resizing the pane resizes the remote PTY;
  - the pane's title becomes `user@host`.
- **SSH domains:** a line `ssh.NAME = user@host[:port]` in `spindle.conf` makes `ssh NAME [COMMAND]` log in there.
- `ssh --password` no longer echoes the password.

## Network (a policy change; please look at this part)
Until now, programs started in a terminal pane never got the network. Now:
- Spindle's `spindle` command opens the terminal window with `RUN_NETWORK`, the same way `kaleidoscope` and `sexshop` get it.
- The window asks for the network only when it starts `ssh` (`NETWORK_PROGRAMS`).
- Shell grants a terminal's run the network only when that terminal holds the network itself (`NETWORK_RUNS`). This is the same inheritance rule `sex_pdx::launch` children already follow.
- Every other program typed in a pane still runs without the network.

## Code
- `apps/ssh`: in raw mode it sends a PTY request with the pane's size, forwards raw keys from a reader thread and polls `size_changes` to forward resizes. It restores the mode on every exit.
- `crates/sex-app`: adds `relay::start_net_at`.
- `apps/term`: picks the network flag, expands SSH domains, adds help text.
- `crates/spindle-panes`: adds `Config::ssh` and `SshDomain`, with a test.
- `servers/silk-shell`: one line at the `by_program` `OP_RUN` site.
- `apps/spindle`: the `spindle` command passes `RUN_NETWORK`.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p spindle-panes`: 11 passed, including the new `config_names_ssh_domains`.
- `scripts/tests/test_relay_grant_policy.py` and `test_program_term_native_denial.py` pass.
- `term`, `ssh` and `silk-shell` type-check for their SexOS targets.
- QEMU (CI, "ssh program logs in to OpenSSH on the host"): `scripts/ssh_gate.py` now also opens a Spindle window and runs `ssh -p PORT user@10.0.2.2` there. It checks three things:
  - the PTY size reported by `[ssh.pty]` matches the pane, and the remote `stty size` agrees;
  - `echo sexos-pane-ok` runs on the remote side;
  - `exit` ends the session with status 0.

No rate, marker or semantic fingerprint moved.
- A review note, `docs/sources/provider-contract-review-2026-11-18.md`, and one changelog entry.

No price, no rate and no connector code changes.

### Verified before opening

- The daily sync was exercised end to end on macOS against the real service: setup under standing consent, the launchd agent and its plist (`plutil -lint` OK), one scheduled run started with `launchctl kickstart` (exit 0, facts accepted), a second setup leaving one job and one retained copy, and removal leaving no service, no plist and no sync directory. This closes the manual test listed in #153 as not yet run.
- On `0246cc64`, in CI's order: typecheck, the whole vitest suite (86 files, 2,443 tests), build, `check:source-fixtures`, `check:source-docs`, `check:release-packages`, `check:provider-contracts` (40/40) and `check:public-boundary` all pass. `d0ecb531` changes only the pin and the review note, which no test reads.

Tag `v0.9.19` on the merge commit, run CI on the tag (the exact-ref gate), then publish `@agent-finops/core`, `@agent-finops/report`, `ai-spend-agent` and `aibill` in that order, and check each `dist.shasum` against a fresh `npm pack` from the tag.

author: pplupo
body:
On KDE Plasma (and other environments using kio-extras without GVfs MTP), plugging in an Android/MTP device exposed an empty /run/user/<UID>/kio-fuse-* drive entry, while kio-fuse blacklists the mtp scheme and KDE Device Notifier URLs (mtp:udi=...) failed to resolve.

- Filter fuse.kio-fuse mounts in uDriveWatcher.CheckMountEntry so empty kio-fuse mount points do not appear in the drive list.
- Implement a direct org.kde.kmtpd5 D-Bus client (org.kde.kmtp.Daemon, Device, and Storage) and TKmtpFileSource in uKde, registered as the 'KMTP' virtual file source (list, copy in/out, delete, mkdir, rename, properties, statistics).
- Enumerate KMTP devices and subscribe to devicesChanged signals in uGVolume so connected MTP devices appear natively in the drive bar.
- Preserve GVfs mtp:// handling in TGioFileSource on non-KDE desktops while routing mtp:// on KDE (and non-KDE systems without GVfs MTP) through TKmtpFileSource.
- Preserve and resolve mtp:udi=..., mtp:/..., and kio-fuse MTP UDI paths in uCmdLineParams, uDCUtils, uFileSourceUtil, and fMain.

The API JSON export allocates far more on `develop` than on v0.12.1, and the inherited-member derived properties added in #1915 are where it goes: `Type::input`, `Type::output` and `Type::directedFeature` each read the direction of every effective feature of a type, and each of those reads walks the owner's general types.

**Relation to #2377.** #2377 memoizes `structureOwnedFeatures` and `structureOwnedSupertypes` for the same walk and is meant to land first. This branch has #2377 merged into it and carries no copy of those two memos; until #2377 is in `develop`, its commit shows in this diff. What this pull request adds on top, per element, in `internal/semantic/metamodel`:

body:
## Resumen

Cierra **F1-09 (OAuth 2.0 client credentials)**, el último elemento abierto del plan.

En la demo pública, el token OAuth salía con `scopes: []` y la API respondía 403 a todo, aunque la credencial tenía concedidos 19 recursos en **API resources**. InvGate solo incluye en el token los permisos que se piden de forma explícita en el parámetro `scope`, con el formato `api.v1.<recurso>:<método>`.

## Cambios

- `OAuth2ClientCredentials` envía `scope` en la solicitud del token. Por defecto pide los 19 permisos que usa el PoC (`DEFAULT_OAUTH_SCOPES`).
- Variable nueva `INVGATE_OAUTH_SCOPES`, separada por espacios o comas, para cambiarlos. Documentada en `.env.example`.
- `docs/VALIDACION_REAL.md` y `docs/POC_EVIDENCIAS.md`: el hallazgo y la evidencia.

## Validación contra `webdemo.cloud.invgate.net` por OAuth

- `make check-invgate ARGS="--write"`: **11/11** (catálogos, crear, leer, actualizar y comentar).
- Aprobación desde Teams («Help Desk IA»): ticket #361, aprobación 41 aceptada por el manager y la observación guardada como comentario.
- Evidencia: `docs/evidencias/invgate-oauth-2026-11-18.txt`, sin credenciales.

## Pruebas

- 182 pruebas en verde, cobertura del 98,05 %.
- Ruff y mypy (`--explicit-package-bases`) sin hallazgos.
- Tests nuevos: los scopes se envían en el token, y los configurados sustituyen a los de por defecto.

author: sareljvr2024
body:
## What

`CvCompare`'s own "Tailored (this tender)" preview (the side-by-side CV card on the Tender Workspace) picked the newest `generated_cvs` row by `requested_at` - when a CV was asked for. The real pack builder (`engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `cv_download_target()`) picks the newest by `completed_at` - when it actually finished - **and** requires a real `storage_path_pdf`; a `status='ready'` row whose PDF conversion never produced a path is invisible to it, falling back to the person's as-is upload instead.

## Why this is real and reachable

A company requests a "detailed" tailored CV for a key person (more content, slower to generate), then shortly after requests a "summary" one for the same person+position - ordinary usage, not a contrived edge case. The summary job, requested second, finishes first (less content to generate). `CvCompare`'s own `requested_at`-ordered query shows the summary CV as "the tailored CV going into this pack." The real pack builder, ordering by `completed_at`, picks whichever finished **last** - by then, the detailed one. The company reviews a document that is not the one their real submission pack will actually contain. Separately, a docx-only "ready" row (PDF conversion failed) could be shown as a valid tailored CV even though the real pack would silently skip it.

## Fix

Extracted the real selection rule into a new, tested pure sibling `cv-compare-logic.ts`'s `pickTailoredCv()` - mirrors `cv_download_target()`'s own rule exactly (newest `completed_at` among rows with a real PDF). `cv-compare.tsx` now selects `completed_at` and calls this function instead of ordering by `requested_at`.

## Test plan
- [x] New test `cv-compare-logic.test.ts` (6 cases)
- [x] RED: swapping in the exact pre-fix rule (newest by `requested_at`, no PDF requirement) fails 2 of 6 cases - exactly the real-bug and no-PDF cases
- [x] GREEN: fix restored, 6/6 pass
- [x] Every one of the 9 `app/tenders/[id]/*.test.ts` files (108 tests total) run individually → all pass - see note below on why "individually" matters
- [x] `npx vitest run` → 894/895 (pre-existing, documented flake unrelated to this change)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` → zero errors in touched files (pre-existing, documented `app/layout.tsx` gap only)
- [x] `npx eslint` on all 3 touched/added files → clean
- [x] Confirmed `main` unchanged at `d85efd27` before and after this branch was cut

**Incidental tooling note, not a product issue:** discovered that Node's `--test` flag, given many explicit file arguments via `$(find ... -name "*.test.ts")`, silently drops every test file under an `app/tenders/[id]/` path from the run. Confirmed this predates this fix - even the already-existing `position-cv-jobs-logic.test.ts` in the same directory is equally absent from that aggregate tally, with or without this change - so verified every file in that directory individually instead rather than trusting a misleadingly-unchanged aggregate count.

Per the standing guardrail, this is opened as its own PR and will not be merged without Sarel's explicit go-ahead.

body:
## Problem

- The audit log filter dropdowns take 30 to 50 s to load for large organizations.
- `available_filters` counts every activity log row in the organization on each request. It only needs to know whether the count is above 20,000.

## Changes

- The filters load in milliseconds for large organizations. The response does not change.
- The request path now counts at most 20,001 rows. Postgres stops reading once it reaches that limit.
- The Celery cache rebuild keeps the full count, because it sizes its sampling batches from it.

| Org count, one large organization | Time |
|---|---|
| Full count | 21,973 ms |
| Capped count, 3 runs | 17 to 54 ms |

author: milliec
body:
## What

Third of seven B3 (stand-in part) steps. Plain code with no model, not wired in yet (steps 5 and 7).

- `backend/domain/schemas.py`: the output shapes of the three agent steps (`ExtractionResult`/`Row`, `VerificationResult`/`Flag`, `Verdict`) with the shared vocabulary from sad.md §2. Unknown fields are refused. Offsets are a period rule or a fixed day and month, never a calendar date.
- `backend/domain/guardrails.py`: one guardrail function per agent card. It returns the parsed output or the refusal reason. The extractor's cited paragraph must be in its document and the recipient code must be in the list (the quote is **not** checked here; W-04 runs afterwards). The verifier's evidence must be word for word (QN-1 reused). The judge may cite only IDs from its input, and gives `missing_information` exactly when unsure.

## Operator decision: "no date-shaped value"

A date-shaped value is refused **unless it is copied word for word from the agent's input**. Read literally, the SAD's wording fails correct output: the `SRC-VATLAW-P1` quote contains "31 October", and an applicability rule may name the "Law of 17 December 2010". Month names count only when capitalised. **H-052** asks `@system.arch` to match the SAD wording.

## Checks

- `pytest tests`: 194 passed (39 new in `tests/tier1/test_guardrails.py`)
- Real-name scan: nothing found
- `aamad validate`: only the known missing-artifact findings
- Visual check: not run (no page change)

author: abiassi
body:
## Why

The free Vercel team has used its 4 h/month of Fluid Active CPU. In a 30-minute sample, `/og` used 3.9 of the 4.5 CPU seconds, about 2 s per uncached render (Satori + resvg). The CDN cached each image, but every production deploy emptied that cache, and each of the 260 distinct images was then drawn again on its next request.

## What changed

Pages now link `/og/t/<id>.png`. `next build` draws each of those once, and the files are served as static output. Serving one runs no function.

- **What an image depends on.** The renderer ignores `subtitle` and pages never send `lang`. An image is therefore a function of `(title, color)` alone. `src/lib/seo/og-image-spec.ts` normalizes those two values and hashes them into an 11-character ID (cyrb53).
- **Registry.** `src/data/og-images.json` is generated. It maps each ID to its spec. `createOgImagePath()` returns `/og/t/<id>.png` when the ID is registered, and otherwise the old `/og?…` URL, so an unregistered title still gets the right image at request time. Breathing pages now go through the same helper (`createBreathingOgImagePath`), because `/og/[slug]` was only `(hero title, pattern color)`.
- **Static route.** `src/app/og/t/[file]/route.tsx`: Node runtime, `dynamic = 'force-static'`, `dynamicParams = false`, `generateStaticParams` from the registry. An unknown ID returns a 404 and renders nothing.
- **Fonts.** The fonts are vendored in `assets/og-fonts/` under the OFL, with the licence files included. Inter 400/700 are byte-for-byte the TTFs Google Fonts served at runtime. For Japanese titles, `@vercel/og` used to fetch a Noto Sans JP subset containing only the glyphs Inter lacks. Satori picks one font per word from the word's first character, so the full font would draw `60` in `：60秒` in Noto instead of Inter Bold. The vendored copy is therefore subset the same way, with Google's layout features. The steps are in `assets/og-fonts/README.md`. The build fetches nothing: every character in the 260 titles is covered.
- **Keeping it current.** `scripts/build-og-registry.mjs` reads `og:image`, `twitter:image` and JSON-LD `image` URLs from the built HTML and rewrites the registry (`pnpm og:registry`). With `--check` it fails and names the pages that fell back to request-time rendering. CI runs `pnpm run check:og-registry` right after `pnpm exec next build` in the "Tests, typecheck, lint, Expo Doctor" job. The rule is added to CLAUDE.md "Rules that checks enforce" and to tools-and-data-sources.md, gotcha 29.

### Why route handlers (option a) rather than PNGs written to `public/`

The prerendered PNGs are part of `next build`'s own output, which Vercel serves as static files. Writing to `public/` after `next build` would rely on Vercel collecting `public/` after the build command runs. Feature branches get no preview, so I couldn't verify that here. Every OG URL a page emits must also be known before the build. A committed registry with a CI check gives that list without a second build. It works like the i18n inventory.

## Old URLs (social caches)

| Request | Behavior | Runtime CPU |
|---|---|---|
| `/og?title=…` for a registered title (`color` optional) | 307 to `/og/t/<id>.png`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, s-maxage=31536000` | One edge invocation that hashes and redirects, about 1 ms, then cached at the CDN for the deployment. No Satori. |
| `/og/<slug>` (any `cb`) | 307 to the slug's `/og/t/<id>.png` | Same as above |
| `/og?…&lang=xx`, `/og/<slug>?lang=xx` (old proxy era), unregistered titles, unknown slugs | Rendered as before (unchanged code path, Google Fonts fetch) | About 2 s per uncached URL, as today. Nothing on the site links these any more. |

The redirect is a 307, not a 308. A client that cached it still reaches the old handler if an ID ever leaves the registry.

## Results

- **Images generated:** 260. Every distinct `og:image` / `twitter:image` / JSON-LD image across the 343 prerendered pages, plus the layout default used by the dynamic `/stats` and `/recommend`.
- **Build time (local, cold `.next`, Apple Silicon):** 34.2 s → 52.5 s wall (+18 s). User CPU went from 66.8 s to 159.2 s (+92 CPU-s, about 0.35 CPU-s per image). On Vercel's build machine expect +25–45 s depending on cores. I have not measured it there.
- **Match:** 252 of 260 are **pixel-identical** to the images the current code renders. All 240 Latin-script images are byte-identical. **8 Japanese titles are visually indistinguishable but not identical**: glyphs move about 1 px. Google built a subset per title, and opentype.js kerning depends on which glyphs are in the subset. One vendored font can't reproduce all of them. I tried three feature sets; this one has the fewest differences.
- Two production images (home, `/og/box`) were fetched and are pixel-identical to the new static files, which confirms the local "before" matches production. Both were CDN misses, which cost about 4 CPU-s in total.

## Evidence

Each image shows before, after, and a diff mask (white = changed). Details, the route table and HTTP checks are in [`docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/README.md`](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/README.md).

**English home (0 px differ)**
![English home](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/en-home.png?raw=true)

**/breathe/box (0 px)**
![box](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/breathe-box.png?raw=true)

**/breathe/4-7-8 (0 px)**
![4-7-8](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/breathe-4-7-8.png?raw=true)

**Japanese home (0 px)**
![ja home](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/ja-home.png?raw=true)

**Long title, clamped to 72 characters (0 px)**
![long title](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/long-title-es.png?raw=true)

**Worst Japanese case (4,649 px), with a 2× zoom of the title strip**
![ja worst](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/ja-worst-case.png?raw=true)
![ja worst zoom](https://github.com/abiassi/deepbreathing/blob/8b6a323/docs/evidence/og-static-images-2026-11-18/ja-worst-case-zoom.png?raw=true)

### Build output: no OG route left on the hot path

```
├ ƒ /og                    (legacy: redirect, or render for lang/unknown)
├ ƒ /og/[slug]             (legacy: redirect, or render for lang)
├ ● /og/t/[file]
├   ├ /og/t/00cgzg9ux8l.png
├   └ [+257 more paths]
```
`prerender-manifest.json` lists `/og/t/[file]` with `fallback: false`, and each path with `initialRevalidateSeconds: false` and `initialHeaders` `content-type: image/png` and `x-robots-tag: noindex`.

### `next start` checks

```
/ -> https://deepbreathingexercises.com/og/t/0ib7kwl33rk.png
/ja -> https://deepbreathingexercises.com/og/t/19kw9pi0xjc.png
/breathe/box -> https://deepbreathingexercises.com/og/t/2ej6oetr05q.png
/ja/breathe/box -> https://deepbreathingexercises.com/og/t/2ej6oetr05q.png
/es/for/anxiety -> https://deepbreathingexercises.com/og/t/0zb4n90i1pz.png
/stats, /recommend -> https://deepbreathingexercises.com/og/t/0ib7kwl33rk.png

GET /og/t/0ib7kwl33rk.png -> 200 image/png, x-robots-tag: noindex, x-nextjs-cache: HIT
GET /og?title=Free+Breathing+Visualizer%3A+Calm+Anxiety+in+60+Seconds -> 307 /og/t/0ib7kwl33rk.png
GET /og/box -> 307 /og/t/2ej6oetr05q.png
GET /og/box?lang=ja -> 200 image/png (rendered, as before)
GET /og/t/notregistered.png -> 404
```
All 260 old URLs, fetched with redirects followed, returned their image in 0.9 s total. The old routes took 90 s.

## Tests and checks

- `pnpm lint`: no new warnings. `pnpm typecheck`: clean. `node --test scripts/tests/*.test.mjs`: 465 pass, 0 fail.
- `pnpm run check:og-registry` after the final build: "OG registry is current: 260 static images."

author: kushuh
body:
## Summary

- **Open lists frost the page again.** #375 (v0.25.0) moved Select's list into the internal Listbox and dropped the `@supports` block that also held the list's `background: none`. A list is a popover, so the browser painted its default opaque `Canvas` under the frost layer (`::before`, `z-index: -1` inside the popover's stacking context), and the frost blurred only that flat gray. The list now paints nothing of its own; the frost layer reaching past it carries its well, as in v0.24.1. ActionMenu frosts its own box and was not affected.
- **Brighter outlines.** `--color-border-default` rises a quarter step along the neutral ramp (OKLCH lightness 0.351 to 0.371), the developer's pick between a quarter and a half step. `--color-border-item` now aliases it, so ghost cards (Studio's project cards) and fields outside a card take the outline button's border instead of a dimmer translucent ring (about 0.319 on the canvas). Checkbox, switch and radio outlines, the avatar ring and the spinner track use the same token and brighten with it.
- **Slightly deeper tags.** Each `--color-label-*` fill (badges, genres, tags, role badges, chosen chips) sits a quarter step deeper along its own ramp, mixed in OKLab with the step below, so no hue clips. Contrast with the label text rises: neutral 4.85 to 5.34, brand 4.79 to 5.12, accent 5.18 to 5.45, highlight 4.88 to 5.27. The mixes stay inside Display P3, as the ramp steps do.

## Breaking changes

None. Token names and component APIs are unchanged; only rendered values move, so this is a patch.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint` (generated colors and the color contract included)
- [x] Unit, SSR and browser projects: 74 files pass in the Playwright 1.65.1 image
- [x] New Listbox browser test: a Select and a Combobox list paint no background and frost with a blur; both fail with the reset removed
- [x] Card test now pins a ghost card's ring to the outline button's border
- [x] CI green (only `review-gate` waits on a review)
- [x] Screenshots: all 137 Storybook screenshots match master's references. Each shift is a couple of sRGB levels, inside Vitest's default per-pixel color tolerance, so the gate cannot see it; the developer reviewed rendered before/after captures of Studio's projects page, badges and chips locally and chose the quarter step.

- `docs/INVESTIGATION-ASSOCIATION.md` line 132: "The study skipped the 314 ambiguous measurements out of 28590." is now "The 314 ambiguous measurements out of 28590 carry no label, so they cannot count as steals." No table or other sentence changed; 314 and 28590 are unchanged.
- `ROADMAP.md`: R24 ticked. `docs/BUILD-LOG.md`: R24 row added.

### Code reference for the ambiguous-measurement claim

- `tools/study_common.hpp`, `label_of`: returns a label only if the nearest truth vehicle is within the 3 m gate and at least `kLabelMarginM` (1 m) nearer than the second nearest; otherwise the `CarLabel` (`std::optional<int>`) is empty, which the studies call ambiguous.
- `tools/kite_association_study.cpp` `run_seed`: line 194 counts a measurement with an empty label as ambiguous (`result.ambiguous += labels.back() ? 0 : 1`). Lines 197-201 skip any tentative track whose measurement has no label (`!labels[*tentative.measurement]` then `continue`), so an ambiguous measurement is never recorded as a steal. A steal is defined by the label (`const int car = *labels[...]`), which an ambiguous measurement does not have.

body:
### 🛰️ Quick Summary

Reruns under `mise run site:affected` only the tests a changed trigger file reaches, so editing a file the tests read from disk or run reruns the tests that read it, and a page, workflow, or task no test reads reruns none, where any of them reran the whole suite. A change to `docs/bun.lock`, `.mise/config.toml`, `.mise/mise.lock`, or the crate's sources and manifests still reruns every test, and the `☂️ Coverage` row still runs the whole suite on every push.

---

### 📻 Key Changes

- Adds `READS` in `docs/.vitepress/tests/common/reads.ts`, mapping each test or module to the globs of the files it reads or runs without importing them, which the `reads` plugin in `docs/.vitepress/tests/vitest.config.ts` adds to that module's graph as watched files, keyed in Vitest's module cache on the files each glob matches so an added file selects its readers on a warm cache

- Narrows `forceRerunTriggers` in `docs/.vitepress/tests/vitest.config.ts` to the lockfiles, the mise config, and the crate's manifest, lockfile, and sources, dropping the globs over the workflows, the tasks, the pages and stylesheets, the public files, and the suite's stand-in binaries, whose readers `READS` now declares

- Selects the readers of a deleted file and of a renamed file's old path by wrapping `vitest.vcs` in the plugin's `configureVitest`, listing the changes with `diff.renames=false` added to the git config the environment carries, and selects `docs/.vitepress/tests/reads.test.ts` wherever a deletion leaves a `READS` entry stale

- Fails `runTask` in `docs/.vitepress/tests/common/tasks.ts` where the running test declares no read of the task it runs, and checks in `docs/.vitepress/tests/reads.test.ts` that each `READS` module exists and each glob matches a file

body:
Implementa el flujo comercial completo entre Bot, CxC y Odoo:
- Lista comercial activa por defecto (ej. Pago VES Nov 2026 / Pago VES Sept 2026)
- Catálogo de descuentos de CxC y evaluación contra parámetros del motor e historial sincronizado (alertas en tiempo de cotización)
- Preview HTML compartible e imprimible (/cotizacion/<token>) con botón para convertir en Pedido
- Estado Pedido pendiente por aprobación (PENDIENTE_APROBACION) y acción protegida por ventas.aprobar_pedidos
- Envío autorizado a Odoo con precios normales de lista (sin descuentos en líneas) y detalle completo de descuentos en nota y chatter de Odoo
